title: [Feature] Support function-level attributes to avoid embedding metadata in the function body
body:
### Summary

Introduce **function-level attributes** (a structured metadata bag attached to a `Function` / `pl.function`, analogous in spirit to op call kwargs but scoped to the whole function) so that auxiliary configuration, hints, or bookkeeping data does not need to be represented **inside the function body** as extra IR.

### Motivation / Use Case

Today, metadata that is not really part of the SSA computation often ends up **serialized into the body** (extra statements, dummy values, or ad-hoc patterns). That inflates IR size, complicates passes and dumps, and mixes concerns. Allowing small, typed or string-keyed **attrs on the function object** would keep the body focused on real compute and make it easier to thread information through the pipeline without polluting every pass with body-only workarounds.

### Proposed API / Behavior

- **IR (`Function`)**: extend the function definition with an optional map of attributes (key → value with a constrained type set consistent with existing op attr conventions where possible), preserved through round-trip and visible in dumps.
- **Python surface**: e.g. `pl.function(..., attrs={...})` or an explicit helper, subject to API design.
- **Passes / codegen**: read attrs where needed without synthesizing equivalent IR in the body.

Exact schema (which keys, which value types, and printer/bindings shape) can be decided in implementation; the goal is a **first-class** place for function-scoped metadata.

### Additional Context

Related direction (not duplicate): orchestration and `pl.function` ergonomics are evolving (e.g. parameter-only outputs in [#615](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/615)); function attrs would complement those by separating **metadata** from **body** without overloading parameters or the body.

title: fix(codegen): allocate GM pipe buffer via add_output(TensorCreateInfo) in orchestration
body:
## Summary

On Ascend910B (a2a3), the `__gm_pipe_buffer` parameter was incorrectly treated as a host-provided tensor in orchestration codegen, causing:
1. `expected_arg_count=4` while host only provides 3 tensors
2. Pipe buffer silently dropped from kernel task params (name resolved to `""` due to `__` delimiter in `auto_name::Parse`)

## Fix

- Skip `__gm_pipe_buffer` from host arg extraction and `expected_arg_count`
- Emit `TensorCreateInfo` + `add_output()` to let simpler runtime allocate GM space from its per-ring heap (**no new runtime API needed**)
- Fix name resolution to use full name instead of `GetSSABaseName`
- Set `manual_dep=true` to skip TensorMap registration (pipe buffer needs no cross-task dependency tracking)

## Generated orchestration (before → after)

**Before** (broken):
```cpp
.expected_arg_count = 4,  // host only provides 3!
Tensor ext_ = from_tensor_arg(orch_args.tensor(3));  // crashes
// pipe buffer missing from task params
```

**After** (fixed):
```cpp
.expected_arg_count = 3,
TensorCreateInfo __gm_pipe_buffer_ci(..., /*manual_dep=*/true);
params_t0.add_output(__gm_pipe_buffer_ci);  // runtime allocates GM
```

title: [Codegen] Identity pto.tmov (dst == src) causes ptoas to insert spurious sync, hanging on A5
body:
When a `tile.move` op's source and destination resolve to the same address/MemRef, pypto codegen still emits a `pto.tmov ins(x : T) outs(x : T)` instruction. ptoas treats any `pto.tmov` as a data-movement op and inserts sync instructions around it; for a no-op tmov these syncs are spurious and cause synchronization errors that hang the kernel on A5. The same code passes on A3 due to different sync behavior between the two platforms.

The only existing identity check is in `MakeTileAssembleCodegenPTO` (`pto_ops_common.cpp` line ~288: `if (target != dst)`). The generic `tile.move` codegen path (`MakeNaryCodegenPTO`, `pto_ops_common.cpp` line ~1113) has no such guard.

## Reproducer

[fa5_softmax_rescale.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26403743/fa5_softmax_rescale.py)

title: [Pass] ConvertTensorToTileOps: assemble-to-store rewrite not handled for IfStmt branches
body:
`RewriteReturnedAssembleLoopToStore` in `src/ir/transforms/convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp` converts a `tile.assemble` that drives a `ForStmt` iter-arg into an in-place `tile.store` inside the loop body. There is no equivalent handling for `IfStmt`: when a `tensor.assemble` is the return value of an `IfStmt` (either from the then- or else-branch), the pass does not sink the store into the branches, leaving the assemble unrewritten.

PR #783 addressed the `ForStmt` case and noted "no store sinking into branches needed" for the IfStmt scenario it fixed (where the store was placed outside). The missing case is a `tensor.assemble` whose result is yielded inside an `IfStmt` branch and returned as the if-expression result — the store may need to be placed inside the then/else branches analogously to the ForStmt treatment.

[fa5_softmax_rescale.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26404599/fa5_softmax_rescale.py)

title: fix(ir,parser): fix TensorView/TileView int support and add column-accurate enum diagnostics
body:
## Summary

Two independent fixes bundled in one PR:

### Commit 1: fix(ir): add int64 constructor overloads for TensorView and TileView

Fixes the broken int support introduced in #813. That PR used Python monkey-patching to intercept `TensorView.__init__`, but nanobind C++ types use a C-level `tp_init` slot that bypasses Python `__init__` attribute assignment, so the monkey-patching silently had no effect and all 7 new tests were failing.

**Fix:**
- Add `TensorView(std::vector<int64_t>, ...)` and `TileView(std::vector<int64_t>, ...)` constructors in C++ header and implementation
- Expose `nb::init<int64_t>` overloads in the Python binding
- Replace broken monkey-patching with Python factory classes backed by custom metaclasses: `__call__` normalizes mixed `int`/`Expr` lists, `__instancecheck__` preserves `isinstance()` compatibility with C++-created instances
- Add `python/pypto/ir/__init__.pyi` stub so pyright treats `ir.TensorView`/`ir.TileView` as the canonical C++ types

### Commit 2: fix(parser): add column-accurate enum diagnostics for pl.parse() (#807)

When `pl.parse()` encounters an invalid enum value such as `pl.FunctionType.BadType`, the error was a bare `AttributeError` at column 0 with no hint about valid values.

**Fix:** Pre-validate `@pl.function` decorator kwargs (`type=`, `level=`, `role=`) at AST level before `exec()`. The AST node carries precise column offsets.

Before:
```
Error: AttributeError: ...
  --> <string>:2:0
```

After:
```
Error: Unknown FunctionType value: BadType
  --> <string>:2:34
  |
2 | @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.BadType)
  |                                   ^^^^^^^ Unknown FunctionType value
  |
   = help: Valid values: Opaque, Orchestration, InCore, AIC, AIV, Group
```

Also improves `RoundtripInstrument` to use `ErrorRenderer` for formatted parse failure messages instead of dumping raw IR.

## Testing

- All 3305 unit tests pass
- clang-tidy clean on changed C++ files
- All pre-commit hooks pass (ruff, pyright, clang-format, cpplint, markdownlint)
- 7 previously failing tests from #813 now pass
- 7 new tests for #807 diagnostics

## Related Issues

Fixes #807
Also fixes the broken implementation from #813

title: fix(codegen): remove redundant pto.tmov from IfStmt emit_branch for tile returns
body:
MemoryReuse's YieldFixupMutator ensures all IfStmt branch yields and the return_var share the same canonical MemRef (same physical address). The codegen-level pto.tmov emitted by emit_branch was therefore always a no-op (addr B → addr B), wasting a cycle.

Remove the tmov generation from emit_branch. The pre-declared tile buffer for the return_var (via AllocNewTileBuf) is kept for SSA visibility after the scf.if block. The IR-level tile.move (inserted by YieldFixupMutator when then/else yields have different MemRefs) handles the actual copy.

Fixes #803

title: fix(ir): tensor.matmul type deduction missing K-dimension validation
body:
### Description

`DeduceTensorMatMulType` in `src/ir/op/tensor_ops/matmul.cpp` computes output shapes without validating that the inner (K) dimensions of lhs and rhs actually match. This allows mathematically invalid matmul configurations to pass type deduction silently.

For example, `test_tensor_matmul_with_transpose` in `tests/ut/debug/test_torch_codegen.py` uses tensor shapes that are invalid under the specified transpose flags, but the test passes because K is never checked:

```python
def test_tensor_matmul_with_transpose():
    """tensor.matmul with a_trans/b_trans should emit .mT."""
    a = _tensor_var("a", [64, 128])
    b = _tensor_var("b", [128, 64])
    out = _tensor_var("out", [64, 64])
    call = _op_call("tensor.matmul", [a, b], {"a_trans": True, "b_trans": False, "c_matrix_nz": False})
    assign = ir.AssignStmt(out, call, _span())
    func = _simple_function("f", [a, b], assign)
    code = torch_codegen(func)
    assert "a.mT" in code
    assert "torch.matmul" in code
```

The `a_trans=True` kwarg is passed to `tensor.matmul` via `_op_call`, which calls `ir.create_op_call("tensor.matmul", ...)` and ends up in `DeduceTensorMatMulType`. In the type deduction logic, `a_trans=True` means:

- `lhs_k = a_trans ? lhs_shape[0] : lhs_shape[1]` → `lhs_shape[0]`
- `rhs_k = b_trans ? rhs_shape[1] : rhs_shape[0]` → `rhs_shape[0]`

With the original shapes `a=[64, 128]` and `b=[128, 64]`:
- `lhs_k = 64`, `rhs_k = 128` → **K mismatch (64 ≠ 128)**

### Root Cause

In the 2D×2D branch of `DeduceTensorMatMulType` (lines 107-111), only M and N dimensions are extracted — K is never computed or validated:

```cpp
} else if (lhs_shape.size() == 2 && rhs_shape.size() == 2) {
    ExprPtr m_dim = a_trans ? lhs_shape[1] : lhs_shape[0];
    ExprPtr n_dim = b_trans ? rhs_shape[0] : rhs_shape[1];
    output_shape = {m_dim, n_dim};
}
```

The same missing validation exists in all other branches: 1D×1D dot product, 2D×1D matrix-vector, 1D×2D vector-matrix, and batched matmul.

By contrast, `DeduceTensorMatMulAccType` (lines 206-217) correctly validates K dimensions, as do all `tile.matmul` variants.

### Fix

Add K-dimension matching checks (when statically known) to all branches of `DeduceTensorMatMulType`, following the existing `matmul_acc` pattern. Fix the test to use valid shapes: `a=[128, 64]`, `b=[128, 64]` → `K=128` on both sides.

title: [Pass Bug] Reshape [1,N]→[N,1] split missing sub-block row offset causes wrong inv_rms for upper sub-block
body:
### Pass Name

SplitVectorKernel

### Description

SplitVectorKernel splits the AIV vector kernel into 2 sub-blocks (split=UP_DOWN), each handling BATCH_TILE/2 rows. When a [1, N] tile is loaded and reshaped to [N, 1], the pass correctly updates the output tile type annotation from [N, 1] to [N/2, 1] (one half per sub-block), but does not add a sub-block row offset to the reshape. Both sub-blocks end up reading from the same UB buffer start address, so sub-block 1 reads elements [0:N/2] instead of [N/2:N].

Concrete example (BATCH_TILE=16, N=16):

sub-block 0 (rows 0–7): inv_rms_b0__tile[0:8, 0] = inv_rms[0:8] ✓
sub-block 1 (rows 8–15): inv_rms_b0__tile[0:8, 0] = inv_rms[0:8] ✗ (should be inv_rms[8:16])
Result: row_expand_mul for sub-block 1 multiplies with wrong scale factors → all output rows 8–15 of q_proj are incorrect. Mismatched elements: 81920/81920 (all elements).

### Git Commit ID

 a04875d513a5e1255654beec04d9db764b4aba32

### Before IR (Input)

```python
Pass 17 (17_after_ExpandMixedKernel.py) — correct:
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.AIV, attrs={"split": pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN})
def q_proj_incore1_incore_0_aiv(self, ...):
    subblock_idx: pl.Scalar[pl.INT64] = pl.tile.get_subblock_idx()
    for ob__ci_idx_v0, ... in pl.parallel(4, ...):
        # Load full [1, 16] inv_rms — no sub-block offset needed here
        inv_rms_b0_T__tile: pl.Tile[[1, 16], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Vec] = \
            pl.tile.load(inv_rms_tile__ssa_v0, [0, b0__idx_v0], [1, 16], [1, 16], ...)
        # Reshape to [16, 1] — both sub-blocks should share first half / second half respectively
        inv_rms_b0__tile: pl.Tile[[16, 1], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Vec] = \
            pl.tile.reshape(inv_rms_b0_T__tile, [16, 1])
        for kb__idx_v0, ... in pl.range(40, ...):
            # hidden_states load correctly uses subblock_idx * 8 offset:
            t__tile: pl.Tile[[16, 128], ...] = pl.tile.load(hidden_states, [b0__idx_v0, k0__ssa_v0], ...)
            t__tile_1: pl.Tile[[16, 128], ...] = pl.tile.row_expand_mul(x_chunk__tile, inv_rms_b0__tile)
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

```python
Pass 18 should generate per-sub-block slices with correct offsets:
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.AIV, attrs={"split": pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN})
def q_proj_incore1_incore_0_aiv(self, ...):
    subblock_idx: pl.Scalar[pl.INT64] = pl.tile.get_subblock_idx()
    for ob__ci_idx_v0, ... in pl.parallel(4, ...):
        inv_rms_b0_T__tile: pl.Tile[[1, 16], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Vec] = \
            pl.tile.load(inv_rms_tile__ssa_v0, [0, b0__idx_v0], [1, 16], [1, 16], ...)
        # After split: each sub-block should get its own 8 elements with correct offset
        inv_rms_b0__tile: pl.Tile[[8, 1], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Vec] = \
            pl.tile.slice(pl.tile.reshape(inv_rms_b0_T__tile, [16, 1]),
                          [8, 1], [subblock_idx * 8, 0])
        for kb__idx_v0, ... in pl.range(40, ...):
            t__tile: pl.Tile[[8, 128], ...] = \
                pl.tile.load(hidden_states, [b0__idx_v0 + subblock_idx * 8, k0__ssa_v0], [8, 128], ...)
            t__tile_1: pl.Tile[[8, 128], ...] = pl.tile.row_expand_mul(x_chunk__tile, inv_rms_b0__tile)
```

### Actual IR or Error

```shell
Pass 18 (18_after_SplitVectorKernel.py) — type updated, offset missing:
        inv_rms_b0_T__tile: pl.Tile[[1, 16], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Vec] = \
            pl.tile.load(inv_rms_tile__ssa_v0, [0, b0__idx_v0], [1, 16], [1, 16], ...)
        # BUG: type annotation shrunk to [8,1] but reshape arg is still [16,1],
        #      and NO sub-block offset is applied — both sub-blocks read inv_rms[0:8]
        inv_rms_b0__tile: pl.Tile[[8, 1], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Vec] = \
            pl.tile.reshape(inv_rms_b0_T__tile, [16, 1])

Generated C++ (confirmed in q_proj_incore1_incore_0_aiv.cpp):
// v36=[1,16] loaded at UB offset v28=16384 — contains inv_rms[0..15]
TLOAD(v36, v39);
// v40=[8,1] ColMajor ALSO assigned from v28=16384 — ALWAYS reads inv_rms[0..7]
Tile<TileType::Vec, float, 8, 1, BLayout::ColMajor, ...> v40;
TASSIGN(v40, v28);   // ← same buffer, no offset for sub-block 1

// sub-block 0 (v33=0): x_chunk rows 0-7 * inv_rms[0:8]  ✓
// sub-block 1 (v33=1): x_chunk rows 8-15 * inv_rms[0:8] ✗ (should be inv_rms[8:16])
TROWEXPANDMUL(v54, v49, v40);

Runtime error:
AssertionError: Output 'q_proj' does not match golden.
Mismatched elements: 81920/81920
rtol=0.01, atol=0.01
```

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

Other (please specify in description)

### Host Platform (if relevant)

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- The hidden_states load is split correctly: pl.tile.load(..., [b0__idx_v0 + subblock_idx * 8, k0__ssa_v0], [8, 128], ...) — using subblock_idx * 8 as row offset. The same pattern is missing for the reshape result.
- The output store also correctly uses subblock_idx * 8: pl.tile.store(t__tile_3, [b0__idx_v0 + subblock_idx * 8, q0__ssa_v0], ...).
- Only the reshape path lacks the offset — SplitVectorKernel needs to recognise that after reshaping [1, N]→[N, 1], the split along the row dimension of the output requires subblock_idx * (N/2) as a slice offset.

Fix strategy:
In SplitVectorKernel, when a reshape result tile is split along its row dimension, insert a tile.slice(..., [N/2, 1], [subblock_idx * N/2, 0]) after the reshape, analogous to the sub-block offset already applied to global-memory loads.

title: [Pass Bug] SplitVectorKernel fails on pure AIC/AIV functions marked with SplitMode.UP_DOWN
body:
### Pass Name

SplitVectorKernel

### Description

`auto_incore(split=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)` marks **all** generated incore functions (AIC, AIV, Group) with `attrs={"split": pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN}`. The `SplitVectorKernel` pass then processes every function bearing this attribute, including pure AIC and pure AIV functions that don't need splitting. When a pure AIV function contains tiles with an odd-sized dimension (e.g., `[1, 16]`), the pass crashes with `SplitVectorKernel requires an even split dimension, got 1`.

### Git Commit ID

7fa07332ef943a1330d14e98466c328088ffdf43

### Before IR (Input)


title: [Bug] Dynamic orchestration codegen emits narrowing conversions into uint32_t shape/offset arrays
body:
## Summary

Dynamic orchestration/tensor codegen emits `uint32_t` shape and offset arrays from unconstrained expressions such as `int64_t` config values. Clang rejects the generated initializer lists as narrowing conversions, which breaks CPU-sim system tests before the kernels can even be built.

## Reproducer

On April 2, 2026, the following test failed on `a2a3sim` before local generator patching:

```bash
python -m pytest 'tests/st/codegen/test_dynamic_paged_attention.py::TestDynamicPagedAttentionKernels::test_dynamic_paged_attention[256-16-128-128-8192-32768]' --forked --platform=a2a3sim -q
```

Representative generated C++ failures looked like:

```cpp
uint32_t qi_shapes[2] = {16, head_dim_cfg};
uint32_t qi_offsets[2] = {cur_offset, 0};
uint32_t kj_shapes[2] = {block_size_cfg, head_dim_cfg};
```

where `head_dim_cfg`, `block_size_cfg`, and `cur_offset` were emitted as dynamic `int64_t` expressions.

## Root Cause

These generators declare arrays as `uint32_t[...]` but directly splice `GenerateExprString(...)` into the initializer list:

- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`
- `src/codegen/tensor_op_codegen.cpp`

For dynamic shape/offset expressions, the emitted C++ is not explicitly cast, so Clang treats the list initialization as a narrowing conversion error.

## Minimal Fix

Wrap emitted expressions for `uint32_t` shape/offset arrays with `static_cast<uint32_t>(...)` in the affected generators.

## Validation

A temporary local patch doing exactly that made the failing node above pass, and the full CPU-sim ST sweep then completed successfully:

- `131 passed, 67 skipped`

That local patch was reverted after validation; this issue is to track the real fix in `pypto`.

title: [Bug] Orchestration codegen emits unused const Tensor& alias variables
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

Orchestration codegen generates unused `const Tensor&` alias variables in the output C++ code. These variables are assigned but never referenced by any subsequent statement, producing dead code that may trigger compiler warnings (`-Wunused-variable`).

Example from `Scope3Incore4` orchestration output (`scope3_incore_4.cpp`):

```cpp
// Group scope3_incore_4_incore_0: MixedKernels (AIC + AIV)
Arg params_t0;
params_t0.add_inout(ext_down_proj_tile);
params_t0.add_input(ext_mlp_chunk_bf16);
params_t0.add_input(ext_w_down);
params_t0.add_scalar(dob);
MixedKernels mixed_0 = {0, 1, INVALID_KERNEL_ID};
pto2_rt_submit_task(mixed_0, params_t0);
const Tensor& down_proj_tile__co_l1_rv_v1 = ext_down_proj_tile;  // ← never used
```

The variable `down_proj_tile__co_l1_rv_v1` is emitted as a `const Tensor&` alias to `ext_down_proj_tile` but is never consumed before the enclosing scope ends. The codegen should either skip emitting variables that have no downstream consumers, or perform a dead-code elimination pass on the generated statements.

Related: #631

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Compile the `Scope3Incore4` program (or any program where the last IR value in a scope aliases an external tensor without further use)
2. Inspect the generated orchestration C++ file (`scope3_incore_4.cpp`)
3. Observe unused variable `down_proj_tile__co_l1_rv_v1` at line 72

### Expected Behavior

Generated orchestration code should not contain unused variables. If an IR value is not consumed by any subsequent operation in the generated code, the codegen should omit the variable definition entirely.

### Actual Behavior

The codegen emits `const Tensor& down_proj_tile__co_l1_rv_v1 = ext_down_proj_tile;` which is never used. This is dead code.

### Git Commit ID

8573714c782b698e3896b3cfee0cd3eea5d0ccd2

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

macOS (aarch64)

title: [Feature] Add pl.print DSL function to generate pto.tprint
body:
### Summary

Add a `pl.print` function to the Python DSL that lowers to the `pto.tprint` IR operation, allowing users to print tile buffer contents for debugging purposes.

### Motivation / Use Case

There is currently no way to print or inspect tile buffer values from the DSL level during development and debugging. A `pl.print` helper would let users insert debug print statements in their `@pl.program` kernels that lower to `pto.tprint` in the generated IR, making it much easier to trace data flow and verify intermediate tile values.

### Proposed API / Behavior

**DSL usage:**
```python
@pl.program
def my_kernel(...):
    tile = ...  # some tile_buf
    pl.print(tile)
```

title: [Code Health] Refactor loop escape handling from orchestration codegen into an IR lowering pass

labels.name: code health
labels.description: Technical debt, robustness concerns, code quality improvements

body:
### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Codegen

### Description

The orchestration codegen (`OrchestrationStmtCodegen::VisitStmt_(ForStmt)` in `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`) contains complex logic to handle "escaping loop returns" — ForStmt return variables that are referenced after the loop ends. This violates the project's [strict 1-to-1 mapping design principle](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/blob/main/docs/en/dev/codegen/01-orchestration_codegen.md#design-principle-strict-1-to-1-mapping) for orchestration codegen.

**What the current code does:**

1. `LoopEscapeInfoCollector` (analysis pass) detects which ForStmt `return_vars_` are referenced in subsequent statements.
2. In `VisitStmt_(ForStmt)`, codegen synthesizes a `__loop_state` tensor via `make_tensor_external(nullptr, ...)` to hold the last iteration's output.
3. After each task submit inside the loop, the output tensor is copy-assigned to this state tensor: `state = outs_tN.get_ref(i);`
4. Post-loop references use the `__loop_state` variable instead of the original return var.

This introduces two extra maps (`active_loop_output_states_`, `escaped_loop_return_exprs_`), a synthetic variable naming convention (`__loop_state`), and special-case code in `EmitTaskSubmitAndBind()` — all in the codegen layer.

**Why this is a problem:**

- Codegen should be a mechanical 1-to-1 translation from IR, not performing semantic analysis or synthesis
- The special-casing makes the codegen harder to reason about and test
- It's the same category of issue as #814 (analysis in codegen that belongs in a pass)

### Location

- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:287-338` — `VisitStmt_(ForStmt)` escape handling
- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:606-636` — `EmitTaskSubmitAndBind()` state copy-assignment
- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:972-974` — `escaped_loop_return_exprs_`, `active_loop_output_states_` maps
- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_analysis.cpp:284-334` — `LoopEscapeInfoCollector`

### Proposed Fix

Introduce an IR lowering pass (before codegen) that explicitly materializes the escaping loop state:

1. For each ForStmt whose return_vars are referenced post-loop, the pass inserts an explicit `tensor.create` for the state tensor before the loop.
2. Inside the loop body, after the relevant function call, the pass inserts a `tensor.assemble` (or equivalent copy op) to write the output into the state tensor.
3. Post-loop references are rewritten to use the state tensor directly.

After this pass, the IR explicitly represents the state tensor and its updates, so codegen can generate the corresponding C++ via the existing `tensor.create` / task submit paths without any special-case logic. The `LoopEscapeInfoCollector`, `escaped_loop_return_exprs_`, `active_loop_output_states_`, and the `__loop_state` synthesis code in codegen can all be removed.

Related: #814

### Priority

Low (no impact today, good to fix eventually)

title: [Refactor] Consolidate duplicated variable/memref collection utilities into common utils

labels.name: code health
labels.description: Technical debt, robustness concerns, code quality improvements

body:
### Summary

There are **30+ IR visitor classes** scattered across passes and codegen that collect variable uses, variable definitions, or MemRef references. Many are near-duplicates with identical semantics, reimplemented locally in each compilation unit. These should be consolidated into shared utilities.

### Motivation / Use Case

The current duplication leads to:
- **Maintenance burden**: bug fixes or API changes must be replicated across many files
- **Inconsistency risk**: subtly different collection semantics across passes (e.g., whether `iter_args` are included)
- **Code bloat**: each pass re-implements the same visitor pattern

**Key duplicates identified:**

| Category | Instances | Files |
| -------- | --------- | ----- |
| **Var use/ref collectors** | 5+ | `scope_outline_utils.h` (`VarRefCollector`), `memory_reuse_pass.cpp` (`VarUseCollector`), `convert_to_ssa_pass.cpp` (`UseCollector`), `warning_unused_var.cpp` (`UseCollector`), `convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp` (`VarUseVisitor`) |
| **Var def/assignment collectors** | 3+ | `scope_outline_utils.h` (`VarDefCollector`), `convert_to_ssa_pass.cpp` (`AssignmentCollector`, `TypeCollector`) |
| **MemRef collectors** | 5+ | `allocate_memory_addr_pass.cpp` (`MemRefCollectorVisitor`), `pto_codegen.cpp` (`MemRefCollectorVisitor`), `insert_sync_pass.cpp` (`MemRefCollector`), `init_memref.cpp` (`NonDDRMemRefCollector`), `legalize_pto_buffer_reuse_pass.cpp` (`MemRefUsageCollector`) |

The existing `scope_outline_utils.h` already provides a good public API with `VarRefCollector`, `VarDefCollector`, `StoreTargetCollector`, and `VarCollector` — but most passes don't use them and instead roll their own.

### Proposed API / Behavior

1. **Audit and unify Var collectors**: Extend `scope_outline_utils.h` (or create a new `include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/var_collect_utils.h`) to cover the common patterns:
   - Collect all used `Var*` in expressions (what `UseCollector` does in 3+ places)
   - Collect all defined `Var*` from statements (what `AssignmentCollector` / `VarDefCollector` do)
   - Check if a specific `Var*` is used in a subtree (what `VarUseVisitor` does)

2. **Audit and unify MemRef collectors**: Create `include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/memref_collect_utils.h` for:
   - Collect all `MemRef` from tile-typed variables
   - Collect with filtering (by memory space, by dedup)

3. **Migrate passes** to use the shared utilities, removing local duplicates.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Leave as-is**: Each pass keeps its own collector. Simpler in the short term but accumulates tech debt as more passes are added.
- **Template-based generic collector**: A single parameterized collector class. May be over-engineered for the current use cases.

title: [Pass Bug] ConvertToSSA: variables in TensorView.valid_shape not substituted
[Bug] IR printer emits spurious pl.dynamic() for locally-defined variables in valid_shape
body:
### Component

Printer

### Description

The IR Python printer emits spurious `pl.dynamic()` declarations for locally-defined scalar variables when they appear in `TensorView.valid_shape` expressions.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run any program that uses a locally-computed scalar in `valid_shape`, then dump the IR:

```python
import pypto.language as pl

@pl.program
class MyProgram:
    @pl.function
    def main(self, x: pl.Tensor[[16, 64], pl.FP32],
             n_tensor: pl.Tensor[[1], pl.INT32]) -> pl.Tensor[[8, 64], pl.FP32]:
        n: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32] = pl.tensor.read(n_tensor, [0])
        valid_len: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX] = pl.min(64, pl.cast(n, pl.INDEX))
        chunk: pl.Tensor[[8, 64], pl.FP32] = pl.tensor.slice(
            x, [8, 64], [0, 0], valid_shape=[8, valid_len]
        )
        return chunk
```

Compile with `dump_passes=True` and inspect the frontend dump.

### Expected Behavior

The dumped IR should NOT contain a `pl.dynamic("valid_len")` declaration. `valid_len` is locally defined as `pl.min(64, ...)` — it is not a global dynamic dimension.

```python
# Expected: no pl.dynamic() line — valid_len is local
import pypto.language as pl

@pl.program
class MyProgram:
    @pl.function
    def main(self, x: pl.Tensor[[16, 64], pl.FP32], ...):
        ...
        valid_len: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX] = pl.min(64, ...)
        chunk: ... pl.TensorView(valid_shape=[8, valid_len], ...) ...
```

### Actual Behavior

The printer emits a spurious global dynamic declaration:

```python
import pypto.language as pl

valid_len = pl.dynamic("valid_len")  # ← SPURIOUS: valid_len is a local scalar, not a global dynamic

@pl.program
class MyProgram:
    @pl.function
    def main(self, x: pl.Tensor[[16, 64], pl.FP32], ...):
        ...
        valid_len: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX] = pl.min(64, ...)  # correct local definition
        chunk: ... pl.TensorView(valid_shape=[8, valid_len], ...) ...
        #                                         ^^^^^^^^^ references the global dynamic, not the local
```

### Git Commit ID

d765fc00beff9bed72dde85fd05565a2b1f48cb3

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Additional Context

**Root cause**: In `src/ir/transforms/python_printer.cpp`, `CollectDynVarMapping` (lines 1412-1510) scans the entire function body (line 1499: `collector.VisitStmt(func->body_)`). For every `Var`, it collects vars from the Var's type annotation (line 1480-1483). When the collector encounters a `TensorType` whose `tensor_view_.valid_shape` contains a Var reference, it extracts it via `collect_vars_from_expr` (line 1444-1445), treating any Var found there as a global dynamic — even if that Var is locally defined.

**Fix direction**: The collector should exclude Vars that are defined in the function body (i.e., appear as LHS of `AssignStmt` or as `ForStmt` loop vars). Only Vars from function parameter/return types that are NOT locally defined should become `pl.dynamic()` declarations.

**Related issues**: #853, #855, #856

title: [Bug] UseAfterDefChecker does not verify variable references in type expressions
body:
### Component

Other (please specify in description)

### Description

The `UseAfterDefChecker` verifier does not traverse variable references inside type expressions (e.g., `TensorView.valid_shape`). This means undefined or dangling variable references in type metadata go undetected.

This is a verifier gap — the checker intentionally skips type expressions based on the assumption that "dynamic shape vars embedded in types are not defined by any statement in the function body." That assumption is incorrect when locally-defined scalars appear in `valid_shape`.

### Steps to Reproduce

Construct IR where a `TensorType`'s `TensorView.valid_shape` references a variable that is NOT in scope:

```python
import pypto.language as pl

# This IR is what ConvertToSSA produces (incorrectly) — valid_len in valid_shape
# is the ORIGINAL var, not the SSA-renamed valid_len__ssa_v0.
# The verifier should flag "valid_len" as undefined, but does not.

@pl.program
class BrokenIR:
    @pl.function
    def main(self, x__ssa_v0: pl.Tensor[[16, 64], pl.FP32],
             n__ssa_v0: pl.Tensor[[1], pl.INT32]) -> pl.Tensor[[8, 64], pl.FP32]:
        n_val__ssa_v0: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32] = pl.tensor.read(n__ssa_v0, [0])
        valid_len__ssa_v0: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX] = pl.min(64, pl.cast(n_val__ssa_v0, pl.INDEX))
        # valid_shape references "valid_len" (not in scope — only valid_len__ssa_v0 exists)
        chunk__ssa_v0: pl.Tensor[[8, 64], pl.FP32, pl.TensorView(
            valid_shape=[8, valid_len],  # ← undefined variable, should be caught
            stride=[], layout=pl.TensorLayout.ND
        )] = pl.tensor.slice(
            x__ssa_v0, [8, 64], [0, 0], [8, valid_len__ssa_v0]
        )
        return chunk__ssa_v0
```

### Expected Behavior

The verifier should report an error: `Variable 'valid_len' used before definition in function 'main'`.

### Actual Behavior

No error is reported. The verifier silently skips variable references inside type expressions.

### Git Commit ID

d765fc00beff9bed72dde85fd05565a2b1f48cb3

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Additional Context

**Root cause**: In `src/ir/verifier/verify_use_after_def.cpp`, lines 68-81:

```cpp
void VisitVarLike_(const VarPtr& op) override {
    if (!op) return;
    if (in_scope_.find(op.get()) == in_scope_.end()) {
        // ... report error ...
    }
    // Do not call IRVisitor::VisitVarLike_ — type shape expressions are not
    // data-flow uses and dynamic shape vars embedded in types are not defined
    // by any statement in the function body.
}
```

The comment's assumption is incorrect: `valid_shape` CAN reference locally-defined variables (scalars computed at runtime). After SSA renames the definition, the old reference becomes dangling.

**Fix direction**: The verifier could track which `Var*` pointers are known global dynamics (from function parameter types). For vars found in type annotations, skip checking only if they are known globals; flag vars in types that are NOT global dynamics AND NOT in scope.

**Related issues**: #853 (root cause — SSA doesn't substitute), #854 (printer masks the issue)

title: [Bug] TensorView type stub rejects DynVar in valid_shape parameter
body:
### Component

Python Bindings

### Description

The type stub for `TensorView.__init__` declares `valid_shape: Sequence[Expr | int]`, but `pl.dynamic()` returns `DynVar` — which is neither `Expr` nor `int`. Pyright flags `TensorView(valid_shape=[8, some_dynvar])` as a type error even though `valid_shape` can legitimately contain dynamic dimension variables.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import pypto.language as pl

M = pl.dynamic("M")  # returns DynVar

# Pyright error: Argument of type "list[int | DynVar]" cannot be assigned
# to parameter "valid_shape" of type "Sequence[Expr | int]"
view = pl.TensorView(valid_shape=[8, M], stride=[], layout=pl.TensorLayout.ND)
```

### Expected Behavior

No pyright error. The `TensorView` type stub should accept `DynVar` in `valid_shape`.

### Actual Behavior

Pyright reports a type mismatch because `DynVar` (from `python/pypto/language/typing/dynamic.py`) is a DSL-layer class that is NOT a subclass of `ir.Expr`.

### Git Commit ID

d765fc00beff9bed72dde85fd05565a2b1f48cb3

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Additional Context

The type stub in `python/pypto/pypto_core/ir.pyi` (lines 382-387):

```python
class TensorView:
    @overload
    def __init__(
        self,
        stride: Sequence[Expr | int],
        layout: TensorLayout,
        valid_shape: Sequence[Expr | int] = ...,  # Missing DynVar
    ) -> None: ...
```

**Fix options**:

- **Option A** — Widen the type stub: `valid_shape: Sequence[Expr | int | DynVar]`
- **Option B** — Make `DynVar` compatible with `Expr` through a protocol or base class

Option A is simpler and aligns with the DSL's `IntLike = int | Scalar | Expr` pattern (which may also need `DynVar`).

**Related issues**: #854 (printer emits `pl.dynamic()` for local vars, which then hits this type error in dumped IR)

title: [Bug] Cross-function calls should evaluate dynamic shape variables at call site
body:
### Component

Other (please specify in description)

### Description

When an Orchestration function calls an InCore function, the return type carries the InCore's dynamic shape variables (e.g., `M`, `N`) verbatim instead of evaluating/substituting them against the actual call arguments. The type inference should map dynamic shape vars to concrete values at the call site.

For example, if `add_kernel` has signature `(Tensor[[M, N], FP32], ...) -> Tensor[[M, N], FP32]` and is called from `orchestrator` with `Tensor[[128, 128], FP32]` arguments, the return type of the call should be `Tensor[[128, 128], FP32]`, not `Tensor[[M, N], FP32]`.

This causes `M` and `N` to appear as undefined variables in the caller's scope, which the `UseAfterDefChecker` verifier now correctly flags (see #855).

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import pypto.language as pl
from pypto import passes

M = pl.dynamic("M")
N = pl.dynamic("N")

@pl.program
class Example:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def add_kernel(
        self,
        a: pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32],
        b: pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32],
        c: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]],
    ) -> pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]:
        a_tile = pl.load(a, [0, 0], [128, 128], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        b_tile = pl.load(b, [0, 0], [128, 128])
        result = pl.add(a_tile, b_tile)
        out = pl.store(result, [0, 0], c)
        return out

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
    def orchestrator(
        self,
        a: pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.FP32],
        b: pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.FP32],
    ) -> pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.FP32]:
        c: pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.FP32] = pl.create_tensor([128, 128], dtype=pl.FP32)
        c_out = self.add_kernel(a, b, c)
        # c_out has type Tensor[[M, N], FP32] — should be Tensor[[128, 128], FP32]
        return c_out

passes.run_verifier()(Example)
```

### Expected Behavior

The call `self.add_kernel(a, b, c)` should:
1. Map `M=128, N=128` from the actual arguments
2. Validate that `a`, `b`, `c` shapes are consistent with each other
3. Return a value with type `Tensor[[128, 128], FP32]`

### Actual Behavior

The return value `c_out` retains type `Tensor[[M, N], FP32]`. `M` and `N` are undefined in the orchestrator scope.

91b898d645beace81ea62a8e13eaba692cd8a933

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

title: [Pass Bug] InitMemRef drops variable scope for dynamic valid_shape in TileType
body:
### Pass Name

InitMemRef

### Description

The `InitMemRef` pass introduces a new, undefined variable in `TileView.valid_shape` when processing IfStmt phi-node return variables.

**Before** `InitMemRef`, the phi return var `result__phi_v2` has `valid_shape=[1, valid_len__ssa_v0]` — the same variable that is defined in the body (`valid_len__ssa_v0 = ctx_len__ssa_v0 + 0`).

**After** `InitMemRef`, the phi return var has `valid_shape=[1, valid_len__ssa_v0_1]` — a new, cloned Var that is never defined by any statement. This causes a post-verification failure:

```
Post-verification failed after pass 'InitMemRef':
[1] ERROR - UseAfterDefCheck
  Message: Variable 'valid_len__ssa_v0' used before definition in function 'repro'
```

The pass likely clones or creates a fresh Var when updating types on IfStmt return vars, instead of reusing the existing in-scope variable.

### Git Commit ID

3250975a7062fbebd409cead47856491ead81247

### Before IR

IR before `InitMemRef` (after all preceding passes in the default pipeline):

```python
@pl.program
class Prog:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.AIV)
    def repro(
        self, flag__ssa_v0: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX],
        input__ssa_v0: pl.Tensor[[1, 120], pl.FP32],
        ctx_len__ssa_v0: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX],
        out__ssa_v0: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[1, 120], pl.FP32]]
    ) -> pl.Tensor[[1, 120], pl.FP32]:
        valid_len__ssa_v0: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX] = ctx_len__ssa_v0 + 0
        seed__ssa_v0: pl.Tile[[1, 120], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Vec,
            pl.TileView(valid_shape=[1, valid_len__ssa_v0])] = pl.tile.load(...)
        updated__ssa_v0: pl.Tile[[1, 120], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Vec,
            pl.TileView(valid_shape=[1, valid_len__ssa_v0])] = pl.tile.muls(seed__ssa_v0, 1.0)
        if flag__ssa_v0 == 0:
            result__ssa_v0 = seed__ssa_v0
            result__phi_v2: pl.Tile[...,
                pl.TileView(valid_shape=[1, valid_len__ssa_v0])] = pl.yield_(result__ssa_v0)
                                             # ^^^ uses valid_len__ssa_v0 — CORRECT
        else:
            result__ssa_v1 = updated__ssa_v0
            result__phi_v2: pl.Tile[...,
                pl.TileView(valid_shape=[1, valid_len__ssa_v0])] = pl.yield_(result__ssa_v1)
                                             # ^^^ uses valid_len__ssa_v0 — CORRECT
        ...
```

### Expected IR

After `InitMemRef`, the phi node return vars should still reference `valid_len__ssa_v0` (the defined variable) in their `valid_shape`:

```python
        if flag__ssa_v0 == 0:
            ...
            result__phi_v2: pl.Tile[..., mem_vec_2, pl.Mem.Vec,
                pl.TileView(valid_shape=[1, valid_len__ssa_v0])] = pl.yield_(result__ssa_v0)
                                             # ^^^ still valid_len__ssa_v0
```

### Actual IR or Error

After `InitMemRef`, the phi node return vars reference a **new, undefined** variable `valid_len__ssa_v0_1`:

```python
valid_len__ssa_v0_1 = pl.dynamic("valid_len__ssa_v0_1")  # ← never defined by any statement

        if flag__ssa_v0 == 0:
            ...
            result__phi_v2: pl.Tile[..., mem_vec_2, pl.Mem.Vec,
                pl.TileView(valid_shape=[1, valid_len__ssa_v0_1])] = pl.yield_(result__ssa_v0)
                                             # ^^^ valid_len__ssa_v0_1 — WRONG (undefined)
```

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Additional Context

Related: #855 (UseAfterDefChecker now correctly verifies variable references in type expressions, which exposed this bug)

**Reproduction** — run the full default pipeline on this program:

```python
import pypto.language as pl
from pypto import passes

@pl.program
class Prog:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def repro(
        self,
        flag: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX],
        input: pl.Tensor[[1, 120], pl.FP32],
        ctx_len: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX],
        out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[1, 120], pl.FP32]],
    ) -> pl.Tensor[[1, 120], pl.FP32]:
        valid_len: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX] = ctx_len + 0
        seed: pl.Tile[[1, 120], pl.FP32] = pl.tile.load(
            input, [0, 0], [1, 120], [1, valid_len],
            target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec, transpose=False,
        )
        updated: pl.Tile[[1, 120], pl.FP32] = pl.tile.muls(seed, 1.0)
        if flag == 0:
            result = seed
        else:
            result = updated
        final: pl.Tensor[[1, 120], pl.FP32] = pl.tile.store(result, [0, 0], out)
        return final

passes.compile(Prog)  # Fails at post-verification after InitMemRef
```
