title: fix(ir): Propagate Mat requirement backward through tensor.reshape
body:
## Summary

- `ConvertTensorToTileOps` only recorded **direct** consumer memory-space requirements, so the pattern `tensor.slice → tensor.reshape → tensor.matmul` lowered the slice into `tile.load(target_memory=Vec)`. Matmul's auto-bridge then inserted a redundant `Vec → Mat` move, which some backends (e.g. `a2a3`) reject outright.
- Added a `pass_through_arg` field to `ConversionEntry` and marked `tensor.reshape` as pass-through on arg 0. `ConsumerSpaceCollector` now records pass-through edges during its forward scan and walks them in reverse program order afterward, so non-`Vec` requirements flow from consumers back to producers.
- The slice now emits `tile.load(target_memory=Mat)` directly, and the reshape inherits `Mat` via `tile.reshape`'s existing `set_output_memory_inherit_input` semantics — no extra move.

## Root cause

See issue #1068. `ConsumerSpaceCollector` in `src/ir/transforms/convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp` only scanned direct op consumers. `tensor.reshape` was registered in the conversion registry with no `input_reqs`, so the `Mat` requirement declared by `tensor.matmul` on its lhs never reached the `tensor.slice` producing the reshape's input.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit test `TestSliceMatmulConversion::test_slice_reshape_then_matmul` verifies the canonical `slice → reshape → matmul` pattern lowers to a single `tile.load(Mat)` followed by `tile.reshape` inheriting `Mat`, with no intermediate move.

title: fix(cross-core): support no-split mixed kernels on A2A3
body:
## Summary

  This PR enables `no_split` mixed-kernel execution on A2A3 and adds corresponding parser/codegen/test coverage. Fixes hw-native-sys/pto-isa#83.

  ## Current no-split scheme

  On A2A3, `no_split` still cannot dispatch only a single AIV lane, because the AIC side needs to synchronize with both AIVs
  during cross-core pipe handshakes. If only one AIV participates, the pipeline can hang.

  The current implementation therefore keeps both homogeneous AIV kernels active:

  - both AIVs run the same compute path and the same push/pop synchronization path
  - one AIV keeps the normal store path
  - the other AIV suppresses store-related operations, so it does not produce duplicated visible writes

  In short: both AIVs participate in compute + sync, and one lane masks out its store side effects to make `no_split` cases
  run through correctly.

  This PR also makes omitted `split` default to `no_split`, while keeping explicit `no_split` coverage in
  `test_cross_core.py`.

  ## Future optimization

  The current scheme is functionally correct but not optimal, because the secondary AIV still performs real push/pop data
  movement.

  Once PTOAS fully supports `validShape` on push/pop, we can optimize this path by letting one AIV push/pop an object whose
  `validShape` is `0`. That would allow an "empty" push/pop to participate in synchronization without carrying real payload
  data.

  One thing still needs design attention there: special cases such as scalar payloads may need separate handling under the
  `validShape=0` approach.

title: feat(ir): Propagate scalar constants through the Simplify pass
body:
## Summary

- Extend `Simplify` to propagate scalar constant `AssignStmt`s (`ConstInt`/`ConstFloat`/`ConstBool`) into every downstream use: expressions, Call arguments, `Var`/`IterArg` type annotations, and loop `iter_args`/`return_vars`. Done via `Analyzer::Bind` plus a `Var` remap; `SimplifyType` walks `TensorType`/`TileType` shape/stride/valid_shape/start_offset. `Call.type_` is refreshed alongside args so roundtrip equality holds.
- Place `Simplify` after `ConvertToSSA` in the `Default` and `DebugTileOptimization` pipelines so single-assignment is guaranteed. A `MultiAssignCollector` pre-pass gates binding on `Var`s assigned exactly once, which keeps the pass safe even when run standalone on pre-SSA IR (the existing tests exercise this).
- Unblocks passes like `ConvertTensorToTileOps` that require static shape/step values: user-written constants inside `@pl.program` (e.g., `CHUNK_K = 512`, `BATCH_TILE = 1`) are now folded into `tile.full` shape args, `pl.range` steps, and `Tensor[[...]]` annotations.

On the qwen3 decode program, symbolic `BATCH_TILE`/`CHUNK_K` references drop from 83 to 2 post-`Simplify` (the 2 remaining are the now-dead original declarations, reserved for a future DCE pass).

title: fix(ir): Compare symbolic shape dims via arithmetic simplifier
body:
## Summary

- Route symbolic shape dimensions through the arithmetic analyzer so semantically equal expressions (e.g. `(x + C) - x` vs `C`, `x * s + s - x * s` vs `s`) compare equal during shape checks and variable reassignment.
- Fixes spurious \"shape mismatch\" from `BroadcastShapes` and \"Cannot reassign with a different type\" from the parser on common subscript patterns like `a[:, k : k + CHUNK]` used inside a loop.

## Details

Three touch points, all gated so the fast pointer / ConstInt paths stay unchanged:

- **`DimensionsEqual` (src/ir/op/type_inference.cpp)** — falls back to `arith::Analyzer::CanProveEqual` when pointer-equality and literal-ConstInt comparison miss. Fixes the `tensor.sub` error reported as `requires compatible shapes, but got [1, kv_col + 64 - kv_col] and [1, kv_col + 128 - (kv_col + 64)]`.
- **`_types_match` (parser)** — runs outer shape dims through a shared `arith.Analyzer().simplify(...)` before the structural `==` check. Scoped to outer `shape`; TileView / TensorView sub-fields (`valid_shape`, `stride`, `start_offset`, ...) are unchanged.
- **`_build_slice_shape_expr` (parser)** — simplifies `upper - lower` at slice-op construction and demotes to an `int` when the result is a constant. Downstream checks see literal extents for the common `x[:, k : k + C]` and `x[:, i * s : (i + 1) * s]` forms.

Performance: `DimensionsEqual` allocates one `Analyzer` per symbolic call (only hit on the slow path); `_types_match` now constructs a single shared `Analyzer` and also short-circuits when every shape dim is already a `ConstInt`.

## Testing

- [x] `pytest tests/ut/language tests/ut/ir/operators tests/ut/ir/arith` — 1503 passed
- [x] Full suite via `testing` skill — 3721/3721 passed
- [x] Clang-tidy clean on changed C++

title: feat(jit): implement @pl.jit preprocessor and JIT compilation pipeline
body:
## Summary

Implements the `@pl.jit` decorator as specified in issue #878 / #915.

- **`python/pypto/jit/decorator.py`** — `JITFunction` class with `@pl.jit` and `@pl.jit.incore` decorators. Supports Style A (inline `pl.at(level=CORE_GROUP)` scope) and Style B (explicit multi-function cross-call). `__call__` specializes, runs the full pass pipeline, and caches the resulting `ir.Program` in an L1 in-memory cache keyed by `(source_hash, shapes, dtypes, scalar_values)`. Dynamic dims (via `bind_dynamic`) are stored as `None` in the key so different concrete values share the same cache entry.
- **`python/pypto/jit/specializer.py`** — AST transformer that converts `@pl.jit` source into type-annotated `@pl.program` DSL source. Inlines static shape dims as `ConstInt`, preserves dynamic dims as `Var`, rewrites `a.shape[i]` references, removes `bind_dynamic` calls, and promotes `pl.dynamic("M")` declarations to module level.
- **`python/pypto/jit/cache.py`** — Cache key construction with PyPTO version stamp for automatic invalidation on upgrades.
- **`python/pypto/language/typing/tensor.py`** — Adds `bind_dynamic(dim, dynvar)` method to `Tensor`.
- **`python/pypto/language/__init__.py`** — Exports `jit`, restores `PtrType`/`Ptr` aliases.

Bug fixes during rebase:
- Propagate dynamic dims from `@pl.jit.incore` deps back to entry function so params use `Var(M)` not `ConstInt(64)`.

title: [Pass Bug] ExpandMixedKernel splits pure-AIC kernel because `tile.create` is misclassified as VECTOR
body:
### Pass Name

ExpandMixedKernel (root cause in `ClassifyCallAffinity` at `src/ir/transforms/utils/core_affinity.cpp`)

### Description

A scope containing `pl.create_tensor` (lowered to `tile.create`) together with `pl.matmul` / `pl.matmul_acc` is incorrectly classified as a **mixed** kernel and sent through `ExpandMixedKernel`'s AIC/AIV split path, even though every real compute op in the scope runs on the cube unit. The split produces broken IR — the AIV half references a tile defined only in the AIC half — and codegen later aborts with:

```
Internal error: no MLIR mapping for MemRef base 'mem_vec_3'
Check failed: it != fs_.memref_to_mlir.end() at src/codegen/pto/pto_codegen.cpp:790
```

**Root cause.** `ClassifyCallAffinity` at `src/ir/transforms/utils/core_affinity.cpp:82-134` handles cube ops, `tile.move`, `tile.load`, tile-arg-classified ops, and cross-core ops explicitly; everything else under `tile.*` falls through to the catch-all at line 132:

```cpp
if (name.substr(0, 5) == "tile.") return CoreAffinity::VECTOR;
```

`tile.create` is a pure declaration (no compute, no data motion, no execution side) and hits this catch-all, returning VECTOR. Combined with CUBE from `tile.matmul` / `tile.matmul_acc` in the same scope, `CombineAffinity(VECTOR, CUBE)` returns `MIXED` (`core_affinity.cpp:33`). `ExpandMixedKernel` then enters the mixed path at `expand_mixed_kernel_pass.cpp:1409`:

```cpp
bool is_mixed = (combined == CoreAffinity::MIXED || combined == CoreAffinity::BOUNDARY);
if (!is_mixed) { /* relabel to AIC or AIV, done */ }
// mixed path: warn about SplitMode::None, then split anyway — produces broken IR
```

The split warns `Mixed kernel '...' use none split mode not supported by isa now` (`expand_mixed_kernel_pass.cpp:1428-1432`) but continues and emits an AIV half consisting of just `pl.tile.store(down_acc__rv_v2, ...)` where `down_acc__rv_v2` is defined only in the AIC half. Codegen of that dangling reference is what explodes at `pto_codegen.cpp:790`.

**Fix.** Add `tile.create` to the `shared_tile_ops` set at `core_affinity.cpp:127-130`:

```cpp
static const std::unordered_set<std::string> shared_tile_ops = {
    \"tile.get_block_idx\",
    \"tile.get_block_num\",
    \"tile.create\",   // pure declaration; inherits affinity from consumers
};
```

`tile.full` should stay VECTOR — it writes a constant and is a real vector op. `tile.create` alone is the phantom/declaration case.

### Git Commit ID

50fb980845990e7e255fe0dc2a51ec27c21bc1eb

### Before IR (Input)

```python
import pypto.language as pl

M, N, K = 16, 128, 256
KC = 64

@pl.program
class Repro:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Opaque)
    def down_matmul(
        self,
        a: pl.Tensor[[M, K], pl.BF16],
        b: pl.Tensor[[K, N], pl.BF16],
        out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]],
    ) -> pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]:
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP):
            acc = pl.create_tensor([M, N], dtype=pl.FP32)  # declaration only
            for k in pl.range(0, K, KC):
                a_tile = pl.slice(a, [M, KC], [0, k])
                b_tile = pl.slice(b, [KC, N], [k, 0])
                if k == 0:
                    acc = pl.matmul(a_tile, b_tile, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
                else:
                    acc = pl.matmul_acc(acc, a_tile, b_tile)
            out = pl.assemble(out, acc, [0, 0])
        return out
```

Every real op in the `CORE_GROUP` scope — `tile.matmul`, `tile.matmul_acc`, plus `tile.slice`/`tile.store` on Acc tiles — is cube-side. `tile.create` is just a declaration of `acc`.

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

`ExpandMixedKernel` should relabel the InCore function to `FunctionType.AIC` with no split (the `!is_mixed` branch at `expand_mixed_kernel_pass.cpp:1411-1425`):

```python
@pl.program
class Expected:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.AIC)
    def down_matmul_incore_0(
        self,
        a: pl.Tensor[[16, 256], pl.BF16],
        b: pl.Tensor[[256, 128], pl.BF16],
        ret0: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 128], pl.FP32]],
    ) -> pl.Tensor[[16, 128], pl.FP32]:
        # Single AIC kernel. acc lives in Acc memory throughout; no
        # AIC->AIV boundary, no tpush/tpop, no split.
        acc = pl.tile.create([16, 128], dtype=pl.FP32, target_memory=pl.Mem.Acc)
        for k, (acc_iter,) in pl.range(0, 256, 64, init_values=(acc,)):
            ...  # matmul / matmul_acc chain producing an Acc tile
            acc_rv = pl.yield_(...)
        ret0_store = pl.tile.store(acc_rv, [0, 0], ret0)
        return ret0_store
```

### Actual IR or Error

After `ExpandMixedKernel` the function is split into `..._aic` and `..._aiv`. The AIV half references `down_acc__rv_v2` with no corresponding definition:

```
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.AIV)
def qwen3_decode_incore_16_aiv(
    self, mlp_tile__rv_v2, w_down__ssa_v0, n__idx_v0, ret0__out,
) -> pl.Tensor[[16, 384], pl.FP32]:
    mem_vec_3: pl.Ptr = pl.tile.alloc(pl.Mem.Vec, 24576)
    ret0__store = pl.tile.store(down_acc__rv_v2, [0, 0], ret0__out)  # undefined!
    return ret0__store
```

Stderr at compile time:

```
E | Mixed kernel 'qwen3_decode_incore_16' use none split mode not supported
    by isa now; consider using split=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN on its auto_incore scope
Failed to compile group 'qwen3_decode_incore_16' [qwen3_decode_incore_16_aic,
qwen3_decode_incore_16_aiv]: Internal error: no MLIR mapping for MemRef base 'mem_vec_3'
Check failed: it != fs_.memref_to_mlir.end() at src/codegen/pto/pto_codegen.cpp:790
```

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Additional Context

**User-visible symptom.** Hit in a full Qwen3 decode pipeline when writing the down-projection loop with the idiom `if k == 0: matmul else: matmul_acc` inside a `pl.range`. The conventional workaround is to peel the first iteration and use `pl.matmul_acc` in the loop body (which is how the other matmul loops in the same program are written).

**Secondary issue to consider once the classifier is fixed.** `InferTileMemorySpace` currently places the `pl.create_tensor` result in `Mem.Vec` because no explicit memory kwarg is given, which in turn makes the if/else phi a Vec tile even though both branches produce Acc tiles. Once the classifier fix lands, the scope will be pure AIC but the accumulator memory-space inference may still need adjusting so the accumulator lives in L0C (Acc) consistent with the matmul output. Worth covering in a follow-up test.

**Proposed test.** `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_expand_mixed_kernel_pass.py` — before/after with the pattern above, asserting the resulting function has `FunctionType.AIC` and no `_aic`/`_aiv` split functions are generated.

title: feat(ir): Add conservative scalar DCE to Simplify pass
body:
## Summary

- Adds a conservative scalar DCE step at the end of the Simplify pass so constant-propagated scalar bindings (`N: Scalar = 4`) don't linger after all their uses are folded out.
- Predicate is deliberately narrow — only `AssignStmt`s with a scalar LHS and a **non-`Call`** RHS are eligible for removal; Call-backed assignments are always preserved because the IR has no purity annotation yet and the call may have observable side effects.
- Factors the existing `EliminateDeadCode` into a predicate-parameterized `EliminateDeadCodeCore` so both the default full DCE and the new scalar-only variant share liveness analysis, fixed-point propagation, and filtering.
- Caches each assignment's RHS uses once before the fixed-point loop so long dependency chains don't re-walk expressions per iteration.
- Incidentally fixes the default `EliminateDeadCode` path to treat `ForStmt.chunk_config_.size` as a live-root expression.

## Test plan

- [x] New `TestScalarDCE` class in `test_simplify_pass.py` covers unused-scalar removal, cascading chains, Call-RHS preservation, and in-use preservation.
- [x] Existing simplify tests rewritten to route scalars through an observable sink (`pl.tensor.write` / `ReturnStmt`) so the fold result stays visible after DCE.
- [x] `test_simplify_pass.py` — 38 passed.
- [x] DCE callers (`test_expand_mixed_kernel_*`, `test_split_vector_kernel`) — 72 passed.
- [x] Full IR suite — 2693 passed, 13 skipped.
- [x] Full unit suite — 3725 passed, 16 skipped.
- [x] `clang-tidy --diff-base HEAD` — clean.

## Docs

- `docs/en/dev/passes/00-pass_manager.md` and `docs/zh-cn/dev/passes/00-pass_manager.md` — added a paragraph under the Simplify pass describing the new conservative scalar DCE step.

title: refactor(ir): Replace pl.range(unroll=F) with pl.pipeline(N, stage=F)
body:
## Summary

Introduces `pl.pipeline(*range_args, stage=F)` as a standalone loop iterator alongside `pl.range` / `pl.parallel` / `pl.unroll`, replacing the previous `pl.range(N, unroll=F)` kwarg. The new surface is driven by a `ForKind::Pipeline` enum value; the pipeline depth rides on `attrs_[\"pipeline_stages\"] = F`.

### User-visible change

```python
# Before
for i in pl.range(64, unroll=4):
    tile = pl.tile.load(a, [i * 128], [128])
    pl.tile.store(tile, [i * 128], out)

# After
for i in pl.pipeline(64, stage=4):
    tile = pl.tile.load(a, [i * 128], [128])
    pl.tile.store(tile, [i * 128], out)
```

`pl.range(..., unroll=F)` is removed (hard break, not deprecated).

### Lowering + IO-order changes

- **`LowerPipelineLoops`** (renamed from `PartialUnrollTileLoops`): trigger switched from `attrs[\"unroll_factor\"]` to `kind == Pipeline && HasAttr(\"pipeline_stages\")`. The lowered outer loop **keeps `kind=Pipeline`** as a marker for the downstream reorder and strips `pipeline_stages` so the pass is idempotent on its own output.
- **`CanonicalizeIOOrder`**: scoped to bodies of `ForKind::Pipeline` loops via a depth counter — sibling plain `pl.range` loops in the same function are no longer reordered. On exit, demotes the outer kind to `Sequential` and strips any stale `pipeline_stages` attr so the `(attr ⇒ kind)` invariant holds.
- Pass order is unchanged (`LowerPipelineLoops → CanonicalizeIOOrder`), so the reorder still sees the post-replication load/store cluster.

### Invariant enforcement

New `IRProperty::PipelineResolved` (produced by `CanonicalizeIOOrder`) with a verifier that checks:
1. No `ForKind::Pipeline` survives past `CanonicalizeIOOrder` (transient marker).
2. `pipeline_stages` attr may only coexist with `kind == Pipeline`.

### Printer

`kind == Pipeline` + attr present prints as `pl.pipeline(..., stage=F)`; `stage=` is surfaced as a kwarg and never leaks in the printed `attrs={...}` dict — the kind drives the textual form, not the storage mechanism.

### Shared utilities

`include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/attrs.h` — `kPipelineStagesAttr` constant + `StripAttr(attrs, key)` free function, consumed by the lowering pass, canonicalize, printer, and verifier to keep the attr key typed at a single site.

## Test plan

- [x] **Migrated tests** — `test_range_unroll_kwarg.py` → `test_pipeline_kwarg.py` (12 cases: parse, round-trip, error paths, removal check for old `unroll=`); `test_partial_unroll_tile_loops.py` → `test_lower_pipeline_loops.py` (9 cases, all existing scenarios — static/dynamic bounds, iter_args, step≠1, nested — with flipped fixtures + idempotency assertion).
- [x] **New tests** — `test_canonicalize_io_order.py` gains `test_function_body_outside_pipeline_is_not_reordered` (verifies plain `pl.range` loops and function-level SeqStmts are untouched). `test_lower_pipeline_loops.py` adds `stage=1` demotion coverage.
- [x] **Full unit suite** — 3725 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped (`python -m pytest tests/ut -n auto --maxprocesses 8`).
- [x] **Round-trip** — `pl.pipeline(N, stage=F)` parses to `ForStmt(kind=Pipeline, attrs={\"pipeline_stages\": F})`, prints as `pl.pipeline(N, stage=F)`, reparses to an identical IR (structural_equal).
- [x] **Invariant** — `IRProperty::PipelineResolved` reports pre-lowering Pipeline kind + catches orphan `pipeline_stages` attr on non-Pipeline kinds.

## Breaking changes

- `pl.range(..., unroll=F)` removed — use `pl.pipeline(N, stage=F)`.
- `passes.partial_unroll_tile_loops()` → `passes.lower_pipeline_loops()`.
- `attrs[\"unroll_factor\"]` → `attrs[\"pipeline_stages\"]` (on `ForKind::Pipeline` loops).

title: codegen: local Out -> InOut promotion serializes independent q_proj tile writes
body:
## Summary

A recent codegen change promotes locally allocated `Out` tensors to `InOut` at the orchestration call site so the runtime can establish WAW dependencies for tasks that share the same buffer. This is correct for overlapping writes, but it currently over-serializes independent tiled writes into disjoint slices of the same locally allocated tensor.

This showed up in Qwen3-32B decode: the full decode path serializes the `q_proj` projection tasks, while the standalone scope1 example keeps them parallel.

## Reproducer

Compare these two examples:

```bash
python modules/pypto-lib/examples/models/qwen3/qwen3_32b_decode.py -p a2a3 -d 1 --runtime-profiling
python modules/pypto-lib/examples/models/qwen3/qwen3_32b_decode_scope1.py -p a2a3 -d 1 --runtime-profiling
```

Relevant source shape:

- Full decode allocates `q_proj` locally:
  `modules/pypto-lib/examples/models/qwen3/qwen3_32b_decode.py`

  ```python
  q_proj = pl.create_tensor([batch, hidden], dtype=pl.FP32)
  ...
  for ob in pl.parallel(q_out_blocks, chunk=4):
      ...
      q_proj = pl.assemble(q_proj, q_acc, [b0, q0])
  ```

- Standalone scope1 receives `q_proj` as an external output parameter:
  `modules/pypto-lib/examples/models/qwen3/qwen3_32b_decode_scope1.py`

  ```python
  q_proj: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[batch, hidden], pl.FP32]]
  ...
  for ob in pl.parallel(q_out_blocks, chunk=4):
      ...
      q_proj = pl.assemble(q_proj, q_acc, [b0, q0])
  ```

## Observed codegen difference

Full decode generated orchestration:

```cpp
// Task 1: qwen3_decode_incore_1
Arg params_t1;
params_t1.add_inout(q_proj);
params_t1.add_input(normed_tile__rv_v2);
params_t1.add_input(ext_wq);
```

Standalone scope1 generated orchestration:

```cpp
// Task 1: qwen3_scope1_incore_1
Arg params_t1;
params_t1.add_output(ext_q_proj);
params_t1.add_input(normed_tile__rv_v2);
params_t1.add_input(ext_wq);
```

The `add_inout(q_proj)` path makes every q_proj tile write perform TensorMap lookup/insert on the same large buffer, producing conservative WAW dependencies even though each `ob` writes a disjoint `[b0, q0]` tile. The `add_output(ext_q_proj)` path does not create those edges, so the 32 q projection tasks can run in parallel.

## Likely root cause

Introduced by commit `35fdb7bcf9136293ea29381289a17b909897e54f` (`fix(codegen): use add_inout for locally allocated Out tensors (#1046)`).

That commit added `CallSiteDirectionResolver`, which promotes locally allocated `Out` arguments to `InOut`:

- `include/pypto/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_analysis.h`
- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_analysis.cpp`
- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`

The commit message says the goal was to establish WAW dependencies between tasks sharing the same local buffer. The current behavior is too coarse for partitioned writes where the write regions are provably disjoint.

## Profiling signal

For standalone scope1 on A2A3, q projection stayed parallel:

- `func_1_b` count: 32
- total test time: ~333.86 us
- fanout/fanin edges: 0

For full decode, generated code uses `add_inout(q_proj)`, and profiling shows q_proj tasks serialized in the front of the run.

## Expected behavior

Independent tile writes to disjoint slices of a locally allocated tensor should not be serialized just because the root buffer is the same.

Possible directions:

- preserve `OUTPUT_EXISTING` / `add_output(const Tensor&)` when compile-time slice regions are disjoint inside a `pl.parallel` loop;
- emit dependency information at slice/view granularity instead of whole-root-buffer granularity;
- add a codegen/runtime tag for write-only existing tensor with precise region metadata;
- make the local Out -> InOut promotion conditional on possible overlap rather than unconditional.

## Impact

This causes a real performance regression in Qwen3 decode scope1 inside the full decode pipeline: q projection tile tasks that should be parallel become serialized by conservative TensorMap WAW dependency tracking.

title: refactor(backend): centralize per-backend behaviour via BackendHandler
body:
Introduce a BackendHandler virtual interface that names every behavioural
difference between backends (PTO target arch, runtime API names, hazard
workarounds, cross-core layout rules, etc.). Each Backend subclass owns a
singleton handler; passes and codegen consume it via
PassContext::GetBackendHandler() (delegating to BackendConfig) instead of
branching on BackendType.

Replace nine BackendType conditionals across:
  * legalize_pto_buffer_reuse_pass.cpp  (split-load tpop workaround)
  * expand_mixed_kernel_pass.cpp        (cross-core view, V-to-C fractal
                                         adapt, GM pipe buffer injection)
  * pto_codegen.cpp                     (target_arch attribute)
  * orchestration_codegen.cpp           (launch_spec core-count method)
  * pto_backend.py / runner.py          (ptoas flags, runtime subblock,
                                         platform arch)
  * compiled_program.py / compile.py    (default sim platform, codegen
                                         gate)

Also extract BackendTypeToString to clean up backend_config.cpp diagnostics
and expose BackendHandler / Backend.get_handler / get_backend_instance via
nanobind plus type stubs.

Adding a new backend is now a self-contained change: subclass Backend,
subclass BackendHandler, override Backend::GetHandler(), append the enum
value to the GetBackendInstance / BackendTypeToString factory. No pass or
codegen file needs to change.

Refs: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/948

title: ci(daily): auto-open issue on failure and run all qwen3 cases
body:
## Summary

Two improvements to `.github/workflows/daily_ci.yml`:

1. **Auto-open issue on failure.** Add a `notify-on-failure` job that runs only on scheduled runs (`schedule` event) and either creates a new issue or appends a comment to the existing open issue labeled `daily-ci-failure` whenever `qwen3-decode` or `a5-system-tests` fails. The issue body includes the workflow run URL, commit, ref and the list of failed jobs, so on-call developers can pick up regressions quickly without spam.
   - Job runs on `ubuntu-latest` with `permissions: issues: write`, scoped to the job only.
   - Manual `workflow_dispatch` runs intentionally do **not** open issues, to avoid noise during debugging.
   - Deduplication is by label + title; existing open issues get a new comment instead of a fresh issue.

2. **Run every qwen3 decode case.** The `Run qwen3 decode examples` step previously stopped at the first failing case (because `set -e` aborts the loop). It now collects failures into an array, emits `::error file=...` annotations, and exits non-zero only after every case has been attempted. This ensures one broken case no longer hides regressions in the others, and the failure list is visible at a glance in the run summary.

## Notes

- The label `daily-ci-failure` does not yet exist in the repository. The first failing run will auto-create it (default color); feel free to pre-create it in repo settings with a chosen color/description.
- No source/runtime code is touched, so no unit/system tests are affected.

## Testing

- [x] `python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/daily_ci.yml'))"` — YAML validates.
- [ ] Trigger Daily CI manually via `workflow_dispatch` once after merge to confirm the new job is wired correctly (it should be skipped because event != `schedule`).
- [ ] Next scheduled failure should auto-open or comment on the tracking issue.

title: fix(ir): Classify tile.create as SHARED and promote accumulator memory
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1083. A CORE_GROUP scope holding a `tile.create` accumulator that feeds `matmul_acc` was being mis-classified as MIXED, which routed it through ExpandMixedKernel's split path and produced broken AIC/AIV IR that crashed codegen with `no MLIR mapping for MemRef base`.

This PR fixes the issue end-to-end across the classifier and the `InferTileMemorySpace` pass.

### 1. Classifier fix (`src/ir/transforms/utils/core_affinity.cpp`)

`tile.create` is a declaration-only op (no compute, no data motion), but `ClassifyCallAffinity`'s catch-all was routing it to `VECTOR`. A CORE_GROUP scope with a `tile.create` accumulator + a `matmul_acc` body therefore combined to `MIXED` and entered the split path. Classify `tile.create` as `SHARED` so it no longer forces scope affinity.

### 2. Back-propagate yielded memory space onto accumulator chain (`infer_tile_memory_space_pass.cpp`)

Extend the `ForStmt` visitor to propagate the body's yielded memory space back onto the `iter_arg` and its init value. Fall back to reading `memory_space_` from the yield var's `TileType` so that `IfStmt` return_vars, which this analyzer does not otherwise track, are still picked up.

### 3. Three follow-ups surfaced while running the user's repro end-to-end

- **Scope `created_moves_` per `SeqStmts` visit.** The cache was an instance member shared across sibling blocks. When Phase 3 emitted a `tile.move` inside an `if` branch and then processed the `else` branch of the same `IfStmt`, the consumer lookup hit the cached key and skipped the move — leaving the `else` branch with a dangling SSA reference to a `Var` defined only in the `then` branch.
- **Rewrite `tile.create` when the LHS `Var` is promoted.** After Phase 1 back-propagates `Acc` memory onto the `tile.create` init `Var`, the init `Call` still carried `target_memory=Vec` in its kwargs and a `Vec`-style result type. Rebuild the `Call` with the promoted kwarg and a `TileType` whose `TileView` matches the implicit view for the new memory space.
- **Refresh the `TileView` of any promoted `Var`, not only the `tile.create` output.** `IterArg` and `ForStmt` return_var types were carrying the old `Vec`-style view forward into memory spaces where those values are nonsense (`Acc` expects `col_major`/`row_major`/`fractal=1024`, not the `Vec` defaults). Later `tmov` lowering then produced invalid ops.

## Test plan

- [x] Build in worktree with nanobind cmake path
- [x] New end-to-end case: `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_expand_mixed_kernel_a2a3.py::test_accumulator_with_tile_create_classifies_as_pure_aic` passes
- [x] Full transforms suite: `python -m pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/ -n auto` — 1066 passed, 12 skipped, no regressions

Fixes #1083

title: fix(ir): Remap type annotations in DeepClone
body:
## Summary

`DeepClone` was reusing the source `Var`'s `TypePtr` verbatim when creating the fresh clone. Types may embed expressions (shape dims, `TileView` `valid_shape`/`stride`/`start_offset`, `MemRef.byte_offset`) that reference scope `Var`s, so after a scope-substituting clone (e.g. `UnrollLoops` replacing `loop_var` with `ConstInt`, or a future `PartialUnrollTileLoops` substituting a loop var), the cloned `Var` carried a type still pointing at out-of-scope source `Var`s. The printer rendered those dangling references as `pl.dynamic(...)` forward declarations inside the transformed body.

The fix walks the embedded expressions through the mutator's `expr_map_` and rebuilds the type via `CloneTypeWithMemRefAndRemapExprs`, so the fresh `Var`/`IterArg` carries a type consistent with the cloned scope.

- `src/ir/transforms/utils/deep_clone_utils.cpp` — new private `RemapType` helper; `CloneVar` and `VisitExpr_(IterArgPtr)` use it instead of reusing `op->GetType()` verbatim.
- `python/bindings/modules/ir.cpp` + `.pyi` — `ir.deep_clone` now accepts an optional `var_map` seed (matching the C++ API), so tests can directly exercise the type-remapping path.
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_deep_clone.py` — regression test verifying that a `TileType.tile_view.valid_shape` expression referencing a scope var is remapped to the substituted var after cloning.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_deep_clone.py -v` (all 7 pass; the new tests fail without the fix and pass with it)
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/ut/ir/ -n auto` (2706 passed, 13 skipped — no regressions)

title: refactor(ir): Use structural_equal in MemoryReuse tile compatibility
[Feature] Relax MemoryReuse tile compatibility to fuse across different valid_shape
[New Op] Add TCI (tile.ci / tensor.ci) — contiguous integer sequence generation
body:
### Operation Level

Other (please specify): **both tile-level and tensor-level**. The op must be registered at both layers (`tile.ci` and `tensor.ci`) with a tensor-to-tile conversion, mirroring how other tensor ops lower to their tile counterparts.

### Proposed Name & Signature

IR-level C++ ops: `tile.ci` and `tensor.ci`.

Python IR / DSL wrappers — propose `ci(...)` (matching ISA) with an `arange(...)` convenience alias:

```python
# IR layer — python/pypto/ir/op/tile_ops.py, python/pypto/ir/op/tensor_ops.py
def ci(
    start: int | Expr,
    *,
    shape: Sequence[int | Expr] | None = None,      # required for tensor.ci; tile.ci may receive it via result_type
    dtype: DataType = DataType.INT32,
    descending: bool = False,
    span: Span | None = None,
) -> Call: ...

# DSL layer — python/pypto/language/op/tile_ops.py, python/pypto/language/op/tensor_ops.py
def ci(start: int | Scalar, shape: Sequence[IntLike], dtype: DataType = pl.INT32,
       descending: bool = False) -> Tile: ...         # tile.*
def ci(start: int | Scalar, shape: Sequence[IntLike], dtype: DataType = pl.INT32,
       descending: bool = False) -> Tensor: ...       # tensor.*

# Convenience alias
arange = ci   # so users can write pl.arange(0, shape=[4, 32])
```

### Semantics Description

`TCI` generates a contiguous integer sequence into a destination tile/tensor. For a linearized index `k` over the valid elements:

- Ascending: `dst[k] = start + k`
- Descending: `dst[k] = start - k`

The linearization order depends on tile layout (implementation-defined).

Reference: `pto-isa/docs/isa/TCI.md` and figure `pto-isa/docs/figures/isa/TCI.svg`.

**Inputs**

- `start`: scalar, same dtype as destination
- `shape`: output shape
- `dtype`: destination dtype
- `descending`: bool kwarg (default `false`)

**Output**

- Tile or tensor with shape `shape` and dtype `dtype`, populated per the formula above.

**Constraints (per ISA)**

- `dtype` must be one of `INT32`, `UINT32`, `INT16`, `UINT16`.
- Destination `Cols != 1` (column vectors not supported).
- Hardware uses `dst.GetValidCol()` as sequence length; does not consult `GetValidRow()`.
- Scalar `start` dtype must match destination dtype.

### Example Usage

```python
import pypto.language as pl

@pl.program
class Example:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def main_incore_0(self, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[4, 32], pl.INT32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[4, 32], pl.INT32]:
        # Generate [0, 1, 2, ..., 31] per row (linearization order is layout-defined)
        idx: pl.Tensor[[4, 32], pl.INT32] = pl.tensor.ci(0, shape=[4, 32], dtype=pl.INT32)
        # Or equivalently via the arange alias
        idx2: pl.Tensor[[4, 32], pl.INT32] = pl.arange(0, shape=[4, 32], dtype=pl.INT32)
        return idx
```

A typical use is preparing the `idx` operand for `tile.sort32` / `tensor.sort32`, where the user currently has to materialize the 0..N-1 sequence manually.

### Hardware Support Considerations

- Maps directly to the existing PTO-AS instruction `pto.tci`. The backend codegen is already partially wired: `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp:456` (`MakeCiCodegenPTO`) and the registration at `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp:1566` target `tile.ci`, but the IR-level op is not registered (`ir.is_op_registered(\"tile.ci\") == False`). This issue is to add the missing IR/DSL/conversion layers so that codegen actually fires.
- No CPU fallback needed for this hardware-specific sequence generator.
- Runs in `MemorySpace::Vec` on Ascend 910B / A2A3 (aligned with other tile compute ops).

### Motivation / Use Case

1. **`sort32` usability.** `tile.sort32` / `tensor.sort32` require an `idx` tile/tensor initialized to a sequence (`[0, 1, ..., 31]` for FP16 src, `[0, 2, ..., 62]` for FP32 src). Without `arange`/`ci`, users must fabricate the sequence via orchestration, which is awkward and precludes a fully on-device kernel. See `tests/st/runtime/test_sort.py`, which currently constructs `idx` externally.
2. **Index generation for masking / gather.** Many kernels need a row/column index tile — `tensor.gather`, position-encoded ops, softmax length masks, etc. `arange` is a standard primitive in numpy/torch/triton/JAX; its absence forces users to fake it with external tensor inputs.
3. **Backend already supports it.** Codegen for `tile.ci → pto.tci` exists; the front-end and IR gap is the only thing blocking usage. Closing the loop is low-risk and unlocks immediate value.

### Additional Context

- ISA reference: `pto-isa/docs/isa/TCI.md` (ascending/descending contiguous integer sequence, `descending` attribute).
- Existing backend codegen: `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp:456` and `:1566`.
- Related tests that would benefit: `tests/st/runtime/test_sort.py` (`test_sort32_fp32`, `test_sort32_gather_fp32`).
- Framework analogues: `numpy.arange`, `torch.arange`, `tl.arange` (Triton), `jax.numpy.arange`.

**Suggested implementation scope (Phase A + Phase B of the `add-op` skill):**

- C++ `REGISTER_OP(\"tile.ci\")` with 1 arg (start scalar), `descending` bool attr, `Vec` output memory, dtype restricted to {INT16, UINT16, INT32, UINT32}.
- C++ `REGISTER_OP(\"tensor.ci\")` similarly (no memory spaces).
- Python IR wrappers in `python/pypto/ir/op/{tile,tensor}_ops.py`.
- Python DSL wrappers + `arange` alias in `python/pypto/language/op/{tile,tensor}_ops.py`.
- `RegisterSimple(\"tensor.ci\", \"tile.ci\")` in `src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp`.
- Unit tests + conversion tests.
- Docs update in `docs/en/dev/ir/05-operators.md` + `docs/zh-cn/...`.

title: feat(ir): Top-down retargeter for MemoryReuse accumulator chains
body:
## Summary

- Add a Step-0 **top-down retargeter** to `MemoryReuse` that rewrites each `ForStmt`'s yield-chain producer to land directly in the iter_arg's MemRef (eliminates `tile.move` insertions for accumulator chains).
- Tighten the **InitMemRef** invariant so `return_vars` share the *iter_arg*'s MemRef (not the yield value's), giving the retargeter a consistent `(initValue, iter_arg, return_var)` target.
- Update 8 existing tests whose expectations described the old `tile.move`-insertion pattern; add 2 new tests for the retargeter's positive (Acc `matmul_acc` chain) and negative (target-still-live) paths.

## Motivation

For `Acc` → `Acc` accumulator chains (`matmul → matmul_acc → matmul_acc …`) the old lifetime-coloring step reconciled a yield/iter_arg MemRef mismatch by inserting a `tile.move` at the yield. An `Acc → Acc` `tile.move` lowers to a `pto.tmov` on `Acc` memory that the codegen backend rejects, so otherwise-legal accumulator loops failed to compile end-to-end (follow-up to the work in #1083).

## Algorithm

On entry to `MemoryReuse`, a new Step-0 walks each `ForStmt` top-down. For every `iter_arg → yield-value` pair it takes the iter_arg's MemRef as the canonical "target" and tries to retype the yield producer directly onto that MemRef.

- **Unconstrained producers** (plain `add`, `move`, `matmul`, …): retyped to write directly into the target MemRef, provided the target's base `Ptr` is not read between the producer and the yield in the same branch body (liveness check).
- **Pinned producers** (ops with `set_output_reuses_input`, e.g. `matmul_acc`): the output MemRef cannot be changed, so the retargeter recurses onto the pinned input (typically the iter_arg itself) and only plans the LHS retype once the upstream placement is feasible.
- **IfStmt return_vars**: recurse into both branches' yield values with the same target; retype the return_var when both branches succeed.

When the retargeter succeeds, the producer lands directly in the loop-carry buffer and the downstream `YieldFixup` pass has nothing to reconcile, so no `tile.move` ops are emitted. When it declines (e.g. target still live after the producer), `YieldFixup` handles the mismatch exactly as before.

### InitMemRef invariant the retargeter depends on

The retargeter assumes `initValue`, `iter_arg`, and `return_var` all share a single MemRef for the whole loop. `InitMemRef` previously patched `return_vars` from the *yield value*'s MemRef, which left the iter_arg out of sync whenever the yield producer lived in a different buffer. This PR patches `return_vars` from the *iter_arg*'s MemRef instead, so the retargeter can consume a consistent target.

### Complexity note

The retargeter runs a single O(N) IR walk to build the def map, then one `TryRetargetVar` per iter_arg plus recursion into `IfStmt` branches. The liveness check scans the tail of the `AssignStmt`'s containing body; in the worst case of a deep linear chain this is O(N²). In practice body tails are short (matmul/accumulator loops have a handful of producers each), so the realised cost is well below that bound. This super-linear worst case is documented in a comment at the top of the retargeter section per the project's `pass-complexity.md` rule.

## Test expectation updates — per-test justification

Each of the 8 updated tests had Expected IR describing the *old* `producer-on-fresh-buffer + tile.move-at-yield` pattern. Every update swaps that pattern for the retargeter's direct-retype behaviour. No test's *semantic* intent is relaxed — only the tactical buffer-allocation detail changes.

| Test | Old expected | New expected | Why the new expectation is correct |
| ---- | ------------ | ------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| `TestYieldFixup::test_producer_retyped_to_iter_arg_buffer` (was `test_tile_move_inserted_when_memrefs_diverge`) | `next_0` on fresh `mem_vec_3`; `tile.move(next_0) → mem_vec_2` | `next_0` directly on `mem_vec_2`; `extra_0` keeps `mem_vec_3` | Loop-carry unified with iter_arg — exactly what the test name promised, achieved without the intermediate move |
| `TestYieldFixup::test_simple_loop_memrefs_unified` | `next_0` on `mem_vec_3`; `tile.move` to `mem_vec_2` | `next_0` directly on `mem_vec_2`; `mem_vec_3` dropped | Loop-carry unified — stricter: one buffer total |
| `TestYieldFixup::test_multiple_iter_args_producers_retyped_independently` (was `…_partial_mismatch`) | Two `tile.move`s unifying `next_0/next_1` back to iter buffers | `next_0` on `mem_vec_2`, `next_1` on `mem_vec_3`; `extra_*` share `mem_vec_4` | Each iter_arg gets its own producer placed directly in its buffer |
| `TestControlFlow::test_var_used_in_nested_if_shares_iter_arg_buffer` (was `…_not_reused_in_loop`) | `tile_c` on fresh `mem_vec_3`; `tile.move(if_result) → mem_vec_2` | `tile_c`, `if_result`, `loop_out` all on `mem_vec_2` | `tile_a`/`acc` already share `mem_vec_2` via `InitMemRef`; retargeter collapses the yield chain |
| `TestControlFlow::test_loop_local_var_can_be_reused` | `tile_x/y/z` share `mem_vec_3`; `tile.move(tile_z) → mem_vec_2` | `tile_x/y` share `mem_vec_3`; `tile_z` directly on `mem_vec_2` | Loop-locals can still share their own scratch; the yield producer is retyped |
| `TestControlFlow::test_nested_for_loops_outer_var_extends_to_outer_end` | Moves at both inner and outer yields; 4 allocations | `tile_b` on inner iter buffer `mem_vec_4`; `tile_d` on outer iter buffer `mem_vec_3`; 3 allocations | Nested loop-carry unification at both levels |
| `TestControlFlow::test_for_with_if_multiple_vars_competing` | `tile_c/tile_d` on `mem_vec_5`; `tile.move(if_result) → mem_vec_4` | `tile_c/tile_d/if_result/loop_out` all on `mem_vec_4` | Cross-branch producer sharing via the iter buffer |
| `TestControlFlow::test_loop_return_var_blocks_init_memref_reuse` (#768 regression) | `acc_next` on `mem_vec_5`; move to `mem_vec_3` | `acc_next` directly on `mem_vec_3`; `resid` still on `mem_vec_5` (NOT `mem_vec_3`) | **The critical #768 invariant still holds:** `resid` does not clobber the loop-carry buffer. Only the now-unnecessary move is removed. |

## New tests

- `TestTopDownRetargeter::test_acc_chain_pinned_producer_shares_iter_arg_buffer` — a `matmul_acc` chain over `Acc` memory. Exercises the pinned-producer path: `matmul_acc`'s `set_output_reuses_input(0)` forces the retargeter to recurse through the pin to the iter_arg (already on target), then retype `acc_next`. Verifies that the full chain shares a single `mem_acc_*` allocation and that **no** `tile.move` ops remain in the loop body.
- `TestTopDownRetargeter::test_retargeter_declines_when_target_still_live` — a loop body where an op reads `acc_0` *after* the yield producer writes. Verifies the retargeter correctly declines to retype (leaves the producer on its own buffer), so that `YieldFixup` can insert the `tile.move` safely.

## Test plan

- [x] `cmake --build build --parallel` succeeds in the worktree
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_memory_reuse.py` (36 tests, includes the 8 updated + 2 new) — pass
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_init_memref.py` — pass
- [x] Full IR suite `tests/ut/ir/ -n auto` — 2706 passed, 13 skipped
- [x] `clang-tidy` clean on the diff
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (clang-format, cpplint, ruff, pyright)

title: feat(ir): Add tensor-level sort32, mrgsort, and gather operators

## Summary

Add tensor-level counterparts to the existing tile-level sort/gather ops so users can write sort/gather pipelines over tensors and let `ConvertTensorToTileOps` handle the tile.load / tile.store bridging.

### New tensor ops

- **`tensor.sort32`** — 1:1 mapping to `tile.sort32`.
- **`tensor.mrgsort_format1` / `tensor.mrgsort_format2`** — 1:1 mapping to tile variants. Python DSL exposes a single `mrgsort()` dispatcher that selects format by argument count.
- **`tensor.gather`** (index form, MVP: rank-2, `dim=-1`) — lowered to a per-row `tile.load` + `tile.gather` + `tile.assemble` loop; Phase-3 rewrites the loop to write directly into an added `Out` tensor param via `tile.store`.
- **`tensor.gather_mask`** — 1:1 mapping to `tile.gather_mask` with `mask_pattern` (P0101..P1111) and optional same-bit-width `output_dtype`.

- **C++ op defs** — `src/ir/op/tensor_ops/sort.cpp`, `src/ir/op/tensor_ops/gather.cpp`

title: [Bug] Parser error renderer truncates inline caret message at first '.' in dotted identifiers
body:
### Component

Parser

### Description

`ErrorRenderer._render_caret_line` in `python/pypto/language/parser/diagnostics/renderer.py` produces a truncated inline annotation next to the caret whenever the error message contains a dotted identifier (e.g. `pl.range()`, `pl.pipeline()`).

The renderer tries to pull out the "first sentence" of the error message with `message.split(".")[0]`, but `.` is not a reliable sentence terminator — every code reference like `pl.foo` contains one. The first `.` encountered is inside the code token, so the split chops the sentence mid-word.

Example — writing `pl.piepline(...)` (typo) in a for-loop iterator currently renders as:

```
Error: For loop must use pl.range(), pl.parallel(), pl.unroll(), pl.pipeline(), or pl.while_()
  --> /home/syfeng/pypto/qwen3_bak.py:170:38
    |
168 |                             tile_b = pl.slice(wq, [Q_CHUNK_K, Q_LOOP_CHUNK], [0, q0])
169 |                             q_acc = pl.matmul(tile_a, tile_b, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
170 |                             for k0 in pl.piepline(Q_CHUNK_K, hidden, Q_CHUNK_K, stage=3):
    |                                       ^^ For loop must use pl
171 |                                 tile_a_i = pl.slice(normed_tile, [BATCH_TILE, Q_CHUNK_K], [0, k0])
172 |                                 tile_b_i = pl.slice(wq, [Q_CHUNK_K, Q_LOOP_CHUNK], [k0, q0])
    |
   = help: Use pl.range(), pl.parallel(), pl.unroll(), pl.pipeline(), or pl.while_() as the iterator
```

The inline annotation `For loop must use pl` is nonsense on its own — it cuts off before the list of valid iterators that makes the message actionable. Any parser error whose first sentence references a dotted identifier will hit this.

A related secondary issue (same file, `_calculate_token_length`): the caret is only `^^` (2 chars) because the token scanner stops at the first non-alnum/underscore character, so it highlights only `pl` instead of the full `pl.piepline` callee. Not the main focus of this bug but worth fixing at the same time since both stem from treating `.` as a word boundary.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Write a PyPTO DSL function whose `for` loop iterator is a misspelled / unsupported call, e.g.:

   ```python
   import pypto.language as pl

   @pl.program
   class P:
       @pl.function
       def main(self):
           for i in pl.piepline(0, 64, 4, stage=3):
               pass
   ```

2. Trigger parsing (import / compile the program).
3. Observe the rendered `ParserSyntaxError`: the inline message beside the caret reads ``For loop must use pl`` instead of a useful summary of the full message.

### Expected Behavior

The inline annotation should either:

- Reproduce the full first sentence of the error message (dotted identifiers kept intact), or
- Be omitted entirely if no safe short summary can be extracted.

For the example above, a useful inline message would be something like ``expected pl.range / pl.parallel / pl.unroll / pl.pipeline / pl.while_``, or the renderer could simply print the caret with no trailing annotation and rely on the top-line `Error:` message.

### Actual Behavior

The inline annotation is cut off at the first `.` character in the message, which (for any message that references a `pl.*` or `module.attr` API) falls inside the code token:

```python
# renderer.py:360
short_msg = message.split(".")[0].split("\n")[0]
if len(short_msg) < 50:
    inline_msg = self._red(f" {short_msg}")
```

For ``\"For loop must use pl.range(), pl.parallel(), ...\"``, `split(\".\")[0]` returns `\"For loop must use pl\"` (length 20, passes the `< 50` gate), which is then rendered as the inline annotation — misleading to users.

### Git Commit ID

50fb980845990e7e255fe0dc2a51ec27c21bc1eb

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Source location: `python/pypto/language/parser/diagnostics/renderer.py:360` (truncation); `python/pypto/language/parser/diagnostics/renderer.py:263` (`_calculate_token_length`, related caret-width bug).
- Every `ParserSyntaxError` whose message mentions a dotted identifier is affected, not just the for-loop iterator check.

title: chore(runtime): bump simpler runtime to bb7965f
body:
## Summary

Bumps the \`runtime/\` submodule from \`a9f3ea9\` to \`bb7965f\` (27 commits).

Notable upstream changes:
- Drop \`Dist\` prefix from runtime types, files, and constants (\`DistWorker → Worker\`, \`DistOrchestrator → _Orchestrator\`, \`DIST_MAILBOX_SIZE → MAILBOX_SIZE\`, ...).
- Variadic templates for \`Arg::add_input/add_output/add_inout/add_no_dep/add_scalar\`.
- New \`ChipWorker.bootstrap_context\` one-shot chip bring-up (L5) and \`ChipBootstrapChannel\` handshake.
- HCCL / sim backends for \`comm_*\` C API.
- AICPU scheduler hot-loop optimization and cacheline-aligned field layout.
- \`pto_runtime_c_api.h\` gains \`device_malloc_ctx\` / \`device_free_ctx\` / \`copy_to_device_ctx\` / \`copy_from_device_ctx\`.

## Why no pypto-side adaptation

Cross-layer audit of the three pypto integration points against \`bb7965f\`:

1. \`simpler.task_interface\` / \`simpler.worker\` (imported by \`python/pypto/runtime/task_interface.py\`, \`device_runner.py\`): every symbol pypto imports — \`ChipCallable\`, \`ChipCallConfig\`, \`ChipStorageTaskArgs\`, \`CoreCallable\`, \`Worker\`, \`make_tensor_arg\`, \`scalar_to_uint64\` — is still re-exported. The renamed \`Dist*\` symbols are not referenced anywhere in pypto (verified by grep). The L2 \`Worker(level=2, device_id=..., platform=..., runtime=...)\` / \`init\` / \`run\` / \`close\` surface used by \`execute_on_device\` is unchanged.
2. Orchestration codegen (\`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp\`): emits \`#include \"pto_orchestration_api.h\"\` and single-arg \`add_input/add_output/add_inout/add_scalar\` calls. The new variadic \`template<typename... Args> void add_X(Args&&...)\` signatures are backward-compatible with single-arg calls.
3. Distributed codegen (\`src/codegen/distributed/distributed_codegen.cpp\`): targets the Linqu \`LevelRuntime\` API (\`linqu::LinquTensor\`, \`submit_worker\`, \`submit_orchestrator\`, ...). These symbols are not provided by simpler at either \`a9f3ea9\` or \`bb7965f\`, so the L3+ rename sweep does not affect them.

\`simpler_setup\` public APIs used by pypto — \`simpler_setup.environment.PROJECT_ROOT\` (\`python/pypto/runtime/env_manager.py\`) and \`simpler_setup.runtime_builder.RuntimeBuilder\` (\`__init__\`, \`get_binaries\`, \`RuntimeBinaries\`) — are unchanged; \`runtime_builder\` only gains internal git-HEAD cmake-cache invalidation.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run \`tests/ut/codegen/\` to confirm orchestration / distributed codegen still emits valid C++.
- [ ] Run an end-to-end example that exercises \`execute_on_device\` on a simulator platform to validate the L2 \`Worker\` path.

title: fix(parser): Keep dotted identifiers intact in diagnostic renderer
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1102. The parser error renderer treated `.` as a word boundary in two places, which broke whenever error messages or source lines contained dotted code tokens (`pl.range()`, `module.attr`, ...):

- **Inline caret annotation**: `message.split(\".\")[0]` truncated any message with a dotted identifier at the first `.`. For the reported case, `\"For loop must use pl.range(), pl.parallel(), ...\"` rendered as the bogus fragment `\"For loop must use pl\"` next to the caret.
- **Caret width**: `_calculate_token_length` stopped at the first non-alnum/underscore character, so a pointer at `pl.piepline(...)` highlighted only `pl` (`^^`) instead of the full callee.

Fix:

- `_render_caret_line`: extract the short message with a sentence-boundary regex (`\.(?=\s|$)`), i.e. only split on `.` when followed by whitespace or end of string. Dotted identifiers are preserved; for messages that are a single long sentence (like the reported one), the `< 50` length gate now correctly suppresses the inline annotation instead of emitting a misleading fragment.
- `_calculate_token_length`: extend the token scan across `.` when identifier characters sit on both sides, so callees like `pl.piepline` and `foo.bar.baz` render as a single `^^^^^^^^^^^` span.

## Rendered before / after

Before:

```
    |                                       ^^ For loop must use pl
```

After:

```
    |                                       ^^^^^^^^^^^
```

The full message is still carried by the top-line `Error:` header and the `help:` line — no information is lost.

## Test plan

- [x] New regression test: `tests/ut/language/parser/test_diagnostics_renderer.py` — 9 cases covering `_calculate_token_length` (dotted callee, multi-segment dotted ident, plain ident, trailing/leading `.`) and `_render_caret_line` (bug repro, short-sentence inline annotation, dotted reference mid-message). All pass.
- [x] Existing parser error tests (`test_error_cases.py`, `test_error_wrapping.py`) — unchanged, 38 cases still pass.
- [x] Full suite: `cmake --build build --parallel && pytest tests/ut -n auto` — 3730 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed.

title: feat(torch_codegen): cross-core split + scheduler for tpush/tpop ops
body:
## Summary

Make `torch_codegen` produce numerically faithful PyTorch for the four
cross-core pipe ops in both unidirectional and bidirectional Group
bodies, and for `split` modes that fan a tile out to two AIV subblocks
running in parallel.

Closes #1032.

## Why

The previous codegen for the cross-core ops had two shortcomings:

1. `tpop_from_aic(split>0)` returned only subblock 0's half and dropped
   subblock 1's data. End-to-end comparison against the hardware was
   therefore impossible whenever a kernel used UpDown / LeftRight split.
2. Group bodies that used bidirectional pipes (V↔C) or same-side
   feedback (push + pop on the same direction) deadlocked at codegen
   time because each AIC/AIV body ran to completion before the other
   side started, so the receiver popped from an empty deque.

Both made `torch_codegen` unusable as a precision-debugging reference
for any cross-core kernel beyond the simplest unidirectional, no-split
case.

## What changed

### Codegen / runtime helpers

- Preamble adds four direction-specific helpers (`_tpush_to_aiv`,
  `_tpush_to_aic`, `_tpop_from_aic`, `_tpop_from_aiv`) plus
  generator-mode variants (`_tpush_to_aiv_g`, …) that `yield`
  `_WaitPop` / `_WaitPush` at every pipe sync point.
- `_tpop_from_aic(pipe, split)` now reassembles the two queued halves
  via `torch.cat`, so the legacy single-AIV roundtrip path returns the
  full tile instead of dropping half the data.
- Per-subblock pipes (`to_aiv_sb0/sb1`, `to_aic_sb0/sb1`) plus a
  `_current_sb[0]` mutable singleton model two AIV subblocks running
  the same kernel on different halves of a split tile. The scheduler
  injects the active subblock id before each `next()` / `send()` and
  the AIV body reads it via `tile.get_subblock_idx`, mapped to
  `_current_sb[0]`.
- `_run_scheduler` is a cooperative round-robin over generator-style
  AIC/AIV bodies. It raises a clear deadlock error when no task can
  make progress.

### Codegen visitor

- `_detect_scheduled_groups` triggers the scheduler path on
  bidirectional pipe usage, same-side feedback, **or** any pipe op
  carrying `split>0`. AIV members that touch `split>0` are emitted as
  two scheduler tasks (one per AIV subblock id).
- `_walk_pipe_calls` / `_function_uses_split` / `_scan_pipe_ops`
  centralize pipe-op IR walking so detection stays in one place.
- `visit_program` emits AIC/AIV → Opaque/Other → Group → Orchestration,
  with `_visit_group_function` adding a `# Group: ...` comment and
  `_generate_entry_point` wrapping multi-function programs in
  `def run(...)`.
- `_stable_hints` + `_var_refs` prevent nanobind GC id recycling from
  silently remapping function params; `_visit_expr_str` dispatches
  nested `ir.Call` nodes through `visit_call` so handlers are reached
  for all argument shapes.

## End-to-end shape (split = UpDown example)

```
AIC: matmul(a, b) = R(4×4)
   ├─ tpush_to_aiv split=1 ──► to_aiv_sb0 = R[0:2]   to_aiv_sb1 = R[2:4]
   │
AIV#0 (sb=0):                       AIV#1 (sb=1):
  half = pop sb0 (2×4)                 half = pop sb1 (2×4)
  res_half = slice(residual,           res_half = slice(residual,
              offset=0*2)                            offset=1*2)
  out_half = half + res_half           out_half = half + res_half
  tpush_to_aic split=1 ──►             tpush_to_aic split=1 ──►
    to_aic_sb0 = out_half                to_aic_sb1 = out_half
   │                                    │
AIC: tpop_from_aiv split=1 ──► cat([sb0, sb1], dim=-2) = full(4×4)
     store(out)
```

`out == matmul(a, b) + residual` for every split mode.

## Tests

- **UT** (`tests/ut/debug/test_torch_codegen.py`)
  - split semantics for the four cross-core ops
  - multi-Group isolation
  - qwen3-style cross-core matmul + residual (UpDown / LeftRight),
    full-tile correctness
  - bidirectional pipe smoke tests, error / unsupported-op cases
  - legacy roundtrip tests updated to expect the full reassembled tile
- **ST** (`tests/st/codegen/test_torch_codegen_cross_core.py`)
  - V2C and C2V × {NoSplit, UpDown, LeftRight} `torch_codegen` ≈ torch
    golden, with `split>0` paths driving the bidirectional reassembly
- **ST** (`tests/st/codegen/test_torch_codegen_scheduler.py`)
  - cooperative scheduler over bidirectional, same-side-feedback,
    plain unidirectional, and deadlock cases

All 76 `torch_codegen` tests pass locally; remaining failures in
`tests/st/codegen/` (paged_attention etc.) are pre-existing in this
worktree and unrelated to this change.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd pypto_torch_codegen
source .venv/bin/activate
pytest tests/ut/debug/test_torch_codegen.py \
       tests/st/codegen/test_torch_codegen_cross_core.py \
       tests/st/codegen/test_torch_codegen_scheduler.py -q
```

title: test(runtime): require explicit cross-core platform
body:
## Summary

  This PR makes `tests/st/runtime/test_cross_core.py` require an explicit `--platform` and derives the backend type
  strictly from that platform.

  Previously, the test file instantiated `PTOTestCase` without an explicit backend, so it could silently fall back to
  the default backend. In practice, that meant `--platform a5` did not reliably exercise the A5 backend and could
  trigger misleading platform-mismatch failures.

  ## What Changed

  - Added an explicit platform-to-backend mapping in `test_cross_core.py`
    - `a2a3` / `a2a3sim` -> `BackendType.Ascend910B`
    - `a5` / `a5sim` -> `BackendType.Ascend950`
  - Added validation so the test file now fails fast if `--platform` is not provided
  - Added `pytest_generate_tests` to inject a single `backend_type` parameter from `--platform`
  - Updated all cross-core test cases to instantiate `PTOTestCase` with the resolved `backend_type`
  - Updated the `__main__` entry point to require `--platform` as well

  ## Why

  The goal is to make platform selection explicit and reliable for the cross-core runtime tests.

  This avoids silent fallback to the default backend and ensures that:
  - `--platform a5` actually runs against the A5 backend
  - `--platform a2a3` actually runs against the A2A3 backend
  - missing platform configuration is reported immediately instead of causing confusing downstream failures

  ## Scope

  This PR only changes the cross-core test harness logic in `tests/st/runtime/test_cross_core.py`.
  It does not change runtime, codegen, or ISA behavior.

  ## Validation

  Verified with:

title: feat(ir): add tile.ci / tensor.ci ops (arange) — #1095
body:
## Summary

Register TCI (contiguous integer sequence) at the IR / DSL / conversion layers so the already-wired `pto.tci` codegen actually fires. Before this PR, `ir.is_op_registered("tile.ci") == False` blocked all usage despite backend codegen being in place.

Fixes #1095

## Usage

```python
import pypto.language as pl

# Ascending: dst[k] = start + k
idx: pl.Tile[[1, 32], pl.INT32] = pl.tile.ci(0, [1, 32], dtype=pl.INT32)

# Descending: dst[k] = start - k
idx: pl.Tile[[1, 32], pl.INT32] = pl.tile.ci(31, [1, 32], dtype=pl.INT32, descending=True)

# Tensor variant (lowers to tile.ci via conversion pass)
idx: pl.Tensor[[1, 32], pl.INT32] = pl.tensor.ci(0, [1, 32], dtype=pl.INT32)

# arange alias
idx = pl.arange(0, [1, 32], dtype=pl.INT32)
```

Primary motivation: supply the `idx` operand for `tile.sort32` / `tensor.sort32` without fabricating it via orchestration.

## Inputs / Outputs

| Param         | Type                  | Notes                                                    |
| ------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `start`       | scalar                | same dtype as destination                                |
| `shape`       | `Sequence[IntLike]`   | innermost dim must be != 1                               |
| `dtype`       | `DataType`            | **`{INT16, INT32}` only** (see note below)               |
| `descending`  | `bool` (default `False`) | ascending vs. descending                              |

**Output**: tile/tensor of the given `shape` / `dtype` populated per the formula.

## Important ISA Constraint — only the first row is populated

Per `_deps/pto-isa/docs/isa/tile/ops/irregular-and-complex/tci.md` (Constraints section):

> The implementation uses `dst.GetValidCol()` as the sequence length and does not consult `dst.GetValidRow()`.

This means for shape `[M, N]` with `M > 1`, **only row 0 gets `[start, start±1, …, start±(N-1)]`**; rows 1..M-1 retain UB residue. Typical correct usage is `shape=[1, N]`, which matches sort32's `idx` operand. Multi-row arange is out of scope for this PR and should be built on top via broadcast (future work).

## Why dtype is narrowed to `{INT16, INT32}` (no UINT)

The ISA doc nominally allows `{INT16, UINT16, INT32, UINT32}` (`tci.md:96`), but the PTOAS lowering pipeline has a gap on the unsigned path:

1. MLIR `arith.constant` requires **signless** integer types (`i32`, not `ui32`).
2. Bridging signless → unsigned via `builtin.unrealized_conversion_cast` produces valid MLIR but PTOAS recovers the template parameter `T` from the SSA def chain, **ignoring the cast**.
3. The result: `TCI<Tile<..., uint32_t, ...>, int32_t, 0>(...)` — `T=int32_t` mismatches `TileData::DType=uint32_t`, triggering `static_assert<is_same<DType, T>>` failure in `_deps/pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a2a3/TCI.hpp:20`.
4. Official PTOAS ST (`_deps/pto-isa/tests/npu/a2a3/src/st/testcase/tci/tci_kernel.cpp`) only instantiates `int32_t` and `int16_t` — the unsigned path was never validated upstream.

Frontend UTs added (`test_tile_ci_rejects_uint_dtype`, `test_tensor_ci_rejects_uint_dtype`) guard this restriction. Re-enable UINT16/UINT32 once PTOAS supports it properly.

## Changes

- **C++ IR**: `REGISTER_OP("tile.ci")` in `src/ir/op/tile_ops/memory.cpp`; `REGISTER_OP("tensor.ci")` in `src/ir/op/tensor_ops/memory.cpp`.
- **Python IR**: `ci(...)` in `python/pypto/ir/op/{tile,tensor}_ops.py`.
- **Python DSL**: `ci(...)` + `arange` alias in `python/pypto/language/op/{tile,tensor}_ops.py`.
- **Conversion**: `RegisterSimple("tensor.ci", "tile.ci")` in `op_conversion_registry.cpp`.
- **Backend**: small `MakeCiCodegenPTO` tweak to emit DPS-form type annotations (`ins(%v {attr} : type) outs(%d : type)`).
- **Docs**: en/zh operator table entries.
- **Tests**: UTs for both ops, conversion test, ST (`tests/st/runtime/test_ci.py`).

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: `pytest tests/ut/ir/operators/ -v -k ci`
- [x] Conversion test: `pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/ -v -k ci`
- [x] ST (PTOAS path on 910B): `pytest tests/st/runtime/test_ci.py` — ascending start=0, ascending start=10, descending, all passed
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` passed

title: feat(ir): introduce two-layer direction model with Call::arg_directions_
body:
Split argument direction into two layers: ParamDirection on Function parameters (callee-side contract) and a new ArgDirection on Call nodes (call-site behavior, mirroring TensorArgType plus Scalar). Codegen now consumes Call::arg_directions_ as the single source of truth, so dependency tracking and allocation match runtime semantics.

Highlights:
- Add ArgDirection enum and Call::arg_directions_ field with reflection, structural equal/hash, serializer, mutator, and Python bindings (pypto.ir.directions).
- Add DeriveCallDirectionsPass that derives per-arg directions from callee signatures and tensor argument origin; runs in the standard pipeline before the final Simplify.
- Add CallDirectionsResolved IRProperty + property verifier so the pass pipeline auto-checks the post-condition (no standalone pass).
- Add pl.adir.* DSL helpers (input/output/inout/output_existing/ no_dep/scalar) and round-trip them through python_printer ↔ ast_parser, keeping arg_directions stable across print → parse.
- Switch orchestration_codegen / orchestration_analysis to read from Call::arg_directions_ instead of recomputing from callee params.
- Document the model and DSL surface in docs/{en,zh-cn}/dev/ir/08-direction_model.md.

Collateral fixes surfaced by the new round-trip checks:
- tensor.transpose DSL/IR now accept both int and ConstInt for axis1/axis2.
- tensor.create gains a manual_dep kwarg (only emitted when True) so passes that set it round-trip cleanly.
- expand_mixed_kernel uses DataType::INDEX for shape ConstInts to match the parser's bare-int convention.
- Update test_pass_manager expected pass order; rewrite test_expand_mixed_kernel_a2a3 shape literals to bare ints.

Tests: tests/ut full suite — 3914 passed, 16 skipped.

title: chore(runtime): bump simpler runtime to bb7965f
body:
## Summary

Bumps the \`runtime/\` submodule from \`a9f3ea9\` to \`bb7965f\` (27 commits).

Notable upstream changes:
- Drop \`Dist\` prefix from runtime types, files, and constants (\`DistWorker → Worker\`, \`DistOrchestrator → _Orchestrator\`, \`DIST_MAILBOX_SIZE → MAILBOX_SIZE\`, ...).
- Variadic templates for \`Arg::add_input/add_output/add_inout/add_no_dep/add_scalar\`.
- New \`ChipWorker.bootstrap_context\` one-shot chip bring-up (L5) and \`ChipBootstrapChannel\` handshake.
- HCCL / sim backends for \`comm_*\` C API.
- AICPU scheduler hot-loop optimization and cacheline-aligned field layout.
- \`pto_runtime_c_api.h\` gains \`device_malloc_ctx\` / \`device_free_ctx\` / \`copy_to_device_ctx\` / \`copy_from_device_ctx\`.

## Why no pypto-side adaptation

Cross-layer audit of the three pypto integration points against \`bb7965f\`:

1. \`simpler.task_interface\` / \`simpler.worker\` (imported by \`python/pypto/runtime/task_interface.py\`, \`device_runner.py\`): every symbol pypto imports — \`ChipCallable\`, \`ChipCallConfig\`, \`ChipStorageTaskArgs\`, \`CoreCallable\`, \`Worker\`, \`make_tensor_arg\`, \`scalar_to_uint64\` — is still re-exported. The renamed \`Dist*\` symbols are not referenced anywhere in pypto (verified by grep). The L2 \`Worker(level=2, device_id=..., platform=..., runtime=...)\` / \`init\` / \`run\` / \`close\` surface used by \`execute_on_device\` is unchanged.
2. Orchestration codegen (\`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp\`): emits \`#include \"pto_orchestration_api.h\"\` and single-arg \`add_input/add_output/add_inout/add_scalar\` calls. The new variadic \`template<typename... Args> void add_X(Args&&...)\` signatures are backward-compatible with single-arg calls.
3. Distributed codegen (\`src/codegen/distributed/distributed_codegen.cpp\`): targets the Linqu \`LevelRuntime\` API (\`linqu::LinquTensor\`, \`submit_worker\`, \`submit_orchestrator\`, ...). These symbols are not provided by simpler at either \`a9f3ea9\` or \`bb7965f\`, so the L3+ rename sweep does not affect them.

\`simpler_setup\` public APIs used by pypto — \`simpler_setup.environment.PROJECT_ROOT\` (\`python/pypto/runtime/env_manager.py\`) and \`simpler_setup.runtime_builder.RuntimeBuilder\` (\`__init__\`, \`get_binaries\`, \`RuntimeBinaries\`) — are unchanged; \`runtime_builder\` only gains internal git-HEAD cmake-cache invalidation.

## Test plan

- [x] Rebuild pypto (\`cmake --build build --parallel\`) to pick up the new submodule.
- [x] Run \`tests/ut/codegen/\` to confirm orchestration / distributed codegen still emits valid C++.
- [x] Run an end-to-end example that exercises \`execute_on_device\` on a simulator platform to validate the L2 \`Worker\` path.

## Summary

Relax `MemoryReuse` tile compatibility so two 2D tile allocations with identical storage shape but different `valid_shape` can share a backing allocation.

- Drop `valid_shape` from `AreTileViewsEqual` in `src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp` so it no longer participates in the per-tile equality check.

title: [Feature] Allow Python-style variable rebinding in @pl.jit
body:
### Summary

Inside `@pl.jit` kernels, let users rebind a variable to a value of a different type — the way plain Python allows. Today this raises `Cannot reassign '<name>' with a different type`, even though `@pl.jit` is meant to feel like Python. The strict one-name-one-type rule should continue to apply to the `@pl.program` DSL, which is a surface syntax over the IR; this request is scoped to the JIT user interface only.

### Motivation / Use Case

`@pl.jit` (see #878) is positioned as the user-friendly entry point — "write Python, call it with torch tensors, it compiles." A natural consequence of "it's Python" is that users expect to reuse variable names freely, just as they do in PyTorch, NumPy, and Triton JIT.

In practice this pattern shows up constantly:

```python
@pl.jit
def scale_and_norm(x: pl.Tensor, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    with pl.incore():
        M, N = x.shape
        t = pl.load(x, [0, 0], [M, N])    # t is a Tile
        s = pl.reduce_sum(t)               # s is a Scalar
        t = pl.mul(t, 1.0 / s)             # fine — Tile → Tile
        t = s                               # ❌ rejected today: Tile → Scalar
        pl.store(t, [0, 0], out)
    return out
```

The final rebind is idiomatic Python, but PyPTO currently errors out and suggests inventing a new name. Asking users to manually number their intermediates (`t1`, `t2`, `t_final`) undercuts the "feels like Python" promise of the JIT interface and adds friction that other kernel JIT frameworks don't impose.

The strict behavior is *correct* for `@pl.program` — that's a DSL where each Python identifier is a direct handle to an IR `Var` with a fixed type, and relaxing it there would break the IR contract. But `@pl.jit` users aren't writing IR; they're writing Python.

Users who benefit: anyone authoring kernels through `@pl.jit`, especially those coming from PyTorch/Triton/JAX where this is the default.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Inside `@pl.jit` (and any `@pl.jit.incore` sub-kernels), the following should work without errors:

```python
@pl.jit
def example(a: pl.Tensor, b: pl.Tensor, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    with pl.incore():
        M, N = a.shape
        x = pl.load(a, [0, 0], [M, N])     # Tile
        x = pl.reduce_sum(x)                # rebind: Tile → Scalar
        x = pl.cast(x, pl.FP16)             # rebind: dtype changes
        ...
```

Expected behavior:

- Rebinding to the same type — works today, continues to work.
- Rebinding to a different shape, dtype, or kind (Tile/Scalar/Tensor) — should compile, matching Python's name-binding semantics.
- Subsequent reads of the name see the most recent binding, as in Python.
- Error messages and diagnostics should still refer to the user's original name (no leaking of internal renames).

Out of scope for this request: relaxing the same rule in `@pl.program`. That remains strict and unchanged.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Rename manually** — works today but is noisy (`t1`, `t2`, `t_final`) and contradicts how users write Python everywhere else.
- **Wrap intermediates in helper functions** — forces unnecessary refactoring for what is a trivial rebind in Python.
- **Stay on `@pl.program`** — loses the ergonomic gains of the JIT entry point.

### Additional Context

- Extends the JIT interface proposed in #878.
- The current error is raised in the parser when the Python name maps to an existing `ir.Var` whose type doesn't match the new value; the strict check was introduced in #642 and is appropriate for the DSL.
- PyTorch, Triton JIT, and JAX traced functions all allow arbitrary Python rebinding — this request aligns `@pl.jit` with that common expectation.

title: [Feature] pl.spmd: support compile-time Python variables for core_num
body:
### Summary

`pl.spmd(core_num=...)` currently requires `core_num` to be an integer literal in the source code. Python variables that hold compile-time constant integers are rejected, even though their value is fully known at parse/compile time.

### Motivation / Use Case

When writing parameterized programs inside a builder function, shape constants are computed from function arguments and stored as Python variables:

```python
def build_qwen3_decode_program(max_seq: int = 4096, ...):
    max_ctx_blocks = (max_seq + SEQ_TILE - 1) // SEQ_TILE  # Python int, e.g. 64

    @pl.program
    class Qwen3Decode:
        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
        def orchestrator(self, ...):
            with pl.spmd(core_num=max_ctx_blocks, sync_start=True):  # ❌ Error
                ...
```

The parser currently checks `isinstance(kw.value, ast.Constant)` at the AST level, so any `ast.Name` node (a variable reference) is rejected — even if the variable is a plain Python `int` evaluated at program-build time.

The error message is:
```
Error: core_num must be an integer literal
   = help: Use 'with pl.spmd(core_num=8):'
```

This forces users to hard-code magic numbers or use string formatting / `exec` workarounds, which hurts readability and defeats the purpose of parameterized builder functions.

### Proposed API / Behavior

The parser should evaluate the `core_num` expression in the enclosing Python scope and accept any value that resolves to a positive `int` at program-build time. The constraint should be semantic ("must be a positive integer known at build time"), not syntactic ("must be a literal in source").

```python
# Should work: variable bound to a compile-time int
max_ctx_blocks = (max_seq + SEQ_TILE - 1) // SEQ_TILE
with pl.spmd(core_num=max_ctx_blocks, sync_start=True):   # ✅

# Should work: simple constant expression
with pl.spmd(core_num=MAX_CTX_BLOCKS // SB_BATCH, sync_start=True):  # ✅

# Should still fail: runtime IR node (e.g. result of pl.tensor.read)
ctx_blocks = (ctx_len + SEQ_TILE - 1) // SEQ_TILE  # IR node
with pl.spmd(core_num=ctx_blocks, sync_start=True):  # ❌ runtime value, should remain an error
```

### Alternatives Considered

Hard-coding the integer literal (e.g. `core_num=64`) works but breaks parameterization. Using `exec()` or string templates to generate source with the literal baked in is possible but significantly complicates the builder pattern.
