title: [Pass Bug] InlineFunctions emits self-referential post-call binding when an inline callee rebinds a pl.Out parameter
body:
### Pass Name

InlineFunctions

### Description

When an `@pl.jit.inline` (a.k.a. `FunctionType.Inline`) callee rebinds one of its `pl.Out` parameters in its body (typical pattern: `out = pl.tensor.assemble(out, acc, [0, 0])`) and returns it, the `InlineFunctions` pass plumbs the **original call-site argument** as the call's return value at the use site, instead of the **inlined re-bound SSA temp**.

For each call site `lhs = self.callee(..., out=actual_out)` the pass produces the IR equivalent of `lhs = actual_out` after splicing the body, even though the body contains a rebinding `out = assemble(out, ...)` whose result is what `return out` was supposed to plumb back. The rebound `out` SSA temp becomes dead.

This is invisible when the same inline callee is invoked **once** (the dead `out` is collapsed and the result happens to alias the same buffer), but becomes a hard failure when the **same** inline callee is called **multiple times** rebinding distinct pl.Out parameters of the entry: orchestration codegen lowers the post-call SSA self-aliases into C++ `auto X = X;` lines, which gcc rejects with `error: use of 'X' before deduction of 'auto'`.

Minimal repro: [`pypto-lib/examples/intermediate/multi_proj.py`](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-lib/blob/feat/dsv4-moe-router-orchestration/examples/intermediate/multi_proj.py) — a `proj` inline kernel called three times for Q/K/V from a `qkv_proj` JIT entry. Pass dump (`01_after_InlineFunctions.py`) clearly shows `q_out_v1 = q_out`, `k_out_v1 = k_out`, `v_out_v1 = v_out` instead of binding to the inlined `out` rebound in each pl.at scope.

Related: #1184 (orchestration codegen drops aliases for tuple-returned InOut), #631 (orchestration codegen drops Scalar return values), #1221 (broader function-to-function call composition).

### Git Commit ID

f2a90331

### Before IR (Input)

```python
import pypto.language as pl


@pl.program
class Before:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Inline)
    def proj(
        self,
        x: pl.Tensor[[16, 256], pl.BF16],
        w: pl.Tensor[[256, 256], pl.BF16],
        out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 256], pl.FP32]],
    ) -> pl.Tensor[[16, 256], pl.FP32]:
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="proj"):
            tile_x = pl.tensor.slice(x, [16, 64], [0, 0])
            tile_w = pl.tensor.slice(w, [64, 256], [0, 0])
            acc = pl.tensor.matmul(tile_x, tile_w, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
            for kb in pl.range(1, 4):
                k0 = kb * 64
                tile_x_i = pl.tensor.slice(x, [16, 64], [0, k0])
                tile_w_i = pl.tensor.slice(w, [64, 256], [k0, 0])
                acc = pl.tensor.matmul_acc(acc, tile_x_i, tile_w_i)
            out = pl.tensor.assemble(out, acc, [0, 0])
        return out

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration, level=pl.Level.CHIP, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
    def qkv_proj(
        self,
        x: pl.Tensor[[16, 256], pl.BF16],
        wq: pl.Tensor[[256, 256], pl.BF16],
        wk: pl.Tensor[[256, 256], pl.BF16],
        wv: pl.Tensor[[256, 256], pl.BF16],
        q_out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 256], pl.FP32]],
        k_out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 256], pl.FP32]],
        v_out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 256], pl.FP32]],
    ):
        q_out_v1 = self.proj(x, wq, q_out)
        k_out_v1 = self.proj(x, wk, k_out)
        v_out_v1 = self.proj(x, wv, v_out)
        return q_out_v1, k_out_v1, v_out_v1
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

```python
@pl.program
class Expected:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration, level=pl.Level.CHIP, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
    def qkv_proj(self, x, wq, wk, wv, q_out, k_out, v_out):
        # --- Q call site: inlined body ---
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="proj"):
            tile_x_inline_q = pl.tensor.slice(x, [16, 64], [0, 0])
            tile_w_inline_q = pl.tensor.slice(wq, [64, 256], [0, 0])
            acc_inline_q = pl.tensor.matmul(tile_x_inline_q, tile_w_inline_q, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
            for kb_inline_q in pl.range(1, 4):
                k0 = kb_inline_q * 64
                tile_x_i = pl.tensor.slice(x, [16, 64], [0, k0])
                tile_w_i = pl.tensor.slice(wq, [64, 256], [k0, 0])
                acc_inline_q = pl.tensor.matmul_acc(acc_inline_q, tile_x_i, tile_w_i)
            out_inline_q = pl.tensor.assemble(q_out, acc_inline_q, [0, 0])
        q_out_v1 = out_inline_q     # ← bind to inlined return SSA, NOT to q_out
        # ... same shape for k_out_v1 = out_inline_k, v_out_v1 = out_inline_v
        return q_out_v1, k_out_v1, v_out_v1
```

### Actual IR or Error

`01_after_InlineFunctions.py` (excerpt — same shape repeats for k_out and v_out):

```python
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="proj"):
    tile_x_inline6 = pl.tensor.slice(x, [16, 64], [0, 0])
    tile_w_inline5 = pl.tensor.slice(wq, [64, 256], [0, 0])
    acc_inline4 = pl.tensor.matmul(tile_x_inline6, tile_w_inline5, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
    for kb_inline3 in pl.range(1, 4):
        k0_inline2 = kb_inline3 * 64
        tile_x_i_inline1 = pl.tensor.slice(x, [16, 64], [0, k0_inline2])
        tile_w_i_inline0 = pl.tensor.slice(wq, [64, 256], [k0_inline2, 0])
        acc_inline4 = pl.tensor.matmul_acc(acc_inline4, tile_x_i_inline1, tile_w_i_inline0)
    out = pl.tensor.assemble(q_out, acc_inline4, [0, 0])     # ← rebound 'out' becomes dead
q_out_v1 = q_out                                              # ← BUG: should be `q_out_v1 = out`
```

Downstream orchestration codegen for the entry (`build_output/.../orchestration/qkv_proj.cpp`):

```cpp
PTO2_SCOPE() {
    // Task 0: proj
    Arg params_t0;
    params_t0.add_input(ext_x);
    params_t0.add_input(ext_wq);
    params_t0.add_inout(ext_q_out);
    pto2_rt_submit_aic_task(0, params_t0);
    auto q_out = q_out;     // gcc: error: use of 'q_out' before deduction of 'auto'
    // ... same auto k_out = k_out; auto v_out = v_out; for the other two calls
}
```

Build error:

```
orchestration/qkv_proj.cpp:42:22: error: use of 'q_out' before deduction of 'auto'
   42 |         auto q_out = q_out;
      |                      ^~~~~
orchestration/qkv_proj.cpp:50:22: error: use of 'k_out' before deduction of 'auto'
orchestration/qkv_proj.cpp:58:22: error: use of 'v_out' before deduction of 'auto'
```

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Additional Context

Workaround: switch the inline callee to `@pl.jit.incore` (a separate IR sub-function called by the orchestration). The bug does not occur because the post-call SSA temp comes from a real call boundary, not from an inlined splice.

Source repo / branch for full repro: `hw-native-sys/pypto-lib` @ `feat/dsv4-moe-router-orchestration`, file `examples/intermediate/multi_proj.py`. Reproduces deterministically with `python examples/intermediate/multi_proj.py -p a2a3sim`.

title: fix(ir): Substitute inline callee params at def-sites too
body:
## Summary

Fixes the InlineFunctions sub-bug from #1281: when an `@pl.jit.inline` callee
rebinds one of its `pl.Out` params (typical pattern: `out = pl.tensor.assemble(out, ...); return out`), the pass produced a self-referential post-call binding `lhs = actual_arg` because the LHS of the rebinding was left as the callee's original param Var while every use-site got substituted to the actual arg.

## Root cause

`SpliceInlineCall` split substitution into two disjoint maps:

- `param_subst` (`Var → Expr`) — applied only at use-sites via `VisitExpr_(VarPtr)`.
- `rename_map` (`Var → Var`) — applied only at def-sites via `VisitStmt_(AssignStmtPtr/...)`.

A line in the rename-map seeding loop explicitly skipped any Var that was also a param (`if (param_subst.count(v) > 0) continue;`). That assumed params never appear at def-sites, which is true for ML-style functions but false in pre-SSA imperative IR — `out = pl.assemble(out, ...)` rebinds the param Var. The skip left the LHS in neither map, so the original param Var leaked into the caller, while the substituted return-site `return out` plumbed the original actual arg back to the call's LHS — yielding `lhs = actual_arg`. Downstream codegen then lowered that to `auto X = X;` in C++.

## Fix

Replace the hand-rolled split-map substitution with a single
`DeepClone(callee->body_, seed, /*clone_def_vars=*/true)` call. `DeepClone` already routes def-site Vars through the same `VisitExpr_(VarPtr)` substitution as use-sites, so one combined `Var → Expr` seed map handles both:

- Param Var → actual-arg Expr — for a Var actual arg the rebinding collapses naturally to `actual = pl.assemble(actual, ...)`, the pre-SSA in-place semantics; for a non-Var actual arg at a def-site the base IRMutator's Var-cast check raises a clear span-tagged error.
- Locally-defined Var → fresh `_inlineN` Var — preserves the existing naming so multi-call-site expansions stay distinguishable in IR dumps.

Removes the `VarSubstituteMutator` class entirely (~95 lines) along with its split-map machinery.

## Tests

- All 13 pre-existing tests in `test_inline_functions.py` still pass.
- Adds `TestInlineFunctionsParamRebinding` with two new cases:
  - `test_single_callsite_pl_out_rebinding` — single inline call rebinding a `pl.Out` param (the minimal trigger from #1281's second comment).
  - `test_multi_callsite_distinct_rebindings` — three call sites (Q/K/V shape), confirming each emits an independent rebinding of its own actual arg with no cross-site aliasing.
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` full suite: 1191 passed, 25 unrelated skips.

## Scope of this PR — partial fix for #1281

This addresses **only** the InlineFunctions root cause (the title symptom of #1281). End-to-end empirical verification with `pypto.ir.compile()` shows that after this fix, the IR going into orchestration codegen is self-alias-free at every pipeline stage (the post-call alias is between distinct SSA versions). However, `orchestration/qkv_proj.cpp` still emits `auto q_out = q_out;` because of a separate, codegen-side bug:

- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_analysis.cpp:294-331` — `VarLineageCollector` propagates the entry's `pl.InOut` param identity through call results (the call's LHS Var inherits the param's lineage via the Out/InOut argument).
- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:1303-1310` — `emit_name_map` seeding then assigns the param's emit name (`q_out`) to every Var in that lineage. Both LHS and RHS of the post-call alias resolve to `q_out`, and the catch-all AssignStmt emit at line 338-342 produces `auto q_out = q_out;`.

That codegen bug fires regardless of how InlineFunctions handles param rebinding — fresh-local form (`result = pl.assemble(out, ...)`) reproduces the same C++ symptom on this branch. A follow-up PR is needed in the orchestration codegen.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_inline_functions.py -v` (13 existing + 2 new pass)
- [x] `pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/ -n auto` (1191 pass, 25 unrelated skips)
- [x] End-to-end `ir.compile()` on the issue's repro confirms the IR going into codegen is clean (no self-alias at any pipeline stage)
- [ ] CI

Refs: #1281

title: fix(codegen): Skip no-op X=X alias in orchestration emit
body:
## Summary

Fixes sub-problem #2 of #1281: orchestration codegen emitted `auto q_out = q_out;` from clean IR, which gcc rejects with `use of 'q_out' before deduction of 'auto'`. This PR is intentionally scoped to the codegen-layer fix and lands alongside #1282, which fixes sub-problem #1 (InlineFunctions) at the IR layer; the two are independent and can land in any order.

## Trigger

Two sequential AssignStmts in the orchestration body, where the first is a Call-RHS that threads the entry's `pl.Out` param into a callee's Out/InOut arg, and the second is a Var-RHS alias of the call result:

```python
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration, ...)
def entry(self, x, q_out: pl.Out[...]):
    t = self.kern(x, q_out)   # call result: lineage(t) = q_out
    u = t                     # Var-RHS alias: lineage(u) = q_out (chained)
    return u
```

`VarLineageCollector` collapses every Var rooted in the entry's `pl.Out` param onto that param's emit name — `t`, `u`, and `q_out` all share emit name `"q_out"`. The Call-RHS path already had a symmetric guard in `EmitTensorAlias` (`if (alias_name != out_arg)`), so it suppressed the no-op for Form B. The catch-all Var-RHS `else` branch in `VisitStmt_(AssignStmtPtr)` had no such guard and emitted `auto q_out = q_out;` literally.

## Fix

Add the symmetric guard to the catch-all Var-RHS branch. When the value is a Var and its emit name matches the LHS emit name, drop the AssignStmt — `VarLineageCollector` already records that both Vars alias the same buffer, so the assignment is identity at the C++ level.

This is a codegen-layer band-aid; the FIXME marks the cleaner home as an IR-level copy-propagation pass that drops lineage-redundant Var-RHS AssignStmts before codegen sees them. Today's `Simplify` pass only does scalar constant propagation, not tensor-Var copy prop, so a new pass is needed to retire this guard.

## Tests

New `TestNoOpAliasSkip` class with three tests bracketing the trigger:

| Form | Pattern | Status pre-fix | Status post-fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `return self.kern(...)` | ✓ no `auto X = X;` | ✓ no `auto X = X;` |
| B | `t = self.kern(...); return t` | ✓ guard in `EmitTensorAlias` | ✓ unchanged |
| C | `t = self.kern(...); u = t; return u` | ❌ `auto q_out = q_out;` | ✓ alias dropped |

Form C also asserts the kernel task submission survives, so the new guard cannot over-fire and drop real work.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/ut/codegen/` (234 pass, includes the 3 new regression tests)
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` (1191 pass — no adjacent-pass regressions)
- [x] clang-tidy on the diff (no new issues)
- [x] pre-commit hooks (clang-format, cpplint, ruff, pyright — all pass)

## Related

- Companion to #1282 (sub-problem #1 — InlineFunctions). Both PRs together close #1281 end-to-end.

title: [Feature] AssignTypeSymmetry: structural verifier enforcing var.type == value.type on every AssignStmt
[Bug] pl.range body: cross-iteration rebind of tile-typed variables is dropped during IR lowering
body:
### Component

Codegen / IR lowering (pl.range loop body)

### Description

When using `pl.range(N)` for a runtime layer loop in a `@pl.function`, python-level rebinds of tile-typed variables inside the loop body (e.g., `state = pl.assemble(state, ..., ...)` or `current = next`) do not chain across iterations. Each iteration sees a fresh tile, and the final committed state on the host either equals the initial input (no rebind ever observed) or is uninitialized memory (NaN bytes).

This blocks the most natural pattern for multi-layer fused kernels:

```python
current_hidden = ...load input...
for layer_idx in pl.range(num_layers):
    next_hidden = pl.create_tensor([batch, hidden], dtype=pl.BF16)
    # ... compute attention + MLP, write to next_hidden ...
    current_hidden = next_hidden          # rebind across iterations
out = pl.assemble(out, current_hidden, ...)
```

`pl.unroll(num_layers)` works for the same source code (each iteration is fully expanded at compile time, so the rebind is materialized in the IR). `pl.range` is required at production scale (40-layer Qwen3, 60+ layer DeepSeek) because full unroll explodes binary size and compile time.

### Steps to Reproduce

In `hw-native-sys/pypto-lib`, branch `feat/hf-compare-framework`, file `examples/models/qwen3/14b/qwen3_14b_decode_full.py`:

1. Confirm line 162 reads `for layer_idx in pl.range(num_layers):`
2. Run end-to-end with truncated 4-layer model:

```bash
task-submit --device <free> --run "python llm/examples/qwen3_14b_npu_generate.py \
    --model-dir <Qwen3-14B-4L-path> \
    --prompt '你好' --platform a2a3 \
    --max-seq-len 128 --max-new-tokens 4"
```

Add a probe comparing decode kernel `in` vs `out`:
```python
diff_max = (out.float() - hidden.float()).abs().max().item()
```

### Expected Behavior

`out` should equal a 4-layer transformer forward pass on `hidden_states`, with non-zero `diff_max` reflecting attention + MLP contributions.

### Actual Behavior

`diff_max == 0.000e+00` byte-exact for every decode step, every input token. The kernel is an identity passthrough on the python-visible output. Per-element comparison of `out_first5` vs `in_first5` shows bit-exact equality across 5120-dim `hidden`.

If a per-layer debug GM tensor is added (`debug_per_layer = pl.assemble(debug_per_layer, current_hidden, [layer_idx * batch, 0])`), the host reads back NaN bytes for every layer — confirming the assemble writes never materialize at the device.

The same source code with line 162 changed to `pl.unroll(num_layers)` gives `diff_max ≈ 30` (residual stream growth) and per-layer debug tensors populated correctly.

### Numerical Summary

| `pl.range` num_layers | `out diff_max` | per-layer debug | residual flow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~5–10 ✓ | populated | OK |
| 2 | 0 (passthrough) | NaN | broken |
| 4 | 0 (passthrough) | NaN | broken |

Single iteration works because there's no cross-iteration rebind required.

### Working Hypothesis

The IR lowering for `pl.range` does not preserve the SSA chain when a python-level variable holding a tile is reassigned inside the loop. Each iteration's `pl.assemble(target, ...)` creates a new SSA value; when the loop body terminates and the next iteration begins, the IR generator binds the loop-carried `target` back to the original (loop-entry) version rather than the previous iteration's last assignment.

### Why This Matters

Multi-layer fused kernels are unusable without this. The only working alternative (`pl.unroll`) generates 762 kernel binaries for 4 layers — extrapolating to 40 layers (Qwen3-14B) is intractable for compile time and code size.

### Git Commit ID

Ascend 910B

title: [Bug] Fused multi-layer kernel: last layer's add_inout write to k_cache is not flushed back to host
body:
### Component

Runtime / device-host sync (RT2)

### Description

When a fused multi-layer kernel uses `pl.unroll(N)` to repeatedly write to the same `pl.Tensor` parameter (which the orchestration codegen emits as `add_inout` in `pto2_rt_submit_aiv_task` calls), the **last iteration's writes do not propagate back to the host buffer** after the kernel call returns. The kernel computation succeeds on the device side (downstream attention reads see the just-written K and produce correct outputs), but the host-visible buffer is byte-identical before and after the call.

### Steps to Reproduce

In `hw-native-sys/pypto-lib`, branch `feat/hf-compare-framework`, file `examples/models/qwen3/14b/qwen3_14b_decode_full.py`:

1. Confirm line 162 reads `for layer_idx in pl.unroll(num_layers):`
2. Run a single decode step with the 3-layer model:

```bash
task-submit --device <free> --run "python llm/examples/qwen3_14b_npu_generate.py \
    --model-dir <Qwen3-14B-3L-path> \
    --prompt '你好' --platform a2a3 \
    --max-seq-len 128 --max-new-tokens 1"
```

3. In `llm/core/pypto_executor.py` `run_decode`, snapshot `k_cache` before/after the kernel call:

```python
k_cache_before = k_cache.clone()
compiled.decode(..., k_cache, ..., out, ...)
for li in range(num_layers):
    base = li * layer_cache_rows
    modified = not torch.equal(
        k_cache_before[base:base + layer_cache_rows],
        k_cache[base:base + layer_cache_rows],
    )
    print(f"L{li}: modified={modified}")
```

### Expected Behavior

For `num_layers=3`, all three layers' K cache regions should be modified (every layer's `pl.assemble` writes to `k_cache` at slot offset `layer_idx * layer_cache_rows + ...`).

### Actual Behavior

Only L0 and L1 are modified on host:

```
[probe-decode-perlayer] L0:max_abs=8.875e+00 | L1:max_abs=1.662e+01 | L2:max_abs=2.912e+01
[probe-decode-kvwrite]  L0:modified=True,diff_max=109 | L1:modified=True,diff_max=31 | L2:modified=False,diff_max=0
[probe-decode]          out: finite=True max_abs=29.12   ← out is correct!
```

L2's K cache region (rows `[2 * layer_cache_rows, 3 * layer_cache_rows)`) is byte-identical to the snapshot before the kernel call.

Critically, **the kernel's internal compute is correct**:
- L2's `hidden` output (29.12) is finite and shows the expected residual stream growth (8.87 → 16.62 → 29.12)
- For L2's attention to produce a finite output, it must have read the K it just wrote at slot 1 (other positions are from prefill)
- So **the K write does land on the device side**, but never gets flushed back to host

For `num_layers=4`, both L2 and L3 are modified=False; L1 develops NaN as a secondary effect on subsequent decode steps because the cross-call KV cache reuse picks up stale data/w00956228/newpto.

### Codegen Evidence

In `build_output/Qwen3Decode_*/orchestration/qwen3_decode.cpp`:

```cpp
// L0: first K write — uses add_output (presumably always flushed)
params_t6.add_output(ext_k_cache);

// L1, L2, L3: subsequent writes — all use add_inout
params_t26.add_inout(ext_k_cache);   // L1
params_t46.add_inout(ext_k_cache);   // L2  ← submitted, but not flushed
params_t66.add_inout(ext_k_cache);   // L3  ← submitted, but not flushed (4L only)
```

All four `pto2_rt_submit_aiv_task(N, params_tN)` calls are emitted. The corresponding `qwen3_decode_incore_*.cpp` kernel files all contain `TSTORE` instructions targeting the K cache pointer with the correct per-layer offsets (verified by inspecting `v77 = (slot_block * num_kv_heads + ki) * BLOCK_SIZE + slot_offset + layer_offset_const`).

### Numerical Summary

| Config | L0 | L1 | L2 | L3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3L unroll | modified=True ✓ | modified=True ✓ | **modified=False ✗** | — |
| 4L unroll | modified=True ✓ | modified=True ⚠ NaN | **modified=False ✗** | **modified=False ✗** |

### Working Hypothesis

For an `add_inout` tensor written multiple times within a single fused kernel call, RT2's host-flush logic only flushes the first ~N-1 writes (where the count of intermediate writes that get RAW-followed by reads in the same call). The very last write to that tensor — even if subsequent decode-step kernel calls will read it as input — appears to be elided from the host writeback path.

### Why This Matters

This makes fused multi-layer decode kernels produce silently wrong KV cache on host, breaking any usage that requires KV cache reuse across decode steps (i.e., all autoregressive generation). A 3-layer model produces gibberish text; a 4-layer model produces NaN logits.

The single-layer kernel (`qwen3_14b_decode.py`) called N times from python (per-layer loop in the executor) works correctly because each call only has 1 inout write. The fused multi-layer version is the target architecture for performance, but is unusable until this is fixed.

### Git Commit ID

repo: `hw-native-sys/pypto-lib`, branch `feat/hf-compare-framework`, kernel file `examples/models/qwen3/14b/qwen3_14b_decode_full.py`; pypto commit dd8d521e or later

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

title: fix(ir): Set TileType memory_space from target_memory in DeduceTileLoadType
body:
## Summary

- `DeduceTileLoadType` now passes `target_memory_opt` as the constructed `TileType`'s `memory_space_` so the layout (`tile_view`) and memory space agree at construction time.
- `CanonicalizeTileViewInPlace` can then collapse the explicit Mat-style `tile_view` against the matching implicit, giving a unique canonical encoding that round-trips through print/parse.
- Adds layered regression coverage in `test_flatten_tile_nd_to_2d.py`:
  - Deducer-level invariant parametrized over `target_memory ∈ {Mat, Vec}`.
  - Rank-3 Mat `tile.load` → `tile.move` → `store` program that exercises the previously-uncovered Form A construction in `FlattenTileNdTo2D` under the autouse `RoundtripInstrument`.

## Why CI didn't catch the original issue

Two layered protections kept the bug dormant in main:

1. `OpRegistry::Create` already backfills `memory_space_` from the `target_memory` kwarg via `set_output_memory_from_kwarg` (issue #553's fix). Any `tile.load` created through the public path gets a coherent type for free, regardless of what `DeduceTileLoadType` returns.
2. Every existing rank>2 Mat `tile.load` in the test suite is consumed by `tile.batch_matmul[_acc]`, which routes through Strategy 1 and skips the Form A construction altogether.

Tests that opt out of `RoundtripInstrument` via `VerificationLevel.NONE` were also checked — none use rank>2 Mat `tile.load`, so enabling the instrument on them would not have caught this. The gap was structural test coverage, not suppressed verification.

The fix in `DeduceTileLoadType` makes the deducer self-consistent so the result is correct independent of `OpRegistry::Create`'s backfill, and the regression tests close the coverage gap.

## Verification

Tests added were verified to actually catch the bug. With both protections temporarily disabled (the new `DeduceTileLoadType` fix reverted **and** the `OpRegistry::Create` backfill turned off), all three new tests fail with the exact symptom from the issue: printed annotation `pl.Tile[[16, 128], pl.FP16]` (no `pl.Mem.Mat`) and `RoundtripInstrument` raising `TileType tile_view presence mismatch` after `FlattenTileNdTo2D`. With only the `DeduceTileLoadType` fix in place (backfill still off), all three pass — confirming the fix is sufficient on its own.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest tests/ut/ir/` — 2964 passed, 27 skipped, 0 failed (was 2961, +3 new)

title: [New Op] Add tensor/tile cos and sin APIs with pass-time lowering to primitive ops
body:
### Operation Level

Other (Tensor-level and Block-level/tile-level)

### Proposed Name & Signature

```python
pl.cos(x: pl.Tensor) -> pl.Tensor
pl.sin(x: pl.Tensor) -> pl.Tensor

pl.tile.cos(x: pl.Tile) -> pl.Tile
pl.tile.sin(x: pl.Tile) -> pl.Tile
```

### Semantics Description

Introduce first-class `cos` and `sin` interfaces for both tensor and tile values.

- Input requirements:
  - Floating-point tensor/tile inputs (at least FP16/FP32); integer inputs should be rejected or explicitly cast.
- Output shape/type:
  - Same shape/layout as input; dtype follows existing unary-op promotion rules.
- Mathematical definition:
  - `y = cos(x)` and `y = sin(x)` element-wise.
- Lowering requirement:
  - During pass expansion, replace these ops with compositions of existing primitive ops instead of introducing mandatory backend intrinsics.
  - A practical baseline is polynomial/Taylor-style approximation with range reduction (for numerical stability), implemented as reusable pass patterns.
- Edge cases:
  - Define behavior for NaN/Inf consistently with existing math-op policy.
  - Document approximation error bounds per dtype/range and fallback strategy when precision target cannot be met.

### Example Usage

```python
@pl.program
class TrigExample:
    @pl.function
    def main(self, x: pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.FP32]) -> pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.FP32]:
        a = pl.cos(x)
        b = pl.sin(x)
        return a + b
```

```python
# Tile-level usage sketch in a tile compute region
t = ...  # pl.Tile[...] produced by tile.load or block compute
u = pl.tile.cos(t)
v = pl.tile.sin(t)
out = u + v
```

### Hardware Support Considerations

- Should not require dedicated trig ISA support to be usable.
- Prefer pass-time decomposition to existing arithmetic primitives so CPU fallback and multiple NPUs can share semantics.
- If backend has native trig support, allow optional later canonicalization to backend-specific intrinsics.

### Motivation / Use Case

- Trigonometric ops are fundamental for many kernels (signal processing, positional encoding variants, scientific workloads).
- Users currently need manual decomposition or out-of-graph preprocessing, which hurts readability and optimization opportunities.
- Providing both tensor and tile interfaces keeps API coverage consistent across frontend expression levels.

### Additional Context

- Related implementation strategy: range reduction + polynomial approximation (e.g., truncated Taylor/Chebyshev-style forms).
- The exact approximation family and degree can be selected by pass policy (accuracy vs throughput).

title: fix(codegen): preserve loop-carried tensor rebinds in orchestration ForStmt
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1286.

The orchestration codegen for `pl.range` (and any `ForStmt` with iter_args) silently dropped python-level rebinds inside the loop body, causing fused multi-layer kernels to byte-exact passthrough their input. Two coupled bugs:

1. **iter_arg / return_var aliased to init's emit name.** For yields that rebind to a *different* tensor (e.g. `current = next` where `next` is a freshly-created `pl.create_tensor`), the carry never updates — every iteration reads the loop-entry value, post-loop reads the same untouched buffer.
2. **`current_return_vars_` cleared before visiting the body.** The `YieldStmt` handler's `i < current_return_vars_.size()` guard was always false, so no rebind assignment was ever emitted.

`pl.unroll` was unaffected because each iteration is fully expanded at compile time, so rebinds chain naturally in the same SSA scope. `pl.unroll` is a workaround but unusable at production scale (40+ layer Qwen3 / DeepSeek explodes binary size and compile time).

## Approach

In `VisitStmt_(ForStmtPtr)`:

- Pre-scan the body to compute, per iter_arg, an **alias-equivalence class** — the set of Vars that name the same backing buffer as the iter_arg. Forward dataflow over body assignments, covering:
  - (a) `tensor.assemble(member, ...)` results
  - (b) Nested `ForStmt` return_vars threaded through the parent's carry
  - (c) `Call` `OutputExisting` / `InOut` first output arg
  - (d) `TupleGetItemExpr` extracts (multi-output InCore kernels)
- A yield is a **true rebind** iff its value is *not* in the iter_arg's class. Only true rebinds get a mutable carry predeclare (`auto carry_name = init;`); trivial yields keep the legacy aliasing so the runtime's `Tensor*` identity-based dep tracker keeps producer/consumer chains intact.
- `current_return_vars_` is now populated with `return_var` for rebind slots and `nullptr` for trivial slots; the `YieldStmt` handler skips null slots and emits `carry = value;` for the rest.

**Drive-by:** `for _ in pl.range(...)` was emitting `for (int64_t  = 0; ...)` (empty loop var name — the SSA-renamed `_` got stripped to "" by `GetSSABaseName`). Falls back to a synthetic `i`. Compiled by accident before because no body referenced the loop var.

## Test plan

- [x] New ST `test_orch_range_carry_rebind` minimally reproduces #1286 (orchestration `pl.range(4)` + `pl.create_tensor` + `current = next`). FAIL → PASS (output goes from `c == a` to `c == a + 4`).
- [x] Full ctrl_flow ST suite: 7 passed / 0 regressions.
- [x] Adjacent ST suites that exercise orchestration For codegen (dyn_orch_shape, assemble, compiled_program, dag): 18 passed / 0 regressions. **Total 25 passed / 0 regressions on a2a3sim.**
- [x] **End-to-end on a2a3 hardware**: Qwen3-14B 4L `decode_full` via `hf_compare`. With the fix, `pl.range` produces **byte-identical numerics** to `pl.unroll` (`out max_abs=1.83e-1`, `cosine=0.99997`, `pass_rate=0.995`). Before the fix `pl.range` gave `diff_max == 0.000e+00` byte-exact identity passthrough.

title: feat(distributed): DistributedTensorType + CommGroup IRNode + AOT comm-manifest sidecar
body:
## Summary

L3 distributed DSL milestone N1 — IR + DSL + runtime infrastructure that later milestones (alloc op / dispatch `device=` / cross-rank ops / `CollectCommGroups` pass) build on. Single squashed commit; review-friendly diff against `upstream/main`.

Three layers (one squashed commit, the layers map cleanly to file groups):

1. **`ir.DistributedTensorType` IR subclass + `pld.DistributedTensor` DSL.** Precise-`ObjectKind` subclass of `TensorType` so cross-rank op verifiers (later milestone) can reject plain `Tensor` arguments via `As<DistributedTensorType>`. DSL surface mirrors `pl.Tensor` (same 2/3/4-slot subscript: shape, dtype, [layout|memref|view], [memref]); only the IR ObjectKind differs. Reflection / serializer / structural-eq / printer share TensorType comparison via `static_pointer_cast`; printer head differs (`pld.DistributedTensor` vs `pl.Tensor`).

2. **`ir.WindowBuffer` / `ir.CommGroup` IRNodes + `Program.comm_groups_` field.** `WindowBuffer{name, size: ExprPtr, dtype, load_from_host: bool, store_to_host: bool}` — allocation-spec only, 1:1 to `simpler.task_interface.ChipBufferSpec`. `CommGroup{devices: vector<int64_t>, slots: vector<WindowBufferPtr>}` — empty `devices` ⇒ "all devices" (resolved by driver against `DistributedConfig.device_ids`); non-empty ⇒ explicit subset. `Program` gains a `(functions, comm_groups, name, span)` ctor overload, registered as `UsualField` (participates in structural eq / hash). Reflection visitors get a new `VisitLeafField(const std::vector<int64_t>&)` overload to handle the device list.

3. **AOT comm-manifest sidecar.** `python/pypto/ir/comm_manifest.py` lifts `program.comm_groups` into `output_dir/orchestration/comm_manifest.json` (v2 schema: `{"devices": [...], "slots": [...]}`). The runner reads the file at submit time and constructs `ChipBootstrapConfig` directly — no `Program` object required. Comm-less programs skip the manifest entirely so `multi_chip_dispatch` / `parallel_reduce` are unaffected.

## Scope (NOT in this PR)

- `pld.alloc_window_buffer` op + parser (next milestone)
- `pld.world_size()` host-only op + dispatch `device=r` kwarg
- `CollectCommGroups` pass (the producer of `program.comm_groups` from alloc ops)
- `pld.tile.remote_load` / `pld.system.notify` / `pld.system.wait` ops + verifier
- `pld.CommCtx` / `dist_t.comm.rank` desugar
- End-to-end `AllReduceProgram` system test

title: feat(language): manual_dep on Tensor params + pl.no_dep call-site override
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 + 2 of the manual-dependency surface plan. Lets the user opt out of the simpler runtime's automatic OverlapMap-based dependency tracking at two granularities:

- **Per-tensor (Phase 1)**: `pl.Tensor[..., pl.ManualDep]` — every reference to that buffer skips OverlapMap lookup and TensorMap insert. Useful when the user can guarantee disjoint writes (e.g. assemble-inside-kernel patterns where each iteration touches a distinct region).
- **Per-arg (Phase 2)**: `pl.no_dep(arg)` — at a single kernel call site, mark one argument as no-dep without affecting the other args. Other arguments still get auto-dep.

Both wirings are additive — default behaviour is unchanged. Already-existing `pl.create_tensor(manual_dep=True)` continues to work as today; this PR completes the symmetry by extending the flag to function parameters and adding the per-arg overlay.

### Phase 1 — `pl.Tensor[..., pl.ManualDep]`

```python
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
def orch(self, big: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[64, 64], pl.FP32, pl.ManualDep]]):
    for i in pl.parallel(M):
        big = self.write_tile(big, i, big)
    return big
```

Codegen emits `from_tensor_arg(orch_args.tensor(N), /*manual_dep=*/true)` so the runtime treats `big` as opt-out for OverlapMap.

### Phase 2 — `pl.no_dep(arg)`

```python
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
def orch(self, q, k_cache, out):
    for i in pl.range(BATCH):
        out = self.matmul(q, pl.no_dep(k_cache), out)
    return out
```

Pipeline: parser strips wrapper → `attrs['arg_direction_overrides']` → `DeriveCallDirections` overwrites slot to `NoDep` → codegen already emits `add_no_dep`. The `CallDirectionsResolved` verifier accepts `NoDep` on `In` params and rejects on `Out`/`InOut` (would suppress producer registration for a writer).

## Files changed

**Phase 1 (14 files, +399 / -26):**
- `include/pypto/ir/type.h` — `TensorType.manual_dep_` field + reflection descriptor + new ctor overloads
- `src/ir/transforms/structural_equal.cpp` + `structural_hash.cpp` — distinguish on the flag
- `src/ir/transforms/python_printer.cpp` — emit `pl.ManualDep` marker for round-trip
- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp` — `from_tensor_arg(.., true)` when set
- `python/bindings/modules/ir.cpp` + `pypto_core/ir.pyi` — new constructor overloads / `Final[bool]` field
- `python/pypto/ir/type.py` — pass-through wrapper
- `python/pypto/language/typing/manual_dep.py` (new) + `tensor.py` + `__init__.py` — `pl.ManualDep` marker, accepted in any tail position of `Tensor[...]`
- `python/pypto/language/parser/type_resolver.py` — strip `pl.ManualDep` from subscript, thread `manual_dep` to `ir.TensorType`
- `tests/ut/ir/expressions/test_tensor_type_manual_dep.py` (new) — 15 tests

**Phase 2 (8 files, +318 / -14):**
- `include/pypto/ir/expr.h` — `kAttrArgDirectionOverrides` + `WithArgDirectionOverridesAttr` helper
- `src/ir/transforms/derive_call_directions_pass.cpp` — apply overrides post-derivation
- `src/ir/verifier/verify_call_directions.cpp` — allow `NoDep` on `In` params
- `python/bindings/modules/ir.cpp` — accept `list[int]` for `arg_direction_overrides` attr
- `python/pypto/language/op/tensor_ops.py` + `__init__.py` — `pl.no_dep` marker
- `python/pypto/language/parser/ast_parser.py` — `_strip_no_dep_wrappers` helper at `self.method(...)` call sites
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_derive_call_directions.py` — 4 new tests

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/ut/ir/ tests/ut/codegen/` → **3221 passed, 29 skipped** (19 new + 3202 existing)
- [x] `cmake --build build --parallel` → clean build on rebased base (currently `d2981ed4 chore(runtime): bump simpler runtime to 551a79c (#1292)`)
- [x] `pre-commit run` on all changed files → clang-format / cpplint / markdownlint / ruff / pyright all pass
- [x] Round-trip: parse → IR → print → parse stable for both `pl.ManualDep` and `pl.no_dep` annotations

## Notes for review

- Both features are user-facing additions only; **no existing IR / golden output / behavior changes**. Default-false omission keeps every existing codegen test bytewise stable.
- Phase 1 marker is a class (`pl.ManualDep`), not a callable — chosen to mirror existing `pl.NZ` / `pl.MemRef` marker style. Subscript syntax doesn't support kwargs, so a sentinel class beats `manual_dep=True` here.
- Phase 2 marker is a function (`pl.no_dep(t)`) returning the tensor unchanged — it's parser-recognized at AST level and never appears in IR. Equivalent to manual `make_call(directions=[..., no_dep, ...])` but ergonomic at call sites.
- `pl.no_dep` on `Out`/`InOut` params is rejected at the verifier (would suppress producer registration). Test `test_no_dep_on_inout_param_rejected` documents the contract.
- Related future work (out of scope): MANUAL scope mode, explicit `add_dep` task edges. Both build on the foundation laid here.

title: [RFC] Self-consistent IR TensorType layout representation
body:
### Summary

PyPTO IR's `TensorType.tensor_view_` field has two conflicting semantics for the `layout` (DN) tag, depending on whether `stride` is empty. Codegen disambiguates via `tensor_view_->stride.empty()` — same `TensorType` structure, different meanings of `shape_`. This RFC proposes a self-consistent canonical form where `shape_` is always logical, `stride` is per-logical-dim element step, and `layout` is a derivable / asserted constraint tag.

### Motivation

Two conflicting paths producing the same IR shape:

**Semantic A — matmul B^T path**: User writes `pl.Tensor[[N, K], pl.FP32]`; `ResolveTransposeLayout` adds DN tag with empty stride. `shape_` is the **source-tensor shape**; codegen swaps trailing two dims when emitting `pto.make_tensor_view` (`get_shape_source_idx` in `pto_codegen.cpp`). `tile.load` similarly swaps offsets/sizes via `dn_swap`.

Reference: `tests/st/runtime/test_matmul.py::TestMatmulOperations::test_matmul_btranspose`, output dir `build_output/matmul_btranspose_32x64x32_*`.

**Semantic B — `tensor.transpose` path** (post commit c6b60273): `transpose([8, 16] ND)` produces `Tensor[[16, 8], DN, stride=[1, 16]]`. `shape_` is the **logical post-transpose shape**; stride explicitly describes col-major access. Codegen uses `(shape, stride)` as-is via `has_explicit_stride`.

Reference: `tests/st/runtime/test_trans.py`, output dir `build_output/TransposeSliceRepro_*`.

**Root cause**: A single `TensorType` structure carries two incompatible interpretations of `shape_`. c6b60273 patched `tensor.transpose` with explicit stride to coexist with the legacy DN-swap convention, but the underlying ambiguity remains. Any new pass / op touching DN tensors must navigate this ambiguity.

Fixing this enables:
- Mechanical codegen (no `dn_swap`, no `has_explicit_stride` branching).
- Composability between `tensor.transpose`, slice, and matmul B^T paths without special cases.
- Clear contract for orch / IR / Incore / `.pto` boundaries.

Related symptoms: #1213 (matmul b_trans=True wrong results), #1230 (ND→ColMajor Vec tile rejection).

### Design

A full design proposal is published in the first comment below.

1. Background and conflict examples.
2. Canonical TensorType invariants (`shape_` = logical; `stride` per logical dim; `layout` consistent with stride).
3. Layout family table (ND-packed / ND-strided / DN-packed / DN-strided / NZ).
4. `BuildLogicalStridesFromLayout(shape, layout)` formula.
5. \"Codegen entry must have explicit stride\" contract via new `MaterializeTensorStrides` pass + `VerifyTensorViewCanonical`.
6. Five frontend examples covering ND / explicit DN / matmul B^T / `tensor.transpose` / DN-slice.
7. Orch ↔ IR ↔ Incore ↔ `.pto` field-by-field mapping table.
8. New virtual op `tensor.as_layout` for orch↔Incore type bridging.

### Open Questions

1. Should `tensor.as_layout` be exposed in the user-facing Python DSL, or kept as an internal IR-only op produced by `LowerTransposeLoadParamLayout`?
2. For symbolic strides where `stride[-1] >= shape[-2]` cannot be statically verified, do we accept the structural equality `stride[-2] == 1` only and skip the `>=` check, or require an explicit constraint annotation?
3. Inside `convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp`, the layout kwarg propagated to `tensor.create()` currently includes the legacy DN-swap convention — what changes here once IR is canonical?

### Git Commit ID

1810c34d5d5a768d53fbe5394d58062b50e3044b

title: feat(ir): Add tile.comm_notify, tile.comm_wait, tile.comm_test cross-rank signal ops
body:
## Summary

Add three cross-rank signaling ops on AIV that wrap PTOAS's `pto.comm.*` custom dialect:

- `pl.tile.comm_notify(signal, value, *, op)` — write or atomic-add an INT32 value into a remote rank's signal slot. `op ∈ {"set", "atomic_add"}`. Lowers to `pto.comm.tnotify`.
- `pl.tile.comm_wait(signal, cmp_value, *, cmp)` — block until a local INT32 signal slot satisfies a comparison. `cmp ∈ {"eq","ne","gt","ge","lt","le"}`. Lowers to `pto.comm.twait`.
- `pl.tile.comm_test(signal, cmp_value, *, cmp)` — non-blocking poll of the same comparison; returns a `pl.Scalar(BOOL)`. Lowers to `pto.comm.ttest` (returns i1).

`signal` is a 1-element INT32 `pl.Tensor` viewing a slot in the rank's HCCL window (typically obtained via `import_peer_buffer`). `value` / `cmp_value` accepts Python `int`, `pl.Scalar`, or `pl.Expr` and is normalised to INT32.

Mirrors the two real usage patterns from simpler's `ep_dispatch_combine` kernels (count exchange via atomic_add, done barrier via atomic_add + wait ge).

## Layers updated

- C++ op registrations + IR-level validators — `src/ir/op/tile_ops/cross_core.cpp`
- PTO codegen (signal lowered to `!pto.partition_tensor_view<Nxi32>`, generic MLIR op syntax) — `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp`
- Python IR wrappers — `python/pypto/ir/op/tile_ops.py`
- DSL wrappers (re-exported via `pl.tile.*`) — `python/pypto/language/op/system_ops.py`, `python/pypto/language/op/tile_ops.py`
- UT for IR + PTO codegen — `tests/ut/ir/operators/test_tile_ops.py`, `tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen_ops.py`
- ST loopback (count exchange + done barrier + wait-only) — `tests/st/runtime/test_notify_wait.py`
- Bilingual docs — `docs/en/dev/ir/05-operators.md`, `docs/zh-cn/dev/ir/05-operators.md`
- PTOAS bumped to 0.37 (exposes the `pto.comm.tnotify/twait/ttest` custom ops) — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

## Key design / fix notes

- **Naming**: `comm_*` prefix groups these under cross-rank signaling, parallel to the `pto.comm.*` MLIR namespace.
- **Codegen**: signal Var is lowered through `make_tensor_view → partition_view` to produce a `!pto.partition_tensor_view<Nxi32>` covering the full signal shape. Assembly uses generic MLIR op syntax (`"pto.comm.tnotify"(%sig, %v) {...} : (...) -> ()`) because PTOAS defines no custom `assemblyFormat` for these ops.
- **Validation**: `f_deduce_type` enforces 1-element INT32 signal + INT32 scalar at IR construction, so misuse fails at `@pl.program` decoration time.
- **Orchestrator pattern**: side-effect kernels must bind the call (`signal = self.kernel(signal); return signal`); a bare `return self.kernel(...)` is silently dropped (KERNELS=[]).

## Testing

- [x] UT (22/22): `TestTileCommNotifyOp`, `TestTileCommWaitOp`, `TestTileCommTestOp`, `TestTileNotifyPtoCodegen`, `TestTileWaitPtoCodegen`, `TestTileTestPtoCodegen`.
- [x] ST `tests/st/runtime/test_notify_wait.py` — gated on `PTOAS_HAS_COMM_NOTIFY_WAIT=1` so infra without the upgraded PTOAS skips cleanly. Three programs: `CountExchangeProgram` (atomic_add), `WaitOnlyProgram` (wait ge), `DoneBarrierProgram` (notify + wait combined).

## Notes

- Lint/format/pyright pre-commit hooks pass.
- No new global state, no IR design changes — additive op registrations following the existing CrossCoreOp pattern (mirror of `tpush_*` / `tpop_*` / `tfree_*`).

title: [Bug] Nested @pl.jit.inline calls fail with Unsupported function call
body:
### Component

Parser / JIT frontend

### Description

`@pl.jit` supports a direct call from the entry function to one layer of `@pl.jit.inline` dependencies, but a `@pl.jit.inline` helper cannot call another `@pl.jit.inline` helper.

The nested inline case fails during JIT specialization/parsing with `Unsupported function call`.

This makes it hard to factor reusable JIT operator implementations across files or through nested helper functions.

### Steps to Reproduce

Create `/tmp/pypto_jit_call_jit_demo.py`:

```python
import torch
import pypto.language as pl


@pl.jit.inline
def inline_leaf(a: pl.Tensor, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP):
        tile = pl.load(a, [0, 0], [32, 32])
        pl.store(tile, [0, 0], out)
    return out


@pl.jit
def jit_entry_calls_inline(a: pl.Tensor, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    out = inline_leaf(a, out)
    return out


@pl.jit.inline
def inline_leaf2(a: pl.Tensor, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP):
        tile = pl.load(a, [0, 0], [32, 32])
        pl.store(tile, [0, 0], out)
    return out


@pl.jit.inline
def inline_mid_calls_inline(a: pl.Tensor, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    out = inline_leaf2(a, out)
    return out


@pl.jit
def jit_entry_calls_nested_inline(a: pl.Tensor, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    out = inline_mid_calls_inline(a, out)
    return out


def main():
    a = torch.randn(32, 32)
    out = torch.empty(32, 32)

    print("@pl.jit -> @pl.jit.inline -> @pl.jit.inline")
    try:
        jit_entry_calls_nested_inline.compile_for_test(a, out)
        print("OK")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(type(exc).__name__)
        print(exc)

    print()
    print("ordinary @pl.jit -> @pl.jit.inline")
    try:
        program = jit_entry_calls_inline.compile_for_test(a, out)
        print("OK")
        print("functions:", [gv.name for gv in program.functions])
    except Exception as exc:
        print(type(exc).__name__)
        print(exc)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run:

```bash
python /tmp/pypto_jit_call_jit_demo.py
```

### Expected Behavior

At least one of the following should be supported or clearly diagnosed:

- nested JIT inline dependencies are recursively discovered, so `@pl.jit.inline` can call another `@pl.jit.inline`, or
- the frontend emits an explicit diagnostic explaining that only entry-direct JIT inline dependencies are supported.

The direct `@pl.jit -> @pl.jit.inline` case already succeeds, so nested inline composition is the minimal extension needed for reusable helper factoring.

### Actual Behavior

Current output:

```text
@pl.jit -> @pl.jit.inline -> @pl.jit.inline
UnsupportedFeatureError
Unsupported function call: inline_leaf2(a, out)

ordinary @pl.jit -> @pl.jit.inline
OK
functions: ['jit_entry_calls_inline', 'jit_entry_calls_inline_incore_0']
```

The likely cause is that `JITFunction._get_deps()` / `_discover_deps()` only discovers direct callees from the entry function, and `_build_dep_context()` passes `dep_names=[]` for dependency functions. As a result, nested calls inside a JIT dependency are not rewritten to `self.<callee>(...)`, and the nested callee is not emitted into the specialized program.

### Git Commit ID

`1810c34d5d5a768d53fbe5394d58062b50e3044b`

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Python: 3.10.20
- Reproduction uses `compile_for_test()` only; no NPU execution is required.
- pypto-lib commit used while reproducing: `72e6af0`

title: fix(codegen): Infer static v_row/v_col when source valid >= slice size
body:
## Summary

- Adds a third inference case in `InferSubviewTileTypeComponents` (`src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp`): when the source tile's valid extent in a dimension is a static constant `>= slice size`, the sliced valid extent is statically known as `size` regardless of the (possibly dynamic) offset.
- Fixes a missing `return;` after the zero-offset equivalence case (Case 2), which would have fallen through into the new case.

## Background

`pto.subview` with a dynamic loop offset (e.g. `k0 = i * K`) was emitting dynamic `v_row`/`v_col` even when the source tile is large enough that any valid offset leaves exactly `size` valid elements. This caused PTOAS to reject otherwise-valid programs. The new inference case handles this: if `source_valid >= slice_size` (both static constants), the subview valid extent is trivially `size`.
