title: refactor(manual_scope): explicit pl.task_id_of DSL + drop DeriveManualScopeDeps pass
body:
## Summary

Rebuilds the `with pl.manual_scope():` dependency surface around an explicit, user-named TaskId API. The compiler no longer performs closure analysis to synthesize TaskId companions from tensor-typed `deps=[...]` lists; users name every dependency directly via `pl.task_id_of(producer)` / `pl.task_id_invalid()`. Net code change is **+1832 / −1685 lines**, dominated by the removal of a 660-line lowering pass that becomes unnecessary in the new model.

The series is structured as 4 atomic commits, each independently buildable + green, in dependency order:

| # | Commit | Scope |
|---|--------|-------|
| 1 | [`0d09e8dd`](../../commit/0d09e8dd) | codegen: emit `set_dependencies(arr, count)` per simpler #761; bump submodule to `a94d5140` |
| 2 | [`50e4a4ec`](../../commit/50e4a4ec) | language: expose `pl.TASK_ID` / `pl.TaskId` / `pl.task_id_invalid()` / `pl.task_id_of(...)` (additive) |
| 3 | [`3a1b3778`](../../commit/3a1b3778) | tests: migrate manual_scope ST + codegen UT to the new explicit API |
| 4 | [`2ba53c93`](../../commit/2ba53c93) | refactor: remove `DeriveManualScopeDeps`, `kAttrUserManualDepEdges`, `kAttrTaskIdVar`, and the parser's tensor-deps branch |

## Why

1. **Runtime ABI catch-up.** The simpler runtime replaced `Arg::add_dep` with `Arg::set_dependencies(ptr, count)` (single-shot, caller-owned array, no PTO2_MAX_EXPLICIT_DEPS cap). PR 1 makes orchestration codegen emit the new shape and bumps the submodule pointer.
2. **Cleaner user model.** The legacy `deps=[tensor]` form required the compiler to do closure analysis (4-stage pass, 660 lines) to figure out which kernel `Call` produced that tensor and thread a TaskId companion through every enclosing loop. The new explicit form (`tid = pl.task_id_of(producer); deps=[tid]`) makes the dependency edge a first-class value that the user threads themselves — same semantics, no analysis, much smaller surface.
3. **Drop unneeded complexity.** With the user writing TaskIds directly, the lowering pass, the dual-attr indirection (`user_manual_dep_edges` → `manual_dep_edges`), the `task_id_var` companion attr, and the per-call edge cap all disappear.

## User-facing API

```python
with pl.manual_scope():
    out = self.stage1(x)
    out_tid = pl.task_id_of(out)                       # NEW: explicit TaskId
    out2 = self.stage2(x, deps=[out_tid])              # deps=[<Scalar[TASK_ID]>]
```

Loop carry (sequential):

```python
prev_tid = pl.task_id_invalid()
for step in pl.range(N):
    out = self.kernel(..., deps=[prev_tid])
    prev_tid = pl.task_id_of(out)
```

Phase fence (outer seq × inner parallel — codegen still auto-promotes the TaskId scalar to a per-branch array carry):

```python
prev_tid = pl.task_id_invalid()
for phase in pl.range(N_PHASES):
    for branch in pl.parallel(N_BRANCHES):
        out = self.kernel_stripe(..., deps=[prev_tid])
        prev_tid = pl.task_id_of(out)
```

## Generated C++ shape

```cpp
PTO2_SCOPE(PTO2ScopeMode::MANUAL) {
    TaskOutputTensors task_0_outs = rt_submit_aiv_task(0, params_t0);
    PTO2TaskId stage1_tid = task_0_outs.task_id();        // ← from pl.task_id_of

    Arg params_t1; /* ... */
    PTO2TaskId params_t1_deps[1];
    uint32_t   params_t1_deps_count = 0;
    params_t1_deps[params_t1_deps_count++] = stage1_tid;
    params_t1.set_dependencies(params_t1_deps, params_t1_deps_count);   // ← new ABI
    TaskOutputTensors task_1_outs = rt_submit_aiv_task(1, params_t1);
}
```

## Breaking changes

- `kernel(..., deps=[tensor_var])` is no longer accepted — `deps=[...]` requires `pl.Scalar[pl.TASK_ID]` entries (wrap with `pl.task_id_of(tensor_var)`).
- The pass `DeriveManualScopeDeps` and the Python wrapper `passes.derive_manual_scope_deps()` are removed. Hand-built `OptimizationStrategy` lists that referenced it must drop the entry.
- IR attrs `Call.attrs["user_manual_dep_edges"]` and `Call.attrs["task_id_var"]` are removed. The single resolved attr is `Call.attrs["manual_dep_edges"]` (now written directly by the parser, each entry a `Scalar[TASK_ID]` Var).
- The `PTO2_MAX_EXPLICIT_DEPS = 16` codegen cap is removed (runtime no longer enforces).

## What's preserved

- Same Python parsing entry points (`pl.manual_scope()`, `deps=` kwarg shape).
- Same codegen output shape for the manual scope block (`PTO2_SCOPE(PTO2ScopeMode::MANUAL)` wrapper, per-task `TaskOutputTensors task_<n>_outs` capture, TaskId iter_arg array carry for `pl.parallel`).
- Same dependency semantics — the user-named TaskId model is strictly more expressive (no closure-analysis edge cases), and we verified that all three pattern shapes (intra-iter, branch chain, phase fence) lower identically to before.

## Verification

| Layer | Result |
|---|---|
| C++ build (`cmake --build build --parallel`) | clean |
| Pre-commit hooks (clang-format / cpplint / markdownlint / ruff / pyright) | all 4 commits passed |
| Full unit suite (`pytest tests/ut/`) | **4588 passed**, 41 skipped (down from 4590; 2 legacy regression tests deleted alongside the pass) |
| Manual-scope codegen UTs (`TestManualScopeCodegen`) | 7 passed (5 migrated + 1 dynamic-trip rejection + 1 new explicit-TaskId test) |
| Manual codegen inspection | hand-verified generated C++ for all 3 patterns matches expected `set_dependencies` shape |
| ST tests (`tests/st/runtime/`) | not runnable on this machine — system-installed `_task_interface.so` is from an older simpler. The runtime submodule bump should be picked up by CI which installs simpler from the repo. |

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py::TestManualScopeCodegen -v` — 7 passed
- [x] `pytest tests/ut/language/parser/test_task_id_dsl.py -v` — 6 passed
- [x] `pytest tests/ut/language/parser/test_manual_scope_parsing.py -v` — passes  
- [x] `pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_flatten_call_expr_pass.py -v` — passes
- [x] `pytest tests/ut/` full suite — 4588 / 41 skipped
- [ ] CI: ST runtime tests (`tests/st/runtime/test_manual_scope_pipeline.py`) require fresh simpler install — verify on CI
- [ ] CI: full build + lint matrix

title: refactor(passes): merge NormalizeStmtStructure and manual-scope lowering
body:
## Summary

Per the pass-pipeline audit, consolidate two pairs of passes whose ordering dependency had leaked into the Default strategy:

- **`ResolveBackendOpLayouts` self-normalizes.** The pass already broke the flat-SeqStmts invariant via `MakeSeqOrSingle`, requiring the pipeline to schedule a follow-up `NormalizeStmtStructure`. Calling `NormalizeStmtStructure(new_func)` before returning makes the contract local to the pass. PassProperties now lists `NormalizedStmtStructure` as produced (not invalidated), and the standalone follow-up pipeline entry is removed.
- **`DeriveManualScopeDeps` folded into `DeriveCallDirections` as Phase 2.** The lowering logic moved to a new public utility `LowerManualDepsToTaskId` (header at `include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/`), called from `DeriveCallDirections` immediately after the existing arg_directions mutator. The standalone pass, its `PassProperties`, Python binding, `.pyi` entry, and pass-doc are removed; `derive_call_directions()` keeps its existing name and factory.

Default pipeline drops from 36 to 34 passes.

## Why

Two implicit ordering dependencies — "`NormalizeStmtStructure` must follow `ResolveBackendOpLayouts`" and "`DeriveManualScopeDeps` must follow `DeriveCallDirections`" — are now localized inside the respective pass implementations, so future pass-list edits can't accidentally drop them.

## What changed

- C++: `src/ir/transforms/resolve_backend_op_layouts_pass.cpp`, `src/ir/transforms/derive_call_directions_pass.cpp`, new `utils/lower_manual_deps_to_task_id.{h,cpp}` (rename detected — 92% similar to deleted `derive_manual_scope_deps_pass.cpp`).
- PassProperties + factory cleanup: `pass_properties.h`, `passes.h`.
- Python surface: `python/bindings/modules/passes.cpp`, `python/pypto/pypto_core/passes.pyi`, `python/pypto/ir/pass_manager.py`.
- Tests: pipeline-list assertions in `test_pass_manager.py`; `test_derive_manual_scope_deps.py` rewritten to drive the merged pass and assert Phase 2 idempotence; cross-reference comments in `test_flatten_call_expr_pass.py`, `test_orchestration_codegen.py`, `test_manual_scope_pipeline.py`.
- Comments: updated cross-references in `expr.h`, `stmt.h`, `ast_parser.py`, `orchestration_codegen.cpp`.
- Docs (en + zh-cn parallel): rewrote `33-derive_call_directions.md` as two-phase pass; deleted `34-derive_manual_scope_deps.md`; updated `00-pass_manager.md`, `19-resolve_backend_op_layouts.md`, `ir/01-hierarchy.md`, `ir/02-types.md`, `ir/05-operators.md`, `language/00-python_syntax.md`, `codegen/01-orchestration_codegen.md`. Slot 34 reserved as a numbered gap in `.claude/rules/pass-doc-ordering.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cmake --build build --parallel` clean (post-rebase onto upstream main).
- [x] `pytest tests/ut/` — 4751 passed, 44 skipped.
- [x] Pre-commit hooks (clang-format, cpplint, ruff, pyright, markdownlint) clean.
- [x] All previous `DeriveManualScopeDeps` mentions either preserved as historical "was DeriveManualScopeDeps" notes or removed; no functional code path references the deleted name.

## Risks

- The 16-deps-per-submit cap (`PTO2_MAX_EXPLICIT_DEPS`) was previously documented as a pass-time check; the actual enforcement has always lived at orchestration codegen (`CHECK` in `orchestration_codegen.cpp`). Docs are now corrected — no behavior change for users.
- The new utility is invoked unconditionally per function in `DeriveCallDirections`; for programs with no manual scope, Phase 2 short-circuits on `needs_tid_.empty()`.

title: fix(runtime): drop hard-coded block_dim=24 default and plumb override end-to-end
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1173.

- `execute_on_device` and the generated `RUNTIME_CONFIG` no longer hard-code `block_dim = 24` (and `aicpu_thread_num = 4`). On devices whose usable cores for the chosen core type were below 24, every dispatch unconditionally asked for 24 logical SPMD blocks and `worker.run()` hung — the orchestrator scheduled logical blocks that never got a physical core. The recent simpler-side `aclrtGetStreamResLimit`-based validation (simpler #760) converts the hang into a clear error, but pypto's hard-coded value still forced users to hit that error with no way to override short of monkey-patching.
- `execute_on_device(block_dim, aicpu_thread_num)` are now `int | None = None`. When `None`, the field is **not** written to `ChipCallConfig` and simpler's own runtime default takes effect.
- `compile_and_assemble` returns `(chip_callable, runtime_name, runtime_config)` so callers can read `RUNTIME_CONFIG` defaults from `kernel_config.py`.
- `compile()` gains `block_dim: int | None = None`. When supplied, `_generate_config_file` bakes `"block_dim": N` into `RUNTIME_CONFIG`; otherwise the key is omitted entirely.
- `RunConfig.block_dim` and `execute_compiled(block_dim=..., aicpu_thread_num=...)` provide per-invocation override (precedence: explicit caller arg > `RUNTIME_CONFIG` > simpler default).
- L3 `DistributedRunner` / `DistributedConfig` path is unchanged — it already carries `block_dim` per program.

### Why pypto only emits / requires override

simpler currently exposes **no** Python-side accessor for the device's real core count. PR #760 added validation inside `DeviceRunner::run()` only; the nanobind bindings (`ChipWorker` in `python/bindings/task_interface.cpp`) still expose only `device_id` / `initialized` / `device_set`. So `min(kernel_required_blocks, worker.block_dim)` auto-discovery (issue #1173's long-term direction) requires a follow-up simpler change. This PR delivers the short-term half: drop the hard-coded default and let users specify the value.

`aicpu_thread_num` is plumbed for symmetry with the same precedence rules, but the generated `RUNTIME_CONFIG` keeps its `4` default — `tensormap_and_ringbuffer` requires 4 (3 schedulers + 1 orchestrator on thread 3), not a device-dependent number.

## Testing

- [x] New `tests/ut/backend/test_kernel_config_block_dim.py` (4 cases) — verifies `_generate_config_file` omits `"block_dim"` by default and emits it when set. Runs without simpler.
- [x] New `tests/ut/runtime/test_block_dim_plumbing.py` (5 cases) — verifies `execute_on_device` skips `cfg.block_dim` assignment when `None`, sets it when explicit, and `execute_compiled` reads from `RUNTIME_CONFIG` with caller override taking precedence. Skipped without simpler (mirrors `test_execute_compiled_device_tensor.py` pattern).
- [x] `tests/ut/` full suite passes (4588 passed / 42 skipped pre-rebase; 89 passed / 19 skipped in `tests/ut/runtime/` + `tests/ut/backend/` post-rebase).
- [x] Smoke-checked the generated `kernel_config.py` for both `compile()` (no `block_dim` key) and `compile(block_dim=8)` (key present with the right value).

## Related Issues

- Fixes #1173
- Builds on hw-native-sys/simpler#760 (runtime-side `validate_block_dim`)

title: [RFC] Automatic manual-scope task dependency derivation
body:
### Summary

`with pl.manual_scope():` currently requires the user to declare **every** task→task dependency by hand: extract a `TaskId` from each producer, thread it through loop `iter_args`, and pass it in `pl.submit(..., deps=[...])`. This RFC proposes an **opt-in** automatic derivation algorithm — `pl.manual_scope(auto_deps=True)` — that computes a precise dependency edge set from per-buffer read/write interval analysis and emits the same `Call.attrs["manual_dep_edges"]` the explicit API produces, so codegen is unchanged. The explicit `pl.submit(..., deps=[...])` API remains as the escape hatch.

### Motivation

The explicit-TaskId model (introduced in #1364) is correct and predictable, but for non-trivial pipelines it is verbose and error-prone:

- Every producer kernel must be invoked via `pl.submit(...)` to capture its `TaskId`.
- Cross-iteration dependencies require manually threading a `TaskId` (or `Array[N, TASK_ID]`) through `pl.range` / `pl.parallel` `iter_args`.
- A missed edge is a silent correctness bug — `manual_scope` disables the runtime OverlapMap, so nothing backfills the omission.

An earlier pass, `DeriveManualScopeDeps`, attempted naive SSA-dataflow derivation but produced **false edges** whenever a buffer was reused in-place across unrelated kernels (it keyed edges on Var identity, not on the actual byte ranges touched). It was removed in #1364. This RFC is about doing the derivation **correctly** so the common case needs no hand-written deps, while keeping the explicit API for cases the analysis can't prove.

### Design

#### Core idea: per-buffer-region interval analysis

For every kernel `Call` inside an `auto_deps=True` manual scope, compute the set of `(buffer_root, byte_interval, access_kind)` triples it touches:

- `buffer_root` — the root tensor/`MemRef` the arg resolves to (reuse the existing `BufferRootCollector`).
- `byte_interval` — derived from `tensor.slice` / `tensor.assemble` `offset` + `shape` on the arg; a full-tensor arg is `[0, size)`.
- `access_kind` — `Read` / `Write` / `ReadWrite`, from the resolved `ArgDirection` (`DeriveCallDirections` already computes this).

Build the dependency edge set by the standard hazard rules over **overlapping intervals on the same buffer root**:

| Prior access | Current access | Edge |
| ------------ | -------------- | ---- |
| Write / ReadWrite | Read / Write / ReadWrite | RAW / WAW |
| Read | Write / ReadWrite | WAR |

Two accesses with **disjoint** intervals on the same buffer produce **no edge** — this is exactly the false-positive class the old pass got wrong.

#### Loop-carry intersection

Within `pl.range` / `pl.parallel` bodies, an edge whose producer is in an earlier iteration is realized by threading the producer `TaskId` through an `iter_arg` (scalar carry) or an `Array[N, TASK_ID]` carry (parallel fan-in) — i.e. the algorithm emits the *same* IR shapes the explicit API already supports. The derivation runs after `DeriveCallDirections` and before codegen; it only writes `Call.attrs["manual_dep_edges"]`, so **no codegen change is required**.

#### API surface

```python
# Opt-in: compiler derives every edge.
with pl.manual_scope(auto_deps=True):
    for i in pl.range(M):
        scratch = self.stage1(x, scratch, i)        # plain call — no pl.submit needed
        out     = self.stage2(scratch, out, i)      # RAW on `scratch` auto-derived

# Explicit (unchanged) — the escape hatch when the analysis can't prove an edge,
# or the user wants a dependency the dataflow doesn't imply.
with pl.manual_scope():
    scratch, tid = pl.submit(self.stage1, x, scratch, i)
    out, _       = pl.submit(self.stage2, scratch, out, i, deps=[tid])
```

`auto_deps=True` and explicit `pl.submit(..., deps=[...])` may coexist in the same scope: derived edges are unioned with user-declared ones.

### Affected Files

- `include/pypto/ir/stmt.h` — **Modify** — add an `auto_deps` flag to `RuntimeScopeStmt`.
- `python/pypto/language/scope.py` + parser — **Modify** — accept `pl.manual_scope(auto_deps=True)`.
- `src/ir/transforms/` — **New** — a derivation pass (or a phase of `DeriveCallDirections`) implementing the interval analysis; reuses `BufferRootCollector` and the resolved `arg_directions`.
- `src/ir/transforms/utils/` — **New** — byte-interval extraction from `tensor.slice` / `tensor.assemble` offsets+shapes.
- Codegen — **Unchanged** — consumes `Call.attrs["manual_dep_edges"]` exactly as today.

### Testing Plan

- Unit tests for the interval-extraction utility: full-tensor, static slice, symbolic-offset slice (must conservatively treat unprovable disjointness as overlapping).
- Pass tests: RAW / WAR / WAW edge derivation; the in-place-reuse case that broke the old pass (disjoint slices → **no** edge); loop-carry threading (scalar + array fan-in).
- Equivalence tests: for the 3 ST patterns in `test_manual_scope_pipeline.py`, assert `auto_deps=True` derives the same `manual_dep_edges` as the hand-written `pl.submit(..., deps=[...])` form.
- ST sim run: numerical correctness + swimlane fence shape identical to the explicit form.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Naive SSA-dataflow derivation** (the removed `DeriveManualScopeDeps`): keyed edges on Var identity, ignored byte ranges → false edges on in-place buffer reuse. Rejected — this RFC's interval analysis is the fix.
- **Always-on auto derivation** (no opt-in): risky — a conservative analysis may over-serialize, and users lose the predictable explicit model. Rejected in favor of opt-in.
- **Runtime OverlapMap** (the AUTO-scope mechanism): already exists for non-manual scopes; `manual_scope` deliberately disables it for cases where the user needs compile-time-fixed ordering. Not a replacement.

### Rollout / Migration

- Purely additive: `auto_deps` defaults to `False`, so all existing `manual_scope` code is unaffected.
- The explicit `pl.submit(..., deps=[...])` API stays permanently as the escape hatch.
- Migration is opt-in per scope — no forced rewrite.

### Open Questions

- **Symbolic offsets**: when a slice offset is a non-const `Scalar`, disjointness can't be proven statically. Conservatively emit an edge (correct but possibly over-serialized), or require the user to fall back to explicit `deps=` for that scope? Proposal: conservative edge + a perf-hint diagnostic.
- **Granularity**: byte-interval per buffer root, or per-dimension-range? Byte-interval is simpler and sound; per-dimension may derive fewer false edges for strided access.
- **Phase placement**: a standalone pass, or a second phase of `DeriveCallDirections` (which already has the `arg_directions` + buffer-root data)?

---

Follow-up to #1364 (the explicit-TaskId manual_scope refactor).

title: feat(ir): CollectCommGroups pass + WindowBuffer visitor wire-up
body:
## Summary

Implements the `CollectCommGroups` pass that traces the `pld.alloc_window_buffer → pld.window → dispatch(device=r)` chain in each host_orch function and materialises the per-rank `WindowBuffer` / `CommGroup` metadata that downstream runtime + codegen will consume. See #1127 for the overall design and implementation plan.

After this PR the IR carries:

- One `WindowBuffer` per `pld.alloc_window_buffer` Call, wrapping the alloc's plain `Var(PtrType)` (`base`) and per-rank byte count (`size`).
- `DistributedTensorType.window_buffer_` back-references on every `pld.window` result Var (host_orch only; chip_orch / InCore params remain `nullopt`).
- `Program.comm_groups_` populated by clustering allocations on their inferred `DeviceDescriptor` (`kAll` for `for r in pl.range(pld.world_size())`; explicit subset for `device=ConstInt(N)` or `for r in pl.range(ConstInt(N))`).

### Pipeline placement

The pass runs at the very end of the default pipeline, immediately before the trailing `Simplify`. None of the intervening passes touches the host_orch alloc / window / dispatch chain — host_orch is never tile-lowered, and L2 chip_orch is never inlined into L3 — so the alloc / view / dispatch sites are still discoverable. Running last keeps the producing IR fully canonicalised before descriptor analysis, and any constant folding that the trailing `Simplify` does on collected size expressions is applied uniformly.

### Prerequisite: visitor framework wire-up

`WindowBuffer` is a `Var` subclass (introduced in N2) but was not in the `ExprFunctor`/`IRVisitor`/`IRMutator` dispatch tables. This PR adds:

- Pure-virtual + dispatch entry in `ExprFunctor::VisitExpr`
- `IRVisitor::VisitExpr_(WindowBufferPtr)` (no-op default) + python trampoline / `.pyi`
- `IRMutator::VisitExpr_(WindowBufferPtr)` mirroring `MemRef` (remap `base`/`size`, copy-on-write)
- `python_printer` overload (mirrors `MemRef`, prints `name_hint`)
- Trivial placeholders for the 7 downstream functor subclasses (`int_set`, `modular_set`, `const_int_bound`, `canonical_simplify`, `rewrite_simplify`, `deep_clone_utils`) so any future pass that visits IR containing a constructed `WindowBuffer` does not fall through to `TypeError`.

### Printer / parser fixes surfaced by roundtrip verification

The pass exercised the default roundtrip verification path on distributed programs for the first time, surfacing:

- Printer emitting `pl.pld.window(...)` (double-namespaced) for any `pld.*` op — fixed to print bare.
- Printer dropping `device=` attr on host→chip dispatches — fixed to surface it as a kwarg.
- Printer emitting `name='buf'` kwarg on `pld.alloc_window_buffer` which the parser explicitly rejects — fixed to omit on print (re-derived from LHS on reparse).
- Parser rejecting the printer's annotated form `buf: pl.Ptr = pld.alloc_window_buffer(N)` — fixed to route annotated alloc through the same path as the unannotated form.
- `text_parser.parse(...)` not auto-importing `pld` — fixed.

### IRProperty

`IRProperty::CommGroupsCollected` is produced by the pass (no required / invalidated properties).

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_window_buffer_visitor.py` — 5 new tests covering visitor / mutator dispatch on `WindowBuffer`, identity vs. fresh-mint copy-on-write, host-staging-flag preservation.
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_collect_comm_groups.py` — 10 new tests: kAll / ConstInt subset / bounded-loop subset descriptors, single-group multi-slot in alloc order, multi-group, multi-view sharing same `WindowBuffer`, chip_orch param types unchanged, dead-alloc rejection, idempotence, comm-less no-op.
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_pass_manager.py` — `TENSOR_OPTIMIZATION_PASSES` / `DEBUG_TILE_OPTIMIZATION_PASSES` snapshots updated to seat `CollectCommGroups` between `DeriveCallDirections` and the final `Simplify`.
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/parser/test_window_op.py`, `tests/ut/ir/parser/test_world_size.py` — parser regressions covering the printer / parser fixes; raw-regex match strings.
- [x] Existing schema / parser regressions for the distributed DSL continue to pass.
- [x] CI: full `tests/ut/` + `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_distributed.py` + `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_parallel_reduce.py` (comm-less paths exercise the no-op branch).

## Doc changes

- `docs/{en,zh-cn}/dev/passes/34-collect_comm_groups.md` — new per-pass doc, numbered to match the pass's end-of-pipeline position (slot 34 was previously a reserved gap).
- `.claude/rules/pass-doc-ordering.md` — registers slot 34 for `CollectCommGroups`.
- `docs/{en,zh-cn}/dev/passes/00-pass_manager.md` — threads `CollectCommGroups` into the per-pass property table (between `DeriveCallDirections` and `Simplify`) and into the tile-stage pipeline list.

## References

- Design and implementation plan: #1127

title: [Bug] Tile unary ops drop TileView valid_shape and generate mismatched validCol on NPU
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

A tile produced from `pl.slice(..., valid_shape=[...])` preserves its `TileView(valid_shape=...)` through `pl.tile.muls`, but the next unary tile op (`pl.tile.neg`) drops the `TileView`. The generated NPU C++ then calls `TNEG(dst, src)` with mismatched valid shape metadata: the source tile has `validCol=4`, while the destination tile has `validCol=8`.

This appears to be a PyPTO/codegen/type propagation issue because the invalid state is already visible in the generated PyPTO IR before PTOAS runs. PTOAS/PTO-ISA could still add a defensive validation for this mismatch, but the root cause is that PyPTO does not preserve `TileView(valid_shape)` across the unary op.

Related but not duplicate: #594 is about automatic valid_shape inference; #1031 is about odd-dimension split with padding + valid_shape.

### Steps to Reproduce

Minimal repro:

```python
import torch
import pypto
import pypto.language as pl
from pypto_lib import compile_and_run


@pypto.jit(
    kernel_kind=pypto.KernelKind.MIX,
    out_shape=[
        [16, 4],  # mix_dbg
        [16, 4],  # plain_raw
        [16, 4],  # valid_raw
        [16, 4],  # valid_scaled
        [16, 4],  # valid_neg
        [16, 4],  # plain_sigmoid
        [16, 4],  # valid_sigmoid
    ],
    out_dtype=[pl.FP32] * 7,
)
def valid_shape_slice_repro(
    x: pl.Tensor[[16, 32], pl.FP32],
    mix_dbg: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 4], pl.FP32]],
    plain_raw: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 4], pl.FP32]],
    valid_raw: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 4], pl.FP32]],
    valid_scaled: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 4], pl.FP32]],
    valid_neg: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 4], pl.FP32]],
    plain_sigmoid: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 4], pl.FP32]],
    valid_sigmoid: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 4], pl.FP32]],
) -> pl.Tensor[[16, 4], pl.FP32]:
    plain_tile: pl.Tile[[16, 8], pl.FP32] = pl.slice(x, [16, 8], [0, 0])
    valid_tile: pl.Tile[[16, 8], pl.FP32] = pl.slice(
        x, [16, 8], [0, 0], valid_shape=[16, 4]
    )

    plain_calc: pl.Tile[[16, 8], pl.FP32] = pl.sigmoid(plain_tile * 0.5) + 1e-6
    valid_scaled_tile: pl.Tile[[16, 8], pl.FP32] = valid_tile * 0.5
    valid_neg_tile: pl.Tile[[16, 8], pl.FP32] = -valid_scaled_tile
    valid_calc: pl.Tile[[16, 8], pl.FP32] = pl.sigmoid(valid_scaled_tile) + 1e-6

    mix_dbg = pl.store(valid_scaled_tile, [0, 0], mix_dbg)
    plain_raw = pl.store(plain_tile, [0, 0], plain_raw)
    valid_raw = pl.store(valid_tile, [0, 0], valid_raw)
    valid_scaled = pl.store(valid_scaled_tile, [0, 0], valid_scaled)
    valid_neg = pl.store(valid_neg_tile, [0, 0], valid_neg)
    plain_sigmoid = pl.store(plain_calc, [0, 0], plain_sigmoid)
    valid_sigmoid = pl.store(valid_calc, [0, 0], valid_sigmoid)
    return mix_dbg


def golden(x: torch.Tensor):
    x_valid = x[:, :4]
    valid_scaled = x_valid * 0.5
    return (
        valid_scaled,
        x_valid,
        x_valid,
        valid_scaled,
        -valid_scaled,
        torch.sigmoid(valid_scaled) + 1e-6,
        torch.sigmoid(valid_scaled) + 1e-6,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    x = torch.arange(16 * 32, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(16, 32) / 64 - 2
    compile_and_run(valid_shape_slice_repro, [x], golden(x), rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-5)
```

Run on sim:

```bash
python examples/debug/valid_shape_slice_repro.py -p a2a3sim
```

Run on NPU:

```bash
task-submit --device auto --env PYTHONPATH --env ASCEND_HOME_PATH --env PTOAS_ROOT --env PTO_ISA_ROOT --run "python examples/debug/valid_shape_slice_repro.py -p a2a3 -d {}"
```

### Expected Behavior

The valid-shape tile path should match the full tile path for the first 4 columns:

- `valid_raw == x[:, :4]`
- `valid_scaled == x[:, :4] * 0.5`
- `valid_neg == -(x[:, :4] * 0.5)`
- `valid_sigmoid == sigmoid(x[:, :4] * 0.5) + 1e-6`

Unary/same-shape elementwise tile ops should preserve the input `TileView(valid_shape=[16, 4])` on their output tile, or the lowered destination tile should use the same runtime valid shape as the source.

### Actual Behavior

On `a2a3sim`, all outputs pass.

On real NPU, `valid_raw` and `valid_scaled` pass, but `valid_neg` is the first failing output and `valid_sigmoid` also fails:

```text
[RUN]   'mix_dbg' PASS  shape=(16, 4) dtype=torch.float32
[RUN]   'plain_raw' PASS  shape=(16, 4) dtype=torch.float32
[RUN]   'valid_raw' PASS  shape=(16, 4) dtype=torch.float32
[RUN]   'valid_scaled' PASS  shape=(16, 4) dtype=torch.float32
[RUN]   'valid_neg' FAIL  shape=(16, 4) dtype=torch.float32
[RUN]   'plain_sigmoid' PASS  shape=(16, 4) dtype=torch.float32
[RUN]   'valid_sigmoid' FAIL  shape=(16, 4) dtype=torch.float32
Output(s) does not match golden: ['valid_neg', 'valid_sigmoid']
  'valid_neg' FAIL  shape=(16, 4) dtype=torch.float32
    Mismatched elements: 64/64  rtol=1e-05 atol=1e-05
    first 20 mismatches:
    [0] actual=0.2689414322376251, expected=1.0
    [1] actual=0.270480215549469, expected=0.9921875
    [2] actual=0.27202457189559937, expected=0.984375
    [3] actual=0.2735744118690491, expected=0.9765625
```

Generated IR evidence from `passes_dump/*_after_Simplify.py`:

```python
valid_tile__tile: pl.Tile[[16, 8], pl.FP32, ..., pl.TileView(valid_shape=[16, 4])] = pl.tile.load(...)
valid_scaled_tile__tile: pl.Tile[[16, 8], pl.FP32, ..., pl.TileView(valid_shape=[16, 4])] = pl.tile.muls(valid_tile__tile, 0.5)
valid_neg_tile__tile: pl.Tile[[16, 8], pl.FP32, ..., pl.Mem.Vec] = pl.tile.neg(valid_scaled_tile__tile)
```

Generated C++ evidence:

```cpp
Tile<..., 16, 8, ..., -1, -1, ...> v46(...)(v16, v12);  // source validCol = 4
TMULS(v46, v29, v11);

Tile<..., 16, 8, ..., -1, -1, ...> v48(...)(v16, v13);  // destination validCol = 8
TNEG(v48, v46);
```

So `TNEG` receives a source tile with `validCol=4` and a destination tile with `validCol=8`. This mismatch is not rejected in the NPU run and produces incorrect output.

### Git Commit ID

`dfb7321d87b19c068852ca3b0a05c3c270b924f6`

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Environment used to reproduce:

- pypto: `dfb7321d87b19c068852ca3b0a05c3c270b924f6` on `main`
- simpler/runtime: `a94d51407ba13206439dfda25266c1d10d78be5a`
- pypto-lib repro host commit: `13990a5`
- CANN: `8.5.0.alpha001`
- ptoas: `0.38`
- Python: `3.10.20`
- Task id for the failing NPU repro: `task_20260514_171354_26356316509`

This was originally found while optimizing `models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py` in pypto-lib. Removing `valid_shape` from the problematic slice is a local workaround, but it loses the intended valid-shape semantics and should not be required.

title: fix(passes): drop unsound disjoint-store exception in DeriveCallDirections
body:
## Summary

- `DeriveCallDirections` R-seq rule had an exception that kept a callee `Out` as `OutputExisting` (instead of `InOut`) inside a sequential loop when the callee's `tile.store` offset depended on a parameter — on the assumption that a parameter-keyed offset implies disjoint per-iteration writes.
- That check was purely **syntactic**: it never verified offset stride vs. tile extent, offset injectivity, or other write paths to the same buffer. So it could **silently drop real WAW edges** — e.g. `stride < tile extent` (partial stripe overlap), or a non-injective offset like `step // 2` (multiple iterations hit the same slot).
- This PR removes the exception: a callee `Out` under any sequential ancestor is now promoted to `InOut` **unconditionally**. A genuinely-disjoint optimization can be reintroduced later behind a sound dependence analysis (affine offset extraction, stride-vs-extent, injectivity, cross-procedural composition).
- Deletes the now-dead helpers (`CalleeHasOnlyVariableOffsetStores`, `DisjointStoreVisitor`, `ScalarDefCollector`, `ExprReferencesAnyOf`/`ExprReferencesAnyOfExpanded`, `IsScalarOrTupleOfScalarsType`), the corresponding `CallDirectionMutator` members/ctor params, and the now-unused `scalar_expr.h` include.
- Updates the pass docs (en + zh-cn): direction table + R-seq prose.
- UT: converts `test_out_param_variable_offset_store_in_seq_loop_*` to expect `InOut`, drops three tests that only exercised the removed exception path.

Net: +53 / -450 lines.

## Testing

- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_derive_call_directions.py` — 28 passed
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` + `tests/ut/codegen/` — 1535 passed, 25 skipped (1 pre-existing unrelated failure in `test_split_vector_kernel.py` deselected — confirmed failing on `main` independent of this change)
- [x] clang-tidy on the diff — clean (the `bugprone-unchecked-optional-access` flags are on pre-existing unmodified `PriorWriterCollector` lines surfaced only by hunk shift)
- [x] Code review completed
- [x] Documentation updated (en + zh-cn)

title: feat(language): unified pl.cmp and pl.set_validshape dispatch wrappers
body:
## Summary

- Promote `cmp` and `set_validshape` to the unified namespace so DSL users write `pl.cmp(lhs, rhs)` / `pl.set_validshape(t, vr, vc)` regardless of whether the operand is a Tensor or a Tile.
- For Tile inputs, `pl.cmp` automatically routes a scalar `rhs` to `tile.cmps`; for Tensor inputs it dispatches to `tensor.cmp` (which already accepts both tensor and scalar rhs).

title: TEST CI
[Bug] IR does not fold `i - (i-1) = 1` in range-slice bounds, breaks col_expand_mul static row-dim check
body:
### Component

Other (please specify in description) — IR shape inference / static constant folding for `tensor.slice` bounds.

### Description

When a pypto kernel uses a range-slice expression whose lower and upper bounds are **different symbolic expressions** (e.g. `tensor[i - 1 : i, ...]`), the IR does not algebraically fold `i - (i - 1)` into the constant `1`. The resulting slice tensor keeps a symbolic row dimension instead of a static `1`. Downstream tile ops that require the row dim to be statically known as `1` (notably `pl.col_expand_mul`) then fail their constant-row check at op verification time.

Rewriting the slice to use the **same symbol with a `+ 1` offset** (e.g. `pos = i - 1; tensor[pos : pos + 1, ...]`) compiles cleanly — the IR folds `(pos + 1) - pos = 1` and the row dim becomes a static `1`. Both forms are semantically identical, so this is purely a missing algebraic simplification in slice shape inference.

This was hit in real kernel code (`models/deepseek/v3_2/deepseek_v3_2_decode_front.py`) while migrating scalar-indexed slices `rope_cos[pos, ...]` to range-slice form `rope_cos[pos : pos + 1, ...]` (per the existing recommendation to avoid the 5-arg `tensor.slice + drop_dims` lowering). The pattern `rope_cos[ctx_len - 1 : ctx_len, ...]` was a natural first attempt and looked correct, but failed to compile.

### Steps to Reproduce

Inside any `@pl.function` body (real example from `pypto-lib`):

```python
@pl.function
def kernel(
    rope_cos: pl.Tensor[[MAX_SEQ, ROPE_DIM], pl.FP32],
    q_proj:   pl.Tensor[[BATCH, ROPE_DIM], pl.BF16],
    seq_lens: pl.Tensor[[BATCH], pl.INT32],
    ...,
):
    for b in pl.parallel(BATCH):
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="q_rope"):
            ctx_len = pl.read(seq_lens, [b])
            # BROKEN: lower and upper bound are different symbolic expressions
            cos_row = rope_cos[ctx_len - 1 : ctx_len, 0 : ROPE_DIM]
            q_row   = pl.cast(q_proj[b : b + 1, 0 : ROPE_DIM], target_type=pl.FP32)
            out     = pl.col_expand_mul(q_row, cos_row)  # crashes at verify time
```

Then compile any model using this construct on `a2a3`.

### Expected Behavior

The IR should recognize that `(ctx_len) - (ctx_len - 1)` is the constant `1` and infer the slice's row dim as a static `1`. `pl.col_expand_mul` should then accept the operand and compile successfully — identical to the equivalent rewrite below.

```python
pos     = ctx_len - 1
cos_row = rope_cos[pos : pos + 1, 0 : ROPE_DIM]   # IR folds (pos + 1) - pos = 1
out     = pl.col_expand_mul(q_row, cos_row)        # OK
```

### Actual Behavior

```
Error: pl operation 'col_expand_mul': The operator tensor.col_expand_mul requires
second argument's second-to-last dimension (row) to be 1, but got 0x17fba9f0
Check failed: col_row_const && col_row_const->value_ == 1
  at /data/czq/pypto/src/ir/op/tensor_ops/broadcast.cpp:125
  at /data/czq/pypto-lib/models/deepseek/v3_2/deepseek_v3_2_decode_front.py:209:42

C++ Traceback (most recent call last):
 File "./python/bindings/modules/ir.cpp", line 624
 File "./src/ir/op_registry.cpp", line 132
```

The `0x17fba9f0` is the symbolic-shape pointer — the verifier asked for a constant integer and got a symbol because the algebraic identity `i - (i - 1) = 1` was never folded.

The same kernel compiled cleanly after rewriting to `pos = ctx_len - 1; rope_cos[pos : pos + 1, ...]` (now committed as part of the migration). Verified end-to-end (compile + runtime + golden) on the `a2a3` platform — see `models/deepseek/v3_2/deepseek_v3_2_decode_front.py` post-fix.

### Git Commit ID

382293cb2106231876bf6a5fabd94d3854cc3af0

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related work in pypto-lib: this issue surfaced while extending the existing rule "avoid scalar-indexed slices on pypto tensors; use range slice `[i : i + 1, ...]` instead" from rank-≥3 tensors (the original MoE-weight case) to rank-2 tensors (RoPE tables, per-batch projections). The drop_dims path is unreliable for the consumers (`pl.cast`, `pl.col_expand_mul`, etc.), so range slices are the recommended form. But the range-slice form silently breaks when the bounds aren't the canonical `i : i + 1` shape.

Possible fix locations:
- The simplifier responsible for shape expressions of `tensor.slice` should normalize `upper - lower` and recognize equivalent algebraic forms — at minimum `(a + k) - a -> k` and `a - (a - k) -> k` for constant `k`.
- Alternatively, op verifiers like `col_expand_mul` could ask the symbolic engine "is this expression equal to 1?" instead of "is this a constant equal to 1?".

title: feat(distributed): pld.system.notify / wait ops + CommContext layout pin (N6)
body:
## Summary

Implements **N6** of the L3 distributed DSL plan(`temp/l3_distributed_implementation_plan.md` §N6): the cross-rank
synchronisation IR surface that pairs with `pld.tile.remote_load`(#1367), plus the compile-time `CommContext` layout pin that the forthcoming N7 codegen path will consume.

After this PR the IR carries:

- `pld.system.notify(target, peer, offsets, value, *, op: NotifyOp)` and `pld.system.wait(signal, offsets, expected, *, cmp: WaitCmp)` ops, both side-effect-only (`UnknownType` result) and rejecting plain `pl.Tensor` for `target` / `signal` (`As<DistributedTensorType>` — exact ObjectKind match per `.claude/rules/ir-kind-traits.md`).
- `NotifyOp.{AtomicAdd, Set}` / `WaitCmp.{Eq, Ge}` enums on the C++ side, exposed at `ir.NotifyOp` / `ir.WaitCmp` and re-exported at `pld.NotifyOp` / `pld.WaitCmp`.
- A `comm_layout::k*` constexpr family (`include/pypto/codegen/distributed/comm_layout.h`) pinning the runtime `CommContext` field offsets at PyPTO build time.

### CommContext layout pin (N6 P0)

`CommContext` is an ABI contract with two parties that never see the runtime header at the same time (see `runtime/src/common/platform_comm/comm_context.h:42-69`): HCCL MESH (`comm_hccl.cpp` `reinterpret_cast`s HCCL's returned device-context pointer as `CommContext*`, sound only if our layout matches HCCL's internal struct) and CCEC-built device kernels (different alignment rules than host `gcc`). The runtime header pins its own layout. PyPTO needs an **independent** mirror because N7 will lower `CommRemotePtr()` with literal byte offsets baked into emitted kernel source — without an independent pin, a runtime header change would flow silently through `offsetof(::CommContext, ...)` and emitted kernels would index the wrong byte with no compile failure anywhere.

`comm_layout.h` sources its values from `offsetof()` and then `static_assert`s them to `16 / 20 / 32 / 544 / 8 / 1056`. The values are also exposed via the new `ir.comm_layout` Python submodule so a regression test can pin them against the literals that N7 codegen will emit — catching the case where the runtime header and the C++ `static_assert`s get edited together but the emit template lags.

### Enum kwarg ABI

Both ops carry their semantics in an `int` kwarg (`op` / `cmp`) rather than a richer attr type. Adding a new enum to the existing `Op::SetAttrType` allowlist would touch `structural_equal` / `structural_hash` / `python_printer` / `serializer` for one bit of surface gain. Instead, bindings translate `nb::enum_<NotifyOp>` / `nb::enum_<WaitCmp>` into `int` in `CreateKwargsFromPyDict`, the C++ deducer validates the int falls within the enum range so codegen can cast back without a separate guard, and the parser refuses raw-int kwargs at the call site — `op=1` is rejected, only `op=pld.NotifyOp.Set` is accepted.

The enums are deliberately **not** exposed via `nb::enum_::export_values()`:
members named `Eq` / `Ge` / `Set` would shadow `ir.Eq` / `ir.Ge` operator classes and the Python `Set` builtin at the `ir` module level. Users access them as `pld.NotifyOp.AtomicAdd` etc.

### Parser dispatch

`pld.system.<op>` joins `pld.tile.<op>` as a 3-segment dispatch path in `ast_parser.py`. `_parse_pld_system_op` delegates to per-op handlers (`_parse_pld_system_notify` / `_parse_pld_system_wait`) to keep each branch under the ruff PLR0912 ceiling. The enum kwarg flows through the existing `_parse_op_kwargs` machinery — attribute-form kwargs resolve against the user closure, so `pld.NotifyOp.AtomicAdd` reaches the parser as the actual `IntEnum` value rather than a textual reference.

### Scope

Codegen lowering (`CommRemotePtr()` emit consuming `comm_layout::k*`, ctx pointer plumbing into incore params, TNOTIFY / TWAIT translation) lands in **N7**. This PR is op-surface only.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/ut/ir/test_distributed_ops.py` — `+10` op-deducer cases for notify / wait (positive, plain-Tensor target rejection, non-scalar peer / expected, offsets rank mismatch, invalid enum int).
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/parser/test_system_ops.py` — new file, 13 cases: DSL→IR lifting for both ops (incl. arg / kwarg packing), missing kwarg / unknown kwarg / zero positional / plain-Tensor target / non-enum kwarg rejections, unknown sub-op routing.
- [x] `tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_comm_layout.py` — 2 cases pinning the binding-exposed constants against the literal contract values, plus a cross-check that `windowsIn` spans exactly `64 × WINDOW_SLOT_STRIDE`.
- [x] Full `tests/ut/ir/` + `tests/ut/codegen/distributed/` regression: 3267 passed, 27 skipped, 0 failed.
- [x] `python tests/lint/clang_tidy.py --diff-base HEAD` — clean.
- [x] pre-commit (clang-format / cpplint / ruff / pyright) — all pass.

## References

- Design and implementation plan: `temp/l3_distributed_design.md` §1, `temp/l3_distributed_implementation_plan.md` §N6
- Parallel: #1369 (`CollectCommGroups` pass + `WindowBuffer` visitor wire-up, N4)
- Prior in series: #1367 (`pld.tile.remote_load`, N6 first op)

title: fix(codegen): restore dynamic dim Vars from shape expressions in kernel wrapper
body:
When a tensor parameter's shape contains an expression that references
a dynamic Var (e.g. `BATCH * 128`, `batch_padded`), the kernel-wrapper
arg-unpacker has to recover the Var's runtime value from the tensor's
``shapes[]`` array. Two pieces are needed:

1. Collect Vars recursively from shape expression trees (PTO codegen).
2. Invert the expression against the runtime shape (wrapper codegen).

Codegen-side (`src/codegen/pto/pto_codegen.cpp`):
- Recursively collect Vars across BinaryExpr / UnaryExpr / Call /
  TupleGetItemExpr / Cast, preserving first-seen order.
- Reserve trailing ``%argN`` names from the same recursive collection
  (``ShapeExprVarKey``, aligned with ``PTOCodegen::GetVarKey``).

Wrapper-side (`python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py`):
- Module-level collectors/inverters; two-phase walk to prefer invertible
  sources when the same Var appears in multiple tensor shapes.
- Invert single-var affine forms: ``var``, ``var +/-/*// const_int``,
  and ``const_int * var`` for multiplication.
- Raise ``ValueError`` when no invertible source exists (no silent fallback
  to raw ``shapes[i]``, which would assign wrong values and cause OOB).
- Dedup by ``Var.unique_id``.

Bindings: expose ``Var.unique_id``.

Tests (`tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen.py`):
- Mixed invertibility, non-invertible ``BATCH * BATCH``, const-left mul,
  multi-var shape ``[BATCH, HEAD, static]``, affine +/-/*//, SPMD pl.dynamic
  rows on pass-pipeline ``spmd_kernel`` (not hand-built IR only).

title: feat(manual_scope): orthogonal auto/explicit-dep DSL (deps=, pl.at deps=, manual_dep=True)
body:
## Summary

Aligns the PyPTO DSL with the runtime's orthogonal dep model. The runtime has two independent mechanisms:

1. **Auto-dep opt-out** (3 granularities, all orthogonal to each other):
   - `with pl.manual_scope():` — scope-wide
   - `pl.create_tensor(..., manual_dep=True)` — tensor-lifetime
   - `pl.no_dep(t)` at a kernel-call arg — single-task per arg
2. **Explicit edges** — `pl.submit(..., deps=[...])` / `pl.at(..., deps=) as tid`

Final task fanin = *auto-tracked deps* ∪ *explicit deps*. The two mechanisms are orthogonal: explicit edges work even when auto-dep tracking is active. Before this PR the language surface conflated them — `deps=` was gated on `manual_scope`, the `pl.at`-style block API had no edge surface at all, and `manual_dep=True` was documented as Internal-only.

Three commits, each independent:

**1. `refactor(manual_scope): make pl.submit deps= orthogonal to manual_scope`**

Lifts the parser/codegen requirement that `pl.submit(..., deps=[...])` only be legal inside `with pl.manual_scope():`. Explicit edges are now independent of the auto-tracking opt-out; use one, the other, or both.

**2. `feat(language): pl.at(..., deps=) as tid: DSL surface`**

Adds the `pl.at`-block analogue of `pl.submit`'s deps= surface. `pl.at(level=CORE_GROUP)` blocks are outlined-kernel-and-call sites; this PR threads explicit dep edges + a TaskId capture through them:

```python
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP) as tid_a:
    ...                                     # body becomes an outlined InCore kernel
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, deps=[tid_a]) as tid_b:
    ...                                     # consumer waits on tid_a's task
```

Implementation: adds `attrs_` (key-value vector) to `ScopeStmt` mirroring `ForStmt::attrs_`; introduces `kAttrTaskIdVar` carrying a `VarPtr`. The parser emits a placeholder `AssignStmt(tid, system.task_invalid())` *before* the scope to satisfy SSA's def-before-use rule; the outliner drops the placeholder once the real `AssignStmt(tid, TupleGetItem(ret, N))` is synthesised from the kernel call's augmented return tuple `(result, TaskId)`.

**3. `feat(language): promote pl.create_tensor(..., manual_dep=True) to user-facing`**

Rewrites the `manual_dep` docstring from "Internal-only" to describe its place as the tensor-lifetime granularity in the three-knob auto-dep opt-out model. The IR / codegen / runtime path already handled it end-to-end (`InjectGMPipeBuffer` has used it internally since #1208); only the docstring gate was missing. Adds a user-facing codegen regression verifying `TensorCreateInfo` emits the trailing `/*manual_dep=*/true`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/ut/language/parser/test_manual_scope_parsing.py` — manual_scope / pl.submit / pl.at deps parsing
- [x] `pytest tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py` — orchestration codegen, incl. new `test_tensor_create_with_manual_dep`
- [x] `pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_inject_gm_pipe_buffer.py` — internal `manual_dep` consumer pass unaffected

title: fix(arith): match structurally-equal subexprs in pattern matcher
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1377. The IR failed to fold `i - (i - 1) = 1` in range-slice bounds, so `tensor[i - 1 : i, ...]` kept a symbolic row dim and `pl.col_expand_mul` failed its static-row-dim check at op verification.

Root cause sits in the pattern matcher, not in any algebraic identity:

- `PEqualChecker<ExprPtr>` compared expressions by **pointer identity** (with a constant-leaf fallback for `ConstInt`/`ConstBool`), so when a `PVar<ExprPtr>` rebound to a second occurrence it required pointer equality.
- The parser inserts a **fresh `cast(scalar, INDEX)` Call** at every use of a non-INDEX scalar in a slice-bound context, so the extent expression for `tensor[ctx_len - 1 : ctx_len]` is `Sub(Cast1, Sub(Cast2, 1))` with two structurally-equal but pointer-distinct `Cast` children.
- The rewriter applied `x - (y - z) => (x + z) - y` (different PVars, no equality needed), but the follow-up `(x + y) - x => y` rebinding check then failed pointer identity on Cast1 vs Cast2 and the extent stayed symbolic.

Fix: fall back to `structural_equal` (from `pypto/ir/transforms/structural_comparison.h`) after the pointer-identity and constant-leaf fast paths, with an early kind-mismatch short-circuit to keep the rewrite hot path cheap.

## Testing

- [x] New regression test `test_sub_structurally_equal_compound_subexprs` in `tests/ut/ir/arith/test_rewrite_simplify.py` — mirrors the parser-built shape with two distinct `cast(c, INDEX)` Call nodes.
- [x] Full `tests/ut/ir/` suite: 3243 passed, 27 skipped (was 3242 + the new test), 0 regressions.
- [x] End-to-end reproduction from the issue (`rope_cos[ctx_len - 1 : ctx_len, 0:8]` + `pl.col_expand_mul`) now compiles cleanly; `cos_row` shape becomes `pl.Tensor[[1, 8], pl.FP32]`.
- [x] clang-tidy clean on the diff.

## Related Issues

Fixes #1377

title: feat(distributed): pld.get_comm_ctx + dist_t.comm.rank/.nranks desugar (N5)
body:
## Summary

Lands the **N5** stage of the L3 distributed implementation plan
(`temp/l3_distributed_implementation_plan.md` §N5): the ``CommContext``
accessor IR surface that lets InCore kernels read ``rankId`` / ``rankNum``
from the comm group that owns a ``DistributedTensor``.

After this PR the IR carries:

* ``CommCtxType`` — singleton marker type (no per-instance fields, mirrors
  ``WindowBufferType`` / ``MemRefType``). Different comm groups are
  distinguished by the ``DistributedTensor`` that spawned the
  ``get_comm_ctx`` call, not by the result type.
* ``pld.get_comm_ctx(target) -> CommCtxType`` — verifier refuses plain
  ``pl.Tensor`` (``As<DistributedTensorType>`` exact ObjectKind match per
  `.claude/rules/ir-kind-traits.md`).
* ``pld.comm_ctx.rank(ctx)`` / ``pld.comm_ctx.nranks(ctx) -> Scalar<INT32>``
  — verifier refuses anything that isn't ``CommCtxType``.

### Parser desugar

`parse_attribute` learns two distributed-DSL patterns dispatched on the LHS
IR type:

* ``dist_t.comm`` (LHS = ``DistributedTensorType``) lifts to
  ``pld.get_comm_ctx(dist_t)``.
* ``ctx.rank`` / ``ctx.nranks`` (LHS = ``CommCtxType``) lift to the
  matching field-read op.

User code reads as a Python attribute chain (``data.comm.rank``) while the
IR sees explicit op calls. Unknown attributes on either type raise
``ParserTypeError`` with specific guidance rather than the generic
\"standalone attribute access not supported\" error.

The IR-type dispatch is critical: any alias of a ``DistributedTensor``
(function parameter, ``pld.window(...)`` result, threaded-through tensor
argument) routes through the same desugar — the lookup keys off the IR
type, not on the textual name.

### Codegen note (scope)

This PR is the IR surface only. The handle gets reified at codegen time
into a synthesised incore ctx pointer keyed by ``group_idx`` of the source
``WindowBuffer`` (filled in by ``CollectCommGroups`` in #1369). The actual
byte-offset reads against ``CommContext.rankId`` / ``rankNum`` (offsets
pinned in ``include/pypto/codegen/distributed/comm_layout.h``) land in **N6
codegen**, not here.

## Test plan

- [x] ``tests/ut/ir/test_distributed_ops.py`` (+8 cases): CommCtxType
  singleton, get_comm_ctx return type, plain-Tensor rejection, no-kwargs
  rejection, comm_ctx.rank/nranks return INT32, non-ctx arg rejection.
- [x] ``tests/ut/ir/parser/test_dist_tensor_comm.py`` (new, 6 cases):
  ``dist_t.comm.rank`` / ``.nranks`` chain lifting, composability with
  arithmetic (``data.comm.rank + data.comm.rank`` produces 2 calls), plain
  ``pl.Tensor.comm`` rejection, unknown attribute on ``DistributedTensor``
  / ``CommCtx`` rejection.
- [x] Full ``tests/ut/ir/`` regression: 3268 passed, 27 skipped, 0 failed.
- [x] pre-commit (clang-format / cpplint / ruff / pyright) all pass.

## References

- Plan: ``temp/l3_distributed_implementation_plan.md`` §N5
- Design: ``temp/l3_distributed_design.md`` §2.1.1
- Required by N6 codegen (#1379, paused awaiting this PR): provides the
  ``dist_t.comm.rank`` parse path so end-to-end allreduce programs can be
  written.

title: Add incore-profiling skill: msprof op-simulator kernel profiler
body:
## Summary

Adds an **incore-profiling** skill: cycle-accurate, per-pipe (CUBE / VECTOR / MTE) in-core profiling of any PTOAS kernel via the Ascend `msprof op simulator` (camodel).

- **`incore_profile.py`** — orchestrates `generate → build → camodel → collect` per kernel, with a TL-capable-CANN preflight and degenerate-trace detection.
- **`gen_profiling_case.py`** — a compact, `.pto`-driven testcase generator. It reads the kernel ABI from the one `__global__`/`_aic` line in the `.cpp` and sizes every GM buffer from the sibling `.pto`'s static `make_tensor_view` shapes, then emits `main.cpp` / `launch.cpp` (`<<<1, …>>>` single-core) / `CMakeLists.txt` / `golden.py`. Mixed cube+vector kernels get a trivial merged `__global__` dispatcher (`#if __DAV_CUBE__ → _aic`, `#if __DAV_VEC__ → _aiv`).
- **`SKILL.md`** — usage, prerequisites (needs the kernel's sibling `.pto`), caveats for data-dependent kernels, and trace-output conventions.

Pairs with `pypto.tools.clean_sim_trace` (already in `main`) to turn the raw `visualize_data.bin` into a de-cluttered per-pipe trace + `instr_metrics.json`.

## Validation

title: feat(runtime/debug): one-command replay of build_output via debug/run.py
body:
## Summary

Closes #1327 via Option B — a dedicated `pypto.runtime.debug` replay path,
plus an auto-emitted `debug/run.py` so that re-executing any
`build_output/<jit_dir>/` is always **one command**:

```bash
python build_output/<jit_dir>/debug/run.py
```

No more hand-rolling a `SceneTestCase` wrapper, re-deriving `signature`
lists from the orchestration cpp, or re-running the slow IR-compile path
just to reproduce a runtime bug pinned to a specific build_output.

### What's in this PR

- **`pypto.runtime.debug.replay`** — re-execute an existing build_output
  directly from its on-disk `kernel_config.py`. Supports `--validate`
  against a sibling `golden.py`, `--log-level` for runtime verbosity,
  and skips the front-end IR compile entirely (the bug-under-test
  artefact is never regenerated).
- **`golden.py` generation** — `ir.compile()` now writes a self-contained
  `golden.py` next to the build_output with `generate_inputs()` +
  `compute_golden()`. Callable globals referenced by the source program
  are inlined so the generated file is import-clean.
- **`debug/run.py` auto-emission** — `CompiledProgram` /
  `DistributedCompiledProgram` write a thin runner that calls
  `replay`, materialises inputs (from `golden.generate_inputs()` when
  available, else from shape/dtype metadata for the JIT path), and
  validates against `compute_golden`. JIT path additionally exposes a
  `_user_compare(<param_names>)` hook for hand-rolled
  `torch.allclose` assertions.
- **CLI lifted into `replay._main`** — the emitted `debug/run.py` is now
  a thin shim that forwards `sys.argv` to `replay._main` with three
  keyword hooks (`inline_inputs`, `user_compare`, `default_platform`).
  Adding a new replay flag no longer requires a parallel edit in
  `run_script_writer`; `--validate` is `BooleanOptionalAction` so
  `--no-validate` is discoverable via `--help`. A drift test asserts
  the generated shim cannot silently re-grow an argparse block.
- **Edit-`.pto`-and-replay** — when `ptoas/<unit>.pto` is newer than
  its sibling `.cpp`, replay reruns `ptoas` and splices the
  preprocessed body into matching `kernels/<core>/<func>.cpp` between
  `BEGIN`/`END` sentinels, then rebuilds the `.so`. Sentinel format
  and the preprocess pipeline are guarded by drift tests against
  `pto_backend`. Opt out via `--no-rebuild-from-pto` or
  `PYPTO_REBUILD_FROM_PTO=0`.
- Toggle: `PYPTO_EMIT_DEBUG_RUNNER=0` disables emission globally for
  bulk-compile pipelines (the `replay` CLI is still usable directly).
- Docs (`docs/{en,zh-cn}/dev/03-runtime-dfx.md`) describe the workflow.
- Tests in `tests/ut/runtime/` and `tests/ut/backend/`.

### Relationship to #1327

The issue suggested two options. This PR ships **Option B** (a runtime
replay entrypoint) because it does not require freezing a new contract
into `kernel_config.py` codegen — the `signature` / `CALLABLE` shape
proposed in Option A would have been a heavier external-API change.
The same end-user pain point is solved: re-running an existing
build_output no longer needs manual wrapping.

## Testing

- [x] `tests/ut/runtime/test_run_script_writer.py` — emitted script
      shape, env-var gating, `_user_compare` placement on JIT path only,
      drift guard against argparse/RunConfig re-appearing in the shim
- [x] `tests/ut/runtime/test_replay.py` — golden / replay coverage,
      `_main` keyword-hook contracts (inline fallback, user_compare vs
      golden validation, default_platform baking)
- [x] `tests/ut/runtime/test_pto_rebuild.py` — pto->cpp splice path,
      staleness detection, sentinel matching
- [x] `tests/ut/backend/test_ptoas_sentinels_match.py` — drift guard
      tying sentinel format to `pto_backend`
- [x] Doc updates kept in lockstep (en + zh)

## Related Issues

Closes #1327

title: [Bug] Flaky CI: test_paged_attention_spmd_ptoas[64-64-256-64-8192-32768] intermittently fails with Ascend AICPU runtime errors
body:
### Component

Other (please specify in description) — CI infrastructure / Ascend runtime environment on the self-hosted `npu-1` runner.

### Description

`tests/st/codegen/test_paged_attention_spmd.py::TestPagedAttentionSpmdKernels::test_paged_attention_spmd_ptoas[64-64-256-64-8192-32768]` (a.k.a. `paged_attention_spmd_64bat_64h_256d_64bs_8192ctx_ptoas`) intermittently fails the `system-tests` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

When this test fails, it typically takes down a large cascade of subsequent real-device system tests (50+) on the same runner with the same Ascend AICPU stream-creation errors, suggesting the runner enters a stuck device state and cannot recover within the job. The simulator job (`system-tests-a5sim`) is unaffected, so the issue is specific to the real-NPU runner, not the test code or codegen.

### Steps to Reproduce

The failure is non-deterministic; re-running the same job often passes. To observe:

1. Push any branch to a PR (or merge to main) so the `system-tests` job runs on the self-hosted `npu-1` runner.
2. Inspect the `Test system tests` step in the `system-tests` job.
3. With some probability, `test_paged_attention_spmd_ptoas[64-64-256-64-8192-32768]` fails first, followed by cascading `prepare_callable failed with code 507899` failures across the rest of the suite.

Observed instances:

- PR #1384 re-run [`26007737111` (2026-05-18)](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/actions/runs/26007737111/job/76442255905) — flake (first fail = this test)
- main run [`25910733455` (2026-05-15)](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/actions/runs/25910733455) on commit `37cfb1f1` — same Ascend error signatures

### Expected Behavior

`test_paged_attention_spmd_ptoas[64-64-256-64-8192-32768]` either passes consistently, or — if a known device-state issue exists — the runner cleanup hooks reset the NPU before the job starts so a single bad run doesn't cascade through the whole suite.

### Actual Behavior

The test fails with:

```
E   AssertionError: SPMD paged attention test failed:
    RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
[ERROR] run: [device_runner.cpp:748] aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
[ERROR] validate_runtime_impl: [runtime_maker.cpp:350] PTO2 runtime failed:
        orch_error_code=2 sched_error_code=0 runtime_status=-2
```

After this first failure the device enters a state where every subsequent test fails to set up a stream:

```
E   RuntimeError: prepare_callable failed with code 507899
[ERROR] configure_aicore_op_timeout: [device_runner.cpp:302]
        aclrtSetOpExecuteTimeOutV2(1000000 us) failed: 507901
[ERROR] prepare_run_context: [device_runner.cpp:388]
        rtStreamCreate (AICPU) failed: 507899
```

(Error codes 507018 / 507899 / 507901 are Ascend ACL runtime errors centred on AICPU stream setup and operator timeout configuration.)

### Git Commit ID

37cfb1f1d44e04b75a3d1dfbaea2b0cd0bb5bf9f

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Runner: self-hosted `npu-1` (`liteserver-hps-365a-00001`), CANN 9.0.0, runtime image `localhost:5000/ci-device-py310:latest`.
- `system-tests-a5sim` (simulator) passes the same suite, confirming the failure is hardware/driver-state-bound rather than test/codegen logic.
- Possible mitigations to investigate: pre-job NPU reset (`npu-smi`), retry-on-507018, or skipping the SPMD test on real hardware until the root cause is identified.

title: test(st): add hand-written L3 over L2-only PyPTO program
body:
## Summary

Adds an ST that covers the pattern where PyPTO compiles only the chip (L2) layer and the user describes the L3 layer directly via simpler's `Worker` / `TaskArgs` API — no HOST DSL, no generated `host_orch.py` / `sub_workers/*.py`.

The test pins the public boundary that PyPTO's own `DistributedCompiledProgram` already relies on:

- `compile_and_assemble(out_dir, platform)` → `ChipCallable` from an L2 build
- `Worker(level=3, ...)` with manual `register` / `init` / `run`
- `TaskArgs` + `make_tensor_arg` + `TensorArgType` for argument marshalling
- A Python SubWorker that **closes over host-side state** (`done_flag`) — a capability the DSL form (`@pl.function(level=HOST, role=SubWorker)`) cannot express because its body is captured as `InlineStmt` and only sees module globals

Computation: `f = a + b`; a closure-captured SubWorker validates the result on the host side and flips a shared-memory flag the test asserts on, proving both the device write and the SubWorker side-effect.

## Why

This complements the existing `test_l3_distributed.py` (DSL-driven L3 generated by PyPTO) by exercising the opposite end of the spectrum: PyPTO emits only L2 artefacts and the caller owns L3. The two together fix the contract on both sides, so future refactors to `compile_and_assemble` / the runner glue (`_tensor_from_continuous`, `make_tensor_arg`) cannot silently break callers that bypass `DistributedCompiledProgram`.

## Test Plan

- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/st/distributed/test_l3_manual.py -v` passes on a host with at least one device
- [ ] Test is collected by pytest discovery (verified locally via `--collect-only`)
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks pass (ruff check, ruff format, pyright)

title: fix(simplify): fold dead if-guards keyed on loop-affine scalars
body:
## Summary

An always-false branch guard such as `if o0 == 0`, where `o0 = ob_idx * 256 + 256` and `ob_idx` is a loop variable, survived the Simplify pass. The qwen3 `down_proj` chunk guard `if o0__ssa_v2_1 == 0` is the motivating regression.

Two restrictions blocked the fold — the analyzer never learned the scalar's range:

1. The `AssignStmt` handler only bound scalars whose RHS was a literal constant, so a symbolic affine value was never registered.
2. `MultiAssignCollector` flagged *every* assignment inside a loop body or branch as unsafe, so a loop-body scalar landed in `multi_assigned_` regardless.

## Changes

- **`AssignStmt`** registers any single-assigned scalar with the analyzer. A constant at function-body top level is bound fully (literal substituted into uses); a symbolic RHS — or a constant inside a loop/branch — contributes only a `ConstIntBound`, enough to prove dead guards without inlining the scalar.
- **`MultiAssignCollector`** now flags only genuinely reassigned vars; the over-broad nesting check is removed.
- **Scoped unbinding** — analyzer scalar bindings are logged and unbound when the mutator leaves the `For`/`If`/`While`/`Spmd` region they were made in, keeping the fold sound for pre-SSA callers.
- **`scope_depth_` gate** keeps full constant substitution at function-body top level, preserving existing constant-propagation behavior and avoiding a printer roundtrip gap for in-loop literals.
- Drops the unused `tensor_view_semantics.h` include; updates the Simplify pass docs (en + zh-cn).

Verified end-to-end on the qwen3 decode model: `down_proj`'s always-false second-chunk guard is folded away (else-branch lifted into the loop) while the legitimate first-chunk guard is kept, and the scalar is not inlined.

## Testing

- [x] All tests pass — `tests/ut/` 4824 passed, 27 skipped
- [x] New regression test `test_always_false_via_loop_affine_scalar`
- [x] Code review completed
- [x] clang-tidy clean
- [x] Documentation updated (en + zh-cn `05-simplify.md`)

title: fix(printer): print non-INDEX integer constants with explicit dtype
body:
## Summary

`ConstInt` with `DEFAULT_CONST_INT` (= `INT64`) and `INDEX` both printed as
bare integers, collapsing two distinct dtypes into identical text. Since the
parser reconstructs `INDEX` from a bare integer literal, a typed `INT64`
literal could not round-trip through print → reparse — e.g. a `tensor.write`
value into an `INT64` tensor, where the op deducer requires an exact dtype
match (`src/ir/op/tensor_ops/memory.cpp:601`).

- **Printer fix** (`python_printer.cpp`, `VisitExpr_(ConstIntPtr)`): make
  `python_print` injective over integer constants — only `INDEX` prints bare;
  every other integer dtype (`INT64` included) prints as explicit
  `pl.const(value, pl.<DTYPE>)`. The parser already round-trips that form, so
  no parser change is needed.
- **Test fixtures**: migrate hand-built test IR that used `INT64` for
  index / offset / loop-bound constants to the canonical `INDEX` dtype
  (shape dims, MemRef byte-offsets, range bounds). Assertions are unchanged —
  these correct non-canonical fixtures to match what the parser produces.
- **Regression test**: add a print → reparse fixed-point test for an `INT64`
  literal as a `tensor.write` value.
- **Docs**: document that bare literals are `INDEX`-typed and other dtypes use
  `pl.const(...)` (EN + zh-CN).

## Testing

- [x] All tests pass (`tests/ut/`: 4824 passed, 0 failed)
- [x] Code review completed
- [x] clang-tidy passed on the C++ change
- [x] Documentation updated (EN + zh-CN synchronized)

title: [Bug] Orchestration codegen silently drops `return Call(...)` (no intermediate var)
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

`OrchestrationCodegen::VisitStmt_(const ReturnStmtPtr&)` in [`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:976`](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/blob/main/src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp#L976) is a no-op (comment: "return tensors are already make_tensor_external"). When a chip Orchestration function body is just `return self.kernel(...)` — a direct Call wrapped in a ReturnStmt with no intermediate variable — the wrapped Call expression is never visited, so the kernel dispatch is silently dropped from the generated chip orchestration. The emitted `aicpu_orchestration_entry` ends up with an empty `PTO2_SCOPE()` body.

Compounding factor: `FlattenCallExpr` ([`src/ir/transforms/flatten_call_expr_pass.cpp`](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/blob/main/src/ir/transforms/flatten_call_expr_pass.cpp)) does not normalize `ReturnStmt(Call(...))` into `AssignStmt(tmp, Call); ReturnStmt(tmp)`. It only flattens calls nested inside other expressions (args, conditions, binop operands, loop bounds), so `return Call(...)` survives the pass untouched and reaches codegen in the unhandled shape.

The convention used across the codebase (`tests/st/distributed/test_l3_distributed.py`, `tests/st/runtime/test_ci.py`, ...) is to always bind the call to a local first, so this bug stays hidden — but any user who writes the more idiomatic Python form hits a silently-broken compile.

Fix options:

1. `FlattenCallExpr` should normalize `ReturnStmt(Call)` → `AssignStmt(tmp, Call); ReturnStmt(tmp)`. This preserves three-address form for downstream passes too.
2. Or `OrchestrationCodegen::VisitStmt_(ReturnStmt)` should visit and emit the wrapped Call for its side effects.

Option (1) is preferable since other passes also assume three-address form.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Define a chip orchestration that directly returns the kernel call (no intermediate):

   ```python
   @pl.program
   class Prog:
       @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
       def tile_add(self, a, b, f):
           ta = pl.load(a, [0, 0], [128, 128])
           tb = pl.load(b, [0, 0], [128, 128])
           tf = pl.add(ta, tb)
           return pl.store(tf, [0, 0], f)

       @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
       def chip_orch(self, a, b, f):
           return self.tile_add(a, b, f)   # direct return — bug
   ```

2. Compile: `ir.compile(Prog, output_dir=out, platform="a2a3")`
3. Inspect `out/orchestration/chip_orch.cpp` — the `PTO2_SCOPE()` body is empty (no `rt_submit_aiv_task` call).
4. Run on hardware via Worker(level=3) / Worker(level=2) — the chip immediately fails with `RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018` (`aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed`).

This was hit in CI for PR #1389 (`tests/st/distributed/test_l3_manual.py::TestL3Manual::test_manual_l3`); rewriting the body as `out_f = self.tile_add(a, b, f); return out_f` made the same test pass on identical hardware.

### Expected Behavior

Either:

- `FlattenCallExpr` rewrites `ReturnStmt(Call)` to `AssignStmt(tmp, Call); ReturnStmt(tmp)` so codegen sees a normalized form; or
- `OrchestrationCodegen` emits the kernel dispatch for any `Call` nested inside `ReturnStmt`.

Generated `chip_orch.cpp` should contain the kernel dispatch (`rt_submit_aiv_task` / `rt_submit_aic_task`) regardless of whether the user bound the call to a temp first.

### Actual Behavior

The generated `chip_orch.cpp` looks like:

```c++
void aicpu_orchestration_entry(const ChipStorageTaskArgs& orch_args) {
    Tensor ext_a = from_tensor_arg(orch_args.tensor(0));
    Tensor ext_b = from_tensor_arg(orch_args.tensor(1));
    Tensor ext_f = from_tensor_arg(orch_args.tensor(2));

    PTO2_SCOPE() {
    }
}
```

The kernel dispatch is missing entirely. Running this on hardware reports:

```
[ERROR] run: [device_runner.cpp:748] aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
[ERROR] validate_runtime_impl: [runtime_maker.cpp:350] PTO2 runtime failed: orch_error_code=0 sched_error_code=100 runtime_status=-100
RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
```

### Git Commit ID

a45791d39e89807a1dd78bcfda819c7c91e29326

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Symptom is hardware-visible (AICPU sync timeout), but root cause is a pure codegen / IR-normalization bug — the generated `.cpp` is wrong regardless of platform.
- Related (different bugs in the same codegen path): #631 (drops return values for Scalar tuple elements), #1184 (missing aliases for InOut tensors).
- Surfaced while debugging the CI failure in #1389; that PR worked around the bug at the test level (use `out = self.kernel(...); return out`) and intentionally left this issue for a separate fix.

title: fix(ir): unary tile ops must propagate input TileView.valid_shape
body:
## Summary

Unary tile-op type deducers (`DeduceTileUnaryType`, `DeduceTileRsqrtType`, `DeduceTileCastType`, and the inline lambda for `tile.not`) were setting the result `TileView.valid_shape` to `tile_type->shape_` (the static allocation shape), discarding any `valid_shape` carried by the input tile. As a result, a chain like

```python
valid_tile     = pl.slice(x, [16, 8], [0, 0], valid_shape=[16, 4])
valid_scaled   = pl.tile.muls(valid_tile, 0.5)   # valid_shape preserved (binary path was correct)
valid_neg      = pl.tile.neg(valid_scaled)       # valid_shape dropped (this bug)
```

produced `TNEG(dst[validCol=8], src[validCol=4])` on NPU and returned garbage data on Ascend 910B (`a2a3sim` happened to mask the bug).

## Fix

- Promote the file-local `GetValidShape` helper out of `src/ir/op/tile_ops/elementwise.cpp` into `include/pypto/ir/type_inference.h` as an `inline` function, alongside `InheritTileViewLayout`.
- Replace the four `tile_view.valid_shape = tile_type->shape_` sites in `src/ir/op/tile_ops/unary.cpp` with `GetValidShape(tile_type)`, so the result inherits the input's `valid_shape` if present and falls back to the static shape otherwise. This covers `tile.neg`, `tile.exp`, `tile.recip`, `tile.sqrt`, `tile.log`, `tile.abs`, `tile.relu`, `tile.sin`, `tile.cos`, `tile.rsqrt`, `tile.cast`, and `tile.not` — matching the scalar-binary path (`tile.muls`, `tile.adds`, ...) that was already correct.

## Testing

- [x] New regression tests in `tests/ut/ir/operators/test_tile_ops.py` cover `tile.neg`, `tile.exp`, `tile.cast`, `tile.rsqrt`, and `tile.not`. Each test feeds a `tile.slice(..., valid_shape=[8, 4])` (under static shape `[8, 16]`) into the unary op and asserts the result `tile_view.valid_shape` is preserved.
- [x] Local suite (`tests/ut/ir/operators/`, `tests/ut/ir/transforms/`, `tests/ut/codegen/`): 1986 passed, 25 skipped, no regressions.
- [x] pre-commit (clang-format, cpplint, ruff, pyright) passes.

## Related Issues

Fixes #1370

title: feat(codegen): compile multiple L2 Orchestrations in one program
body:
## Summary

A PyPTO program can already define more than one L2 ``Orchestration``
function, but only the first one used to be compiled — ``_generate_single_chip``
silently picked the head orch via ``next(...)`` and dropped the rest. This PR
makes every L2 orch in a program compile and become independently callable
without requiring an L3 HOST wrapper.

### Codegen

Top-level ``generate()`` now detects ``orch_count > 1`` and dispatches to a
new ``_generate_multi_chip``, which emits each Orchestration as a
self-contained sub-build under ``next_levels/{orch_name}/`` — the same
layout ``_generate_with_distributed`` already produces for the chip tier
of L3+ programs. ``host_orch.py`` / ``sub_workers/`` are intentionally
not emitted because there is no L3 host driver.

### User-facing API

``CompiledProgram`` grows a sub-dispatch surface so callers can choose
which orch to run:

```python
compiled = ir.compile(MyTwoOrchProgram)
compiled.orchestration_names           # ['chip_orch_add', 'chip_orch_sub']
compiled.chip_orch_add(a, b, f_add)    # attribute lookup
compiled['chip_orch_sub'](a, b, f_sub) # subscript lookup
compiled(a, b, f)                      # TypeError — asks user to pick
```

Single-orch programs are unchanged; ``compiled(...)`` still works as
before.

### Refactor

``_extract_param_infos``, ``_build_full_args``, ``_validate_device_tensor``
and the per-call dispatch body are extracted into module-level helpers
(``_extract_func_param_infos`` / ``_invoke_compiled``) so the single-orch
``CompiledProgram.__call__`` and the new multi-orch ``_SubChipCallable.__call__``
share one path.

## Testing

- ``tests/ut/ir/test_compiled_program.py``: updated import to use the
  newly module-level ``_build_full_args``. All existing single-orch unit
  tests continue to pass (38/38).
- ``tests/st/distributed/test_l2_multi_orch.py`` *(new)*:
  - ``test_codegen_emits_per_orch_subdirs`` — verifies both orchs land
    in ``next_levels/<name>/`` with the right kernels and that no flat
    ``orchestration/`` directory is left at the root.
  - ``test_dispatch_surface`` — covers ``compiled.orchestration_names``,
    subscript / attribute access, and the error paths
    (``compiled(...)`` rejection, ``KeyError`` for unknown orch,
    ``AttributeError`` for unknown attribute that doesn't shadow an orch).
  - ``test_execute_both_orchs_on_device`` — gated on ``--device`` and
    ``not --codegen-only``; compiles with ptoas and dispatches both
    orchs through subscript and attribute access, asserting their
    outputs are independent and correct.

## Test plan

- [x] Codegen + dispatch surface tests pass under ``--codegen-only`` on macOS
- [x] Full unit-test sweep on ``tests/ut/ir/test_compiled_program.py`` (38 passing)
- [x] Rebased onto upstream main; adopts new ``execute_compiled(dfx=..., block_dim=..., aicpu_thread_num=...)`` signature
- [ ] On-device execution of ``test_execute_both_orchs_on_device`` on a host with Ascend toolchain + ``--device``

title: fix(ir): flatten Call out of ReturnStmt in FlattenCallExpr (#1394)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1394. `FlattenCallExpr` left `ReturnStmt(Call(...))` untouched, and `OrchestrationCodegen::VisitStmt_(ReturnStmtPtr)` is a no-op — so the idiomatic Python form `return self.kernel(...)` silently produced an empty `PTO2_SCOPE()` body and crashed on hardware (`aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018`).

Implements the issue's preferred option (option 1): normalize at the IR layer so downstream passes / codegen never see a `Call` wrapped directly in a `ReturnStmt`.

## Changes

- `src/ir/transforms/flatten_call_expr_pass.cpp`
  - Added `VisitStmt_(ReturnStmtPtr)` override — extracts any `Call` value into an `AssignStmt` temp via the existing `ExtractCallToTemp` mechanism.
