title: fix(memory_reuse): allow reuse between no-view and storage-trivial-view tiles
body:
## Summary

`AreTileTypesCompatible` rejected reuse whenever one tile carried a `TileView` and the other did not (`has_view1 != has_view2`). After `SplitVectorKernel` the two **mutually-exclusive** arms of a dual-AIV dispatch `if` are structural clones, but one arm's tiles carry a trivial `valid_shape` view while the other's carry none. The presence mismatch blocked any cross-arm reuse, so every `[M, N]` intermediate (e.g. the FlashAttention online-softmax `oi` recurrence) got its own vec slot, inflating UB usage.

A tile with no `TileView` has default physical storage (contiguous, zero offset, row-major / none-box, default fractal, no pad). A tile whose view sets only `valid_shape` (all storage fields at their defaults) is physically identical. This PR recognises that via a new `IsStorageTrivialTileView` helper and treats the two as storage-compatible. `valid_shape` is per-use metadata already excluded from storage identity (and already allowed to differ for 2D tiles).

Lifetime, transitive-overlap and in-place-safety checks are untouched — this only enables provably-safe reuse, never bypasses interference checks.

On a fused FlashAttention decode kernel this collapses the cross-arm vec allocation (8 → 4 of the 32KB `oi` slots), cutting vec memref usage from ~290KB to ~145KB.

> Note: this addresses the MemoryReuse mechanism described in #1547. The kernel's remaining over-budget vec usage comes from the C2V cross-core pipe ring buffer (separate subsystem), which is out of scope here — hence `Refs` rather than `Fixes`.

## Testing

- New regression test `TestValidShapeDivergence::test_view_present_vs_absent_can_reuse` (a view tile and a later no-view tile with non-overlapping lifetimes now share one MemRef).
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_memory_reuse.py`: 43 passed.
- Full `tests/ut/ir/transforms/`: 1346 passed, 26 skipped — no regressions.
- Docs updated (`docs/en` + `docs/zh-cn` `29-memory_reuse.md`).

## Related Issues

Refs #1547

title: fix(pto_codegen): keep IfStmt tensor return_vars out of scf.if results
body:
## Summary

A scratch tensor written inside an `if`-branch (e.g. via `pl.assemble`) becomes an SCF-if phi after control-flow lowering. PTO codegen routed such `TensorType` `IfStmt` return_vars through `scf.if` **results**, which retyped them to a fully-dynamic `!pto.tensor_view<?x?>` and dropped the concrete memref dims. A later `pto.partition_view` on that phi tensor was then rejected by ptoas:

```
'pto.partition_view' op operand #0 must be , but got 'memref<?x?xf32, strided<[?, ?], offset: ?>>'
```

`partition_view` on function-parameter views (also printed `<?x?>`) works because each has a `pto.make_tensor_view` carrying concrete `shape`/`strides` operands that ptoas resolves to a concrete memref. The scf.if phi result has no such concretizing op, so its memref stays fully dynamic.

## Fix

Tensors are mutable references mutated in place — exactly like the existing `ArrayType` / `TileType` `IfStmt` return_vars and like loop-carried tensors in `ForStmt`. Treat them the same:

- Keep `TensorType` `IfStmt` return_vars **out of** `scf.if` results; bind the merged return var to the shared backing `tensor_view` both branches mutate in place, so the concrete `make_tensor_view` flows straight into `partition_view`.
- Normalize tensor yields in the `YieldStmt` visitor to their canonical `tensor_view` (a branch may yield either a stored-into tensor bound to its view, or an unchanged param bound only to its base ptr), so both branches agree on the shared backing SSA. For/While loops keep only scalar yields, so their lowering is unaffected.

## Testing

- [x] Full unit suite: 5255 passed, 28 skipped (no regressions)
- [x] New regression test `tests/ut/codegen/test_if_tensor_return_partition_view.py` — reproduces the cross-`if` phi chain; asserts no `scf.if -> (tensor_view)` results and that `partition_view` sources the concrete base view, not a phi
- [x] code-review passed; clang-tidy clean

## Related Issues

Fixes #1533

title: feat(dsl): add ring_slots knob on pl.split() to size the cross-core ring
body:
## Summary

Closes #1472. Adds a user-facing `ring_slots` knob on `pl.split(...)` so authors of UB-constrained scopes can trade cross-core pipelining depth for buffer footprint:

```python
with pl.at(
    level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP,
    optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN, ring_slots=2)],
    name_hint="exp_w2",
):
    ...
```

Today `cross_core_pipe` hardcodes the consumer-side ring depth to 8 (single direction) / 4 (bidirectional). On the fused INT8 w2 matmul + dequant scope cited in #1472 this alone reserved 262144 B in UB and blew the 192 KB budget. The only workaround was shrinking the kernel tile, which also degraded matmul tiling.

The knob:

- Sizes the consumer-side `system.reserve_buffer` as `slot_size * ring_slots` instead of `slot_size * 8`.
- Forwards the value to PTOAS as the existing `local_slot_num` attr on the frontend `pto.aic/aiv_initialize_pipe` ops, which already accepts the full 1..8 (single-direction) / 1..4 (bidirectional) range and propagates it through to the generated `TPipe<...>` template instantiation (see PTOAS lit test `tpush_tpop_frontend_local_slot_num_a3.pto`).
- Defaults to today's behaviour when omitted — no diff for existing IR / codegen.

## What this does *not* do

PTOAS's GM-ring `slot_num` is still hardcoded 8/4 in `PTOLowerFrontendPipeOpsPass.cpp` and the internal verifier still rejects anything other than 4 or 8 (`PTO.cpp:12063-12064`). The underlying `pto-isa` `TPipe<>` template already accepts `SlotNum >= 1`; tracked as a separate request at hw-native-sys/PTOAS#709. Once that lands, the same `ring_slots` knob can drive both attrs together.

## Plumbing

Routed through the existing `ScopeStmt.attrs_` channel — no new IR field, no serializer / reflection / Python-binding change:

1. **DSL** (`python/pypto/language/optimizations.py`): `Split` dataclass + `split()` factory accept `ring_slots: int | None`.
2. **Parser** (`python/pypto/language/parser/ast_parser.py`): `_try_parse_pl_split` accepts the `ring_slots=` kwarg (validated 1..8 at parse time); `_AtKwargState` carries it; `_parse_at_scope` appends `("ring_slots", N)` to `scope_attrs`. Both `pl.at` and `pl.spmd` forms.
3. **Outliner** (`include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/scope_outline_utils.h`): forwards `attrs_["ring_slots"]` from the `InCoreScopeStmt` / `AutoInCoreScopeStmt` onto the outlined `Function::attrs_`.
4. **Function helper** (`include/pypto/ir/function.h`): `GetRingSlots()` reader, mirroring `GetSplitMode()`.
5. **Cross-core pipe** (`src/ir/transforms/utils/cross_core_pipe.{h,cpp}`): `BuildAutomaticPipeSetup` and `CreateInitializePipe` take the override, size the UB `reserve_buffer` by `slot_size * ring_slots`, validate against `dir_mask` (≤4 for bidirectional), and emit `local_slot_num` on the initialize_pipe call only when the user overrode the default.
6. **ExpandMixedKernel** (`src/ir/transforms/expand_mixed_kernel_pass.cpp`): passes `func->GetRingSlots()` to the cross-core pipe builder.
7. **Op + codegen** (`src/ir/op/sync_ops/cross_core.cpp`, `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp`): `system.aic/aiv_initialize_pipe` accepts the optional `local_slot_num` kwarg; `FormatInitializePipeAttrs` emits `, local_slot_num = N` to PTOAS MLIR only when present (existing IR is byte-identical when the knob is unused).
8. **Python helper** (`python/pypto/ir/op/system_ops.py`): `aic_initialize_pipe()` / `aiv_initialize_pipe()` accept `local_slot_num=`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/ut/ir/parser/test_at_optimizations.py` — 5 new parser tests: kwarg appears on `ScopeStmt.attrs`, default leaves it unset, out-of-range / zero / unknown-kwarg rejected, `Split` dataclass constructor accepts `ring_slots=` at runtime.
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_expand_mixed_kernel_a2a3.py` — 2 new end-to-end tests:
  - `ring_slots=2` on a unidirectional C2V scope shrinks `reserve_buffer` size from 32768 to 8192 (slot_size 4096 * 2) and emits `local_slot_num=2` on both aic/aiv `initialize_pipe` calls.
  - Bidirectional `ring_slots=8` is rejected with a clear "exceeds platform maximum of 4 for bidirectional" message at `BuildAutomaticPipeSetup` time.
- [x] Full sweep across `tests/ut/ir/transforms/`, `tests/ut/ir/parser/`, `tests/ut/codegen/`, `tests/ut/language/parser/`, `tests/ut/ir/core/`, `tests/ut/ir/statements/`: **2562 passed, 26 skipped, 0 failed** — no regressions.
- [x] CMake build green (`cmake --build build --parallel`).

title: feat(passes): materialize orchestration PTO2_SCOPE as IR scopes
body:
## Summary

Move the orchestration codegen's implicit `PTO2_SCOPE()` placement out of the printer and into the IR.

- **New pass `MaterializeRuntimeScopes`** (last in the pipeline, after the final `Simplify`): for every `Orchestration` function it inserts explicit AUTO `RuntimeScopeStmt` (`manual=false`) nodes wrapping the function body and each `ForStmt` / `IfStmt` branch body, suppressed inside a manual scope (the runtime forbids AUTO nested in MANUAL).
- **Orchestration codegen** no longer derives scope structure from `for` / `if`: the three implicit `PTO2_SCOPE()` emission sites are removed and codegen emits `PTO2_SCOPE` 1:1 from `RuntimeScopeStmt` nodes. Generated code is **byte-identical** to the previous behavior. A small `UnwrapAutoScope` helper keeps the hand-written structural scans (`GetLastYieldStmt`, GM-pipe sizing) transparent to the inserted wrappers.
- **New `pl.auto_scope()` DSL surface** (parser + printer) so the inserted AUTO scopes are first-class, round-trippable IR. The printer recurses through the scope so a trailing return-var yield keeps its `var = pl.yield_(...)` LHS; the parser treats a yield inside `pl.auto_scope()` as the enclosing for/if return-var.
- New `RuntimeScopesMaterialized` IRProperty (required: `SplitIncoreOrch`, `CallDirectionsResolved`).
- Ignore the local `.scratch/` directory.

## Testing

- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_materialize_runtime_scopes.py` — function/for/if wrapping, manual-scope suppression, idempotency, non-Orchestration untouched
- [x] `tests/ut/language/parser/test_auto_scope_parsing.py` — `pl.auto_scope()` parse / round-trip / nesting restriction
- [x] `tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py` — emitted `PTO2_SCOPE` output unchanged
- [x] Full `tests/ut` suite (5262 passed)
- [x] clang-tidy clean on changed C++ files
- [x] EN + zh-CN docs updated (new pass doc `36-`, pass_manager, orchestration codegen, python_syntax, pass-doc-ordering)

title: [Bug] pl.at(deps=...) shape-rejection diagnostic caret points at the wrong source line
body:
### Component

Parser

### Description

When `pl.at(deps=...)` is passed an expression whose AST shape is not one of the accepted forms (list literal, tuple literal, or comprehension), the DSL parser correctly rejects it with the message `Error: 'pl.at()' deps= must be a list / tuple / comprehension of TaskId values` and a helpful hint. The **message itself is fine** — but the source-location caret (`^`) and the snippet window point at the wrong line, typically several lines past the actual `deps=` argument, under an unrelated statement inside the `with pl.at(...):` body.

For someone hitting this for the first time, the caret pointing under (for example) a `w_down[...]` tile slice is misleading — it makes the reader hunt for an invalid TaskId expression inside the slice rather than look at the `deps=` argument two or more lines above. The caret should point at the `deps=` expression's own span.

The most likely root cause is that the validation routine attaches the diagnostic to the surrounding `with` block's span (or to the last lexical token of the first body statement), rather than to the AST node of the `deps=` argument itself. The argument's own `lineno` / `col_offset` is the right anchor.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Inside any `pl.manual_scope()` body, write a `with pl.at(...)` whose `deps=` is a list-concatenation (`[a] + [b for ... ]`) — semantically a flat list of `TaskId`s, but syntactically a `BinOp(Add)` rather than a single list/tuple/comprehension literal:

   ```python
   with pl.manual_scope():
       silu_tids = pl.array.create(N_TILES, pl.TASK_ID)
       with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="down_seed") as seed_tid:
           ...
       for n_out in pl.parallel(DOWN_ON):
           n0 = n_out * DOWN_TN
           for k_split in pl.range(K_SPLITS):
               k0 = k_split * DOWN_TN
               with pl.at(
                   level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP,
                   name_hint="down_proj",
                   deps=[seed_tid] + [silu_tids[4 * k_split + i] for i in range(4)],
               ) as down_tid:
                   a0 = mlp_tile[:, k0 : k0 + DOWN_TK]
                   w0 = w_down[k0 : k0 + DOWN_TK, n0 : n0 + DOWN_TN]
                   c_acc = pl.matmul(a0, w0, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
   ```

2. Run the program with `--smoke` (or any path that exercises `@pl.jit`'s parser).

3. Observe the error and note the caret location.

### Expected Behavior

The error span and caret should point at the `deps=` argument expression on the `with pl.at(...)` line — i.e. under the `[seed_tid] + [silu_tids[...] for i in range(4)]` text itself. A reader should be able to glance at the highlighted span and immediately see which argument is the wrong shape.

### Actual Behavior

The caret points several lines past the `deps=` argument, under the closing `]` of an unrelated statement inside the `with` body. Verbatim console output:

```text
Error: 'pl.at()' deps= must be a list / tuple / comprehension of TaskId values
  --> <string>:302:86
    |
300 |                     with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint='down_proj', deps=[seed_tid] + [silu_tids[4 * k_split + i] for i in range(4)]) as down_tid:
301 |                         a0 = mlp_tile[:, k0:k0 + 128]
302 |                         w0 = w_down[k0:k0 + 128, n0:n0 + 1024]
    |                                                               ^
303 |                         c_acc = pl.matmul(a0, w0, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
304 |                         for lk in pl.pipeline(1, 8, stage=2):
    |
   = help: Use deps=[tid] where tid is a TaskId from a prior `_, tid = pl.submit(...)`, a loop iter_arg, `arr[i]` on a TASK_ID array, or `None`.
```

The `^` is at line 302, column 86 — the end of the `w_down[k0:k0+128, n0:n0+1024]` slice expression, which has nothing to do with the deps argument. The actual problem is on line 300, inside `pl.at(...)`.

### Git Commit ID

567eb669dba0d16e7a04dea8b25afe452b6d5f9e

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- The bug is purely cosmetic / debuggability — once you know the rule, the fix is to rewrite the deps as a single literal (`[seed_tid, silu_tids[...], silu_tids[...], ...]` or a single comprehension).
- Likely fix area: the DSL parser handler that validates `pl.at(...)` keyword arguments (path under `python/pypto/language/parser/`). The diagnostic should be raised against the keyword argument's `value` AST node and its own `(lineno, col_offset, end_lineno, end_col_offset)`, not against the enclosing `with` statement's span or the first body statement.
- Severity: low. The error itself is correct and the rule is easy to satisfy once you spot it — only the caret position misleads.

title: fix(codegen): require row_major layout for tile.cast (pto.tcvt)
body:
## Summary

`pto.tcvt` (the lowering of `tile.cast`) silently **mis-orders elements when its source tile is `col_major`** — e.g. a reshaped `[n, 1]` index vector narrowed `i32 -> i16`. The same cast on a `row_major` source is correct, so the failure is silent wrong output with no diagnostic. This is what produced reversed scatter rows in the FP16 `tensor.scatter_update` lowering (issue #1549).

PyPTO already drives this exact class of ISA constraint through the `ResolveBackendOpLayouts` pass, which reshapes a `[n, 1] col_major` vector to `[1, n] row_major` around a constrained op and restores the layout afterwards. `tile.cast` simply had **no layout spec**, so it was never repaired.

### Changes

- **`src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp`**: register `tile.cast` with `set_input_layout(0, row_major)` + `set_output_layout(row_major)`, mirroring `tile.rsqrt` / `tile.cmps` / `tile.sort32`. `ResolveBackendOpLayouts` now repairs every `col_major` caller generically. Row-major callers are unaffected (no repair, zero overhead).
- **`tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_resolve_backend_op_layouts_pass.py`**: pass-level regression for a `col_major [16, 1]` `i32 -> i16` cast being repaired through a `[1, 16] row_major` reshape.
- **`tests/st/runtime/ops/test_cast.py`**: new end-to-end ST — a `col_major [N, 1]` `i32 -> i16` narrow (the #1549 regression, must preserve element order) plus a `row_major [1, N]` control case.
- **`docs/en` + `docs/zh-cn` `20-resolve_backend_op_layouts.md`**: list `tile.cast` among the constrained ops.
- **`src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp`**: comment-only trim of the `scatter_update` lowering — its i32-compute / narrow-at-the-end design is kept for the alignment benefit. No behavior change: this path narrows only the **row-major `[n, d]`** flat index, so it never feeds a `col_major` source to `tile.cast`, and the new layout spec is a no-op for it.

## Testing

- [x] New + existing `ResolveBackendOpLayouts` UTs pass (5/5)
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` + `tests/ut/codegen/`: 1687 passed, 26 skipped
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/operators/test_tile_ops.py`: 237 passed
- [x] Pre-commit hooks (clang-format, cpplint, ruff, pyright, markdownlint) pass
- [ ] On-device ST `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_cast.py::TestCast::test_tile_cast_col_major_narrow` (hardware, to be confirmed by reviewer) — the direct col_major-cast regression for this fix.

> Note: `test_scatter_update.py::...::test_tile_scatter_update_fp16` is **not** a target of this PR. That path was already worked around in #1537 (narrow only the row-major `[n, d]` flat index), so this PR does not change its codegen and it needs no re-confirmation here.

## Related Issues

Fixes #1549

title: fix(codegen): preserve outer task ids inside pl.manual_scope
body:
## Summary

- Fix `OrchestrationCodegen::VisitStmt_(RuntimeScopeStmtPtr)` so `pl.submit(..., deps=[outer_tid])` inside `pl.manual_scope()` keeps its explicit edge to an outer-scope task. Previously the map was cleared on scope entry and the edge was silently dropped.
- Snapshot `manual_task_id_map_` / `array_carry_vars_` by **copy** instead of `std::move` + `clear()`, so the live maps keep the outer entries visible inside the inner scope. Restore the outer-only snapshot on exit so inner-scope adds (which name C++ identifiers that die with the inner `{` block) do not leak to the parent.
- Update the field-level docstring on `manual_task_id_map_` to describe the new snapshot/restore semantics.
- Add a regression test `TestManualScopeCodegen::test_manual_scope_inner_deps_can_reference_outer_scope_tid` that asserts the generated orchestration C++ contains the inner kernel's `params_t1_deps` array, the `outer_tid.is_valid()` guard, and the `params_t1.set_dependencies(...)` call.

## Root cause

`VisitStmt_(RuntimeScopeStmtPtr)` used to `std::move` the live maps into a saved snapshot and then `clear()` them on manual-scope entry, treating each manual scope as a hermetic task-id namespace. `CountManualDeps` then returned 0 for any `deps=` edge pointing to a producer emitted in the enclosing scope (early-return on the lookup miss at line 1544), so `EmitManualDeps` skipped the entire `set_dependencies(...)` emit for that inner task. With auto-dep also off inside the manual scope, the inner kernel had no fence on the outer producer.

The hermetic-namespace assumption was correct when manual_scope was first introduced (PR #1307) because the parser at the time rejected `deps=` outside a manual scope. That restriction was later relaxed — `Arg::set_dependencies` is now documented as "Orthogonal to scope mode" — but the codegen's clear-on-entry was never revisited.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py::TestManualScopeCodegen` — 13/13 pass (12 existing + 1 new).
- [x] Full unit test suite — 5253 pass / 0 fail / 28 skipped (162.99s, parallel).
- [x] clang-tidy on the diff — clean (no new warnings).
- [x] End-to-end manual verification on a real Qwen3 program: an outer auto-scope `post_rmsnorm` `pl.at(...) as post_norm_tid` followed by `with pl.manual_scope()` containing `pl.at("gate_proj", deps=[post_norm_tid])` and `pl.at("up_proj", deps=[post_norm_tid])` now emits the expected `params_tN.set_dependencies(...)` calls in the generated orchestration C++.

title: [Bug] PTOAS does not insert pipe_barrier before pto.comm.tnotify — signal write races ahead of remote MTE3 TSTOREs
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

When PTOAS lowers `pto.comm.tnotify` to `pto::comm::TNOTIFY(...)`, it does not insert any pipe synchronization before the call. Because `pto.tstore` to a peer address (used by `pld.tile.remote_store`, `pld.tensor.put`'s underlying tput, and ring/allreduce loops) issues an asynchronous SDMA write on PIPE_MTE3, and the signal store inside `TNOTIFY_IMPL` (`st_atomic` / `*sigPtr = value`) runs on the scalar pipe *before* `TNOTIFY_IMPL`'s own trailing `pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL)`, the signal can land on the peer before the prior remote TSTORE data has actually been transferred. The peer's `TWAIT` then returns, the peer reads its window, and observes stale (often zero) bytes where the remote write was supposed to land.

This is a correctness gap in the auto-sync logic of PTOAS: when emitting `pto.comm.tnotify`, PTOAS should insert a barrier that drains all prior pipes (in particular MTE3) before the notify call, or equivalently pass the appropriate `WaitEvents` to `TNOTIFY(...)`. The fix should not depend on each caller manually inserting a sync — the same race exists in every kernel that combines a remote write with a notify.

Workaround currently in tree: `pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL)` added at the entry of `TNOTIFY_IMPL` in `pto-isa`'s `pto/comm/a2a3/TNotify.hpp` and `pto/comm/a5/TNotify.hpp`. This is correct but lives in the runtime header, not in the synthesizer that produces the kernel — PTOAS itself should emit the barrier so callers do not need a runtime-side workaround.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out PyPTO at the affected commit.
2. Run `pytest tests/st/distributed/test_l3_remote_store.py::TestL3RemoteStore::test_subview_halves -v` on a 2-device a2a3 setup (the smallest reliable repro — two `pld.tile.remote_store` calls to disjoint offsets of the same peer window, followed by a single `pld.system.notify` + `pld.system.wait`).
3. Inspect the generated kernel at `build_output/SubviewRemoteStore_*/next_levels/chip_orch/ptoas/half_push_step.cpp`. The relevant pattern is:

   ```cpp
   TSTORE(v37, v28);                              // second remote store
   set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID1);     // only consumed later by a TLOAD
   [scalar setup for notify args]
   pto::comm::TNOTIFY(v42, v15, v10);             // no MTE3 drain in between
   ```

4. The assertion fails intermittently (`max diff = 163.0` when it does, with rank 0's high half observed as zeros). Re-running the same binary will sometimes pass and sometimes fail, confirming a race.

### Expected Behavior

PTOAS should emit a barrier ensuring that all prior pipe operations (in particular MTE3 remote stores) are visible on the peer before `TNOTIFY` is called. The simplest correct lowering would be to emit `pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL);` (or an equivalent `set_flag` / `wait_flag` chain pinning MTE3 against the scalar pipe) immediately before the generated `pto::comm::TNOTIFY(...)` call.

After such a fix, `test_subview_halves` should pass deterministically without the runtime-side workaround, and every other `<remote write> + tnotify` kernel (allreduce, ep dispatch/combine, ring shuffle, future remote_store callers) gets the same guarantee for free.

### Actual Behavior

PTOAS emits no synchronization between the last `pto.tstore` to a remote address and the following `pto.comm.tnotify`. The race is observable in `test_subview_halves` and theoretically present in every kernel that combines remote writes with a notify:

- `test_l3_remote_store::test_subview_halves` — actively flaky (2 remote stores + 1 notify, smallest race window).
- `test_l3_remote_store::test_ring_shuffle` — same shape (1 remote store + 1 notify), currently passes because the single 256-byte SDMA usually wins the race against scalar setup + `st_atomic`, but the gap is not guaranteed.
- `test_l3_allreduce` — `reduce_step.cpp` has `TSTORE` at line 76 then `TNOTIFY` at line 84 with no MTE3 wait in between.
- `test_l3_ep_dispatch_combine` — `dispatch_step.cpp` ends a long chain of remote TSTOREs with a single `TNOTIFY` (last `TSTORE` at line 1290 → `TNOTIFY` at line 1297).

Observed actual values for the failing run (`device_ids=[4,5]`, `--platform a2a3`):

```
rank 0 actual: [100..131, 0, 0, ..., 0]   # high half from peer never landed
rank 0 expect: [100..163]
rank 1 actual: [0..63]                    # both halves landed
rank 1 expect: [0..63]
```

Only `rank 1 → rank 0`'s second remote store consistently loses the race. Direction asymmetry suggests the failing path is the one whose SDMA happens to be slightly slower than scalar/atomic dispatch — i.e. a true timing race, not a logic bug.

### Git Commit ID

a96e2878bd099d59d179bfa3b097abbfec7e1fbc

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Confirmed root cause by patching `pto-isa/include/pto/comm/a2a3/TNotify.hpp` to add `pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL);` at the entry of `TNOTIFY_IMPL`. After that change, `test_subview_halves` passes deterministically across re-runs.
- The same patch is needed in the `a5` variant (`pto/comm/a5/TNotify.hpp`) for parity, but the principled fix is in PTOAS so that the runtime header does not have to compensate.
- Comparison with `pld.tensor.put` clarifies why `tput` is safe: its `TPUT_IMPL` ends with a self-wait `set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0); wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0)` that drains MTE3 before returning. `pto.tstore` has no such drain, so the burden falls on whatever runs after it — and `pto.comm.tnotify` does not pick up that burden today.

title: Add compiler-derived manual task dependencies
body:
## Summary
- Add `AutoDeriveTaskDependencies`, a program pass that derives compiler-owned dependency edges inside manual runtime scopes while preserving user-written `deps` separately.
- Extend task-id/storage lineage, region/alias hazard handling, control-flow root tracking, and conservative fallback from manual scope to runtime auto scope when static dependencies cannot be encoded safely.
- Update orchestration codegen to merge user deps and compiler deps into one `set_dependencies` emission, and wire the pass into the default and debug tile pipelines.
- Add English and Chinese documentation for the new pass, pass ordering, and orchestration dependency behavior.

## Testing
- Remote validation on `myserver` under `/data/sunkaixuan/all_pyptos/auto-deps`.
- Validated pushed commit: `059e23a3d86f479299d83d0ff99e6d9e250855f3`.
- Exact requested case set passed remotely, covering RAW/RAR/WAW/WAR manual-scope hazards, user/compiler dep merging, static and symbolic region behavior, MemRef may-alias handling, if/loop lineage, fallback cleanup, codegen dep merging, and pass-manager registration.
- Earlier full target-file remote validation also passed on the same commit: `test_auto_derive_task_dependencies.py` (`22 passed`), `test_pass_manager.py` (`12 passed`), and `test_orchestration_codegen.py` (`83 passed, 9 warnings`).

## Notes

- After the remote validation, upstream `main` advanced from `567eb669dba0d16e7a04dea8b25afe452b6d5f9e` to `32f97ff591fb50bb987ec8cf25622b6bd1210b1c`; keeping Draft status leaves room for a final refresh/rebase before marking ready.

title: feat(distributed): L3 GEMM and allreduce-GEMM programs ST tests
body:
This PR adds STests on:

-  a PyPTO DSL program for L3 GEMM + 4-phase peer-to-peer allreduce

Data-parallel A + replicated B

title: [Bug] Codegen: cube matmul -> per-row scatter to distinct GM rows in one CORE_GROUP scope silently produces all-zero output
body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto** — compiles clean, runs on a2a3, output is all zeros on every written row. A single `pl.matmul` whose FP32 output is materialized into a scope-local `create_tensor` and then **read back per-row and scattered into distinct (strided) GM rows**, all inside one `CORE_GROUP` scope, silently produces zero data on device.

Distinct from the existing reports:
- **#1525** (chained matmul → cast → matmul) explicitly has *no slice* and adds *acc-reuse* between two matmuls. This case has **one matmul**, **no acc-reuse**, and **does** slice (per-row subview) + scatter. Neither contains the other.
- **#1507** (cube→vec bridge drops matmul `valid_shape`, breaking a downstream vec subview) is the closest mechanism — but it is **CLOSED**, and this still reproduces on current `main`, so this is either an uncovered sibling of that fix or a regression on the matmul→store→subview→scatter path.
- Related: #1523, #1352.

### Description

In one `CORE_GROUP` scope (`pl.split(NONE)`):
1. `kv_final[:, :] = pl.matmul(x, w, out_dtype=pl.FP32)` — cube matmul, whole-tile store into a scope-local `create_tensor`.
2. `for b in pl.range(B): cache[b*CACHE : b*CACHE+1, :] = pl.cast(kv_final[b:b+1, :], BF16)` — per-row subview read + scatter to a distinct strided GM row.

Compiles clean, runs (`compile done`, `runtime done`), but the output `cache` is all-zero on every written row (`actual=0.0`, expected nonzero). The cube→vector RAW dependency from the whole-tile store to the per-row reads is dropped: the first reads see uninitialized (zero) data. The result is **deterministic** (same rows zero across runs), not a race.

#### ~30-line repro (`-p a2a3`)

```python
import pypto.language as pl

B = 16
H = 64
CACHE = 256


def build_program():
    @pl.program
    class Repro:
        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Opaque)
        def fused(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[B, H], pl.BF16],
            w: pl.Tensor[[H, H], pl.BF16],
            cache: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[B * CACHE, H], pl.BF16]],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[B * CACHE, H], pl.BF16]:
            kv_final = pl.create_tensor([B, H], dtype=pl.FP32)
            with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.NONE)]):
                kv_final[:, :] = pl.matmul(x, w, out_dtype=pl.FP32)   # cube matmul, whole-tile store
                for b in pl.range(B):                                 # per-row scatter to distinct cache rows
                    cache[b * CACHE : b * CACHE + 1, :] = pl.cast(kv_final[b : b + 1, :], target_type=pl.BF16, mode="rint")
            return cache

    return Repro


def golden(values):
    out = (values["x"].float() @ values["w"].float()).to(values["cache"].dtype)
    for b in range(B):
        values["cache"][b * CACHE] = out[b]
```

Observed: `'cache' FAIL`, `Mismatched elements: 1577/262144`, first 20 mismatches all `actual=0.0` vs nonzero expected.

Notes:
- `UP_DOWN` instead of `NONE` does not help: it fails earlier at `SplitVectorKernel requires an even split dimension, got 1` (the per-row `[1, H]` slice cannot be row-halved).
- Reading the matmul SSA value directly (no `create_tensor`) fails ptoas: `'pto.subview' op boxed layout subview sizes must be multiples of inner shape` (single row of the L0C-boxed matmul output).
- Forcing a vector materialize (`pl.mul(acc, 1.0)`) compiles but the whole [B,H] FP32 tile overflows Vec UB.
- An older revision of this repro **deadlocked** on device (`aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018`, `sched_error_code=100`); on the current stack the same code silently miscompiles to zeros instead — same fused-scope bug, two manifestations.

#### Real kernel

`models/deepseek/v4/decode_indexer_compressor.py` — the `kv_hadamard` + `kv_and_cache_write` scopes cannot be mix-fused for this reason. The unfused two-scope form (matmul→GM `kv_final`, then a separate scatter scope) is correct and passes; merging them into one scope produces 3 zero rows in `kv`/`kv_cache`.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `3834f3d` |
| pypto | `78e44c6` (branch: main) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `e03faff` |
| pto-isa | `0f171f73` |
| ptoas | 0.41 |
| CANN | 9.0.0 |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

title: fix(codegen): Emit per-kernel ArgDirection signatures + selective dump_tag
body:
## Summary

End-to-end fix for `--dump-tensor` on codegen workloads, in two parts (kernel-signature contract + selective-dump DSL marker).

**Kernel ArgDirection signatures (resolves the root cause in #1458):**

- Codegen kernels were registered with an empty `CoreCallable` signature: `kernel_config.py`'s `KERNELS` entries carried no `signature` field, so the runtime built each callable with `sig_count()==0`. The TRB tensor dump then skipped every codegen task because the summed per-active-subtask tensor-arg count did not match the task payload `tensor_count` (count 0 != payload N).
- Orchestration codegen now records each kernel's runtime `ArgDirection` signature from the same `ParamEntry` vector that emits the task payload (`add_input/output/inout/scalar`) calls — guaranteeing the signature's non-`SCALAR` entries line up 1:1 with the payload tensors. The signature is threaded through `OrchestrationResult` and emitted as a `signature` field of `simpler.task_interface` `ArgDirection` members. Kernels without a recorded signature fall back to the prior empty-signature behavior.
- Scalars are intentionally excluded from the per-kernel `CoreCallable` signature: the signature array is sized to `CORE_MAX_TENSOR_ARGS`, and recording every `ParamEntry` (including scalars) overflowed `make_callable`'s `MaxSig` guard on kernels with many params (observed building Qwen3-14B decode kernels). Scalars live in a separate scalar-arg store and the runtime tensor dump skips `SCALAR` entries anyway.
- Populating signatures affects only the tensor dump: the leaf `CoreCallable` signature is unconsumed by the dispatch / arg-marshalling path on both runtimes.

**Selective dump (`pl.dump_tag`) for large workloads:**

- New DSL marker `pl.dump_tag(t)` (parser-only, orchestration-scoped). On large workloads (e.g. paged-attention 64bat/8192ctx) the full dump saturates the host-side collector (~42 MB/s drain) with 1 GB-scale KV-cache bindings and trips the STARS op-execute timeout. The marker lets users opt in to a subset.
- Parser pre-scans the function body, records tagged `Var` `name_hint`s on `Function::attrs_[kAttrDumpTaggedNames]`. Orchestration codegen emits a single `enable_dump_tensor_selective();` at orch entry (only when at least one tagged tensor reaches a kernel call) and `<task>.dump(<tagged-tensors>);` after each kernel call for entries whose `Var` matches.
- Marker also accepted inside `@pl.jit.inline` helpers: the `InlineFunctions` pass merges each callee's `kAttrDumpTaggedNames` list onto the caller before the callee is dropped, with `_inline<N>` suffixes stripped by `auto_name_utils::GetCompatibleBaseName` so tagged names still match after alpha-rename. Multi-level inlining converges at the pass fixpoint.
- `examples/models/09_paged_attention_spmd.py` uses the marker to keep `--dump-tensor` viable at production shapes.

**Docs:**

- EN + zh-CN updates to `03-runtime-dfx.md` (selective-dump section, limitations table) and `passes/01-inline_functions.md` (function-level attribute merge).

## Commits

- `4f0f2940` fix(codegen): Emit per-kernel ArgDirection signatures in kernel_config
- `de274389` fix(pr): resolve issues for #1466 — exclude scalars from the per-kernel signature
- `b518966f` feat(dsl): Add pl.dump_tag marker for selective tensor dump
- `dad8c1f4` feat(dsl): Accept pl.dump_tag inside @pl.jit.inline helpers
- `957e57cd` docs(dump_tag): Document limitations and inline attr merge

## Testing

- [x] Regression tests for `kernel_config.py` signature emission and `OrchestrationResult.func_name_to_signature` population
- [x] UT coverage for `pl.dump_tag` parser (form / scope / dedup), codegen (toggle + per-task, no-tag, stray-tag), inline-merge fixpoint
- [x] ST repro for `pl.dump_tag` end-to-end
- [x] `examples/models/09_paged_attention_spmd.py` exercises the selective path

## Related Issues

Fixes #1458

Replaces the closed #1466 (same branch).

title: fix(ci): repair Daily CI — qwen3-14b prefill path + AICPU thread plumbing
body:
## Summary

Repair the two failing Daily CI jobs tracked in #1546 (`qwen3-pypto-lib` and `a5-system-tests`).

Fixes #1546

## qwen3-pypto-lib — missing 14B prefill script

The job ran `models/qwen3/14b/qwen3_14b_prefill.py`, but pypto-lib restructured its 14B model and that file no longer exists:

```
python: can't open file '.../pypto-lib/models/qwen3/14b/qwen3_14b_prefill.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

The current prefill entry point is `models/qwen3/14b/prefill_fwd.py` — same `-p`/`-d` CLI, runs `run_jit` with golden validation and exits non-zero on failure. The 32B decode in the same step kept passing because its filename is unchanged. Updated the workflow path.

## a5-system-tests — AICPU stream sync timeout (507046)

`test_qwen3_decode_scope3_mixed[a5]` failed with `run_prepared failed with code 507046` (`ACL_ERROR_RT_STREAM_SYNC_TIMEOUT`):

```
[ERROR] Stream sync timeout: stream=AICPU timeout_ms=2000 device_id=1 block_dim=24
[ERROR] PTO2 runtime failed: orch_error_code=0 sched_error_code=100 runtime_status=-100
```

Both `compile_and_assemble` call sites in `tests/st/harness/core/test_runner.py` discarded the returned `runtime_config` (the 3rd tuple element) with `_`, so neither `block_dim` nor `aicpu_thread_num` baked into `kernel_config.py` reached the C++ `ChipCallConfig`. The `tensormap_and_ringbuffer` runtime requires `aicpu_thread_num=4` (3 schedulers + 1 orchestrator pinned to thread 3); the C++ default is 3, so without forwarding it the orchestrator is missing, AICPU ops are never scheduled, and `aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout` times out after 2000 ms. The user-facing `execute_compiled` path already forwarded these; the symmetric ST harness path was missed.

### Changes

- `python/pypto/runtime/runner.py`: add keyword-only `block_dim` / `aicpu_thread_num` to `_execute_on_device`, forward to `execute_on_device`.
- `tests/st/harness/core/test_runner.py`: add `runtime_config` to `CompileArtifact`, capture it at both `compile_and_assemble` sites, and forward `block_dim`/`aicpu_thread_num` to `_execute_on_device` (fused-execute task + inline `TestRunner.run`).

This consolidates the harness-plumbing fix previously opened standalone in #1514 (which can be closed in favour of this PR).

## Note on the residual a5 failure

With the thread plumbing in place, the AICPU host timeout (507046) is resolved, but earlier validation surfaced a deeper failure: `aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018` with `sched_error_code=100` (`PTO2_ERROR_SCHEDULER_TIMEOUT`) — a genuine scheduler stall (`MAX_IDLE_ITERATIONS` ≈ 20 s of no progress) in the qwen3 decode scope-3 mixed kernel on a5. That is a separate, hardware-specific scheduling issue and is not addressed here; this PR is the necessary prerequisite that gets a5 past the host-side timeout.

## Test plan

- [ ] Daily CI `qwen3-pypto-lib` job passes (14B prefill + 32B decode).
- [ ] Daily CI `a5-system-tests` job gets past the 507046 AICPU host timeout (residual 507018 scheduler stall tracked separately).
- [ ] No regression in other ST runtime tests.

title: feat(distributed): add pld.tile.remote_store subview push op
body:
## Summary

- Adds `pld.tile.remote_store`: a tile-level cross-rank push op that writes a local tile into a sub-region of a peer rank's window-bound `DistributedTensor`. Mirror of `pld.tile.remote_load`, lowers via the same peer-addressing helpers (`CommRemoteOffset` + `addptr` + `make_tensor_view` + `partition_view`) with the final emit flipped from `tload` to `tstore`. Unlike `pld.tensor.put` (whole-tensor only), this lets cross-rank pushes target a sub-region of a larger remote tensor.
- Fixes a pre-existing offsets-lowering gap in `remote_load` / `notify` / `wait` / `remote_store` codegen: `GetExprCodes` returned raw SSA names, so runtime i32 scalars in offsets reached `pto.partition_view` (which expects index) and PTOAS rejected the kernel. Routed all four call sites through `LowerTupleToIndexSSA`.
- Refactors the L3 EP dispatch+combine ST to match the runtime example 1:1 (per-rank signal cells, dynamic `pl.range` loops, host-backed staged outputs, golden replay of dispatch).

## Changes

**New op — `pld.tile.remote_store`:**
- IR op + verifier in `src/ir/op/distributed/remote_store.cpp`
- Codegen `MakeRemoteStoreCodegenPTO` in `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp`
- Python IR builder in `python/pypto/ir/op/distributed/tile_ops.py`
- DSL wrapper in `python/pypto/language/distributed/op/tile_ops.py`
- Re-exports in the three `pld` `__init__` / `unified_ops` files

**Test refactor — `test_l3_ep_dispatch_combine.py`:**
- Switched every `pl.unroll` to `pl.range` (runtime uses dynamic loops).
- Resized barrier signals to `[N_RANKS, 1]` with per-src signal cells (`count_done_sig[N]` / `data_done_sig[N]` / `combine_done_sig[N]`); dropped the `peer` scalar param.
- Added stage_out phase: dispatch emits host-backed `recv_x_out` / `recv_w_out` / `recv_idx_out` / `recv_count_out`; local_expert and combine read from these staged outputs instead of windows.
- Replaced `pl.array.create(1, ...) / acc[0]` scalar accumulator boilerplate with plain `pl.const(0, ...)` + reassignment (SSA pass auto-promotes to loop-carried IterArg).
- Added `_compute_golden_recv` host replay to verify per-rank `recv_x` / `recv_w` / `recv_idx` / `recv_count` in addition to the combined `routed_y` check.

title: [Bug] scf.if else branch yields raw ptr instead of tensor_view inside pl.spmd
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

When `pl.spmd` body contains an `if` (with no `else` user code) that performs a conditional slice-assign or `pl.assemble` write to an outer-scope tensor passed into the spmd-outlined function, pypto codegen emits an `scf.if` whose `if` branch yields a `tensor_view` (via `pto.partition_view`) while the empty `else` branch yields the raw `!pto.ptr<f32>` function argument. The `scf.if` itself is typed `!pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32>`, so ptoas rejects the MLIR.

### Steps to Reproduce

Save the minimal repro (~30 lines) and run:

```bash
python repro_spmd_if_yield.py -p a2a3sim
```

Repro file:

```python
import pypto.language as pl

N_BLOCKS = 32
N_COLS = 16


@pl.jit
def repro_spmd_if_write(
    flag: pl.Tensor[[N_BLOCKS], pl.INT32],
    out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N_BLOCKS, N_COLS], pl.FP32]],
):
    for idx in pl.spmd(N_BLOCKS, name_hint="spmd_if_write"):
        cond = pl.read(flag, [idx])
        if cond > 0:
            tile = pl.full([1, N_COLS], dtype=pl.FP32, value=1.0)
            out[idx : idx + 1, :] = tile
```

Full standalone harness (with golden + `run_jit` boilerplate) lives at `pypto-lib models/deepseek/v4/repro_spmd_if_yield_draft.py` on branch `perf-cmp128` (commit `9f6641ff`). The same pattern is also currently in the dsv4 decoder `models/deepseek/v4/decode_compressor_ratio128.py` `softmax_pool` scope (same branch).

### Expected Behavior

Compilation succeeds. Both branches of `scf.if` should yield a value of the declared `!pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32>` type (e.g. the unmodified `%out__ssa_v0_view` produced earlier by `pto.make_tensor_view %arg1`).

### Actual Behavior

```
Failed to compile function 'spmd_if_write': ptoas compilation failed:
loc("..../spmd_if_write.pto":22:15): error: use of value '%arg1'
expects different type than prior uses:
'!pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32>' vs '!pto.ptr<f32>'
```

Generated `spmd_if_write.pto` excerpt (note the mismatch on the else yield):

```mlir
%out__ssa_v0_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg1, shape = [...] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32>
%out__phi_v2 = scf.if %1 -> (!pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32>) {
  ...
  %out__ssa_v0_pview = pto.partition_view %out__ssa_v0_view, ...
  pto.tstore ins(%tile__tile : ...) outs(%out__ssa_v0_pview : ...)
  scf.yield %out__ssa_v0_view : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32>   // OK
} else {
  scf.yield %arg1 : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32>               // raw ptr instead of view
}
```

### Git Commit ID

1bb34f41

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910C

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1533 (earlier SCF-phi `partition_view` fix for `pl.assemble` inside `pl.range`+`if`). The same pattern in `pl.spmd` still produces the malformed yield. Reproducible with either a slice-assign write or `pl.assemble` write — both trigger the same mismatch.

Workaround in pypto-lib: hoist the write out of the conditional so it runs unconditionally (wasting cycles on blocks where the result is unused).

title: fix(pass): fence cube-to-vector GM handoff; fix scratch/output aliasing
body:
## Summary

Fixes a wrong-output bug for a `matmul -> per-row scatter` fused in one `CORE_GROUP` scope on Ascend910B (issue #1564). Two independent root causes:

- **`FuseCreateAssembleToSlice` aliased a scratch onto the output.** A call's single return value resolved its buffer root to the *first* `Out`/`InOut` param in param order. When an `InOut` scratch (the matmul's `kv_final`) precedes the real `Out`, the scratch's `tensor.create` was fused into `tensor.slice(output)` — aliasing an FP32 scratch onto the BF16 output and corrupting it. Now the return root is selected by matching the return type.

- **`ExpandMixedKernel` skipped the cube→vector fence across loop nesting.** The GM cross-lane sync only paired a producer store with a consumer load in the *same structural body*. A cube store at function top level feeding a vector load *inside a loop* got no fence, so the lanes raced (the first iterations read the scratch before the matmul store landed). Now a consumer nested under the store's body is paired, and the fence `tpop` is hoisted before the enclosing loop — one `tpush` ↔ one `tpop`, no count mismatch.

## Testing

- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` full suite (1358 passed, 26 skipped)
- [x] clang-tidy clean on the C++ diff
- [x] New regression UTs: `test_inout_scratch_before_out_not_fused`, `test_gm_sync_hoisted_before_consumer_loop_on_a2a3`
- [x] End-to-end ST repro `test_fused_matmul_scatter.py` passes on device (a2a3) for both `SplitMode.NONE` and `LEFT_RIGHT`

## Related Issues

Fixes #1564

title: fix(ci): isolate dist-system-tests installs in per-job venv
body:
## Summary

`dist-system-tests` had three intertwined issues that surfaced one after the other while triaging this PR:

1. **Concurrent install collision** — the job runs directly on the self-hosted host (not in a container) and shares the `py310` conda env across runners. Two concurrent PRs both `pip install pypto` / `pip install ./runtime` into the same `site-packages`, racing each other and leaving the env in inconsistent state.

2. **Tests loading stale pypto** — even after adding a per-job venv, `pytest` resolved via `PATH` to py310 base's `pytest`. With `--system-site-packages`, pip saw the existing `pytest` in py310 base and skipped installing it into the venv, so `venv/bin/pytest` doesn't exist; the py310 `pytest` script's shebang forces py310's python, which doesn't see the venv → `import pypto` falls back to py310 base's stale copy. Traceback paths showed `/home/ci-runner/miniconda3/envs/py310/lib/...` instead of the venv.

3. **HCCL 507018 on L3 tests** — the runner's systemd `Environment=` injects `PTO2_RING_HEAP` / `PTO2_RING_TASK_WINDOW` / `PTO2_RING_DEP_POOL` into every step. These specific values aren't compatible with the L3 distributed tests' HCCL setup (`test_l3_allreduce`, `test_l3_notify_wait`) and cause `comm_init` to fail with error 507018. The other NPU jobs (`system-tests`, `pypto-lib-model`) still rely on these values via container `-e` passthrough, so they remain set there.

## Fix

1. **Per-job venv** layered on conda `py310` with `--system-site-packages`. Heavy deps (torch, etc.) reuse from py310 base; only `pypto` / `runtime` install into the venv. `pip` always rebuilds path installs, so each run gets its own freshly-built `pypto` regardless of what's in py310 base.
2. **`python -m pytest`** instead of `pytest` in the test step. The venv's `python` runs pytest, and pytest itself can load from py310 base (fine — it's just a runner); but `import pypto` resolves to the venv's site-packages first.
3. **`unset PTO2_RING_*`** at the end of activate.sh so the L3 tests don't inherit the host-injected values. Scoped to `dist-system-tests` only (other jobs still get them via container env passthrough).

Also moves to a generated `activate.sh` pattern that every later step sources, replacing the previous `$GITHUB_ENV`-dump trick. Matches `runtime/.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s per-step activate convention; each step is self-contained and individually retry-able.

## Out of Scope

- Container jobs (`system-tests`, `pypto-lib-model`, `clang-tidy`) — already isolated per-run by container ephemerality, and they still need `PTO2_RING_*` for the non-L3 tests
- Network/proxy reliability for `actions/checkout` and the `pto-isa` clone (separate concern, can be a follow-up)
- Removing `PTO2_RING_*` from the runner's systemd unit override file — a host-side operation across all NPU runners, outside this PR's scope. We unset at activate-time instead.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes on this PR
- [ ] Verify `pytest tests/st/distributed` imports the venv's `pypto`, not py310 base's (traceback paths in failures should contain `dist-checkout/venv/lib/...`)
- [ ] Verify L3 HCCL tests (`test_l3_allreduce`, `test_l3_notify_wait`) pass without error 507018
- [ ] Trigger a second concurrent PR (or `workflow_dispatch`) and verify both `dist-system-tests` runs complete without cross-contamination

title: feat(language): explicit runtime scope control via pl.scope + auto_scope
body:
## Summary

Lets users place orchestration runtime scopes (`PTO2_SCOPE`) explicitly instead of relying on the compiler's blanket insertion, and makes `RuntimeScopeStmt` transparent to SSA so scoped loop/branch bodies are handled correctly.

### Frontend
- **Unified block primitive `pl.scope(mode=pl.ScopeMode.AUTO|MANUAL)`** (new `ScopeMode` enum). `pl.manual_scope()` is kept as an alias; the transitional `pl.auto_scope()` is removed.
- **`@pl.function(auto_scope=False)`** (stored in `Function.attrs`): the compiler stops auto-inserting AUTO scopes and the user places them by hand with `with pl.scope()`. In the default `auto_scope=True` mode a hand-placed AUTO scope is rejected (the compiler owns placement); MANUAL scopes are allowed in either mode (a dependency-semantics choice).

### Pass / printer
- `MaterializeRuntimeScopes` early-returns for opt-out functions and marks a materialized function `auto_scope=False`, so the pass is idempotent and its output round-trips (the inserted `with pl.scope()` parses back only under `auto_scope=False`).
- Printer emits `pl.scope(mode=...)` and a dedicated `auto_scope=False` kwarg (filtered out of `attrs={}`).

### Scope transparent to SSA
A for/if carry-`pl.yield_` wrapped in a `with pl.scope()` is now handled:
- `ConvertToSSA`: `ExtractYield` / `ReplaceOrAppendYield` look through a trailing `RuntimeScopeStmt` (find/replace the carry-yield inside the scope, preserving the wrapper).
- `SSAVerify`: `GetLastStmt` / `CheckNoMidBodyYield` look through the scope.

This also fixes round-trip of **compiler-inserted** AUTO scopes that wrap a loop-carried yield.

## Testing

title: [Bug] Orchestration codegen scrambles phi assignments when one task writes 3+ outer-loop carries
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

When a single InCore `with pl.at(...)` scope inside a `for x in pl.parallel(B):` (or `pl.range`) outer loop writes to **three or more outer-scope tensors that are also carried across loop iterations**, the orchestration cpp codegen emits **scrambled phi-node assignments** after the task call. Each phi gets assigned the wrong source tensor — e.g. `cmp_kv_pool_flat__phi = normed_kv` even though they have different shapes/dtypes.

Downstream behavior:
- If the wrongly-aliased tensor is later passed to a `tensor.reshape`, AICPU hits `Assertion failed: valid_reshape(new_shapes, new_ndims)` at `runtime/tensor.h:435` and the device stalls on never-resolved task deps.
- If the bad alias is only consumed by another InCore task, the scheduler reports `TIMEOUT_EXIT after_idle_iterations=800000` — all cores idle waiting on a dependency that can never be satisfied.

### Steps to Reproduce

Trigger in pypto-lib branch `perf-cmp128`, by merging `models/deepseek/v4/decode_compressor_ratio128.py` `kv_write_and_scatter_next` scope into `rmsnorm_rope`:

```python
for global_c_idx in pl.parallel(B):
    ...
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="rmsnorm_rope"):
        # ... RMSNorm + RoPE writes to normed_kv ...
        # MERGED tail (was its own pl.at scope):
        if pos_b + S >= COMPRESS_RATIO:
            kv_flat[global_c_idx*S:global_c_idx*S+1, :] = ...      # carry #1
            cmp_kv_pool_flat[phys_cmp_row:phys_cmp_row+1, :] = ... # carry #2
            for s in pl.range(pre_tokens_b, S):
                kv_state_pool_flat[state_blk_id:state_blk_id+1, ...] = ...  # carry #3
```

Then run `python models/deepseek/v4/decode_compressor_ratio128.py -p a2a3 --hetero-start-pos`.

### Expected Behavior

After the task call, each phi node receives the corresponding output of the task. With outputs `[kv_flat, cmp_kv_pool_flat, kv_state_pool_flat]`, the phis should be:

```cpp
kv_flat__phi          = kv_flat__rv;
cmp_kv_pool_flat__phi = cmp_kv_pool_flat__rv;
kv_state_pool_flat__phi = kv_state_pool_flat__rv;
```

### Actual Behavior

Generated `orchestration/compressor_test.cpp`:

```cpp
params_t3.add_inout(normed_kv_inline48);          // per-batch tile [16, 512] FP32
params_t3.add_output(kv_flat_inline26);
params_t3.add_output(cmp_kv_pool_flat_inline34__rv_v2);
params_t3.add_output(kv_state_pool_flat_inline24__rv_v8);
rt_submit_aiv_task(3, params_t3);
const Tensor& cmp_kv_pool_flat_inline34__phi_v4 = normed_kv_inline48;       // WRONG (normed_kv has shape [16,512] FP32, cmp_kv_pool_flat is [8192,512] BF16)
const Tensor& kv_flat_inline26__phi_v4          = kv_flat_inline26;
const Tensor& kv_state_pool_flat_inline24__phi_v13 = cmp_kv_pool_flat_inline34__rv_v2;  // WRONG (cross-assignment)
cmp_kv_pool_flat_inline34__rv_v2 = cmp_kv_pool_flat_inline34__phi_v4;
kv_state_pool_flat_inline24__rv_v8 = kv_state_pool_flat_inline24__phi_v13;
```

AICPU device log:

```
[ERROR] AICPU assert_impl "Assertion failed: valid_reshape(new_shapes, new_ndims)"
[ERROR] Location: .../runtime/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/runtime/tensor.h:435
```

Then the scheduler stalls and times out. Full log: `build_output/simpler_log/debug/device-*/device-*_<timestamp>.log`. Orchestration cpp: `build_output/_jit_compressor_test_<timestamp>/orchestration/compressor_test.cpp` (both available under pypto-lib `perf-cmp128` branch).

### Git Commit ID

90220ebb

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910C

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related to but distinct from #1390 (Out-window name collision in dual-output return aliases — fixed). The same class of orchestration mis-naming surfaces again when one task carries **3 or more** outer-scope tensors. Workaround: keep the scope split into separate `with pl.at(...)` blocks (one task per carry), which pypto-lib `e729ccf8` does.
