title: fix(codegen): Per-kernel ArgDirection signatures + Var-identity selective dump (#1458)
body:
## Summary

End-to-end fix for `--dump-tensor` on codegen workloads (#1458), in three parts: a kernel-signature contract fix that addresses the root cause, a selective-dump DSL surface so large workloads stay within the host collector's budget, and adoption of the runtime's leveled dump model (off/partial/full).

### Kernel ArgDirection signatures (root cause of #1458)

- Codegen kernels were registered with an empty `CoreCallable` signature: `KERNELS` entries carried no `signature`, so the runtime built each callable with `sig_count() == 0`. The TRB tensor dump then skipped every codegen task because the summed per-active-subtask tensor-arg count did not match the task payload `tensor_count` (count 0 != payload N).
- Orchestration codegen now records each kernel's runtime `ArgDirection` signature from the same `ParamEntry` vector that emits the task payload (`add_input/output/inout/scalar`), guaranteeing the signature's non-`SCALAR` entries line up 1:1 with the payload tensors. The signature is threaded through `OrchestrationResult` and emitted as a `signature` field of the `task_interface` `ArgDirection` members. Kernels without a recorded signature fall back to the prior empty-signature behavior.
- Scalars are intentionally excluded from the per-kernel signature: the signature array is sized to `CORE_MAX_TENSOR_ARGS`, and recording scalars overflowed `make_callable`'s `MaxSig` guard on kernels with many params (observed on Qwen3-14B decode kernels). Scalars live in a separate scalar-arg store and the tensor dump skips `SCALAR` entries anyway.

### Selective dump by Var identity (`pl.dump_tag` / `dumps=`)

On large workloads (e.g. paged-attention 64bat/8192ctx) a full dump saturates the host-side collector with GB-scale KV-cache bindings and trips the STARS op-execute timeout. Two layered primitives let users opt into a subset, both tracked by **Var identity** (never by name):

- `pl.dump_tag(t)` — declarative forward-sticky per-tensor marker that merges the tagged `Var` into every subsequent consuming call's `dump_vars` set. Consumed at parse time; emits no IR statement of its own. Accepted inside `@pl.jit.inline` helpers.
- `pl.submit(..., dumps=[...])` / `pl.at(..., dumps=[...])` — submit-side kwarg (symmetric with `deps=`) feeding the same `dump_vars` set. This is the explicit dump surface on a submit; the printer round-trips it as a `dumps=[...]` kwarg (emitted after `deps=`).

The `dump_vars` attr (`vector<VarPtr>`) rides on `Call` / `Submit` / `Scope` attrs and is rewritten by SSA, substituted on inline, counted as a use by DCE/liveness, compared in `structural_equal`, and printed back — all by `Var` identity. Codegen matches each `args_[i]` against the set by `VarPtr` identity.

Coverage extends to the `@pl.jit` / tensor-op style where kernel dispatches are synthesised post-parse by the outline passes: `pl.dump_tag` seeds the enclosing scope's dump set, `InlineFunctions` transfers an inline call's dump set onto the scopes it splices in, and the outliner translates captured scope dump `Var`s onto the synthesised dispatch (mirroring the `arg_direction_overrides_vars` path).

**Auto-outlined SPMD loops (for-form / split):** the `for i in pl.spmd(N):` and `with pl.spmd(N, optimizations=[pl.split(...)])` forms build their `InCore` scope directly instead of routing through `_parse_scope_body`, so a body-local `pl.dump_tag` was silently dropped. Both paths now call `_merge_forward_sticky_dump` and attach the result to the auto-outlined `InCore` scope, so the tag survives outlining onto the inner kernel `Call`. Orchestration codegen's `BuildWrapperReorderedParams` correspondingly matches selective-dump vars against the **inner** kernel Call's `dump_vars` (where a body-local tag lands after `OutlineIncoreScopes`) in addition to the outer wrapper Call's.

### Leveled tensor dump (runtime simpler#953)

The runtime now latches the dump **level** host-side at `dump_tensor_init` from `CallConfig.enable_dump_tensor`, race-free regardless of submit order — replacing the orch-body `enable_dump_tensor_selective()` toggle.

- `RunConfig.enable_dump_tensor` becomes an `int` level: `0`=off, `1`=partial (only `pl.dump_tag` / `dumps=` marked tensors), `2`=full (every task). `bool` stays back-compatible (`True`→`1`, `False`→`0`).
- `--dump-tensor` takes an optional `LEVEL` (bare flag = `1`) in `conftest` and `replay`; `RunConfig` / `_DfxOpts` / `execute_on_device` thread the level through and gate DFX on `> 0`.
- Orchestration codegen drops `enable_dump_tensor_selective()` and the `selective_dump_emitted_` gating; it now emits only the per-task `Arg::dump(...)` markers.

### Docs & runtime

- EN + zh-CN updates to `03-runtime-dfx.md` (flag matrix → int level, selective-dump section, three-level semantics) and `language/00-python_syntax.md`.
- Runtime submodule bumped to `48980572` (latest `simpler` main) — brings in the leveled `--dump-tensor` (off/partial/full) and race-free selective dump (simpler#953) plus subsequent runtime main commits.

## Testing

- [x] UT for `kernel_config` signature emission and `OrchestrationResult` signature population
- [x] UT for `pl.dump_tag` / `dumps=` parser, codegen (forward-sticky, post-outline), and inline/outline propagation
- [x] UT for for-form / split `pl.spmd` dump_tag propagation (`test_dump_tag_reaches_for_form_spmd_dispatch`) — IR inner-call `dump_vars` + emitted `.dump(...)`
- [x] UT for `RunConfig` leveled `enable_dump_tensor` (level + bool back-compat, DFX gating)
- [x] ST repro exercising selective dump end-to-end
- [x] Full UT suite green

## Related Issues

Fixes #1458

title: [Bug] TaskId array element scalar deps are not registered in auto-scope codegen
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

`pl.submit(..., deps=[...])` supports explicit TaskId dependencies in ordinary auto-tracked orchestration, not only inside `pl.manual_scope()`. However, when a user first reads a `TaskId` array slot into a scalar variable and then uses that scalar as an explicit dependency, orchestration codegen fails:

```python
prev = tids[0]
out, _ = pl.submit(self.consumer, x, deps=[prev])
```

The IR correctly represents `prev` as:

```python
prev__ssa_v0: pl.Scalar[pl.TASK_ID] = pl.array.get_element(tids__ssa_v1, 0)
```

and the downstream call still carries:

```python
deps=[prev__ssa_v0]
```

But `EmitManualDeps()` resolves every explicit dependency through `manual_task_id_map_`, and `array.get_element(Array[TASK_ID]) -> Scalar[TASK_ID]` is not registered there in ordinary auto scope. The result is an internal codegen error:

```text
Internal error: manual_dep_edge var 'prev__ssa_v0' has no producer task in current manual scope
```

There is also a related implementation hazard: simply registering every `TaskId` scalar outside manual scopes is not sufficient by itself, because `manual_task_id_map_` is currently restored only for `manual_scope`, not for every generated C++ lexical `PTO2_SCOPE`. A separate witness can generate C++ where a `PTO2TaskId` local declared inside an inner `PTO2_SCOPE` is referenced from the outer scope.

So the fix likely needs two parts:

1. Register `array.get_element` results of `Array[TASK_ID]` as valid scalar explicit dependency sources.
2. Make `manual_task_id_map_` bindings obey C++ lexical scope lifetime, for example with scoped undo frames tied to `PushCppScope()` / `PopCppScope()`.


### Steps to Reproduce


Use this orchestration shape:

```python
@pl.program
class ManualTaskIdMapArraySlotDepWitness:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def k1(self, x: pl.Tensor[[64], pl.FP32]) -> pl.Tensor[[64], pl.FP32]:
        return x

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def k2(self, x: pl.Tensor[[64], pl.FP32]) -> pl.Tensor[[64], pl.FP32]:
        return x

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def k3(self, x: pl.Tensor[[64], pl.FP32]) -> pl.Tensor[[64], pl.FP32]:
        return x

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
    def main(
        self,
        x: pl.Tensor[[64], pl.FP32],
        out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[64], pl.FP32]],
    ) -> pl.Tensor[[64], pl.FP32]:
        tids = pl.array.create(1, pl.TASK_ID)
        seed, seed_tid = pl.submit(self.k1, x)
        a, tid = pl.submit(self.k2, x)
        tids[0] = tid
        prev = tids[0]
        b, _ = pl.submit(self.k3, x, deps=[seed_tid, prev])
        return b
```

Then run the program through the default pipeline / orchestration codegen.


### Expected Behavior


`prev = tids[0]` should be usable as a scalar `TaskId` explicit dependency source.

Codegen should emit a dependency stack array for the consumer and fill it from the scalar `prev` binding, preserving the snapshot semantics of the local scalar value.


### Actual Behavior


Codegen fails in `EmitManualDeps()` because `prev__ssa_v0` is not present in `manual_task_id_map_`:

```text
Internal error: manual_dep_edge var 'prev__ssa_v0' has no producer task in current manual scope
Check failed: it != manual_task_id_map_.end()
src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:1636
```

The relevant passdump still contains the expected dependency edge:

```python
tids__ssa_v1: pl.Array[1, pl.TASK_ID] = pl.array.update_element(tids__ssa_v0, 0, tid__ssa_v0)
prev__ssa_v0: pl.Scalar[pl.TASK_ID] = pl.array.get_element(tids__ssa_v1, 0)
_submit_tmp__ssa_v0_2 = self.k3(
    x__ssa_v0,
    deps=[seed_tid__ssa_v0, prev__ssa_v0],
    attrs={"arg_directions": [pl.adir.input]},
)
```


### Git Commit ID

90220ebba957907a689be85e812fc2d830357461

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

macOS (aarch64)

### Additional Context


A related lifetime witness shows why this should not be fixed as a one-line registration change only.

This program shape:

```python
with pl.auto_scope():
    a, scoped_tid = pl.submit(self.k1, x)
b, _ = pl.submit(self.k2, x, deps=[scoped_tid])
```

can generate C++ like:

```cpp
PTO2_SCOPE() {
    PTO2_SCOPE() {
        TaskOutputTensors task_0_outs = rt_submit_aiv_task(0, params_t0);
        PTO2TaskId scoped_tid = task_0_outs.task_id();
    }

    PTO2TaskId params_t1_deps[1];
    uint32_t params_t1_deps_count = 0;
    if (scoped_tid.is_valid()) params_t1_deps[params_t1_deps_count++] = scoped_tid;
    params_t1.set_dependencies(params_t1_deps, params_t1_deps_count);
}
```

Here `scoped_tid` is declared inside the inner C++ block but referenced outside it. This suggests `manual_task_id_map_` needs lexical-scope-aware lifetime management, not just more registrations.

title: [Pass Bug] `FlattenTileNdTo2D` rejects non-`ConstInt` tile dimensions on 3D+ dynamic tensors
body:
### Pass Name

`FlattenTileNdTo2D`

### Description

When operating on 3D+ tensors with a **dynamic** leading dimension inside
`pl.at` (InCore), the tile shapes forwarded to `FlattenTileNdTo2D` contain
non-`ConstInt` scalars.  The pass requires all tile dimensions to be static
(`ConstInt`) before it can flatten ND tiles to 2D for the hardware.

With **2D tensors** the same pattern works because tile ops are already 2D
and `FlattenTileNdTo2D` has nothing to flatten.  This only triggers when the
tensor rank is 3+ and a dynamic dimension contributes to the tile shape.

### Git Commit ID

90220ebb

### Before IR (Input)

```python
import pypto.language as pl

B_DYN = pl.dynamic("B_DYN")
S_DYN = pl.dynamic("S_DYN")


@pl.jit.inline
def kernel(
    x: pl.Tensor[[B_DYN, S_DYN, 512], pl.BF16],
    out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[B_DYN, S_DYN, 512], pl.FP32]],
):
    b_dim = pl.tensor.dim(x, 0)
    TILE = 8
    for batch_base_idx in pl.parallel(0, b_dim // TILE):
        batch_base = batch_base_idx * TILE
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="inner"):
            for inner in pl.range(TILE):
                global_idx = batch_base + inner
                # 3D tensor + dynamic dim -> FlattenTileNdTo2D rejects
                out[global_idx : global_idx + 1, :] = pl.cast(
                    x[global_idx : global_idx + 1, :], target_type=pl.FP32)
    return out
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

```python
`FlattenTileNdTo2D` should handle dynamic tile dimensions by either:
- Emitting a runtime-computed flatten (loop over the dynamic dimension)
- Or passing dynamic dimensions through without flattening when possible
```

### Actual IR or Error

```shell
ValueError: FlattenTileNdTo2D: tile dimension 1 must be static (ConstInt) for tile op 'tile.load'
Check failed: As<ConstInt>(tile_type->shape_[i]) at src/ir/transforms/flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp:255
```

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform (if relevant)

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

## Workaround

Reshape to 2D before entering InCore:

```python
x_flat = pl.reshape(x, [bs, 512])
out_flat = pl.reshape(out, [bs, 512])
for idx in pl.parallel(0, bs):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="inner"):
        out_flat[idx : idx + 1, :] = pl.cast(x_flat[idx : idx + 1, :], target_type=pl.FP32)
out = pl.reshape(out_flat, [b_dim, s_dim, 512])
```

title: [Bug] `pl.spmd` composite dynamic `core_num` not materialized in orchestration codegen
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

`pl.spmd` accepts compile-time constants or a single `pl.Scalar` variable as
`core_num`.  When a **composite expression** involving a dynamic dimension
(e.g. `b_dim * STATIC` or `b_dim // TILE`) is passed, the IR accepts it but
the orchestration C++ codegen fails to materialize the expression as a named
variable, producing an undeclared-variable error.

### What works

| Expression | Result |
|---|---|
| `pl.spmd(512)` (ConstInt) | OK |
| `pl.spmd(b_dim * s_dim)` (dyn * dyn) | OK — pypto folds correctly |
| `pl.spmd(b_dim * 64)` (dyn * static) | **Broken** |
| `pl.spmd(b_dim // 8)` (dyn // static) | **Broken** |

### Steps to Reproduce

```markdown
## Steps to Reproduce

Save as `repro_spmd_composite.py` and run `python repro_spmd_composite.py -p a2a3sim`:


import pypto.language as pl

B_DYN = pl.dynamic("B_DYN")
STATIC_DIM = 64


@pl.jit.inline
def kernel(
    x: pl.Tensor[[B_DYN, STATIC_DIM, 64], pl.BF16],
    out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[B_DYN, STATIC_DIM, 64], pl.FP32]],
):
    b_dim = pl.tensor.dim(x, 0)
    CORES = b_dim * STATIC_DIM  # dyn * static composite
    for idx in pl.spmd(CORES, name_hint="fail"):
        out[idx : idx + 1, :, :] = pl.cast(x[idx : idx + 1, :, :], target_type=pl.FP32)
    return out


@pl.jit
def kernel_test(
    x: pl.Tensor[[B_DYN, STATIC_DIM, 64], pl.BF16],
    out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[B_DYN, STATIC_DIM, 64], pl.FP32]],
):
    x.bind_dynamic(0, B_DYN)
    out.bind_dynamic(0, B_DYN)
    out = kernel(x, out)
    return out


def build_specs():
    import torch
    from golden import TensorSpec

    B = 8
    return [
        TensorSpec("x", [B, 64, 64], torch.bfloat16),
        TensorSpec("out", [B, 64, 64], torch.float32, is_output=True),
    ]


def golden_fn(values):
    import torch
    values["out"] = values["x"].float()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from golden import run_jit

    result = run_jit(
        fn=kernel_test,
        specs=build_specs(),
        golden_fn=golden_fn,
        runtime_cfg=dict(platform="a2a3sim", device_id=0),
    )
    print(f"PASSED={result.passed}")
    if result.error:
        print(f"ERROR: {result.error}")
```

### Expected Behavior

`pl.spmd(b_dim * 64)` should compile and run.  The orchestration codegen
should materialize the composite expression as a local `int64_t` variable
before passing it to `launch_spec.set_block_num()`.

### Actual Behavior

```
orchestration/kernel_test.cpp:36:45: error: 'CORES_inline1' was not declared in this scope
```

The generated C++ references `CORES_inline1` but never declares it.


### Git Commit ID

90220ebb

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

## Workaround

Use `pl.parallel` (dynamic) instead of `pl.spmd` for dynamic iteration counts:

```python
for idx in pl.parallel(0, b_dim):
    for hb in pl.spmd(STATIC_DIM // TILE, name_hint="ok"):
        ...
```

Or split the outer dimension into `pl.parallel` + inner static `pl.spmd`.

title: [Pass Bug] ConvertToSSA + orchestration codegen: phi node naming swap when Scalar and Tensor are mixed in loop carry
body:
### Pass Name

`ConvertToSSA` + orchestration C++ codegen

### Description

When a `pl.Scalar` variable (e.g. `global_c_idx`) is defined inside a `pl.spmd`
body and the same name is reused in a later `pl.parallel` + `pl.at` +
`pl.range` scope that writes to multiple output tensors, the `ConvertToSSA`
pass promotes the scalar into the outer `pl.parallel` `init_values` tuple,
**mixed with** the tensor carries.  The orchestration codegen then generates
phi nodes with swapped variable names, assigning `const Tensor&` to `int64_t`
or referencing undeclared variables.

This is **not a dynamic-shape issue** — it reproduces with fully static
dimensions.  The root cause is the combination of:
1. Same variable name used across two scopes
2. Scalar promoted into init_values mixed with Tensors
3. Phi node codegen loses track of types during name assignment

### Git Commit ID

90220ebb

### Before IR (Input)

```python
import pypto.language as pl

B = 64
DIM = 512
TILE = 8


@pl.jit.inline
def kernel(
    x: pl.Tensor[[B, DIM], pl.BF16],
    out_a: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[B, DIM], pl.FP32]],
    out_b: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[B, DIM], pl.FP32]],
    out_c: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[B, DIM], pl.FP32]],
):
    # Scope A: pl.spmd defines "global_c_idx" inside body
    for idx in pl.spmd(B, name_hint="scope_a"):
        global_c_idx = idx
        tile = pl.cast(x[global_c_idx : global_c_idx + 1, :], target_type=pl.FP32)
        out_a = pl.assemble(out_a, tile, [global_c_idx, 0])

    # Scope B: reuses "global_c_idx" + multiple tensor carries
    for batch_base_idx in pl.parallel(0, B // TILE):
        batch_base = batch_base_idx * TILE
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="scope_b"):
            for inner in pl.range(TILE):
                global_c_idx = batch_base + inner
                tile = pl.cast(x[global_c_idx : global_c_idx + 1, :], target_type=pl.FP32)
                out_b[global_c_idx : global_c_idx + 1, :] = tile
                out_c[global_c_idx : global_c_idx + 1, :] = tile
    return out_a, out_b, out_c
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

```python
The orchestration C++ should generate phi nodes with correct types —
`int64_t` for scalar carries, `const Tensor&` for tensor carries — and
correctly pair each phi assignment with its corresponding variable name.
```

### Actual IR or Error

```shell
orchestration/kernel_test.cpp:68:32: error: 'out_b__rv_v4' was not declared in this scope
             out_b__rv_v2 = out_b__rv_v4;


Generated orchestration C++ shows the swap:


int64_t global_c_idx_inline5__rv_v2 = global_c_idx_inline5;
Tensor out_b__rv_v2 = ext_out_b;
Tensor out_c__rv_v2 = ext_out_c;
// ...
rt_submit_aiv_task(1, params_t1);
int64_t global_c_idx_inline5__rv_v4 = 0;
const Tensor& out_c__rv_v4 = out_b__rv_v2;       // WRONG: out_c assigned out_b
const Tensor& tile_inline4__rv_v4 = out_c__rv_v2; // WRONG: tile assigned out_c
global_c_idx_inline5__rv_v2 = global_c_idx_inline5__rv_v4;
out_b__rv_v2 = out_b__rv_v4;                      // WRONG: out_b__rv_v4 undeclared
out_c__rv_v2 = out_c__rv_v4;
tile_inline4__rv_v2 = tile_inline4__rv_v4;


The phi node for `out_b` is named `out_b__rv_v4` but the codegen emits it as
`out_c__rv_v4`.  The variables are rotated by one position.
```

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform (if relevant)

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

## Root Cause Chain

1. `ConvertToSSA` sees `global_c_idx` used across two scopes and promotes it
   into the `pl.parallel` init_values tuple alongside `out_b`, `out_c`, etc.
2. The init_values become `(Tensor, Tensor, Scalar, Tensor, ...)` — mixed types.
3. Orchestration codegen emits phi nodes after the InCore task but assigns
   variable names with an off-by-one or swapped mapping for the mixed tuple.

## Workaround

Use **distinct variable names** in each scope, or restructure so the scalar
is a loop iterator variable (not defined inside spmd body):

```python
# Option A: unique names
for idx in pl.spmd(B, name_hint="scope_a"):
    row_idx = idx  # unique name, not reused
    ...

# Option B: pl.parallel for outer, spmd only for inner static count
for global_c_idx in pl.parallel(0, B):
    for col_idx in pl.spmd(DIM // TILE, name_hint="scope_a"):
        ...
```

title: fix(codegen): map orchestration return aliases via callee ReturnStmt
body:
Fixes #1573.

Orchestration tuple/submit alias generation mapped each return-tuple element onto a callee Out/InOut param using a tail-alignment heuristic over all Out/InOut indices. When a kernel takes an InOut param that is written in place but not part of the return tuple, that param still sat in the index list, so `tuple_arity < out_indices.size()` forced a base of 0 and shifted every alias by one — each loop carry / phi bound to the wrong source tensor (wrong shape/dtype). Downstream this triggered an AICPU `valid_reshape` assert or a scheduler timeout on deps that could never resolve.

Generalize `FindReturnedParamIndex` to `FindReturnedParamIndices`, which traces every `ReturnStmt` value back to its source param, giving a precise return-position to param map. `GenerateTupleReturnAliases` and `GenerateSubmitReturnAliases` now consume it (memoized per callee), and fall back to the legacy direction-based heuristic only when the callee has no traceable top-level ReturnStmt (Group/Spmd wrappers) or a tensor return position fails to trace.

title: fix(codegen): make array-slot TaskId reads usable as submit deps
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1577.

- **Register `array.get_element` TASK_ID results as explicit dep sources.** Reading a TaskId array slot into a scalar (`prev = tids[k]`) produced a `PTO2TaskId` snapshot local that was never registered in `manual_task_id_map_`, so a downstream `pl.submit(..., deps=[prev])` aborted orchestration codegen with *"manual_dep_edge var '...' has no producer task in current manual scope"*. The slot read is now registered (bound to the snapshot local), so it resolves as a valid dependency source. Binding to the local — not the `arr[k]` slot — preserves snapshot semantics: a later `tids[k] = ...` overwrite does not retroactively change `prev`.
- **Scope TaskId / array-carry bindings to every `PTO2_SCOPE` (AUTO and MANUAL), not just manual scopes.** A binding produced inside a scope names a C++ local that dies at the block's closing brace; without scoping it leaked to the enclosing scope, where a later `set_dependencies` referenced a now-out-of-scope identifier (uncompilable C++). The snapshot is by copy so outer bindings stay visible inside the block; loop/branch carries are registered before their body's `PTO2_SCOPE` and so correctly survive.

## Changes

- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp` — both fixes above.
- `tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py` — two regression tests:
  - `test_array_slot_task_id_usable_as_submit_dep` — the issue's primary witness (`prev = tids[0]` → `deps=[seed_tid, prev]`).
  - `test_task_id_binding_does_not_leak_past_pl_scope` — a producer TaskId inside a nested `pl.scope()` is no longer referenced after the block closes.
- `docs/en/dev/codegen/01-orchestration_codegen.md` + zh-cn mirror — document the array-slot dep source and the lexical-scope lifetime rule.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/ut/codegen/` — 344 passed (manual_scope / array-carry / submit-deps coverage).
- [x] New regression tests pass; both fail on the pre-fix codegen.
- [x] `test_manual_scope_inner_deps_can_reference_outer_scope_tid` still passes (snapshot-by-copy preserves outer-tid visibility inside a scope).

## Notes

- The regression tests scope the pipeline to BASIC (property) verification, mirroring existing orchestration codegen tests: `pl.submit(..., deps=[...])` in an auto orchestration does not survive a print→parse roundtrip after `DeriveCallDirections` (a separate, pre-existing printer/parser issue, unrelated to the codegen behaviour fixed here; production compile does not run the roundtrip instrument).
- Known follow-up: an explicit dep crossing an AUTO `pl.scope()` boundary is now dropped rather than emitting broken C++. Emitting it correctly requires hoisting the producer TaskId's declaration (cross-scope liveness), out of scope here.

title: fix(spmd): Preserve composite dynamic core_num through Simplify DCE
body:
## Summary

`pl.spmd(core_num)` with a composite dynamic expression (e.g. `b_dim * 64`, `b_dim // 8`) failed orchestration C++ codegen with `'CORES_inline1' was not declared in this scope`.

**Root cause:** scope outlining moves the `core_num` expression onto the dispatched Spmd function as a function attr whose Vars are defined in the *caller* Orchestration function. Orchestration codegen evaluates `core_num` at the call site, so the defining scalar must survive in the caller. The final per-function `Simplify` scalar-DCE deleted it — it sees no in-function use, because the only consumer is a *sibling* function's attr — leaving codegen to reference an undeclared variable.

## Changes

- **`Simplify` is now program-aware** (`TransformSimplifyProgram`): collects every Var referenced by any function's `core_num` attr and shields them from scalar DCE, so the defining scalar survives. Per-function behavior is otherwise unchanged.
- **`EliminateDeadScalarAssignments`** gains an opt-in `protected_vars` overload; `EliminateDeadCodeCore` seeds them as live roots (transitive RHS uses stay live via the existing fixed point).
- **`RenderLaunchCoreNum`** falls through to `GenerateExprString`, so a composite scalar expression also renders correctly (same path used for `ForStmt` bounds).
- **`pl.spmd(core_num)`** is typed `RangeArg` (`int | Scalar`), aligning with `pl.range` / `pl.parallel`.

## Testing

- New functional ST `tests/st/codegen/dsl/test_spmd_dynamic_core_num.py` dispatches `pl.spmd` with `dyn*static` (`b_dim * MID`) and `dyn//static` (`b_dim // 2`) core_num expressions and verifies the output matches a torch golden end-to-end (passes on device, `--platform=a2a3`).
- C++ builds clean; clang-tidy/clang-format/cpplint/ruff/pyright pass.
- Regression suites pass: transforms UT, pass UT, spmd UT, DCE/Simplify UT.

## Related Issues

Fixes #1579

title: feat: cross-core pipe slot_num/local_slot_num + ptoas v0.42
body:
## Summary

- **Bump ptoas to v0.42** across all CI jobs (aarch64 + x86_64 SHA256).
- **Expose explicit cross-core ring-buffer depth**: add optional `slot_num` and `local_slot_num` kwargs to `pl.aic_initialize_pipe` / `pl.aiv_initialize_pipe`, so users can pin the depth instead of relying on the PTOAS-derived default (8 unidirectional, 4 per direction bidirectional).
- Wired end-to-end: DSL → `system.aic/aiv_initialize_pipe` op attrs → PTO codegen → `MixedKernelExpanded` verifier. Attributes are emitted **only when set**; omitting them keeps the current behavior (PTOAS default).

## Arch-dependent reserve-buffer sizing

When you set these knobs you size the reserved/imported buffer yourself, and the formula depends on the target arch:

- **a3**: `slot_size * local_slot_num`
- **a5**: `slot_size * slot_num`

`local_slot_num` is a2/a3 only (must be `> 0` and `<= slot_num`; the consumer buffer must lower to a `local_addr`).

## Validation

- New tests: codegen emission (`slot_num` + `local_slot_num`), print/parse round-trip, and negative DSL validation.
- Local run: 116 cross-core / mixed-kernel / system-op unit tests pass.
- Verified against the real **ptoas v0.42** binary: `slot_num=16, local_slot_num=4` accepted on a3 and a5; `slot_num=0` and `local_slot_num > slot_num` rejected by the ptoas op verifier.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on the v0.42 toolchain
- [ ] Cross-core system tests on device (a3 / a5)

title: [Bug] Orchestration codegen mis-infers add_output for partial slice-write to outer pl.create_tensor in pl.spmd body
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

When an outer-scope `pl.create_tensor` is **partial-slice written** from inside a `pl.spmd(N)` body — where a single spmd block writes multiple disjoint sub-slices (typically via an inner `pl.range`), the orchestration codegen mis-infers the tensor's IO role as `params.add_output(...)` instead of `params.add_inout(...)`. In ratio4 decode_compressor this causes the downstream consumers to read partly correct, partly garbage data, manifesting as ~5% magnitude drift in the kv / cmp_kv_cache outputs.

The codegen heuristic appears to be: "tensor is first written here → emit add_output". This is correct only when one spmd block produces THE WHOLE tensor (1:1 mapping between task index and a complete slice). It is **wrong** when a block writes a strict subset of the tensor and other blocks contribute the rest — the runtime semantics of `add_output` then make the partial writes lost / aliased per-task instead of aggregated, while `add_inout` would correctly share the GM allocation across all blocks.

Counter-intuitively, even though `pooled_kv` is genuinely first written in `softmax_pool` (no prior consumer), it MUST be `add_inout` for this multi-partial-writer pattern, because the producer is collective across all spmd blocks, not one block.

I attempted a minimal repro with several variants (B=8/64, with/without POST padding, with/without `if`-gate, with multi-stage V compute) — orchestration always emits the same `add_output(buf)` mis-inference, but the runtime correctly handles the partial writes in all those simpler cases. The failure only manifests in the full ratio4 site, suggesting the runtime path that loses partial writes additionally requires something specific to ratio4's DAG (cross-scope alias chain, block_table indirection, scheduling order, or buffer size threshold). The codegen-side mis-inference is independent of that runtime trigger.

### Steps to Reproduce

```
1. Check out the perf-cmp4 branch of pypto-lib at commit f680e61a.

2. Modify softmax_pool from the flat form
       for idx in pl.spmd(B * (HEAD_DIM // HEAD_TILE), name_hint='softmax_pool'):
           c_idx = idx // (HEAD_DIM // HEAD_TILE)
           h0 = (idx % (HEAD_DIM // HEAD_TILE)) * HEAD_TILE
           ...
           pooled_kv[c_idx * POST_TILE : c_idx * POST_TILE + 1, h0 : h0 + HEAD_TILE] = pooled_chunk
   to the nested form
       for c_idx in pl.spmd(B, name_hint='softmax_pool'):
           ...
           if pos_b + S >= COMPRESS_RATIO:
               for hb in pl.range(HEAD_DIM // HEAD_TILE):
                   h0 = hb * HEAD_TILE
                   ...
                   pooled_kv[c_idx * POST_TILE : c_idx * POST_TILE + 1, h0 : h0 + HEAD_TILE] = pooled_chunk

3. Run:
   python models/deepseek/v4/decode_compressor_ratio4.py -p a2a3 -d 0

4. Inspect orchestration/compressor_test.cpp Task 2 — it emits:
   params_t2.add_output(pooled_kv_inline51);
   params_t2.launch_spec.set_block_num(64);

5. Hand-patch the orchestration to:
   params_t2.add_inout(pooled_kv_inline51);
   then rerun with --runtime-dir <build_dir> --golden-data <build_dir>/data.
   All three outputs (kv / compress_state / cmp_kv_cache) PASS and spmd still launches with set_block_num(64) — i.e. truly parallel, partial writes correctly aggregated.
```

### Expected Behavior

When a spmd / parallel body writes only a strict subset of an outer-scope `pl.create_tensor` (i.e. one block's writes do not cover the entire tensor's address space), codegen should emit `params.add_inout(...)` for that tensor. The current heuristic of "first-write → add_output" is only correct for full-tensor producers (1:1 block-to-slice mapping where a single block writes a complete identifiable region). Detecting the multi-partial-writer case requires looking at slice coverage per block, not just write-vs-read direction.

### Actual Behavior

Codegen emits `params.add_output(pooled_kv)` whenever the spmd body first-writes the tensor, regardless of whether the block writes the whole tensor or a partial slice. Hand-patching `add_output` → `add_inout` corrects the ratio4 outputs.

Confirmed via runtime_dir + golden_data hand-patch on commit f680e61a (perf-cmp4 branch of pypto-lib) — changing only that one line in `orchestration/compressor_test.cpp` makes all three validated outputs PASS while keeping `set_block_num(64)` (i.e. truly parallel; spmd add_inout does NOT serialize).

Note: the same hand-patch on a `pl.parallel(N)` variant of the same code (instead of `pl.spmd(N)`) also corrects the outputs but serializes the tasks — `pl.parallel + add_inout` enforces RAW dep across blocks, `pl.spmd + add_inout` does not. So the codegen IO inference bug is independent of the spmd-vs-parallel distinction, but the workaround "just force inout" gives different perf characteristics depending on loop kind.

### Git Commit ID

90220ebba957907a689be85e812fc2d830357461

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- pypto-lib commit: f680e61a (branch perf-cmp4), pto-isa: 2c607938 on main, pypto runtime submodule: 324df3d6.
- Quick verification trick: use runtime_dir + golden_data, hand-edit `orchestration/<test>.cpp` `add_output(pooled_kv...)` → `add_inout(pooled_kv...)`, rerun with `--runtime-dir <build>` `--golden-data <build>/data`. If the failing test starts to PASS without recompilation, the codegen IO inference is the bug.
- Minimal repro attempts (B=8/64, POST padding, if-gate, multi-stage V compute) all showed the same `add_output(buf)` mis-inference in orchestration but PASSed validation, suggesting the runtime path that loses partial writes additionally requires the full ratio4 DAG. The codegen-side bug is independent and easily diagnosable from the orchestration cpp.

title: [Bug] pl.tensor.scatter on 1-row src tile triggers tile.ci cols!=1 ISA check
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

`pl.tensor.scatter(dst [1, N], index [1, M], src [1, M], dim=-1)` — i.e. any scatter where the destination buffer has exactly 1 row — fails compilation at `convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass` with:

\`\`\`
ValueError: The operator tile.ci requires the innermost dimension (Cols) to be != 1, got 1
Check failed: last_dim && last_dim->value_ != 1 at /data/czq/pypto/src/ir/op/tile_ops/memory.cpp:486
\`\`\`

Bumping the row count to ≥ 2 (e.g. 16) makes the same pattern compile fine. So the lowering of the gather→scatter chain on a single-row tile creates an internal `[1, 1]` tile.ci which the ISA rejects.

This blocks shrinking RoPE-reassembly POST_TILE padding from 16 down to 1 in `models/deepseek/v4/decode_compressor_ratio4.py`. The reassembly is:

\`\`\`python
kv_rope_slice = normed_kv[c_idx * POST_TILE : c_idx * POST_TILE + 1, NOPE_HEAD_DIM : HEAD_DIM]  # [1, ROPE_HEAD_DIM]
even_tile = pl.gather(kv_rope_slice, mask_pattern=pl.tile.MaskPattern.P0101)
odd_tile = pl.gather(kv_rope_slice, mask_pattern=pl.tile.MaskPattern.P1010)
rope_buf = pl.full([1, ROPE_HEAD_DIM], dtype=pl.FP32, value=0.0)
rope_buf = pl.tensor.scatter(rope_buf, dim=-1, index=even_idx[0:1, :], src=rope_even)
rope_buf = pl.tensor.scatter(rope_buf, dim=-1, index=odd_idx[0:1, :], src=rope_odd)
\`\`\`

The same code shape with `POST_TILE` rows everywhere works. Single-row variant fails as above.

### Steps to Reproduce

Minimal repro file (40 lines) — toggle `ROWS = 1` (fails) vs `ROWS = 16` (compiles):

\`\`\`python
import pypto.language as pl

B = 4
ROWS = 1        # 1: triggers tile.ci cols!=1 bug. 16: compiles.
RHD = 64
HALF = RHD // 2
ROW_DIM = B * ROWS

@pl.jit.inline
def kernel(x, even_idx, odd_idx, out):
    for b in pl.parallel(B):
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint='repro'):
            x_slice = x[b * ROWS : (b + 1) * ROWS, 0 : RHD]                          # [ROWS, RHD]
            even_tile = pl.gather(x_slice, mask_pattern=pl.tile.MaskPattern.P0101)    # [ROWS, HALF]
            odd_tile = pl.gather(x_slice, mask_pattern=pl.tile.MaskPattern.P1010)
            rope_buf = pl.full([ROWS, RHD], dtype=pl.FP32, value=0.0)
            rope_buf = pl.tensor.scatter(rope_buf, dim=-1, index=even_idx, src=even_tile)
            rope_buf = pl.tensor.scatter(rope_buf, dim=-1, index=odd_idx, src=odd_tile)
            out[b * ROWS : (b + 1) * ROWS, 0 : RHD] = rope_buf
    return out
\`\`\`

Full repro committed: `models/deepseek/v4/repro_1row_scatter_draft.py` in pypto-lib branch `perf-cmp4` at f680e61a.

Run:
\`\`\`
python models/deepseek/v4/repro_1row_scatter_draft.py -p a2a3 -d 0
\`\`\`

With ROWS=1 → compile fails with tile.ci cols!=1. With ROWS=16 → compiles fine (validation off because the golden is identity but the kernel is non-trivial — that part is unrelated to the bug).

### Expected Behavior

The `pl.tensor.scatter` chain on a 1-row src/dst tile should compile and produce correct semantics — scatter is shape-polymorphic on the row dimension; the ISA's cols!=1 constraint applies to the COLUMN dimension and shouldn't transitively block a row=1 case via an internal `[1, 1]` lowering.

### Actual Behavior

\`convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass\` lowering of the gather→scatter chain on a row=1 tile internally creates a `[1, 1]` tile.ci that fails the ISA `cols != 1` check. The error position reported is `<string>:13:30` which corresponds to the function parameter list (i.e., not the actual op site — the trace is misleading), but the root cause is the scatter lowering path.

### Git Commit ID

90220ebba957907a689be85e812fc2d830357461

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- pypto-lib: f680e61a (branch perf-cmp4), pto-isa: 2c607938 on main, pypto runtime submodule: 324df3d6.
- Workaround: keep RoPE reassembly at POST_TILE=16 rows. The first row is meaningful, rows 1..15 are zero padding artifacts. Wasteful (2MB normed_kv vs 128KB) but functional.
- Related observation: `pl.read(tile, [0, 0])` + `pl.mul(tile [1, N], scalar)` DOES work in pypto and lets RMSNorm normalize step use a 1-row scalar broadcast instead of POST_TILE col_vec. The blocker is only the RoPE scatter step.

title: fix(codegen): emit scalar return carries as scalars, not Tensor aliases (#1580)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1580 — orchestration phi-node naming swap for a mixed scalar/tensor `pl.parallel` loop carry.

This builds on #1581 (which landed first). When `ConvertToSSA` promotes a `pl.Scalar` (defined in a `pl.spmd` body, reused by name in a later `pl.parallel` + `pl.at` + `pl.range` scope) into the parallel loop's `init_values`, the carry tuple becomes `(global_c_idx, out_b, out_c, tile)` — a scalar leads, output tensors sit in the middle, a passthrough tile trails.

- **#1581** fixed the **tensor-rotation** half: the precise return→param map (`FindReturnedParamIndices`) now binds `out_b`/`out_c`/`tile` to the correct source tensors instead of rotating them by one.
- This PR fixes the remaining **scalar** half. A scalar carry that traces to a scalar param was still routed through the tensor-aliasing path, because the scalar default was only emitted in the `!param_idx_opt` (untraced) branch. A scalar that *resolved* to a param fell through to `EmitTensorAlias`:

```cpp
int64_t       global_c_idx__rv_v2 = global_c_idx;
const Tensor& global_c_idx__rv_v4 = global_c_idx__rv_v2;   // binds Tensor& to int64_t → won't compile
```

## Fix

In `GenerateTupleReturnAliases` and `GenerateSubmitReturnAliases`, hoist the `ScalarType` check **ahead of** the param-writeback aliasing. A scalar return position carries no runtime output (the device cannot hand a scalar back through task submission), so it materializes a safe `<ctype> name = 0;` default and skips aliasing — regardless of whether the precise map resolved it to a param. The `!param_idx_opt` branch is now tensor-only (untraced tensor → left undeclared, unchanged).

Resulting phi block for the #1580 scenario:

```cpp
int64_t       global_c_idx__rv_v4 = 0;
const Tensor& out_b__rv_v4 = out_b__rv_v2;
const Tensor& out_c__rv_v4 = out_c__rv_v2;
const Tensor& tile__rv_v4  = tile__rv_v2;
```

## Changes

- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`: scalar-type guard before tensor aliasing in both return-alias functions.

## Tests

- `tests/st/codegen/dsl/test_mixed_scalar_tensor_carry.py` — hardware-free codegen guard: asserts no undeclared `__rv_v*` rvalue, no tensor carry aliased to a different carry's value, and **no Tensor binding to a scalar-typed carry**. The third check fails on the #1581-only codegen and passes after this fix (verified by building `origin/main` and re-running).
- `tests/st/runtime/scheduling/test_mixed_carry_phi_swap.py` — end-to-end reproduction: compiles and runs the mixed scalar/tensor parallel-loop carry and checks all three outputs equal `x` cast to FP32.

## Validation

- Rebased onto latest `origin/main` (includes #1581).
- New codegen guard fails on `origin/main` (Tensor bound to scalar `global_c_idx__rv_v2`), passes on this branch.
- All 369 codegen UTs (incl. the 88 orchestration UTs / #1581's additions) pass.
- The runtime ST kernel passes orchestration codegen cleanly; full device run needs the ptoas toolchain / device.

title: feat(ir): preserve dynamic valid_shape when FlattenTileNdTo2D flattens >2D tiles (#1578)
body:
## Problem

A 3D+ tensor with a `pl.dynamic` dimension that flows into a tile shape inside an `pl.at` (InCore) scope produces a >2D tile with a dynamic extent. `FlattenTileNdTo2D` must lower that tile to 2D for the hardware, but it required *every* tile dimension to be a compile-time `ConstInt` and bailed out:

```
ValueError: FlattenTileNdTo2D: tile dimension 1 must be static (ConstInt) for tile op 'tile.load'
```

The 2D case works because there is nothing to flatten; the failure is specific to rank-3+ tensors where a dynamic dimension contributes to the tile shape.

## Approach (the user writes the loop)

Hardware tiles map to fixed-size on-chip buffers, so the *physical* tile shape genuinely must be static; the runtime extent belongs in `TileView.valid_shape`. The chunk size is a real performance knob, so the pass does not synthesize a loop. Instead the user chunks the dynamic dimension themselves: iterate it with `pl.range` in a static `CHUNK` step and load each chunk as a static physical `[1, CHUNK, 512]` tile whose `valid_shapes` carries the runtime tail `min(CHUNK, s - c)`.

```python
# User-written: chunk the dynamic S dim, clamp the tail in valid_shapes.
for c, (o,) in pl.range(0, s_dim, CHUNK, init_values=(out,)):
    valid = pl.min(CHUNK, s_dim - c)
    t = pl.load(x, [b, c, 0], [1, CHUNK, 512], valid_shapes=[1, valid, 512])
    t = pl.cast(t, target_type=pl.FP32)
    o = pl.store(t, [b, c, 0], o)        # static physical [1, CHUNK, 512], dynamic valid
    pl.yield_(o)
```

Each per-chunk tile is physically `[1, CHUNK, 512]` (static) with a dynamic `valid_shape` `[1, min(CHUNK, s - c), 512]`.

## Pass change (what FlattenTileNdTo2D now does)

The pass's only job here is to flatten that >2D per-chunk tile to 2D *while preserving the dynamic `valid_shape`*. Previously the flatten built the flattened tile view from the physical 2D shape only, resetting `valid_shape` to the full static shape and dropping the runtime tail.

- **`ComputeMergedValidShape`** (new helper in `src/ir/transforms/flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp`): symmetric to `ComputeMergedShape` but tolerates non-`ConstInt` entries. It folds the leading dims of `valid_shape` (static factors collapse into one `ConstInt`, the identity factor `1` is dropped, a dynamic entry is carried/multiplied through) and keeps the last dim, so `[1, CHUNK, 512]` valid `[1, min(CHUNK, s-c), 512]` flattens to `[CHUNK, 512]` with valid `[min(CHUNK, s-c), 512]`.
- **`TransformBody`** now calls `ComputeMergedValidShape` when a per-dim `valid_shape` is present (`orig_tv.valid_shape.size() == result_tile->shape_.size()`) and builds the flattened `TileView` from it; otherwise the flattened tile is fully valid (`valid_shape == physical 2D shape`), as before.
- **Actionable error messages**: `GetStaticDim` and `PreconditionChecker` now reject a >2D tile whose *physical* shape is dynamic with a message that names the constraint and points to the two real fixes — chunk/iterate the dynamic dim with `pl.range`/`pl.parallel`, or reshape to 2D before the InCore (`pl.at`) scope.

Net change to the pass is exactly +53/-6 lines; no new pass, binding, or pass property.

## Tests

- **UT** (`tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_flatten_tile_nd_to_2d.py`): `TestFlattenTileNdTo2DDynamicValid` covers (1) static physical `[1, 16, 512]` + dynamic valid `[1, S, 512]` flattening to a 2D tile whose merged `valid_shape` keeps the dynamic row extent (not reset to 16) while the physical shape is static 2D; (2) a fully static 3D chain flattening to 2D normally; (3) a >2D tile with a dynamic *physical* shape erroring with the actionable message. The existing `test_dynamic_shape_error` was updated to assert the new actionable text (`cannot be flattened to 2D`, plus the presence of `pl.parallel` and `reshap` in the message).
- **ST** (`tests/st/codegen/dsl/test_flatten_dynamic_tile_3d.py`): end-to-end `@pl.jit` compile (via `compile_for_test`) of the issue #1578 kernel (cast a 3D tensor with a dynamic middle dim, user-chunked with `CHUNK=16`, `S=40` to exercise full + partial tail chunks) — the full pass pipeline now compiles where it previously raised.

Docs for the pass are updated (en + zh) to document the dynamic-`valid_shape` behavior and the user-written chunk loop.

Closes #1578.

title: fix(codegen): handle single-row tensor.scatter in tile lowering
body:
Fixes #1586

## Problem

`pl.tensor.scatter` on a destination/source with exactly **1 row** fails compilation in `convert_tensor_to_tile_ops`:

```
ValueError: The operator tile.ci requires the innermost dimension (Cols) to be != 1, got 1
```

The scatter lowering turns the gather-style column index into the flattened index the hardware (`pto.tscatter`) expects via `flat_idx[i,j] = i*dst_cols + index[i,j]`. To build the per-row base offset it emits a `tile.ci` arange of shape `[1, rows]`. For `rows == 1` that is `[1, 1]`, which violates the `pto.tci` "innermost dim (Cols) != 1" ISA constraint. `gather` is unaffected because its `tile.ci` is always `[1, K]` with `K > 1` (output column count).

## Fix

When `rows == 1` the only row base offset is `0 * dst_cols = 0`, so the flat index equals the column index directly. Skip the `tile.ci`/`reshape`/`muls`/`row_expand_add` arange in that case and use the index tile as-is. Per first-principles, the fix is in the pass only; the IR definition and the ISA constraint are unchanged.

`scatter_update`'s lowering is not affected: it builds a column arange `[1, d]` (`d > 1`) and a row base via `index.reshape([n,1]) * d`, with no `tile.ci([1, rows])`.

## Test

Adds a single-row FP32 regression to `tests/st/runtime/test_scatter.py`:
- `Scatter1RowProgram`: `base [1,16]` / `idx [1,8]` / `val [1,8]`, `dim=-1` index-form scatter — the exact shape from the issue repro.
- `Scatter1RowTestCase` + `test_scatter_1row`, reusing the existing golden (`_apply_scatter`) and dtype/alignment conventions.

Before the fix this case fails to compile; after it should compile and pass numeric validation.

title: fix(codegen): guard scalar carry return_vars from param lineage propagation
body:
## Summary

- `VarLineageCollector` was propagating `return_var → init-param` lineage for **all** loop carry types, including Scalars.
- When a Scalar carry (e.g. `global_c_idx = batch_base + inner`) is overwritten in the loop body, its return_var holds a freshly computed value with no connection to the init param.
- This incorrect lineage caused `FindReturnedParamIndices` to map the Scalar return element to a param index, making `EmitTensorAlias` emit `const Tensor& int_var = int_carry` — a C++ type mismatch that causes a compile error.
- Fix: guard the `return_var → param` propagation in `VarLineageCollector` (`ForStmt` and `WhileStmt` handlers) with an `AsTensorTypeLike` check. Only Tensor-type carries get buffer lineage; Scalar return_vars are left untraced and handled by the existing `int64_t = 0` scalar default path.

title: [Bug] Dynamic-address GM scatter on the vec side of a cube+vec mix CORE_GROUP scope deadlocks (507018); dynamic reads + contiguous writes are fine
body:
### Summary

A `CORE_GROUP` mix scope (`pl.split(...)`) that fuses a cube op (matmul) with a **per-row dynamic-address GM scatter** on the vec side **compiles clean but deadlocks at runtime with `507018`** (`aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018`). Reproduces under both `SplitMode.NONE` and `SplitMode.UP_DOWN`.

A **dynamic-address READ** and a **contiguous-address WRITE** in the same mix scope are both fine — only the **dynamic-address WRITE** deadlocks (isolation matrix below).

> Note: I have **not** root-caused the mechanism or the owning layer (pypto codegen vs runtime vs pto-isa FFTS). This report is the **reproducible observed behavior + isolation only**; please treat the cause as open.

### Where it shows up

`models/deepseek/v4/decode_indexer_compressor.py`: trying to fuse the `kv_hadamard` (cube matmul) and `kv_and_cache_write` (per-row block-table scatter into `kv_flat` + paged `idx_kv_cache`) scopes into one mix scope.

Pattern (per POST_CHUNK group, NONE mix):

```python
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.NONE)], name_hint="kv_hadamard_cache_write"):
    kv_final = ...                      # cube: hadamard matmul -> [POST_CHUNK, HEAD_DIM]
    for r in pl.range(POST_CHUNK):      # vec: per-row scatter
        c_idx = c0 + r
        if gate(c_idx):
            kv_row = kv_final[r:r+1, :]
            kv_flat = pl.assemble(kv_flat, kv_row, [c_idx*S, 0])                 # contiguous store -> OK
            cache_row = block_table_lookup(c_idx)                                # idx_block_table read -> OK
            idx_kv_cache_flat = pl.assemble(idx_kv_cache_flat,                   # DYNAMIC-ADDRESS store -> 507018
                                            pl.cast(kv_row, pl.BF16, mode="rint"),
                                            [cache_row, 0])
```

### Symptom

- Compiles clean (no codegen error).
- Runtime: `507018` on a2a3. Both NONE and UP_DOWN.

### Isolation matrix (a2a3 device, reproducible)

| Variant in the mix scope | Result |
|---|---|
| matmul + per-row **dynamic-address** scatter (`idx_kv_cache[cache_row]=`) | **507018 deadlock** |
| matmul + per-row **contiguous** write only (`kv_flat[c_idx*S]=`) | runs (no deadlock) |
| matmul + dynamic-address **READ** of `idx_kv_cache[cache_row]` + contiguous write | runs (no deadlock) |
| existing `score_fused` (NONE mix, block-table **reads** + contiguous `score_flat` write) | works |

So the trigger is specifically the **dynamic-address (data-dependent) GM store on the vec side of a mix scope**. Block-table reads and contiguous stores are fine.

### Observation (NOT a confirmed cause)

In the generated `kernels/aiv/kv_hadamard_cache_write_aiv.cpp` for the deadlocking case, the active lane (`get_subblockid()==0`) does the full `TLOAD`/`TSTORE`/dynamic-`TSTORE` with its pipe-flag sequence, while the inactive lane (`else`) takes a structurally different, shorter branch (a degenerate `valid_shape=(0,0)` `TCVT` + `pipe_barrier(PIPE_V)`, no `TLOAD`/`TSTORE`). I'm flagging this asymmetry only as an observation — I could **not** establish that it is the cause of the `507018` (the outer pre/post `set_flag`/`wait_flag` frame is balanced on both lanes), so please don't take it as the diagnosis.

### Asks

1. Support a dynamic-address (block-table-indirected) GM scatter on the vec side of a cube+vec mix scope — or determine it's unsupported.
2. Either way, emit a **compile-time diagnostic** instead of compiling clean and deadlocking at runtime.

### Workaround

Keep the scatter in a separate, non-mix scope (the existing 2-pass design: cube `kv_hadamard` scope → GM hand-off → separate per-batch `kv_and_cache_write` scope). That runs and passes.

### Related

- #1564 (SplitVectorKernel degenerate-subblock) — possibly related (mix dual-lane codegen), but I have not confirmed any connection.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `7e1bbd0a` |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `324df3d6` |
| ptoas | `0.43` (CI pins `v0.41`) |
| pto-isa | `0f171f73` |
| pypto-lib | `25ac6cf` (branch `perf/dsv4-decode-indexer-rope-core-spread`) |
| CANN | 9.0.0 |
| Host | Linux (aarch64), a2a3 |

body:

# PTO_PLATFORM=a2a3sim python repro_col_max.py
import pypto.language as pl

@pl.program
class K:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Opaque)
    def compute(in0: pl.Tensor[[64, 256], pl.FP32],
                out0: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[1, 256], pl.FP32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[1, 256], pl.FP32]:

                t = pl.slice(in0, [64, 8], [0, c])   # Tensor view, [64, 8]
                r = pl.col_max(t)                    # <-- raises here
                out0 = pl.assemble(out0, r, [0, c])

title: feat(language): expose manual dummy task DSL
body:
## Summary

- Expose `pl.system.task_dummy(deps=[...])` as a public DSL construct for users who want to write dependency-only dummy barriers explicitly.
- The new DSL reuses the existing `manual_dep_edges` metadata and current `rt_submit_dummy_task(...)` lowering path; it does **not** add runtime APIs or change the automatic `ExpandManualPhaseFence` compression strategy.
- Empty fan-in remains valid: `pl.system.task_dummy(deps=[])` lowers to an invalid `TaskId` and does not submit a dummy task, matching existing codegen behavior for all-invalid deps.

## Changes

- Add `pl.system.task_dummy(deps=[...])` to the Python DSL surface and parser.
- Teach the Python printer to round-trip `system.task_dummy` with explicit `deps=[...]`.
- Update language docs in English and Chinese with the manual dummy barrier semantics and its relationship to automatic phase-fence compression.
- Extend the phase-fence example with a user-written dummy variant.
- Add parser, printer, codegen, pass, ST correctness, and swimlane coverage:
  - parser rejects missing `deps=` and non-`TaskId` deps;
  - printer preserves `pl.system.task_dummy(deps=[...])`;
  - codegen emits `rt_submit_dummy_task(...)` and preserves invalid-empty behavior;
  - mixed manual/auto coverage verifies a user dummy barrier can coexist with an automatically inserted phase-fence barrier on the same source `TaskId` array.

title: [Pass Bug] AutoTileMatmulL0 skips Mem.Vec-fed matmul (fused-attention PV), blocking L0B reuse
body:
### Pass Name

AutoTileMatmulL0 (`auto_tile_matmul_l0`)

### Description

`AutoTileMatmulL0` only L0-tiles matmuls whose **left (A) operand is a `Mem.Mat`-loaded tile**. In a fused flash-attention root (QK → softmax → PV in one mixed cube+vec function), the **PV matmul** (`score·V`) has its left operand in **`Mem.Vec`** — it is the softmax/`exp` output at the cube↔vector (C2V) boundary. The pass tiles the QK matmul but **silently skips PV**.

Consequence: the un-tiled PV matmul keeps its right operand `V` as a full `[SEQ_TILE, 128]` L0B tile. Because it is not tiled into the same `Mem.Right` sub-tile shape as QK, `LegalizePtoBufferReuse` / `MemoryReuse` **cannot alias V's L0B buffer onto the (now-dead) QK matmul's `Mem.Right` buffer**, even though QK fully completes before PV starts. L0B usage therefore doubles:

| `SEQ_TILE` | QK Right (L0B, tiled, double-buffered) | PV Right (L0B, un-tiled) | total | 910B L0B = 64 KB |
| --: | --: | --: | --: | :--: |
| 128 | 32 KB | 32 KB | 64 KB | fits |
| 256 | 64 KB | 64 KB | **128 KB** | **fails** |

This caps the fused-attention KV block (`SEQ_TILE`) at 128 on Ascend 910B and blocks coarser block-level work decomposition. The fix belongs in the **compiler pass** (so every fused-attention kernel benefits automatically), not in per-kernel DSL hand-tiling.

### Git Commit ID

567eb669dba0d16e7a04dea8b25afe452b6d5f9e

### Before IR (Input)

From `passes_dump/16_after_FlattenTileNdTo2D.py` (`fa_fused`, `SEQ_TILE=256`) — **both** matmuls are single untiled `pl.tile.matmul`. Note PV's left operand is `Mem.Vec`, QK's is `Mem.Mat`:

```python
# QK — left operand q_padded is Mem.Mat
k_tile__tile:   pl.Tile[[128, 256], pl.BF16, pl.Mem.Mat] = pl.tile.load(k_cache, ..., transpose=True)
raw_scores__tile: pl.Tile[[16, 256], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Acc] = pl.tile.matmul(q_padded__tile, k_tile__tile)
# ... scale / row_max / exp / cast  (vector) ...
exp_scores_bf16__tile: pl.Tile[[16, 256], pl.BF16, pl.Mem.Vec] = pl.tile.cast(exp_scores__tile, target_type=pl.BF16)
# PV — left operand exp_scores_bf16 is Mem.Vec
v_tile__tile:   pl.Tile[[256, 128], pl.BF16, pl.Mem.Mat] = pl.tile.load(v_cache, ..., [256, 128])
oi_tmp__tile:   pl.Tile[[16, 128], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Acc] = pl.tile.matmul(exp_scores_bf16__tile, v_tile__tile)
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

Both matmuls L0-tiled **symmetrically** — PV should get the same contraction K-loop + `Mem.Left`/`Mem.Right` sub-tile extraction as QK, so V's right buffer is a reusable sub-tile that `MemoryReuse` aliases onto QK's freed L0B (peak L0B = `max(QK, PV)`, not the sum):

```python
# PV tiled like QK (contraction = SEQ_TILE, stepped to fit L0):
for oi_tmp__l0_ko in pl.pipeline(0, 256, 64, stage=2):
    oi_a = pl.tile.extract(exp_scores_bf16__tile, 0, oi_tmp__l0_ko, [16, 64], target_memory=pl.Mem.Left)
    oi_b = pl.tile.extract(v_tile__tile, oi_tmp__l0_ko, 0, [64, 128], target_memory=pl.Mem.Right)  # 64x128x2 = 16 KB
    oi_tmp = pl.tile.matmul / matmul_acc(oi_a, oi_b)
# => PV Right buffer is a reusable sub-tile aliasable onto QK's freed Mem.Right L0B.
```

### Actual IR or Error

From `passes_dump/17_after_AutoTileMatmulL0.py` — QK is tiled, PV is **not**:

```python
# QK: TILED — contraction K-loop, [64,256] Mem.Right sub-tile (double-buffered => 64 KB)
for raw_scores__tile_l0_ko, (...) in pl.pipeline(0, 128, 64, stage=2, ...):
    raw_scores__tile_l0_a: pl.Tile[[16, 64],  pl.BF16, pl.Mem.Left]  = pl.tile.extract(q_padded__tile, ...)
    raw_scores__tile_l0_b: pl.Tile[[64, 256], pl.BF16, pl.Mem.Right] = pl.tile.extract(k_tile__tile, ...)
    ... pl.tile.matmul / matmul_acc ...

# PV: NOT TILED — full V tile -> L0B as [256,128] = 64 KB, un-reusable
v_tile__tile: pl.Tile[[256, 128], pl.BF16, pl.Mem.Mat] = pl.tile.load(v_cache, ..., [256, 128])
oi_tmp__tile: pl.Tile[[16, 128], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Acc] = pl.tile.matmul(exp_scores_bf16__tile, v_tile__tile)
```

Downstream failure at `AllocateMemoryAddr`:

```
[1] ERROR - AllocatedMemoryAddr
  Message: Function 'fa_fused_aic': Right buffer usage (131072 bytes) exceeds platform limit (65536 bytes)
  Error Code: 1
Status: FAILED
```

`131072 = 128 KB = QK Right (64 KB) + PV Right (64 KB)`. With `SEQ_TILE=128` the two are 32 KB each (sum 64 KB) and it compiles — masking the bug until the block size grows.

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform (if relevant)

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Repro: qwen3-14b single-layer fused decode (`fa_fused` mixed cube+vec root, QK + tail-masked softmax + PV) at `SEQ_TILE=256`.

Proposed compiler fix: make `AutoTileMatmulL0` recognize and tile matmuls whose **left operand is `Mem.Vec`-resident** (the PV / `score·V` pattern), emitting the same contraction K-loop with `Mem.Left`/`Mem.Right` L0 sub-tiles it already produces for `Mem.Mat`-fed matmuls. This makes the right buffer reuse-compatible so `MemoryReuse` can alias PV's L0B onto QK's freed buffer. (A reuse-pass enhancement to alias an un-tiled right operand onto a freed tiled right buffer would also resolve it, but tiling PV symmetrically is the cleaner root fix.)

Related (same subsystem, different root cause): #1310 (AutoTileMatmulL0 / MemoryReuse acc->acc `tmov`), #1475 / #1547 (MemoryReuse allocation).

title: feat(ops): add Tensor-level col_max/col_min
body:
## Summary

`pl.col_max` / `pl.col_min` previously only accepted **Tile** operands, so calling them on a `Tensor` (e.g. a `pl.slice` result inside `@pl.program`) raised:

```text
pl.col_max: expected Tensor or Tile operands, got (Tensor)
```

The sibling reductions `row_max` / `row_sum` / `row_min` / `col_sum` already had a Tensor-level (unified → tensor → lower-to-tile) path; `col_max` / `col_min` were the only gap. This surfaced from an inductor+PTO auto-fusion case.

This change mirrors the existing `col_sum` tensor-level path across all layers:

- **C++ IR op** (`src/ir/op/tensor_ops/reduction.cpp`): register `tensor.col_max` / `tensor.col_min`, reusing the shared `DeduceTensorColReductionType` (reduces axis=-2, keep_dim).
- **C++ conversion** (`src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp`): lower 1:1 to `tile.col_max` / `tile.col_min` via `RegisterSimple` — both tile ops are 1-arg (sequential path), exactly like `tile.col_sum`'s 1-arg form, so no `tmp_tile` workspace is needed.
- **Python IR layer** (`python/pypto/ir/op/tensor_ops.py`) and **DSL layer** (`python/pypto/language/op/tensor_ops.py`): add `col_max` / `col_min` wrappers.
- **Unified dispatch** (`python/pypto/language/op/unified_ops.py`): add the `Tensor` branch to `col_max` / `col_min`.
- **Docs** (`docs/en` + `docs/zh-cn` `02-operation_reference.md`): update the col-reduction rows.

## Testing

- [x] Full `tests/ut/` suite passes (5256 passed, 28 skipped, 0 failed)
- [x] New IR type-deduction tests (`test_tensor_col_max` / `test_tensor_col_min`) and unified-dispatch regression tests (`test_col_max` / `test_col_min`)
- [x] End-to-end verified: `ConvertTensorToTileOps` lowers `tensor.col_max` → `tile.col_max`; the issue's repro now builds
- [x] clang-tidy, code review, code simplification all clean

## Related Issues

Fixes #1593

title: Add opt-in out-window externalization switch
body:
## Summary
- Add a default-off `enable_out_window_externalization` compile/pass switch.
- Thread the switch through `PassContext`, Python `ir.compile`, `RunConfig`, JIT forwarding, and the JIT cache key.
- Keep the conservative dependency guard by default; only enable the windowed externalization path when explicitly requested.

## Background
The out-window behavior from d30df60 helped avoid serialized Qwen3 decode execution, but it was reverted in f8731b2 because cross-scope cases could lose dependencies, as tracked by issue 1463. This PR restores the behavior behind an explicit opt-in switch so existing users keep the safer default.

## Testing

title: [Feature] Fine-grained guard for OutWindowExternalizer (Pattern 5) — relax "any later full-parent read disqualifies"
body:
### Summary

The conservative guard added to `OptimizeOrchTensors` Pattern 5 (`OutWindowExternalizer`) in #1468 disables window externalization whenever any later callee reads the rewritten Out's buffer root as a *full parent* tensor. This rule is correct but too coarse — it disqualifies safe and high-value externalization cases where the producer and consumer are already ordered via the same iter-arg chain, so no race is actually possible. We request a more fine-grained safety check (or per-Out / structure-aware decision) so that externalization can resume for these cases.

### Motivation / Use Case

**Observed regression on qwen3-14b decode (pypto-lib `models/qwen3/14b/`):**

Scope-1 `q_proj` / `k_proj` / `v_proj` in `decode_layer.py` use the standard `pl.parallel(0, N, CHUNK)` + `pl.assemble(buf, acc, [b0, q0])` idiom. Before #1468, Pattern 5 (`OutWindowExternalizer`) externalized the windowed write into `slice → windowed callee → assemble`, breaking the loop-carried buffer chain and letting the parallel loop actually fan out across cores. After #1468, the externalization is skipped because the downstream `qk_norm` reads the *full* `q_proj` / `k_proj` tensors:

```python
# passes_dump/14_after_OptimizeOrchTensors.py (qwen3-14b decode_fwd, num_layers=2)
self.qk_norm(..., q_proj_inline102__rv_v2, ..., k_proj_inline78__rv_v2, ...)
#            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
#            full-tensor In arg (triggers HasLaterFullParentReadOfRewrittenOutput)
```

**L2 swimlane evidence (real-device a2a3, 2-layer decode_fwd):** all 20 q_proj tile-tasks land on a *single core* (layer-0: AIC_2), strictly back-to-back (~47 µs each, zero overlap) — i.e., ~940 µs fully serial per layer per projection. k_proj/v_proj show the same pattern (each a 4-tile serial chain). Parallelism only exists *between* q/k/v because they have distinct buffers (three chains on three cores), not *within* each projection.

The qk_norm read is **not** racy: it is sequenced after the producing parallel loop via the same iter-arg chain in the orchestration. The guard's conservative "any later full-parent read disqualifies" rule errs on the safe side at the cost of substantial perf on a very common shape (windowed-writer followed by a callee that takes the producer as a whole-tensor In).

### Proposed API / Behavior

Several non-exclusive options, roughly increasing in scope:

1. **Order-aware guard.** Treat a later full-parent read as *safe* (and allow externalization) when it is statically provable that the read is sequenced after the producing loop has fully completed — e.g., the read sits in a subsequent sibling statement that consumes the loop's `return_var`, so runtime ordering is already implied by SSA. The current guard (`HasLaterFullParentReadOfRewrittenOutput`, `src/ir/transforms/optimize_orch_tensors_pass.cpp:2411`) returns true purely on root-set membership without checking this.
2. **Per-Out granularity.** Today the policy is all-or-nothing across a callee's Outs ("Multi-Out policy is all-or-nothing"). Allow externalizing the safe Outs and leaving the unsafe ones on the parent tensor when the callee shape permits.
3. **Producer/consumer-aware rewrite.** When the only later "full read" is in fact a tile-sliced consumption inside a callee that itself loads windowed sub-ranges (e.g., per-head slices of q_proj inside `qk_norm`), prefer externalizing *both* sides (producer writes windows + consumer reads windows) so the buffer-root identity is preserved while parallelism is recovered.
4. **Opt-in escape hatch.** As a stop-gap, a Function/Call-site attribute (e.g., `pl.attr(allow_window_externalization=True)`) to override the guard when the user knows the producer/consumer ordering is safe.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Rewriting the consumer to take windowed slices** (e.g., make `qk_norm` read per-head slices of `q_proj` / `k_proj` instead of the full tensor). This works around the guard in pypto-lib but requires non-trivial source rewrites in every affected kernel and is fragile to future passes.
- **Promoting scope-1 to `pl.spmd`** (as scope-3 / scope-2 already do in pypto-lib commit `2d6f086`). This bypasses Pattern 5 entirely but changes the loop construct and is a larger refactor than the guard issue warrants.

Neither alternative addresses the root cause — the guard's conservatism — and both leave perf on the table for other models that match the same shape.

### Additional Context

- Guard added in: f8731b22 (#1468 "fix(pass): guard unsafe window externalization", Fixes #1444, 2026-05-22).
- Pass source: `src/ir/transforms/optimize_orch_tensors_pass.cpp` (Pattern 5 = `OutWindowExternalizer`, guard at line 2411, `AddFullRootReadsFromCall` at line 2345).
- Affected pypto-lib path: `models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py` (scope-1 q/k/v projection, ~L201-237) → `decode_fwd.py` (multi-layer driver).
- Reproduction: `python decode_fwd.py -p a2a3 -d 0 --num-layers 2 --enable-l2-swimlane` (run from `models/qwen3/14b/`). Inspect `build_output/<jit_dir>/passes_dump/14_after_OptimizeOrchTensors.py`: the q_proj `tensor.create` remains hoisted outside the parallel loop and is threaded as iter-arg (no externalization). Swimlane shows 20 q_proj tiles on one core per layer.
- The #1444 fix targeted DSv4's `score_flat.view(...)` windowed-writer / full-parent-reader pattern; the conservative rule catches qwen3-14b q/k/v→qk_norm as collateral.
- Related: hw-native-sys/pypto#1468, hw-native-sys/pypto#1444.

**Host Platform:** Linux (aarch64)

title: refactor(runtime): Worker ABC + ChipWorker / DistributedWorker hierarchy
body:
## Summary

Promote the shared device-memory base into a real ``Worker`` ABC and rename the two concrete runtime handles into a symmetric pair, then add the explicit dispatch surface (``run`` / ``register`` / ``RegistrationHandle``) on both concretes.

**Renames (hard break, no alias):**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ``pypto.runtime.device_memory.DeviceMemoryHandle`` | ``pypto.runtime.runtime_base.Worker`` (ABC) |
| ``pypto.runtime.Worker`` (concrete L2) | ``pypto.runtime.ChipWorker`` |
| ``pypto.runtime.distributed_runner.DistributedRuntime`` | ``pypto.runtime.distributed_runner.DistributedWorker`` |

**New on the ABC** (shared by L2 + L3):

- ``_owned_tensors`` auto-track for tensors returned by ``alloc_tensor``.
- ``_close_owned_tensors()`` helper. Concrete ``close()`` calls it before tearing down the backend so any leaked DeviceTensor is reclaimed. Errors during auto-free are logged and swallowed so ``close()`` always completes.
- ``run`` / ``register`` abstract methods. Library code can type-hint against ``Worker`` (ABC) and accept either L2 or L3 runtime.

**New on ``ChipWorker``** (L2):

- ``run(compiled, *args, config=None)`` — explicit dispatch with binding check (``platform`` / ``runtime_name``), no ``ContextVar`` discovery.
- ``register(compiled) -> RegistrationHandle`` — eager registration; the handle's ``__call__`` delegates to ``run``.
- ``aicpu_dlopen_count`` / ``host_dlopen_count`` properties (direct passthrough to simpler).
- ``_check_binding`` private helper.

**New on ``DistributedWorker``** (L3):

- ``run(compiled, *args, config=None)`` — alias for ``__call__``.
- ``register(compiled) -> RegistrationHandle`` — handle calls ``run``.
- Reuses the ABC's auto-track / auto-free for ``alloc_tensor``.

**``RegistrationHandle`` semantics:**

- alias-safe: multiple ``register`` calls on the same callable return aliases of the same underlying cid.
- ``unregister()`` only marks the handle closed — it does NOT call ``simpler.unregister_callable``. Real cid release happens once, in ``Worker.close()``.
- Context manager support: ``with worker.register(compiled) as h:``.

**Naming rationale (Worker family):** symmetric ``ChipWorker`` / ``DistributedWorker`` pair under the user-facing ``Worker`` ABC sticks to simpler's vocabulary while letting library code address either runtime kind through one type. The L2 name ``ChipWorker`` overlaps with simpler's internal C++ ``simpler.worker.ChipWorker`` — that class isn't re-exported through ``task_interface``, so there's no runtime import conflict; the pypto class's docstring calls out the namespace.

## Testing

- [x] New: ``test_chip_worker_explicit_dispatch.py`` — 19 mock-based cases covering ``run`` / ``register`` / ``RegistrationHandle`` (cid reuse, binding mismatch, ``close`` marks handles closed, diagnostic counter passthrough).
- [x] New: ``test_worker_owned_tensors.py`` — 7 mock-based cases covering ABC's auto-track / auto-free, no-double-free, swallow-on-error, raw-malloc-not-tracked.
- [x] Existing ``test_distributed_worker.py`` (renamed from ``test_distributed_runtime.py``) extended with ``TestExplicitDispatchAPI`` for L3 ``run`` / ``register`` mirror + ABC auto-free.
- [x] ``test_runtime_base.py`` (renamed from ``test_device_memory.py``) updated to new ABC name; added ``_owned_tensors`` / ``_close_owned_tensors`` coverage.
- [x] ``test_worker_reuse.py`` / ``test_worker_memory.py`` updated to ``ChipWorker``.
- [ ] On-device verification (model B from the design): training loop with ``alloc_tensor`` + ``register`` + repeated ``handle(...)`` calls, plus L2/L3 symmetry sanity check.

## Notes

- ``alloc_tensor`` / ``free_tensor`` keep their current names and ``init=`` semantics (rollback-safe). Naming churn for these helpers is intentionally not in this PR.
- ``ChipWorker`` keeps ``level=2`` as a hard guard for now; L3+ instantiations go through ``DistributedWorker`` (which doesn't take ``level``).
- The implicit ``with Worker(): compiled(...)`` reuse path becomes ``with ChipWorker(): compiled(...)`` — same ``ContextVar`` mechanism, only the class name changed.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- ``alloc_tensor`` → ``alloc``, ``free_tensor`` → ``free``: deferred (would be another breaking change to a shared interface; main has these names well-established and rollback semantics work).
- A future PR will surface ``DistributedWorker``'s diagnostic surface symmetrically (simpler exposes ``aicpu_dlopen_count`` only at L2).
