title: fix(ir): tile Vec-fed PV matmul and reuse cross-shape L0 buffers
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1595.

`AutoTileMatmulL0` only L0-tiled matmuls whose **left (A) operand was `Mat`-resident**, silently skipping the fused-attention **PV (`score·V`)** matmul whose left operand is the softmax/`exp` output resident in `Mem.Vec` at the cube↔vector (C2V) boundary. The un-tiled PV kept its full `V` tile in L0B, so at `SEQ_TILE ≥ 256` L0B usage doubled and `AllocateMemoryAddr` failed with `Right buffer usage (131072 bytes) exceeds platform limit (65536 bytes)`.

Tiling PV alone is **necessary but not sufficient**: `MemoryReuse` requires identical shapes and `AllocateMemoryAddr` is a bump allocator, so the cross-shape QK (`[k, SEQ]`) and PV (`[k', HEAD]`) Right buffers could never alias. This PR implements both halves:

- **`AutoTileMatmulL0`** — accept a `Vec` left operand (right still must be `Mat`); stage it into `Mat` via a pre-loop `tile.move` so the per-iter `tile.extract` slices from Mat exactly like the QK path. Keeping the `Vec→Mat` crossing a `tile.move` lets `ExpandMixedKernel` lower it through its `tpop_from_aiv` handshake (which lands the data in Mat). Extracting straight from the Vec tile instead left a dangling cross-boundary free variable on the cube side.
- **`MemoryReuse`** — let L0 cube-input (`Left`/`Right`) buffers produced by view ops (`tile.extract`/`tile.slice`/`tile.reshape`) share a slot by **byte size** even when shapes differ, gated on both producers being view ops (a subset of `LegalizePtoBufferReuse::IsLegalViewOp` so the shared MemRef survives that pass). The PV Right buffer then aliases the freed QK Right buffer — peak L0B = `max(QK, PV)`, not the sum.

## Result

Verified end-to-end on the qwen3-14b fused decode (`fa_fused`, mixed cube+vec root) at `SEQ_TILE=256`: the generated `fa_fused_aic` PTO places both QK (`[64,256]`) and PV (`[128,128]`) Right buffers at addresses `0` and `32768`, so the L0B high-water mark drops **128 KB → 64 KB** and the kernel compiles cleanly through codegen.

## Testing

- [x] Full `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` + `tests/ut/jit/` suite: 1573 passed, 26 skipped
- [x] New unit tests: Vec-fed (staged-to-Mat) tiling, Vec-right-operand skip (asymmetry), cross-shape L0 Right reuse + Left size-gate
- [x] Code review, clang-tidy (incl. an include-cleaner fix), code-simplifier
- [x] Documentation updated — `16-auto_tile_matmul_l0.md` and `29-memory_reuse.md` (en + zh)

title: fix(codegen): guard scalar carry return_vars from param lineage propagation
body:
VarLineageCollector mapped return_var → init-param for all loop carry
types, including Scalars. When a Scalar carry is overwritten in the
loop body (e.g. ``global_c_idx = batch_base + inner``), the return_var
holds a freshly computed value with no connection to the init param.
Propagating param lineage to such a Scalar return_var caused
FindReturnedParamIndices to incorrectly assign a param index to the
Scalar return element. The codegen then called EmitTensorAlias on the
Scalar var, emitting ``const Tensor& int_var = int_carry`` — a C++ type
mismatch and compile error.

Guard the return_var → param propagation in VarLineageCollector (ForStmt
and WhileStmt handlers) with an AsTensorTypeLike check so only
Tensor-type carries get buffer lineage. Scalar carries retain iter_arg
lineage (still needed for input arg tracking) but their return_vars are
left untraced — the caller's !param_idx_opt branch correctly handles
them with an ``int64_t = 0`` scalar default.

title: outlining captures dead phi from if/else branches as scalar return, breaks C++ codegen
body:
## Summary

When two SPMD loops live in the two branches of an `if/else` and they both rebind the same Python-scope scalar (`t1 = ob * TILE`), pypto's SPMD outlining captures that dead phi as a `Scalar[INDEX]` return on both outlined functions. The orchestration C++ codegen then fails (or emits ill-typed code) because it can't materialize a meaningful caller-side value from an async `rt_submit_aiv_task` call.

## Repro

Minimal pattern (full repro: pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/gate.py` sort path; trips automatically when `EP_ROUTING_GLOBAL=True` is exercised, or with `python gate.py -p a2a3sim --layer-id 3`):

```python
for ob_g in pl.spmd(T // TILE, name_hint="prep"):
    t1 = ob_g * TILE          # def #1  (gets DCE'd by the rebinds below)
    # ... uses t1 ...

if layer_id < N_HASH_LAYERS:
    for ob_h in pl.spmd(T // TILE, name_hint="route_hash"):
        t1 = ob_h * TILE      # def #2
        # ... uses t1 inside spmd only ...
else:
    for ob_s in pl.spmd(T // TILE, name_hint="route_sort"):
        t1 = ob_s * TILE      # def #3
        # ... uses t1 inside spmd only ...

# t1 has NO consumer after this point.
```

## What happens

Final IR (`39_after_MaterializeRuntimeScopes.py`) gives the two branch-spmd outlines an unwanted Scalar return:

```python
def route_hash(...) -> pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX]:     # ← spurious return
    ...
def route_sort(...) -> pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX]:     # ← spurious return
    ...

# chip_orch call sites:
t1_inline155__ssa_v1: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX] = self.route_hash_spmd(...)
t1_inline155__ssa_v2: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX] = self.route_sort_spmd(...)
```

The same outlining run on the `ob_g` spmd correctly DCE's `t1`: `gate_spmd` returns only the InOut tensors (`route_scores_buf`, `biased_scores_buf`) that have real downstream consumers — t1's def #1 dies because def #2 / #3 overwrite it in both branches.

Generated `chip_orch.cpp` from `orchestration_codegen.cpp` then fails to build:

```cpp
int64_t t1_inline155;
if (static_cast<int64_t>(layer_id) < 0) {
    // ... rt_submit_aiv_task(10, params_t8) — task is fire-and-forget ...
    const Tensor& t1_inline155__ssa_v1 = indices;   // GenerateSingleReturnAlias fallback to out_indices[0]
    t1_inline155 = t1_inline155__ssa_v1;            // const Tensor → int64_t : type error
} else {
    // ... rt_submit_aiv_task(11, params_t9) ...
    const Tensor& t1_inline155__ssa_v2 = indices;
    t1_inline155 = t1_inline155__ssa_v2;
}
// t1_inline155 is NEVER used after this point.
```

Compiler error:

```
chip_orch.cpp:295:32: error: cannot convert 'const Tensor' to 'int64_t' in assignment
chip_orch.cpp:309:32: error: cannot convert 'const Tensor' to 'int64_t' in assignment
```

## Why is this asymmetric (ob_g vs ob_h/ob_s)

- The `ob_g` spmd's t1 (def #1) is killed by def #2 / #3 in both arms of the if/else → SSA pass DCE's it → outlining sees no live-out → no return.
- The `ob_h` / `ob_s` spmds' t1 (def #2 / #3) reach the function exit (if/else has no successor). The SSA pass keeps the phi node, even though the phi has no consumer. Outlining treats every phi predecessor as needing to be returnable, so both branch-spmd outlines pick up `-> Scalar[INDEX]`.

`GenerateSingleReturnAlias` in `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:2156` then falls back to `out_indices[0]` (the first Out param) when it can't trace the return back to a Param, emitting `const Tensor& <ret> = <first_out_param>;` — type-incorrect when the LHS was declared as `int64_t` from the Scalar return.

## Expected

Either:
1. The SSA/outlining pipeline DCEs phi nodes whose result has no users (preferred — it would also shrink the outlined function ABI), OR
2. The codegen of `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` declines to alias when the call's return type is not `TensorType` (defensive; doesn't help the dead-return-type "leaks into outlined ABI" issue, but prevents the type-mismatch crash).

## Possible fixes

- **A (root cause)**: in the SSA pass or outlining pass, drop phi nodes that have no consumers before computing the outlined-function return signature. The `ob_g` path already gets this right; the same DCE should handle the if/else exit phi.
- **B (defensive band-aid)**: in `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` (orchestration_codegen.cpp:2156), early-return when `call->GetType()` is not a `TensorType`. This stops the bad `const Tensor& = indices` alias from being emitted but the leftover `t1_inline155 = <undeclared ssa>;` line is still broken — so A is really what's needed.

## Environment

- pypto HEAD: `6abbf46c`
- Platform: `a2a3sim`
- Repro program: pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/gate.py` sort path (exercised via `python gate.py -p a2a3sim --layer-id 3` or any layer where `layer_id >= num_hash_layers`)

title: fix(pass): DCE dead IfStmt phi return_vars in Simplify
body:
## Summary

- Add `EliminateDeadIfReturnVars` helper that drops `IfStmt::return_vars_` entries with no `Var*` user and the matching slot from each branch's trailing `YieldStmt`.
- Wire it into `TransformSimplify` before the existing scalar DCE so the now-orphan branch-body scalar assigns are collected in the same pass invocation.
- Fixes #1603 — outlining was capturing a dead phi as a spurious `Scalar[INDEX]` return on the outlined function, then orchestration codegen emitted `const Tensor& t = indices; int64_t t1 = <Tensor>;` which fails to compile.

## Why the existing DCE missed it

Two blind spots in `dead_code_elimination.cpp`:

1. `YieldStmt` is unconditionally a live root (line 131-140) — its referenced exprs feed `live` regardless of whether the corresponding `IfStmt::return_vars_[i]` has a downstream consumer.
2. `FindLiveRootsRecursiveImpl` and `FilterDeadCodeImpl` never inspect `IfStmt::return_vars_` for use-count and never rewrite `return_vars_` or `YieldStmt::value_` slots.

The new helper closes the gap by walking IR top-down, identifying return_vars whose `Var*` is not in the use set collected by `VarDefUseCollector`, and rewriting both `return_vars_` and each branch's trailing yield slots. Iterates to a fixed point so cascading deaths (outer phi drop → inner phi becomes dead) are fully collapsed.

## Scope

Type-agnostic: Scalar, Tile, and Tensor `return_vars_` are all candidates when no direct `Var*` use exists. Downstream alias / memref / memory-space readers (`memory_reuse`, `init_memref`, `convert_tensor_to_tile_ops`, `infer_tile_memory_space`, `expand_manual_phase_fence`, `flatten_tile_nd_to_2d`, `tpop_tfree_finalizer`) either skip-on-empty or iterate-per-index — a dropped phi just means less work, never wrong work, because the "no Var* user" precondition rules out any downstream consumer of the alias chain through that index.

Side effects in branch bodies are preserved by the existing `IsRemovableScalarAssign` / `IsSideEffectOp` guards in the downstream scalar DCE.

## Test plan

- [x] New `TestDeadIfReturnVarsDCE` class in `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_simplify_pass.py` with 3 tests:
  - `test_drops_dead_scalar_phi_from_unused_if_else_rebind` (positive, mirrors #1603 minimal repro)
  - `test_keeps_scalar_phi_with_downstream_use` (negative — phi with downstream consumer is preserved)
  - `test_drops_dead_tensor_phi_keeping_side_effect_ops` (positive Tensor case — phi dropped, in-branch `tensor.write` side-effects preserved)
- [x] Full `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` suite: 1397 passed, 26 skipped.
- [x] Wider sweep `tests/ut/ir/ tests/ut/codegen/ tests/ut/pass/`: 3935 passed, 28 skipped.
- [ ] Issue #1603 full repro (`pypto-lib` `models/deepseek/v4/gate.py` sort path) — recommend running on a dev workstation that has `pypto-lib` checked out adjacent to verify the codegen error is gone end-to-end.

title: fix(codegen): propagate tensor view across plain tensor aliases
body:
## Summary

PTO codegen registers loop-result tensor views only inside the `ForStmt` visitor. When a constant-trip stage-2 `pl.pipeline`'s statically-empty main loop is folded by `Simplify` into a plain alias `t__rv = t__iter`, that registration is bypassed and the `AssignStmt` visitor propagated nothing for tensor aliases. A later `tile.store` into the alias then tripped `GetOrCreateTensorView`'s `INTERNAL_CHECK` with an opaque `Tensor view not found for parameter: <synthetic-var>`, giving no hint at the real cause.

This adds a branch to `PTOCodegen::VisitStmt_(AssignStmtPtr)` that, for a plain `lhs_tensor = rhs_var` alias, propagates the tensor view / SSA name / base ptr from RHS to LHS — mirroring the `ForStmt` loop-result registration the fold bypasses. Resolution uses the non-fatal `TryGetTensorView` and falls through on a view miss, so the change is **strictly additive** (never introduces a new throw).

## Testing

- Two regression tests in `tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen.py` covering the plain-`Var` and `IterArg` RHS legs (the latter is the exact post-fold `t__rv = t__iter` shape). Both **fail without the fix** with the documented "Tensor view not found" error and pass with it.
- Full `tests/ut/` suite: 5382 passed, 28 skipped.
- clang-tidy / clang-format / cpplint / pyright clean.

## Notes

- Internal C++ codegen only — no public API, bindings, or type-stub changes.
- The non-fatal `TryGetTensorView` helper already exists upstream; this change only adds a new caller.

title: fix(verifier): reject unwritten Out/InOut params, not just tensor-creating reassigns (#1525)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the real root cause of #1525: a bare reassignment of a `pl.Out`/`pl.InOut` parameter to a **detached** value (e.g. `y = pl.matmul(...); return y`) rebinds the local name and leaves the external output buffer unwritten, so the kernel silently produces its init value (all-zero). This is a front-end output-binding footgun — **not** a device/pto-isa bug (the earlier device-side diagnosis was walked back; pto-isa#149 was closed as not-reproduced).

## What changed

**Generalize the `OutParamNotShadowed` verifier** (`src/ir/verifier/verify_out_param_pass.cpp`) from a tensor-creating-op blacklist (`tensor.create`/`tensor.full` only) to the precise invariant:

> A call-valued reassignment of an Out/InOut param is invalid **unless the call threads the param through its arguments**.

- ✅ Threading reassigns stay valid: `out = pl.assemble(out, tile, off)`, `out = pl.store(value, off, out)`, indexed write `out[...] = value`.
- ❌ Detached reassigns now fail compilation with a clear diagnostic: `out = pl.matmul(...)`, `out = tensor.create(...)`.

**Make the check actually fire**: add `OutParamNotShadowed` to `GetVerifiedProperties()` (`src/ir/transforms/ir_property.cpp`). It was already in the *structural* set but absent from the *verified* set, so the inline pipeline-input check skipped it and the footgun compiled silently. It now runs **once at pipeline input (pre-SSA)** — where the bare reassignment's `AssignStmt.var_` still targets the param Var (post-SSA it detaches into a dead value).

### Why not a broader "no `=` to parameters" rule
Refuted empirically: an AST scan of `examples/`+`tests/` found **889** bare-name `=` assignments to parameters, **741** of which are the blessed accumulator idiom `param = pl.store(t, off, param)` / `pl.assemble`. The distinguishing factor is whether the param is threaded through the rhs, not whether `=` is used.

## Validation

- Bare #1525 form now raises a `VerificationError` at compile time with an actionable message; the idiomatic form compiles clean (no false positive).
- Full `tests/ut` suite green (5346 passed), no false positives.
- New regression tests in `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_verifier.py` (matmul + InOut cases).
- `examples/utils/error_handling.py` and the #1525 device test updated to the new behavior / supported idiom.
- Verifier docs updated (en + zh).

Closes #1525.

title: fix(codegen): carry full-column box for no-split dual-AIV tpush transport
body:
## Summary

On 910B the **no-split dual-AIV dispatch** runs a mixed root's producer on two AIV subblocks that share one FIFO slot while the single cube consumer pops the full slot. `EmitSplitTpushTransportValidShape` early-returned for `split == 0`, so a producer that narrowed its `valid_shape` (e.g. `set_validshape` on a partial attention block) left the slot **columns past `valid_col` stale**, feeding garbage into the consumer matmul. This surfaced as a fused-attention numeric corruption on Qwen3-14B decode (`fa_fused`).

This extends **#1454**'s full-box transport to the `split == 0` dual-AIV case (detected via the new `PTOCodegen::IsDualAivDispatchFunction`), but widens **columns only while preserving the producer's row `valid_shape`**:

- subblock 0's real push carries the full column box (fixing the stale-col feed into the consumer matmul);
- subblock 1's `valid_shape=(0, 0)` replay stays a **true 0-row no-op** — widening its rows to the full box would race garbage rows into subblock 0's shared slot.

Genuine `split == 1/2` paths keep widening both axes (the row split is real there); plain `split == 0` **without** `dual_aiv_dispatch` is unchanged (no transport emitted), so non-dual-AIV cross-core pipes are byte-identical.

## Validation

- **New UT** `test_no_split_dual_aiv_tpush_widens_cols_preserves_rows` (`tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen_cross_core.py`): asserts the transport `set_validshape` widens cols (`%c16_index`) but **preserves rows** (`%arg1`), and that the logical -> transport -> restore triple is emitted. Without this fix `split == 0` emits no transport (a single `set_validshape` line) and the test fails.
- **Regression**: `test_pto_codegen_cross_core.py` + `test_split_vector_kernel.py` + `test_pto_codegen.py` -- 126 passed locally.
- **Lint**: clang-format, ruff check/format, cpplint (<=110), check-english-only, check-headers, markdownlint-cli2 (project config) all clean.
- **Docs**: the codegen transport contract is documented in `docs/{en,zh-cn}/dev/passes/23-split_vector_kernel.md`.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on the current toolchain
- [ ] (follow-up) on-device fused-attention parity for the pipelined dual-AIV case

## Notes

This is the **transport-correctness half** of the no-split dual-AIV bidirectional-pipe fix: it stops subblock 1's replay from clobbering subblock 0's slot and carries the producer's fillpad'd columns. The remaining pipelined-iteration FIFO-slot isolation (two `pl.pipeline` iterations sharing one bidirectional ring) is a separate follow-up.

## Related

Extends #1454 (full-box transport for `split == 1/2`).

title: fix(ir): accept TileType input in tensor.gather conversion
body:
## Summary

`tensor.gather` previously crashed in `convert_tensor_to_tile_ops` with `CHECK(input_tensor_type)` when an upstream conversion had already lowered its input/index to `TileType` (e.g. when a preceding `tensor.create` had been rewritten to `tile.create`).

This PR makes the converter accept either `TensorType` or `TileType` for both `input` and `index`:

- Extract `shape`/`dtype` from whichever type the arg carries.
- Route the per-row materialization through a new `emit_load_or_slice` helper: it emits `tile.load` when the source is still a `TensorType` (original behavior, valid at any rank) and `tile.slice` when an upstream pass has already produced a `TileType` (only reached on rank-2 paths today, because `FlattenTileNdTo2D` rejects `tile.slice` on >2D tiles).
- The rank-3 paths therefore keep emitting `tile.load`, so the rank-3 lowering is bit-identical to before.

title: [Feature] Software-pipeline pl.pipeline across the fused cube/vector C2V/V2C (tpush/tpop) boundary
body:
### Summary

`pl.pipeline` over a loop whose body is a **fused cube+vector root** (cube matmul → vector op → cube matmul, with the C2V/V2C moves lowered to `tile.tpush_to_aiv` / `tile.tpop_from_aiv` through the GM pipe) does **not** software-pipeline across the `tpush`/`tpop` boundary. The pass keeps every iteration strictly serial, so the cube (AIC) stalls at each `tpop` waiting for the vector (AIV), and the two engines never overlap across iterations.

A user can recover the overlap **only** by hand-writing a manual unroll that reorders the body engine-grouped (all cube ops of N iterations, then all vector ops, then the next cube ops). The request is for `pl.pipeline` (via `LowerPipelineLoops` / the pipeline scheduler) to perform that cross-iteration reordering automatically — i.e. hoist iteration `i+1`'s cube matmul ahead of iteration `i`'s vector-dependent `tpop`/second matmul — so the declarative form matches the hand-unrolled performance.

### Motivation / Use Case

Fused flash-attention is the concrete case. The per-head loop body is:

```
QK matmul (AIC/cube) → softmax (AIV/vector) → SV matmul (AIC/cube)
```

with C2V (`tpush_to_aiv`) moving QK scores to the vector core and V2C (`tpop_from_aiv`) moving the softmax result back to the cube. On A2/A3 this round-trips through GM, so the cube sits idle during the vector's softmax and vice-versa.

Measured on a single-layer Qwen3-14B decode (BATCH=16, SEQ_TILE=256, GP_SIZE=8 heads per work item), `fa_fused` kernel `Exec` time:

| Form | AIC Exec | AIV Exec |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Serial `pl.range(GP_SIZE)` (baseline) | 111.3 µs | 109.8 µs |
| **`pl.pipeline(GP_SIZE, stage=2)`** | 108.1 µs (−3%) | 106.8 µs (−3%) |
| **Manual 2-way unroll** (engine-grouped) | **98.1 µs (−12%)** | **96.7 µs (−12%)** |

The manual unroll's ~12% comes from overlapping the cube's `QK(gp_{i+1})` with the vector's `softmax(gp_i)`. `pl.pipeline` only achieves ~3% (incidental load double-buffering) because it does not reorder across `tpush`/`tpop`.

The user-facing problem: the *declarative* `pl.pipeline` is the natural way to ask for software pipelining, but today it forces users to hand-write the unrolled, engine-grouped program to actually get the cube/vector overlap. Closing this gap makes the cube/vector software pipeline a one-line `pl.pipeline` instead of a manual unroll.

### Proposed API / Behavior

No new API — make the existing `pl.pipeline` deliver the overlap:

```python
# Today the user must hand-unroll + reorder engine-grouped to get the overlap:
for gp_pair in pl.range(GP_SIZE // 2):
    rs0 = pl.matmul(q0, k0, b_trans=True)      # AIC: QK gp0
    rs1 = pl.matmul(q1, k1, b_trans=True)      # AIC: QK gp1   (issued before softmax0)
    e0, m0, l0 = softmax(rs0)                   # AIV
    e1, m1, l1 = softmax(rs1)                   # AIV
    oi0 = pl.matmul(e0, v0)                     # AIC: SV gp0
    oi1 = pl.matmul(e1, v1)                     # AIC: SV gp1
    ...stores...

# Desired: the declarative form should produce the SAME overlapped schedule.
for gp in pl.pipeline(GP_SIZE, stage=2):
    rs  = pl.matmul(q, k, b_trans=True)         # AIC: QK
    e, m, l = softmax(rs)                        # AIV (C2V/V2C tpush/tpop)
    oi  = pl.matmul(e, v)                        # AIC: SV
    ...stores...
```

Concretely, when scheduling a `pl.pipeline` loop whose body crosses an AIC→AIV→AIC boundary via `tpush`/`tpop`, the AIC instruction stream should become:

```
QK_i, tpush_i, QK_{i+1}, tpush_{i+1}, tpop_i, SV_i, tpop_{i+1}, SV_{i+1}, ...
```

i.e. iteration `i+1`'s cube `QK` is hoisted ahead of iteration `i`'s `tpop`/`SV`, so the cube stays busy while the vector consumes iteration `i`'s scores. Today `LowerPipelineLoops` instead emits the strictly-serial `QK_i, tpush_i, tpop_i, SV_i, QK_{i+1}, ...` (verified in the generated ptoas AIC stream).

### Alternatives Considered

- **Manual unroll** (`for gp_pair in pl.range(GP_SIZE // 2): ...` with the body reordered engine-grouped): works and yields the full ~12%, but requires the user to hand-write the unrolled program — exactly what `pl.pipeline` is supposed to abstract away. It also doesn't compose well with other axes (e.g. adding K-dim double-buffering on top busts the L0B budget).
- **`pl.pipeline(stage=3)`**: deeper staging does not help — the scheduler still doesn't cross the `tpush`/`tpop` boundary, so the per-iteration serialization remains.

### Additional Context

- Evidence: generated ptoas AIC stream for the `pl.pipeline(stage=2)` form shows `QK_i, tpush_to_aiv_i, tpop_from_aiv_i, SV_i, QK_{i+1}, ...` — no reordering across the fused boundary.
- Pass to enhance: `LowerPipelineLoops` (`src/ir/transforms/lower_pipeline_loops_pass.cpp`) / the pipeline scheduler, which currently treats `tile.tpush_to_aiv` / `tile.tpop_from_aiv` as a per-iteration barrier.
- Related (cube/vector pipeline stalls, but different root cause — MemoryReuse buffer-reuse policy rather than pipeline reordering): #1475, #1352.
- Repro branch/commit: `issue-1595-autotile-vec-fed-matmul` @ `e2866596`.

title: fix(language): align diagnostic caret with span for <string> sources
body:
Fixes #1558

## Problem

When `pl.at(deps=...)` is given an expression whose AST shape is rejected (e.g. `deps=[seed_tid] + [silu_tids[...] for i in range(4)]`, a `BinOp` rather than a list/tuple/comprehension literal), the error message is correct but the caret (`^`) points several lines **past** the `deps=` argument — under an unrelated body statement.

## Root cause (differs from the issue's hypothesis)

The issue guessed the diagnostic was attached to the wrong AST node. It is **not** — `ast_parser.py` already raises the `ParserTypeError` with `span=get_span(deps_kw.value)`, and that span is **correct** (it points exactly at `[seed_tid]` on the `with pl.at(...)` line, in module/file coordinates).

The actual bug is a coordinate-system mismatch in error-source-line attachment:

- Diagnostic spans carry **module** line numbers — each entity's local AST line is shifted by its `line_offset` in `SpanTracker.get_span`.
- But for `<string>` sources (`pl.parse` / `@pl.jit`), `open("<string>")` fails, so `_attach_source_lines_to_error` fell back to the **entity block** from `inspect.getsourcelines`, which starts at the `@pl.program`/`def` line and is thus offset by `line_offset`. So `source_lines[begin_line - 1]` resolved to a line `line_offset` rows too far, and the caret drifted that many lines past the real span.

This affected **every** `<string>`-parsed error, not just `deps=` (verified with an unrelated `Unknown operation` error whose caret was off by the same `line_offset`).

## Fix

`_attach_source_lines_to_error` (`python/pypto/language/parser/decorator.py`) now produces **module-indexed** source lines, with a clear resolution order:

1. Real files — read the whole file (line N → `source_lines[N-1]`).
2. `<string>` sources — `linecache.getlines` returns the full module text (`text_parser.parse` populates it before `exec`); already module-indexed.
3. Last resort — pad the entity block with `line_offset` blank leading lines to restore module indexing.

Both call sites (`@pl.function`, `@pl.program`) pass `line_offset`. No IR / binding / type-stub changes (pure Python).

## Before → After (issue repro via `pl.parse`)

Before — caret lands two lines below, under `w_down[...]`:
```
15 |  with pl.at(..., deps=[seed_tid] + [...]) as down_tid:
16 |      a0 = mlp_tile[:, k0:k0 + 128]
17 |      w0 = w_down[k0:k0 + 128, n0:n0 + 1024]
   |                                            ^
```
After — caret on the `with pl.at(...)` line under `[seed_tid]`:
```
15 |  with pl.at(..., deps=[seed_tid] + [...]) as down_tid:
   |                            ^
```

## Tests

- New `TestErrorCaretAlignment` in `tests/ut/language/parser/test_text_parser.py` — parses a `@pl.program` via `pl.parse` and asserts the rendered caret lands on the span's line (deps shape rejection + a generic op error). Verified to fail pre-fix, pass post-fix.
- Green: 742 `tests/ut/language/parser/`, plus full `tests/ut/language` and `tests/ut/jit` (1043 tests).

title: [Feature] @pl.jit diagnostics: report real source provenance instead of "<string>"
body:
### Summary

When a `@pl.jit` kernel fails to parse or compile, the diagnostic header and code snippet reference a synthesized `<string>` source rather than the user's real kernel file. `@pl.jit` re-derives the kernel into a fresh `@pl.program` **source string** (via `ast.unparse`, `specializer.py:1418`) and parses that string with no filename (`decorator.py:1288` → `pl.parse(source)`), so `text_parser.parse` falls back to `filename="<string>"` (`text_parser.py:144`). Improve the error provenance so a JIT compile error can be mapped back toward the original source the user wrote.

### Motivation / Use Case

- For `@pl.jit` kernels, parse/compile errors print `--> <string>:N:C` plus a snippet of the **generated (specialized)** program — not the user's file. A reader hunts for the error at a file/line that doesn't correspond to what they wrote. This is exactly what made #1558 confusing to triage.
- Plain `@pl.function` / `@pl.program` parsed from a real file already report the real path + line numbers (`decorator.py:676-798`); only the JIT path loses provenance.
- Even a minimal improvement (naming the failing kernel in the header) makes the error far more navigable.

Note: #1611 already fixed the caret to be correct **within** the printed `<string>` snippet, so JIT errors are actionable today. This issue is specifically about source *provenance / navigability*, not correctness of the caret.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Two tiers, smallest first.

**Tier 1 — cheap, no semantic risk (recommended starting point).**
Pass a descriptive `filename` into the JIT parse call (`decorator.py:1288`):

```python
# before
parsed = pl.parse(source)
# after
parsed = pl.parse(source, filename=f"<jit:{self.__name__}>")
```

The header then reads e.g. `--> <jit:matmul>:15:86` instead of an anonymous `<string>`, so the user immediately knows which kernel failed. Line numbers still index the generated source, which the diagnostic already prints in full.

**Tier 2 — larger, design discussion (optional source map).**
Build a `generated_line -> (original_file, original_line)` map in the specializer and translate spans before rendering (consumed in `SpanTracker.get_span` or at render time), so the `-->` can point into the user's actual `.py`.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Feed the transformed AST directly to `ASTParser`** (skip the `unparse -> reparse` round-trip) so original `lineno`/`col_offset` survive. Moderate refactor of `ASTParser.__init__` + `SpanTracker`; still hits the transformed-text caveat below.
- **Do nothing.** #1611 makes the caret correct within the printed snippet, so errors are already actionable — this is purely a provenance/UX enhancement.

### Additional Context

**Why a clean real-file remap is hard.** The generated string is a *transformed* program, so there is no 1:1 line/column mapping back to the user's source, and original AST positions are lost across `unparse -> reparse`. The transformations that break the mapping:

- `ast.unparse` collapses multi-line statements onto a single line (this is why #1558's `with pl.at(...)` shows as one line).
- Variables are alpha-renamed (`_rename_map`, `x -> x_v1`).
- Tensor shapes are baked in, scalars folded, dynamic dims rewritten to `pl.tensor.dim(...)`.
- Statements are added / removed / reordered (e.g. `M, N = a.shape` expanded; `bind_dynamic` stripped; loop bridge assignments synthesized).

Consequence: pointing at the original file can show text that does not match the (transformed) error context. Errors about the user's **literal syntax** (e.g. the `deps=` shape in #1558) map cleanly; errors about **synthesized content** do not. `_rewrite_jit_error` (`decorator.py:84-110`) already un-renames variables in the error **message text** but intentionally does not remap `span` / `file` / `source_lines`.

**Pointers:** `decorator.py:1288` (parse call), `specializer.py:1418` (`ast.unparse`), `text_parser.py:144` (default filename), `decorator.py:84-110` (`_rewrite_jit_error`), `span_tracker.py:37-55` (`get_span` adds `line_offset`).

Related: #1558 (caret bug found while diagnosing this; fixed in #1611), #1305 (source mapping for verifier output).

title: feat(ir): software-pipeline pl.pipeline across the cube/vector tpush/tpop boundary
body:
## Summary

`pl.pipeline` over a fused cube→vector→cube body (QK matmul → softmax → SV matmul, with the cross-core moves lowered to `tile.tpush_to_aiv` / `tile.tpop_from_aiv`) did not overlap the AIC (cube) and AIV (vector) engines across iterations — the cube stalled at each `tpop` instead of running the next iteration's matmul, recovering only ~3% vs a hand-written engine-grouped unroll's ~12%.

The fix is in `CanonicalizeIOOrder` (the pass that already reorders pipeline bodies for ping-pong), not `LowerPipelineLoops` (which only replicates). Its priority ladder lumped the producer matmul, `tpush`, `tpop`, and consumer matmul into one `TileCompute` tier, so the replicated body stayed per-clone serial.

### What changed

- **Generalize the stage ladder across the AIC↔AIV boundary** (first commit): add `CrossCorePush` / `CrossCorePop` / `ConsumerCompute` tiers so each cross-core stage clusters across the replicated clones. The body regroups from `QK0,tpush0,tpop0,SV0, QK1,…` to `QK0,QK1 | tpush0,tpush1 | tpop0,tpop1 | SV0,SV1`, keeping sibling `raw_scores`/result tiles co-live so `MemoryReuse` double-buffers them. A forward "downstream of a cross-core pop" sweep classifies post-pop compute; a `tile.create` refinement keeps a consumer's accumulator init beside it.

- **Defer consumer-only L0 `tile.move`** (second commit): a `tile.move` into L0 (Left/Right) feeding only consumer-stage ops (e.g. the V operand prep) is kept with its consumer instead of hoisted, so sibling clones share one L0 buffer rather than partitioning the scarce L0 space — the right default since L0 capacity, not cross-iteration overlap, is usually the binding constraint.

Why ordering (not instruction overlap) is the lever: Ascend executes event/dependency-driven, so program order only changes the buffer live-ranges `MemoryReuse` sees. Clustering keeps sibling tiles co-live (distinct buffers → ping-pong); interleaving collapses them (shared buffer → false WAR → serialization). Bodies without cross-core ops are unaffected.

## Testing

- New `TestCrossCorePipeline` suite: AIC/AIV stage clustering, 3-clone, create/move placement, `tpush`-not-sunk, load/store invariance, transitive consumer chain, `tfree`, FIFO/causal order, no-cross-core regression, replicate-then-reorder.
- `tests/ut` regression green; qwen3 jit integration test green; clang-tidy + code review clean.
- Verified end-to-end on the qwen3 `fa_fused_aic` kernel: the AIC stream clusters `tpush,tpush,tpop,tpop`; the scores/result ping-pong is preserved (2 distinct Acc buffers); L0B footprint halved (1 shared buffer vs 2 partitioned).
- Docs updated (`docs/en` + `docs/zh-cn`).

## Related Issues

Fixes #1610

title: feat(jit): map @pl.jit diagnostics to the user's real source
body:
## Summary

`@pl.jit` re-derives each kernel into a generated `@pl.program` string (via `ast.unparse`) and reparses it, so parse/compile errors pointed at an anonymous `<string>` source instead of the user's `.py`. This adds a source map so diagnostics point back at the real file.

- **Specializer** builds a `generated_line → (orig_file, orig_line, orig_col)` map (`Specializer.source_map`) by reparsing the assembled program and zipping its statements against the transformed AST, which still carries the original linenos.
- **`pl.parse(..., source_map=...)`** publishes the map via a `ContextVar` so `SpanTracker.get_span` emits original-source coordinates. Because IR-node spans carry the real location, **both parse errors and compile/pass errors** (which embed `span.to_string()` via `INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN`) now point at the real file.
- **Error renderer** reads the snippet from the real file via `linecache`, falling back to the exception's `source_lines` for synthetic filenames.

Mapping is **statement-granular**: multi-line statements resolve to their start line; synthesized statements (loop bridges, expanded `M, N = a.shape`, stripped `bind_dynamic`) keep the generated `<jit:name>` coordinates. The `source_map` parameter defaults to `None`, a no-op for all non-JIT parsing.

## Testing

- [x] 11 new tests across specializer / span-tracker / renderer / decorator (map building, span remap, real-file snippet, end-to-end provenance)
- [x] Full `tests/ut/` suite: 5391 passed, 28 skipped
- [x] Code review completed
- [x] Documentation updated (`docs/en` + `docs/zh-cn` `ir/07-parser.md`)

Fixes #1612

title: [Pass Bug] 8 passes skip the Submit IR kind (exact-kind Call dispatch) inside pl.manual_scope
body:
### Pass Name

Umbrella tracking issue across **8 passes** (shared root cause). Per-pass checklist below: `normalize_return_order`, `inject_gm_pipe_buffer`, `inline_functions`, `flatten_call_expr`, `convert_tensor_to_tile_ops`, `optimize_orch_tensors`, `materialize_tensor_strides`, `fuse_create_assemble_to_slice`.

### Description

Each of these passes walks call-like IR nodes via **exact-kind** `As<Call>` / `VisitExpr_(CallPtr)` / the `GetCallFromStmt` helper (`include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/transform_utils.h:84`, which is `As<Call>`-only). `Submit` is a **sibling `ObjectKind`** (emitted by `pl.submit` inside `pl.manual_scope`), **not** a `Call` subclass, so these passes silently skip it — the exact failure mode documented in `.claude/rules/pass-submit-awareness.md`.

All 8 run **before** `DeriveCallDirections` (pass 34, the point where `Submit` is lowered to `Call`), so they genuinely see live `Submit` nodes. `DeriveCallDirections` itself was already made submit-aware in #1552 and is the reference implementation.

Each item below has a committed `xfail(strict=False)` regression test (branch `test/pass-before-after-coverage`) that encodes correct behavior and **fails today**; it flips to passing once its pass is fixed.

- [x] **normalize_return_order** — `normalize_return_order_pass.cpp:241` (`TupleIndexPermutationMutator`): `Submit` result `TupleGetItem` indices not remapped after Out-param reorder → unpacked names bind the wrong output buffers. Repro: `test_normalize_return_order.py::TestNormalizeReturnOrderSubmit::test_submit_swapped_returns_remapped`
- [x] **inject_gm_pipe_buffer** — uses `GetCallFromStmt`: a Group launched via `pl.submit` on Ascend910B is invisible → no `tensor.create` placeholder, `__gm_pipe_buffer` not forwarded. Repro: `test_inject_gm_pipe_buffer.py::test_gm_pipe_injection_handles_submit_launched_group`
- [x] **inline_functions** — `CalledInlineCollector`/`InlineCallsMutator`: `pl.submit` of an Inline fn is not inlined; the fn is dropped but the dangling `Submit` survives and `InlineFunctionsEliminated` misses it. Repro: `test_inline_functions.py::TestInlineFunctionsSubmitCallSite::test_submit_of_inline_eliminates_reference`
- [x] **flatten_call_expr** — no `VisitExpr_(SubmitPtr)`: a nested `Call` arg of a `Submit` is not hoisted → three-address invariant violated. Repro: `test_flatten_call_expr_pass.py::TestFlattenPreservesAttrs::test_nested_call_arg_in_submit_is_flattened`
- [x] **convert_tensor_to_tile_ops** — `CallSiteUpdateMutator`: a `pl.submit` call site to a transformed InCore gets no `tensor.create` and the appended Out arg is not forwarded. Repro: `test_convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.py::TestSubmitCallSiteUpdate::test_submit_call_site_gets_tensor_create`
- [x] **optimize_orch_tensors** — `OrchRewriter::TryRewriteCall`: the `IsSubmitCall` branch is dead for real `Submit` nodes → a windowable kernel launched via `pl.submit` stays baseline. Repro: `test_optimize_orch_tensors.py::TestOutWindowSubmitCall::test_submit_windowable_kernel_is_externalized`
- [x] **materialize_tensor_strides** — no `VisitExpr_(SubmitPtr)`: a `Submit` node's own return type keeps an empty stride while every other reachable `TensorType` is materialized. Repro: `test_materialize_tensor_strides_pass.py::test_submit_return_type_materialized`
- [x] **fuse_create_assemble_to_slice** — `BufferRootCollector` (`As<Call>`): a `pl.submit` callee never propagates its Out-param buffer root → create+assemble around a submit is left unfused. Repro: `test_fuse_create_assemble_to_slice.py::test_submit_create_assemble_fused_to_slice`

Related (context, different root cause): #1368.

### Git Commit ID

35731d4833cdef3c49d8da254bba1d9a145be92f

### Before IR (Input)

Representative case — `normalize_return_order`. The InCore `kernel` returns `(out_b, out_a)` (reversed vs Out-param order); the orchestrator launches it via `pl.submit` and unpacks `(a, b)`:

```python
@pl.program
class Before:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def kernel(self, x: pl.Tensor[[16], pl.FP32],
               out_a: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16], pl.FP32]],
               out_b: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16], pl.FP32]]) -> tuple[pl.Tensor[[16], pl.FP32], pl.Tensor[[16], pl.FP32]]:
        x_tile = pl.load(x, [0], [16])
        a_tile = pl.tile.add(x_tile, x_tile)
        b_tile = pl.tile.mul(x_tile, x_tile)
        out_b_store = pl.store(b_tile, [0], out_b)
        out_a_store = pl.store(a_tile, [0], out_a)
        return (out_b_store, out_a_store)   # reversed vs (out_a, out_b)

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
    def main(self, x, out_a: pl.Out[...], out_b: pl.Out[...]) -> tuple[...]:
        with pl.manual_scope():
            (a, b), tid = pl.submit(self.kernel, x, out_a, out_b)
        return (a, b)
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

Step A reorders the kernel's returns to match Out-param order `(out_a, out_b)`; Step B must then **remap the caller's projections** so `a`/`b` still bind the same logical buffers (encoded as the swapped `(b, a)` unpack):

```python
class Expected:
    def kernel(...) -> tuple[...]:
        ...
        return (out_a_store, out_b_store)   # normalized order

    def main(...) -> tuple[...]:
        with pl.manual_scope():
            (b, a), tid = pl.submit(self.kernel, x, out_a, out_b)  # _submit_tmp indices remapped
        return (a, b)
```

### Actual IR or Error

Step A reorders the kernel returns, but `TupleIndexPermutationMutator` matches `As<Call>` only and never tracks the `Submit` result, so the caller's `TupleGetItem` indices are left unchanged:

```python
    def main(...) -> tuple[...]:
        with pl.manual_scope():
            (a, b), tid = pl.submit(self.kernel, x, out_a, out_b)  # NOT remapped — stale indices
        return (a, b)
```

`ir.assert_structural_equal(After, Expected)` fails on `['main'].body` (the manual_scope projection order differs). Net effect: after the kernel's outputs are reordered, `a` and `b` silently bind the wrong output tensors.

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Additional Context

**Common fix shape** (same for all 8): make each call-walk Submit-aware — use `AsCallLike` / a `SubmitToCallView` adapter, preserve Submit-ness through rewrites, relax the args-vs-params size guard to the **prefix invariant** (`args_.size() <= params_.size()`, not `==`), and account for the trailing `Scalar[TASK_ID]` in the return tuple. See `.claude/rules/pass-submit-awareness.md` and the reference fix in #1552 (`DeriveCallDirections`).

The 8 `xfail(strict=False)` regression tests are committed on branch `test/pass-before-after-coverage`; each will flip to passing (xpass) once its pass is fixed, so they double as ready-made acceptance checks.

---

**Status: implemented** on branch `test/pass-before-after-coverage` (commit `b24d7409`). All 8 passes are now Submit-aware; the 8 committed before/after regression tests (previously `xfail`) pass as normal tests, and the full `tests/ut/ir` transforms suite is green. `DeriveCallDirections` reference fix: #1552.

title: test(passes): before/after IR coverage + Submit-awareness fixes (#1615)
body:
## Summary

Two related changes, in order:

1. **`test(passes)`** — add the project's canonical Before/After/Expected
   (`assert_structural_equal`) coverage across the HIGH+MEDIUM-priority transform
   passes: ~109 new structural tests + 16 conversions of weak property/smoke
   tests, targeting previously-uncovered branches (`pl.manual_scope`/`pl.submit`
   handling, control-flow bodies, backend gates, edge cases).

2. **`fix(passes)` — Fixes #1615** — the new tests surfaced a family of 8
   "submit-awareness" bugs: `pl.submit` (inside `pl.manual_scope`) emits the
   `Submit` IR kind, a *sibling* of `Call` (not a subclass), and 8 passes walked
   call-like nodes via exact-kind `As<Call>` / `GetCallFromStmt` and silently
   skipped `Submit`. Each is now Submit-aware, preserving Submit-ness
   (`deps_`/`kwargs_`/`attrs_` and the trailing `Scalar[TASK_ID]` return) where
   it rewrites the node.

## The 8 fixes (#1615)

| Pass | Fix |
| ---- | --- |
| `normalize_return_order` | track Submit results → remap `TupleGetItem` projection indices after Out-param reorder |
| `materialize_tensor_strides` | `VisitExpr_(SubmitPtr)` → materialize the Submit's own return-type strides |
| `flatten_call_expr` | `VisitExpr_(SubmitPtr)` → hoist nested Call/Submit args (preserve `deps_`) |
| `fuse_create_assemble_to_slice` | route Submit through the Out/InOut buffer-root analysis via `SubmitToCallView` |
| `inject_gm_pipe_buffer` | Submit-aware call graph + both rewriters + recurse `RuntimeScopeStmt` so a `pl.submit`-launched Group gets its `__gm_pipe_buffer` |
| `convert_tensor_to_tile_ops` | `HandleSubmitCallSite` → allocate + forward appended runtime-Out args at a Submit call site |
| `optimize_orch_tensors` | dispatch `TryRewriteCall` on the Submit's Call view, rebuild a Submit for window-write externalization |
| `InlineFunctionsEliminated` verifier | flag a dangling `pl.submit` to a dropped Inline function |

Reference implementation: #1552 (`DeriveCallDirections`). The 8 committed
before/after regression tests (initially `xfail`) now pass as normal tests.

## Verification

- `tests/ut/ir/` + `tests/ut/pass/`: **3680 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed**.
- clang-tidy, clang-format, cpplint, ruff, pyright all clean.
- Test-only commit changes no source; the fix commit changes no IR definitions
  or bindings (pass-internal only).

introduced in #1599 on real silicon — coverage the existing `PTOTestCase`
harness does not provide (it never touches `ChipWorker` / `DistributedWorker`).

title: feat(logging): add CHECK_SPAN/UNREACHABLE_SPAN and fix pass CHECK misuse
body:
## Summary

Introduce `CHECK_SPAN` and `UNREACHABLE_SPAN` macros so user-facing failures
can attach the IR `Span` — symmetric to the existing `INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN` /
`INTERNAL_UNREACHABLE_SPAN`. When a DSL writer trips a user-facing check
deep inside the compiler (e.g. inside a pass, or while loading a `.pto` file),
the failure message now ends with `[file:line:col]` pointing back to their
source.

Also reclassifies pass-internal `CHECK` calls (157 sites across 17 files)
that were really enforcing IR invariants — passes operate on IR that earlier
passes have already verified, so a failed invariant inside a pass indicates
a compiler bug, not a user error. These become `INTERNAL_CHECK` (and
`INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN` wherever a `Span` was already in scope).

### Net effect for users

- `.pto` deserialization errors now include the originating DSL source line
  in the message (6 sites in `type_deserializers.cpp` migrated to
  `CHECK_SPAN`).
- Op-conversion failures during `ConvertTensorToTileOps` now include the
  user's source line (54 sites in `op_conversion_registry.cpp`).
- Documented user-facing limitations — e.g. *"only 2D scatter_update is
  currently supported"*, *"unsupported (rank, dim) for tensor.gather"*,
  *"i16 flat-index limit"* — remain `CHECK_SPAN` (user can fix), while
  arg-count / type / unreachable checks become `INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN`
  (compiler bug).

### What does NOT change

`flatten_tile_nd_to_2d`, `l0_tile_chooser`, and the `lower_transpose`
double-transpose rejection genuinely surface user-facing constraints (their
tests assert `ValueError`). They keep `CHECK`.

## Files

- `include/pypto/core/logging.h` — new `CHECK_SPAN` / `UNREACHABLE_SPAN` macros
- `src/ir/serialization/type_deserializers.cpp` — 6× `CHECK` → `CHECK_SPAN`
- `src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp` — 53 `INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN`, 3 `CHECK_SPAN`, 4 `INTERNAL_UNREACHABLE_SPAN`
- 16 other passes in `src/ir/transforms/` — `CHECK` → `INTERNAL_CHECK` / `INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN`
- `docs/en/dev/02-error-handling.md` + `docs/zh-cn/dev/02-error-handling.md` — document the new macros and the "inside passes" policy
- `.claude/rules/error-checking.md` — same policy for AI sessions

## Test plan

- [x] `cmake --build build --parallel` clean
- [x] `pytest tests/ut/` — 5563 pass, 1 skipped; the 1 fail + 2 errors (`test_run_config.py`, `test_block_dim_plumbing.py`) are pre-existing on `main` and unrelated (`Worker.current` attribute, from the runtime refactor).
- [x] Tests that assert user-facing `ValueError` still pass (`TestFlattenTileNdTo2DErrors`, `TestL0TilingInvariants`, `TestDoubleTransposeRejected`, `TestAutoTileMatmulL0KOnly::test_k_not_divisible_skipped`)
- [x] `clang-format`, `cpplint`, `markdownlint`, header / English / large-file pre-commit hooks all green

title: feat(jit): expose CompiledProgram via JITFunction.compile() — closes #1455
body:
## Summary

Add ``JITFunction.compile(*args, **kwargs) -> CompiledProgram`` so callers can drive worker runtime APIs (``ChipWorker.run`` / ``ChipWorker.register`` or a hand-rolled ``simpler.worker.Worker``) on a ``@pl.jit`` kernel directly — without writing a separate ``@pl.program`` wrapper around the same logic.

This closes the runtime-side gap that issue #1455 flagged: the worker-side infrastructure landed in #1496 (CompiledProgram extraction surface) and #1599 (Worker ABC + ChipWorker / DistributedWorker + run/register/RegistrationHandle), but ``@pl.jit`` kept its compiled artefacts strictly private in ``self._cache``. ``compile()`` is the missing accessor.

## Implementation

Factor the cache-lookup / on-miss compile pipeline out of ``__call__`` into a private ``_resolve_compiled(args, kwargs)`` helper that does:

- ``config=`` keyword extraction (so it never leaks into the decorated function's signature)
- ``_bind_args`` shape / dtype classification
- platform + strategy cache-key construction
- on-miss ``_compile()`` invocation populating ``self._cache``

Both ``__call__`` (which then dispatches the cached CompiledProgram on device) and the new public ``compile()`` (which returns it) call this helper. There is exactly one implementation of the binding / cache-key / compile sequence; the two entry points are guaranteed to share the cache and never recompile for the same specialization key.

## Use case

\`\`\`python
@pl.jit
def my_kernel(x, w, out):
    ...

worker = ChipWorker(config=RunConfig(platform=\"a2a3\"))
# Specialize + compile for the shape implied by sample args.
compiled = my_kernel.compile(sample_x, sample_w, sample_out)
# Preload static weights once, dispatch many.
w_dev = worker.alloc_tensor(real_w.shape, real_w.dtype, init=real_w)
h = worker.register(compiled)
for batch in stream:
    h(batch.x, w_dev, batch.out)
\`\`\`

The returned ``CompiledProgram`` exposes the full extraction surface from PR #1496 — ``chip_callable``, ``runtime_name``, ``runtime_config``, ``build_orch_args``, ``build_call_config``, ``output_dir``, ``platform``, ``output_indices`` — so users who need to drive ``simpler.worker.Worker`` directly can do so.

This covers the issue's requirements:

- Worker.run(...) — via ChipWorker.register(compiled) / ChipWorker.run(compiled, ...)
- Explicit CallConfig.block_dim — via RunConfig.block_dim or compiled.build_call_config(block_dim=...)
- Persistent child_memory=True tensors — via worker.alloc_tensor (already automatic for DeviceTensor args)
- Pre-uploaded static weights / KV cache — via alloc_tensor(init=...)
- Generated host orchestration callable extraction — via compiled.chip_callable / compiled.runtime_name

## Testing

New file ``tests/ut/jit/test_jit_compile_extraction.py``:

- ``test_compile_returns_compiled_program_instance`` — return type check
- ``test_compile_cache_hit_returns_same_instance`` — two ``compile()`` calls share the cache
- ``test_call_then_compile_returns_cached_instance`` — ``compile()`` after a prior cache-populating call hits the cache (verified through ``compile_for_test`` since unit tests don't have a device for ``__call__``)
- ``test_compile_cache_miss_on_different_shape`` — distinct specialization → distinct CompiledProgram
- ``test_compile_extracts_config_kwarg`` — ``config=RunConfig(...)`` is consumed by JIT, not forwarded to the kernel
- ``test_compiled_program_has_extraction_attributes`` — returned object exposes the worker-integration attributes (assertion-based, no device required)

No on-device tests in this PR — the artefact is identical to what a direct ``ir.compile(@pl.program-wrapper-of-the-jit-body)`` would produce, so existing ``__call__`` integration tests already cover end-to-end behaviour.

## Notes

- ``compile_for_test`` is unchanged and still returns ``ir.Program`` (its existing purpose: structural-equality comparison in pass tests). The new ``compile`` returns ``CompiledProgram`` (the full post-pass + codegen artefact).
- ``_resolve_compiled`` is private; ``compile_for_test`` keeps its existing path (it has slightly different semantics — best-effort cache population + always-succeed Program return — that don't fit the shared helper).

Closes #1455

title: [Bug] tensor.gather on local TileType input can overwrite source row during lowering
body:
### Component

IR / `ConvertTensorToTileOps` / `tensor.gather` lowering for `TileType` inputs

### Description

`tensor.gather` can mutate or alias its local TileType input when the input is a local tensor lowered to a tile.

The repro below creates a local `[16, 256]` FP32 tensor `local_scores`, reads it with a scalar loop, then calls:

```python
gathered_tile = pl.gather(local_scores, dim=-1, index=idx)
```

The gather output itself is correct. However, reading the same `local_scores` again with the same scalar loop after `pl.gather` returns wrong values: row 0 behaves as if it has been overwritten by row 15.

This violates the expected read-only semantics of `gather`: neither the source input nor the index input should be modified by the operation.

This was observed on PyPTO main after #1609, where `tensor.gather` now accepts `TileType` input/index and no longer fails at compile time.

### Minimal Reproducer

Save this as `repro_tensor_gather_local_alias.py` and run it with the normal PyPTO runtime environment configured.

```python
import argparse

import pypto.language as pl
import torch
from pypto.runtime.runner import RunConfig


ROWS = 16
COLS = 256
TOPK = 8


@pl.jit
def repro_kernel(
    scores: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
    idx: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, TOPK], pl.INT32],
    before: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, TOPK], pl.FP32]],
    gathered: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, TOPK], pl.FP32]],
    after: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, TOPK], pl.FP32]],
):
    for _ in pl.spmd(1, name_hint="gather_alias_repro"):
        local_scores = pl.create_tensor([ROWS, COLS], dtype=pl.FP32)
        local_scores[:, :] = scores[:, :]

        local_idx = pl.create_tensor([ROWS, TOPK], dtype=pl.INT32)
        local_idx[:, :] = idx[:, :]

        before_tile = pl.full([ROWS, TOPK], dtype=pl.FP32, value=0.0)
        for r in pl.range(ROWS):
            for k in pl.range(TOPK):
                col_i32 = pl.read(local_idx, [r, k])
                col = pl.cast(col_i32, pl.INDEX)
                val = pl.read(local_scores, [r, col])
                pl.write(before_tile, [r, k], val)
        before[:, :] = before_tile

        gathered_tile = pl.gather(local_scores, dim=-1, index=idx)
        gathered[:, :] = gathered_tile

        after_tile = pl.full([ROWS, TOPK], dtype=pl.FP32, value=0.0)
        for r in pl.range(ROWS):
            for k in pl.range(TOPK):
                col_i32 = pl.read(local_idx, [r, k])
                col = pl.cast(col_i32, pl.INDEX)
                val = pl.read(local_scores, [r, col])
                pl.write(after_tile, [r, k], val)
        after[:, :] = after_tile


def make_scores() -> torch.Tensor:
    row = torch.arange(ROWS, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(ROWS, 1) * 1000.0
    col = torch.arange(COLS, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(1, COLS)
    return row + col


def make_idx() -> torch.Tensor:
    base = torch.tensor([7, 9, 3, 128, 255, 0, 64, 11], dtype=torch.int32)
    return torch.stack([(base + r * 13) % COLS for r in range(ROWS)])


def first_mismatch(actual: torch.Tensor, expected: torch.Tensor) -> str:
    neq = actual != expected
    if not bool(neq.any()):
        return ""
    flat_idx = int(torch.nonzero(neq.reshape(-1), as_tuple=False)[0].item())
    idx = torch.unravel_index(torch.tensor(flat_idx), actual.shape)
    idx_tuple = tuple(int(x) for x in idx)
    return f"{idx_tuple}: actual={actual[idx_tuple].item()} expected={expected[idx_tuple].item()}"


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("-p", "--platform", default="a2a3sim", choices=["a2a3", "a2a3sim", "a5", "a5sim"])
    parser.add_argument("-d", "--device", type=int, default=0)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    scores = make_scores()
    idx = make_idx()
    expected = torch.gather(scores, dim=-1, index=idx.long())
    before = torch.zeros_like(expected)
    gathered = torch.zeros_like(expected)
    after = torch.zeros_like(expected)

    repro_kernel(
        scores,
        idx,
        before,
        gathered,
        after,
        config=RunConfig(platform=args.platform, device_id=args.device, dump_passes=True),
    )

    for name, actual in {"before": before, "gathered": gathered, "after": after}.items():
        ok = torch.equal(actual, expected)
        print(f"{name}: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
        if not ok:
            print(f"  first mismatch: {first_mismatch(actual, expected)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run:

```bash
python repro_tensor_gather_local_alias.py -p a2a3sim
```

### Expected Behavior

All three outputs should match `torch.gather(scores, dim=-1, index=idx)`:

```text
before: PASS
gathered: PASS
after: PASS
```

`before` and `after` use the same scalar-read loop:

```python
val = pl.read(local_scores, [r, col])
pl.write(out_tile, [r, k], val)
```

The only operation between them is `pl.gather(local_scores, dim=-1, index=idx)`, which should not mutate `local_scores`.

### Actual Behavior

Observed result:

```text
before: PASS
gathered: PASS
after: FAIL
  first mismatch: (0, 0): actual=15007.0 expected=7.0
```

The input is constructed as:

```python
scores[row, col] = row * 1000 + col
```

Therefore `15007.0` means the `after` scalar-read path read row 15, col 7 where row 0, col 7 was expected. The scalar-read loop itself is not the cause, because the same loop passes before `pl.gather`.

### Preliminary Analysis

The generated PTO shows that the TileType-input `tensor.gather` path materializes each source row into a scratch tile before calling `pto.tgather`. The scratch tile for the sliced `[1, 256]` row aliases the same base address as the full `local_scores` tile:

```mlir
%local_scores__tile = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c96_i64 ... rows=16, cols=256
...
%0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c96_i64 ... rows=16, cols=256
...
%gather_inp_row = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c96_i64 ... rows=1, cols=256
%slice_view = pto.subview %0[%gather_lv, %c0_index] sizes [1, 256] ...
pto.tmov ins(%slice_view) outs(%gather_inp_row)
pto.tgather ins(%gather_inp_row, %gather_idx_row, %gather_row_tmp) outs(%gather_row)
```

Since `%gather_inp_row` starts at the same address as `local_scores`, every row materialization writes the current source row into `local_scores` row 0. The gather result is still correct in the same iteration because `pto.tgather` immediately consumes that scratch row. After the loop finishes, row 0 has been overwritten by the last materialized row, row 15. This explains the `after` mismatch:

```text
after[0, 0] reads local_scores[0, 7]
actual = 15007.0  # row 15, col 7
expected = 7.0    # row 0, col 7
```

This suggests that the TileType-input `tensor.gather` lowering needs to ensure its row materialization scratch does not alias the source input tile, or otherwise avoid materializing by writing into the source tile's address range.

### Environment

Observed with:

```text
PyPTO: b5341e805fae2c4ee0b3ec1615b59755fa1015f9
ptoas: 0.42
platform: a2a3sim
```

### Related

- #1609 fixed the compile-time `TileType` acceptance path for `tensor.gather`.
- This issue tracks a separate runtime correctness problem after the code can compile and execute.

title: feat(verifier): make PH001 innermost-dim hint memory-space aware, deduped, clearer (#1305)
body:
## Summary

Improves the PH001 `TileInnermostDimGranularity` performance hint so it produces actionable, low-noise output on real kernels:

- **Memory-space aware**: the recommended-bytes threshold models an L2 cache-line concern. Tiles whose `target_memory` is cube-private L0/L1 (Mat/Left/Right/Acc, detected via `IsCubeMemorySpace`) never traverse L2, so they are now skipped instead of being flagged with a misleading "L2 cache line" message.
- **Deduped on transfer facts**: hits are collapsed to a single diagnostic per `(file, line, col, op, dtype, innermost_bytes, target_memory)` site with an occurrence count, so loop-unroll / per-fragment expansion no longer floods the channel — while distinct transfers sharing one source span (multiple loads on a line, macro expansion) keep their own accurate hit instead of conflating onto the first-seen tuple. Invalid/unknown spans bypass dedup and are emitted individually (they'd otherwise all collapse onto one bogus site).
- **Clearer message**: the diagnostic now echoes the evaluated `(dtype[innermost], target_memory)` tuple so the reported byte figure can be reconciled against the IR.

Addresses #1305.

## Test plan

- **Host-side unit tests** (`tests/ut/ir/verifier/test_perf_hint_tile_innermost_dim.py`): cube-memory-space suppression (L0/L1 tiles are not flagged), the `(dtype[innermost], target_memory)` tuple in the message, dedup behavior, and span propagation.
- **Docs**: `docs/en/dev/passes/92-diagnostics.md` and `docs/zh-cn/dev/passes/92-diagnostics.md` updated for the extended dedup key and invalid-span handling.

## Deferred

The following parts of #1305 are intentionally out of scope here, because the required metadata is not threaded onto `TileType`, the `Call` op, or `Span` today:

- DSL source-span reporting (ask 2): mapping the hint back to the originating DSL source location.
- Inner-dim constant naming (ask 3): surfacing the symbolic/named inner-dim constant instead of the raw byte figure.

The message and docs now note precisely what is missing and why.

title: fix(codegen): materialize Scalar tuple-return elements in orchestration (#631)
body:
## Summary

When an incore kernel returns a tuple that mixes `Tensor` and `Scalar` elements, the orchestration codegen mapped each return position to an `Out`/`InOut` param. A `Scalar` element (e.g. an index `o0 = ob * 32` computed from an input param) is not backed by an `Out` param, so it resolved to no param index and was dropped. The generated C++ then referenced an undefined variable (or, after an earlier stop-gap, a wrong `o0 = 0`), breaking compilation or producing incorrect runtime values.

This is the full fix: the orchestration codegen now materializes `Scalar` tuple-return elements at the call site (e.g. emitting `int64_t o0 = (ob * 32);`) instead of dropping them. It traces the callee's `ReturnStmt` value at that position, inlines its local scalar definitions, substitutes each callee param with the expression actually passed for it, and renders via the existing `GenerateExprString` path. When an element cannot be traced to a pure arithmetic function of the call args, it falls back to the prior `0` default so generated code stays compilable. The fix is applied on both the plain tuple-return path and the `pl.submit` return-alias path.

Addresses #631

## Test plan

- Host-side unit test added: `tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py::test_scalar_tuple_return_materialized`, which verifies the generated orchestration C++ materializes the Scalar tuple-return element instead of dropping it.
- The on-device ST scenario for this issue must be validated manually via `task-submit` on device 9. CI does not run device ST, so this is not exercised automatically here.

title: feat(codegen): wire rank-reducing tensor.slice drop_dims in orchestration view (#1349)
body:
## Summary

Wires orchestration `tensor.slice` `drop_dims` (numpy-style `C[i]` / `C[i, j, :, :]`) so that rank-reducing slices lower correctly. The implementation builds a full-rank view of the source tensor and then applies a rank-reduced reshape, producing the expected reduced-rank result.

This path is intentionally guarded to a **leading prefix** of dropped axes (e.g. `C[i]`, `C[i, j, :, :]`). Non-leading dropped axes (such as `C[:, i, :]`) are explicitly rejected with an actionable error message rather than silently miscompiling. A contiguity guard additionally requires every kept axis after the outermost to span its full extent, so the zero-copy `view().reshape()` lowering never emits a strided view that would assert on device.

The `>2D` `tile.slice` `drop_dims` path in `FlattenTileNdTo2D` remains rejected, but now emits a clearer hint describing what is still required (a `>2D` sliced-window merge plus a reduced-rank runtime tile binding).

Addresses #1349.

## Test plan

Host-side unit tests in `tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py` covering:
- Leading-prefix rank-reducing orchestration slices (`C[i]`, `C[i, j, :, :]`) lowering through the full-rank view + rank-reduced reshape.
- Rejection of non-leading dropped axes (`C[:, i, :]`) with the actionable error.
- Rejection of a strided inner kept axis (partially-sliced non-outermost axis) and coverage of the 0D scalar (`reshape(nullptr, 0)`) path.
- The clearer rejection hint for the `>2D` `tile.slice` `drop_dims` path in `FlattenTileNdTo2D`.

On-board system test in `tests/st/runtime/control_flow/test_dyn_orch_shape.py` (`test_dyn_orch_drop_dims_slice_add`), which CI runs on real a2a3 hardware:
- Orchestration slices `a[batch_index]` (numpy `C[i]`) on a `[nbatch, rows, cols]` DDR tensor, dropping the leading axis to a `[rows, cols]` sub-tensor forwarded to a 2D InCore add kernel.
- A non-zero `batch_index` forces a non-trivial `start_offset` fold (a buggy offset-0 lowering would still pass on batch 0); a lowering that ignored `drop_dims` would mismatch the 2D kernel-call binding. Validated end-to-end against the PyTorch reference (`c = a[batch_index] + b`).

## Deferred

Intentionally out of scope for this PR:
- Non-leading dropped-axis orchestration slices (e.g. `C[:, i, :]`) — currently rejected with an actionable error.
- The `>2D` `tile.slice` `drop_dims` path in `FlattenTileNdTo2D`, which requires a `>2D` sliced-window merge and a reduced-rank runtime tile binding.

## Summary

Adds a runtime regression repro for #1592 to `tests/st/runtime/test_fused_matmul_scatter.py`: a cube matmul fused with a **per-row, block-table-indirected (dynamic-address) GM scatter** in one `CORE_GROUP` mix scope, in both `SplitMode.NONE` and `SplitMode.UP_DOWN`.

Per the issue's isolation matrix, this dynamic-address WRITE on the vec side of a cube+vec mix scope compiles clean but deadlocks at runtime (`507018`), while the static-address WRITE (#1564, already in this file) runs. This PR adds the repro only — **no fix yet** — to confirm the behavior on a2a3 CI before committing to a fix.

New programs/cases (golden identical to the #1564 static variants — only the addressing mode differs):
- `FusedMatmulDynScatterProgram` / `…NoSplitProgram` — scatter row read from a block table at runtime (`cache_row = pl.read(block_table, [b]) * CACHE`; the `* CACHE` keeps the offset `index`-typed so codegen is clean, matching the issue).
- `TestFusedMatmulDynScatter` / `TestFusedMatmulDynScatterNoSplit`.

## Why a repro-only PR

I grounded the diagnosis offline (generated the post-PTOAS `aiv.cpp` via `--codegen-only --save-kernels`). Findings:
- Both AIV lanes (`subblockid==0` real vs the `else` replay) are **independently pipe-flag balanced** — matching the reporter's note that the outer `set_flag`/`wait_flag` frame is balanced. This **disproves the lane-asymmetry theory**.
- Diffing the generated AIV against the working #1564 contiguous kernel, the only op-level difference is one added block-table scalar load plus the dynamic store base address.

So it is possible this minimal repro does **not** deadlock. CI on a2a3 is the decisive signal:
- If it deadlocks (`507018`) → repro confirmed; proceed with the fix on this branch.
- If it passes → enrich the repro toward the real `models/deepseek/v4/decode_indexer_compressor.py` shape (the `gate(c_idx)` guard + block-table-via-tile-load path).

title: [Feature] pl.col_expand_add 需要补一下
body:
### Summary

"""Minimal PyPTO repro: `pl.col_expand_add` is missing.

Run:
    PTO_PLATFORM=a2a3sim python inductor_pto/docs/repro/repro_col_expand_add.py

Background
----------
PyPTO's unified ops provide column-broadcast `sub`, `mul`, `div` and the row
counterpart `row_expand_add`, but there is **no `col_expand_add`**. Column
broadcast add is `[1, N] + [M, N]` — a 1-D weight/bias added to every row of a
2-D tile (e.g. `a[N] + b[M, N]`). Without `col_expand_add` this pattern has no
correct primitive: plain `pl.add([1, N], [M, N])` does not expand along rows and
produces wrong numbers.

What this script shows
----------------------
1. Symbol table: `col_expand_{sub,mul,div}` and `row_expand_add` exist;
   `col_expand_add` does not.
2. A real `@pl.program` that column-broadcasts with `col_expand_mul` builds
   fine — proving the shapes / tiling are valid PyPTO.
3. The identical program written for **add** cannot be expressed: there is no
   `pl.col_expand_add` to call.

Desired fix
-----------
Add `col_expand_add` to `pypto/python/pypto/language/op/unified_ops.py` (plus
the matching `ir/op/tensor_ops.py` + tile lowering), aligned with the existing
`col_expand_{sub,mul,div}` and `row_expand_add`.
"""
import pypto.language as pl


def report_symbol_table():
    present = [n for n in ("col_expand", "col_expand_sub", "col_expand_mul",
                           "col_expand_div", "row_expand_add")
               if hasattr(pl, n)]
    missing = [n for n in ("col_expand_add",) if not hasattr(pl, n)]
    print("present :", present)
    print("missing :", missing)
    assert hasattr(pl, "col_expand_mul"), "expected col_expand_mul to exist"
    assert hasattr(pl, "row_expand_add"), "expected row_expand_add to exist"
    assert not hasattr(pl, "col_expand_add"), \
        "col_expand_add now exists — gap is fixed, update inductor_pto _PTO_COL_EXPAND_OPS"


# A column-broadcast MUL program — builds today (proves the pattern is legal).
@pl.program
class ColBroadcastMul:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Opaque)
    def compute(self,
                a: pl.Tensor[[256], pl.FP32],            # 1-D weight
                b: pl.Tensor[[128, 256], pl.FP32],
                out0: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[128, 256], pl.FP32]]
                ) -> pl.Tensor[[128, 256], pl.FP32]:
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, optimization=pl.chunked_loop_optimizer):
            for r in pl.parallel(0, 128, 32, chunk=1):
                col_vec = pl.reshape(pl.slice(a, [256], [0]), [1, 256])  # [1, 256]
                tile = pl.slice(b, [32, 256], [r, 0])                    # [32, 256]
                res = pl.col_expand_mul(tile, col_vec)                   # broadcasts col_vec across rows
                out0 = pl.assemble(out0, res, [r, 0])
        return out0


def show_add_has_no_primitive():
    # The same column broadcast for ADD has no callable: the only way to write
    # `a[N] + b[M, N]` correctly would be pl.col_expand_add, which is absent.
    fn = getattr(pl, "col_expand_add", None)
    print("pl.col_expand_add =", fn)
    if fn is None:
        print("=> CONFIRMED GAP: cannot express column-broadcast add "
              "([1, N] + [M, N]) without pl.col_expand_add.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    report_symbol_table()
    print("ColBroadcastMul program object:", ColBroadcastMul)  # builds OK
    show_add_has_no_primitive()
    print("OK: gap demonstrated (col_expand_mul works; col_expand_add missing).")

title: [Feature] Support Gather Directly to L1 — Eliminate GM Round-Trip
body:
### Summary

We need the pypto framework to support gathering data directly into L1, so that the subsequent Cube compute can read from L1 without going through GM.

Specifically:
1. **L1 buffer allocation**: A way to allocate buffers in L1 (currently `pl.create_tensor()` only creates GM tensors)
2. **Gather into L1**: The gather operation should be able to write its output directly to L1 instead of GM
3. **Cube reads from L1**: matmul and other Cube operations should be able to consume L1 buffers as input, skipping GM loads
4. **Synchronization**: When gather and compute are fused in one task, the compute side must wait until the gather side finishes writing to L1


### Motivation / Use Case

In sparse attention decode, the KV gather stage (`gather_kv`) gathers scattered KV rows from two paged KV pools (sliding-window + compressed cache) and writes the result to GM (`sparse_kv`). The subsequent QK/PV compute stage (`qk_pv`) must then reload that same data from GM into L1→L0. This GM write+read round-trip costs ~90 us per token, dominating the critical path.

Current data flow:
```
gather_kv: GM(ori_kv/cmp_kv) → GM(sparse_kv)    ## gather writes to GM
qk_pv:    GM(sparse_kv) → L1 → L0               ## compute reads back from GM
```

Desired data flow:
```
fused gather+compute: GM(ori_kv/cmp_kv) → L1 → L0  ## gather directly into L1, compute reads from L1
```

title: feat(tools): add clean_sim_trace simulator trace cleaning CLI
body:
## Summary

Adds `pypto.tools.clean_sim_trace`, a stdlib-only CLI that **converts the MindStudio Insight binary file (`visualize_data.bin`) emitted by the Ascend op-simulator into a Perfetto-viewable AI-core pipeline trace** (Chrome Trace Event JSON), plus a per-core instruction-metrics sidecar.

**Why read the binary instead of the sibling `trace.json`?** The simulator also writes an *official* Perfetto/Chrome trace (`trace.json`), but **that file is lossy — it carries strictly less information than `visualize_data.bin`.** The binary container holds the full set of MindStudio Insight blocks: the trace events *plus* the per-instruction `API_INSTR` metrics, source mapping, and other detail blocks. `trace.json` exports only the trace events. So `clean_sim_trace` reads the richer binary file directly, recovering the per-instruction metrics that the official Perfetto export drops.

- **`visualize_data.bin` parser** — length-prefixed block reader (TRACE + API_INSTR blocks).
- **`trace.clean.json`** — keeps pipeline lanes (MTE2/MTE1/CUBE/VECTOR/FIXPIPE/MTE3), drops scalar/sync noise, re-anchors `SET_FLAG`→`WAIT_FLAG` pairs as flow arrows, orders lanes by dataflow.
- **Sub-lane packing** — software-pipelined instructions on a pipe partially overlap; Chrome-trace `X` events on one `tid` must be disjoint or strictly nested, so each pipe's overlapping instructions are split into sub-lanes (`MTE1`, `MTE1#1`, …), one row per concurrently-live instruction — preserving the true pipeline depth in the viewer (it previously collapsed to ~2).
- **`instr_metrics.json`** — per-core instruction records (pipe, cycles, vector-utilization) reshaped from the API_INSTR block.

## Testing

- 21 unit tests in `tests/ut/tools/test_clean_sim_trace.py` (block parsing, rebuild rules, sync-arrow re-anchoring, sub-lane split, metrics reshape).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` / `pyright` clean.

## Docs

- `docs/en/dev/04-simulator-trace-cleaning.md` and `docs/zh-cn/...` — binary→Perfetto conversion, the lossiness of the official `trace.json`, file format, usage, rebuild rules, metrics sidecar.

title: feat(ir): add pl.col_expand_add for [1,N] + [M,N] broadcast
body:
## Summary

Adds the missing fourth column-broadcast arithmetic op alongside the existing
`col_expand_{mul,sub,div}` and the row counterpart `row_expand_add`.

Column-broadcast add (a 1-D bias added to every row of a 2-D tile, i.e. `a[1,N] + b[M,N]`)
had no correct primitive in PyPTO: plain `pl.add([1,N], [M,N])` only detects `[M,1]` row
broadcast via `DetectRowBroadcast` and silently produces wrong numbers for the column case.
ptoas already supports `pto.tcolexpandadd`, so this is a pipeline-plumbing gap rather than
a hardware capability gap.

This change is symmetric with the existing siblings:

- C++ IR ops: `tile.col_expand_add` and `tensor.col_expand_add` registered with the same
  type-deduction helpers as `col_expand_mul/sub/div`.
- Conversion: `tensor.col_expand_add → tile.col_expand_add` (RegisterSimple).
- Backend codegen: `tile.col_expand_add → pto.tcolexpandadd` in `kSimpleOps`. The codegen
  subview-materialization guard previously hard-coded `pto.tcolexpandmul`; extended to the
  whole `tcolexpand` family, with the materialization debug tag now derived from
  `pto_op_name` so future additions only need a `kSimpleOps` entry.
- Python: IR builder, language DSL, unified dispatch (`pl.col_expand_add`), and re-exports
  in `pypto.language` and `pypto.language.op`.
- Docs: en + zh-cn broadcast/expand tables updated.

Out of scope: extending `DetectRowBroadcast` to also detect `[1, N]`-shaped column
broadcast in plain `pl.add`. Users still need to explicitly call `pl.col_expand_add`
(same pattern as the existing `col_expand_mul/sub/div`).

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/ut/ir/operators/test_tensor_ops.py tests/ut/ir/operators/test_tile_ops.py tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.py tests/ut/language/test_unified_ops.py tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen_ops.py -k "col_expand_add or col_expand"` — 38 passed
- [x] Broader sweep of affected test files (719 tests) — all pass
- [x] Issue's reproducer program builds end-to-end with `pl.col_expand_add`
- [x] Codegen test asserts `pto.tcolexpandadd` appears in generated MLIR
