title: Consider integrating pre-runtime pass IR validation into the compile flow
body:
## Background

`pypto.debug.torch_codegen.validate_pass_ir_codegen_results` (python/pypto/debug/torch_codegen.py) can re-run each dumped pass IR via `torch_codegen` and numerically compare against golden outputs, giving us per-pass correctness checking before ever touching the device.

Today this is a standalone debug utility that is **not** wired into the compile flow:

- `pypto.ir.compile` (python/pypto/ir/compile.py) only emits the per-pass IR into `output_dir/passes_dump/` when `dump_passes=True`. It never calls the validator.
- Each consumer has to discover `passes_dump/`, prepare golden inputs/outputs, and call `validate_pass_ir_codegen_results` themselves.

## Where this is currently being wired up

The integration is presently being done downstream, at the test-harness level, in pypto-lib:

- hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#162 — adds `RunConfig.validate_ir` / `validate_ir_only` to the golden runner and calls `validate_pass_ir_codegen_results` between input generation and runtime.

## Question / proposal

Should pypto expose this as a first-class, optional step so consumers don't each re-implement the wiring? For example:

- an optional `validate_ir` path on `pypto.ir.compile` (or a thin helper next to it) that, given golden inputs/expected outputs + tolerances, runs the per-pass validation right after `passes_dump` is produced; or
- a documented, supported entry point that makes the `passes_dump` → `validate_pass_ir_codegen_results` contract official.

Looking for guidance on whether this belongs in pypto's compile flow, or should remain a debug-only utility that downstreams (like pypto-lib) integrate as needed.

Filed per discussion; closing pypto-lib#162 in favor of this issue.

title: [Feature] Support pld.DistributedTensor parameters in @pl.jit / @pl.jit.inline
body:
### Summary

The JIT specialization path does not recognize `pld.DistributedTensor` as a parameter kind. `@pl.jit` / `@pl.jit.inline` functions can only declare `pl.Tensor` params, so any kernel taking HCCL window tensors (`DistributedTensor`) or doing cross-rank communication cannot be authored as a jit function — it must be a `@pl.function(InCore)` inside a `@pl.program` class.

### Motivation / Use Case

Single-card compute kernels (hc_pre / gate / expert / …) are clean `@pl.jit.inline` functions composed by a top-level `@pl.jit` (`models/deepseek/v4/moe.py`). The cross-rank dispatch/combine stages take `DistributedTensor` window params and use `pld.system.notify` / `pld.system.wait` / `pld.tile.remote_store`. To keep the EP MoE (`moe_ep.py`) consistent with that jit composition style, we want dispatch/combine as `jit.inline` in their own files — impossible today, forcing two divergent authoring styles (jit for single-card, `@pl.program`/`@pl.function` for EP) for conceptually identical kernel composition.

### Proposed API / Behavior

```python
@pl.jit.inline
def dispatch_ep(
    indices: pl.Tensor[[T, TOPK], pl.INT32],
    recv_x: pld.DistributedTensor[[N_LOCAL * RECV_MAX, D], pl.INT8],
    ...
):
    pld.tile.remote_store(x_tile, target=recv_x, peer=dst, offsets=[row, 0])
```

The specializer's annotation classifier (`_is_tensor_annotation`, `pypto/python/pypto/jit/specializer.py:1176`) should recognize the subscripted `pld.DistributedTensor[[...], dtype]` form and route it to the right param kind — the way the `@pl.function` parser already does for InCore methods.

### Alternatives Considered

Author the cross-rank kernels as standalone `@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)` functions in separate files, called as bare cross-function calls from a `@pl.program` orchestration method. This works (verified — compiles end-to-end) but the EP kernels can't share the `jit.inline` style and can't be unit-tested via `run_jit` like single-card `dispatch.py`/`combine.py`.

### Additional Context

- Root cause: `_is_tensor_annotation` only matches `Tensor` (bare/subscripted), not `DistributedTensor`; zero references to `DistributedTensor` under `pypto/python/pypto/jit/`.
- The `@pl.function` parser path already resolves `pld.DistributedTensor` annotations for InCore methods.
- Concrete case: pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/{dispatch_ep.py, combine_ep.py, moe_ep.py}`.
- Related: #1127, #1320.
- pypto commit: `e851ba54` (main).

title: fix(codegen): make tile.slice a pure pto.subview view (fixes #1622)
body:
## Summary

`tile.slice` codegen is now always a single `pto.subview`. When the 4-arg form carries an explicit `valid_shape`, the value is encoded directly into `pto.subview`'s `valid [%vr, %vc]` clause — the same syntax `tile.assemble` already uses. The previous materializing path (`pto.subview` + `pto.tmov ins(view) outs(result)` + `pto.set_validshape`) is removed entirely.

Removing this **eager** materializing path fixes issue #1622 at the root: `tile.slice` is declared `set_output_memory_inherit_input`, so the slice result's MemRef shares the source base. For dynamic offsets the alloc pass falls back to bare `src_base` (see `allocate_memory_addr_pass.cpp:346-353`'s "safe because `tile.slice` re-derives offset from operands" note — which held only for the pure-subview path, not for `tmov+set_validshape`). The previous per-row `tmov` therefore wrote into the source allocation's row 0, silently corrupting source rows after the gather loop completed. The slice op's own emission can no longer do this — it emits only a `pto.subview`, with no destination buffer to overlap the source.

**Scope note:** this removes the *eager* `tmov` path only. A separate, pre-existing lazy path remains — when a slice feeds `pto.tcolexpandmul`/`pto.tcolexpandadd`, those consumers materialize the subview operand via `pto.textract` into the slice's (inherited) result buffer, which can still alias the source for a dynamic-offset slice of a local tile. That path predates this change (#1217) and is unchanged here; it is tracked separately in #1640. No current model exercises it (real `col_expand` call sites slice GM tensor params → `tile.load`, not `tile.slice`).

The 3-arg path is unchanged in shape (still a single `pto.subview`); the lambda/early-return structure is collapsed and the now-unused `tmov`/`set_validshape` emission code is gone. `SubviewMaterializationInfo` is registered for all slices (3-arg and 4-arg) so `pto.tcolexpandmul`'s eager-materialization fallback continues to work (its pre-existing aliasing hazard is tracked in #1640).

A follow-up commit also fixes a per-dim `valid_shape` typing bug surfaced by the pypto-lib qwen3-14b `lm_head_store` kernel: for `valid_shape=[dynamic, static]`, the explicit-valid branch must reflect each dim's static/dynamic-ness independently (not promote both to dynamic), otherwise PTOAS rejects the static `valid_col` operand against a `v_col=?` result type.

## Changes

- `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp` — collapse `tile.slice` codegen to a single `pto.subview` branch; explicit `valid_shape` overrides `InferSubviewTileTypeComponents`'s `v_row`/`v_col` per-dim (no promote-both-to-dynamic) and feeds the subview's `valid [...]` clause.
- `tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen.py` — invert two tests that previously mandated `tmov + set_validshape` (one renamed from `..._uses_set_validshape` to `..._uses_subview_valid`).
- `tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen_ops.py` — invert `test_tile_slice_codegen_with_valid_shape` to expect the subview-`valid` form; add `test_tile_slice_mixed_dynamic_static_valid_shape_per_dim_type` (the `lm_head_store` per-dim regression).
- `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_gather.py` — add `test_gather_tile_input_source_unchanged`: builds a local tile via `pl.create_tensor` + `pl.assemble`, runs `pl.tensor.gather`, then echoes the local tile back out and asserts it is bit-identical to the input.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/ut/codegen/` — 385 tests pass.
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` — 1534 tests pass.
- [x] `tests/ut/{ir/operators,ir/printing,ir/parser,ir/statements,ir/expressions,ir/core,core,pass,language}/` — 2248 tests pass.
- [x] `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_gather.py::TestGatherIndex` on `a2a3sim` — 7/7 pass, including the new `test_gather_tile_input_source_unchanged` #1622 regression.
- [x] `examples.kernels.dyn_valid_shape` compiles for both partial-block (`vlen < BLOCK_COL`, dynamic valid) and full-block (`vlen == BLOCK_COL`) variants — i.e. the dynamic-`valid_shape` codegen path still works end-to-end.
- [x] Original #1622 reproducer (from issue body) on `a2a3sim`: `before: PASS / gathered: PASS / after: PASS`.
- [x] Negative-control: temporarily reverting the codegen change makes the new st regression fail with exactly 64/1024 mismatching elements (row 0 of the `[16, 64]` source) — matching the corruption pattern described in #1622.
- [x] pypto-lib qwen3-14b `decode_layer.py` (`lm_head_store`) compiles end-to-end (compile-only) with the rebuilt pypto + ptoas 0.43 — previously failed PTOAS with `'pto.subview' op expects result valid_shape[1] to match inferred/explicit valid_col`. Verified the old/new subview forms directly against ptoas with hand-written `.pto`.

Fixes #1622

Follow-up: #1640 (pre-existing lazy `pto.textract` materialization aliasing hazard, out of scope here).

title: [Feature] Host-orchestrator JIT signature to author distributed programs without @pl.program
body:
### Summary

Add a JIT decorator/signature variant for **HOST-level orchestration** so distributed programs can be authored entirely with `@pl.jit` functions instead of a `@pl.program` class. Today the host orchestrator — the function that allocates HCCL windows (`pld.alloc_window_buffer` / `pld.window`), loops `for r in pl.range(pld.world_size())`, and dispatches each rank via `chip_orch(..., device=r)` — can only be a `@pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)` method inside a `@pl.program` class. There is no jit equivalent.

### Motivation / Use Case

We're aligning the 2-rank EP MoE (`models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py`) with the clean single-card jit composition style (`moe.py`: `@pl.jit.inline` kernels composed by a top-level `@pl.jit`). With #1635 (DistributedTensor params in jit), the **chip-level orchestration** (`chip_orch`) can be expressed as a jit function. But the **host layer** still forces `@pl.program`, so the program can't fully drop the class form. A host-orchestrator jit variant would let the entire distributed program — host loop + chip orchestration + InCore kernels — be authored as jit functions, giving one consistent authoring style for single-card and EP.

### Proposed API / Behavior

A distinct decorator (not the default `@pl.jit` / `@pl.jit.inline`) that carries HOST + Orchestrator semantics and permits window allocation + the `world_size` rank loop + per-rank `device=` dispatch, e.g.:

```python
@pl.jit.host          # or @pl.jit(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
def host_orch(... per-rank inputs/outputs ..., layer_id):
    pub_counts_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(N_RANKS * N_RANKS * N_LOCAL * 4)
    ...
    for r in pl.range(pld.world_size()):
        pub_counts = pld.window(pub_counts_buf, [...], dtype=pl.INT32)
        ...
        chip_orch(..., pub_counts, ..., layer_id, r, device=r)   # chip_orch is a @pl.jit orchestration fn
```

Key requirements the new signature must support that default jit does not: (1) `pld.alloc_window_buffer` / `pld.window`; (2) `pld.world_size()` and the per-rank loop; (3) the `device=` dispatch kwarg targeting a jit chip-orchestration function.

### Alternatives Considered

Keep `host_orch` (and the enclosing `@pl.program` class) as the only non-jit shell while everything below it is jit — i.e. a thin `@pl.program` that just hosts `host_orch` + bare-calls jit `chip_orch`. This is the current fallback and works, but it means the program can never be fully `@pl.program`-free, so two authoring paradigms persist.

### Additional Context

- Depends on / pairs with **#1635** (DistributedTensor params in jit) — that unblocks `chip_orch`; this unblocks `host_orch`.
- Builds on **#1127** (L3 Distributed Programming Interface RFC).
- Current reference shape: `host_orch` in `models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py` (`@pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)`).
- pypto commit: `e851ba54` (main).

title: feat(jit): recognize pld.DistributedTensor params in @pl.jit / @pl.jit.inline
body:
## Summary

Teach the JIT annotation classifier to accept `pld.DistributedTensor[[shape], dtype]` annotations alongside `pl.Tensor`, so cross-rank dispatch/combine kernels can be authored as `@pl.jit.inline` helpers in the same style as single-card kernels. The specializer now round-trips the annotation as `pld.DistributedTensor[...]` in the generated `@pl.program` source and adds `import pypto.language.distributed as pld` to the preamble when needed.

Before this change, the classifier (`_is_tensor_annotation`) only matched `Tensor`, so `pld.DistributedTensor[...]` annotations were silently dropped — the parameter fell through and the generated source emitted it without a type annotation. The `@pl.function` parser path already supports `DistributedTensor` for `InCore` methods; this change brings the JIT specializer to parity.

## Changes

- `python/pypto/jit/specializer.py`
  - `_is_tensor_annotation` now matches both `Tensor` and `DistributedTensor` (bare or subscripted).
  - New `_is_distributed_tensor_annotation` helper distinguishes the two kinds.
  - `_classify_params` returns a 4-tuple, adding `distributed_params: set[str]`.
  - `_build_tensor_annotation` accepts `is_distributed: bool` and emits `pld.DistributedTensor[[shape], dtype]` when True.
  - `Specializer._build_params` threads `distributed_params` through and flips a `_needs_pld_import` flag.
  - `Specializer.specialize()` conditionally emits `import pypto.language.distributed as pld` in the generated module preamble.

body:
## Summary

Pure docs + example PR. Surface the runtime APIs that landed in PR #1496 (CompiledProgram extraction), PR #1599 (Worker ABC + ChipWorker / DistributedWorker + run/register/RegistrationHandle), and PR #1620 (JITFunction.compile()) so external users have a single place to learn the new patterns.

### Example: `examples/runtime/explicit_dispatch.py`

Two @pl.jit kernels + one shared ChipWorker, exercising three end-to-end patterns:

- **mode_a_inference_service** — pre-register N compiled kernels, dispatch by name (the serving-runtime pattern from issue #1455).
- **mode_b_training_loop** — persistent weight DeviceTensor via `alloc_tensor(init=host_weight)` plus a hot register/run loop with per-step inputs.
- **mode_c_register_dispatch_overhead** — assert `aicpu_dlopen_count` stays at +1 across 20 dispatches after a single `register()`.

All three modes share a single `ChipWorker` (one init / one close) and use `JITFunction.compile()` for stage-1 compile + `worker.register()` for stage-2 dispatch.

title: [Bug] tile.slice → col_expand lazy pto.textract materialization can overwrite source tile (dynamic offset)
body:
### Component

Codegen / `tile.slice` lazy subview materialization (`pto.textract`) for `pto.tcolexpandmul` / `pto.tcolexpandadd` consumers

### Summary

When a `tile.slice` view of a **local tile** is consumed by `pl.col_expand_mul` / `pl.col_expand_add`, codegen lazily materializes the subview via `pto.textract ins(source, off) outs(result_target)`. For a **dynamic-offset** slice, `result_target` is the slice's own result buffer, which — because `tile.slice` is `set_output_memory_inherit_input` — falls back to the **source allocation base** (`AllocateMemoryAddr` cannot encode a dynamic offset as a `ConstInt` address, so it uses the bare base). The `pto.textract` therefore writes the extracted row back into **row 0 of the source tile**, corrupting it. This is the same corruption class as #1622, but reached through the lazy `pto.textract` path instead of the eager `pto.tmov` path.

This is **pre-existing**: the `materialize_target_ssa = result_target` registration and the `pto.textract` materialization were introduced in #1217 ("Rewrite tile.slice lowering"). It is independent of #1636 (which removes the *eager* materialization path; the lazy path is unchanged by that PR).

### Why it is not hit today

No model currently chains "**dynamic-offset slice of a local tile** → `col_expand_mul/add` → re-read of the source tile". Real RoPE / MoE call sites slice **GM tensor parameters**, which lower to `tile.load` (a fresh Vec-memory load), not `tile.slice` (subview) — so they never enter the lazy `pto.textract` path. The hazard is latent but one kernel away.

### Minimal trigger (constructed)

```python
import pypto.language as pl

ROWS, COLS = 16, 256

@pl.program
class Trigger:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def kernel(
        self,
        scores: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
        gamma: pl.Tensor[[1, COLS], pl.FP32],
        out_scaled: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
        out_echo: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
    ) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]:
        local: pl.Tile[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32] = pl.load(scores, [0, 0], [ROWS, COLS])   # local tile
        gamma_t: pl.Tile[[1, COLS], pl.FP32] = pl.load(gamma, [0, 0], [1, COLS])
        acc: pl.Tile[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32] = pl.tile.create(
            [ROWS, COLS], dtype=pl.FP32, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec
        )
        for r in pl.range(ROWS):
            row: pl.Tile[[1, COLS], pl.FP32] = pl.tile.slice(local, [1, COLS], [r, 0])   # dynamic-offset slice
            scaled: pl.Tile[[1, COLS], pl.FP32] = pl.col_expand_mul(row, gamma_t)         # lazy textract
            acc = pl.tile.assemble(acc, scaled, [r, 0])
        out_scaled = pl.store(acc, [0, 0], out_scaled)
        out_echo = pl.store(local, [0, 0], out_echo)   # re-read local: exposes corruption
        return out_echo
```

### Generated PTO (the bug)

```mlir
%local__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0_i64 ...                 // local @ addr 0
scf.for %r__idx_v0 = 0 to 16 {
  %row__ssa_v0   = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0_i64 ...               // slice result @ addr 0 == local base (inherited + dynamic offset)
  %slice_view    = pto.subview %local__ssa_v0[%r__idx_v0, 0] sizes [1,256] -> ...
  pto.textract ins(%local__ssa_v0, %r__idx_v0, 0) outs(%row__ssa_v0)   // writes local[r,:] into addr 0 = local row 0
  pto.tcolexpandmul ins(%row__ssa_v0, %gamma_t) outs(%scaled__ssa_v0)
  ...
}
pto.tstore ins(%local__ssa_v0) outs(out_echo)                      // re-reads local; row 0 now = row 15
```

`%row__ssa_v0` shares `addr = %c0_i64` with `%local__ssa_v0`, so each iteration's `pto.textract` overwrites the source's row 0. After the loop, `out_echo` row 0 reads row 15's data.

### Expected Behavior

`col_expand_mul/add` consuming a `tile.slice` must not mutate the slice's source tile. The lazy `pto.textract` materialization must write into a buffer that does **not** inherit / alias the source allocation.

### Proposed fix direction

Materialize the subview operand into a **fresh non-inherited scratch tile** rather than the slice's `result_target` (which inherits source memory). Options:
- give the materialization a dedicated scratch buffer (codegen needs a non-aliased address source, currently absent post-`AllocateMemoryAddr`), or
- at the IR level, ensure a `tile.slice` feeding a materializing consumer (`col_expand_mul/add`) does not inherit source memory for its result buffer.

### Location

- `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp` — `MaterializeSubviewOperandIfNeeded` (`outs(mat->materialize_target_ssa)`), and the `tile.slice` codegen registering `mat_info.materialize_target_ssa = result_target`.
- Origin: #1217.

### Severity

Medium (latent — no live trigger today; silent data corruption if a kernel writes the trigger pattern).

title: fix(memory_reuse): align loop-carried MemRefs to reused init (#1352)
body:
## Summary

Root-cause fix for the invalid `acc→acc pto.tmov` that ptoas rejects on Ascend 910B (`'pto.tmov' op expects a supported tmov address-space pair for this target`) when MemoryReuse reuses an Acc buffer across nested pipelined `matmul_acc` accumulators.

**Why it happened:** MemRef sharing only retypes `AssignStmt`-defined producer/init vars; the loop-carried `iter_arg`/`return_var` nodes are excluded from the lifetime and sharing maps and keep their original buffer. For nested pipelined `matmul_acc` (e.g. the Qwen3-32B `gate_up_silu` shape, where `up` reuses `gate`'s freed Acc buffer), this splits the accumulator chain across two Acc buffers. `YieldFixupMutator` (bottom-up) then bridges them with `acc→acc tile.move` ops that have no hardware path on 910B.

**The fix:** add `AlignLoopCarriesToInitMutator` as MemoryReuse **Step 3.5** — it walks `ForStmt`s **top-down** and re-types each loop's `iter_arg`/`return_var` to its now-reused `initValue` MemRef, seeding `var_remap_` before recursing so a nested loop observes the corrected outer `iter_arg` as its init. Once producers and carries agree on one buffer, `YieldFixupMutator` inserts no spurious move. It only ever aligns a carry to its own init (a no-op when reuse already left them consistent), so a loop that legitimately yields a different buffer than its init still gets its move from `YieldFixupMutator`.

This is a proper IR-layer fix, in line with the project's first-principles rule (fix the pass, not via a codegen workaround). The net change to `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp` is zero — codegen `tile.move` elision stays at the original #1310 behavior (same-space, same-address only).

## Changes

- `src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp` — new `AlignLoopCarriesToInitMutator` (Step 3.5), O(N log N), single top-down traversal.
- `tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen_ops.py` — codegen regression reworked to the realistic dual-accumulator gate_up shape that triggers reuse; asserts no `acc→acc pto.tmov` in generated MLIR.
- `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_matmul.py` — runtime regression + docstrings describing the reuse-based behavior.
- `docs/en/dev/passes/29-memory_reuse.md`, `docs/zh-cn/dev/passes/29-memory_reuse.md` — document the new step (en + zh-cn synced).

## Testing

- [x] `tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen_ops.py::TestTileMoveAccNoopElision` — 2 passed (fails without the fix)
- [x] C++ builds cleanly; clang-tidy introduces no new findings
- [x] Runtime ST (`tests/st/runtime/ops/test_matmul.py`) require Ascend hardware / device runtime — not runnable in this environment
- [x] Code review completed
- [x] Documentation updated (en + zh-cn)

## Related Issues

Fixes #1352

title: [Bug] PTO codegen elides tile view ops to disconnected same-address alloc_tile, dropping PTOAS PIPE_S→PIPE_V handshake (scatter race)
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

PyPTO's PTO kernel emission lowers metadata-only tile **view** ops (`tile.reshape`, `tile.as_layout`, col-major reinterpret) into **separate `pto.alloc_tile` ops that share the same UB address but carry no dataflow edge** back to the producer, instead of threading the producer SSA through a `pto.treshape` view. This severs the SSA def-use chain that PTOAS's dependency analyzer relies on, so a required cross-pipe **`set_flag/wait_flag(PIPE_S, PIPE_V)`** handshake is never emitted. The result is a non-deterministic data race in the generated AICore kernel.

This is the PyPTO-side root cause of the a2a3 column-scatter corruption tracked downstream in simpler issue `hw-native-sys/simpler#967` (investigated in `simpler#969`). simpler PR #878 only shifted binary layout/timing enough to surface a latent race; the missing handshake is emitted (or rather, *not* emitted) here.

**Mechanism, confirmed end-to-end:**

1. The scatter row-offset iota chain is lowered correctly at the IR level — `tile.ci → tile.reshape → tile.muls → tile.row_expand_add`, all threaded through SSA Vars (`src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp:1581-1587`).

2. At PTO emission, `tile.reshape` is **elided to nothing** whenever the per-var alloc model already pre-declared the result var's `alloc_tile` — `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp:3629-3632`:
   ```cpp
   auto existing_type = codegen.GetSSATileBufType(result_target);
   if (!existing_type.empty() && existing_type == result_type) {
     return std::string("");   // emits no pto.treshape, drops ins(src)
   }
   ```
   `existing_type` and `result_type` both derive from the **result** var's TileType, so they are ~always equal → the `pto.treshape` fallback is effectively dead, and the reshape result becomes a bare same-address `alloc_tile`.

3. The emitted `.pto` therefore has the producer (`pto.tci outs(%scatter_ci_rows)`) and the consumer (`pto.tmuls ins(%scatter_row_base__rm_a0_tmp_v0)`) reading **two distinct `pto.alloc_tile` ops both at `addr = 5152`**, with no view op linking them.

4. PTOAS's `MemoryDependentAnalyzer::MemAlias` for local/UB memory keys on **SSA root-buffer identity** (`GetRealRoot` peels `ViewLikeOpInterface`/cast ops but stops at `alloc_tile`). Two distinct allocs at the same address resolve to different roots → `realRootA != realRootB` → **no dependency** → no sync. The address-range-overlap check exists but is gated behind root identity and is never reached here.

Net effect: TCI (PIPE_S) and TMULS (PIPE_V) touch the same UB bytes with no handshake; TMULS can read stale high lanes of the iota, zeroing the per-row offset for rows 14/15 and collapsing them onto row 0.

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
# Build, then run the column-scatter ST on a2a3 silicon and save kernels:
pytest tests/st/runtime/ops/test_scatter.py::TestScatterIndexForm::test_scatter_fp16[a2a3] \
  --save-kernels --kernels-dir /tmp/scatter_repro
```

1. Inspect the saved `ptoas/main_incore_0.pto`: the row-offset iota chain emits multiple `pto.alloc_tile addr = %c5152_i64` for `scatter_ci_rows` / `scatter_row_arange` / `scatter_row_base__rm_a0_tmp_v0` / `scatter_row_base`, with **no `pto.treshape`** linking them.
2. Inspect the PTOAS-emitted `ptoas/main_incore_0.cpp`: between `TCI(...)` (PIPE_S) and `TMULS(...)` (PIPE_V) over the shared buffer there is only a no-op `pipe_barrier(PIPE_V)` — no `set_flag/wait_flag(PIPE_S, PIPE_V)` pair.
3. On a2a3 the test corrupts intermittently (`val[14,*]`/`val[15,*]` land at row 0); manually inserting `set_flag(PIPE_S,PIPE_V)/wait_flag` after the `TCI` makes it pass deterministically (verified in simpler#969).

### Expected Behavior

The view chain should preserve the SSA dataflow edge so PTOAS sees the cross-pipe RAW and emits the `set_flag/wait_flag(PIPE_S, PIPE_V)` handshake. Concretely, `tile.reshape` / `tile.as_layout` should emit a `pto.treshape %src` (`ViewLikeOpInterface`, `getViewSource()=src`) that PTOAS's `GetRealRoot` can peel back to the producer's `alloc_tile`, restoring root identity — rather than a disconnected same-address `alloc_tile`.

### Actual Behavior

`tile.reshape` (and the col-major reinterpret) are elided to bare same-address `pto.alloc_tile` ops with no `ins(src)`. PTOAS finds distinct SSA roots, infers no dependency, and omits the handshake. The generated kernel races, corrupting the high rows of the scatter output non-deterministically.

### Git Commit ID

a09f425138b10e29c314a1b71df4468260401ee1

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

**Suggested fix (PyPTO side, primary):** stop eliding view ops to disconnected allocs — always emit `pto.treshape %src` for `tile.reshape` (guard/remove the early-return at `pto_ops_common.cpp:3629-3632`, route through the existing treshape fallback) and add view-result vars to the alloc skip set (`src/codegen/pto/pto_codegen.cpp:1324-1326`, mirroring tpop/scatter-alias) to avoid orphan allocs. The whole chain must be threaded: the `.pto` has ~4 view break points (reshape, the row-major reinterpret before `tmuls`, the col-major reinterpret `scatter_row_base` before `row_expand_add`), each from a metadata view that is currently elided — all must emit `treshape`/view ops or any remaining break re-severs the root.

**Alternative (PTOAS side, defense-in-depth):** make `MemAlias` for local memory fall back to address-range overlap when SSA roots differ but both accesses have concrete overlapping `baseAddresses`. Needs careful evaluation against intentional address reuse (disjoint-lifetime allocs sharing an address).

Related: #1475 (MemoryReuse same-address cross-pipe WAR hazards), #1640 (tile view materialization writing to the wrong address). Downstream: simpler#967, simpler#969.

title: fix(ir): sync loop-carry MemRef on PTO buffer reuse split
body:
## Summary

`LegalizePTOBufferReuse` rewrites a tile's `MemRef` by SSA-value identity (the `splits_` map is keyed on `AssignStmt` writers). A loop-carry's `IterArg` and its `return_var` are separate SSA values that are never `splits_` keys, so when a writer used as a loop `init_values` carry is split, the carry's **declared storage was left behind on the abandoned `MemRef`** while only the init value followed the split.

This is a latent type/storage inconsistency in the loop carry. It does not crash today (the abandoned slot survives, owned by the writer that kept it), but the carry then declares a different slot than where its data actually lives — which can mislead downstream address assignment.

The bug has two coupled halves — both fixed here, since fixing only one leaves an equivalent skew on the other:

- **`IterArg`** — `MemRefSplitMutator::VisitExpr_(IterArgPtr)` now syncs the `IterArg`'s declared `TileType` to its **remapped init value**'s `MemRef`, instead of only updating when the `IterArg` itself is a `splits_` key (which a loop carry never is).
- **`return_var`** — new `LoopCarryReturnVarCollector` pre-pass registers each loop `return_var` whose init writer was split into the `splits` set, so `VisitExpr_(VarPtr)` rewrites it uniformly — both in the `return_vars` list and at later use sites.

After the fix the whole carry chain (`init`, `iter_arg`, `yield` writer, `return_var`) coherently lands on the fresh `MemRef`.

## Changes

- `src/ir/transforms/legalize_pto_buffer_reuse_pass.cpp` — the fix (IterArg init-following + `LoopCarryReturnVarCollector`); inline phase banners renumbered to the five-phase model.
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_legalize_pto_buffer_reuse.py` — new before/after test `test_split_follows_loop_carry` (guards **both** halves: fails if either `iter_arg` or `return_var` is left behind).
- `docs/en|zh-cn/dev/passes/30-legalize_pto_buffer_reuse.md` — five-phase algorithm, new component, "Loop carry follows the split" example, updated helper/test tables.

## Complexity

`LoopCarryReturnVarCollector` is a single O(N) IR traversal with O(log N) map ops per carry — O(N log N) overall, per `pass-complexity.md`.

## Testing

- `test_legalize_pto_buffer_reuse.py`: 15 passed (incl. new test)
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/`: 1395 passed, 26 skipped (no regressions)
- `tests/ut/codegen` + `tests/ut/pass`: 393 passed (incl. `test_for_loop_with_inplace_return_after_passes`, full-pipeline in-place return)
- clang-tidy on diff: clean

title: feat(ir): pl.paged_gather — paged gather directly into L1/UB (#1629)
body:
## Summary

Adds `pl.paged_gather`, a paged KV gather that lands directly into an on-chip buffer (L1 / `MemorySpace.Mat`, or UB / `MemorySpace.Vec`) — the framework support requested in #1629 to eliminate the GM round-trip of the sparse-attention `gather_kv → qk_pv` pipeline.

```python
out = pl.paged_gather(src, indices, block_table, block_size, size, max_indices,
                      space=pl.MemorySpace.Mat, col_off=0, is_trans=False)
```

The whole gather runs **fully scalar on the Cube core (AIC)**: per gathered row it scalar-reads the logical index + page table from GM (`pto.load_scalar`), resolves the physical row in scalar registers (`phys = block_table[idx/bs]*bs + idx%bs`), and DMAs that row `GM → on-chip` (`pto.tload`). Only the small index/page-table metadata touches scalar GM reads; the bulk KV data never goes through UB.

## How it works

- **`tensor.paged_gather`** (new op) lowers in `ConvertTensorToTileOps` to a `ForStmt` of the scalar index translation + a per-row **`tile.gather_row`** (new DPS op): `pto.subview` (of the accumulator) + `pto.partition_view` (GM) + `pto.tload` straight into the sub-region — **no `pto.tmov`** (an L1→L1 `tmov` is unsupported on a2a3; L1 can only be filled via GM→L1 `tload`, mirroring CANN's `TGatherInL1`).
- **Boxed (NZ) sub-region alignment.** The L1 accumulator carries the matmul-operand NZ fractal layout, so `pto.subview` sizes must be whole multiples of the inner box. `tile.gather_row` codegen emits a box-aligned physical size (rows → `M0 = 16`, cols → `C0 = fractal_bytes / dtype_bytes / 16`) while marking only the real extent valid (`[1, size]`); the `tload` fills just that row. ND (Vec, `slayout = none_box`) tiles have no inner box and keep the exact `[1, size]` size.
- `max_indices` sizes the on-chip buffer statically; the runtime indices count drives the loop bound (dynamic gather counts supported).
- No new codegen for control flow / scalar math — those reuse the existing `ForStmt`/`load_scalar` paths.

## Conversion-pass fix

Consuming the gathered L1 tile with `pl.matmul` exposed a latent dangling-pointer bug in `ConvertTensorToTileOps`: `var_remap_` is keyed by raw `Expr*`, and a freed converter-temp Var's address could be reused, so the matmul result mis-resolved to a stale scalar (`tensor.assemble ... got ScalarType`, allocation-order dependent). Fixed by retaining mapped-from Vars for the pass lifetime (`TypePropagatingMutator::RetainVar`).

## Status

- ✅ **`space=Vec` (gather to UB): passes on-device (a2a3).**
- ✅ **`space=Mat` (gather to L1): passes on-device (a2a3).** The gather lands a box-aligned per-row `tload` into the NZ L1 accumulator, then the tile is consumed the way an L1 operand is meant to be — by `pl.matmul` — and validated numerically (`eye @ gathered == gathered`) against a torch golden. (Pushing the raw NZ L1 tile cross-core to GM is unsupported by ptoas, so the Mat path is verified through its natural matmul consumer rather than a direct GM store.)

## Tests

- Unit: `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_paged_gather.py` (lowering structure, transpose, Vec, dynamic rows, full-pipeline, type-deducer errors).
- On-device: `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_paged_gather.py` — `test_paged_gather_vec[a2a3]` and `test_paged_gather_mat[a2a3]` both pass on a2a3.
- Full IR unit suite green (1661 transform tests); matmul ST regression-checked on a2a3.

## Docs

`docs/{en,zh-cn}/dev/passes/12-convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.md` — Paged Gather Lowering section (tile.gather_row + NZ box alignment).

Fixes #1629

title: feat(jit): add @pl.jit.host for HOST-level orchestration
body:
## Summary

Adds `@pl.jit.host`, a JIT decorator variant for HOST-level orchestrators, so distributed programs can be authored entirely with `@pl.jit` functions instead of falling back to a `@pl.program` class. Pairs with #1638 (DistributedTensor params in jit), which unblocked chip-level jit orchestration — this is the host-side counterpart.

- New `@pl.jit.host` sub-decorator (and `@pl.jit.host()` parens form), reusing the existing `_SubFunctionDecorator` machinery; `level=` is rejected (HOST is implicit).
- Specializer's `_build_decorator` emits `@pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)` for `func_type == "host"` — the canonical spelling already accepted by the parser and used by `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_allreduce.py`.
- `_discover_deps` is gated by the caller's `_func_type`: a host entry additionally admits `orchestration` deps (its chip orchestrators), while plain `@pl.jit` entries still ignore other `@pl.jit` entries so two top-level kernels never silently fold into one program.
- The caller's `_func_type` is threaded through `_scan_dep_io` → `_extract_local_tensor_metas` → `_resolve_dep_call_metadata` → `_build_contexts` (via a new `func_type_by_id` map) so meta propagation through `v = chip_orch(args)` honours the same gating.

```python
@pl.jit
def chip_orch(a: pl.Tensor, c: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    return c

@pl.jit.host
def host_orch(inp: pl.Tensor, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    for r in pl.range(pld.world_size()):
        chip_orch(inp, out, device=r)
    return out
```

## Scope

Decorator + specializer + dep discovery. Runtime distributed dispatch (plumbing `distributed_config` through `JITFunction._compile` so a host-orchestrator jit kernel can be executed end-to-end) is **out of scope** here and tracked as follow-up. The parser, IR pipeline, and `ir.compile()` already accept the generated source; the JIT runtime side just needs a way for the user to specify `distributed_config` (likely through `RunConfig`).

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/ut/jit/test_decorator.py` — `TestJitHostDecoration` (5 cases: bare/parens form, `level=` rejection, name preservation, `pl.jit.host` access) and `TestHostDiscoversOrchestrationDep` (3 cases: host pulls orchestration dep, plain `@pl.jit` does not, host still discovers incore deps).
- [x] `tests/ut/jit/test_specializer.py` — `test_jit_host_emits_host_orchestrator_decorator`, `test_jit_host_with_orchestration_dep` (decorator emission + multi-function rewrite with `device=r` preserved).
- [x] Full `tests/ut/jit/` suite — 210 passed.

title: feat(distributed+st): generalize L3 allreduce ST to N-rank mesh and provide two codegen fixes for distributed
body:
## Summary

This PR adds **N-rank mesh allreduce** system-test coverage (P=2 and P=4) to the distributed ST suite, and ships **two independent codegen fixes** discovered during NPU bring-up.

### ST feature (3 files)

Generalizes `test_l3_allreduce.py` from a P=2-only neighbor shortcut to the **N-rank mesh** pattern matching simpler's `allreduce_kernel.cpp`:

- **Phase 1:** `pl.store` local input into window-bound `data`
- **Phase 2:** all-peer notify/wait barrier on `signal[[nranks, 1]]`
- **Phase 3:** `pl.load` self + loop `peer ≠ my_rank: remote_load + add`
- **Phase 4:** `pl.store` accumulator → output

`_build_allreduce_program(n_ranks)` enables separate compilation per world size. Tests are parametrized over `n_ranks ∈ {2, 4}` with automatic skip when devices are scarce. Golden: `outputs[r] == sum(inputs[*])` for every rank `r`.

### Codegen fix 1: INT32 rank/nranks (6 files)

`pld.rank()` and `pld.nranks()` previously returned `ScalarType(UINT32)`. `GetTypeString(UINT32)` emitted `"ui32"` in the generated MLIR, which PTOAS rejects in `arith.trunci` and `arith.index_cast`. The fix changes the IR type to `INT32`, which maps directly to MLIR `i32` without conversion. The runtime already uses `int32_t` for `rankId`/`rankNum`, so this is both simpler and semantically correct.

### Codegen fix 2: host orchestrator temp unwrap (3 files)

When early passes (SSA, `FlattenCallExpr`) hoist `pld.world_size()` into a temp (`n = pld.world_size()`), and that temp is subsequently used in `alloc_window_buffer(n * 4)`, the generated `host_orch.py` must emit the `alloc_window_buffer` sizing inside `EmitCommDomainAllocations`. However `EmitCommDomainAllocations` runs *before* the function-body walk that assigns `n`, causing an `UnboundLocalError` at runtime.

The fix mirrors `UnwrapStopExpr` in `CollectCommGroups`: a pre-pass (`CollectHostOrchVarDefs`) scans the function body for `AssignStmt` definitions, then `GetCommSlotSizeAsCode` unwraps hoisted temps back to the original expression (e.g. `n * 4` → `world_size() * 4`) during comm-domain emission.

## File map

### Contribution A — ST feature (3 files)

| `docs/zh-cn/dev/distributed_ops.md` | ±6 — same in Chinese |

| `python/pypto/ir/op/distributed/system_ops.py` | ±2 — docstrings |

| `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp` | ±4 — comments |

| `tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_distributed_pto_codegen.py` | +42 — tightened MLIR assertions + `test_rank_var_reuse_no_ui32_in_notify_and_compare` |

### Contribution C — Host orch temp unwrap (3 files)

**No other files changed.** `pto_type_utils.{h,cpp}`, `pto_codegen.cpp`, and `pto_scalar_expr_codegen.cpp` are identical to `origin/main`.

title: [RFC] Unify pl.spmd with pl.parallel + pl.at to avoid re-indentation when switching dispatch
body:
### Summary

`pl.parallel` + `pl.at` and `pl.spmd` express the same intent — dispatch independent work blocks across cores, each block running an InCore region — but with different *nesting depth*. `pl.parallel` + `pl.at` is two indentation levels (the `with pl.at` wraps the body); `pl.spmd` is one (the body is implicitly InCore and an explicit `pl.at` is currently disallowed). Because of this, every time we convert a `pl.parallel`+`pl.at` block to `pl.spmd` (or back), we must re-indent the entire loop body. This proposes letting the two forms share the same structure so switching the dispatch model is a one-line change to the `for`/`with` header, not a whole-body re-indent.

### Motivation

Switching a region between `pl.parallel`+`pl.at` and `pl.spmd` is a routine operation during kernel development (e.g. when a per-core parallel region needs SPMD dispatch for block-index addressing, or when profiling pushes us one way or the other). Today the two forms differ in nesting depth:

**Before — `pl.parallel` + `pl.at` (two levels):**
```python
for b0 in pl.parallel(0, batch_padded, BATCH_TILE):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="rmsnorm"):
        x = pl.slice(inp, [b0, 0], [BATCH_TILE, HIDDEN])
        y = pl.rmsnorm(x, gamma)
        pl.assemble(out, y, [b0, 0])
```

**After — `pl.spmd` (one level; whole body re-indented):**
```python
for b0 in pl.spmd(BATCH_BLOCKS, name_hint="rmsnorm"):
    x = pl.slice(inp, [b0, 0], [BATCH_TILE, HIDDEN])
    y = pl.rmsnorm(x, gamma)
    pl.assemble(out, y, [b0, 0])
```

The compute body is byte-for-byte identical, yet the diff touches every line because the `with pl.at` wrapper disappeared. This produces noisy diffs, error-prone manual re-indentation, and merge friction — for a change that is semantically just "use SPMD dispatch for this region."

### Design

Two candidate designs, presented as open options for discussion. Both reduce a dispatch switch to a header-only diff; neither moves the compute body or its indentation.

**Option A: allow an explicit `pl.at` inside a `pl.spmd` body.**

Today the rule is "No surrounding `pl.at` is needed or allowed" inside `pl.spmd`. Relax it so a single `with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, ...)` directly inside the `pl.spmd` loop body is *permitted* and simply marks the InCore region that `pl.spmd` already creates implicitly (the `pl.at` becomes the explicit handle for that region rather than a second, nested one). The structure then matches `pl.parallel`+`pl.at` exactly:

```python
# parallel form
for b0 in pl.parallel(0, batch_padded, BATCH_TILE):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="rmsnorm"):
        body            # unchanged

# spmd form — identical body & indentation, only the `for` header changed
for b0 in pl.spmd(BATCH_BLOCKS, name_hint="rmsnorm"):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="rmsnorm"):
        body            # unchanged
```

Converting between the two becomes a one-line edit of the `for` header; the body and its indentation never move. The bare (no-`pl.at`) `pl.spmd` form stays valid for brevity. This adds the least new surface — it only relaxes an existing restriction and reuses `pl.at`'s existing `name_hint`/`level` arguments — and keeps `pl.spmd` as the construct that owns SPMD semantics (block-index binding, `sync_start`, outlining).

**Option B: a `dispatch=` kwarg on `pl.at`.**

Keep `pl.parallel` as the outer loop and select the InCore dispatch model on the `pl.at`:

```python
for b0 in pl.parallel(0, batch_padded, BATCH_TILE):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, dispatch=pl.Dispatch.SPMD, name_hint="rmsnorm"):
        body
```

`dispatch=pl.Dispatch.PARALLEL` (default) lowers as today; `dispatch=pl.Dispatch.SPMD` lowers the region to an SPMD-outlined function with the loop variable bound to the block index. Switching is a single kwarg; the two-level structure is preserved for both modes. This keeps a single outer-loop spelling but overloads `pl.parallel`'s loop-variable semantics depending on the `dispatch` mode.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Status quo + editor auto-indent.** Doesn't address noisy diffs or the conceptual asymmetry, and still requires manual fix-ups when the body has nested blocks.
- **A separate sugar macro** that expands to either form. Adds a third spelling for the same concept; worsens rather than reduces cognitive load. The existing `pl.parallel(..., chunk=N)` sugar shows the project already favors collapsing these patterns, but it goes the opposite direction (hides `pl.at`); this RFC instead makes the explicit forms structurally interchangeable.

### Open Questions

- Under Option A, when both `pl.spmd(name_hint=...)` and the inner `pl.at(name_hint=...)` carry a `name_hint`, which wins for the outlined-function label? (One possibility: `pl.at`'s if present, else `pl.spmd`'s.)
- Should an explicit `pl.at` inside `pl.spmd` be allowed only as the *sole* top-level statement of the body (mirroring the context-manager form), or anywhere?
- For Option B, does binding the `pl.parallel` loop variable to a block index under `dispatch=SPMD` conflict with `pl.parallel`'s documented "iterations may be split/reordered" contract?

title: [Bug] vec-produced GM tensor used as matmul RIGHT operand in a later scope is not dependency-ordered (intermittent reads of zero-init data)
body:
### Component

Codegen — IR dependency tracking / task scheduler (missing producer → matmul-RHS edge)

### Description

A GM tensor produced by a **vector** scope and then consumed as the **right operand (B / weight matrix)** of a `pl.matmul` in a **later scope** is not reliably dependency-ordered. The matmul intermittently executes before the producing scope's store completes, reading the still **zero-initialized** tensor, which yields non-deterministic wrong results.

Passing the *same* tensor as a kernel input (i.e. no in-kernel producer) always passes. This isolates the missing dependency edge to the **vec-producer → matmul-RHS** path. It reproduces with a single-task `CORE_GROUP` matmul consumer (not SPMD), so it is not about many concurrent readers. Likely shares a root cause with #1503 (dependency-edge gap) but is more general: any vec-produced tensor used as a matmul right operand.

### Steps to Reproduce

Self-contained kernel, run on `-p a2a3` (real device) ~3 times:

```python
import pypto.language as pl

M, K, N = 128, 64, 64

@pl.jit
def rhs_race_test(
    a: pl.Tensor[[M, K], pl.BF16],
    w_param: pl.Tensor[[K, N], pl.BF16],
    out_inkernel: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]],
    out_param: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]],
):
    # Build identity W in-kernel via vector ops (arange + cmp + cast)
    w_build = pl.create_tensor([K, N], dtype=pl.BF16)
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="build_w"):
        ones = pl.full([K, N], dtype=pl.FP32, value=1.0)
        col = pl.col_expand_mul(ones, pl.cast(pl.arange(0, [1, N], dtype=pl.INT32), target_type=pl.FP32))
        row = pl.cast(pl.reshape(pl.arange(0, [1, K], dtype=pl.INT32), [K, 1]), target_type=pl.FP32)
        w_build[:, :] = pl.cast(pl.cmp(col, pl.row_expand_mul(ones, row), cmp_type=0), target_type=pl.BF16)
    # Consume W as matmul RIGHT operand in a SEPARATE scope -> intermittently wrong
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="mm_inkernel"):
        out_inkernel[:, :] = pl.matmul(a[:, :], w_build[:, :], out_dtype=pl.FP32)
    # Control: same matmul, but W is a kernel input (no producer) -> always correct
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="mm_param"):
        out_param[:, :] = pl.matmul(a[:, :], w_param[:, :], out_dtype=pl.FP32)
    return out_inkernel, out_param
```

Driver: `a` = random BF16 `[128, 64]`; `w_param` = identity `[64, 64]`. Since `W = I`, both outputs must equal `a`. Run 3 times.

### Expected Behavior

`out_inkernel == out_param == a` on every run. The `build_w` → `mm_inkernel` dependency should force the vector store of `w_build` to complete before the matmul reads it.

### Actual Behavior

`out_param` PASSes on every run; `out_inkernel` is **non-deterministic** (observed PASS / FAIL / PASS over 3 consecutive runs). On a failing run the mismatches are `actual=0.0, expected=<nonzero>` (e.g. `[55] actual=0.0 expected=0.126953125`), ~127/8192 elements — i.e. the matmul read `w_build` before it was written (zero-initialized memory).

The same pattern caused an in-kernel-select matmul RoPE in pypto-lib (`decode_qkv_proj_rope.py`) to fail ~1–2% of elements standalone and ~79% end-to-end (attention amplifies the q/kv error), with the error ratio varying run-to-run.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `f9ad3fa0` (branch `main`) |

title: [Bug] ptoas rejects pto.tmov (non-mat, mismatched src/dst shapes) when slicing sub-columns of a matmul output's vec epilogue
body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto** (PTO codegen / subview materialization). ptoas correctly rejects a malformed `pto.tmov` that pypto emits: when a sub-column slice of a cube (matmul) output — after a vec epilogue lands it in Vec ND — is materialized, pypto allocates the destination tile with **unset** `valid_shape` (`v_row=?, v_col=?`) while the source subview carries `v_row=16, v_col=8`. A non-mat `tmov` requires matching src/dst shapes, so ptoas (correctly) fails.

This is the same family as #1507 (cube→vec bridge drops `valid_shape`) / #1535 (subview valid_shape inference) / #1505 (broadcast op valid_shape propagation): those fix the subview's *own* valid_shape, but the **spill/materialization copy still mismatches** on this path.

### Description

Slicing sub-columns of a matmul result that has been brought into Vec ND by a vector epilogue fails ptoas codegen. Minimal repro (a2a3 real device):

```python
import pypto.language as pl

M, K, N, SUB = 16, 128, 32, 8

@pl.jit
def repro(
    x: pl.Tensor[[M, K], pl.BF16],
    w: pl.Tensor[[N, K], pl.FP32],
    out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M, SUB], pl.FP32]],
):
    for ob in pl.spmd(1, name_hint="cube_slice"):
        x_f   = pl.cast(x[0:M, 0:K], target_type=pl.FP32)
        w_s   = pl.slice(w, [N, K], [0, 0], valid_shape=[24, K])
        acc   = pl.matmul(x_f, w_s, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32)  # [M,N] cube/L0C
        acc_nd = pl.mul(acc, 1.0)                # vec epilogue: land cube output in Vec ND
        sub    = pl.mul(acc_nd[0:M, 0:SUB], 2.0) # <-- in-place sub-column slice -> fails
        out[0:M, 0:SUB] = sub
    return out
```

**Result:**
```
ptoas compilation failed: error: 'pto.tmov' op expects A2/A3 non-mat tmov to use matching src/dst shapes
```

**Generated `.pto` (the offending tmov):**
```
%342 = pto.subview %115[0,0] sizes [16,8] : tile<...rows=16,cols=32...> -> tile<...rows=16,cols=8, v_row=16, v_col=8...>
pto.tmov ins(%342 : ...v_row=16, v_col=8) outs(%116 : ...v_row=?, v_col=?)   # <-- dst valid_shape unset -> mismatch
```

The subview `%342` correctly carries `v_row=16, v_col=8` (so #1535 is working), but the destination `alloc_tile %116` that the materialization copies into has `v_row=?, v_col=?`, and ptoas rejects the shape mismatch. The fix should either propagate the subview's `valid_shape` onto the materialization target, or avoid emitting the materializing `tmov` (let the consumer read the subview directly).

Origin: trying to fuse `models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py` into one spmd — slicing the `mixes` (matmul → `row_expand_mul`) result in place for the pre/post/comb split. The workaround is the existing GM bridge (spill `mixes` to GM, reload sub-ranges with `pl.load`).

Notes for minimizing (two *unrelated* errors mask this one if not avoided):
- A `[M,1]` FP32 tile (4B row) trips `alloc_tile` 32B-row-alignment first → use a scalar `pl.mul(acc, 1.0)` as the epilogue, not a `[M,1]` operand.
- Slicing the **boxed/L0C** matmul output directly trips `boxed tile cols must be multiple of innerCols(16)` → the vec epilogue (to Vec ND) + slice width ≥ 8 (32B) is required to expose the `tmov` bug cleanly.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `a64563c` (branch: `perf/dsv4-decode-attention-csa`) |
| pypto | `f9ad3fa0` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `324df3d6` |
| pto-isa | `8bd3ac8f` |
| ptoas | `0.43` |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1507, #1535, #1505. Full standalone repro: `models/deepseek/v4/repro_hc_pre_blocker1_cube_slice_tmov.py` (pypto-lib) — attaching to this issue.

title: [Bug] AICPU scheduler deadlock (507018) when one fanned-out spmd scope both writes and reads the same GM scratch (intra-scope self-RAW)
body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto runtime / simpler scheduler** (intra-scope dependency scheduling). A single fanned-out `pl.spmd` scope that **both writes and reads the same GM scratch tensor** compiles to a legal, acyclic orchestrator program but **deadlocks at runtime** with `507018`. The emitted orch DAG is acyclic and GM dependencies are tracked at **whole-tensor** granularity, so the read-side fan-out units depend on *all* write-side units; under limited core co-residency the units wait on each other and the AICPU scheduler deadlocks. pypto is only an enabler (it permits such a scope); the failure is a runtime scheduling deadlock, not a codegen error, not ptoas/pto-isa, not hardware.

### Description

Within one `pl.spmd` scope, storing to a GM scratch and later reading it back (here via tensor-subscript + `pl.transpose`) deadlocks:

```
aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
PTO2 runtime failed: orch_error_code=0 sched_error_code=100 runtime_status=-100
RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
```

The deadlocking kernel is `models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py` fused into 3 spmd scopes; the offending **scope 2** does (per 16-row tile):

```python
mixes_gm   = pl.create_tensor([T, MIX_PAD], pl.FP32)   # written by scope 1 (matmul)
pre_val_gm = pl.create_tensor([T, HC_PAD],  pl.FP32)   # scratch

for ob in pl.spmd(T // TILE, name_hint="hc_post"):     # scope 2
    t0 = ob * TILE
    # pre: read mixes_gm, compute, WRITE pre_val_gm
    pre_in = pl.load(mixes_gm, [t0, 0], [TILE, HC_PAD], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
    ...
    pl.store(pl.add(pre_sig, HC_EPS), [t0, 0], pre_val_gm)   # write scratch
    # post: read mixes_gm, write `post`
    ...
    # mix_x: READ the just-written pre_val_gm (same task), transpose, write x_mixed
    pre_tile   = pre_val_gm[t0:t0 + TILE, 0:HC_PAD]          # <-- self read-after-write
    pre_tile_t = pl.transpose(pre_tile, axis1=0, axis2=1)
    ... pl.row_expand_mul(x, pre_k) -> x_mixed_view[...] ...
```

**Splitting `mix_x` into its own 4th spmd scope (so no scope reads a scratch it wrote) runs the identical data flow and passes precision** — i.e. the GM round-trip is valid; only the intra-scope self-RAW is fatal.

### Evidence (which layer)

- **Orchestrator DAG is acyclic.** With `--enable-dep-gen` on the *working* 4-spmd variant, `deps.json` has 1 task per spmd scope and only forward edges (`pred < succ`). The deadlocking 3-spmd compiles (static IR `MaterializeRuntimeScopes`) to a legal sequential program: `mixes_gm = hc_pre_spmd(); x_mixed = hc_post_spmd(); hc_comb_spmd()`. So this is **not** a pypto graph-construction cycle.
- **GM deps are whole-tensor granularity.** Every GM arg in `deps.json` has `start_offset=0` + full shape (even the per-tile-accessed `mixes_gm[128,32]` / `pre_val_gm[128,8]`); per-tile sub-ranges are internal to the kernel and invisible to the scheduler. So a scope that is `INOUT` on `pre_val_gm` forces every read-unit to wait on every write-unit across the whole tensor.
- `deps.json` is **not** flushed when the run deadlocks (killed before dump), so it can only be captured on the working variant.

### Isolation

- A standalone single-task store-then-`pl.load` of a GM scratch (same rows): **passes** (no deadlock).
- Standalone store-then-(tensor-subscript + `pl.transpose`) read of a GM scratch: **passes**.
- The deadlock needs the fuller scope: cross-scope `mixes_gm` read + self-written `pre_val_gm` + the `post` store + the `mix_x` transpose, all in one fanned-out spmd task. (So a *truly minimal* self-RAW does not reproduce — the full repro kernel is required.)

### Asks

1. Handle an intra-scope self-RAW on a GM tensor correctly (disambiguate by `start_offset`/`shape` so a fan-out unit only depends on its own write, or serialize without deadlock) — rather than deadlocking.
2. Failing that, emit a compile-time diagnostic instead of compiling clean and deadlocking at runtime.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `a64563c` (branch: `perf/dsv4-decode-attention-csa`) |
| pypto | `f9ad3fa0` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `324df3d6` |
| pto-isa | `8bd3ac8f` |
| ptoas | `0.43` |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1592 — same `507018` symptom, but a **different trigger** (that was a cube+vec `CORE_GROUP` mix with a **dynamic-address** GM scatter, now closed/resolved). This one is a **pure-vec `pl.spmd`** scope with **static-offset** self-RAW, and reproduces on current `main` (`f9ad3fa0`). Full repro: `models/deepseek/v4/repro_hc_pre_blocker2_selfraw_507018.py` (3-spmd deadlocks; the 4-spmd `hc_pre_fused_draft.py` passes) — attaching to this issue.

title: [Bug] FlattenTileNdTo2D: standalone N-D tile.transpose fails — auto tmp flattened to 2D while transpose input stays N-D (tmp rank != input rank)
body:
### Component

Codegen — IR pass `FlattenTileNdTo2D` (`src/ir/transforms/flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp`)

### Description

A **standalone** N-D `tile.transpose` (transpose of the last two axes of a 3D+ tile, with leading batch dims) fails to compile. This is exactly the primitive needed to de-interleave columns for an interleaved RoPE the way the pypto2.0 frontend does it (`reshape [T, d] -> [T, d/2, 2] -> transpose(1,2) -> [T, 2, d/2] -> [T, d]`), so without it the only way to express de-/re-interleave on this stack is the much slower `pl.gather`/`pl.tensor.scatter` mask path.

**Root cause (traced):**
- The frontend auto-allocates the transpose scratch tile correctly at **input rank** — `python/pypto/ir/op/tile_ops.py:2223`: `tmp = create(list(input_type.shape), ...)` → a 3D input gets a 3D tmp.
- In `FlattenTileNdTo2D`, the `tile.create`/`tile.full` handler (`flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp:1718`) flattens that 3D tmp down to **2D**.
- But there is **no handler for a standalone `tile.transpose`** — the pass only special-cases transpose when it is a `tile.batch_matmul` operand (`flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp:1799`). A plain transpose falls through to the generic "substitute args + re-create" path, which leaves its **input 3D**.
- The re-created `tile.transpose` is then re-verified with **input rank 3 but tmp rank 2**, tripping the CHECK in `DeduceTileTransposeType` (`src/ir/op/tile_ops/transform.cpp:335`).

### Steps to Reproduce

Self-contained kernel (`-p a2a3`), fails at compile (in `run_passes`):

```python
import pypto.language as pl

T, RD = 128, 64
RH = RD // 2

@pl.jit
def nd_transpose_test(
    x: pl.Tensor[[T, RD], pl.FP32],
    even_out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[T, RH], pl.FP32]],
    odd_out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[T, RH], pl.FP32]],
):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="deint"):
        x3d = pl.reshape(x, [T, RH, 2])
        x3d_t = pl.transpose(x3d, axis1=1, axis2=2)   # 3D transpose of last two axes
        x_deint = pl.reshape(x3d_t, [T, RD])
        even_out[:, :] = x_deint[:, :RH]
        odd_out[:, :] = x_deint[:, RH:RD]
    return even_out, odd_out
```

Driver: `x = arange(T*RD).reshape(T, RD)`; expect `even_out = x[:, 0::2]`, `odd_out = x[:, 1::2]`.

### Expected Behavior

The N-D transpose compiles: `FlattenTileNdTo2D` lowers `[T, RH, 2] transpose(1,2)` to a batched 2D `pto.ttrans` (`[RH,2] -> [2,RH]` with `T` merged into the partition/outer), allocating a matching **2D** tmp so input and tmp ranks stay consistent. Result de-interleaves the columns.

### Actual Behavior

Compile aborts in `FlattenTileNdTo2D`:

```
ValueError: tile.transpose: tmp rank must match input rank, got input rank=3 tmp rank=2
Check failed: input_type->shape_.size() == tmp_type->shape_.size()
  at src/ir/op/tile_ops/transform.cpp:335
C++ Traceback:
  ... src/ir/transforms/flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp:1870
  ... src/ir/transforms/flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp:1833
```

(Reproduces both when the reshape/transpose are written at tile level and at tensor level — tensor-level `pl.transpose` also lowers to `tile.transpose` and hits the same pass.)

### Suggested Fix

Add a dedicated `tile.transpose` handler in `FlattenTileNdTo2D` (next to the `tile.load`/`tile.store`/`tile.sum`/`tile.batch_matmul` handlers around `:1799`) for the common "last-two-axes transpose with leading batch dims" case:
- merge leading batch dims into the partition/outer dim (mirror the `tile.batch_matmul` handler at `:1778`),
- emit a batched 2D `pto.ttrans` of the inner `[A,B] -> [B,A]`,
- flatten the tmp to the matching **2D** `[A,B]` so input/tmp ranks agree.

`MakeTileTransposeCodegenPTO` (`src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp:480`) already emits a 2D `pto.ttrans`; it likely needs the batch-loop emission mirrored from batch_matmul codegen. Transposes that involve a batch axis (e.g. `transpose(0,1)` on 3D) can be rejected with a clear error for now.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `f9ad3fa0` (branch `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `324df3d6` |
| pto-isa | `8bd3ac8f` |
| ptoas | `0.43` |
| pypto-lib (repro driver) | `a64563c` |
| CANN | not detected |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64). Fails at compile time (IR pass) — not hardware-specific.

### Additional Context

Related: #1578, #1349 (both touch `FlattenTileNdTo2D` / N-D handling, but for dynamic dims and rank-reducing slices respectively — not the standalone-transpose tmp-rank gap). Unblocking this enables a scatter-free, matmul-free interleaved RoPE on the `pl` frontend (the pypto2.0 `models/deepseek_v4` rope approach). Full driver in pypto-lib at `models/deepseek/v4/_tmp_nd_transpose.py`.

title: feat(ir): add pl.spmd_submit SPMD task-launch construct
body:
## Summary

Adds `pl.spmd_submit(self.kernel, *args, core_num=N, sync_start=False, deps=[...])` — the SPMD sibling of `pl.submit`. It dispatches a kernel across `N` blocks (one orchestration task → one `PTO2TaskId`) and captures that producer TaskId, so an SPMD launch can be named as a dependency of later tasks in `pl.manual_scope` (or used as a precision edge in auto scope).

```python
with pl.manual_scope():
    out,  tid  = pl.spmd_submit(self.incore_kernel, x, y, core_num=8, sync_start=True)
    out2, tid2 = pl.submit(self.consumer, out, deps=[tid])
```

### What changed
- **IR** (`expr.h`): `Submit` gains first-class `core_num_` (`std::optional<ExprPtr>`) and `sync_start_` fields, reflection descriptors (auto structural-equal/hash), constructor validation; `SubmitToCallView` surfaces them as Call attrs for codegen.
- **Pass-awareness**: every `Submit` reconstruction site + the base mutator (remaps `core_num_`) + visitor (walks `core_num_`) forward the launch spec, so no pass silently downgrades an SPMD launch to a single-block submit (`.claude/rules/pass-submit-awareness.md`).
- **Codegen**: refactored `EmitLaunchSpec` + new `EffectiveLaunchSpec` resolver emit the launch spec on the direct AIC/AIV path (previously missing), the Spmd-wrapper path, and both Group paths; TaskId capture + `set_dependencies` wiring reuse the existing `pl.submit` path. Backend-aware (`set_block_num` on 910B, `set_core_num` on 950).
- **Parser/DSL/bindings/printer/stub**: recognize `pl.spmd_submit` (tuple / single-LHS / annotated / bare-error forms), required keyword-only `core_num`, validation shared with `pl.spmd`, full print↔parse round-trip.
- **Serialization**: handle `Submit` (incl. the new fields) and `RuntimeScopeStmt` in the msgpack serializer/deserializer, so `manual_scope` + `spmd_submit` programs round-trip.
- **Docs**: Python syntax + IR hierarchy (en + zh-cn).

## Testing

title: fix(passes): fix windowed consumer input dependencies in OptimizeOrchTensors
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the remaining window-level dependency gap behind the pattern discussed in
hw-native-sys/pypto#1444.

The issue is not that the generated C++ scope alone hides tensor windows from runtime
dependency discovery. The runtime dependency graph is built from the tensors registered
through orchestration task arguments, especially `params.add_input(...)` and
`params.add_output(...)`. Before this change, `OptimizeOrchTensors` could externalize
producer output windows, so producer tasks registered precise `add_output(window)`
regions. However, a later windowed consumer could still register the full parent tensor
as its input. In that case TensorMap only saw a coarse/full-parent read, instead of the
actual consumer read window, and it could not derive the intended window-level
producer/consumer edges.

This change extends `OptimizeOrchTensors` to also optimize eligible consumer input
windows. For a windowed callee that reads a tensor slice, the pass now synthesizes the
same read window at the orchestration callsite, passes that window into the cloned
`__windowed` callee, and localizes the callee's internal read offset to the window
origin. The existing codegen path then naturally emits `params.add_input(window)`, so no
codegen change is required.

## Motivation

Consider an orchestration pattern where one phase writes disjoint windows of `score`,
and a later phase reads wider windows from `score`:

```python
for r0 in pl.parallel(0, N, SCORE_R):
    for c0 in pl.parallel(0, M, SCORE_C):
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="produce"):
            x_window = x[r0 : r0 + SCORE_R, c0 : c0 + SCORE_C]
            score = pl.assemble(score, pl.add(x_window, x_window), [r0, c0])

for r0 in pl.parallel(0, N, PROBE_R):
    for c0 in pl.parallel(0, M, PROBE_C):
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="consume"):
            block = score[r0 : r0 + PROBE_R, c0 : c0 + PROBE_C]
            probe = pl.assemble(probe, pl.add(block, block), [r0, c0])
```

For `SCORE_R x SCORE_C = 32 x 32` and `PROBE_R x PROBE_C = 32 x 64`, each consumer
task should depend on the two producer windows that overlap its `32 x 64` read. It
should not depend on every producer that wrote any part of the full `score` tensor.

The runtime TensorMap overlap check can build those precise edges only if both sides
register precise regions:

- producer task: `params.add_output(score_window)`
- consumer task: `params.add_input(score_read_window)`

The old transform produced the first item but not the second.

## Concrete Example

For the regression case in this PR:

- `score` shape: `64 x 128`
- producer window: `32 x 32`
- consumer read window: `32 x 64`
- producer tasks: `2 * 4 = 8`
- consumer tasks: `2 * 2 = 4`

The intended dependency shape is:

```text
consumer(0, 0)  reads score[0:32, 0:64]    -> depends on producer(0, 0), producer(0, 32)
consumer(0, 64) reads score[0:32, 64:128]  -> depends on producer(0, 64), producer(0, 96)
consumer(32, 0) reads score[32:64, 0:64]   -> depends on producer(32, 0), producer(32, 32)
consumer(32,64) reads score[32:64,64:128]  -> depends on producer(32,64), producer(32,96)
```

Before this change, producer tasks were already registered with precise output windows,
but consumer tasks could still register the full parent tensor:

```cpp
// producer task, already precise
Tensor score_window = score_flat.view(/* shape = [32, 32], offset = [r0, c0] */);
params_t0.add_output(score_window);

// consumer task, too coarse before this PR
params_t1.add_input(score_flat);
```

After this change, `OptimizeOrchTensors` creates the consumer read window at the
orchestration callsite, so the generated task argument registration becomes:

```cpp
// producer task
Tensor score_window = score_flat.view(/* shape = [32, 32], offset = [r0, c0] */);
params_t0.add_output(score_window);

// consumer task
Tensor score_read_window = score_flat.view(/* shape = [32, 64], offset = [r0, c0] */);
params_t1.add_input(score_read_window);
```

The cloned consumer receives `score_read_window` as its parameter. Its internal read is
then localized to the window origin:

```python
# before cloning/localization
block = score[r0 : r0 + 32, c0 : c0 + 64]

# inside the windowed callee after this pass
block = score_window[0:32, 0:64]
```

With `--enable-dep-gen`, the verified remote a2a3 result for this case contains
12 tasks and 8 TensorMap edges. Each consumer has exactly two producer predecessors,
which matches the four dependency groups above and confirms that the graph is not
full-parent/all-to-all.

## Changes

- Extend `OptimizeOrchTensors` analysis to detect simple tensor input reads in
  windowed callees.
- Synthesize callsite `tensor.slice(parent, window_shape, callsite_offsets)` for
  eligible writable-root input arguments.
- Pass the synthesized input window into the cloned `__windowed` callee.
- Rewrite the cloned callee's local `tensor.slice` / `tile.load` offset to zero,
  because the parameter itself is now the window.
- Keep conservative fallback behavior for ambiguous or mixed-root callsites, so the
  pass does not rewrite cases where the same callee input is sometimes backed by a
  writable output root and sometimes by an unrelated full input.
- Preserve the existing output-window externalization behavior.
- Avoid codegen changes. The generated orchestration already emits the right
  `params.add_input(...)` once the pass gives it a window tensor argument.

## Validation

- Unit tests:

```bash
pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_optimize_orch_tensors.py -q
```

Result: `39 passed`.

title: fix(ir): Materialize col_expand slice operand via tile.extract (fixes #1640)
body:
## Summary

A Vec `tile.slice` consumed by `tile.col_expand_mul` / `tile.col_expand_add` was materialized by codegen's lazy `pto.textract` into the slice's **own result buffer**. Because `tile.slice` is `set_output_memory_inherit_input`, the result MemRef shares the source allocation base; for a **dynamic-offset** slice of a local tile, `AllocateMemoryAddr` cannot encode the offset as a `ConstInt` address and falls back to the bare source base. The `pto.textract` therefore wrote the extracted row into **row 0 of the source tile**, silently corrupting it (same corruption class as #1622, reached via the lazy `pto.textract` path instead of the eager `pto.tmov` path removed by #1636).

This is latent today (no model chains a dynamic-offset local-tile slice → `col_expand` → re-read), but it is one kernel away.

## Fix

Extend `CanonicalizeMatSlice` (the pass that already folds `tile.slice` → `tile.extract` for matmul/extract consumers) to also rewrite a Vec `tile.slice` operand of `tile.col_expand_mul` / `tile.col_expand_add` into a fresh `tile.extract(target_memory=Vec)`. `tile.extract` is **not** `inherit_input`, so its result gets its own non-aliasing allocation; the materialization then lands in a distinct buffer and the source is left intact. The rewrite runs before `InitMemRef` / `AllocateMemoryAddr`, so the new tile gets a real address.

- Existing Mat `tile.slice` → extract/matmul folding is now gated on the slice's memory space (`is_mat`) and is **unchanged**.
- Full-window const-`[0,0]` slices are left untouched (their codegen self-copy is safe).
- Reuses the existing `tile.extract` op and `BuildOperandExtract` helper — no new pass, no boilerplate.

## Changes

- `src/ir/transforms/canonicalize_mat_slice_pass.cpp` — generalize the slice collector (tag `is_mat`), gate Mat consumers, add `TryRewriteColExpand` for `col_expand_mul`/`col_expand_add`.
- `tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen_ops.py` — parametrized codegen regression (no `pto.subview`; `pto.textract` outs is a distinct fresh buffer consumed by the col-expand op) for both ops.
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_canonicalize_mat_slice.py` — before/after rewrite tests for both ops + a full-window no-op test.
- `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_broadcast.py` — runtime ST: slice a local tile per row, `col_expand_mul`, then echo the source and assert it is bit-identical to the input.
- `docs/en|zh-cn/dev/passes/17-canonicalize_mat_slice.md` — document the new Vec col-expand canonicalization.

## Testing

- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` + `tests/ut/codegen/` — 1928 pass (incl. the new cases; existing Mat-slice canonicalization unchanged).
- **Negative control**: temporarily disabling the rewrite + rebuilding makes both the codegen and transform regression tests fail (the source-aliasing `pto.subview` reappears); restoring makes them pass.
- The runtime ST runs on real a2a3 in CI.

Fixes #1640
