title: [Feature] Dispatch @pl.jit.host distributed kernels end-to-end via the JIT runtime
body:
### Summary

A `@pl.jit.host` host-orchestrator kernel — per-rank dispatch of a `@pl.jit` chip
orchestrator over `pld.window` buffers — can be **specialized and compiled** today
(thanks to #1638 DistributedTensor params + #1645 `@pl.jit.host`), but it cannot be
**run end-to-end through the JIT runtime**:

1. There is no way for a JIT caller to supply a `distributed_config`. `JITFunction.__call__` / `_resolve_compiled` derive `ir.compile()` kwargs only from a `RunConfig` (`_run_config_compile_kwargs`), and `RunConfig` has no `distributed_config` field. (`JITFunction._compile` *does* forward `**ir_compile_kwargs` verbatim to `ir.compile()`, so the plumbing only needs a caller-facing entry point.)
2. The post-compile path does not recognize or dispatch a `DistributedCompiledProgram`. An L3 HOST orchestrator has no top-level `kernel_config.py`, so the normal `execute_compiled` / runner path cannot drive it — it must be invoked as a per-rank callable with a `pypto.runtime.RunConfig`.

This is exactly the runtime follow-up that #1645 deferred:

> Runtime distributed dispatch (plumbing `distributed_config` through `JITFunction._compile` so a host-orchestrator jit kernel can be executed end-to-end) is **out of scope** here and tracked as follow-up. The parser, IR pipeline, and `ir.compile()` already accept the generated source; the JIT runtime side just needs a way for the user to specify `distributed_config` (likely through `RunConfig`).

### Motivation / Use Case

We refactored `pypto-lib`'s `models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py` (2-rank EP MoE) from the
`@pl.program` class form to the `@pl.jit` family: a `@pl.jit` chip orchestrator
`moe_ep`, a `@pl.jit.host` driver `host_orch`, plus `@pl.jit.incore` dispatch/combine
and `@pl.jit.inline` compute deps. Specialization + `ir.compile(distributed_config=...)`
succeed and the kernel validates on 2 NPUs — but only via a **private-API workaround**,
because there is no supported way to run a host-orchestrator JIT kernel.

Current workaround (in `moe_ep.py`'s test harness):

```python
# run_jit() can't dispatch an L3 host orchestrator (uses _execute_via_runner,
# which needs a top-level kernel_config.py). So we stop at the specialized
# ir.Program and hand it to the @pl.program-style run() path instead.
program = host_orch._compile_to_program(   # test-only private API
    tensor_meta, scalar_values, scalar_dtypes, dynamic_dims, pl,
)
run(program=program, compile_cfg=dict(distributed_config=DistributedConfig(...)))
```

`host_orch._compile_to_program(...)` is documented "intended for testing only", and the
caller must hand-replay the `_bind_args` prelude. Closing this gap removes the workaround
and makes `@pl.jit.host` a first-class, runnable authoring form (the stated goal of #1645).

### Proposed API / Behavior

Let the JIT caller specify a `distributed_config` (per #1645's own suggestion, likely a
new `RunConfig.distributed_config` field forwarded through `_run_config_compile_kwargs`
→ `ir.compile()`), and have the post-compile path recognize a `DistributedCompiledProgram`
and route it through the L3 per-rank dispatch instead of `execute_compiled`:

```python
from pypto.runtime import RunConfig

# host_orch is a @pl.jit.host kernel; today this cannot run end-to-end.
host_orch(
    *args,
    config=RunConfig(platform="a2a3", distributed_config=DistributedConfig(device_ids=[0, 1])),
)
# JITFunction.__call__ detects the DistributedCompiledProgram and dispatches per-rank,
# the same way golden run()'s _try_l3_dispatch already does for @pl.program L3 programs.
```

### Alternatives Considered

- **Bridge through `run(program=...)`** (current workaround): call the test-only
  `host_orch._compile_to_program(...)` to get a parsed `ir.Program`, then feed the
  existing `@pl.program` `run()` path (whose `_try_l3_dispatch` already handles
  `DistributedCompiledProgram`). Works, but depends on private API and a hand-rolled
  `_bind_args` prelude — not a supported user-facing flow.
- **Keep `@pl.program` for distributed kernels** — defeats the purpose of #1638/#1645,
  which exist to let distributed programs be authored entirely with `@pl.jit`.

### Additional Context

- Precursors (both merged): #1638 (recognize `pld.DistributedTensor` params in `@pl.jit` / `@pl.jit.inline`), #1645 (add `@pl.jit.host`).
- A companion PR fixes three **specializer** correctness gaps surfaced by the same refactor (per-rank subscript-arg metadata `chip_orch(x[r], ...)`, `pld.window(...)` local metadata, and body-level annotation constant inlining). Those are independent of this runtime-dispatch request and are filed separately as a PR.
- Reference end-to-end consumer: `pypto-lib` `models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py`.

title: fix(ir): guard ConvertToSSA scope boundaries against bogus escaping (#1351)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1351.

`ConvertScope` inherited `future_needs_` unchanged into the body of every `ScopeStmt` subclass. When a variable was first defined inside `pl.at` (`InCoreScopeStmt` / `HierarchyScopeStmt` / `SpmdScopeStmt` / `ClusterScopeStmt` / `AutoInCoreScopeStmt`) and later referenced after the scope, that downstream reference put the variable into `future_needs_`. Nested loops inside the scope body then saw it in their escaping-variable detection and tried to promote it to `init_values`; `FindInitValue` had no matching pre-loop scalar so it manufactured an unversioned placeholder, producing IR like:

```python
for ob__idx_v0, (k0__iter_v0,) in pl.parallel(N, init_values=(k0__FREE_VAR,)):
    for kb__idx_v0, (k0__iter_v2,) in pl.range(K, init_values=(k0__iter_v0,)):
        k0__ssa_v4 = kb__idx_v0 * K_CHUNK__ssa_v0
        ...
        k0__rv_v3 = pl.yield_(k0__ssa_v4)
    k0__rv_v1 = pl.yield_(k0__rv_v3)
out_scalar__ssa_v1 = k0__rv_v1  # cross-scope reference, SSAVerify rejects it
```

## Fix

- `ConvertScope` now trims `future_needs_` to variables already in `cur_` at scope entry, so the inner-loop escaping path in `ConvertFor` / `ConvertWhile` ignores scope-local newly-defined vars.
- `cur_` itself is left transparent because `InterchangeChunkLoops` and similar later passes intentionally emit `out = pl.assemble(...)` inside `pl.at` and use `out` outside it (covered by `test_host_side_assemble_after_parallel_chunk_not_wrapped` and friends).
- `RuntimeScopeStmt` (`pl.scope()`) stays fully transparent — it is a thin codegen wrapper, not a boundary.

## Test plan

- [x] 3 new regression tests in `TestScopeOutlineBoundary`:
  - `test_scope_blocks_escaping_var_promotion_in_inner_loop` — reproduces #1351 and asserts the inner loops have no `iter_args`.
  - `test_scope_preserves_pre_existing_carried_var` — accumulator pattern (outer parameter reassigned inside `pl.at`) still carried.
  - `test_runtime_scope_remains_transparent_to_escaping` — `pl.scope()` keeps existing transparent behavior.
- [x] All 62 tests in `test_convert_to_ssa_pass.py` pass.
- [x] All 1538 tests in `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` pass (verifies no downstream pass regresses on the same IR).
- [x] Broader `tests/ut/` suite: 5645 passed (3 unrelated runtime test failures exist on `main` too).

## Documentation

- `docs/en/dev/passes/04-convert_to_ssa.md` and `docs/zh-cn/dev/passes/04-convert_to_ssa.md`: added an algorithm bullet describing the scope-boundary escaping guard.
- `include/pypto/ir/stmt.h`: updated the `ScopeStmt` doxygen to spell out the new boundary semantics and the `RuntimeScopeStmt` exception.

Extends `@pl.jit` / `@pl.jit.host` compile-time metadata inference to cover two host-orchestration distributed patterns, plus a specializer fix for shape constants in body-level annotations.

- **Per-rank sliced dispatch** — a host orchestrator dispatching one chip orchestrator per rank via subscripting (`chip_orch(inputs[r], ...)`). Threaded through arg extraction, param mapping, and dep-call resolution; the DynDim cascade correctly skips sliced args (the dropped rank dim carries no DynDim).
- **`pld.window` views** — a `_window_meta` handler (sibling to `create_tensor` / `slice`) propagates per-rank window-buffer locals into the chip orchestrator's `pld.DistributedTensor` parameters. Shared dtype parsing is factored into `_dtype_from_kw`.

title: feat(jit): dispatch @pl.jit.host distributed kernels end-to-end
body:
## Summary

A `@pl.jit.host` host-orchestrator kernel could be **specialized and compiled** today
(via #1638 DistributedTensor params + #1645 `@pl.jit.host`), but had no supported way to
**run end-to-end through the JIT runtime**: a JIT caller could not supply a
`distributed_config`, so `ir.compile()` never produced a `DistributedCompiledProgram`.

This wires `distributed_config` through the JIT runtime so a host-orchestrator JIT kernel
runs end-to-end:

```python
from pypto.runtime import RunConfig
from pypto.ir.distributed_compiled_program import DistributedConfig

host_orch(*args, config=RunConfig(platform="a2a3",
                                  distributed_config=DistributedConfig(device_ids=[0, 1])))
```

### Changes

- **`RunConfig.distributed_config`** (`python/pypto/runtime/runner.py`): new optional field,
  defaults to `None`, consumed only on the `@pl.jit` path. Typed under `TYPE_CHECKING` to
  avoid a runtime import cycle — `distributed_compiled_program` already imports from
  `pypto.runtime`.
- **`_run_config_compile_kwargs`** (`python/pypto/jit/decorator.py`): forwards
  `distributed_config` to `ir.compile()` **only when set**, so non-distributed callers keep
  the single-chip default and don't perturb the cache key. Mirrors the existing `output_dir`
  forwarding pattern.
- Docstring updates on `RunConfig`, `_run_config_compile_kwargs`, and the `JITFunction`
  class (removing the "follow-up work" note that #1645 left).

`JITFunction._compile` already forwards `**ir_compile_kwargs` to `ir.compile()`, and
`JITFunction.__call__` already dispatches polymorphically via
`compiled(*ordered_args, config=run_config)`. So once the config reaches compile, the
resulting `DistributedCompiledProgram.__call__` drives per-rank dispatch with no further
plumbing — confirming issue item #2 is satisfied by polymorphism (no guard rejects a `host`
entry at call time). This removes the private-API `_compile_to_program(...)` +
`run(program=...)` workaround in `pypto-lib`'s `models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py`.

## Testing

- [x] New UT in `TestCompileKwargForwarding` (`tests/ut/jit/test_decorator.py`): config
  forwarded when set, omitted when unset, and threaded through `_compile` into a faked
  `ir.compile()`.
- [x] Full JIT UT suite: `python -m pytest tests/ut/jit/ -n auto` → **212 passed**.
- [x] ruff check + format clean.
- [ ] End-to-end on 2 NPUs (manual): adapt the `pypto-lib` `moe_ep.py` harness to call
  `host_orch(*args, config=RunConfig(distributed_config=DistributedConfig(device_ids=[0,1])))`.

This is a pure-Python change (no C++/bindings/type-stub changes needed).

## Related Issues

Fixes #1657

title: feat(ir): add AssignTypeSymmetry structural verifier (#1285)
body:
## Summary

Implements the `AssignTypeSymmetry` property verifier from #1285. For every
`AssignStmt(var, value)` it asserts `structural_equal(var->GetType(), value->GetType())`,
turning silent LHS/RHS type corruption into a localized, diagnosable error at the
pass that caused it (rather than three passes later at codegen).

This is **Phase 1** of the issue's two-phase rollout: the verifier is registered in
`PropertyVerifierRegistry` but **not yet** added to `GetStructuralProperties()`.

## What it covers

`structural_equal` is the IR's own type-equality contract (the one the roundtrip
verifier uses). The verifier therefore compares:

- **TileType**: dtype, shape, `tile_view`, `memory_space`
- **TensorType**: dtype, shape, `tensor_view` (DistributedTensorType also `window_buffer`)
- **TupleType**: every element recursively (so `Submit`'s `TASK_ID`-augmented return tuples are handled)

`memref_` is **intentionally excluded** — it is an allocation detail bound to the Var,
governed by `HasMemRefs` / `AllocatedMemoryAddr`, and `structural_equal` does not compare
it. (Note: `memory_space` exists only on `TileType`, not `TensorType`.) This corrects the
issue's original "covers memref" wording.

## Empirical finding

Running the verifier after **every** pass:

- **`tests/ut` — 5,415 tests: 0 violations** (full 38-pass Default pipeline, including
  `InferTileMemorySpace` (#1262), `InitMemRef`, and all distributed/SPMD/`CollectCommGroups`/
  `window_buffer` passes).
- **`tests/st/codegen` — exactly 1 latent violation**: the transposed-weight (`b_trans=True`)
  3D batch-matmul path. `LowerTransposeLoadParamLayout` rewrites the `w_k__tile` load's RHS to
  a DN-reshaped param (re-deduces to rank 3) without updating the LHS Var (stays rank 2) →
  `TileType shape rank mismatch (2 != 3)`. This is the IR-level root of the already-known
  DN→NZ TLOAD codegen failure, caught 3 passes earlier.

So #1262/#1278 are confirmed fixed; **Phase-2 promotion to `GetStructuralProperties()` is
deferred** until the `LowerTransposeLoadParamLayout` rank asymmetry is fixed (else CI would
hard-fail that compile path).

## Changes

- New verifier `src/ir/verifier/verify_assign_type_symmetry.cpp` + factory decl + registry registration + CMake source
- `IRProperty::AssignTypeSymmetry` enum + `IRPropertyToString`
- Python binding `.value(...)` + type stub
- Unit test (positive; memory_space/dtype/shape/tile_view/tuple negatives; by-design memref tolerance)
- Verifier docs (en + zh-cn)
- Drive-by include hygiene in two files that `#include verifier.h`
  (`interchange_chunk_loops_pass.cpp`: add `kind_traits.h`;
  `verify_array_not_escaped.cpp`: add `error.h`/`<cstddef>`, drop unused `span.h`) —
  surfaced by clang-tidy's changed-header dependency expansion.

## Testing

- [x] New unit test passes (8/8)
- [x] Full `tests/ut` suite green (5,415 passed; the verifier added 0 false positives across the sweep)
- [x] clang-tidy clean on the diff
- [x] Build clean

## Related issues

- Implements #1285
- Surfaces the IR-level root of the transposed-weight batch-matmul codegen bug (tracked locally; gates Phase-2 promotion)
- Complements #1262 / #1278 (both fixed)

title: fix(codegen): emit nested allocate_domain per CommGroup
body:
## Summary

`DistributedCodegen` previously `CHECK`-failed when a program contained more than one `CommGroup`. This change lifts that restriction:

- Iterate `program_->comm_groups_` and emit one nested `with orch.allocate_domain(...)` per group.
- Build a `WindowBuffer -> group_idx` lookup (`unordered_map<const WindowBuffer*, size_t>`) once per `Generate()` from `CollectCommGroups` slots; reuse it to route each Submit's per-arg `device_ctx` handle to the correct domain.
- `INTERNAL_CHECK` on the lookup — a missing entry indicates `CollectCommGroups` did not run before codegen (pass-invariant violation, not user error).

Complexity: O(N) build + O(1) amortized lookup per arg; well within the project's O(N log N) pass-complexity bound.

## Testing

- [x] Added UT `test_two_groups_emit_nested_allocate_domain` — verifies emission order, indentation nesting (d1 nested inside d0), and per-arg handle routing.
- [x] Added UT `test_two_groups_handle_routing_is_per_dispatch_not_state_bleed` — regression against per-callee handle caching: same callee, two dispatch sites, distinct windows must produce distinct handles.
- [x] Added ST `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_multi_group.py` — 3-rank multi-group HCCL bring-up (gated by `if len(device_ids) < 3: pytest.skip(...)`).
- [x] Code review completed.

## Notes

The previous code already carried a TODO ("Multi-group will need a WindowBuffer->group_idx lookup") at the exact spot this change addresses. No IR / binding / type-stub changes — codegen-only.

title: docs(distributed): fix TPUT staging tile lowering description
body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** `distributed_ops.md` (EN + zh-cn) described TPUT’s VEC staging tile as synthesized at codegen — the same story as TGET. That contradicts the implementation and misleads anyone debugging put lowering.
- **Fix:** Document that `ConvertTensorToTileOps` materializes `tile.create` + internal `pld.tile.put` before codegen; `MakePutCodegenPTO` only emits `pto.comm.tput` with the already-allocated `buf(%stage)`. Explicitly contrast with TGET (stage still synthesized in `MakeGetCodegenPTO`).
- **Also:** Document the subregion `pld.tensor.put(dst, peer, src, dst_offsets, src_offsets, shape, *, atomic=)` signature and verifier (full-slice vs subregion).

## Proof (implementation)

| Layer | Evidence |
|-------|----------|
| IR | `src/ir/op/distributed/put.cpp` — staging via `ConvertTensorToTileOps`; 6-arg subregion form |
| Pass | `src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp` (~1830) — `pld.tensor.put` → `tile.create` + `pld.tile.put` |
| Codegen | `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp` `MakePutCodegenPTO` (2662–2664): “The VEC staging tile is **not** synthesized here” |
| TGET contrast | Same file `MakeGetCodegenPTO` (2688–2693): `%stage = pto.alloc_tile` at codegen |

title: feat(ir): lower standalone N-D tile.transpose in FlattenTileNdTo2D
body:
## Summary

Add lowering for a **standalone >2D `tile.transpose`** (one not consumed by a `tile.batch_matmul`) in `FlattenTileNdTo2D`, and in the process make that pass the **sole owner of the `pto.ttrans` scratch buffer**.

Previously a standalone N-D transpose had no lowering: the pass left the transpose input at rank>2 while its DSL-emitted scratch `tmp` was flattened to rank 2, tripping the input-rank == tmp-rank `CHECK` in `DeduceTileTransposeType`.

## What changed

### 1. Scratch is now a codegen detail, not a high-level operand

The `pto.ttrans` scratch is required only by the 2D backend codegen — it is not a semantic operand of a transpose. So the high-level op no longer carries it:

- **`tensor.transpose` conversion** and both **DSL builders** (`pl.tile.transpose`, `ir.op.tile_ops.transpose`) now emit the **3-arg** form `(input, axis1, axis2)` with no `tile.create` scratch.
- **`DeduceTileTransposeType`** accepts **3 or 4** args, validating the `tmp` operand only when present.
- **`FlattenTileNdTo2D`** materializes the codegen-ready **4-arg** form for *both* 2D and per-page >2D transposes, still before the memory allocator runs (so the scratch gets a real UB address).
- **`TileOps2DVerifier`** now requires every post-flatten `tile.transpose` to be the 4-arg form.
- The `tmp`/`tmp_tile` parameter is kept *optional* on the Python builders **only** so the lowered 4-arg IR round-trips through the printer/parser (`RoundtripInstrument`). User code never supplies it; it is never auto-created at the high level.

This removes the old generate-then-elide dead-scratch handling: the conversion used to emit a whole-tile `tmp` that, for an >2D input, could not be flattened and had to be specially skipped by a pre-scan. With the conversion emitting no scratch, that pre-scan/skip is **deleted** entirely.

### 2. `LowerNdTranspose` — standalone last-two-axes swap

Handles axes `{ndim-2, ndim-1}` with leading batch dims. The flattened 2D input `[batch*A, B]` is sliced per batch into an `[A, B]` page, transposed via a genuine **2D** `tile.transpose` into `[B, A]`, and assembled into a flat `[batch*B, A]` output. Every emitted transpose is 2D, so **no codegen change is needed**.

- A single flat scratch **pool** `[batch*A, B]` is pre-created and sliced per batch (a partial `tile.slice` → `pto.subview` with static valid `[A, B]`), so each per-page scratch is the same kind of SSA value as the source page — avoiding the dynamic/static type conflict that `create + set_validshape` would cause in ptoas.
- A producer the pass leaves at rank>2 is reshaped down to the merged 2D `[batch*A, B]` first, so the per-batch slice always has a 2D parent.
- A transpose that moves a batch axis is rejected with a clear user-facing error.

## Scope vs #1651

This resolves the **core problem** #1651 raised — a standalone N-D `tile.transpose` now compiles and runs. It does **not** yet make the full #1651 example pass: that example hits a **separate** row-alignment limitation. A trailing dim whose per-page row byte size (`cols * sizeof(dtype)`) is not 32-byte aligned is **rejected with a clear user-facing error** rather than worked around; narrow-column padding will be filed as its own issue. The two ST cases that exercise that gap (`test_simple_transpose`, `test_nd_transpose_deinterleave`) are **skipped** with an explanatory reason pending that fix.

## Testing

UT (`tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_flatten_tile_nd_to_2d.py`):
- `test_nd_transpose_unrolls_to_2d_transposes` (`[2,3,8] -> [2,8,3]`, trailing dim 8 = 32-byte aligned) covers the per-batch unroll. It uses a uniquely-named program class so `@pl.program` (which resolves the class body via `inspect.getsource` by name) compiles the intended program.
- `test_2d_transpose_materializes_scratch` asserts the pass turns a 3-arg 2D transpose into the 4-arg scratch-bearing form.
- `test_batch_axis_transpose_rejected` covers the batch-axis-swap user error.

Operator UT (`tests/ut/ir/operators/test_tile_ops.py`): asserts the high-level builder emits the 3-arg (no auto-tmp) form and passes a 4-arg form through unchanged.

ST (`tests/st/runtime/ops/test_trans.py`):
- `Nd3DTransposeCase` (`[4,24,8]` swap axes 1,2 → `[4,8,24]`) exercises the lowering end-to-end. Both inner dims are multiples of 8 (32-byte-aligned tile rows) but non-16-aligned, keeping the 3D ND tensor-view layout `nd` and avoiding a separate `nz` layout-inference path; the non-square shape makes the swap distinguishable from a no-op.

Docs: `12-convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.md` and `15-flatten_tile_nd_to_2d.md` (en + zh-cn) updated to describe the new scratch-ownership split. `clang-tidy` clean on the diff.

## Related Issues

Addresses #1651 (partial — see Scope above).

title: perf(st): Cap golden torch threads to avoid compile-pool oversubscription
body:
## Summary
- Golden reference computation (`_materialize_tensors` + `compute_expected`) runs inside compile-pool worker **threads**. Without a thread cap, each torch op defaults to ~`nproc` intra-op threads, so every compile worker grabs the full core count and they thrash the process-wide intra-op pool.
- `start_pipeline` now bounds torch intra-op threads to `cores // compile_workers` (clamped to ≥1), keeping `outer × intra ≈ cores` and curbing cross-socket traffic on NUMA hosts for the bandwidth-bound tensor materialisation.
- Override via `PYPTO_GOLDEN_THREADS` when a few heavy goldens dominate the tail and the suite is otherwise idle.

## Testing
- [x] Code review completed
- [x] `ruff check` clean; file parses
- Behavioural impact is ST-harness scheduling only (no codegen/IR surface touched); validated by ST suite on hardware.

## Related Issues
N/A

title: feat(ir): capture SPMD dispatch TaskId via 'with pl.spmd(...) as tid'
body:
## Summary

Adds `with pl.spmd(N, deps=[...]) as tid:` — the SPMD sibling of `with pl.at(...) as tid:`. It captures an SPMD dispatch's grid-wide producer `Scalar[TASK_ID]` in `tid`, so the whole launch can be named as an explicit dependency of later tasks (`deps=[tid]`), stored into a `pl.array.create(N, pl.TASK_ID)`, or crossed into `pl.manual_scope`. Unlike the plain `with pl.spmd(N):` single-call form, the capture form accepts an inline multi-statement body (auto-outlined into an InCore kernel like `for i in pl.spmd(N):`); the per-block index is read via `pl.tile.get_block_idx()`.

The capture rides the existing `kAttrTaskIdVar` rail: the generic `ScopeOutliner` (already keyed on `ScopeKind::Spmd`) lowers the dispatch to an `ir.Submit` with a trailing `Scalar[TASK_ID]`. `core_num` / `sync_start` ride on the outlined `Spmd` Function attrs; codegen reads them via `EffectiveLaunchSpec`'s function-attr fallback (the Submit's own `core_num` is `None`).

## Changes

- **Parser** (`ast_parser.py`): `_parse_spmd_scope_with_tid` records `kAttrTaskIdVar` / `manual_dep_edges` on the `SpmdScopeStmt` and emits the `system.task_invalid()` SSA placeholder; `_parse_spmd_kwargs` gains `allow_deps`. Rejects `deps=` on the for-form, deps-without-`as tid`, tuple `as`-targets, and `pl.cluster()` nesting.
- **Printer** (`python_printer.cpp`): emits `with pl.spmd(...) [optimizations=][deps=] as tid:`.
- **IRMutator / IRVisitor**: walk `SpmdScopeStmt` attr Vars (tid / dep edges) like the `InCore` / `AutoInCore` / `Hierarchy` handlers — satisfies the pass-submit-awareness use-def/substitution contract now that Spmd scopes can carry these attrs.
- **DSL** (`dsl_api.py`): `pl.spmd()` / `SpmdContext` gain `deps=`.
- **Docs**: EN + zh-cn `python_syntax.md`.

## Testing

- [x] Parser/printer: attr capture, placeholder, inline body, deps, split, print↔parse round-trips, rejection cases.
- [x] Outlining: `as tid` → `ir.Submit`; `deps=[tid0]` folds into the consumer `Submit.deps_`.
- [x] Codegen: launch-spec function-attr fallback (`set_block_num` / `set_require_sync_start`); `task_id()` capture + `set_dependencies`.
- [x] JIT: `compile_for_test` end-to-end.
- [x] The 4 pre-existing `pl.spmd` JIT tests (for-form, plain with-form, inline-helper, sibling loops) still pass — no regression.

title: fix(codegen): enable dynamic number of ranks on DistributedTensor (AsTensorTypeLike + scf.for index-cast)
body:
## Summary

This PR closes two related codegen gaps that blocked using `pl.dynamic("NR")` as a rank-count dimension on `DistributedTensor` parameters, and refactors the L3 allreduce system test to demonstrate the feature end-to-end.

---

## Background

The goal is to write a single allreduce program where the number of ranks (`NR`) is determined at runtime — instead of building a separate program per world size via a Python factory closure. Two compiler bugs prevented this from working:

---

## Changes

### 1. `src/codegen/pto/pto_codegen.cpp` — collect dynamic shape vars from `DistributedTensor` params

`CollectTensorShapeDynVars` walks function parameters to find dynamic dimension variables (e.g. `NR`) that need to be added as trailing `index` arguments to the emitted MLIR function signature.

**Bug:** It used `As<TensorType>` which performs an exact `ObjectKind` match. `DistributedTensorType` inherits from `TensorType` but has a different kind, so dynamic dims on `pld.DistributedTensor[[NR, 1], ...]` parameters were silently dropped.

**Fix:** Use `ir::AsTensorTypeLike` — already used at every other tensor-boundary site in the same file — which accepts both `TensorType` and `DistributedTensorType`.

**Effect:** `NR` now correctly appears as a trailing `%argN: index` in the emitted `func.func` signature, and the corresponding `make_tensor_view` shape uses `%argN` instead of a zeroed constant.

---

### 2. `src/codegen/pto/pto_control_flow_codegen.cpp` — auto-cast `scf.for` loop bounds to `index`

`scf.for` in MLIR requires all three bounds (start, stop, step) to be `index` type. The codegen `VisitStmt_(ForStmtPtr)` was passing the evaluated SSA values directly to `scf.for` with no type coercion.

**Bug:** `pld.nranks(ctx)` and `pld.rank(ctx)` return `INT32` (MLIR `i32`). Using them as a `pl.range()` bound compiled at the Python level but produced an `i32` stop value in the emitted MLIR, which failed `ptoas` MLIR verification.

**Fix:** After evaluating each bound, pass it through `EmitCastToIndex(expr, ssa)` — the same helper already used at tensor view dimensions, array offsets, and SPMD block indices. For `ConstInt(INDEX)` bounds (all static `pl.range(8)` etc.) this is a no-op. For `i32` runtime values it emits `arith.index_cast`.

**Effect:** `pl.range(pld.nranks(ctx))` now works without any user-visible `pl.cast(…, pl.INDEX)` workaround.

---

### 3. `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_allreduce.py` — single dynamic-NR allreduce program

Replaces the `_build_allreduce_program(n_ranks)` factory (which compiled a new program per world size using a captured Python integer `nr = n_ranks`) with a single module-level `AllReduceMesh` class that uses `NR = pl.dynamic("NR")` in all shape annotations.

The test is parametrized as `@pytest.mark.parametrize("n_ranks", [2, 4])` — both ranks compile and run the same program; `P=4` skips automatically on 2-device CI hosts.

The allreduce logic is a 4-phase mesh barrier (stage-in → notify/wait → remote_load+add → stage-out) that generalises to any N ranks.

---

### 4. `tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_distributed_dynamic_shape.py` — new unit tests (CPU-only)

Two test groups, no hardware required:

- **`test_distributed_tensor_dynamic_nr_pto_codegen`** — verifies that `NR` on a `DistributedTensor[[NR, 1], ...]` parameter appears as a trailing `index` arg in the emitted MLIR and is wired into the tensor view shape.
- **`test_nranks_range_bound_auto_cast_to_index`** — verifies that `pl.range(pld.nranks(ctx))` produces an `arith.index_cast` instruction whose result is directly used as a `scf.for` bound operand.
- **`test_collect_vars_from_shape_expr_finds_nr`** — unit-tests the C++ `collect_vars_from_shape_expr` Python binding directly on the `NR` dim expression.

---

title: feat(jit): support auto_scope=False on @pl.jit and @pl.jit.host
body:
## Summary

Threads the `auto_scope` flag through the JIT layer so an Orchestration entry (`@pl.jit`) or HOST orchestrator (`@pl.jit.host`) can opt out of compiler-inserted AUTO runtime scopes (`PTO2_SCOPE`) and place them by hand with `with pl.scope()`. The end-to-end path for `@pl.function(auto_scope=False)` already existed (parser → func_attrs → MaterializeRuntimeScopes); this PR wires the JIT decorators into it.

```python
@pl.jit(auto_scope=False)              # Orchestration entry
def orchestrator(a, b, out):
    with pl.scope():
        out = tile_add(a, b, out)
    return out

@pl.jit.host(auto_scope=False)         # HOST orchestrator
def host_orch(...): ...
```

## Changes

- **decorator.py**: `JITFunction` stores `_auto_scope`; `@pl.jit` gains a parenthesized form (`@pl.jit(auto_scope=False)`) alongside the bare form; `_SubFunctionDecorator` grows an `allow_auto_scope` gate so `host` accepts the kwarg while `incore`/`inline`/`opaque` reject it with a clear `TypeError`. The flag is forwarded only to the entry context (deps default to `True`).
- **specializer.py**: `SpecializeContext` carries `auto_scope`; `build_specialize_context` accepts it; `_build_decorator` emits `auto_scope=False` for the host and orchestration-entry decorators.
- **docs**: documents the flag in the user language guide (en + zh-cn), cross-referencing the MaterializeRuntimeScopes pass.

## Testing

- [x] `tests/ut/jit/` — decorator wiring (default `True`, parenthesized form, empty-parens form, host acceptance, sub-function rejection) and the generated `@pl.function` decorator string at the specializer level
- [x] Full `tests/ut/jit/` + `test_auto_scope_parsing` + `test_materialize_runtime_scopes` pass (266 passed)
- [x] End-to-end: `@pl.jit(auto_scope=False)` + manual `with pl.scope()` compiles; default mode correctly rejects a hand-placed AUTO scope
- [x] ruff + pyright clean

title: [Pass Bug] DeriveCallDirections marks a pld.tile.remote_store target as input, so a window write->read across kernels isn't ordered
body:
### Pass Name

DeriveCallDirections

### Description

A kernel that fills a distributed window via `pld.tile.remote_store(..., peer=dst)` (plus a cross-rank barrier) is **not** scheduled before a later kernel that reads that same window.

`DeriveCallDirections` classifies the `remote_store` **target** as `pl.adir.input`: the write lands on a *peer's* copy of the window, so from local dataflow the param looks read-only. The producing kernel is therefore never seen as a producer of the window. A downstream reader (also `input`) gets no producer→consumer (RAW) edge, the two tasks run concurrently, and the reader races on an unfilled window → silent, non-deterministic wrong results.

### Git Commit ID

`89698531`

### Before IR (Input)

```python
# Minimal @pl.program shape. Real trigger: dsv4 models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py
# EP-MoE, where the cross-rank `combine` is split into a push+barrier InCore
# kernel and a separate local-reduce kernel that reads the routed_y_buf window.
import pypto.language as pl
import pypto.language.distributed as pld

@pl.program
class Repro:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)          # writer: cross-rank push + barrier
    def push_step(self, src: pl.Tensor[[N, D], pl.BF16],
                  win: pld.DistributedTensor[[N, D], pl.BF16],
                  done: pld.DistributedTensor[[R, 1], pl.INT32],
                  my_rank: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32]):
        # ... pld.tile.remote_store(tile, win, peer=dst, offsets=[r, 0]) ...
        # ... pld.system.notify / pld.system.wait  (cross-rank barrier) ...
        ...

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Inline)           # reader: local read of the filled window
    def read_step(self, win: pld.DistributedTensor[[N, D], pl.BF16],
                  out: pl.Tensor[[N, D], pl.BF16]):
        # ... pl.load(win, [r, 0], [1, D]) -> out ...
        ...

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
    def chip(self, src, win, done, out, my_rank):
        self.push_step(src, win, done, my_rank)
        self.read_step(win, out)        # must run AFTER push_step's barrier fills `win`
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

```python
# push_step's `win` (the remote_store target) should be classified output/inout,
# so the orchestration emits a producer->consumer edge and read_step is ordered
# AFTER push_step:
self.push_step(src, win, done, my_rank,
    attrs={"arg_directions": [pl.adir.input, pl.adir.output, pl.adir.inout, pl.adir.scalar]})
#                                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ win produced here
self.read_step(win, out,
    attrs={"arg_directions": [pl.adir.input, pl.adir.inout]})
#                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ RAW on win -> read_step ordered after push_step
```

### Actual IR or Error

Real excerpt from `passes_dump/35_after_DeriveCallDirections.py` (dsv4 moe_ep
compile, `python models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py -p a2a3 -d 0,1 --compile-only`):

```
# inside combine_ep, the window `routed_y_buf` is ONLY ever a remote_store target:
pld.tile.remote_store(y_tile__ssa_v0, routed_y_buf__ssa_v0, dst__idx_v0, [r_route__tile, 0])

# orchestration (moe_ep) — both calls mark routed_y_buf as `input`, so no edge:
self.combine_ep(
    recv_y, recv_r_route_out, pub_counts, routed_y_buf, combine_done, my_rank,
    attrs={"arg_directions": [input, input, input, input, input, scalar]},
)                          # routed_y_buf (4th) = input  <-- should be output/inout
self.comb_reduce_spmd(sh, routed_y_buf, ffn_out_flat,
    attrs={"arg_directions": [input, input, inout]})   # routed_y_buf = input (read)

# Both `input` -> no producer -> reduce is not ordered after the push -> race.
```

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific) — the wrong `arg_directions` is visible at `--compile-only`; the resulting race manifests on Ascend 910B.

### Host Platform (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Additional Context

On 2x Ascend 910B the split EP-MoE combine produces `x_next` ~97.9% wrong (`ratio_reldiff`), with values varying run-to-run and `actual ≈ sh` (the routed contributions are missing) — consistent with the reduce reading an unfilled window.

**Workaround:** keep the window write (push + barrier) and the window read in the **same** InCore function — sequential statements in one InCore body are ordered, so the bug only appears once they are split into separate kernels (which is required to parallelize the reduce with `pl.spmd`, since `pl.spmd`/`pl.parallel` aren't valid inside an InCore body).

A host-backed "sync" token (output of the writer, input of the reader) did **not** help when the reader was `@pl.jit.inline` (it is spliced, not a separate task, so the dep wasn't carried); and fundamentally the writer is not recognized as a producer of the window at all.

**Suggested fix:** treat a `pld.tile.remote_store` target (a cross-rank-written, barrier-synchronized window) as producing that window for scheduling — e.g. classify the `remote_store` target as `output`/`inout` in `DeriveCallDirections`, or provide a way to express a window producer→consumer ordering edge across kernels.

Related: #1648, #1503, #1368.

title: [RFC] Replace Program::comm_groups_ with CommDomainScopeStmt IR op
body:
### Summary

Replace the program-level `Program::comm_groups_` metadata vector (and its companion `CommGroup` IRNode) with a new `CommDomainScopeStmt` scope statement that wraps the host-orchestration body. The `CollectCommGroups` pass is repurposed (renamed `MaterializeCommDomainScopes`) to emit the scope chain instead of populating program metadata; distributed codegen lowers each scope to its `with orch.allocate_domain(...)` block. The user DSL (`pld.alloc_window_buffer` / `pld.window` / `device=` dispatches) is unchanged, and the generated `host_orch.py` is byte-identical to today (strict-equivalence nesting). Tracked branch base commit: `b8e0c6f678825cca28e764a104aec38906fe7674`.

Related: #565 (distributed IR foundation), #1127 (L3 distributed programming interface), #1189 (orchestration-level collective communication).

### Motivation

The flat-metadata-on-program shape is a vestige of the old runtime that required communication domains to be constructed statically before worker initialization. The current `simpler` runtime supports per-`orch_fn` `orch.allocate_domain(...)`, so a domain is just another scoped resource inside the host orchestrator body — exactly the shape `RuntimeScopeStmt` already models for `PTO2_SCOPE` (`include/pypto/ir/stmt.h:950-972`, `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:792-821`).

Problems with the status quo:

- Codegen reads program-level metadata to decide nesting structure (`src/codegen/distributed/distributed_codegen.cpp:270-339`). Nesting is implicit in declaration order + indentation tracking, not in the IR.
- Several passes thread `comm_groups_` through Program reconstruction even though the data is purely orchestration-body concern (`simplify_pass.cpp`, `expand_manual_phase_fence_pass.cpp`, `optimize_orch_tensors_pass.cpp`, `passes.cpp`).
- A `WindowBuffer → group_idx` map is rebuilt at codegen entry (`distributed_codegen.cpp:79-84`) instead of being resolvable from the IR ancestor chain.
- Existing scope ops (`RuntimeScopeStmt`, `InCoreScopeStmt`, `ClusterScopeStmt`, `HierarchyScopeStmt`, `SpmdScopeStmt`) all express "wrap a body in a named runtime scope". Communication-domain construction is the obvious next sibling and currently the odd one out.

### Design

#### 1. New IR node: `CommDomainScopeStmt`

Clone `RuntimeScopeStmt`'s shape (`include/pypto/ir/stmt.h:950-972`). Inherits `ScopeStmt` (`body_`, `name_hint_`, `attrs_`, `leading_comments_`) and adds the two fields `CommGroup` carries today:

```cpp
class CommDomainScopeStmt : public ScopeStmt {
 public:
  std::vector<int64_t> devices_;        // empty = all devices (= *range(world_size))
  std::vector<WindowBufferPtr> slots_;  // alloc-order slots

  CommDomainScopeStmt(std::vector<int64_t> devices, std::vector<WindowBufferPtr> slots,
                      std::string name_hint, StmtPtr body, Span span, ...);

  ObjectKind GetKind() const override { return ObjectKind::CommDomainScopeStmt; }
  ScopeKind  GetScopeKind() const override { return ScopeKind::CommDomain; }
  std::string TypeName() const override { return "CommDomainScopeStmt"; }

  static constexpr auto GetFieldDescriptors() {
    return std::tuple_cat(ScopeStmt::GetFieldDescriptors(),
        std::make_tuple(reflection::UsualField(&CommDomainScopeStmt::devices_, "devices"),
                        reflection::UsualField(&CommDomainScopeStmt::slots_, "slots")));
  }
};
```

`name_hint_` is the handle base — codegen derives `__comm_d<n>`. `WindowBufferPtr` identity is preserved end-to-end: the same `shared_ptr<const WindowBuffer>` stays threaded through `DistributedTensorType::window_buffer_` (`include/pypto/ir/program.h:79`), so existing routing logic keeps working without an explicit map.

#### 2. Repurpose `CollectCommGroups` → `MaterializeCommDomainScopes`

The analysis (clustering by merged device descriptor, source-ordering) is unchanged. Only the **output** shape changes:

- **Before** (`src/ir/transforms/collect_comm_groups_pass.cpp:426`): rebuild `Program` with `comm_groups_` populated.
- **After**: rewrite each host-orchestrator function body as

  ```
  CommDomainScopeStmt(group 0)
    └── body: CommDomainScopeStmt(group 1)
                └── body: ... CommDomainScopeStmt(group N-1)
                              └── body: original function body
  ```

  Same outer-to-inner declaration order today's codegen emits, so generated `host_orch.py` is byte-identical.

Pipeline position stays (slot 36, before final `Simplify`). `IRProperty::CommGroupsCollected` → `IRProperty::CommDomainScopesMaterialized`.

#### 3. Distributed codegen migration

`src/codegen/distributed/distributed_codegen.cpp`:

- **Remove** `EmitCommDomainAllocations()` (lines 270-339) and the `with_blocks` indent-balancing in `EmitFunction` (lines 248-264).
- **Remove** the program-init `window_to_group_idx_` map (lines 79-84).
- **Add** `VisitStmt_(const CommDomainScopeStmtPtr&)` that emits the same text `EmitCommDomainAllocations` emits today — workers list, window-size sum, `CommBufferSpec(...)` per slot — then `IncreaseIndent()`, visit `op->body_`, `DecreaseIndent()`. Mirrors `RuntimeScopeStmt`'s handler in the orchestration codegen.
- **Replace** `GroupIdxForWindowBuffer()` (lines 131-138) with an in-codegen open-scope stack: push on entry, pop on exit; look up a `WindowBufferPtr` by scanning the stack inner-to-outer (nesting depth is small and bounded).
- Per-dispatch routing emit sites (lines 667-685, 719-727) switch from `HandleVarForGroup(GroupIdxForWindowBuffer(wb))` to a stack query (same `__comm_d<n>` output).

#### 4. Program cleanup

`include/pypto/ir/program.h`:

- Delete `class CommGroup` and `using CommGroupPtr` (lines 81-112).
- Delete `Program::comm_groups_` field (line 207), the two CommGroup-aware constructors (lines 141-146, 168-169), and the `comm_groups` descriptor in `GetFieldDescriptors` (line 201).
- Remove `ObjectKind::CommGroup` from `include/pypto/ir/kind_traits.h`; add `ObjectKind::CommDomainScopeStmt`.

Passes that thread `comm_groups_` through Program reconstruction (grep `comm_groups_` in `src/ir/transforms/`): drop those lines — `simplify_pass.cpp`, `expand_manual_phase_fence_pass.cpp`, `optimize_orch_tensors_pass.cpp`, `passes.cpp`.

#### 5. Python bindings, type stubs, printer, structural-equal

- `python/bindings/modules/ir.cpp`: drop `program.comm_groups` getter and `CommGroup` class binding; add `CommDomainScopeStmt` binding.
- `python/pypto/pypto_core/ir.pyi`: same surface deltas.
- `python/bindings/modules/passes.cpp` + `python/pypto/pypto_core/passes.pyi`: rename `collect_comm_groups` factory → `materialize_comm_domain_scopes`.
- `python/pypto/ir/pass_manager.py:172-181`: rename the pass entry.
- `src/ir/transforms/structural_equal.cpp`: add `EQUAL_DISPATCH(CommDomainScopeStmt)`; remove the `CommGroup` dispatch.
- `src/ir/transforms/python_printer.cpp`: add `VisitStmt_(const CommDomainScopeStmtPtr&)` that emits a **single leading comment** then descends into `op->body_` at the same indent (no `with` wrapper — it would have no parser surface). Comment format:

  ```
  # pld.comm_domain: devices=[0, 1], slots=[scratch, signal]
  ```

  (`devices=all` when the scope covers every rank.) Reparse produces pre-pass IR (the comment is dropped by the parser); pipeline re-run reconstructs the scope. Round-trip table:

  | Round-trip kind | Path | Works? |
  | --------------- | ---- | ------ |
  | `assert_structural_equal(post-pass A, post-pass B)` | in-memory reflection over stmt subtree, including `devices_` and `slots_` | yes — same as `RuntimeScopeStmt` |
  | Python source: post-pass IR → printer → file → parser → pipeline | printer emits the comment + body (no wrapper); parser drops the comment and produces pre-pass IR; pipeline re-runs `MaterializeCommDomainScopes` and rebuilds the same scope chain | yes — same contract today's `comm_groups_` uses |

- The IR msgpack `ir.serialize` / `ir.deserialize` API has no real consumer in this repo (grep guard) and remains a dead API; we do not need to teach it about `CommDomainScopeStmt` to land this refactor.

#### 6. Documentation

Rename `docs/en/dev/passes/36-collect_comm_groups.md` → `36-materialize_comm_domain_scopes.md` (and the `docs/zh-cn/` mirror). Rewrite to describe the new pass output and update the table in `.claude/rules/pass-doc-ordering.md`.

### Affected Files

**Add**

- `include/pypto/ir/stmt.h` — declare `CommDomainScopeStmt`
- `src/ir/transforms/materialize_comm_domain_scopes_pass.cpp` — replaces `collect_comm_groups_pass.cpp` (rename + rewrite output side)
- `docs/en/dev/passes/36-materialize_comm_domain_scopes.md` and `docs/zh-cn/` mirror

**Modify**

- `include/pypto/ir/program.h` — delete `CommGroup`, `comm_groups_`, the two CommGroup-aware ctors
- `include/pypto/ir/kind_traits.h` — swap `CommGroup` for `CommDomainScopeStmt`
- `include/pypto/ir/transforms/pass_properties.h` — rename `IRProperty::CommGroupsCollected`
- `src/codegen/distributed/distributed_codegen.cpp` / `.h` — remove metadata reader, add scope-stmt handler + open-scope stack
- `src/ir/transforms/python_printer.cpp` — handler for the new stmt
- `src/ir/transforms/structural_equal.cpp` — dispatch updates
- `src/ir/transforms/{simplify,expand_manual_phase_fence,optimize_orch_tensors}_pass.cpp`, `src/ir/transforms/passes.cpp` — drop `comm_groups_` threading
- `python/bindings/modules/{ir,passes}.cpp` — bindings
- `python/pypto/pypto_core/{ir,passes}.pyi` — stubs
- `python/pypto/ir/pass_manager.py` — entry name
- IR msgpack serializer/deserializer — drop optional `comm_groups`

### Testing Plan

1. **Pass-level unit tests** — `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_collect_comm_groups.py`: re-target assertions from `program.comm_groups` to the function-body scope chain (`func.body` is a `CommDomainScopeStmt` whose `body_` is either the next scope or the original body).
2. **Codegen golden** — `tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_host_orch_distributed.py`: assertions should pass byte-identically (strict-equivalence nesting).
3. **End-to-end on hardware** — `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_multi_group.py`, `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_put.py`: should pass unchanged.
4. **Round-trip** — `tests/ut/ir/parser/`: confirm `assert_structural_equal` works across the new stmt.
5. **Grep guard** — after the migration, `git grep -n 'comm_groups_'` should return zero matches outside the rename history; `git grep -n 'CommGroup\b'` should be empty.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Explicit user-facing DSL surface** (e.g. `with pld.comm_domain(devices=..., buffers=[...]):` that users write directly). Rejected for the initial refactor — it expands the surface area significantly (parser + builder + DSL class) and is not required to remove the program-level metadata. The implicit / pass-synthesized path keeps user code unchanged while still achieving the IR cleanup. The explicit DSL can be added later as a separate enhancement.
- **Tighter "actual lifetime" nesting** (sibling scopes when lifetimes don't overlap, instead of strict declaration-order nesting). Rejected for this refactor — within a single `Worker.run` the runtime defers `comm_release_domain_windows` to drain regardless of explicit `release()` timing, so tighter scoping yields no current runtime benefit. Strict equivalence keeps `host_orch.py` byte-identical. Tighter scoping becomes meaningful only if combined with a future "early drain" optimization, which is orthogonal.
- **Two ops (alloc op + release op) rather than one body-wrapping scope op**. Rejected — the `with`-semantics of the runtime API is naturally body-wrapping, and PyPTO already has the `ScopeStmt` family precedent (`RuntimeScopeStmt`, `SpmdScopeStmt`, etc.) for exactly this shape.

### Rollout / Migration

Phased delivery, one PR per phase, each independently buildable:

1. **Phase A ** — Add `CommDomainScopeStmt` IR node end-to-end (header, kind_traits, structural-equal, reflection, visitor/mutator base, transparent-with-comment printer, Python binding, type stub). Pure addition; no producer or consumer yet. Build green.
2. **Phase B** — Repurpose the pass to ALSO wrap host_orch body in scope stmts (dual-write with `comm_groups_` for safety).
3. **Phase C** — `DistributedCodegen` visitor + open-scope stack consumes scope stmts; remove `EmitCommDomainAllocations`.
4. **Phase D** — Remove `Program::comm_groups_`, `CommGroup`, `ObjectKind::CommGroup`, and the threading in other passes.
5. **Phase E** — Clean CommGroup binding/stub, update IR msgpack serializer/deserializer.
6. **Phase F** — Port unit tests, rename docs (en + zh-cn), update `.claude/rules/pass-doc-ordering.md`.
7. **Phase G** — Run unit + st tests; grep guard for residual `comm_groups` references.

User DSL is unchanged throughout. Generated `host_orch.py` is byte-identical after Phase C (strict-equivalence nesting). No downstream consumer of the IR msgpack format exists, so dropping its `comm_groups` field is not user-visible.

### Open Questions

- Should the open-scope stack lookup live on the visitor base (reusable by future scope kinds) or be local to `DistributedCodegen`? Leaning local for now since no other consumer exists; revisit if a second scope-aware codegen path appears.
- Should the `name_hint_` for synthesized scopes follow a convention (e.g. `comm_d0`, `comm_d1`) so dumps are stable across runs, or be left empty (codegen derives `__comm_d<n>` from visit order)? Leaning convention-based for dump stability.
- Should we keep `CollectCommGroups` as the public pass name (Python factory) and only rename internally? Leaning rename to `materialize_comm_domain_scopes` for symmetry with `materialize_runtime_scopes` (slot 37), but flagging as a public-API rename.

title: [Feature] Support tensor-level ops (slice / assemble / slice-assign) on local access of a pld.DistributedTensor window
body:
### Summary

Tensor-level ops reject a `pld.DistributedTensor` (window) operand, so the only way to access window data is the tile-level `pl.load` / `pl.store`. Concretely:

- `pl.slice(win, ...)` / `win[i:i+1, :]` → `tensor.slice requires first argument to be a TensorType, but got DistributedTensorType`
- `pl.assemble(win_view, src, off)` likewise needs a `TensorType`
- so a window can only be read/written through `pl.tile.load` / `pl.tile.store`

A `pld.DistributedTensor` is backed by local GM on each rank; a *local* (own-rank) read/write of it is just a GM access. It would be useful to let the tensor-level slice / assemble / slice-assign ops accept a `DistributedTensor` for local access (treating it as its local GM tensor), the same way they accept a plain `pl.Tensor`.

### Motivation / Use Case

In dsv4 EP-MoE (`models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py`), the cross-rank dispatch/combine kernels stage data through HCCL window scratch. The single-card `dispatch` / `combine` express their scatter/gather with tensor-level idioms — `recv_x_flat = pl.assemble(recv_x_flat, pl.slice(x_norm_i8, [1, D], [t, 0]), [dst, 0])` and `routed_y_buf_flat[dst:dst+1, :] = recv_y_flat[i:i+1, :]`. The EP variants can't reuse those idioms on the window: every window access has to go through `pl.tile.load` / `pl.tile.store` instead.

This matters in two situations:

1. **Pure staging / copies through a window.** A window→host copy (or a reshape-and-row-store of a window) is forced through tile load+store even when no compute is involved. Combined with `ConvertTensorToTileOps`, a `pl.tile.store` to a *reshaped* output view inside a `pl.at(CORE_GROUP)` scope tile-loads the whole output into Vec (separate problem), whereas a tensor-level `assemble`/slice-assign would not.

2. **Trying to express these kernels with tensor-level ops.** When attempting to author the EP combine reduce (read `routed_y_buf` window + `sh` → `ffn_out`) or the EP dispatch stage-out with slice/assemble, the window read immediately fails with the `DistributedTensorType` rejection, so the whole tensor-level path is unavailable and one must fall back to `pl.load` + a `pl.cast` tile + `pl.store`.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Allow `tensor.slice`, `tensor.assemble`, and slice-assign (`dst[...] = src`) to accept a `pld.DistributedTensor` operand for **local** (own-rank) access, lowering it to an op on the window's local GM tensor — i.e. `win[i:i+1, :]` reads the local copy, `win_flat[i:i+1, :] = src_tensor` writes the local copy. Cross-rank access stays via the existing `pld.tile.remote_store` / `pld.tensor.put` / `pld.tensor.get` APIs.

### Additional Context

pypto `89698531`. Surfaced while exploring whether the dsv4 EP dispatch/combine InCore kernels can be authored as `@pl.jit.inline` (they can't, for separate reasons). Related: #1670 (window write→read ordering across kernels).
