title: feat(language): expose pl.scatter as top-level alias for pl.tensor.scatter
body:
## What

Promote the tensor-level `scatter` op to the top-level `pl` namespace so users can write `pl.scatter(...)` instead of the fully-qualified `pl.tensor.scatter(...)` — mirroring the existing `pl.gather` and `pl.scatter_update` top-level aliases.

## Why

`pl.tensor.scatter` is the only one of the column gather/scatter family that lacked a top-level shorthand. `pl.gather` and `pl.scatter_update` are already promoted, so this brings `scatter` in line and shortens the common call site.

## Changes

- **`python/pypto/language/__init__.py`** — import `scatter` from `tensor_ops` and add `"scatter"` to `__all__`, alongside `scatter_update`. `scatter` is already exported from `tensor_ops.__all__`, so this is a pure re-export; both overloads (index form and mask form) are preserved.
- **`tests/st/runtime/ops/test_scatter.py`** — add `scatter_alias_mask_p0101`, an ST case that drives the runnable mask-form scatter path through the new `pl.scatter` alias, pinning that it resolves to the identical `pl.tensor.scatter` op. Placed on the mask-form path (A2/A3) since the index-form suite is currently skipped behind the upstream PTOAS bug.

## Testing

- Pre-commit (pyright + ruff) passes.
- The new ST case runs the alias through the same lowering/device path as the existing `scatter_mask_p0101` case.

title: [Bug] Orchestration cross-assigns __ssa_v aliases for multiple in-place outputs of an inlined InCore scope
body:
### Component
Codegen

### Description
When an `@pl.jit.inline` kernel is inlined into a `@pl.jit` caller and writes
several output tensors **in place inside one `pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP)`
(= ScopeStmt InCore) scope via tile `pl.store`**, those tensors are classified
`add_inout`, and the orchestration codegen emits post-write SSA aliases
(`<name>__ssa_v1`) that are **cross-assigned to the wrong source tensors**.
Downstream consumers then read a completely unrelated tensor — a silent
miscompile producing NaN/Inf and a runtime 507018 (AICPU chip fault).

This is the same cross-assignment class as the (closed) #1573, but a distinct
trigger: #1573 is about 3+ outer-loop **carries** (`__phi` nodes) in a
`pl.parallel`/`pl.range` loop; here there is no loop carry — they are plain
in-place outputs of an inlined kernel, and the scrambled aliases are `__ssa_v1`,
not `__phi`. It still reproduces on current `main` (0ac36c0f, which includes
#1573's closure).

### Steps to Reproduce
In pypto-lib, convert `dispatch_ep` in `models/deepseek/v4/dispatch.py` from
`@pl.jit.incore` to `@pl.jit.inline`, writing the recv_*_out outputs in place
inside one `pl.at(CORE_GROUP)` scope, with `recv_scale_out` / `recv_w_out`
written via tile `pl.store` (TROWSUM form). Then:

    python models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py -d 0,1   # 2-rank EP, 2 NPUs

`recv_scale_out` and `recv_w_out` are `[N_LOCAL, RECV_MAX]` FP32; both written
via tile `pl.store` of full rows -> classified `add_inout`.

### Expected Behavior
Each in-place output's post-write alias references itself, e.g.:

    recv_scale_out__ssa_v1 = recv_scale_out;
    recv_w_out__ssa_v1     = recv_w_out;

### Actual Behavior
Generated `next_levels/moe_ep/orchestration/moe_ep.cpp`:

    // Task 12: dispatch_ep  (params add_inout recv_scale_out, recv_w_out, ...)
    ...
    const Tensor& recv_w_out__ssa_v1   = recv_count_out;   // WRONG (int32 count)
    const Tensor& recv_scale_out__ssa_v1 = ext_recv_x;     // WRONG (FP16 recv_x window)
    ...
    params_t13.add_input(recv_scale_out__ssa_v1);   // exp_gate_up dequant reads recv_x window
    params_t15.add_input(recv_w_out__ssa_v1);       // exp_w2 reads recv_count_out

-> expert_routed dequant reads garbage -> x_next NaN=246680 Inf=1126612, or
RuntimeError 507018. The kernel<->call arg order is otherwise consistent
(verified e.g. v2 = pub_counts). Outputs written write-only via scalar
`pl.write` are classified `add_output`, get no `__ssa_v1`, and are read
correctly via the original handle — that is the current workaround
(recv_count_out / recv_r_route_out always did this).

### Git Commit ID
0ac36c0f

### NPU Kind
Ascend 910B

### Host Platform
Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context
Related: #1573 (loop-carry __phi scramble, closed), #1463 / #1390 (out-window
multi-output alias collisions), #1580 (phi naming swap). Surfaced converting
dsv4 EP dispatch_ep/combine_ep to `@pl.jit.inline` (enabled by #1670 + #1685).
Environment: pypto 0ac36c0f, runtime 48980572, ptoas 0.43, pto-isa 8bd3ac8f.

title: [Pass Bug] ConvertTensorToTileOps rejects a DistributedTensor (window) slice inside an InCore scope
body:
### Pass Name
ConvertTensorToTileOps

### Description
#1685/#1672 made `tensor.slice` / `assemble` / slice-assign accept a
`pld.DistributedTensor` (window) for local access at the tensor/type level. But
ConvertTensorToTileOps still rejects a window slice when it appears **inside an
InCore scope** (`pl.at(CORE_GROUP)`), so the assemble idiom can't be used for
window staging copies inside an InCore kernel — one must fall back to
`pl.load`/`pl.store` (tiles) or scalar `pl.read`/`pl.write`.

### Git Commit ID
0ac36c0f

### Before IR (Input)
A slice-assign copying column 0 of a padded window into an output column,
authored inside an InCore scope:

    # recv_scale: pld.DistributedTensor[[N_LOCAL*RECV_MAX, W_PAD], pl.FP32] (window)
    # recv_scale_out_flat: pl.Tensor[[N_LOCAL*RECV_MAX, 1], pl.FP32]
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="dispatch_ep"):
        ...
        recv_scale_out_flat[:, :] = recv_scale[:, 0:1]   # window slice (local read)

### Expected IR (After Transformation)
The local window slice lowers like a plain `Tensor` slice (the window is local
GM on this rank), producing a valid tile/GM copy — the same way the op is
accepted at the tensor/type level after #1685.

### Actual IR or Error

    pypto.InternalError: tensor.slice conversion: unexpected input type: DistributedTensorType
      at models/deepseek/v4/dispatch.py:291:8
    Check failed: unreachable at src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp:307
      File "src/ir/transforms/convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp", line 1777
      File "src/ir/transforms/convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp", line 1321

Moving the same slice-assign OUTSIDE the InCore scope (to orchestration level)
compiles, but then produces wrong values at runtime (the orchestration lowers it
to `ext_recv_scale.view([M,1],[0,0])` + copy; appears to mishandle the strided
column view / ordering) — likely a separate, related gap worth noting.

### NPU Kind (if relevant)
Ascend 910B

### Host Platform (if relevant)
Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context
Related: #1672 / #1685 (closed; enabled window local tensor ops at the type
level), #1670 (window write->read ordering), #1693 (the multi-output SSA
scramble found in the same conversion). Surfaced converting dsv4 dispatch_ep to
`@pl.jit.inline`. Environment: pypto 0ac36c0f, ptoas 0.43, pto-isa 8bd3ac8f.

title: feat(distributed): runtime-bound SubWorker callbacks via `...` body
body:
## Summary

Makes a HOST `SubWorker` declared with a `...` body an explicit **runtime-bound callback point**. Its implementation is supplied at `compiled.prepare(callbacks={...})` rather than captured at compile time — for closures that need live runtime state (sampling, host-side inspection) and previously had to be smuggled in as a generated placeholder + silent name-based override.

### Before

```python
@pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.SubWorker)
def sample(logits: pl.Tensor[[B, V], pl.FP32]) -> pl.Tensor[[B], pl.INT32]:
    return torch.argmax(logits, dim=-1)   # placeholder body, silently replaced at runtime

with compiled.prepare(sub_worker_overrides={"sample": real_sampler}) as rt:  # optional, name-string only
    ...
```

### After

```python
@pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.SubWorker)
def sample(logits: pl.Tensor[[B, V], pl.FP32]) -> pl.Tensor[[B], pl.INT32]:
    ...   # abstract: implementation bound at runtime

with compiled.prepare(callbacks={"sample": real_sampler}) as rt:  # required; missing → ValueError
    ...
```

## What changed

- **IR**: new `Function.requires_runtime_binding_` field. Reflected, so it round-trips through `.pto` serialization and the Python printer (which re-emits the `...` body). A bare `pass` body stays a concrete no-op SubWorker.
- **Parser**: detects a `...`-only SubWorker body and sets the flag (threaded through the builder → `BeginFunction` → `Function` ctor).
- **Codegen**: emits a guard stub that raises if the callback is dispatched unbound (instead of silently no-op'ing), plus a `sub_workers/__required__.json` manifest listing abstract names.
- **Runtime**: `prepare(callbacks=...)` enforces binding — a missing required callback raises `ValueError` at prepare time, not at dispatch; callback arity is validated. `sub_worker_overrides=` kept as a deprecated alias.
- **Docs**: new "Abstract (runtime-bound) SubWorkers" section in `docs/{en,zh-cn}/dev/ir/01-hierarchy.md`.
- **Example**: `examples/runtime/distributed_callback.py`.

## Testing

- `tests/ut/codegen/test_distributed_codegen.py`: abstract detection, `pass`-is-not-abstract, printer round-trip, `.pto` serialization round-trip, guard-stub emission.
- `tests/ut/runtime/test_distributed_worker.py`: rewrote override/merge coverage onto the `callbacks` API; added missing-required, arity, and deprecated-alias cases.
- Broad `tests/ut` sweep green (pre-existing unrelated `Worker.current` mock failures aside).

title: fix(codegen): rewrite lane1 tile.slice to tile.create in SplitVectorKernel (fixes #1649)
body:
## Summary

Slicing sub-columns of a matmul output's vector epilogue failed device codegen (#1649). After #1636 fixed the ptoas non-mat `tmov` rejection, the repro surfaced a downstream **ccec** failure:

```
no matching member function for call to 'GetValidRow'/'GetValidCol'
```

## Root cause

`SplitVectorKernel` splits the AIV kernel into a real lane and a zero **replay** lane, whose tiles run as empty (`valid_shape=0`) no-ops to keep the cross-core `tpush`/`tpop`/`tfree` handshakes balanced. For a `tile.slice` it injected an explicit **static** `valid_shape=[0,0]`, which codegen lowers to a `v_row=0, v_col=0` subview.

ptoas accepts that, but pto-isa's `Tile::GetValidRow`/`GetValidCol` only have overloads for a static mask `> 0` or `DYNAMIC` — never `0` — so ccec cannot instantiate an op over the static-zero subview. Sibling non-subview replay tiles survive because codegen always renders their valid as dynamic `?`; only the subview (which #1636 made honor explicit valid) breaks.

## Fix

`tile.slice` is a pure view with no cross-core sync side effect, so the replay lane only needs an empty tile of the slice's result shape. Rewrite it to `tile.create` — mirroring the existing `tile.load -> tile.create` replay rewrite. `tile.create` renders with **dynamic** valid (runtime 0), which ccec compiles and which runs as a no-op, matching the sibling replay tiles. The now-unused `MakeZeroTuple`/`MakeZeroTupleLike` helpers are removed.

### Generated `.pto` (zero lane), before → after

Before — static-zero subview, rejected by ccec:
```
%9 = pto.subview %4[0,0] sizes [16,8] valid [%c0, %c0] : ...v_row=?,v_col=? -> ...rows=16,cols=8, v_row=0, v_col=0
pto.tmuls ins(%9 : v_row=0, v_col=0) outs(%6 : v_row=?,v_col=?)
```

After — dynamic-valid empty tile, compiles cleanly:
```
%5 = pto.alloc_tile ... rows=16,cols=8, v_row=?, v_col=?
pto.tmuls ins(%5 : v_row=?, v_col=?) outs(%6 : v_row=?, v_col=?)
```

The real lane is unchanged (`%slice_view = pto.subview ... v_row=16, v_col=8`).

## Tests

- **ST** `tests/st/codegen/dsl/test_subview_tmov_valid_shape.py` — end-to-end `matmul -> vec epilogue -> sub-column slice -> elementwise` (the #1649 repro). Passes on a2a3 device.
- **UT** `test_no_split_dual_dispatch_rewrites_lane1_tile_slice_to_create` — asserts the lane1 `tile.slice` is rewritten to a dynamic-valid `tile.create`.

title: [Bug] Orchestration codegen does not hoist a manual_scope-internal tensor's SSA alias, breaking after-scope readers ("was not declared in this scope")
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

The orchestration C++ codegen emits a tensor's SSA-versioned `const Tensor&` alias at the **current indentation** — i.e. inside the deep `PTO2_SCOPE(MANUAL) { ... }` block when the producing write is inside a `pl.manual_scope` — with **no live-out / hoisting analysis**. When a task placed **after** the `manual_scope` reads that tensor, the generated `add_input(<name>__ssa_v<N>)` is emitted at the outer indent and references the now-out-of-scope alias, so the orchestration `.cpp` fails to C++-compile:

```
error: '<name>__ssa_v<N>' was not declared in this scope
```

This blocks any optimization that moves a consumer of a `manual_scope` `pl.assemble` output to after the scope (e.g. fusing an MLP-tail residual-add / `down_cast_residual`-style writer into an after-scope auto-dep writer).

Atomic/inout tensors are unaffected: their producer-call alias is bound in the outer function body (atomic-add does not mint a deep downstream SSA version), so the after-scope reader resolves to an outer alias. A plain (non-atomic) `pl.assemble` inside the scope mints a new SSA version aliased at deep indent, which dies when the block closes.

**Why it is easy to miss:** `compile_for_test` / `--smoke` generate the orchestration `.cpp` but do **not** C++-compile it, so they pass. The error only surfaces when the `.cpp` is C++-compiled — i.e. a real device dispatch / orchestration C++ build.

Related: #1693 (orchestration codegen `__ssa_v` alias cross-assignment).

### Steps to Reproduce

Self-contained minimal repro (`repro_manual_scope_hoist.py`): a tensor created **before** `pl.manual_scope`, written **inside** it, read by a `pl.at` task **after** it.

```python
import torch
import pypto.language as pl
from pypto.backend import BackendType, set_backend_type
from pypto.runtime import RunConfig

M, N = 16, 256

@pl.jit
def repro(x: pl.Tensor, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    acc = pl.create_tensor([M, N], dtype=pl.FP32)  # atomic-written  (works)
    buf = pl.create_tensor([M, N], dtype=pl.FP32)  # plain-assemble-written (breaks)
    tids = pl.array.create(1, pl.TASK_ID)           # hoisted outside manual_scope (correct usage)

    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="seed") as seed_tid:
        acc = pl.assemble(acc, pl.full([M, N], dtype=pl.FP32, value=0.0), [0, 0])

    with pl.manual_scope():
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="producer", deps=[seed_tid]) as ptid:
            acc = pl.assemble(acc, pl.full([M, N], dtype=pl.FP32, value=1.0), [0, 0], atomic=pl.AtomicType.Add)
            buf = pl.assemble(buf, pl.slice(x, [M, N], [0, 0]), [0, 0])
        tids[0] = ptid

    # AFTER manual_scope: read both acc (atomic, OK) and buf (assemble, bug)
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="consumer", deps=[tids[0]]):
        out = pl.assemble(out, pl.add(pl.slice(acc, [M, N], [0, 0]), pl.slice(buf, [M, N], [0, 0])), [0, 0])
    return out

if __name__ == "__main__":
    set_backend_type(BackendType.Ascend910B)
    x = torch.randn(M, N, dtype=torch.float32); out = torch.zeros(M, N, dtype=torch.float32)
    repro.compile_for_test(x, out)   # PASSES — generates .cpp but does NOT C++-compile it
    cfg = RunConfig(platform="a2a3", device_id=0, backend_type=BackendType.Ascend910B)
    repro(x, out, config=cfg)        # FAILS at the orchestration C++ compile (host-side, before device use)
```

Run: `PYTHONPATH=python python repro_manual_scope_hoist.py`

The generated `repro.cpp` declares `acc__ssa_v2` / `buf__ssa_v1` **inside** the `PTO2_SCOPE(MANUAL) {` block, while the `consumer` task reads them at the outer indent after the block closes.

### Expected Behavior

The orchestration `.cpp` should C++-compile. A tensor created before a `manual_scope`, written inside it, and read by a task after the scope must have its `const Tensor&` alias visible (hoisted) at the after-scope reader — the same way atomic/inout tensors already are.

### Actual Behavior

```
RuntimeError: Orchestration compilation failed with exit code 1:
repro.cpp:68:29: error: 'acc__ssa_v2' was not declared in this scope
         params_t2.add_input(acc__ssa_v2);
repro.cpp:69:29: error: 'buf__ssa_v1' was not declared in this scope
         params_t2.add_input(buf__ssa_v1);
```

(In the real decode_layer fusion the failure was `'post_norm_partial_inline289__rv_v14' was not declared in this scope`; `down_acc_all` — atomic — compiled fine.)

### Git Commit ID

3f421313f02777267cdd48ba1e134e51ecf03b9e

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

**Root cause** (`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`):
- `EmitTensorAlias` (line 2417) emits `const Tensor& <name>__ssa_v<N> = ...;` at **line 2424** using the current `Indent()` — the deep manual_scope block — with no hoisting.
- `VisitStmt_(RuntimeScopeStmtPtr)` (lines 792-821) is the C++ `{ }` scope boundary the alias cannot escape.
- The after-scope reader's `add_input(...)` (`GenerateFunctionCallCode`, ~line 2201) names the out-of-scope alias.
- Same duplicate emit at line 2670 (`GenerateSubmitReturnAliases`).

**Suggested fix:** in `EmitTensorAlias` (and line 2670), when `mutable_tensor_name_scopes_.size() > 1` (inside a nested scope), buffer the `const Tensor& <alias> = <out_name>;` and flush it at function-body scope (after `SetInitialIndent`, ~line 3036) instead of at the deep indent — with a hoisted pointer-holder fallback when `out_name` is not itself body-scope-valid. Alias names are already globally unique (`ReserveUniqueName`). Read-only views, so no semantic change; needs golden `.cpp`/`.pto` updates + an orchestration-codegen test re-run to confirm the atomic path is unchanged.

title: Support multi-program dispatch for DistributedCompiledProgram
body:
## Feature request

`DistributedCompiledProgram` should support a multi-program runtime/worker flow so several compiled HOST programs can be prepared on one L3 worker and dispatched independently while sharing the same child process and device-resident memory.

Reference implementation PR: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/1699

## Motivation

Serving-style generation needs to dispatch Qwen3 prefill and decode JIT HOST programs through the same L3 worker. Prefill writes the KV cache and decode consumes/updates the same KV cache, so the runtime needs one shared worker lifecycle and one worker-resident `DeviceTensor` KV cache across multiple compiled programs.

Without first-class multi-program support, callers must either create a worker per compiled program, which loses shared device-resident state, or fall back to host-backed KV buffers, which adds expensive host/device traffic and degrades decode throughput.

## Desired behavior

- Allow multiple `DistributedCompiledProgram` objects with compatible distributed configs to be prepared on the same L3 worker.
- Register each program's chip callables, sub-worker functions, orchestration entry, base tensors, and parameter metadata independently.
- Provide an API like `worker.run(compiled_program, *args)` that dispatches a selected program on the shared worker.
- Preserve existing single-program behavior and `worker(*args)` compatibility for the primary program.
- Keep worker-resident `DeviceTensor` inputs valid across dispatches from different programs.

## Constraints / validation

Compatible programs should use the same platform, runtime, and device ids. The reference PR implements this by validating compatibility, keeping per-program dispatch state, and preserving single-program compatibility.

title: fix(ir): add UnrollResolved verifier and elevate codegen fallbacks to hard checks
body:
## Summary

Replace silent `LOG_WARN` fallbacks in both codegen backends with hard `INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN` assertions, and add an `UnrollResolved` property verifier so the pass pipeline catches the root cause — stale `ForKind::Unroll`
markers — before they reach codegen.

The key insight: `ForKind::Unroll` is a compile-time-only marker. The only pass that expands it into `SeqStmts` is `UnrollLoops` (pass 2). After pass 2, no downstream pass ever expands `ForKind::Unroll` — chunked Unroll loops that survived carried a stale marker. UnrollLoops (pass 2) expands non-chunked Unroll loops into SeqStmts; SplitChunkedLoops (pass 7) demotes chunked Unroll → Sequential. Together they form the complete resolution chain. Before this fix, they reached codegen where the old `LOG_WARN` fallback generated a sequential `for` loop — the exact same C++ as `ForKind::Sequential`. The IR kind was a lie; runtime behavior
was always Sequential. This fix makes the IR honestly reflect what the generated code actually does. **Zero runtime change.**

## Changes

### 1. SplitChunkedLoops now demotes `ForKind::Unroll` → `Sequential`

`SplitChunkedLoops` (pass 7) decomposes chunked loops into nested ForStmts. Previously it copied `ForKind::Unroll` onto the generated inner/outer loops, leaving stale markers that no downstream pass would ever expand. Now it
demotes `ForKind::Unroll` to `Sequential` via a `DemoteUnrollKind()` helper applied at all 10 ForStmt construction sites across all 4 split methods (LeadingFull, LeadingFullWithIterArgs, Guarded, GuardedWithIterArgs).

### 2. `UnrollResolved` property on `kSplitChunkedLoopsProperties`

A new `UnrollResolvedPropertyVerifier` fires if any `ForKind::Unroll` survives past `SplitChunkedLoops`. The property is declared on `kSplitChunkedLoopsProperties.produced` (not `kUnrollLoopsProperties`),
because chunked Unroll loops are resolved by `SplitChunkedLoops`, not `UnrollLoops`.

### 3. Codegen: `LOG_WARN` → `INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN`

Both `orchestration_codegen.cpp` and `pto_control_flow_codegen.cpp` now hard-fail with an actionable message (naming the responsible passes) when `ForKind::Unroll` or `ForKind::Pipeline` reach codegen.

### Files changed

| Layer | Files |
|-------|-------|
| Pass logic | `split_chunked_loops_pass.cpp` — `DemoteUnrollKind()` helper, 10 call sites |
| Verifier | `verify_unroll_resolved.cpp` (new), `ir_property.h/.cpp`, `pass_properties.h`, `verifier.h`, `property_verifier_registry.cpp`, `CMakeLists.txt` |
| Codegen | `orchestration_codegen.cpp`, `pto_control_flow_codegen.cpp` |
| Bindings | `passes.cpp` (nanobind), `passes.pyi` (type stub) |
| Docs | `07-split_chunked_loops.md` (EN + ZH-CN) |
| Tests | `test_split_chunked_loops.py` — `test_unroll_chunk` expects `Sequential` |


1. **Producer side**: `SplitChunkedLoops` demotes `ForKind::Unroll` → `Sequential`
   and declares `UnrollResolved` as produced; verifier catches any stragglers.
2. **Consumer side**: Codegen asserts no `Unroll`/`Pipeline` loops survive as a
   final safety net with actionable error messages.

title: feat(ir): Add opt-in AUTO-scope task dependency derivation
body:

title: [Bug] Orchestration codegen aliases a multi-output spmd scope's return value to the wrong output tensor (out_indices[0] fallback) -> numel-mismatched reshape -> 507018
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

When a fanned-out `pl.spmd` scope writes **multiple** GM output tensors and the
function's return value is one of the **non-first** outputs, the orchestration
codegen aliases the scope's returned SSA value to the **wrong** output tensor.
Downstream the wrong tensor is reshaped to the return shape; because the two
tensors have different element counts, the AICPU runtime hits
`debug_assert(valid_reshape(...))` (`runtime/.../runtime/tensor.h:435`,
`valid_reshape() = numel()==product(new_shapes)`). The asserting executor thread
aborts that subtask, it never writes FIN, the producer task never reaches
COMPLETED, its consumers' fan-in never closes, the scheduler latches the
GLOBAL_STUCK timeout (`sched_error_code=100`), and the host surfaces it as
`aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018`. A kernel-side shape
bug thus masquerades as a scheduler deadlock.

**Root cause (pinned):** `GenerateSingleReturnAlias`
(`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:2446`):

```cpp
auto returned_idx = FindReturnedParamIndex(callee, program_);
size_t param_idx = returned_idx.value_or(out_indices[0]);  // <-- falls back to FIRST output
EmitTensorAlias(var_name, call, param_idx);
```

For a multi-output `pl.spmd` scope, `FindReturnedParamIndex` returns `nullopt`
(a Spmd wrapper has no traceable top-level `ReturnStmt`), so `param_idx` falls
back to `out_indices[0]` = the **first** Out/InOut arg — but the actually
returned value is a **later** output. The returned SSA value should instead be
aliased to the output arg that shares its SSA base / buffer root.

This is the same **class** as #1573 (closed) and #1693, but a distinct trigger
and code path: #1573 is `__phi` loop carries; #1693 is `__ssa_v1` in-place
outputs of an inlined `pl.at(CORE_GROUP)` InCore scope; **this** is the
`__rv_v` *return-value* alias of a `pl.spmd` scope via the
`GenerateSingleReturnAlias` `out_indices[0]` fallback.

Related: #1693, #1573, #1650, #631

### Steps to Reproduce

In pypto-lib, take the DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre` kernel fused into **3** `pl.spmd`
scopes where the **second** scope (`hc_post`) writes three GM outputs in one
fanned-out spmd task — `pre_val_gm` (inout), `post` (inout), and `x_mixed`
(output, the function's return) — e.g. `hc_pre_fused_draft.py` with `mix_x`
fused into `hc_post`. The function ends with
`x_mixed = pl.reshape(x_mixed_view, [B, S, D]); return x_mixed`.

```
python models/deepseek/v4/repro_hc_pre_blocker2_selfraw_507018.py -p a2a3
```

(Real `FLASH` config: T=128, D=4096, HC_DIM=16384, MIX_HC=24. Run via
`task-submit` on an a2a3 device; the kernel compiles cleanly and deadlocks at
runtime with 507018.)

The 4-spmd variant (mix_x as its **own** scope, so `x_mixed` is that scope's
sole output) passes — confirming the trigger is the multi-output scope, not the
data flow.

### Expected Behavior

The scope's returned SSA value aliases to the output arg it is actually a new
SSA version of:

```cpp
const Tensor& x_mixed_view_inline52__rv_v2 = x_mixed_view_inline52;   // the x_mixed output
```

### Actual Behavior

Generated `orchestration/hc_pre_test.cpp` (multi-output `hc_post` Submit):

```cpp
// hc_post Submit outputs:
params_t1.add_inout(pre_val_gm_inline83);      // [2]  shape [128, 8]   numel = 1024
params_t1.add_inout(post_2d_inline73);         // [3]
params_t1.add_output(x_mixed_view_inline52);   // [4]  shape [128, 4096]  (== x_mixed)
rt_submit_aiv_task(2, params_t1);

const Tensor& x_mixed_view_inline52__rv_v2 = pre_val_gm_inline83;     // WRONG: aliased to output [2]

uint32_t x_mixed_v1_inline4_shapes[3] = {64, 2, 4096};               // numel = 524288
Tensor x_mixed_v1_inline4 = x_mixed_view_inline52__rv_v2.reshape(x_mixed_v1_inline4_shapes, 3);
```

`pre_val_gm` is `[128, 8]` (numel 1024); reshaping it to `[64, 2, 4096]`
(numel 524288) fails `valid_reshape` → AICPU subtask abort → scheduler
GLOBAL_STUCK → host `507018` (`sched_error_code=100 runtime_status=-100`).

Device log (a2a3, two independent task-submit-locked runs):

```
[ERROR] AICPU ... assert_impl "Assertion failed: valid_reshape(new_shapes, new_ndims)"
[ERROR] AICPU ... "Location: runtime/.../tensormap_and_ringbuffer/runtime/tensor.h:435"
        Stack: AicpuExecutor::run -> aicpu_execute -> simpler_aicpu_exec
```

### Git Commit ID

3f421313 (pypto, branch main)

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Fix direction: in `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` (and the analogous tuple/Submit
paths), map the returned SSA result to the output arg sharing its SSA
base/buffer root, instead of the `out_indices[0]` fallback when
`FindReturnedParamIndex` is empty for a Group/Spmd wrapper. See
`.claude/rules/pass-submit-awareness.md` (Submit tuple-return aliasing).

Two secondary observations surfaced while diagnosing this:

1. **Diagnosability:** an AICPU-side `debug_assert(valid_reshape)` aborts the
   subtask silently and the failure only appears as a scheduler 507018/507046
   stream-sync timeout. Printing `numel()` / `new_shapes` / `new_ndims` /
   `kernel_id` at `tensor.h:435` (and latching a distinct error code instead of
   GLOBAL_STUCK when an executor subtask aborts) would point straight at the
   kernel instead of looking like a scheduler deadlock.

2. **Latent (separate):** `next_block_idx` is a non-atomic `int16_t` mutated by a
   concurrent read-modify-write across scheduler threads
   (`scheduler_dispatch.cpp:311-318`) — a real data race at `aicpu_thread_num>1`,
   though it is NOT this failure (the dispatch trace shows all blocks dispatched).

title: fix(passes): lower window (DistributedTensor) slice/compute inside InCore scopes
body:
## Summary

`ConvertTensorToTileOps` rejected a `pld.DistributedTensor` (window) slice / slice-assign that appears **inside an InCore scope** (`pl.at(CORE_GROUP)`), crashing with:

```
pypto.InternalError: tensor.slice conversion: unexpected input type: DistributedTensorType
  Check failed: unreachable at src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp:307
```

#1685/#1672 made `tensor.slice` / `assemble` accept a window at the type level, but the **conversion lambdas** and the **elementwise type deducers** still gated on the exact `As<TensorType>()` kind, which misses the `DistributedTensorType` subclass (own `ObjectKind`). So the window-staging idiom couldn't be used in an InCore kernel — one had to fall back to tile-level `pl.load` / `pl.store`.

## Fix

Inside an InCore scope a window is just this rank's local GM, so its slice / slice-assign / elementwise use must lower exactly like a plain tensor. Swap the exact `As<TensorType>()` gates for `AsTensorTypeLike()` (matches `TensorType` **and** `DistributedTensorType`):

- **`op_conversion_registry.cpp`** — `tensor.slice` → `tile.load` (slice input), `tensor.assemble` → `tile.store` (assemble target + staged source). A window now lowers to a local `tile.load` / `tile.store`.
- **`tensor_ops/unary.cpp` + `elementwise.cpp`** — `cast` / `neg` / `abs` / `exp` / `add` / `sub` / `maximum` / `minimum` / `cmp` / ... type deducers accept a window operand. The result stays a plain `TensorType` — an elementwise op writes fresh local data, **not** a window view (so no DTT-preserving rebuild, unlike slice/assemble).

The conversion side of cast/add needs no change: by the time it runs, the slice's own lambda has already remapped the window to a tile.

Net effect: dsv4 `dispatch_ep` / `combine_ep` can stage and reduce a window at tensor level (slice + cast + add + slice-assign) instead of dropping the whole reduce to tile level.

## Tests

- **UT** `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.py::TestWindowSliceIncoreConversion` (5): window-as-source slice, window-as-target slice-assign, direct window slice, cast on a window slice, and the full `combine_ep` `sh + cast(window)` reduce. Verified to reproduce the exact crash without the fix.
- **Distributed ST** `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_window_slice_incore.py` (3): window-as-source (`dispatch_ep`), window-as-target (`combine_ep` staging), and the compute reduce — validating runtime values on device.

Local regression sweep (conversion + operators + op-validation + unified-ops + #1685 polymorphism): 793 passed.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The orchestration-level workaround for a window column slice lowers to `Tensor::view([M,1],[0,0])`, which mishandles the strided column view and gives wrong runtime values. Now that the in-core path works, that workaround should be deleted in the `combine_ep` orchestrator rather than relied on (separate cleanup).

Fixes #1694

title: fix(codegen): consume extern "C" prefix in ptoas output preprocessing
body:
## Summary

PTOAS was updated and now emits non-mixed-kernel functions with an `extern "C"` prefix ahead of `AICORE void`. PyPTO's ptoas-output preprocessor (`_preprocess_ptoas_output` in `python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py`) only stripped an optional `__global__` qualifier when rewriting the entry to `static __aicore__ void`. With the new prefix it produced the illegal `extern "C" static __aicore__ void` — an external-vs-internal linkage clash that clang rejects, breaking codegen.

## Change

Extend the non-mixed-kernel rewrite regex to also consume an optional `extern "C"` prefix:

```python
result = re.sub(
    r'(?:extern\s+"C"\s+)?(?:__global__\s+)?AICORE\s+void',
    "static __aicore__ void",
    result,
)
```

The wrapper's `kernel_entry` remains the sole `extern "C"` export. The change is backward compatible — output from older PTOAS (no `extern "C"` prefix) is still rewritten correctly since the prefix group is optional.

## Test

Device codegen/run verification driven separately on a2a3 hardware.

title: fix(codegen): resolve manual_scope cross-scope tensors; unify output aliasing on remap
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1697 — the orchestration C++ codegen emitted a tensor's SSA-versioned `const Tensor&` alias at the deep `PTO2_SCOPE(MANUAL) { ... }` indent. A task placed **after** a `pl.manual_scope` that read that tensor referenced the now-out-of-scope alias, so the generated `.cpp` failed to C++-compile:

```
error: '<name>__ssa_v<N>' was not declared in this scope
```

`compile_for_test` / `--smoke` generate the `.cpp` but do **not** C++-compile it, so this only surfaced on a real orchestration build.

A `pl.manual_scope` is a **scheduling** region, not a storage/value scope: a tensor it touches flows transparently to tasks placed after the block. The fix follows from that principle, and a follow-up commit generalizes the mechanism to remove an inconsistency it exposed.

## Commit 1 — `fix(codegen)`: resolve `manual_scope` cross-scope tensors

Two mechanisms keep every after-scope-readable name in the enclosing scope, both gated on one enclosing-scope-validity predicate:

- **Output remap** — a caller-allocated kernel/submit output that aliases an enclosing-scope source is no longer given its own `const Tensor&` decl; its emit name is remapped to the source (the strategy `tensor.assemble` already used), so every reference resolves to the enclosing name directly. The output is the same physical tensor as its source (in-place write), so a shared name is exact. Phi/loop-carry reassignments are excluded.
- **Allocation hoisting** — a buffer *created inside* the block (`alloc_tensors`) has no scheduling dependency, so its declaration is hoisted to the enclosing scope. This covers a `pl.create_tensor` placed inside the scope.

A tensor created **before or inside** the scope and read after it now resolves to a single enclosing-scope `const Tensor& buf = ...;`, with the after-scope task doing `add_input(buf)` — no per-SSA-version alias.

## Commit 2 — `refactor(codegen)`: unify output aliasing on emit-name remap

Since a kernel/submit output is the same physical tensor as the `Out`/`InOut` arg it writes in place, the `const Tensor& <result> = <source>;` rename is pure redundancy. The remap above now applies to **every** caller-allocated output (not just inside manual scopes), dropping the redundant alias decls everywhere and removing the inside/outside-manual-scope inconsistency.

```cpp
// before                              // after
const Tensor& o1 = ext_ta;            (gone)
const Tensor& o2 = ext_tb;            (gone)
...                                    ...
params_t1.add_input(o1);             params_t1.add_input(ext_ta);
params_t1.add_input(o2);             params_t1.add_input(ext_tb);
```

Exclusions unchanged: phi/loop-carry reassignments keep their `<name> = <src>;` form; runtime-allocated `task_<n>_outs.get_ref(...)` outputs keep their real binding.

## Test plan

- New regression tests (`tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py`): a tensor written inside a `manual_scope` and read after it, with the `pl.create_tensor` placed both **before** and **inside** the scope, each verified with a generated-code C++ scope checker (`_out_of_scope_tensor_refs`) that catches the "was not declared in this scope" class without invoking a real compiler.
- The 3 existing tests that asserted the eliminated alias decls now assert the consumer reads the correct source; the name-hint-collision test gives its two calls distinct `Out` args so element→call attachment stays observable under remap.
- Local (worktree build): `tests/ut/codegen/` and `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` — **1985 passed**; `tests/ut/ir/` + `tests/ut/language/` — **3101 passed / 2 skipped**. clang-tidy clean on the diff.

## Docs

Updated `docs/en/dev/codegen/01-orchestration_codegen.md` and the `zh-cn` mirror: rewrote *Alias Generation* → *Output Aliasing (emit-name remap)* and added a *Cross-scope tensors and `manual_scope`* section.

title: feat(distributed): multi-program dispatch on one L3 DistributedWorker
body:
## Summary

Lets several compatible `DistributedCompiledProgram` objects be prepared on a **single** shared L3 `DistributedWorker`, so serving-style prefill/decode programs share one worker lifecycle and one worker-resident `DeviceTensor` KV cache instead of needing a worker per program (which loses shared device-resident state).

- `DistributedWorker` accepts a sequence of programs; per-program dispatch state keyed by `id(program)`. One worker is constructed and `init()`'d **once**, with every program's chip/sub-worker callables registered before the fork (COW propagation).
- Compatibility is validated: programs must agree on platform, runtime, and device ids (`ValueError` otherwise).
- `rt.run(compiled, *args)` selects which prepared program to dispatch. `rt(*args)` stays a single-program shortcut and raises `TypeError` in multi-program mode (ambiguous target).
- `DistributedCompiledProgram.prepare(extra_compiled=[...])` sugar so the existing `with compiled.prepare() as rt:` idiom extends to multi-program.
- Exports `DistributedWorker` from `pypto.runtime`.
- Scalar params (`shape is None`, e.g. `seq_len`) are forwarded verbatim to the entry.

## Testing

title: [Bug] Distributed codegen misses Submit callees in next-level program extraction
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

Distributed PTO backend codegen can drop child task functions that are referenced through orchestration `Submit` expressions instead of normal `Call` nodes. The generated next-level program then omits functions that the orchestration still references, so validation fails when compiling a JIT decode kernel that submits helper kernels such as `down_seed`.

This is reproducible on current PyPTO `origin/main` without a local `_CallCollector.visit_expr(Submit)` hook. Adding Submit callee collection makes the same serving generation compile and run.

### Steps to Reproduce

From `/data/liuxu/pypto-serving`, with PyPTO installed from `hw-native-sys/pypto` commit `0944c7b11e95029d079ca4a8c591744421ee4bb1` but without the local Submit collector hook in `python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py`:

```bash
task-submit --device auto --max-time 900 --run "cd /data/liuxu/pypto-serving && PTO2_RING_HEAP=4294967296 PTO2_RING_TASK_WINDOW=1048576 PTO2_RING_DEP_POOL=1048576 SA_PROFILE_OUTPUT=offline_5_without_submit_collector_trace.json SA_PROFILE_LEVEL=kernel python examples/model/qwen3_14b/npu_generate.py --model-dir /data/linyifan/models/Qwen3-14B --prompt 'Huawei is' --platform a2a3 --max-seq-len 512 --max-new-tokens 5 --profile --device-id {}"
```

The generated error report is at:

```text
/data/liuxu/pypto-serving/build_output/_jit_qwen3_decode_host_20260609_140851/next_levels/decode_fwd/report/codegen_errors.txt
```

### Expected Behavior

The distributed backend should include all GlobalVar callees reachable through `Submit` expressions in the generated child/next-level program. `decode_fwd` should compile successfully, including helper functions such as `down_seed`, `gate_seed`, `up_seed`, and `out_seed` when they are submitted by orchestration.

### Actual Behavior

Compilation fails during distributed backend generation for `decode_fwd`:

```text
Failed to generate orchestration 'decode_fwd': Internal error: function 'down_seed' not found after validation. [/data/liuxu/pypto-serving/pypto-lib/models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py:608:4]
Check failed: callee_func != nullptr at /data/liuxu/pypto/src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:2174
```

The summarized report says:

```text
1 function(s) failed to compile:

  Function    | Error
  ------------+--------------------------------------------------------------
  decode_fwd  | Internal error: function 'down_seed' not found after
              | validation. [/data/liuxu/pypto-serving/pypto-
              | lib/models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py:608:4]
```

### Git Commit ID

`0944c7b11e95029d079ca4a8c591744421ee4bb1`

### NPU Kind

Other (please specify in description)

Ascend910 shown by `npu-smi`; this appears to be a distributed codegen issue rather than hardware-specific.

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

The likely root cause is that `_CallCollector` in `python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py` only records `GlobalVar` callees from normal `Call` nodes. In this generated IR, helper kernels are referenced through `Submit` expressions, so they are not included in the next-level chip program even though orchestration still submits them.

A local one-method fix was enough to make the same generation compile and pass 128-token decode:

```python
def visit_expr(self, expr: _ir_core.Expr) -> None:
    if isinstance(expr, _ir_core.Submit) and isinstance(expr.op, _ir_core.GlobalVar):
        self.callee_names.append(expr.op.name)
    super().visit_expr(expr)
```

With that hook restored, `/data/liuxu/pypto-serving` PR #29 completed a 128-token generation run with 127 decode steps.

title: [Bug] Distributed host codegen drops rank-slice materialization for device child without distributed args
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

A distributed host orchestrator can submit a per-rank child with rank-sliced tensor arguments and `device=r`:

```python
for r in pl.range(pld.world_size()):
    self.child(x[r], y[r], device=r)
```

If the child has no `pld.DistributedTensor` / `pld.window` argument, the generated `host_orch.py` references temporary rank-slice tensors such as `t__tmp_v1` and `t__tmp_v2`, but never materializes them. Runtime then fails with `KeyError: 't__tmp_v1'`.

Adding an unused dummy distributed window argument to the child makes the generated host code materialize the same rank slices before building `TaskArgs`, and the program passes. This looks like a distributed host codegen/materialization bug rather than a model issue.

Related but not duplicate:

- #1349 tracks broader rank-reducing slice codegen work. This repro shows the rank slice is generated correctly on the distributed-child-argument path but omitted on the no-distributed-argument path.
- #1579 was another missing materialization bug, but for `pl.spmd` composite dynamic `core_num`, not distributed host child tensor slices.
- #1707 and #1691 are different distributed codegen/runtime failures.

### Steps to Reproduce

Save the following script as `repro_rank_slice_dummy.py` in a checkout that can import `pypto` and the local golden runner, then run the commands below.

<details>
<summary>Minimal repro script</summary>

```python
import argparse

import pypto.language as pl
import pypto.language.distributed as pld
from pypto.ir.distributed_compiled_program import DistributedConfig


N_RANKS = 2
ROWS = 16
COLS = 32


def build_program(*, with_dummy: bool):
    if with_dummy:
        return build_program_with_dummy()
    return build_program_no_dummy()


def build_program_no_dummy():
    @pl.program
    class RankSliceNoDummyRepro:
        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
        def add_one(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
            y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]:
            for row in pl.parallel(ROWS):
                x_row = pl.slice(x, [1, COLS], [row, 0])
                y_row = pl.add(x_row, 1.0)
                y = pl.assemble(y, y_row, [row, 0])
            return y

        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
        def child(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
            y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]:
            y = self.add_one(x, y)
            return y

        @pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
        def host_orch(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
            y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
        ):
            for r in pl.range(pld.world_size()):
                self.child(x[r], y[r], device=r)

    return RankSliceNoDummyRepro


def build_program_with_dummy():
    @pl.program
    class RankSliceWithDummyRepro:
        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
        def add_one(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
            y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]:
            for row in pl.parallel(ROWS):
                x_row = pl.slice(x, [1, COLS], [row, 0])
                y_row = pl.add(x_row, 1.0)
                y = pl.assemble(y, y_row, [row, 0])
            return y

        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
        def child(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
            y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
            _dummy: pld.DistributedTensor[[N_RANKS, 1], pl.INT32],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]:
            y = self.add_one(x, y)
            return y

        @pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
        def host_orch(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
            y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
        ):
            dummy_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(N_RANKS * 4)
            for r in pl.range(pld.world_size()):
                dummy = pld.window(dummy_buf, [N_RANKS, 1], dtype=pl.INT32)
                self.child(x[r], y[r], dummy, device=r)

    return RankSliceWithDummyRepro


def build_specs():
    import torch
    from golden import TensorSpec

    return [
        TensorSpec("x", [N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], torch.float32, init_value=torch.randn),
        TensorSpec("y", [N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], torch.float32, is_output=True),
    ]


def golden(values):
    values["y"][:] = values["x"] + 1.0


def main():
    from golden import run

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("-p", "--platform", default="a2a3", choices=["a2a3", "a2a3sim", "a5", "a5sim"])
    parser.add_argument("-d", "--device", default="0,1", help="comma-separated device ids; need at least 2")
    parser.add_argument("--with-dummy", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--compile-only", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    device_ids = [int(device) for device in args.device.split(",")]
    assert len(device_ids) >= N_RANKS, f"need at least {N_RANKS} devices, got {device_ids}"

    result = run(
        program=build_program(with_dummy=args.with_dummy),
        specs=build_specs(),
        golden_fn=golden,
        compile_only=args.compile_only,
        compile_cfg=dict(
            distributed_config=DistributedConfig(
                device_ids=device_ids[:N_RANKS],
                num_sub_workers=0,
            ),
        ),
        runtime_cfg=dict(platform=args.platform),
        rtol=1e-5,
        atol=1e-5,
    )
    if not result.passed:
        if result.error:
            print(result.error)
        raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

Compile-only passes for both variants:

```bash
python repro_rank_slice_dummy.py -p a2a3 --compile-only -d 0,1
python repro_rank_slice_dummy.py -p a2a3 --compile-only --with-dummy -d 0,1
```

Run the failing no-dummy case on two devices:

```bash
task-submit --device auto --device-num 2 --run "python repro_rank_slice_dummy.py -p a2a3 -d {}"
```

Run the passing dummy control:

```bash
task-submit --device auto --device-num 2 --run "python repro_rank_slice_dummy.py -p a2a3 --with-dummy -d {}"
```

### Expected Behavior

The no-dummy and with-dummy variants should both materialize `x[r]` and `y[r]` rank slices before submitting the child task. A child that does not otherwise use distributed windows should still be callable with `device=r` from a distributed host orchestrator.

### Actual Behavior

The no-dummy variant compiles but fails at runtime before the child task can run:

```text
[RUN] compile done
[RUN] runtime ...
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "build_output/RankSliceNoDummyRepro_*/orchestration/host_orch.py", line 12, in host_orch
    _ta_0.add_tensor(make_tensor_arg(tensors["t__tmp_v1"]), TensorArgType.INPUT)
KeyError: 't__tmp_v1'
```

The generated no-dummy `host_orch.py` references temporary tensors without creating them:

```python
def host_orch(orch, _args, config, *, tensors, callables, sub_ids, _keep, world_size):
    t__tmp_v0 = world_size
    for r__idx_v0 in range(0, t__tmp_v0, 1):
        _ta_0 = TaskArgs()
        _ta_0.add_tensor(make_tensor_arg(tensors["t__tmp_v1"]), TensorArgType.INPUT)
        _ta_0.add_tensor(make_tensor_arg(tensors["t__tmp_v2"]), TensorArgType.OUTPUT_EXISTING)
        _keep.append(_ta_0)
        orch.submit_next_level(callables["child"], _ta_0, config, worker=r__idx_v0)
```

The with-dummy control passes:

```text
[RUN]   'y' PASS  shape=(2, 16, 32) dtype=torch.float32
[RUN] PASS
```

Its generated `host_orch.py` first materializes the rank slices, then builds `TaskArgs`:

```python
tensors["t__tmp_v1"] = tensors["x__ssa_v0"][r__idx_v0, 0:16, 0:32]
tensors["t__tmp_v2"] = tensors["y__ssa_v0"][r__idx_v0, 0:16, 0:32]
_ta_0.add_tensor(make_tensor_arg(tensors["t__tmp_v1"]), TensorArgType.INPUT)
_ta_0.add_tensor(make_tensor_arg(tensors["t__tmp_v2"]), TensorArgType.OUTPUT_EXISTING)
```

### Git Commit ID

`778dae483dcb3640d69bd271a39a5c8bc17a8b81`

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

This is reproduced through the distributed `a2a3` runner, but the failure is a generated Python host-orchestration `KeyError` before device kernels do meaningful work.

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Diagnosis: **pypto codegen / distributed host orchestration**. The failing program compiles, and the only difference between failing and passing variants is whether the child has an unused distributed window argument.

Observed local evidence:

- no-dummy task: `task_20260609_151815_734577963`, devices `5,7`, failed with `KeyError: 't__tmp_v1'`.
- with-dummy task: `task_20260609_151832_73935324595`, devices `7,9`, passed in `6.25s`.

Environment used for reproduction:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `006673b6745a80ab4adc6055b84838609010948e` |
| pypto | `778dae483dcb3640d69bd271a39a5c8bc17a8b81` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `48980572b3537df4ed5e6d9720cb6162939eb58a` |
| pto-isa | `8e436661958d934be9fb1706c9ecc4a5c827d675` (branch: `main`) |
| ptoas | `0.44` |
| CANN | `not detected` |
| Python | `3.10.20` |

title: fix(ir): round-trip arbitrary Call/Submit attrs through print/parse
body:
## Summary

The Python printer only emitted an allowlisted set of `Call`/`Submit` attrs (`dump_vars`, `arg_directions`) into the `attrs={...}` dict, **silently dropping every other key**. A post-outline `Call` carrying `arg_direction_overrides` (from `pl.at(no_dep_args=...)` / `pl.no_dep(...)`) therefore lost the attr on `print → parse`, breaking the roundtrip verification instrument after `OutlineIncoreScopes`.

This makes attr round-tripping **generic**, mirroring the binary serializer's type-driven model: any attr the printer has no bespoke sugar for is still emitted, and a value type with no DSL renderer fails loud rather than being dropped.

## Changes

- **`python_printer.cpp`** — new `PrintAttrValue`, a type-dispatched renderer that emits every non-sugar attr generically and **fails loud** (`INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN`) on an unrenderable value (never silently drops). The `Call` and `Submit` print paths dump all attrs through it, keeping the bespoke `dump_vars`/`arg_directions` emitters and the `deps=`/`device=`/`dumps=` sugar surfaces unchanged.
- **`ast_parser.py`** — drop the `attrs=` key allowlist; add generic `_parse_attr_value` + `_extract_generic_call_attrs` that recover any key. The `pl.no_dep(...)` / `deps=` sugar paths are untouched.
- **`structural_equal.cpp`** — compare attrs/kwargs as an order-insensitive, unique-keyed map (consume-on-match), so passes that append the same attrs in a different order still compare equal.
- **`structural_hash.cpp`** — fold attr hashes commutatively to preserve the equal-implies-equal-hash invariant, and add `vector<int32_t>` coverage.

## Tests

- Re-enabled the roundtrip verification on `TestOutlineNoDepArgs` (the direct regression coverage for the dropped attr).
- Added a printer roundtrip test for a generic attr key and an attr order-insensitivity (+ `structural_hash`) test.
- Full `tests/ut/ir/` green (3735 passed); ruff / clang-format / clang-tidy / header / english-only checks clean.

## Notes

While re-enabling the bypass, an unrelated **pre-existing** roundtrip gap surfaced: a cross-function call to a kernel with **no return-type annotation** loses its return type on `print → parse` (`UnknownType` vs `TensorType`). That is independent of attrs and out of scope here; `TestNoDepOverride` keeps a `BEFORE_AND_AFTER` verification downgrade for it.

title: test(split_vector): de-NONE tile.load fixtures via canonical 4-op form
body:
## Summary

- Canonicalizes two `TestSplitVectorKernelNoSplitA2A3` hand-built `tile.load` Calls to the builder's 4-operand form (`[tensor, offsets, shapes, valid_shapes]` + `{target_memory, transpose}`), so they match DSL/IR-builder output and survive the print→parse roundtrip verifier.
- Adds the cross-core pipe scaffolding (`import_peer_buffer` + `aiv_initialize_pipe`) the `MixedKernelExpanded` property requires for an AIV function using a V2C op (`tile.tpush_to_aic`).
- Removes both `VerificationLevel.NONE` wrappers; the two tests now run under full `BEFORE_AND_AFTER` property + print→parse roundtrip verification.
- Renames `..._three_arg_tile_load` → `..._tile_load_to_create` (the load is no longer 3-arg).

## Why

The old 3-operand `tile.load` was non-canonical IR — it only existed because the fixture built it via `ir.Call(..., result_type)`, which bypasses `DeduceTileLoadType`'s 4-arg `CHECK`. `SplitVectorKernel` guards load handling with `args_.size() >= 4` and indexes `args_[3]` (`src/ir/transforms/split_vector_kernel_pass.cpp`), so the old form was an artifact the pass would have silently skipped. Canonicalizing makes the tests exercise the production path and removes the need for the verification bypass.

## Testing

- `test_split_vector_kernel.py` (25) + `test_expand_mixed_kernel_a2a3.py` + `test_expand_mixed_kernel_a5.py` — **89 passed** under default (roundtrip) verification.
- Both modified tests confirmed passing individually with no `NONE` bypass.

title: [Bug] Host-composed child kernels with duplicate name_hint fail instead of auto-disambiguating outlined function names
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

When two child kernels reuse the same `@pl.jit.inline` helper, each child can compile independently. However, composing those child kernels in one `@pl.jit.host` program can fail during `OutlineIncoreScopes` if the shared inline helper contains an incore scope with a fixed `name_hint`.

The outlined functions are inserted into one program/global function namespace without suffix-disambiguating duplicate names. In practice, the duplicate `name_hint` often comes from legitimate helper reuse, not from two unrelated code blocks accidentally choosing the same string.

This shows up when building a larger host orchestration from independently runnable pieces. For example, a decode-layer host that composes SWA attention and MoE EP has both subgraphs reusing HC helper code such as `hc_pre` / `hc_post`; those helpers contain common scopes such as `name_hint="linear"`. Each subgraph compiles independently, but the composed host fails with `Duplicate function name "linear"`.

The minimal repro below removes the model logic. It has two child kernels, `single_a` and `single_b`, both calling the same `@pl.jit.inline` helper `shared_helper`. That inline helper contains `name_hint="dup_scope"`. Each child compiles by itself. The host-composed version fails with `Duplicate function name "dup_scope"`.

Diagnosis: **pypto codegen / IR pass**. The failure occurs during pass execution before PTOAS/device execution:

```text
ValueError: Duplicate function name "dup_scope"
Check failed: function_names.find(name) == function_names.end() at src/ir/program.cpp:40
...
src/ir/transforms/outline_incore_scopes_pass.cpp:108
```

Related but not duplicate:

- #1244 is about printer disambiguation for distinct IR variables that share `name_hint`.
- #1708 is about distributed host codegen dropping rank-slice materialization for a device child without distributed args.

### Steps to Reproduce

Save this script as `repro_duplicate_name_hint_host.py` in a checkout that can import `pypto` and the local golden runner:

```python
import argparse

import pypto.language as pl
from golden import TensorSpec, run_jit
from pypto.ir.distributed_compiled_program import DistributedConfig


N_RANKS = 2
N = 16
TILE_N = 8


@pl.jit.inline
def shared_helper(
    x: pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.FP32],
    y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.FP32]],
    scale: pl.Scalar[pl.FP32],
):
    for b in pl.spmd(N // TILE_N, name_hint="dup_scope"):
        i = b * TILE_N
        xi = pl.load(x, [i, 0], [TILE_N, 1])
        yi = pl.mul(xi, scale)
        pl.store(yi, [i, 0], y)
    return y


@pl.jit
def single_a(
    x: pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.FP32],
    y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.FP32]],
):
    return shared_helper(x, y, 1.0)


@pl.jit
def single_b(
    x: pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.FP32],
    y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.FP32]],
):
    return shared_helper(x, y, 2.0)


@pl.jit.host
def host_orch(
    x: pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, N, 1], pl.FP32],
    y_a: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, N, 1], pl.FP32]],
    y_b: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, N, 1], pl.FP32]],
):
    single_a(x[0], y_a[0], device=0)
    single_b(x[1], y_b[1], device=1)


def single_specs():
    import torch

    return [
        TensorSpec(
            "x",
            [N, 1],
            torch.float32,
            init_value=lambda: torch.arange(N, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(N, 1),
        ),
        TensorSpec("y", [N, 1], torch.float32, is_output=True),
    ]


def host_specs():
    import torch

    return [
        TensorSpec(
            "x",
            [N_RANKS, N, 1],
            torch.float32,
            init_value=lambda: torch.arange(N_RANKS * N, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(N_RANKS, N, 1),
        ),
        TensorSpec("y_a", [N_RANKS, N, 1], torch.float32, is_output=True),
        TensorSpec("y_b", [N_RANKS, N, 1], torch.float32, is_output=True),
    ]


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("case", choices=["single-a", "single-b", "host"])
    parser.add_argument("-d", "--device", default="0,1")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.case == "single-a":
        fn = single_a
        specs = single_specs()
        compile_cfg = None
    elif args.case == "single-b":
        fn = single_b
        specs = single_specs()
        compile_cfg = None
    else:
        fn = host_orch
        specs = host_specs()
        device_ids = [int(d) for d in args.device.split(",")]
        compile_cfg = {
            "distributed_config": DistributedConfig(
                device_ids=device_ids[:N_RANKS],
                num_sub_workers=0,
            ),
        }

    result = run_jit(
        fn=fn,
        specs=specs,
        compile_only=True,
        compile_cfg=compile_cfg,
    )
    if not result.passed:
        if result.error:
            print(result.error)
        raise SystemExit(1)
    print(f"{args.case}: compile passed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run the standalone controls:

```bash
python repro_duplicate_name_hint_host.py single-a
python repro_duplicate_name_hint_host.py single-b
```

Observed:

```text
single-a: compile passed
single-b: compile passed
```

Run the host-composed case:

```bash
python repro_duplicate_name_hint_host.py host -d 0,1
```

### Expected Behavior

The host-composed program should compile. PyPTO should automatically disambiguate duplicate outlined function names produced from identical `name_hint` values, especially when they come from the same reused `@pl.jit.inline` helper. A stable suffix such as `_0`, `_1`, or parent/call-site context would be enough.

User code should not need to copy/re-wrap reusable inline helpers and manually rename every internal `name_hint` just because independently valid kernels are composed into a larger host orchestration.

### Actual Behavior

The host-composed case fails during pass execution:

```text
[RUN] compile ...
[RUN] compile done
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File "pypto/ir/pass_manager.py", line 356, in run_passes
    return self._pipeline.run(input_ir)
ValueError: Duplicate function name "dup_scope"
Check failed: function_names.find(name) == function_names.end() at src/ir/program.cpp:40

C++ Traceback (most recent call last):
 ...
 File "src/ir/transforms/outline_incore_scopes_pass.cpp", line 108
 File "src/ir/program.cpp", line 40
```

### Git Commit ID

`778dae483dcb3640d69bd271a39a5c8bc17a8b81`

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

This reproduces in compile-only mode before device execution.

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

title: fix(codegen): trace view-store returns to the real Out param (#1702)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1702. A `pl.spmd` / multi-output scope whose kernel writes its `Out` param through a **view** (`tensor.slice` / `tensor.reshape`) and returns the result produced a return value that `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` could not trace back to a param.

`FindReturnedParamIndex`'s tracer (`TraceVarToParam`, `orchestration_analysis.cpp`) only followed `tensor.assemble` / `tile.store` / `tensor.set_validshape`, so a view-store return resolved to `nullopt` and the alias fell back to `out_indices[0]` — the **first** `Out`/`InOut` param, which for a fanned-out scope is per-block scratch, not the real result. Every downstream consumer of the scope's return was then routed into the wrong buffer; a numel-mismatched reshape tripped the AICPU `valid_reshape` assert, the subtask aborted without writing FIN, and the scheduler latched `GLOBAL_STUCK` — surfacing on the host as `507018`. A kernel-side shape bug thus masqueraded as a scheduler deadlock.

## Fix

Follow `tensor.slice` / `tensor.reshape` to their source buffer (`args[0]`) in `TraceVarToParam`, mirroring the existing `assemble` / `store` / `set_validshape` rules. The return now resolves precisely to the actual `Out` param, so the `out_indices[0]` fallback no longer fires.

> Note: an alternative buffer-root-matching approach (resolving the returned SSA's buffer root and matching it against each out-arg) does **not** work here — `BufferRootCollector` itself falls back to `out_roots[0]` for non-tuple calls, so it reproduces the identical wrong-output selection. Fixing the return tracer is the precise fix.

## Test

Adds a host-side (no device) codegen regression test in `test_orchestration_codegen.py`: a `pl.spmd` scope whose kernel writes an in-place `InOut` scratch (sorted first) plus an `Out` result written through a sliced view, with the scope's single return reshaped downstream. Asserts the alias binds to the real `result` (`ext_result.reshape(`), not the scratch (`ext_scratch.reshape(`). Fails before the fix, passes after.

## Verification

- New regression test: FAIL → PASS with the fix
- Full `tests/ut/codegen/`: **427 passed**, no regressions

Same class as #1573 / #1693 / #1694, distinct trigger and code path.

title: [Bug] manual_scope cross-scope aliasing (#1705) incomplete: windowed (.view) write value-root not remapped, after-scope reader still fails C++ compile
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

Follow-up to #1697 (fixed by #1705). #1705 ("resolve manual_scope cross-scope tensors; unify output aliasing on remap") resolved the plain-`pl.assemble` and atomic/inout cases, but **one path remains broken**: a tensor created before a `pl.manual_scope`, written **inside** it via the **OptimizeOrchTensors Pattern-5 windowed-write** path (`.view()` window externalization), and read by a task **after** the scope, still fails the orchestration C++ compile:

```
error: '<name>__rv_v<N>' was not declared in this scope
```

The remaining trigger is specifically the **windowed write**: it roots the tensor's SSA-version chain at a **block-local `Tensor` value** (`<name>__rv_v2 = <base>;`, a `Tensor` by value, not a `const Tensor&` alias), declared *inside* the `PTO2_SCOPE(MANUAL)` block. #1705's remap follows `const Tensor&` alias chains to an enclosing-scope source, but **stops at that block-local value** — it does not chase the final hop (`value = base`) to the outer base — so the after-scope reader names the deep `__rv_v<N>` alias, which is out of scope.

Contrast (same generated `.cpp`): an atomic/inout tensor with **no** windowing is remapped to its outer base name and compiles fine.

Related: #1697 (closed), #1705 (partial fix), #1693 (inlined-scope `__ssa_v` cross-assignment, different trigger).

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
# in a checkout at/after the #1705 fix:
python decode2l_embed_lmhead.py --model-dir <ckpt> --kv-dir <kv> --device <n> --validate --fused
```

`decode2l_embed_lmhead.py --fused` uses `decode_layer_fused.py`, which moves the MLP-tail residual-add (`down_cast_residual`) out of `manual_scope` into a single after-scope auto-dep writer that reads `post_norm_partial` (the residual `h1`, written inside the scope by `residual_rms_cast`).

NOTE: a standalone `@pl.jit` repro using a plain `pl.assemble` (no windowing) now **passes** after #1705 — so a faithful standalone repro must trigger the Pattern-5 windowed-write path. The concrete artifact is the generated `decode_fwd.cpp` from the command above.

### Expected Behavior

The orchestration `.cpp` should C++-compile. A manual_scope-internal tensor that becomes live-out should have its final version resolvable at the after-scope reader — regardless of whether it was written via a plain assemble (already handled by #1705) or via a Pattern-5 windowed `.view()` write.

### Actual Behavior

Generated `decode_fwd.cpp` (from `decode2l_embed_lmhead.py --fused`):

```
decode_fwd.cpp:977:46: error: 'post_norm_partial_inline265__rv_v14' was not declared in this scope
         params_t30.add_input(post_norm_partial_inline265__rv_v14);
RuntimeError: Orchestration compilation failed with exit code 1
```

Version-chain evidence in that file:

```
line 143 (outer):  const Tensor& down_acc_all_inline74 = alloc_2.get_ref(1);          // atomic, NO windowing -> works (Task 30 add_input(down_acc_all_inline74))
line 148 (outer):  const Tensor& post_norm_partial_inline265 = alloc_2.get_ref(6);    // base
line 319:          PTO2_SCOPE(PTO2ScopeMode::MANUAL) {                                 // manual scope opens
lines 375-381:       ... post_norm_partial_inline265__ssa_v0__window = post_norm_partial_inline265.view(...)   // Pattern-5 windowed write
line 405:            Tensor post_norm_partial_inline265__rv_v2 = post_norm_partial_inline265;   // BLOCK-LOCAL VALUE (chain root)
line 456/507/558/609: const Tensor& __rv_v5/v8/v11/v14 = <prev>;                       // chain, all inside the manual scope
line ~798:         }                                                                   // manual scope closes
line 977:          params_t30.add_input(post_norm_partial_inline265__rv_v14);          // after-scope reader -> __rv_v14 out of scope
```

`post_norm_partial` has 5 `.view()`/window references; `down_acc_all` has 0 — confirming the windowed-write path is the differentiator.

### Git Commit ID

61d289da00c5d931d0fe25f5bedffdda11cf9f77

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

**Fix direction:** in the same `EmitTensorAlias` / output-remap logic touched by #1705 (`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`), the remap that resolves a manual_scope-internal alias to its enclosing-scope source must **chase through the block-local `Tensor` value root** (`<name>__rv_v2 = <base>;`) to the outer `<base>` — OR the windowed-write codegen should root its SSA chain at the enclosing base rather than emitting a block-local `Tensor` value. Either way the after-scope reader should resolve to the outer base name (as the atomic path already does).

**Impact:** blocks fusing a `manual_scope` MLP-tail output (e.g. `down_cast_residual` reading `post_norm_partial`) into an after-scope auto-dep writer — i.e. removing the redundant `out_consolidate` copy in the qwen3 decode kernel.

title: feat(distributed): allow plain Tensor as src in pld.{tensor,tile}.put
body:
## Summary

Relax `pld.tensor.put` / `pld.tile.put` so `src` accepts either a window-bound `DistributedTensor` **or** a plain `Tensor`. TPUT only requires a readable local GM region on the source side — window membership is not needed for src — so kernels can push directly from host-backed inputs without first staging through a window buffer. `dst` is unchanged: it still requires `DistributedTensor` (the peer needs a window slot to receive into).

This unlocks a TPUT-based EP dispatch / combine kernel on the L3 distributed test path: the runtime example's 3-channel push (x BF16 / w FP32 / idx INT32) and the combine routed_y push can now go directly from host-backed input tensors, dropping the previous `pl.load` + `pld.tile.remote_store` two-step.

## Changes

**IR / codegen / DSL — relaxed src contract**
- `src/ir/op/distributed/put.cpp` — verifier switches src type-check from `As<DistributedTensorType>` to `AsTensorTypeLike`; updates `REGISTER_OP` src descriptions for both `pld.tensor.put` and `pld.tile.put`.
- `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp` — `MakePutCodegenPTO` accepts a Tensor-or-DistributedTensor src; tensor_view emission is unchanged.
- `python/pypto/language/distributed/op/{tensor,tile}_ops.py` — split dst/src checks, accept `Tensor | DistributedTensor` for src, update signatures and docstrings.
- `docs/{en,zh-cn}/dev/distributed_ops.md` — document the relaxed src contract in both overview and TPUT verifier sections.

**Test — `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_ep_dispatch_combine.py`**
- Parametrise the program builder over `n_ranks`; cover `n_ranks ∈ {2, 4}` (preserved across this PR; merged in via the rebased `7c256695` test commit).
- Rewrite dispatch (x/w/idx push) and combine (routed_y push) to use the new `pld.tensor.put` TPUT instead of `pl.load` + `pld.tile.remote_store`, exercising the relaxed src contract end-to-end.
- Run at real DeepSeek-V4 FLASH MoE scale: T=128, TOPK=6, D=4096, L=16, R=192.
- Replace the hardcoded 2-element BF16 reduction with a TOPK-loop FP32 accumulator so combine works for any TOPK ≥ 1.
- Drop the input-weight jitter; loosen routed_y tolerance to `rtol = atol = 2**-6` (~2 BF16 ULPs relative) to absorb the larger TOPK summation error.

**Backend**
- `python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py` — strip `extern "C"` wrappers that ptoas occasionally prepends to generated functions in `_preprocess_ptoas_output`, alongside the existing AICORE-qualifier normalisations.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit / verifier paths: `tests/ut/ir/op/distributed/` for the put verifier (covered by existing tests + the relaxed type check).
- [x] L3 ST: `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_ep_dispatch_combine.py::TestL3EpDispatchCombine::test_ep_dispatch_combine[2]` and `[4]` — distributed runtime test, device-gated.
- [x] Documentation rebuilt; English and Chinese docs in sync (verifier + overview).
- [x] clang-tidy clean on the two C++ files; ruff / pyright clean on Python.
