title: fix(codegen): collect Submit callees in next-level program extraction
body:
## Summary

`_CallCollector` in `python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py` only recorded `GlobalVar` callees from plain `Call` nodes, so helper kernels referenced through `Submit` expressions (task launches from `pl.submit` inside `pl.manual_scope`) were dropped from the generated next-level chip program. Distributed backend generation then failed validation:

```
Failed to generate orchestration 'decode_fwd': Internal error: function 'down_seed' not found after validation.
```

`Submit` has no dedicated Python visitor hook, so its `GlobalVar` callee is now collected on the generic `visit_expr` dispatch before delegating to `super()` (which still routes `Call` nodes to `visit_call` and recurses into children). This follows the project's Call-vs-Submit awareness rule: passes that inspect calls must consider both kinds.

## Changes

- `_CallCollector.visit_expr` collects `Submit` `GlobalVar` callees so next-level extraction follows both `Call` and `Submit` references.
- Regression test asserting an InCore kernel reached only via `pl.submit` is included in the collected chip task functions.

## Testing

- [x] New regression test fails without the fix, passes with it
- [x] `tests/ut/codegen/` suite passes (426 tests)

## Related Issues

Fixes #1707

title: fix(ir): materialize hoisted temps in single-statement loop/if bodies
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1708 — a distributed HOST orchestrator that submits a per-rank child with rank-sliced args (`self.child(x[r], y[r], device=r)`) compiled fine but failed at runtime with `KeyError: 't__tmp_v1'` when the child had no `pld.DistributedTensor`/`pld.window` argument. Adding an unused dummy distributed arg made it pass — the red herring in the bug report.

## Root cause — `FlattenCallExpr` (pass 07), not codegen

The bug is in `VisitStmt_(const ForStmtPtr&)` (with byte-identical latent copies in the `WhileStmt`/`IfStmt` visitors):

```cpp
auto range_pending = pending_stmts_;   // save range pending
pending_stmts_.clear();
auto new_body = VisitStmt(op->body_);  // body hoists x[r]/y[r] slices into pending_stmts_
pending_stmts_ = range_pending;        // BUG: overwrite discards the body's pending
```

The comment *"after normalization, body is SeqStmts which handles its own pending"* assumes the body is always a `SeqStmts`. A bare per-rank dispatch loop body is a single `EvalStmt` — no `SeqStmts` visitor ever flushes the hoisted `t__tmp = tensor.slice(x[r])` assigns, and the restore line discards them. The slices become undefined free vars (`t__tmp_v1__FREE_VAR` from the pass-07 dump onward); host_orch codegen then emits `add_tensor(tensors["t__tmp_v1"])` with no materializing line → runtime `KeyError`. A dummy distributed arg makes the body multi-statement (a `SeqStmts`) → pending flushes correctly — hence the workaround. The device kernel `.pto` is byte-identical and unaffected.

## Fix

Route the `ForStmt`/`WhileStmt`/`IfStmt` bodies (and IfStmt then/else) through `FlattenScopeBody`, which wraps a non-`SeqStmts` body together with its pending hoisted temps into a `SeqStmts` (only when `!As<SeqStmts>(body) && !pending_stmts_.empty()`); the surrounding range/condition pending is saved and restored for the parent `SeqStmts`. Per review feedback, `FlattenScopeBody` is a private member of `FlattenCallExprMutator`, shared with the scope-stmt visitors — unifying all body handling on one code path.

## Testing

- [x] UT regression `TestFlattenCallInForRange::test_single_statement_for_body_hoists_into_body` — minimal non-distributed repro (`for r: self.child(x[r], y[r])`); fails on old code, passes on the fix. Full `test_flatten_call_expr_pass.py`: 31 passed.
- [x] ST repro `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_rank_slice_dispatch.py::test_rank_slice_no_dummy` — the exact #1708 scenario (no distributed-window arg) on 2 real NPUs; used to KeyError, now passes in CI `dist-system-tests`.
- [x] Generated `host_orch.py` now materializes `tensors["t__tmp_v1"] = tensors["x__ssa_v0"][r, 0:16, 0:32]` before `TaskArgs`.
- [x] clang-tidy, pre-commit, full CI green.

> CI note: intermittent `test_l3_ep_dispatch_combine` failures during this PR were verified unrelated — the EP program's full compiled output is byte-identical with and without this change.

title: fix(codegen): alias multi-output spmd-scope return to the correct output (#1702)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1702. Orchestration codegen aliased a multi-output `pl.spmd` scope's return value to the **wrong** output tensor, producing a numel-mismatched `Tensor::reshape` that aborts the AICPU subtask and surfaces as a 507018 scheduler deadlock.

## Root cause

`GenerateSingleReturnAlias` (`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`) resolved a scope's single SSA return via:

```cpp
auto returned_idx = FindReturnedParamIndex(callee, program_);
size_t param_idx = returned_idx.value_or(out_indices[0]);   // <-- blind first-output fallback
```

A fanned-out `pl.spmd` scope is outlined into a Spmd wrapper whose body ends in the inner kernel call, so it has **no traceable top-level `ReturnStmt`** → `FindReturnedParamIndex` returns `nullopt` (or mis-traces through the first Out arg). The `out_indices[0]` fallback then aliases the result to the **first** output.

When such a scope writes multiple GM outputs and the function returns a **non-first** output (DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre` with `mix_x` fused into `hc_post`), the generated orchestration was:

```cpp
params_t1.add_inout(pre_val_gm_inline83);      // [128, 8]    numel 1024  (out_indices[0])
params_t1.add_output(x_mixed_view_inline52);   // [128, 4096]  == the returned x_mixed
rt_submit_aiv_task(2, params_t1);
const Tensor& x_mixed_view_inline52__rv_v2 = pre_val_gm_inline83;          // WRONG output
Tensor x_mixed_v1 = x_mixed_view_inline52__rv_v2.reshape({64,2,4096}, 3);  // 1024 != 524288
```

`reshape([128,8] -> [64,2,4096])` fails `valid_reshape` (`runtime/.../tensor.h:435`) on the AICPU executor → the subtask aborts and never FINs → the scope never COMPLETEs → scheduler latches GLOBAL_STUCK (`sched_error_code=100`) → host `aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018`. A kernel-side shape bug masquerading as a scheduler deadlock.

## Fix

The returned SSA result var is an SSA rename of the **output arg** carrying the result, so its SSA base / buffer root is the authoritative signal for which Out/InOut arg the scope returns. Match the result var's SSA base against each Out/InOut arg; when it uniquely identifies one, use it over the unreliable `FindReturnedParamIndex`. Keep the `out_indices[0]` fallback only when there is no unique match (genuine single-Out kernels), plus an `INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN` bound check mirroring `GenerateTupleReturnAliases`.

Same family as #1573 / #1693 (orchestration mis-aliasing multi-output scopes) but a distinct trigger and code path; the tuple / `__ssa_v1` / `__phi` paths are untouched.

## Validation

- On-board (Ascend a2a3): the DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre` kernel fused with `mix_x` in the same multi-output spmd scope **no longer 507018-deadlocks** — it compiles and runs into runtime with this fix (without it, the `valid_reshape` abort hangs the AICPU).
- Local: builds clean (`pip install -e .`), no regression in `tests/ut/ir/verifier/` and `tests/ut/codegen/test_spmd_scope_tid_codegen.py`.

## Note on testing

A standalone `@pl.program` UT does not reproduce the exact mis-alias — it only triggers through the `pl.jit.inline` + tail-appended `create_tensor`-scratch path this kernel exercises (a minimal scope resolves the return to its param directly, bypassing `GenerateSingleReturnAlias`). On-board is the decisive validation here; a faithful regression/ST test is tracked as a follow-up.

Related: #1702, #1693, #1573, #1650

title: fix(codegen): hoist manual_scope loop-carry decls; collapse cross-scope copies
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1713. A tensor written inside a `pl.manual_scope` and read by a task placed **after** the block failed the orchestration C++ compile — the after-scope reader named a block-local identifier declared inside the manual scope:

```cpp
PTO2_SCOPE(PTO2ScopeMode::MANUAL) {
    Tensor acc_rv = acc;          // loop-carry decl, block-local
    for (...) { acc_rv = ...; }
    Tensor acc__ssa_v1 = acc_rv;  // post-loop SSA rebind, block-local
}
Tensor flat = acc__ssa_v1.reshape(...);   // 'acc__ssa_v1' was not declared in this scope
```

#1697/#1705 fixed the plain-submit case (alloc hoist + output remap via `EmitTensorAlias`), but a **loop carry inside the scope** produces two block-local decls those mechanisms never touched: the ForStmt scalar-carry decl and the Var-RHS catch-all copy. A `manual_scope` is a scheduling region, not a storage scope, so a tensor it touches must flow transparently to after-scope readers.

## The fix

Both gated on `IsAtManualScopeBodyIndent()` (shared with the existing alloc hoist):

- **Carry-decl hoist** — a `Tensor carry = init;` whose loop sits directly in a manual-scope body is hoisted into the enclosing scope (a one-time pre-loop copy of an enclosing-valid value, so ordering-inert), registered mutable in the *enclosing* C++ frame. `Tensor` has no public default ctor, so the whole decl is hoisted rather than forward-declared.
- **Var-RHS copy collapse** — a pure SSA tensor copy `X = Y` inside a manual scope is remapped (`emit_name_map_`) onto an enclosing-scope-valid `Y` instead of a scope-local decl, so every reference resolves to `Y` (the same emit-name remap #1705 applies to kernel outputs). The `emit_name_map_`/`GetVarName` cascade collapses an entire `__rv`/`__ssa_v` chain onto the enclosing base in one hop.
- **Snapshot safety** — a hoisted carry is mutable one frame out, so collapse onto it is restricted (via `hoisted_carry_names_` + the body-indent check) to the post-loop, stable rebind; an in-loop copy of the carry keeps its decl, so a pre-yield snapshot can never alias the carry's later value.

## Test plan

- Strengthened `_out_of_scope_tensor_refs` to also flag **method-receiver** (`X.reshape(...)`) and **assignment-RHS** uses — the old `add_*`-only checker silently missed the after-scope `.reshape()` read.
- 5 new regression tests: loop-carry-read-after-reshape, fresh-rebind-carry-hoist (windowed), windowed-submit-read-after, in-loop snapshot-keep, and a non-manual-scope negative control. The 4 positive tests fail without the C++ fix (verified by stashing it).
- Local: `tests/ut/codegen/` **431 passed**; `tests/ut/codegen/` + `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` **2017 passed** (2 unrelated pre-existing `FlattenTileNdTo2DDynamicValid` failures from #1588); `tests/ut/language/` + `tests/ut/jit/` **1188 passed**. clang-tidy clean on the diff.

## Note

Also replaces `std::stable_partition` (param tensors-before-scalars reorder) with a behaviour-identical two-pass `ReorderTensorsBeforeScalars`, and adds `#include <memory>` — required to keep this file clean under the file-level clang-tidy gate (libstdc++ `stable_partition` pulls in the deprecated `get_temporary_buffer`; `std::dynamic_pointer_cast` needs a direct `<memory>` include).

body:
## Summary
`test_distributed_worker_call_stores_last_run_timing` in `tests/ut/runtime/test_run_timing_plumbing.py` is currently failing on `main`, breaking the `pre-commit` (pyright), `unit-tests`, and `dist-system-tests` jobs.

- read per-program state from `self._states[compiled]["param_infos"]` etc.

So the stale stand-in fails twice:

- **runtime** — `AttributeError: 'DistributedWorker' object has no attribute '_multi_program'` at `distributed_runner.py:750`.

## Fix
Update the white-box stand-in to the current internal contract: set `_multi_program`/`_compiled` and a `_states[compiled]` entry carrying `param_infos`/`base_tensors`/`entry_fn`/`chip_cids`/`sub_ids`/`call_config`/`device_nums`. The behavior under test is unchanged — `rt(*args)` stores `_dispatch`'s return value into `last_run_timing`.

title: fix(passes): outlined tile.store SSA scope violation via idempotent ConvertToSSA + escaping promotion (fixes #1693)
body:
## Summary

Two stacked commits that together fix issue #1693 (SSA scope violation in outlined functions when ``tile.store`` is rewritten inside a loop body) by leaning on ConvertToSSA's existing escaping-variable promotion machinery.

### Commit 1 — ``fix(convert_to_ssa): make pass idempotent on already-SSA IR``

The pass doc advertises ``Preserves existing SSA structure`` and ``Keep existing SSA constructs unchanged``, but re-running on already-SSA IR with **dynamic shape / valid_shape / stride Var refs embedded in Tile/Tensor type annotations** dangled those refs. AssignStmt LHS is unconditionally re-versioned (``cur_[OLD] = NEW``), but every iter_arg / phi / return_var construction site read the type from the old Var verbatim — type-embedded refs to OLD survived and SSAVerify reported ``used before definition``.

Fix: thread every Var construction site that reads a type from an existing Var (or from ``TypeCollector.types[]``) through ``SubstType`` so renamed refs stay consistent. Sites: existing iter_args / loop_var / carried / escaping init types in ConvertFor and ConvertWhile; phi var, no-phi rv, mixed rv in ConvertIf. The previously-verbatim existing return_vars push is replaced with a freshen-and-update-cur_ loop; removed the now-redundant ``RegisterExistingReturnVars`` helper.

Tests: added ``TestIdempotence`` with two regression cases (IfStmt phi with dynamic valid_shape, ForStmt iter_arg with dynamic valid_shape). Both fail on baseline with ``used before definition`` and pass after the fix.

Doc: tighten ``04-convert_to_ssa.md`` to make the idempotence guarantee explicit (en + zh-cn).

### Commit 2 — ``fix(passes): rerun ConvertToSSA after outline passes (fixes #1693)``

OutlineScope's ``StoreEvalToAssignMutator`` rewrites EvalStmt-form ``pl.tile.store(t, ..., target)`` into ``_store_var = pl.tile.store(...)`` so the outlined function can return the post-store SSA name. When the store sits inside a for/while/if body, the synthesised AssignStmt is inside-loop while the ReturnStmt that references ``_store_var`` is at function-body depth — SSA scope violation, surfaced as the ``__FREE_VAR`` suffix the SSA verifier rejects.

Fix: re-run ``ConvertToSSA`` right after ``OutlineClusterScopes`` (the last outline pass). The escaping-variable promotion in ConvertToSSA detects "var defined inside loop, used after loop", synthesises IterArg + YieldStmt for each enclosing for/while, and ``FindInitValue`` picks the matching Out/InOut function param as the initial value. The outlined ``return _store_var`` becomes ``return _store_var__rv_vN`` referencing a function-scope yield result — SSA-legal, matches what the user would have written by hand with the equivalent native-DSL escaping store pattern. This relies on the idempotence guarantee from commit 1.

Pipeline-level effect: ``ConvertToSSA_post_outline`` is added between ``OutlineClusterScopes`` and ``ConvertTensorToTileOps``. The original 4th-position ``ConvertToSSA`` is untouched.

## Test plan

- [x] Idempotence regression tests pass (``TestIdempotence::test_rerun_on_if_with_dynamic_valid_shape``, ``test_rerun_on_for_loop_with_dynamic_valid_shape``)
- [x] Existing ConvertToSSA tests pass (65 cases) — no behavioural change on first invocation
- [x] Existing outline pass tests pass (74 cases) — they exercise ``outline_*()`` directly, unaffected by the new pipeline entry
- [x] Default strategy inventory test updated (``test_pass_manager_get_strategy_default`` — ``ConvertToSSA_post_outline`` added to ``TENSOR_ONLY_PASSES``)
- [x] Full ut suite: 5867 passed (3 pre-existing unrelated runtime failures match main — ``pypto.runtime.runtime_base.Worker.current`` attribute)
- [x] Issue #1693 repro: outlined function now emits ``for i, (a__iter_v0,) in pl.range(2, init_values=(a__ssa_v0,)): ... a__rv_v1 = pl.yield_(a__ssa_v2)`` followed by ``return a__rv_v1`` — SSA-legal, no ``__FREE_VAR``

## Related issues

Fixes #1693

title: [Bug] Fused multi-output spmd scope miscompiles: per-head tile buffers coalesce → wrong results
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

When a per-token reduction like `mix_x` (`x_mixed[t] = Σ_h pre[t,h]·x[t,h,:]`) is computed in the **same** multi-output `pl.spmd` scope as other outputs (here `pre`/`post`), the generated AIV kernel computes that output **wrong** (~97.9% of elements off, small systematic error), while the other outputs (`post`, `comb`) in the same scope are correct. The **identical** source placed in its **own** `pl.spmd` scope produces correct results.

At least two distinct codegen defects surface only in the fused context:

1. **Per-head scale buffer coalescing.** The four per-head scales `pre_h = pl.reshape(pre_eps_t[h:h+1, :], [TILE, 1])` (rows of a transposed `[TILE, HC_PAD]` tile) are all allocated at the **same** UB address in the fused scope, so all four `row_expand_mul`s read head 0's coefficient. In a separate scope the same code gets distinct addresses.

   ```
   pre_h alloc addr (ptoas/*.pto):
     fused hc_post   : 74304, 74304, 74304, 74304   ← all coalesced
     separate hc_mix_x: 32768, 32832, 32896, 32960   ← distinct (base +0/+64/+128/+192), correct
   ```

2. **Residual wrongness after forcing distinct buffers.** Materializing each scale into its own buffer (`pre_h = pl.mul(pl.reshape(...), 1.0)`) makes the four addresses distinct (verified `512/576/640/704`) and the generated mix_x then looks **structurally correct** (subviews read rows 0/1/2/3, four distinct x head-slabs, four distinct `trowexpandmul`s), yet the output is **still ~97.9% wrong** on board. This residual defect is not visible at the UB-address level and is **not yet root-caused** — likely the transposed-tile data itself, or a numerical/dependency path specific to the single fused task.

Most-likely area: AIV tile memory-reuse / `pto.subview`+`reshape` of a transposed tile under UB pressure in a fused scope (the InitMemref / MemoryReuse / LegalizePtoBufferReuse / AllocateMemoryAddr pass chain).

### Steps to Reproduce

Using pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/verify_1702_fused_tileform.py` (fuses `mix_x` into the `hc_post` spmd scope):

1. On-board: `task-submit --device auto --run "python models/deepseek/v4/verify_1702_fused_tileform.py -p a2a3"` → `'x_mixed' FAIL ratio=97.94%`, `'post' PASS`, `'comb' PASS`.
2. Static (no device): run the same script locally — it dumps kernels before failing at `rtSetDevice`. Then compare per-head scale buffer addresses:
   ```
   grep -E 'pre[0-3]_inline[0-9]+__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile' build_output/_jit_*/ptoas/hc_post.pto      # fused: identical base addr
   # vs the separate-scope draft (hc_pre_fused_draft.py):
   grep -E 'pre[0-3]_inline[0-9]+__tile = pto.alloc_tile'   build_output/_jit_*/ptoas/hc_mix_x.pto       # distinct addrs
   ```

### Expected Behavior

A multi-output spmd scope that computes a per-head reduction (transpose → per-row `reshape` to `[TILE,1]` → `row_expand_mul`) produces the same correct result whether that reduction is fused into a shared scope or placed in its own scope. Per-head scale buffers must get distinct addresses and the per-head coefficients must be applied correctly.

### Actual Behavior

In the fused scope the per-head scale buffers coalesce to one UB address (all heads read head 0), and even after forcing distinct buffers the fused output remains ~97.9% wrong. The same code in a separate scope is correct.

### Git Commit ID

7fe857a895078333dd95fdc8ab915f733664c063

### NPU Kind

Other (please specify in description) — observed on pypto-lib `--platform a2a3`. Root cause is codegen address allocation (deterministic in the dumped `.pto`), not silicon-specific.

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Related: #1702, #1693, #1573 (same family — orchestration/codegen mis-aliasing of multi-output scopes; distinct triggers).
- Workaround / fallback: keeping `mix_x` in its **own** spmd scope works correctly (3-spmd "Path A" and the 4-spmd draft both pass). This blocks only the further 2-spmd fusion.
- Severity: medium (correct fallback exists).

title: fix(parser): recover call return type from annotation-less callee
body:
## Summary

A `@pl.function` callee that declares no `-> <type>` annotation but does `return <value>` (e.g. an `InCore` kernel returning its `pl.Out` tensor param) has an empty `return_types`. A plain cross-function call `c = self.kernel(...)` then built the call's `value.type` as `UnknownType`.

The printer, however, emits the assignment target's type as an LHS annotation (`c: pl.Tensor[...] = self.kernel(...)`), which the parser uses on reparse to *upgrade* the call to the concrete type. So the original IR carried `UnknownType` while the reparsed IR carried `TensorType`, and the print → parse round-trip failed structural equality at `<fn>.body[i].value.type` (`UnknownType != TensorType`).

Per first principles, the concrete type is the correct one — the original `UnknownType` was the defect.

## Fix

Derive the callee's effective return type from its first value-bearing `return` statement when the callee declares no annotation, so a plain `Call` recovers a concrete type in **both** the original build and the reparse (symmetric round-trip). The derivation flows through `deduce_call_return_type`, so dynamic shapes are substituted per call site.

- **Scoped to plain `Call`**: `pl.submit` (`as_submit`) keeps the declared types only, so its `Tuple[..., TASK_ID]` arity is unchanged (per the submit-awareness rule).
- Derived results are **cached per `Function`** to avoid re-walking the callee body on every call site (stays within the O(N log N) pass-complexity budget).
- The same helper is wired into the external-function call path.

No printed output changes (so no golden churn), and the callee's `return_types` is left untouched (no function-level structural change).

## Testing

- [x] New regression test `tests/ut/ir/parser/test_cross_function_call_return_type.py` (5 cases): reassign-existing-var (the failing case), fresh-var binding, dynamic-shape substitution, explicit-annotation control, and submit-tuple-unchanged.
- [x] Full `tests/ut/` suite: 5905 passed, 2 skipped. (2 unrelated pre-existing `TestFlattenTileNdTo2DDynamicValid` failures are a Python-3.12-only `ir.TensorType` overload issue from #1588, reproducible on `main`.)
- [x] Code review completed; `ruff` / `pyright` clean.

title: fix(passes): refine local window externalization eligibility
body:
## Summary

This PR rewrites the `OptimizeOrchTensors` Pattern 5 window externalization logic
around a stricter eligibility boundary.

The implementation keeps the callsite-local `tensor.slice` model: when a callee
is proven to write or read a local tensor window, orchestration materializes that
window near the callsite and passes it to a cloned `__windowed` callee. The cloned
callee then uses narrowed tensor parameter types and localized internal offsets.

The window externalization path does not add new PyPTO-side explicit dependency
edges, does not generate global window descriptor arrays, and does not restore
the old later full-parent-read guard from #1468. Once the callsite exposes
precise window tensors, dependency correctness is delegated to the runtime
TensorMap overlap logic.

The PR also includes a small `AutoDeriveTaskDependencies` fix: manual-scope
`TaskId` aliases are canonicalized when checking whether user deps already cover
a required edge, so codegen does not emit duplicate equivalent deps.

## Motivation

The old #1468 guard was safe but too coarse: if a later callee read a rewritten
output's parent tensor as a full tensor, `OptimizeOrchTensors` disabled output
window externalization entirely.

That caused the qwen3 legacy decode regression tracked in #1598. In that case,
q/k/v projection producers write statically known disjoint windows, but the later
`qk_norm` call reads `q_proj/k_proj` as full tensors. The guard treated that full
read as enough reason to keep the producers full-tensor, so each projection lost
intra-projection window fanout.

Current v3 fixes the core #1598 regression by allowing strictly eligible output
window producers to remain windowed even when a later full-parent read exists.
The later full read is represented honestly as a full read, and the fixed runtime
TensorMap overlap logic is responsible for building the correct dependencies.

For the legacy non-SPMD qwen decode shape, this PR also externalizes the
aggregate `qk_norm` input windows when the consumer is proven to read only the
current batch-local aggregate window. In that shape, `qk_norm__windowed` receives
`q_proj/k_proj` windows such as `[16, 5120]` and `[16, 1024]`, then performs its
internal head-loop `tile.load`s relative to those window origins.

Important boundary: this does **not** claim to solve newer SPMD qwen decode
forms where `qk_norm` is represented as one launch with a block count. Splitting
or windowing SPMD launches is a separate follow-up.

## Changes

- Refine Pattern 5 into strict static window externalization:
  - output windows are rewritten only when the write region is statically
    provable;
  - multi-`Out` rewrites remain all-or-nothing;
  - if multiple externalized `Out` params at the same callsite resolve to the
    same parent tensor, the callsite stays full-tensor instead of chaining
    multiple `tensor.assemble` updates into one parent state;
  - same-scope sibling writers to the same parent or aliased parent may remain
    windowed when each writer itself satisfies the strict output-window
    eligibility; if that same parent also has an unwindowable full `Out`/`InOut`
    sibling writer, the other writers stay full-tensor as well.
- Add conservative input-window consumer analysis:
  - an `In` tensor parameter can be windowed only when every use inside the
    callee matches the same local window;
  - accepted uses are `tile.load` and `tensor.slice`;
  - transpose loads, unsupported uses, inconsistent windows, and full-shape
    zero-offset reads stay full-tensor.
- Add aggregate input-window consumer analysis for legacy non-SPMD loop shapes:
  - the pass reuses an already-proven aggregate output window loop;
  - the input aggregate window must cover the input parent shape for that loop
    tile;
  - at least one input window offset dimension must vary with the matched loop;
  - partial aggregate reads that cannot be materialized safely stay full-tensor.
- Clone eligible callees to `__windowed` variants with narrowed tensor parameter
  types and localized internal read/write offsets.
- Materialize rewritten windows locally at the orchestration callsite with
  `tensor.slice`.
- Rebind the rewritten parent tensor SSA after `tensor.assemble`, so later
  full-parent consumers in the same orchestration scope see the post-assemble
  value rather than the original parent symbol.
- Preserve existing `Submit` semantics and the existing runtime-overlap
  dependency model for windowed tensors. Input-only `Submit` callsites stay
  full-tensor because full inputs may intentionally express wider manual-scope
  dependencies.
- Canonicalize manual-scope `TaskId` aliases in
  `AutoDeriveTaskDependencies` when checking whether user deps already cover a
  required edge, avoiding duplicate compiler deps while preserving the existing
  fallback behavior for loop-internal dynamic producers.
- Update English and zh-CN pass docs to describe the new eligibility boundary
  and dependence model. The auto-task-dependency implementation summary is also
  updated for the `TaskId` alias dedupe boundary.

## Correctness Boundary

The input-window side is intentionally a conservative sufficient condition, not
a generic "slice every input reader" optimization.

The rule is:

Only when a data-returning callee uses an `In` tensor parameter exclusively as
the same local window through `tile.load` or `tensor.slice`, the pass may
externalize that input window. Otherwise, the input remains the original full
tensor.

Callees with no data return also keep full tensor inputs. These callees may be
side-effect or dependency-fence tasks, where the full tensor argument is used to
carry a wider dependency rather than to describe the exact local data read.

This matters for DeepSeek v4 indexer.py:

- `score_init__windowed` and `score_weighted_reduce__windowed` are allowed to
  write local score windows.
- `topk` keeps reading the full score tensor.
- `topk` remains full-read because the pass cannot prove that its score input is
  a single local-window read. Windowing it naively would be a different
  algorithm, such as local topk plus merge topk, not this pass.

The dependency model is:

- window writers expose precise write regions to runtime TensorMap;
- eligible data-returning window readers expose precise read regions;
- full readers remain full readers;
- input-only `Submit` callsites remain full readers;
- no-data-return fence/side-effect consumers remain full readers;
- runtime TensorMap overlap derives the actual producer/consumer dependencies.

## Non-goals

- No new PyPTO-side explicit TaskId dependency insertion for window
  externalization.
- No canonical region dependency planner.
- No global `Tensor windows[N]` descriptor arrays.
- No later full-parent-read guard.
- No operator-name-specific rule for `topk`, `qk_norm`, or model-specific code.
- No attempt to rewrite global topk into tiled local topk.
- No claim that remaining serial cases such as `rope_kv_cache` are solved here.
- No SPMD launch splitting or SPMD input-window externalization.

## Validation

### Unit tests

```bash
python -m pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_optimize_orch_tensors.py -v
```

Current branch coverage includes:

- pure input-window consumer rewrite;
- aggregate input-window consumer rewrite for the qk_norm-shaped loop case;
- `topk` name not blocking an otherwise eligible local input window;
- full input read blocking input-window externalization;
- DeepSeek indexer-shaped `score -> topk` keeping `topk` full-read;
- same-parent, nested, if-nested, and tuple-return alias sibling writers that
  are individually windowable staying windowed and relying on runtime overlap;
- windowable writers staying full-tensor when the same parent has an
  unwindowable full writer sibling;
- loop-return aliases participating in the same-parent full-writer guard;
- duplicate multi-`Out` same-parent callsites staying full-tensor, because this
  PR does not chain multiple assembles into one accumulated parent state;
- later full-parent consumers reading the post-assemble parent SSA after an
  output-window rewrite;
- input-only `Submit` consumers staying full-tensor;
- later full-parent reads from submit callsites no longer disabling eligible
  output-window externalization;
- manual-scope mixed user/compiler deps avoiding duplicate `TaskId` deps after
  alias canonicalization;
- loop-internal dynamic producers still falling back to AUTO, while post-loop
  consumers with explicit loop-carried `TaskId` deps stay MANUAL.

Additional focused commands run for the PR diff:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py::TestManualScopeCodegen -q
python -m pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_auto_derive_task_dependencies.py -q
python -m pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_flatten_tile_nd_to_2d.py -q
```

### DeepSeek v4 indexer

pypto-lib commit:

```text
8ee6911f5f2c8737489a8d0858d17e6945ff948f
```

Command shape:

```bash
task-submit --device 8 --max-time 300 --run \
  "python models/deepseek/v4/indexer.py -p a2a3 -d {} --enable-l2-swimlane"
```

Result:

```text
'idx_kv_cache' PASS
'score' PASS
'topk_idxs' PASS
[RUN] PASS
```

Note: this PR does not claim to fix #1444 on the PyPTO side. The underlying
runtime TensorMap overlap issue for that case was fixed by
`hw-native-sys/simpler#808`. This indexer run is kept here as regression coverage
for the pass boundary: score writers may be windowed, while global `topk` stays a
full-tensor reader.

Observed orchestration:

- `score_init__windowed` writes local score windows.
- `score_weighted_reduce__windowed` writes local score windows.
- `topk` still uses full score input:

```cpp
params_t23.add_input(score_flat_inline26);
```

### Qwen decode_fwd legacy c458

pypto-lib commit:

```text
c45855eb7493d6dbd790d5cb33bc22fba23b98c5
```

Command shape:

```bash
python models/qwen3/14b/decode_fwd.py \
  -p a2a3 -d 0 --compile-only --num-layers 1 --max-seq 128
```

This was run with `--compile-only` to inspect orchestration without running
golden/runtime. `golden.runner.run_jit` returns immediately after
`_jit_compile_only` when `compile_only=True`, before generate-inputs,
compute-golden, runtime, and validation.

Observed log:

```text
[RUN] compile ...
[RUN] compile done (16.51s)
[RUN] PASS (16.51s)
```

Observed orchestration:

- `q_proj__windowed` uses a callsite-local `q_proj` window.
- `k_proj__windowed` uses a callsite-local `k_proj` window.
- `v_proj__windowed` uses a callsite-local `v_proj` window.
- `qk_norm__windowed` has windowed outputs.
- `qk_norm__windowed` also receives `q_proj/k_proj` input windows in the legacy
  non-SPMD shape:

```cpp
Tensor q_proj_inline184__rv_v2__window =
    q_proj_inline184.view(q_proj_inline184__rv_v2__window_shapes,
                          q_proj_inline184__rv_v2__window_offsets);
Tensor k_proj_inline188__rv_v2__window =
    k_proj_inline188.view(k_proj_inline188__rv_v2__window_shapes,
                          k_proj_inline188__rv_v2__window_offsets);

params_t5.add_input(q_proj_inline184__rv_v2__window);
params_t5.add_input(k_proj_inline188__rv_v2__window);
```

- The q input window is `[16, 5120]` with offset `[b0, 0]`.
- The k input window is `[16, 1024]` with offset `[b0, 0]`.
- Inside `qk_norm__windowed.pto`, q/k head-loop loads are localized to the window
  origin:
  - q load: offsets `[0, h * 640]`, size `[16, 640]`;
  - k load: offsets `[0, h * 128]`, size `[16, 128]`.
- `rope_kv_cache` remains non-windowed; this is left for follow-up work.

Earlier full runtime/swimlane evidence on the same v3 line showed that q/k/v
projection producers are windowed and overlap in the swimlane, while
`rope_kv_cache` remains serial. The newer compile-only orchestration above is
the precise evidence for `qk_norm` input-window externalization.

### DeepSeek v4 compressor_ratio4

pypto-lib commit:

```text
8ee6911f5f2c8737489a8d0858d17e6945ff948f
```

This case is useful as a writer/reader linkage witness:

- `kv_score_proj__windowed` writes disjoint scratch tensor windows.
- `state_scatter` later reads reshape/full-parent views of those scratch
  tensors.
- `kv_hadamard__windowed` writes disjoint `kv_final` windows.
- `kv_and_cache_write` later reads `kv_final`.

Remote validation passed for:

- `kv`
- `kv_state`
- `score_state`
- `kv_cache`

## Related

- Addresses the core qwen producer-side regression described in #1598.
- Keeps the DeepSeek indexer `score -> topk` pass boundary correct by leaving
  global topk as a full-tensor reader. The historical #1444 runtime correctness
  issue is not a PyPTO-side fix in this PR; it was addressed by
  `hw-native-sys/simpler#808`.
- Replaces the old #1654 strategy with a cleaner strict-eligibility,
  callsite-local externalization implementation.

title: feat(distributed): DimExpr IR node: composite dynamic dims (NR*SIZE) at all IR scopes + dynamic NR parity for AG/RS/Bcast STs
body:
## Summary

Introduces **`DimExpr`** — a first-class IR node for composite dynamic dimensions — that makes `NR * SIZE` work at **every** IR scope (HOST, Orch, InCore, chip, distributed), not just the top-level HOST scope. 

## The Problem

Before this PR, `pl.dynamic("NR")` worked as a bare `Var` in shapes. But composite dims like `NR * 64` were raw `Mul(Var("NR"), ConstInt(64))` nodes sitting in a shape list — indistinguishable from runtime arithmetic. This caused three concrete failures:

1. Any attempt to use `NR * 64` in an InCore or Orch tensor shape failed because passes at those scopes walked into the `Mul` node and treated it as runtime code.

2. **SSA verifier rejected all-composite-dim kernels.** `Tensor[[M * 2, N * 3]]` → the verifier did `As<Var>(dim)` on each shape element → `As<Var>(Mul(...))` returned `null` → `M` and `N` were never registered as defined → "undefined variable" error.

3. **Distributed codegen couldn't extract dim values.** The orchestrator codegen had no way to find `Var("NR")` inside a composite dim expression to emit the runtime shape-extraction code.

## The Solution: `DimExpr`

`DimExpr` wraps a composite dimension expression (`NR * 64`) and signals: *"this is a compile-time type annotation, not a runtime value."*

```cpp
class DimExpr : public Expr {
 public:
  ExprPtr body_;  // IgnoreField — visitors, verifiers, serialization skip this

  static constexpr auto GetFieldDescriptors() {
    return std::tuple_cat(
        Expr::GetFieldDescriptors(),
        std::make_tuple(reflection::IgnoreField(&DimExpr::body_, "body")));
  }
};
```

### Key design decisions

**`body_` is `IgnoreField`.** Every automatic visitor walk, verifier, and serializer skips the wrapped expression by default. A new pass or verifier added tomorrow handles composite dims correctly with zero code — no per-pass workarounds needed.

**Intentional unwrap on demand.** Passes that need the inner expression use `As<DimExpr>(expr)->body_`:

| Consumer | How it unwraps |
|----------|---------------|
| `structural_equal` | Unwraps before TypeName check (so `Add` vs `DimExpr(Add)` normalize to `Add` vs `Add`) |
| `AreExprsEqual` | Unwraps before ConstInt/BinaryExpr comparison |
| `SSAVerifier::RegisterTypeVarsFromExpr` | Recursively unwraps `DimExpr` → `BinaryExpr` → `Var` to register dim Vars |
| `DistributedCodegen::EmitShapeDimVarDefs` | Extracts `Var` nodes from DimExpr bodies to emit Python orchestrator defs |
| Printer | Unwraps to inner expression, with `typed_index_consts_` enabled to prevent const-folding |
| Codegen (PTO, distributed) | Unwrap: `GenerateExprString(dim_expr->body_)` |

**Opaque to default IR traversal.** `IRVisitor::VisitExpr_(DimExpr)` is a no-op. `IRMutator::VisitExpr_(DimExpr)` returns identity. This keeps type-annotation variables out of runtime SSA scope checks.

**Full IR plumbing.** `DimExpr` has its own `ObjectKind::DimExpr`, `KindTrait`, visitor/mutator/functor dispatch, Python bindings (`ir.DimExpr`, `ir.dim_expr()`), and `.pyi` stubs.

### DSL impact

```python
# This now works at ANY scope — InCore, Orch, HOST, distributed:
NR = pl.dynamic("NR")
SIZE = 64

@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
def kernel(self, a: pl.Tensor[[NR * SIZE, K], pl.FP32]) -> ...:
    out_tile = pl.load(a, [0, 0], [NR * SIZE, K])  # composite dim in load
    ...
```

The DSL user writes `NR * SIZE` naturally — the parser wraps the `Scalar` arithmetic in `ir.dim_expr(...)` automatically.

title: fix(ir): disambiguate cross-function duplicate scope name_hints
body:
## Summary

Composing independently-runnable child kernels into one `@pl.jit.host` program fails during `OutlineIncoreScopes` when the children reuse a shared `@pl.jit.inline` helper containing a scope with a fixed `name_hint`. Each child outlines the scope to an identically named function, and the two land in one program namespace, so Program construction throws `Duplicate function name "..."`.

Root cause: the three scope-outlining passes (InCore, Hierarchy, Cluster) build their `name_hint` dedup set **per function**, so a name already emitted by another function is invisible and collides only at the end.

## Fix

Thread a program-wide reserved-name set through the shared `ScopeOutliner`, seeded with the existing function names. Collisions are now resolved by shape:

- **Cross-function** (a reused helper outlined by two siblings): namespace the collision under the originating function — `single_a` keeps `dup_scope`, `single_b` gets `single_b_dup_scope`. The first function keeps the bare hint, matching its standalone compilation; call sites and definitions stay consistent.

title: fix(ir): round-trip composite shape dims through print/parse without folding
body:
## Summary

Composite (non-constant, non-Name) shape dims either failed reparse ("Shape dimension must be int literal, variable, or evaluable expression") or constant-folded (`Add(32, 32)` reparsed as `64`), so any IR carrying them failed print->parse roundtrip verification. Print -> parse is now the identity on such dims; folding stays the Simplify pass's job (it runs at the beginning of the pipeline and folds them after parsing).

Three stacked bugs prevented this:

- **`pl.const` folded at eval time.** The runtime `pl.const` stub returns the raw Python number, and shape annotations are resolved via Python `eval()`, so `pl.const(32, pl.INT64) + pl.const(32, pl.INT64)` folded to `64` and dropped the dtype before the parser saw an IR node. The parser now rebuilds composite shape dims from the AST (`_rebuild_composite_dim`) and accepts DSL `Scalar` composites (e.g. `m + 0` over a `pl.dynamic` var) by unwrapping the IR tree they already carry.
- **Spurious TileView from pointer-equality.** `ShapeExprListsEquivalent` / `AreExprsEqual` compared non-ConstInt dims by pointer, so reparsed composite `valid_shape`s never collapsed to the canonical implicit view and gained a `TileView` out of thin air. `AreExprsEqual` now compares binary composites structurally (same kind, recursively equal operands; Var leaves stay pointer-equal), the TileView hash mirrors it, and `ShapeExprListsEquivalent` delegates to it.
- **Pointer-distinct dyn vars.** `ExprEvaluator.get_or_create_dynvar` ignored `DynVar._ir_var`, so annotations and call args resolved the same `pl.dynamic` name to different `ir.Var` instances.

A pure-ConstInt composite would still print as bare `32 + 32` (indistinguishable from user closure arithmetic, which folds by design), so the printer now emits typed leaves (`pl.const(32, pl.INDEX)`) inside composite shape dims and pure-const arithmetic trees; everything else prints unchanged.

The `VerificationLevel.NONE` bypass in the MemoryReuse structural-shape regression is no longer needed and is removed.

## Testing

- [x] New parameterized roundtrip tests in `tests/ut/ir/printing/test_python_printer.py` (bare var, var+const, var*const, var//const, nested, const INDEX composite, const INT64 composite) + typed-leaf printing assertion
- [x] `test_memory_reuse.py` structural-shape regression now runs under default conftest roundtrip verification
- [x] Full UT suite: 5919 passed; the only 2 failures are the pre-existing `TestFlattenTileNdTo2DDynamicValid` mixed int/Var `TensorType` setup failures, also failing on clean main
- [x] clang-tidy clean on changed C++ files; pre-commit hooks pass
- [x] Docs updated (en + zh-cn) for typed const leaves in composite dims

title: [Pass Bug] Orchestration marks pld.tensor.put dst window as add_input, dropping its write deps
body:
### Pass Name

Orchestration codegen (task Arg direction derivation for distributed ops)

### Description

When an InCore scope pushes to a peer's window via `pld.tensor.put`, orchestration codegen declares the **dst** `DistributedTensor` window as `add_input`. The dst of a put is a cross-rank **write** target, so the task graph records no write on the window: a downstream task that reads the same window gets a read-read pair (no RAW edge) and can run before the push completes, reading stale window data.

`pld.tile.remote_store` to the same window correctly emits `add_output`, so the identical kernel with the push expressed as `pl.load` + `remote_store` is race-free.

Found in DeepSeek-V4 2-rank EP MoE (pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/combine.py`): `combine_push` pushes `recv_y` rows to the peer's `routed_y_buf` window, then `combine_reduce` (separate spmd task) reads `routed_y_buf`. With the put form, `combine_reduce` races ahead of `combine_push` → wrong values with shifting locations (~10-30% of points off, validation fails). With `remote_store`, repeated PASS.

### Git Commit ID

454ecc9ab0e0843ffd89e03124e75b82a9d71cd2

### Before IR

InCore scope (jit.inline pl.at, simplified):

```python
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="combine_push"):
    ...
    pld.tensor.put(dst=routed_y_buf, peer=dst, src=recv_y_flat,
                   dst_offsets=[r_route, 0], src_offsets=[idx_lin, 0], shape=[1, D])
    # notify/wait barrier on combine_done ...

for tb in pl.spmd(T // 4, name_hint="combine_reduce"):
    ...  # reads routed_y_buf
```

### Expected IR

Generated orchestration declares the put dst window as a write (same as remote_store form):

```cpp
// Task 16: combine_push
params_t16.add_input(recv_y_flat...);
params_t16.add_output(ext_routed_y_buf);   // write recorded -> RAW edge to combine_reduce
```

### Actual IR / Error

```cpp
// Task 16: combine_push
params_t16.add_input(ext_routed_y_buf);    // dst window declared as input
params_t16.add_input(recv_y_flat...);
```

`combine_reduce` (`add_input(ext_routed_y_buf)`) then has no dependency on `combine_push` and reads the window before the push lands. On 2x a2a3 devices the model output fails ratio_reldiff with errors scattered across rows; flipping only the push back to `pld.tile.remote_store` (dst emitted as `add_output`) passes consistently.

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B (a2a3, 2 devices)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

title: inline sub-functions cannot contain hand-placed scopes (auto_scope=False not inheritable) — blocks manual 4-ring tuning
body:
## Summary

Hand-placed runtime scopes (`with pl.scope()`) cannot be used inside `@pl.jit.inline` sub-functions: the inline decorator rejects `auto_scope=`, and the JIT specializer always re-emits inline functions as `@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Inline)` without an auto_scope suffix. As a result, any model whose kernels are structured with inline sub-functions (the standard layout for layered LLMs) cannot do manual ring-level tuning at all — the only workaround is hand-inlining the whole sub-function into the entry.

## Context / motivation

The PTO2 runtime supports max 4 scope levels (4 HeapRings). With default `auto_scope=True`, compiler-placed AUTO scopes for deep loop nests (7 levels in Qwen3-14B `prefill_fwd`) collapse all inner levels into ring 3 — measured via scope_stats: ring3 carries 1.39 GB / 27.7k task-window slots while r0–r2 sit at ~0%. Hand-placing 4 balanced scopes (entry implicit + layer / token-block / token) reduces ring3 task-window pressure ~38% and moves ~10.5k slots to r0/r2. We could only realize this after manually inlining `prefill_layer` (~460 lines) into the entry.

## Reproduction

```python
@pl.jit.inline
def layer(...):
    for p0_idx in pl.range(tok_blocks):
        with pl.scope():     # Error: a hand-placed AUTO 'with pl.scope()' requires @pl.function(auto_scope=False)
            ...

@pl.jit(auto_scope=False)
def entry(...):
    for layer_idx in pl.range(n):
        with pl.scope():
            layer(...)
```

`@pl.jit.inline(auto_scope=False)` raises:
`TypeError: @pl.jit.inline does not accept an auto_scope= argument`

Patching the runtime flag does not help because the specializer re-parses from source:
- `pypto/jit/decorator.py:1794` — sub-decorators reject `auto_scope=`
- `pypto/jit/specializer.py:1641` — `if ctx.func_type == "inline": return "@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Inline)"` (drops `auto_scope_suffix`)
- `pypto/language/parser/ast_parser.py:3412` — parse-time check rejects hand AUTO scope when flag is true

## Proposed fix

Let inline sub-functions inherit (or accept) the caller's `auto_scope` flag:
1. allow `auto_scope=` on `@pl.jit.inline` (or propagate caller's flag at specialize time — `build_specialize_context(auto_scope=dep._auto_scope)` already plumbs it),
2. emit the suffix in the specializer inline branch: `@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Inline{auto_scope_suffix})`.

Scope semantics are unchanged — after inlining the body, scopes land inside the entry, exactly like the hand-inlined workaround.

## Environment

pypto main 2693682e, simpler 48980572, Qwen3-14B prefill_fwd (pypto-lib 65871d8), a2a3.

title: No way to create/retype tensors with symbolic dynamic dims — loop-carried hidden state forces per-layer copy-back
body:
## Summary

There is no way to create (or retype) a tensor whose dynamic dim carries the same *symbolic* dynamic var as a parameter, so a loop-carried hidden-state variable cannot be reassigned across layers once a sub-function boundary is removed. This blocks the natural ping-pong pattern and forces a full copy-back per layer.

## Reproduction

```python
PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN = pl.dynamic("PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN")

@pl.jit(auto_scope=False)
def entry(hidden_states: pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, HIDDEN], pl.BF16], ...):
    prefill_tokens = pl.tensor.dim(hidden_states, 0)
    for layer_idx in pl.range(num_layers):
        nxt = pl.create_tensor([prefill_tokens, HIDDEN], dtype=pl.BF16)
        ...  # compute layer into nxt
        hidden_states = nxt
        # Error: Cannot reassign 'hidden_states' with a different type:
        #   was pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, 5120], BF16],
        #   got pl.Tensor[[pl.tensor.dim(hidden_states, 0), 5120], BF16]
```

Attempted workarounds, all rejected:
- `pl.create_tensor([PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, HIDDEN])` — dim is recorded as the runtime expression, not the symbolic var, so the types still differ.
- `nxt.bind_dynamic(0, PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN)` on a created tensor — `bind_dynamic` is parameter-only / unsupported there.
- A tiny `@pl.jit.inline` retype shim with the symbolic return annotation — the specializer substitutes the actual dim expression at the inline boundary, so the result type is again the expression.

The only working pattern is per-layer copy-back (`pl.assemble` of every tile into the parameter buffer), costing tokens x hidden x 2B of extra write traffic per layer. Inline sub-functions used to launder the type at the call boundary (callee param re-anchors to the symbolic dyn), which is why the original `prefill_layer` structure compiled — remove the boundary and the limitation surfaces.

## Proposed capability

Either:
1. let `pl.create_tensor` accept symbolic dyn vars and record them as the dim type, or
2. unify the type checker so `pl.tensor.dim(param, 0)` is recognized as equal to the param's symbolic dyn dim, or
3. provide an explicit `pl.retype(t, [PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, HIDDEN])`.

## Environment

pypto main 2693682e, simpler 48980572, Qwen3-14B prefill_fwd (pypto-lib 65871d8), a2a3.

title: fix(parser): unify tensor.dim shape dims with symbolic dyn vars
body:
## Summary

- Loop-carried reassignment of a dynamic-shaped tensor (`hidden_states = nxt` where `nxt = pl.create_tensor([pl.tensor.dim(hidden_states, 0), HIDDEN], ...)`) was rejected with `Cannot reassign ... with a different type` because the parser type check compared the runtime `tensor.dim` Call against the parameter's symbolic dyn var. The only workaround was a full per-layer copy-back.
- The canonicalization lives in the C++ arith layer, not the parser: `RewriteSimplifier` gains a gated rule rewriting `tensor.dim(t, axis)` to `t`'s static shape dim (negative axes normalized, chains resolved depth-bounded via `RecursiveRewrite`). The flag (`set_canonicalize_tensor_dim`) is off by default — the rewrite is only valid in shape/type positions; runtime values must keep the `tensor.dim` call or annotation-only dyn vars would leak past SSA conversion. The same flag can later be enabled in the Simplify pass's `SimplifyType` if pipeline-wide shape canonicalization is wanted.
- The parser's `_types_match` just enables the flag on its analyzer and registers scalar INDEX aliases (`tokens = pl.tensor.dim(h, 0)`) as var substitutions; alias entries drop on reassignment. Genuinely different static dims are still rejected.
- Cross-layer sync: C++ header/impl, nanobind binding, and `arith.pyi` stub updated together.
- Docs: dynamic-shape section now shows the loop-carried ping-pong pattern (EN + zh-CN).

title: [Bug] #1702 follow-up: 507018 still triggers in a separate decoder model after PR #1718 — multi-output spmd return aliasing in additional code paths
body:
**Repository**: `hw-native-sys/pypto` > Filed as a follow-up after locally verifying PR #1718 against an internal > 45-layer decoder model on Ascend a2a3 (real device, single rank, dummy > weights). The orchestration codegen + chip_orch compile chain are **green** > end-to-end, chip workers come up cleanly, and 19 InCore kernels link, but > the very first AICPU stream synchronize still produces > `aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018`. The PR's author > explicitly noted on commit `0f4881cb` that "tuple / `__ssa_v1` / `__phi` > paths are untouched" — we believe one of those paths is what this model > hits. ## Summary PR #1718 (commits `80845cdf` + `0f4881cb`) fixed `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` and `VarLineageCollector::VisitStmt_(AssignStmt)` to disambiguate a multi-Out spmd-scope return via the result Var's SSA base, replacing the blind `out_indices[0]` fallback. That fix is correct and validated on the DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre + mix_x` kernel cited in the PR commit message. **It does not fix the 507018 we hit on a separate decoder model**, which uses sibling InCore patterns that the SSA-base disambiguation cannot uniquely resolve (or that go through one of the explicitly-untouched lineage paths). The downstream symptom is identical to the dsv4 trigger that PR #1718 fixes: all kernels and orchestration compile, the chip becomes `ready`, then the very first stream sync poisons the device with 507018 and `aclrtResetDeviceForce` is needed to unstick the card. Per the original #1702 root-cause write-up, this strongly suggests another instance of the same family (orchestration mis-aliasing a multi-output scope to the wrong output, kernel emits a shape that fails `valid_reshape` on AICPU, scope never FINs, scheduler latches GLOBAL_STUCK). ## What PR #1718 fixes (recap, for context) From the PR's own commit messages: - `80845cdf` — In `GenerateSingleReturnAlias`, when the result Var's SSA base uniquely matches one Out/InOut arg, use that mapping instead of the unreliable `FindReturnedParamIndex().value_or(out_indices[0])`. Validated on board against the DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre` kernel fused with `mix_x` in the same multi-output spmd scope. - `0f4881cb` — Apply the same SSA-base disambiguation in `VarLineageCollector::VisitStmt_(AssignStmt)` (the lineage-tracer sibling path), and add two regression tests in `tests/ut/codegen/test_spmd_scope_tid_codegen.py`. The commit message of `80845cdf` explicitly notes: > Same family as #1573 / #1693 (orchestration mis-aliasing multi-output > scopes), distinct trigger and code path; **those paths > (tuple / `__ssa_v1` / `__phi`) are untouched**. ## What still fails (post-merge, on board) After ff-merging PR #1718 into `main` and rebuilding the Python package, a single-rank single-layer decode through our internal model (TP=8/EP=8 layer on `device_ids=[0]`, `--dummy-weights`) reaches kernel exec but immediately poisons the AICPU on first sync. ### Environment | Component | Pin | |---|---| | pypto | `main` at `0f4881cb` (PR #1718 ff-merged) | | simpler runtime (submodule) | `afb5c5a9` (origin/main, with a local `runtime_compiler.py` host-strip patch — unrelated to this issue) | | pto-isa | `109c9f72` | | PTOAS binary | `v0.44` | | Python | 3.11.14 (`--system-site-packages` over CANN's torch_npu 2.9.0) | | CANN | 9.0.0-beta.1 | | Driver | 25.5.1 | | Hardware | Ascend 910B (a2a3) — 8-card pod, this run uses logical `device_ids=[0]` | ### Reproducer (model command, no isolated minimal repro) > The PR's own commit message acknowledges that this family does **not** > reproduce in a standalone `@pl.program` UT — "it only triggers through the > jit.inline + tail-appended `create_tensor`-scratch path that this kernel > exercises" — and that a faithful regression test was tracked as a follow-up. > The same isolation difficulty applies to our trigger: any standalone scope > we extract drops the surrounding orchestration that drives > `FindReturnedParamIndex` to nullopt + ambiguous SSA base. The reproducer > below uses the full model command; we are happy to bisect further if > instrumentation guidance helps. The model in question (an internal 45-layer MoE/dense-mix decoder with TP=8, EP=8 wave fan-out) is in our private fork; if you can suggest specific orchestration-pass dump flags that would let us pinpoint the offending scope without sharing the model code, we will run them and attach the output. Compile chain that succeeds (sanitized log): ``` V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/full_k_proj.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/full_q_proj.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/full_gate_proj.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_out_proj_aiv.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_head_gate.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/dense_down_proj_tp_aiv.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_out_resid_add.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/dense_residual_add_tp.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/dense_gate_up_silu_tp_aiv.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/dense_gate_up_silu_tp_aic.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/full_v_proj.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/tp_all_reduce.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_qk_norm_zc.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/dense_down_proj_tp_aic.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_rope_kv_cache.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/full_fa_fused_aic.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/dense_post_rmsnorm_zc.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_rmsnorm_zc.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_fa_fused_aiv.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/full_out_proj_aic.cpp V5 [Orchestration] Compiling: .../orchestration/chip_orch.cpp ... 19 InCore objects emitted, all successful (sizes 115k..463k bytes) V5 [Orchestration] Compilation .../chip_orch.cpp.orch_*.so successful: 738120 bytes [chip_process pid=

dev=0] ready ``` Failure (immediate, on first AICPU sync): ``` [ERROR] sync_run_streams: [device_runner_base.cpp:877] aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018 [ERROR] recover_device_or_mark_unusable: [device_runner.cpp:456] Device unrecoverable after AICore error 507018: aclrtSynchronizeDeviceWithTimeout failed: 507046. Marking DeviceRunner unusable; run() will fail fast and finalize() will force-reset the card (a soft in-process reset does not clear the poison). [WARN] force_reset_device: [device_runner.cpp:553] force_reset_device: aclrtResetDeviceForce(0) cleared the poisoned card RuntimeError: WorkerThread::dispatch_process: child failed (code=1): chip_process dev=0: RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018 ``` The 2-second gap between the AICPU 507018 and the `recover_device_or_mark_unusable` line is the same scheduler-stuck signature documented in PR #1718's commit message (scope never FINs → GLOBAL_STUCK latches → host-side timeout). The kernel side and the orchestration side both compiled cleanly through the same passes the dsv4 case goes through; this is not a new error class, just a new trigger of the existing family. ## Suspected scope class The 19 InCore kernels above include several with multi-output, same-shape returns that are good candidates for the untouched `tuple` / `__ssa_v1` / `__phi` paths called out on commit `0f4881cb`. From a static read: - `dense_gate_up_silu_tp_aic` / `..._aiv` — TP-sliced fused (gate, up, silu) tile emits two same-shape (or near-same-shape) GM outputs from a single InCore scope; if the outliner appends scratch/`create_tensor` tails the way the dsv4 kernel did, the same `out_indices[0]` blind fallback could fire. - `tp_all_reduce` — ring all-reduce body has multi-window writes (signal + data) that are different shapes but share an SSA-renamed parent through the per-step phi. - `full_qk_norm_zc` — fused (q-norm, k-norm) with two same-shape outputs. - `full_rope_kv_cache` — co-emits q-rotated, k-rotated, KV-cache slot writes. - MoE dispatch / combine / routed-expert paths — multi-rank fan-out scopes that each return multiple per-expert buffers (this run does not exercise the MoE path because layer 0 is `full_dense`, but the same family applies). We have not yet bisected which of these is the actual offender. The simplest in-house path is to port the dsv4 PR #474 workaround pattern (scalar `pl.write` → `add_output`) into each candidate, but that's a model-side band-aid for a codegen-side root cause and is exactly what PR #1718 was supposed to make unnecessary. ## Suggested fix direction The PR explicitly carves out three sibling lineage paths as untouched — **tuple**, **`__ssa_v1`**, and **`__phi`**. Extending the SSA-base disambiguation introduced in PR #1718 to those paths (or, conversely, hardening every consumer of the lineage tracer / `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` result so it cannot silently fall back to `out_indices[0]` when the SSA base fails to uniquely resolve) would close the family completely. Two concrete asks: 1. Could the team look at whether the PR #1718 SSA-base check can be propagated into `VarLineageCollector` for the tuple/phi/`__ssa_v1` cases — the same pattern (uniquely-matching Out/InOut arg by SSA root) should apply. 2. If a kernel that hits this latches the device with `force_reset_device` needed (vs. a clean Python exception), it would help us a lot if the AICPU diagnostic could surface the **scope name** that failed `valid_reshape` — currently we only see `507018` host-side, with no pointer to which `chip_orch.cpp` line emitted the bad reshape. ## What we tried locally - Verified PR #1718 ff-merges cleanly onto current `main` (`a1b066df`, origin/main as of 2026-06-09), no submodule pin shift. - Rebuilt pypto under Python 3.11 (`pip install --no-build-isolation .`). - Confirmed our smoke probe and an a2a3sim compile of the full layer chain are still green after the merge. - Single-rank, dummy-weights dispatch on a real Ascend a2a3 still produces the 507018 above. ## References - PR #1718 — `fix(codegen): also resolve multi-output spmd return in the lineage tracer; add regression tests (#1702)` - Issue #1702 — original SSA aliasing report (the same downstream symptom we still observe). - Issue #1693 — the predecessor in the same family. - Issue #1573 — earlier in the same family. - DeepSeek-V4 PR #474 — the model-side scalar `pl.write` → `add_output` workaround that some downstream models use to avoid the family entirely. We can attach a sanitized full plog or run a one-off instrumentation patch on our pod if it would help triage. Thanks for getting #1702 across the line at the dsv4 site — happy to chase the residual cases together.

title: fix(ir): treat pld.tile.{put,get} dst as write target in InCore param-dir analysis
body:
## Summary

`ConvertTensorToTileOps` lowers `pld.tensor.{put,get}` to `pld.tile.{put,get}` and then runs `UpgradeWrittenTensorParamDirections` to promote in-place-written InCore params from `In` to `Out`/`InOut`. The per-call read/write classifier `AnalyzeCallAccess` already special-cases `pld.tile.remote_store` (target is a write), but `pld.tile.put` and `pld.tile.get` fell into the catch-all that marks every arg as a read.

As a result, an InCore body whose only window-write was a `pld.tensor.put` (cross-rank TPUT to a peer's window slot) or `pld.tensor.get` (TGET into the local window slot) left its window param as `In`. `DeriveCallDirections` then emitted `ArgDirection::Input` for the host_orch's Submit, and orchestration codegen translated that to `add_input(ext_win)` instead of `add_output(...)`. The task graph recorded no write on the window, a downstream reader saw only read-read with no RAW edge, and races followed (DeepSeek-V4 2-rank EP MoE `combine_push → combine_reduce`, ~10-30% wrong outputs).

## Fix

Add a unified `pld.tile.put` / `pld.tile.get` branch to `AnalyzeCallAccess` and `GetWriteTargetExpr` that marks `dst` (args[0]) as the write target, mirroring the existing `pld.tile.remote_store` handling. The downstream flow (`DeriveCallDirections` → orchestration codegen) is unchanged and now correctly produces `add_output(ext_dst)` for the window slot, restoring the RAW edge.

## Tests

- Updated `test_put_emits_tile_create_plus_tile_put` and `test_get_emits_tile_create_plus_tile_get` Expected programs to declare `dst: pl.Out[pld.DistributedTensor[...]]`, reflecting the corrected post-pass signature.
- Full ut suite green (5963 passed).

Fixes #1732

title: fix(jit): render Array-typed params in specialized source
body:
## Summary

Fix the `@pl.jit` AST specializer so that **parameters that are neither
tensors nor scalars** — specifically fixed-size on-core `pl.Array[N, dtype]`
arrays — round-trip through specialization with their annotation rendered.

The motivating case is the **TaskId-array dependency-threading idiom**: a
`tids: pl.Array[N, pl.TASK_ID]` parameter used to carry `pl.submit` /
`pl.at(deps=...)` task handles across `pl.manual_scope` boundaries (and across
`@pl.jit.inline` helper boundaries).

## Problem

`Specializer._build_params` only knew how to annotate tensor params and scalar
params. Any other annotated param fell through to a bare `else` that emitted
just the name. For an `Array`-typed param the generated `@pl.function` source
then looked like:

```python
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Inline)
def helper(self, a: pl.Tensor[[16, 16], pl.FP32], tids, out: pl.Tensor[[16, 16], pl.FP32]):
    ...
```

…and PyPTO parsing rejected it:

```
ParserTypeError: Parameter 'tids' missing type annotation
```

So an inline/JIT helper could not accept a TaskId array (or any `pl.Array`)
parameter at all.

## Changes

`python/pypto/jit/specializer.py`:

1. **Render the annotation.** In `_specialize_function`, scan params that are
   neither tensor nor scalar; for each one whose typed annotation evaluates to a
   language `Array`, pre-render `pl.Array[<extent>, <dtype>]` with closure
   constants folded (`N` → `4`). Evaluation is best-effort (`try/except`):
   anything that doesn't resolve to an `Array` stays bare, exactly as before.
2. **Thread it through `_build_params`** via a new `extra_anns` argument; the
   previously-bare `else` branch now emits `name: <annotation>`.
3. **Correct dtype rendering** (`_array_dtype_str`): prefer the canonical
   `_DTYPE_TO_PL` map so dtypes whose enum `str` diverges from the DSL constant
   render correctly — **`BF16` → `pl.BF16`**, not the enum-`str` form
   `pl.BFLOAT16` (which does not exist on `pl` and would crash the generated
   module at import). Fall back to the upper-cased enum name for dtypes outside
   the map — notably `TASK_ID`, which is intentionally absent from
   `_DTYPE_TO_PL` (it is not a tensor/tile element dtype) but does have a
   `pl.TASK_ID` constant. BF16 is heavily used in the LLM orchestration kernels
   this idiom targets, so this path is realistic, not theoretical.

After the fix:

```python
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Inline)
def helper(self, a: pl.Tensor[[16, 16], pl.FP32], tids: pl.Array[4, pl.TASK_ID], out: pl.Tensor[[16, 16], pl.FP32]):
    ...
```

## Test plan

New `TestArrayParamAnnotation` in `tests/ut/jit/test_specializer.py`:

- `_build_params` plumbing: `extra_anns` emitted as `name: <annotation>`; bare
  fallback preserved when absent.
- End-to-end `specialize()` rendering for `pl.Array[N, pl.TASK_ID]` with the
  closure constant `N` folded, a literal extent, and a non-TASK_ID dtype
  (`pl.Array[8, pl.INT32]`).
- **BF16 regression**: `pl.Array[4, pl.BF16]` renders as `pl.BF16` and never
  `BFLOAT16` (the case that exposed the dtype-rendering bug).
- Generated source is valid Python (`ast.parse`) and carries no bare param.
- Best-effort path: an unevaluable annotation stays bare without raising.

Verification (worktree build):

- [x] `tests/ut/jit/test_specializer.py` — 88 passed
- [x] `tests/ut/jit/` full directory — 257 passed
- [x] ruff + pyright clean on both changed files
