title: fix(ir): preserve subview offsets when MemoryReuse retargets a sharing group
body:
## Summary
- Root cause of #1723 defect 1: `ApplyMemRefSharing` in `memory_reuse_pass.cpp` propagated the reuse target MemRef wholesale to every sharing-group member, erasing the byte offset/size of subview members (slice/reshape of the shared buffer). In a fused multi-output spmd scope the four per-head `[TILE, 1]` row slices of a transposed scale tile all collapsed onto offset 0, so every head read head 0's coefficients (~97.9% of `x_mixed` wrong on board). The same code in its own spmd scope had no earlier dead buffer to retarget onto and stayed correct.
- Fix: rebase each sharing-group member's MemRef onto the target allocation, preserving its offset relative to the group representative and its own size. Members at the representative's offset/size keep the target MemRef object itself, so plain (non-subview) reuse still shares MemRef identity.

## Testing
- New on-device ST `tests/st/runtime/cross_core/test_spmd_multi_output_subview.py`: fused spmd scope computing a per-token combine plus a per-head reduction with golden compare. Pre-fix the four per-head scale `alloc_tile`s land at one UB address (all heads read head 0); post-fix they sit at distinct offsets (+0/+64/+128/+192).
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` + `tests/ut/codegen/`: 2067 passed.

## Related Issues
Fixes #1723 (defect 1, buffer coalescing). Defect 2 (residual mismatch after forcing distinct buffers) remains under investigation.

title: [Pass Bug] AutoDeriveTaskDependencies demotes user-written pl.manual_scope() to AUTO when deps go through a pl.array of TaskIds → full serialization
body:
### Pass Name

AutoDeriveTaskDependencies

### Description

Since PR #1701 (commit `f9a9e5b1`), `AutoDeriveTaskDependencies` analyzes **user-written `pl.manual_scope()`** bodies in the default pipeline. Hand-tuned MPMD kernels commonly express dependencies by collecting per-iteration TaskIds from a `pl.parallel` / `pl.at` fan-out into a `pl.array.create(..., pl.TASK_ID)`, then referencing them downstream as `deps=[arr[i], ...]`.

The pass cannot resolve a TaskId **array-element** dep (`arr[i]`) back to the loop producer's TaskId var, so for every real RAW/WAW hazard against a loop-fanned producer it computes `covered_by_user_edge=false`. Because that producer is `dynamic_producer=true` (inside a loop), it triggers the `dynamic_prior_producer_requires_scope_lift` fallback, which **strips the scope and demotes it to `manual=false` (AUTO)**.

Once the scope is AUTO, runtime TensorMap/OverlapMap tracking re-engages. The model's tasks atomic-add / `assemble` into shared buffers with overlapping regions, so the runtime conservatively serializes every writer — i.e. the entire scope runs **fully serial**, which is exactly what the user wrote `pl.manual_scope()` to avoid.

Net effect: a valid, idiomatic manual scope (explicit `deps=` only, no runtime tracking) silently loses all its parallelism. The user's `deps=[arr[i]]` edges are correct and complete; the pass just can't statically match them.

### Git Commit ID

f9a9e5b1434b580904dece31e933f2e17a2c5bec

### Before IR (Input)

Condensed structure that triggers the demotion (a real Qwen3-14B decode layer hits this in 4 separate manual scopes). The key shape is: TaskId array + `pl.parallel` producer fan-out writing a shared buffer + a downstream consumer that depends on the producers via `deps=[arr[i]]`.

```python
import pypto.language as pl

@pl.program
class Before:
    @pl.function
    def main(self, x: pl.Tensor[[128, 512], pl.BF16],
             w: pl.Tensor[[512, 512], pl.BF16],
             acc: pl.Tensor[[128, 512], pl.FP32]) -> None:
        with pl.manual_scope():
            prod_tids = pl.array.create(4, pl.TASK_ID)
            # producer fan-out: 4 tasks each atomic-add a column block of `acc`
            for n in pl.parallel(4):
                n0 = n * 128
                with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="producer") as p_tid:
                    c = pl.matmul(x, w[:, n0:n0 + 128], out_dtype=pl.FP32)
                    acc = pl.assemble(acc, c, [0, n0], atomic=pl.AtomicType.Add)
                prod_tids[n] = p_tid               # collect per-iteration TaskId

            # consumer reads ALL of `acc` (true RAW) and depends on the producers
            # ONLY through the TaskId array elements — this is what the pass can't match
            with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="consumer",
                       deps=[prod_tids[0], prod_tids[1], prod_tids[2], prod_tids[3]]):
                s = pl.row_sum(pl.mul(acc, acc))
                # ... uses s ...
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

The `pl.manual_scope()` stays **MANUAL**. The pass adds no compiler edges (the user already covered the hazard via the array deps) and does **not** demote the scope:

```text
RuntimeScopeStmt(manual=True, name_hint="...")
  # producer / consumer tasks keep their user deps=[prod_tids[...]]
  # no compiler_manual_dep_edges added; scope is NOT lifted to AUTO
```

Codegen then emits `PTO2_SCOPE(PTO2ScopeMode::MANUAL)`, runtime TensorMap/OverlapMap tracking stays suppressed, and the fan-out runs in parallel as authored. (Equivalent to pre-#1701 behavior for this scope.)

### Actual IR or Error

Every manual scope is demoted to AUTO; `compiler_manual_dep_edges` is empty everywhere:

```text
=== SCOPE AUTO:.../AUTO:...  (tasks..., user_edges=N, compiler_edges=0) ===   # was MANUAL
RuntimeScopeStmt(manual=False, ...)   # demoted; PTO2_SCOPE() instead of PTO2_SCOPE(MANUAL)
```

With `PYPTO_AUTO_DEPS_LOOP_CARRY_DEBUG=1`, the pass logs the cause for each downstream consumer:

```text
hazard call=consumer prior_task_id=p_tid_..._ssa_v0 covered_by_user_edge=false dynamic_producer=true
fallback_reason=dynamic_prior_producer_requires_scope_lift call=consumer
```

Real-model evidence (Qwen3-14B decode `qwen3_decode_mpmd`, compiled via `compile_for_test`): all 4 manual scopes fall back; consumers `residual_rms_cast{,_0..3}__windowed`, `post_rms_reduce`, `silu`, `down_cast_residual` each report `dynamic_prior_producer_requires_scope_lift` with `covered_by_user_edge=false` against loop producers `out_tid` / `gate_tid` / `down_tid`.

Fallback decision site: `src/ir/transforms/auto_derive_task_dependencies_pass.cpp:973` (the `covered_by_user_edge` check + `dynamic_producer` lift). The matcher `CanonicalizeTaskIds` / `LookupTaskIdForVar` has no lineage for `pl.array` TaskId store/load, so `deps=[arr[i]]` never canonicalizes to the producer var.

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific) — the demotion happens in the IR pass; the serialization manifests at runtime but is independent of NPU arch.

### Host Platform (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Additional Context

**Why model-side can't work around it:** the producers are fundamentally a `pl.parallel` fan-out (tens of tasks), so their TaskIds can only be collected via a `pl.array`; the consumer genuinely reads the whole shared buffer (true RAW, not separable). There is also no switch to skip manual-scope analysis — `analyze_auto_scopes_for_deps` only gates AUTO scopes, and the pass reads only the `PYPTO_AUTO_DEPS_LOOP_CARRY_DEBUG` debug env var.

**Suggested fixes (for discussion):**
1. Teach the pass to resolve TaskId-array element deps: track `pl.array` TASK_ID store/load lineage so `deps=[arr[i]]` (filled by `arr[i] = producer_tid`) canonicalizes to the producer TaskId. Then `covered_by_user_edge=true`, no fallback, scope stays MANUAL — model unchanged.
2. Add an opt-out (e.g. `derive_manual_scope_deps=False` via `RunConfig` / `ir.compile`) so a user-written `pl.manual_scope()` is honored verbatim and never demoted to AUTO (restores pre-#1701 semantics).
3. Design question: should a user's explicit `pl.manual_scope()` be treated as fully user-managed, with AUTO-derivation limited to AUTO / compiler-generated scopes?

Related: RFC #1368 (Automatic manual-scope task dependency derivation) flagged "disjointness can't be proven statically" as an open question; this is a concrete manifestation. Introduced by #1701.

**Reproduction** (no device needed): compile the orchestration via `compile_for_test`, walk each `RuntimeScopeStmt`, and observe `manual=False` with `compiler_edges=0`; re-run with `PYPTO_AUTO_DEPS_LOOP_CARRY_DEBUG=1` to capture the `fallback_reason=dynamic_prior_producer_requires_scope_lift` lines.

title: fix(codegen): trace view-store returns to the real Out param (#1702)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1702. A `pl.spmd` / multi-output scope whose kernel writes its `Out` param through a **view** (`tensor.slice` / `tensor.reshape`) and returns the result produced a return value that `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` could not trace back to a param.

`FindReturnedParamIndex`'s tracer (`TraceVarToParam`, `orchestration_analysis.cpp`) only followed `tensor.assemble` / `tile.store` / `tensor.set_validshape`, so a view-store return resolved to `nullopt` and the alias fell back to `out_indices[0]` — the **first** `Out`/`InOut` param, which for a fanned-out scope is per-block scratch, not the real result. Every downstream consumer of the scope's return was then routed into the wrong buffer; a numel-mismatched reshape tripped the AICPU `valid_reshape` assert, the subtask aborted without writing FIN, and the scheduler latched `GLOBAL_STUCK` — surfacing on the host as `507018`. A kernel-side shape bug thus masqueraded as a scheduler deadlock.

## Fix

Follow `tensor.slice` / `tensor.reshape` to their source buffer (`args[0]`) in `TraceVarToParam`, mirroring the existing `assemble` / `store` / `set_validshape` rules, so the return resolves precisely to the actual `Out` param.

**Crucial refinement (this is why the first attempt was reverted):** unlike the write rules, `slice`/`reshape` are pure **read** views. A kernel may legitimately *return a view of an `In` param* while writing its real result into `out_indices[0]`. The unconditional view rule mis-traced such a return back to the `In` param and aliased the call site to the input buffer — reintroducing the very numel-mismatch / `507018` failure mode it set out to fix (regressed `qwen3 decode_layer` and dist `ep_dispatch_combine` in CI). The slice/reshape trace is therefore **gated on the resolved root being an `Out`/`InOut` param** (effective directions for Group/Spmd wrappers). When the root is an `In` param, the return is treated as untraceable and the legacy `out_indices[0]` fallback is kept — exactly the pre-#1702 behavior for that case.

> Note: a buffer-root-matching approach does **not** work here — `BufferRootCollector` itself falls back to `out_roots[0]` for non-tuple calls, reproducing the identical wrong-output selection. Fixing the return tracer is the precise fix.

## Tests

Host-side (no device) codegen regressions in `test_orchestration_codegen.py`:
- A `pl.spmd` scope writing an in-place `InOut` scratch (sorted first) plus an `Out` result through a sliced view; the single return reshaped downstream must alias `ext_result.reshape(`, not `ext_scratch.reshape(`.
- **Counterpart for the gate:** a kernel that writes its `Out` param but returns a reshape view of its `In` param must alias the `Out` param (`ext_out.reshape(`), never the input view (`ext_a.reshape(`).

Full `tests/ut/codegen/`: **127 passed**, no regressions.

Same class as #1573 / #1693 / #1694, distinct trigger and code path.

title: feat(distributed): add pld.tensor.allreduce composite op
body:
## Summary

Adds an in-place cross-rank **`pld.tensor.allreduce`** intrinsic at the InCore IR level, lowered in `LowerCompositeOps` (pass 14) to the 4-phase notify / wait / remote_load+accumulate / store recipe.

User API mirrors `pl.store`'s rebind idiom:

```python
pub = pld.tensor.allreduce(pub, sig, op=pld.ReduceOp.Sum)
```

- **Lowering** lives in `LowerCompositeOps` so distributed-collective expansion reuses the same infrastructure as `tile.sin` / `tile.cos` — no new pass slot. `LoweringBuilder` grows `EmitFor` / `EmitForReduce` / `EmitIf` / `EmitIfExpr` / `NotEq` callback-based primitives that emit `ForStmt` / `IfStmt` via a nested builder sharing the parent's temp counter, so emitted names stay unique at any nesting depth. The `CompositeLoweringFn` signature is collapsed to `(call, args, builder)`.
- **First version supports `ReduceOp.Sum` only**; `Max` / `Min` / `Prod` are reserved enum values rejected by the deducer until their lowerings land. Loop bounds are runtime queries (`pld.system.nranks`), so no `CommGroup` materialisation is needed and the rule stays at pass 14.
- **Barrier scheme** (validated on NPU at P=2 and P=4): Phase 2 pre-reduce barrier uses race-free `Set 1` / `Eq 1` (single writer per signal cell); Phase 3.5 post-reduce barrier uses `AtomicAdd 1` + `Eq 2` to prevent fast ranks from overwriting their `target` slot while slow ranks are still reading it. The post-reduce barrier is the key correctness fix — without it, P=4 produced wrong sums on slower ranks.
- **Cross-layer sync**: `ReduceOp` enum added to `comm.h`, bound in nanobind, mirrored in `ir.pyi`, re-exported at the `pld` top level. Shared `put` / `get` / `allreduce` DistributedTensor validation is extracted to `_unwrap_distributed_tensors` in `op/_utils.py` (ops with asymmetric signatures like `put`, whose `src` may be a plain `pl.Tensor`, validate inline).
- **Docs**: pass 14 EN + zh-CN updated with the new rule, the `(call, args, builder)` signature, and a pointer to the structured-CF builder helpers.

## Testing

- [x] Transforms / distributed UTs pass without regression (structural op-set invariants, `ForStmt`/`IfStmt` shape, idempotency, deducer rejection of plain `Tensor` target and non-`Sum` `ReduceOp`)
- [x] On-board ST `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_tensor_allreduce_intrinsic.py` validated on NPU at P=2 and P=4 against the same `torch.allclose` golden as the hand-rolled 4-phase reference
- [x] Rebased onto `upstream/main`; resolved a conflict in `op/tensor_ops.py` preserving upstream's permissive `put` `src` (Tensor or DistributedTensor) and region/offset support on `get`

title: fix(ir): Return params explicitly from outlined/wrapper functions
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1702. Also resolves the same alias-miscompile class for #1693 and structurally closes #1573.

A multi-output `pl.spmd` scope whose return value is a **non-first** output was aliased by orchestration codegen to the **wrong** output tensor. The Spmd wrapper has no top-level `ReturnStmt` the codegen can trace, so `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` fell back to `out_indices[0]` (the first `Out`/`InOut`). Downstream the wrong tensor was reshaped; the numel mismatch tripped an AICPU `valid_reshape` assert, and the host surfaced it as a scheduler timeout (`507018`) — a kernel-side shape bug masquerading as a deadlock.

The fix moves the mapping from a codegen heuristic to an IR-level invariant.

## Approach — `ReturnParamsExplicit` invariant

Every `InCore`/`Group`/`Spmd` function returns the param `Var` each tensor result writes through, **by pointer identity**, so the return→param map is a lookup rather than a re-derivation. Kernel-allocated outputs and scalars are exempt.

- **New shared utility `ir::return_lineage`** (`return_lineage_utils`): traces a return value through var copies, loop carries, builtin writebacks (`tile.store` / `tensor.assemble` / `tensor.set_validshape`), `TupleGetItem` of tuple calls, and `Group`/`Spmd` wrappers ending in the inner call. Orchestration analysis `FindReturnedParamIndex/Indices` delegate to it.
- **Producers**: `ScopeOutliner` and `ExpandMixedKernel` build wrapper `ReturnStmt`s from params; `NormalizeReturnOrder` canonicalizes `InCore`/`Group`/`Spmd` returns to params (new step before reordering) and produces `ReturnParamsExplicit`.
- **Verification**: new `ReturnParamsExplicit` property + verifier, registered and added to the Basic verification set; the `InOutUse` verifier skips `Spmd` wrappers.
- **Codegen**: `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` now `INTERNAL_CHECK`s instead of guessing the first `Out` when a multi-output trace fails.

## Testing

- [x] Full unit-test suite green (5709 passed, 1 skipped)
- [x] New regression tests for #1702 and #1693 + a verifier unit test
- [x] Before/after expectations updated across the outlining, mixed-kernel, normalize-return-order, and orchestration-codegen suites (no assertions weakened)
- [x] clang-tidy and all pre-commit hooks pass
- [x] Docs updated (en + zh-cn): pass docs 10/11/21/24 and codegen 01

## Related Issues

Fixes #1702
Also resolves #1693; structurally closes the #1573 class

title: fix(ir): resolve pl.array-routed TaskId deps in AutoDeriveTaskDependencies (#1744)
body:
## Problem

Fixes #1744. A user-written `pl.manual_scope()` that expresses dependencies on a `pl.parallel` / loop producer fan-out by collecting per-iteration TaskIds into a `pl.array` and referencing them downstream as `deps=[arr[i], ...]` was silently **demoted to AUTO**, which re-engages runtime `TensorMap`/`OverlapMap` tracking and serializes the entire fan-out — exactly what the manual scope was written to avoid. A real Qwen3-14B decode layer hits this in 4 separate manual scopes.

### Root cause

`SubmitTaskIdCollector` (in `auto_derive_task_dependencies_pass.cpp`) only built TaskId lineage from whole-SSA-var dataflow (submit tuple tails, bare-var copies, loop carry). A producer TaskId stashed into a `pl.array` lowers to `array.update_element(arr, i, tid)`, and the consumer dep `arr[i]` lowers to `array.get_element(arr, i)` (which the parser further desugars into a *synthesized* dep array). Both are builtin `Call`s the collector had no visitor for, so `deps=[arr[i]]` never canonicalized back to the producer TaskId.

Consequently `covered_by_user_edge` was `false` for every loop-producer hazard, and since the producer is `dynamic_producer=true`, the `dynamic_prior_producer_requires_scope_lift` fallback stripped the scope to `manual=false`.

## Fix

Teach the collector **whole-array TaskId lineage**:

- `array.update_element(arr, i, tid)` records that `arr` carries producer `tid`; a nested `array.get_element` value (the deps-desugarer shape) pulls the source array's carried producers.
- Lineage is propagated across loop boundaries (iter_arg / return Var), so a post-loop `deps=[arr[i]]` resolves.
- `CanonicalizeTaskIds` expands array-typed user edges — whole-array (`deps=[arr]`) or synthesized per-slot (`deps=[arr[i], ...]`) — back to those producers.

Tracking is whole-array (slot-imprecise) by design: a loop-carried producer array is updated at a *dynamic* index, so slot precision is impossible — but coverage only needs "this dep array references producer P", not which slot. This is sound (it can only *recognize* a producer the user explicitly listed) and never widens coverage incorrectly; uncovered hazards still fall back exactly as before.

No IR-node, API, or contract changes — pure pass-level analysis over `Call` args.

## Tests

- `test_array_slot_deps_keep_manual_scope` — the issue repro (loop fan-out → `pl.array` → consumer `deps=[arr[0..3]]`): asserts the scope stays MANUAL with no compiler edges.
- `test_whole_task_id_array_dep_keeps_manual_scope` — the whole-array fence form `deps=[arr]`.

Full `test_auto_derive_task_dependencies.py` (35) and the manual-scope codegen suites (`test_phase_fence_dep_compression.py`, `test_orchestration_codegen.py`, 144) pass locally. Pass doc updated (EN + zh-CN).

title: feat(runtime): replay an already-compiled L3 distributed program from build_output
body:
## Summary

L3 distributed programs (`@pl.jit.host` → `DistributedCompiledProgram`) could not use the `runtime_dir` replay workflow: dispatch only worked while the live post-pass IR was in memory, so pointing a harness at an already-compiled `build_output/` fell through to single-chip `execute_compiled`, which has no top-level `kernel_config.py` for an L3 build.

This persists the only IR-derived bit the runtime needs — the HOST-orchestrator call signature (post-SSA param names, directions, shapes, dtypes, return count) plus platform / backend / `DistributedConfig` — to a `distributed_meta.json` sidecar at compile time, and reconstructs a fully functional program from it without re-running the pass chain:

- `DistributedCompiledProgram.from_dir(output_dir, ...)` rebuilds metadata from the sidecar; chip callables are assembled by walking `next_levels/` (no live IR).
- `execute_distributed_compiled(output_dir, args, ...)` is the one-shot entry (distributed counterpart of `execute_compiled`), exported from `pypto.runtime`.
- `_assemble_chip_callables` is now directory-driven, removing the last `_program` dependency from dispatch.
- `rebuild_kernel_cpp_from_pto` and `invalidate_binary_cache` recurse into `next_levels/<rank>/`, so `.pto` / `.cpp` edits in per-rank sub-builds are picked up.
- `replay()` auto-detects an L3 build (no top-level `kernel_config.py` but an `orchestration/host_orch.py` present) and routes to `execute_distributed_compiled`, fixing the previously-broken L3 debug/run.py.

Reconstruction reuses the existing L3 dispatch path, so a replay is bit-identical to a fresh `compiled(*args)`.

## Testing

- [x] Added unit tests (from_dir round-trip + metadata persistence, directory-driven assembly, next_levels-aware rebuild / invalidate, L3 replay routing)
- [x] Documentation updated (en + zh-cn "Replaying an L3 / distributed build" subsection)

Fixes #1689

title: Add tensor allreduce API and host collective lowering
body:
## Summary

This PR adds the first-stage infrastructure for tensor-level allreduce in distributed PyPTO.

- Add public DSL/IR API `pld.tensor.allreduce(src, signal, op=pld.ReduceOp.Sum)`
- Add `ReduceOp` support for distributed tensor collectives, with `Sum` implemented and `Max` / `Min` / `Prod` reserved for future lowerings
- Add internal-only `builtin.tensor.allreduce` op for compiler-generated host collective dispatch
- Add `LowerHostTensorCollectives` pass to lower host-level `pld.tensor.allreduce` into per-device builtin dispatch calls
- Extend comm-domain materialization so user-provided allreduce signal buffers inherit the data buffer's comm-domain coverage
- Keep regular non-host `pld.tensor.allreduce` on the existing composite lowering path
- Update English and Chinese distributed op docs and add unit coverage

## Motivation

This prepares the host-level collective API path without introducing a separate runtime helper or a new user-facing host namespace. Users call the tensor-level API directly:

```python
data = pld.window(data_buf, [N], dtype=pl.FP32)
signal = pld.window(signal_buf, [nranks], dtype=pl.INT32)

data = pld.tensor.allreduce(data, signal, op=pld.ReduceOp.Sum)
```

For host orchestrators, the compiler keeps the user API as `pld.tensor.allreduce` and lowers it into internal builtin chip dispatches. The signal tensor remains explicit and user-created, matching the current design direction.

## Scope

This PR is PR1 of the staged allreduce work. It covers API, IR, comm-domain handling, pass plumbing, and host lowering infrastructure.

It does not yet include the builtin kernel template/codegen materialization path or real device execution for the host builtin. Those are intended for follow-up PRs.

## Testing

- Added unit tests for `pld.tensor.allreduce` type deduction and validation
- Added parser coverage to reject user-visible `pld.builtin.*`
- Added tests for host allreduce lowering into `builtin.tensor.allreduce`
- Added tests for allreduce signal comm-domain inheritance
- Added pass-manager ordering coverage
- Updated distributed op documentation in English and Chinese

title: feat(debug): Add CompiledProgram.validate_ir for per-pass IR validation
body:
## Summary

Provides a first-class, optional entry point for **pre-runtime pass IR validation** so consumers no longer have to re-implement the `passes_dump/` → validator wiring themselves (per #1634).

- **`CompiledProgram.validate_ir(tensors, expected, *, rtol, atol)`** — resolves `<output_dir>/passes_dump/` automatically and delegates to `validate_pass_ir_codegen_results`. Uses a lazy import so the core `ir` layer keeps no import-time dependency on the `debug` layer. Raises `FileNotFoundError` when the program was compiled with `dump_passes=False`.
- **Promotes `validate_pass_ir_codegen_results`** to the public `pypto.debug` namespace (exported from `debug/__init__.py`), so the low-level entry point is supported for the "I only have a dump dir" case.
- Updates EN/ZH `torch_codegen` debug docs with the convenience method and the now-public import.
- Adds unit tests for both the missing-dump raise and the delegation path.

### Design note

This intentionally does **not** add `validate_ir` parameters to `compile()`. Golden inputs / expected outputs / tolerances are test-harness concepts; threading them through the compile signature would conflate compilation with numeric verification and invert the `compile` → `debug` layering. Exposing the helper on the compiled artifact removes the per-consumer discovery friction while keeping that separation. Downstream golden-runner integration (e.g. pypto-lib) remains the home for supplying golden data.

`DistributedCompiledProgram` (L3+) is intentionally left for a follow-up since its artifact layout differs.

title: fix(jit): track pl.reshape in _extract_local_tensor_metas for inline dips
body:
## Summary

**`_extract_local_tensor_metas` now tracks `pl.reshape`**, enabling reshaped tensors to flow into `@pl.jit.inline` dependencies without compilation
failures.

## Problem

The JIT specializer's `_extract_local_tensor_metas` walks a `@pl.jit` function body to infer tensor metadata (shape + dtype) for local variables produced by
`pl.create_tensor`, `pl.slice`, and `pl.window`. It did **not** track `pl.reshape`, so this pattern failed to compile:

```python
@jit.inline
def helper(x: pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.BF16], ...):
    ...

@jit
def kernel(x: pl.Tensor[[2, 64, 128], pl.BF16], ...):
    x_flat = pl.reshape(x, [128, 128])
    result = helper(x_flat, ...)   # ← ValueError: missing inferred tensor metadata

x_flat had no metadata at all, and any variable reassigned via reshape kept its original (stale) metadata. When the specializer tried to map the inline
dep's parameters to the caller's arguments, it failed.

In pypto-lib, this forced developers to avoid reshape-before-inline patterns. For example, models/deepseek/v4/hc_post.py contains an explicit workaround
comment:

# skip the reshape-back to avoid a static-vs-dynamic type mismatch
# when inlined into callers with concrete shapes (e.g. moe_ep.py).
return y
```

## Fix

- Add _reshape_meta helper that resolves the new shape via _resolve_shape (supporting DynDim propagation) and inherits dtype from the source tensor.
- Add a "reshape" dispatch branch in _walk, following the same pattern as existing create_tensor / slice / window handlers.

## Files Changed

- python/pypto/jit/decorator.py — Add _reshape_meta helper + reshape dispatch in _walk
- tests/ut/jit/test_decorator.py — Add 3 tests (unit + DynDim + e2e compile)

## Tests

- test_extract_local_tensor_metas_reshape — Unit: reshape changes rank, inherits dtype
- test_reshape_propagates_dyndim_via_dim_alias — pl.tensor.dim alias through reshape carries DynDim
- test_inline_with_reshape_compiles — E2E: @pl.jit.inline + pl.reshape in caller compiles successfully

Full suite: 104 tests in test_decorator.py pass, no regressions.

Related Issue: #1755

title: [Bug] _extract_local_tensor_metas does not track pl.reshape — inline dep resolution fails with reshaped tensors
body:
### Component

Other (please specify in description)

### Description

`_extract_local_tensor_metas` in `python/pypto/jit/decorator.py` tracks metadata for local tensor variables produced inside a JIT function body (`pl.create_tensor`, `pl.slice`, `pl.window`, dep call returns), but **does not track `pl.reshape`**. When a caller reshapes tensors before passing them to an `@pl.jit.inline` dep, the specializer passes stale (pre-reshape) metadata to the inline function's parameter resolution, causing compilation failures.

### Steps to Reproduce

```markdown
@jit.inline
def copy_inline(
    x: pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.BF16],
    y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.BF16]],
):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP):
        tile = pl.load(x, [0, 0], [128, 128])
        pl.store(tile, [0, 0], y)
    return y

@jit
def reshape_caller(
    x: pl.Tensor[[2, 64, 128], pl.BF16],
    y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[2, 64, 128], pl.BF16]],
) -> pl.Tensor[[2, 64, 128], pl.BF16]:
    x_flat = pl.reshape(x, [128, 128])
    y = pl.reshape(y, [128, 128])
    y = copy_inline(x_flat, y)
    y = pl.reshape(y, [2, 64, 128])
    return y
```

### Expected Behavior

`_extract_local_tensor_metas` should track `pl.reshape` results so that the specializer can resolve inline dep parameters correctly. The `_walk` function should have a `"reshape"` dispatch branch alongside `create_tensor`, `slice`, and `window`.

### Actual Behavior

```
ValueError: missing inferred tensor metadata for parameter 'x'
```

The metadata for `x_flat` is never created (no meta at all), and `y` keeps its original parameter shape `(2, 64, 128)` instead of `(128, 128)`.

### Git Commit ID

bda839de6be01e75852f57ef4118c42bd9ef408f

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Root cause: the `_walk` function dispatches on `fn.attr` for `pl.*` method calls. It handles `"create_tensor"`, `"slice"`, and `"window"` but has no branch for `"reshape"`. Fix adds a `_reshape_meta` helper that resolves the new shape via `_resolve_shape` and inherits dtype from the source tensor.

title: [Feature] Define DeepSeek V4 KV cache contract for serving integration
body:
## 背景

DeepSeek V4 服务化接入前，需要先把 PyPTO 侧要承载的 KV cache / state metadata contract 定清楚。下面整理 DeepSeek V4 KV cache / state 的目标输入 contract，尽量保留字段边界和讨论结论的完整语义，而不是压缩成简版 tracker。

## 按 Cache 类型整理的目标输入

本节按 KV cache / state 类型整理服务化目标 contract。shape 默认使用
token-major 的调度 batch：

```text
R = num_reqs
T = num_tokens = sum(q_lens)
W = sliding_window
ori_block_size = ordinary sliding-window KV rows per page
cmp_base_block_size = main compressed KV base page size before compression
cmp_page_size = cmp_base_block_size // compress_ratio
idx_base_block_size = CSA indexer KV base page size before compression
idx_page_size = idx_base_block_size // 4
state_block_size = compressor state rows per page
H = num_attention_heads
D = hidden_size
head_dim = DeepSeek V4 MLA row semantic dim, currently 512
idx_head_dim = CSA indexer row semantic dim
C4 = 4
C128 = 128
```

block/page size 定稿：

| 类型 | 目标 contract 口径 | vLLM 对齐口径 | 当前 PyPTO 适配值 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 普通 SWA KV | `ori_block_size = 64` | DeepSeek V4 SWA cache 当前为 64 rows/page | `PY_PTO_BLOCK_SIZE = 128` |
| HCA 主 compressed KV | `cmp_base_block_size = 256`，`cmp_page_size = 2` | `MLAAttentionSpec.storage_block_size = 256 // 128` | 当前 PyPTO tensor 仍用 128 rows/page |
| CSA 主 compressed KV | `cmp_base_block_size = 256`，`cmp_page_size = 64` | `MLAAttentionSpec.storage_block_size = 256 // 4` | 当前 PyPTO tensor 仍用 128 rows/page |
| CSA Indexer KV | `idx_base_block_size = 256`，`idx_page_size = 64` | vLLM V4 indexer backend 支持 base block 256 | 当前 PyPTO tensor 仍用 128 rows/page |
| HCA Compressor State | `state_block_size = 8` | vLLM `DeepseekCompressorStateCache` ratio-128 state block size | `C128_COMPRESSOR_BLOCK_SIZE = 8` |
| CSA Compressor State | `state_block_size = 4` | vLLM `DeepseekCompressorStateCache` ratio-4 state block size | `C4A_COMPRESSOR_BLOCK_SIZE = 4` |

因此服务化接口里不要只暴露一个全局 `block_size`。cache manager 可以内部有统一
allocation policy，但传给 kernel/builder 的 contract 应按 cache 类型使用对应的
`*_page_size` 或 `*_block_size`。

所有 cache 类型共用的基础 metadata：

| 输入 | Shape | Type | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `q_lens` | `[R]` | `int32` | 每个 request 本轮调度的 query token 数。普通 decode 通常为 1，MTP/verifier 可能大于 1，prefill/chunked prefill 可以变长。 |
| `cu_q_lens` | `[R + 1]` | `int32` | `q_lens` 的前缀和。第 `r` 个 request 的 token 行范围是 `[cu_q_lens[r], cu_q_lens[r + 1])`。等价于 vLLM 的 `query_start_loc`。 |
| `context_lens` | `[R]` | `int32` | 本轮调度 token 可见/写入前，已经 committed 的历史长度。MTP 接受/提交边界需要这个字段。 |
| `kv_seq_lens` | `[R]` | `int32` | 本轮调度后的序列长度。等价于 vLLM 的 `seq_lens`；普通 decode/prefill 下通常是 `context_lens + q_lens`。 |
| `token_to_request` | `[T]` | `int32` | 每个 token-major 行所属的 request id。可以由 `cu_q_lens` 推导，但显式传入可以避免 kernel/builder 里反复展开。 |
| `position_ids` | `[T]` | `int32` or `int64` | 每个 token 的绝对位置，用于 RoPE、compressor boundary 判断和 block-table 查表。 |

### 普通 Sliding-Window KV

持久化 cache 目标形态：

```text
逻辑服务化形态:
ori_kv: [ori_num_blocks, ori_block_size, row_dim]

当前 PyPTO kernel 适配形态:
ori_kv: [ori_num_blocks, PY_PTO_BLOCK_SIZE, 1, head_dim]
```

这里第三维 `1` 是当前 PyPTO kernel 沿用通用 paged-KV 布局时的
`num_kv_heads = 1` 维度，不是服务侧必须暴露的语义。DeepSeek V4 MLA 的普通 KV
本质是每 token 一条 latent KV row。当前 BF16 kernel 的 `row_dim = head_dim`；
后续如果接入 FP8 MLA storage backend，可以把每行 pack 成 vLLM DeepSeek V4 的
584-byte row，但这不应改变逻辑 metadata contract。

| 输入 | Shape | Type | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ori_kv` | 逻辑 `[ori_num_blocks, ori_block_size, row_dim]`；当前 PyPTO 适配 `[ori_num_blocks, PY_PTO_BLOCK_SIZE, 1, head_dim]` | 当前为 `bf16`；未来可由 storage backend 决定 | 普通 sliding-window KV 存储。SWA、HCA、CSA attention 都会读写它。 |
| `ori_block_table` | `[R, ori_max_blocks]` | `int32` | request-local 的普通 window block id 到物理 cache block id 的映射。 |
| `ori_slot_mapping` | `[T]` | `int64` | 每个调度 token 的普通 KV 写入物理 row。`-1` 表示 padding/no write。目标公式是 `physical_block * ori_block_size + offset_in_block`，但 kernel 应直接消费这个 row。 |

推荐 builder 行为：

- 用 `position_ids[t]` 计算 request-local window 位置。
- 用 `ori_block_table` 生成 `ori_slot_mapping[t]`。
- 统一使用 `-1` 作为 padding/no-write sentinel。

当前阶段不把 vLLM 的 `decode_swa_indices` / `decode_swa_lens` 纳入普通
Sliding-Window KV 的必需 contract。读侧 sparse visibility 仍由 shared
`sparse_attn` / `cmp_sparse_indices` 负责；如果后续把 SWA 独立成 vLLM-like
backend，再引入这两个字段。

### 主 Compressed KV：HCA / Ratio 128

持久化 cache 目标形态：

```text
逻辑服务化形态:
cmp_kv: [cmp_num_blocks, cmp_page_size, row_dim]

当前 PyPTO kernel 适配形态:
cmp_kv: [cmp_num_blocks, PY_PTO_BLOCK_SIZE, 1, head_dim]
```

这个 cache 每 128 个原始 token 生成 1 个 compressed KV row。HCA 不需要 CSA 的
learned indexer。和普通 SWA KV 不同，vLLM 的 compressed cache 使用
`storage_block_size = cmp_base_block_size // 128` 作为每个 physical block 内的 row 数。
因此服务化 contract 里应显式区分普通 KV 的 `ori_block_size` 和 compressed KV 的
`cmp_page_size`。

| 输入 | Shape | Type | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cmp_kv` | 逻辑 `[cmp_num_blocks, cmp_page_size, row_dim]`；当前 PyPTO 适配 `[cmp_num_blocks, PY_PTO_BLOCK_SIZE, 1, head_dim]` | 当前为 `bf16`；未来可由 storage backend 决定 | ratio-128 层的主 compressed KV 存储。 |
| `cmp_block_table` | `[R, cmp_max_blocks]` | `int32` | request-local compressed block id 到物理 compressed cache block id 的映射。 |
| `cmp_slot_mapping` | `[T]` | `int64` | token-major 的 compressed KV 写入物理 row。只有跨过 128-token boundary 的 token 写有效 row；其他 token 填 `-1`。 |

写入 builder 规则：

```text
pos = position_ids[t]
if (pos + 1) % 128 == 0:
    compressed_pos = pos // 128
    dst = cmp_block_table[req, compressed_pos // cmp_page_size] * cmp_page_size
          + compressed_pos % cmp_page_size
else:
    dst = -1
```

目标 contract 使用 vLLM-style dense `cmp_slot_mapping[T]`。如果当前 PyPTO kernel
更容易消费 compact 写入列表，adapter 可以从 dense mapping 派生
`cmp_write_token_ids[num_cmp_writes]` 和 `cmp_write_slot_mapping[num_cmp_writes]`，
但这不是服务侧首选形态。

当前阶段不把 vLLM 的 `c128a_global_decode_topk_indices` /
`c128a_decode_topk_lens` / `c128a_prefill_topk_indices` 纳入 HCA 主 compressed KV
的必需 contract。读侧 compressed visibility 仍由 shared `sparse_attn` /
`cmp_sparse_indices` 负责；如果后续把 HCA 独立成 vLLM-like C128A backend，再引入
这组字段。

### 主 Compressed KV：CSA / Ratio 4

持久化 cache 目标形态：

```text
逻辑服务化形态:
cmp_kv: [cmp_num_blocks, cmp_page_size, row_dim]

当前 PyPTO kernel 适配形态:
cmp_kv: [cmp_num_blocks, PY_PTO_BLOCK_SIZE, 1, head_dim]
```

这是 ratio-4 CSA 层给主 attention 消费的 compressed KV。它和下面的 indexer KV cache
是两套不同 cache。CSA 还有 overlap compressor state，因此 compressed KV 写入必须和
state update 对齐。vLLM C4A 的主 compressed KV 写入规则和 HCA/C128A 同构，只是
`cmp_page_size = cmp_base_block_size // 4`。

| 输入 | Shape | Type | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cmp_kv` | 逻辑 `[cmp_num_blocks, cmp_page_size, row_dim]`；当前 PyPTO 适配 `[cmp_num_blocks, PY_PTO_BLOCK_SIZE, 1, head_dim]` | 当前为 `bf16`；未来可由 storage backend 决定 | sparse attention 消费的主 compressed KV 存储。 |
| `cmp_block_table` | `[R, cmp_max_blocks]` | `int32` | request-local ratio-4 compressed block id 到物理 block 的映射。 |
| `cmp_slot_mapping` | `[T]` | `int64` | token-major 的主 compressed KV 写入物理 row。只有跨过 4-token boundary 的 token 写有效 row；其他 token 填 `-1`。 |

写入 builder 规则：

```text
pos = position_ids[t]
if (pos + 1) % 4 == 0:
    compressed_pos = pos // 4
    dst = cmp_block_table[req, compressed_pos // cmp_page_size] * cmp_page_size
          + compressed_pos % cmp_page_size
else:
    dst = -1
```

目标 contract 使用 vLLM-style dense `cmp_slot_mapping[T]`。如果当前 PyPTO kernel
更容易消费 compact 写入列表，adapter 可以从 dense mapping 派生
`cmp_write_token_ids[num_cmp_writes]` 和 `cmp_write_slot_mapping[num_cmp_writes]`，
但这不是服务侧首选形态。

`cmp_sparse_indices` / `cmp_sparse_lens` 不属于主 compressed KV 写入 contract，而是
shared `sparse_attn` 的读侧 metadata。CSA 中它们由 learned indexer/topk 结果转换得到；
当前本地 raw encoding 仍是 `-1`、`[0,W)`、`[W,W+q_len)`、`[W+q_len,...)`。
服务化接入时可以把这组读侧 metadata 作为 builder 输出，而不是在
`decode_sparse_attn.py` 内部生成。

### CSA Indexer KV

持久化 cache 目标形态：

```text
逻辑服务化形态:
idx_kv_cache: [idx_num_blocks, idx_page_size, idx_row_dim]

当前 PyPTO kernel 适配形态:
idx_kv_cache: [idx_num_blocks, PY_PTO_BLOCK_SIZE, 1, idx_head_dim]
```

这个 cache 由 CSA indexer/topk 路径消费，不直接给主 attention kernel 使用。它按
ratio 4 存储 compressed/indexer KV row。vLLM DeepSeek V4 indexer cache 也使用
compressed storage block 语义，`idx_page_size = idx_base_block_size // 4`。当前 PyPTO 仍以
BF16 `idx_head_dim` 行存储；vLLM indexer cache 则更接近 packed `uint8` row。

| 输入 | Shape | Type | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `idx_kv_cache` | 逻辑 `[idx_num_blocks, idx_page_size, idx_row_dim]`；当前 PyPTO 适配 `[idx_num_blocks, PY_PTO_BLOCK_SIZE, 1, idx_head_dim]` | 当前为 `bf16`；未来可由 indexer storage backend 决定 | 用于打分/选择 compressed position 的 paged indexer KV cache。 |
| `idx_block_table` | `[R, idx_max_blocks]` | `int32` | request-local indexer compressed block id 到物理 indexer cache block 的映射。 |
| `idx_slot_mapping` | `[T]` | `int64` | token-major 的 indexer KV 写入物理 row。只有跨过 4-token boundary 的 token 写有效 row；其他 token 填 `-1`。 |

写入规则和 ratio-4 主 compressed KV 相同，但使用 `idx_block_table` 和 indexer cache
对应的 storage layout：

```text
pos = position_ids[t]
if (pos + 1) % 4 == 0:
    idx_pos = pos // 4
    dst = idx_block_table[req, idx_pos // idx_page_size] * idx_page_size
          + idx_pos % idx_page_size
else:
    dst = -1
```

旧的 dense prefill CSA 应只作为 adapter 实现看待。目标 contract 是 paged
`idx_kv_cache + idx_block_table + idx_slot_mapping[T]`。如果当前 PyPTO kernel 更容易消费
compact 写入列表，adapter 可以从 dense mapping 派生
`idx_write_token_ids[num_idx_writes]` 和 `idx_write_slot_mapping[num_idx_writes]`。

`idx_seq_lens` 不属于 Indexer KV 持久化/写入 contract，而是 indexer 读侧 metadata；
vLLM 会显式使用 `kv_seq_lens // 4`。当前本地 decode 实现没有该输入，而是在
`decode_indexer.py` 里用 `(start_pos + S) // 4` 推导可读 cache 长度，并在
`decode_attention_csa.py` 里用 `(topk_abs_pos + 1) // 4` 过滤 indexer topk。

`idx_topk_indices` 也不是 Indexer KV cache 输入；它是 learned indexer 的输出，后续转换成
shared `sparse_attn` 使用的 `cmp_sparse_indices`。

### 主 Compressor State

持久化 state 目标形态：

```text
compress_state: [state_num_blocks, state_block_size, state_dim]
```

这不是 attention KV cache row。它保存 compressor 为了最终产出 `cmp_kv` 所需的
partial token state / score state。

| 输入 | Shape | Type | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `compress_state` | `[state_num_blocks, state_block_size, state_dim]` | 当前为 `fp32` | 主 compressor partial state。HCA 使用 ratio-128 state，CSA 使用 ratio-4 overlap state。 |
| `compress_state_block_table` | `[R, state_max_blocks]` | `int32` | absolute-position state block 到物理 state block 的映射。 |
| `state_slot_mapping` | `[T]` | `int64` | token-major 的 partial state 写入物理 row。`-1` 表示 padding/no write。 |

目标写入 contract 使用 explicit slot mapping：

```text
state_slot_mapping[t] = physical_state_block * state_block_size + offset_in_block
```

当前 PyPTO kernel 仍可由 adapter 按现有规则派生这个 mapping：

```text
pos = position_ids[t]
state_logical_block = pos // state_block_size
state_intra = pos % state_block_size
physical_state_block = compress_state_block_table[req, state_logical_block]
state_slot_mapping[t] = physical_state_block * state_block_size + state_intra
```

不再单独保留 `state_position_ids`。主 compressor state 路径直接复用全局
`position_ids[T]` 作为 absolute position，用于选择 APE row、判断 compression
boundary，以及确定 pooling 时读取的历史 state window。`state_write_mask` 也不单独保留，
用 `state_slot_mapping[t] == -1` 表示该 token 不写 state。

state 生命周期必须由 service/cache manager 跟 request 一起管理：prefill 后保留未完成
chunk 的 partial state，decode 继续更新，请求释放时回收对应 state pages。

### CSA Inner Indexer Compressor State

持久化 state 目标形态：

```text
inner_compress_state: [inner_state_num_blocks, inner_state_block_size, inner_state_dim]
```

这是用于产出 `idx_kv_cache` 的 overlap compressor state。

| 输入 | Shape | Type | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `inner_compress_state` | `[inner_state_num_blocks, inner_state_block_size, inner_state_dim]` | 当前为 `fp32` | CSA indexer compressor 的 partial state。 |
| `inner_compress_state_block_table` | `[R, inner_state_max_blocks]` | `int32` | absolute position 到物理 inner state block 的映射。 |
| `inner_state_slot_mapping` | `[T]` | `int64` | token-major 的 inner partial state 写入物理 row。`-1` 表示 padding/no write。 |

目标写入 contract 和主 compressor state 对称：

```text
inner_state_slot_mapping[t] =
    physical_inner_state_block * inner_state_block_size + offset_in_block
```

当前 PyPTO kernel 可由 adapter 按现有规则派生：

```text
pos = position_ids[t]
inner_state_logical_block = pos // inner_state_block_size
inner_state_intra = pos % inner_state_block_size
physical_inner_state_block =
    inner_compress_state_block_table[req, inner_state_logical_block]
inner_state_slot_mapping[t] =
    physical_inner_state_block * inner_state_block_size + inner_state_intra
```

不再单独保留 `idx_state_position_ids`。inner indexer compressor state 路径复用全局
`position_ids[T]`，用于选择 APE row、判断 ratio-4 boundary，以及确定 overlap pooling
读取的历史 inner state window。

这套 state 要和主 `compress_state` 分开管理；两者输出维度不同，消费者也不同。

## Acceptance criteria

- PyPTO/serving integration exposes cache-specific page-size metadata instead of relying on one global `BLOCK_SIZE`.
- Decode and prefill paths can receive explicit `ori_slot_mapping`, `cmp_slot_mapping`, `idx_slot_mapping`, `state_slot_mapping`, and `inner_state_slot_mapping`.
- `-1` is consistently accepted as padding/no-write sentinel for token-major mappings.
- Current PyPTO kernels may keep a 128-row BF16 adapter layout, but the service contract should be able to map from the target vLLM-style page semantics above.
- Read-side sparse-attention metadata remains separate from persistent KV/state write contracts.

title: feat(st): add L3 ring allreduce ST (RS+AG schedule, monolithic InCore)
body:
Port the ring allreduce algorithm from simpler allreduce_ring_distributed (#975) into the PyPTO DSL as a new L3 system test.

Single monolithic InCore kernel (ring_allreduce) collapses all four phases — stage-in, reduce-scatter loop, allgather loop, stage-out — into one AIV task dispatch per rank, eliminating 2*(P-1) kernel-launch overhead vs a multi-kernel chain.

Exchange publish buffer (1*CHUNK FP32 HCCL window) provides an explicit commit-point before each RS/AG barrier, matching simpler's publish pattern and ensuring data visibility across rounds.

Dynamic NR via pl.dynamic('NR'), compact signal layout [2*(NR-1), NR] int32, parameterized tests for P=2 and P=4.  Golden matches mesh allreduce (element-wise sum of all rank inputs).

References:
- simpler ring allreduce: hw-native-sys/simpler#975
- mesh allreduce for comparison: test_l3_allreduce.py
- PTOAS MTE drain fix (enables multi-round barriers): hw-native-sys/PTOAS#718

Docs: distributed_ops.md (en+zh) updated with ring ST entry.

title: feat(scalar): add __rfloordiv__ and __rtruediv__ to Scalar with DSL tests
body:
## Summary

Adds `__rfloordiv__` and `__rtruediv__` reflected operators to `Scalar`, closing a consistency gap in the DSL type system.

## Problem

Expressions like `SIZE // NR` (where `SIZE` is a Python `int` and `NR` is a `DynVar`/`Scalar`) fail with `TypeError` because Python cannot dispatch `int.__floordiv__(int, DynVar)`.

The IR layer (`ir.FloorDiv`, `ir.Div`) already supports const-var binary expressions. `Scalar` already has `__rsub__`, `__rmul__`, `__rlshift__`, and `__rrshift__` — the two division reflected operators were the only missing ones.

## Changes

**`python/pypto/language/typing/scalar.py`** (+6 lines)
- `__rtruediv__(self, other)` → `Scalar(expr=other / self.unwrap())`
- `__rfloordiv__(self, other)` → `Scalar(expr=other // self.unwrap())`

**`tests/ut/language/parser/test_scalar_dispatch.py`** (+147 lines)
- New `TestScalarFloorDivTruediv` class with 6 DSL roundtrip tests:
  - `test_scalar_floordiv` / `test_scalar_truediv` — forward `a // b`, `a / b`
  - `test_scalar_rfloordiv` / `test_scalar_rtruediv` — reverse `100 // a`, `100.0 / a`
  - `test_floordiv_operator_matches_ir` — mixed literal positions
  - `test_truediv_operator_matches_ir` — `pl.div(a, b)` ≡ `a / b`

title: fix(jit): track pl.reshape in local tensor meta inference (#1755)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1755. `_extract_local_tensor_metas` in `python/pypto/jit/decorator.py` tracked the metadata of local tensors produced by `pl.create_tensor`, `pl.slice` and `pl.window`, but had **no branch for `pl.reshape`**. When a caller reshaped a tensor before passing it to an `@pl.jit.inline` dep, the specializer received stale (pre-reshape) or missing metadata and failed parameter resolution:

```
ValueError: missing inferred tensor metadata for parameter 'x'
```

## Root cause

`_walk` dispatches on `fn.attr` for `pl.*` method-call assignments. It handled `create_tensor` / `slice` / `window` but not `reshape`, so:
- the reshaped local (`x_flat = pl.reshape(x, [128, 128])`) got **no meta at all**;
- a reshaped parameter (`y = pl.reshape(y, [128, 128])`) kept its original seed shape `(2, 64, 128)` instead of `(128, 128)`.

## Fix

- Add `_reshape_meta`: source is `args[0]` (a known local), the new shape is `args[1]` / `shape=` resolved via `_resolve_shape` (honouring static ints and `DynDim` aliases), and the dtype is inherited from the source. Unlike a slice, the new shape **fully replaces** the source shape (no per-dim parent fallback). A reshaped parameter overrides its seed meta, so downstream deps propagate the reshaped shape.
- Collapse the per-attr dispatch in `_walk` into an `attr_meta_builders` lookup table — this keeps the function within the branch/statement lint limits and makes future producers a one-line addition.

## Tests

`tests/ut/jit/test_decorator.py`:
- `test_extract_local_tensor_metas_reshape` — a reshaped view carries the new shape with the source dtype, and a reshaped parameter overrides its stale seed meta (covers both failure points from the issue).

## Test plan

- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/ut/jit/test_decorator.py -v`

title: [Pass Bug] SplitVectorKernel deadlocks (507018) on a single-scope cube→vec kernel: cube↔vec pipe ops replayed into both AIV subblocks for a split=0 exchange
body:
### Pass Name

SplitVectorKernel (`src/ir/transforms/split_vector_kernel_pass.cpp`)

### Description

When a single `pl.spmd` scope contains a CUBE matmul whose result is consumed by VEC ops in the **same task** (a fused cube→vec kernel), `SplitVectorKernel` splits the vector body into two `subblock_idx` lanes and **replays all cross-core pipe ops** (`tile.tpush_to_aic` / `tile.tpop_from_aic`) into **both** lanes. But the cube side is generated with **no subblock awareness** and the exchange is `split=0` (the result is not actually halved across subblocks). So the single cube producer pushes **one** `16×32` matmul result while **both** AIV subblocks try to `tpop_from_aic` it (and both push a full operand stream into the depth-4 `DIR_BOTH` TPipe). The ring desyncs, every core spins in-kernel, and the task never completes → host sees `aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018`, `sched_error_code=100`.

This is NOT a GM RAW / auto-dep problem and NOT a scheduler bug. The `mixes_gm` self-RAW in the kernel is handled correctly on the AIV engine (TSTORE `set_flag(MTE3,MTE2)` → TLOAD `wait_flag`). The AICPU scheduler also behaves correctly — it has no visibility into the on-die cube↔vec TPipe handshake. The generated kernel is mis-synchronized by the pass.

### Repro

pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/verify_hc_pre_1spmd.py -p a2a3` — DeepSeek-V4 hc_pre fully fused into ONE `pl.spmd` scope (matmul→`mixes_gm`→pre/post/mix_x/comb, all in one task). The **2-scope** variant (matmul in its own spmd scope, epilogue in a second scope) runs and passes precision — so the dataflow is valid; only the single-scope cube→vec fusion mis-synchronizes.

### Before IR

A single fused mixed kernel where the cube matmul result feeds subblock-split vector ops (`MixedKernels {aic:0, aiv0:1, aiv1:1}`, `block_num=8`, one `rt_submit_task`). The cube produces one (`split=0`) result.

### Expected IR

For a `split=0` cube↔vec exchange (matmul result/operand NOT split across subblocks), the pipe ops (`tpush_to_aic`/`tpop_from_aic` + matched cube-side ops) appear **exactly once** — hoisted above the `scf.if subblock_idx` or guarded to subblock 0 — so a single cube producer pairs with a single vec consumer. Per-lane replay must be reserved for genuinely split (`split=1/2`) exchanges.

### Actual IR / Error

Generated kernel (`build_output/_jit_hc_pre_test_*/ptoas/hc_pre.pto`):
- AIC body (cube): no `subblock` references; pushes one full result `tpush_to_aiv ... {split = 0}`.
- AIV body: `scf.if subblock_idx == 0 { ... } else { ... }` where **both** branches issue `3× tile.tpush_to_aic` + `1× tile.tpop_from_aic {split = 0}` with **identical un-halved `16×32`** result shape.

Device log (`build_output/devlog_1spmd/debug/device-0/*.log`):
```
[STALL thread=0 ...] TASK ring=1 task_id=4294967297 state=RUNNING fanin_refcount=2/2
  kernels=[aic:0 aiv0:1 aiv1:1] running_on=[... core=3(aic) ... core=42(aiv0)]
[STALL ...] SUMMARY completed=1/2 ... scan_running=1
... all cores: busy ... cond_reg_state=ack   (AICore still executing, never returns)
HandleTaskTimeout ... op name[simpler_aicpu_exec] ... timeOut:50000000   -> 507018
```
`fanin_refcount=2/2` (all task-graph deps satisfied; the task DID launch) + every core `cond_reg_state=ack`, `last_progress_iteration=0` → cores spin **in-kernel** on the cube↔vec pipe handshake, never finishing.

Suggested compile-time guard: `MixedKernelExpandedVerifier` should assert that cube vs combined-AIV-subblock `tpush`/`tpop` counts balance, so this fails verification with a clear message instead of producing a kernel that 507018-hangs.

### Git Commit ID

26d5551c (reproduces on current main + the #1702 build)

### NPU Kind

Other (please specify in description) — Ascend a2a3 (pypto-lib `--platform a2a3`)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Related: #1447 (SplitVectorKernel odd-N LEFT_RIGHT), #1034 (RFC: SplitVectorKernel split-axis / GM-mediated semantics).
- `models/deepseek/v4/repro_hc_pre_blocker2_selfraw_507018.py` was filed believing the cause was an intra-task GM self-RAW; this analysis shows the actual cause is the cube↔vec pipe replay under vector subblock split.
- Workaround: keep the cube matmul in its own `pl.spmd` scope (the 2-scope variant passes). Blocks only further 1-scope fusion.

title: fix(SplitVectorKernel): replay lane-1 tile.transpose as an empty tile (#1761)
body:
## Root cause

A fused cube↔vec kernel in one **no-split** `pl.spmd` scope lowers, on Ascend910B (a2a3), to a **dual-AIV-dispatch** mixed kernel. `SplitVectorKernel` replays the AIV body on the secondary subblock (lane 1) as zero-valid tiles. A **`tile.transpose`** replayed that way lowers to a pto-isa op that **hangs the AICore in-kernel** (`AICPU 507018`) on a zero valid extent — the same static/zero-valid hazard #1649 hit for subview slices.

The issue's original analysis (cube↔vec pipe-op replay) was **not** the cause: the cross-core handshake works correctly on its own, and the per-lane replay is required by the dual-AIV protocol. The deadlock only appears when the fused scope also contains a `tile.transpose` (hc_pre's `mix_x` per-head scale extraction), which the lane-1 replay turns into a zero-valid transpose that hangs.

## How it was found

Bisected the DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre` 1-spmd repro on real a2a3 hardware: stripped it section by section until the 507018 disappeared. The deadlock required **both** the cube↔vec matmul section **and** `mix_x`'s `tile.transpose`; neither alone hangs.

## Fix

Since the lane-1 result is discarded, rewrite a replayed `tile.transpose` into an empty `tile.create` of the transposed shape (dynamic-valid), matching the existing `tile.load` / `tile.slice` replay handling in `RebuildLane1CallWithZeroValidShape`.

## Validation

- **a2a3 device**: the full DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre` fully fused into one `pl.spmd` scope no longer 507018-deadlocks and matches golden precision (x_mixed / post / comb all PASS).
- UT: `test_no_split_dual_dispatch_rewrites_lane1_transpose_to_create`.
- No regression: existing dual-dispatch UTs + cross-core codegen-sim tests stay green.

Fixes #1761

title: Add incore-profiling skill: .pto-driven msprof op-simulator kernel profiler
body:
## Summary

Adds an **incore-profiling** skill: cycle-accurate, per-pipe (CUBE / VECTOR / MTE) in-core profiling of any PTOAS kernel via the Ascend `msprof op simulator` (camodel).

- **`incore_profile.py`** — orchestrates `generate → build → camodel → collect` per kernel, with a TL-capable-CANN preflight and degenerate-trace detection.
- **`gen_profiling_case.py`** — a compact, `.pto`-driven testcase generator. It reads the kernel ABI from the one `__global__`/`_aic` line in the `.cpp` and sizes every GM buffer from the sibling `.pto`'s static `make_tensor_view` shapes, then emits `main.cpp` / `launch.cpp` (`<<<1, …>>>` single-core) / `CMakeLists.txt` / `golden.py`. Mixed cube+vector kernels get a trivial merged `__global__` dispatcher (`#if __DAV_CUBE__ → _aic`, `#if __DAV_VEC__ → _aiv`).
- **`SKILL.md`** — usage, prerequisites (needs the kernel's sibling `.pto`), caveats for data-dependent kernels, and trace-output conventions.

Pairs with `pypto.tools.clean_sim_trace` (already in `main`) to turn the raw `visualize_data.bin` into a de-cluttered per-pipe trace + `instr_metrics.json`.

## Validation

Validated across operator types on the Ascend910B1 camodel — **all build + run**; non-degenerate per-pipe traces for cube matmul (gate_proj / q_proj / down_proj), vector (silu / online_softmax / rope_qkv / rms-reduce), mixed attention (fa_fused), and memset (q_seed). `gate_proj` reproduces the known-good pipe split (MTE2 40 / CUBE 33 / MTE1 24); `fa_fused`'s mixed dispatcher matches the per-pipe physics of a hand-inlined merge.

## Notes

title: fix: support composite shape dims in function parameter types
body:
## Summary

A function parameter whose tensor shape carries a composite dim — e.g.
`pl.Tensor[[M * 2, N], pl.FP32]` where `M` is a `pl.dynamic` var, so the dim
is a `Mul(Var, ConstInt)` expression rather than a bare `Var` — failed to
compile. Two independent bugs were on the critical path:

- **SSA verifier** registered dynamic shape vars from parameter/return
  `TensorType` shapes by matching bare `Var` dims only, so the inner `M` of a
  composite dim was never registered. Any reference to it — including the
  verifier walking the parameter type itself — reported `"used outside its
  defining scope"`. Fixed by recursively collecting every `Var` leaf through
  `BinaryExpr`/`UnaryExpr` shape expressions.

- **PTO codegen** flushed the function's constants section before rendering the
  tensor-view/alloc prologue, so a constant that appears only inside a shape
  expression (the `2` in `M * 2`) was declared *after* the section was written
  out — leaving the emitted `arith.muli` referencing an undeclared
  `%c2_index` (invalid MLIR). Fixed by rendering the prologue into a buffer
  before finalizing the constants section.

Docs (en + zh-cn) updated to describe the constant-ordering behavior for
composite shape dims.

## Testing

- [x] UT: `TestCompositeShapeDimVerification` (verifier) and
  `test_add_kernel_composite_dim_constant_declared` (codegen) — confirmed to
  fail before the fixes, pass after.
- [x] ST on real NPU via task-submit: single-device
  (`tests/st/runtime/control_flow/test_composite_shape_dim.py`) and 2-device L3
  distributed (`tests/st/distributed/test_l3_composite_shape_dim.py`), both
  executing a composite-dim kernel end-to-end with correct output.
- [x] Full UT suites for the verifier, dynamic-shape codegen, and distributed
  codegen pass.

title: ci(perf): add daily Qwen3-14B decode performance monitoring (warn-only)
body:
## Summary

Adds **advisory, non-failing** performance monitoring for `models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py`. Following review feedback, the perf check runs in the **scheduled daily CI** (not on every PR) and samples the model **multiple times, averaging** the result — perf is noisy (~8.5% run-to-run jitter), so per-PR gating would be flaky and slow.

Per-PR `ci.yml` keeps only the **functional correctness** run of the Qwen3 decode example; all perf measurement moves to `daily_ci.yml`.

## What changed

- **`.github/workflows/daily_ci.yml`** — new `qwen3-perf` job. Runs on the same **a2a3 / npu-1-device** container as the former per-PR job (so the committed baseline stays comparable). It runs `decode_layer.py --enable-l2-swimlane --max-seq --seed 1234` **5×**, appending each run's stdout to one log, then invokes the guard. Wired into `notify-on-failure` so a hard failure (build/device) still opens the daily issue; a perf regression does **not** (it is warn-only).
- **`.github/scripts/perf_guard.py`** (new, stdlib-only) — parses **all** `Total Test Time: <X> us` lines from the log and **averages** them (vs. the first match), reports the per-run samples + min/max spread, and compares the average against the baseline. Emits a `::warning::` annotation + Step Summary row and exits non-zero on regression / missing data, while `continue-on-error` keeps the job green.
- **`.github/perf_baselines/qwen3_14b_decode.json`** (new) — `value=1016.66us` (median of 3 on-device a2a3 runs), `threshold_pct=15` to absorb the ~8.5% jitter, `pypto_ref` pinned to the capturing commit. Refresh via PR when a perf change is intentional.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — drop the perf run + guard steps from `pypto-lib-model`; keep the functional Qwen3-14B decode example run.

### Why warn-only
GitHub Actions has no native per-job "yellow/neutral" conclusion. The guard exits non-zero on regression and the step carries `continue-on-error: true`, so the step renders yellow ⚠ while the job conclusion stays green. Perf is a signal, not a gate.

### Baseline maintenance
The baseline is updated **manually via PR** only when a perf change is intentional — lower it to lock in an optimization, never raise it to silence a real regression. The 15% threshold absorbs normal jitter, so routine PRs never need to touch it.

## Testing

- [x] `perf_guard.py` verified across paths: multi-run averaging (5 samples → mean + spread), within-threshold → green, regression → yellow + exit 1, unseeded baseline → report-only, missing/empty log → warning + exit 1.
- [x] `decode_layer.py -p a2a3 --enable-l2-swimlane --max-seq --seed 1234` confirmed to run, PASS correctness on device, and emit the `Total Test Time` line.
- [x] Both workflow YAMLs parse; `qwen3-perf` job structure and `notify-on-failure` wiring validated.
- [x] pre-commit (check-headers, ruff, pyright, check-yaml) green.

title: feat(pass): add SkewCrossCorePipeline cross-core software pipeline
body:
## Summary

Adds `SkewCrossCorePipeline`, a dedicated pass that software-pipelines mixed
cube/vector (cross-core) `pl.pipeline` loops so the two cores overlap.
Previously cross-core loops were handled implicitly by `LowerPipelineLoops`
(unroll) + `CanonicalizeIOOrder` (IO clustering), which produced back-to-back
`tpop`s that serialised the vector consumer.

The pass runs immediately before `LowerPipelineLoops`:

- **Single-round-trip producer role** (exactly one `tpush` + one `tpop`,
  FIFO-decoupled from the body): skew the producer one iteration ahead —
  `produce(start)` prologue, a `ForKind::Sequential` steady loop pairing
  `produce(k+step)` / `consume(k)`, and a `consume(last)` epilogue. The cube
  issues iteration k+1's QK while the vector runs iteration k's softmax.
- **Consumer role / multi-round-trip / non-statically-skewable**: demote to a
  plain `ForKind::Sequential` loop (order-preserving; overlap comes from the
  peer core's producer skew).

Either way a cross-core loop always leaves the pass as `ForKind::Sequential`
(no `pipeline_stages` marker), so it never reaches `LowerPipelineLoops` or
`CanonicalizeIOOrder` as a Pipeline body.

**Result:** −19.3% `qk_pv` phase wall on the DS v4 sparse-attention decode
kernel (device, min-of-5).

## Changes

- New pass `src/ir/transforms/skew_cross_core_pipeline_pass.cpp` + full
  cross-layer registration (header, `pass_properties`, binding, stub,
  `pass_manager`, `CMakeLists`).
- Remove the cross-core IO-clustering from `CanonicalizeIOOrder` — it is now
  same-core only.
- `LowerPipelineLoops` keeps only the generic same-core unroll (cross-core
  skew removed).
- Docs: new `25-skew_cross_core_pipeline` (EN + zh-CN); renumber
  `25..38 -> 26..39`; update the `pass-doc-ordering` rule and cross-references.

## Known limitation

Multi-round-trip cross-core loops (e.g. `C->V->C->V`) are **demoted to
Sequential, not skewed** — skewing only the lead message would reorder the
in-order cross-core FIFO (a silent wrong-data bug the verifiers don't model).
A whole-FIFO-group skew is left as a documented `TODO(crosscore-skew)` for a
follow-up.

## Incidental

Adding the new pass declaration to the widely-included `passes.h` /
`pass_properties.h` headers pulls dependent pass translation units into the
clang-tidy diff gate. This surfaced pre-existing include-cleaner / modernize /
performance findings in 7 unrelated pass files, fixed here (no behavior
change) so the gate stays green.

## Testing

- `cmake --build` clean; `clang_tidy.py --diff-base` 0 errors.
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` — 1647 passed, including the new
  `test_skew_cross_core_pipeline.py` (producer-skew both directions,
  consumer/multi-round-trip demote, non-cross-core passthrough).

title: [Pass Bug] orchestration codegen hoists the injected GM pipe buffer above the dynamic dim it is sized by → 't_dim...' was not declared in this scope
body:
### Pass Name

Orchestration codegen — `EmitBatchedAllocTensors` in `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp` (interacting with the injected GM pipe buffer from `InjectGMPipeBuffer`, pass #22).

### Description

A kernel fused into ONE `pl.spmd` scope that contains a CUBE matmul feeding VEC ops, **with a dynamic token dim**, fails to compile the generated orchestration C++:

```
error: 't_dim_inline53' was not declared in this scope
```

The injected cube↔vec GM pipe buffer (`InjectGMPipeBuffer`) is sized by the dynamic grid block count (`t_dim // 16`), but its `alloc_tensors` is **hoisted to the top of `PTO2_SCOPE()`**, while the `t_dim` local (`= orch_args.tensor(0).shapes[0]`) is emitted as the first BODY statement — *after* the alloc that uses it → use-before-declaration.

### Repro

- `models/deepseek/v4/verify_hc_pre_1spmd_dyn.py` (pypto-lib): DeepSeek-V4 hc_pre fully fused into one `pl.spmd(t_dim // T_TILE)` scope, dynamic token dim via `bind_dynamic(0, T_DYN)`.
- **Static** token dim (`verify_hc_pre_1spmd.py`) compiles fine — `core_num` is a `ConstInt`, the pipe-buffer size is constant, no local dep.
- **Multi-scope** dynamic (`hc_pre.py`) compiles fine — the matmul is its OWN spmd scope, so no GM pipe buffer is injected.

So it only triggers at: single-scope cube→vec fusion (⇒ GM pipe buffer injected) × dynamic dim (⇒ pipe size references a body-local).

### Before IR

A single fused mixed kernel (cube matmul + vector epilogue in one task) whose grid `block_num = t_dim // T_TILE` is dynamic; `InjectGMPipeBuffer` adds a placeholder `tensor.create([1])` GM pipe buffer whose real size (`slot_size * block_num`) is applied as a codegen size-override.

### Expected IR

In the generated orchestration C++, the dynamic-dim local (`int64_t t_dim_... = orch_args.tensor(0).shapes[0];`) is declared **before** any `alloc_tensors`/`TensorCreateInfo` whose size expression references it.

### Actual IR / Error

Generated `orchestration/hc_pre_test.cpp` (top of `PTO2_SCOPE()`):

```cpp
PTO2_SCOPE() {
    uint32_t gm_pipe_buffer_0_ci_shapes[1] = {static_cast<uint32_t>((8192) * ((t_dim_inline53 / 16)))};  // USES t_dim
    TensorCreateInfo gm_pipe_buffer_0_ci(gm_pipe_buffer_0_ci_shapes, 1, DataType::FLOAT32, /*manual_dep=*/true);
    TaskOutputTensors alloc_0 = alloc_tensors(gm_pipe_buffer_0_ci);
    const Tensor& gm_pipe_buffer_0 = alloc_0.get_ref(0);
    int64_t t_dim_inline53 = (int64_t)orch_args.tensor(0).shapes[0];   // DECLARED too late
    ...
    params_t0.launch_spec.set_block_num((t_dim_inline53 / 16));
}
```
→ `error: 't_dim_inline53' was not declared in this scope`.

### Root cause (source-verified, HEAD eea4735d)

`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`:
- `VisitStmt_(SeqStmtsPtr)` (line 1172) calls `EmitBatchedAllocTensors(seq->stmts_)` **first**, emitting hoisted `tensor.create` allocs at the scope top, then visits body stmts (skipping the hoisted creates).
- `EmitBatchedAllocTensors` guards hoisting with `ShapeDependsOnLocalVars(call, ...)` (line 2290), which inspects the create's **IR shape**. The injected GM pipe buffer is a placeholder `tensor.create([1])` — its IR shape references nothing, so it is hoisted.
- The real dynamic size is applied *afterward* as a string override in the `IsInjectedGMPipeCreateVar` branch (lines 2297–2309): `size_expr = 8192 * core_num_expr` where `core_num_expr = "(t_dim_inline53 / 16)"`, stashed into `tensor_create_size_expr_by_emit_name_` and consumed by the create handler (line 339). This dependency on the body-local `t_dim` is **invisible** to the hoist guard at line 2290.
- `t_dim_inline53` is a `tensor.dim` AssignStmt emitted in body order → lands after the hoisted alloc.

### Fix

In `EmitBatchedAllocTensors`, in the `IsInjectedGMPipeCreateVar` branch (lines 2297–2310): when the resolved `core_num_expr` is **non-constant** (references body-local `tensor.dim` scalars), route that create out of the hoisted batch into the per-op path — exactly the escape hatch `ShapeDependsOnLocalVars` already uses for normal dynamic creates — so the pipe-buffer alloc is emitted **after** the `t_dim` local. (Sizing the pipe buffer by a static upper bound is not cleanly available: the `bind_dynamic` symbol carries no static max to the orchestration codegen layer — it reaches codegen only as the runtime read `orch_args.tensor(0).shapes[0]` — so inventing a max risks under-allocation.)

### Git Commit ID

eea4735d

### NPU Kind

Other (please specify in description) — Ascend a2a3 (pypto-lib `--platform a2a3`); the defect is in host orchestration codegen (compile-time), not silicon-specific.

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Same cube↔vec single-scope fusion area as #1761 (that one was the runtime 507018 deadlock from per-subblock pipe replay; this is a compile-time ordering bug for the dynamic-shape case). With #1761 fixed, the static 1-spmd hc_pre runs; this bug is the remaining blocker for the **dynamic-shape** 1-spmd hc_pre.

title: [Feature] Detailed per-buffer breakdown in AllocateMemoryAddr memory report
body:
### Summary

The memory report from the `AllocateMemoryAddr` pass (`build_output/<case>/report/memory_after_AllocateMemoryAddr.txt`) only prints per-function, per-space **totals** — `Used / Limit / Usage% / MemRefs` for Vec/Mat/Left/Right/Acc. It does not show **which** buffers/tensors consume the space, their individual sizes, or their live ranges. Add a detailed per-MemRef breakdown, ideally behind a verbose flag so the default stays compact.

### Motivation / Use Case

When planning a kernel fusion or restructure, you need to know whether the combined buffers fit in a space (UB / L0 / L1). Today the report only gives the per-function total, so you must **estimate by hand**.

Concrete example: assessing whether folding inverse-RoPE into `merge_norm` fits Vec. The report shows:

```
--- merge_norm ---   Vec  112.6 KB / 192.0 KB  (58.7%)  MemRefs 16
--- rope ---         Vec   68.4 KB / 192.0 KB  (35.6%)  MemRefs 16
```

To estimate the fused footprint I had to guess the rope scratch (~15–20 KB) by hand — because the report lists neither per-buffer sizes nor which buffers are simultaneously live at the peak (which is what actually decides whether a fusion fits). A detailed breakdown would make this exact instead of a guess.

### Proposed API / Behavior

- Per-MemRef rows under each function: buffer/tensor name (or IR id + role), space, size, and live-range.
- The **peak composition**: the set of buffers simultaneously alive at the high-water mark (the set that determines headroom), not just the running total.
- Keep the current compact summary as the default; gate the detailed view behind a flag / env var (e.g. `PYPTO_MEMORY_REPORT=verbose`).

### Additional Context

- Report path: `build_output/<case>/report/memory_after_AllocateMemoryAddr.txt`
- Current format: per-function `{space: Used / Limit / Usage% / MemRefs count}`, Backend `910B`.

title: fix(codegen): keep dynamic GM pipe buffer alloc after its sizing local
body:
## Summary

A cube matmul feeding a vector epilogue, fused into **one** `pl.spmd` scope with a **dynamic** block count, makes `InjectGMPipeBuffer` (Ascend910B) inject a placeholder `tensor.create([1])` GM pipe buffer whose real size is `slot_size * core_num`. When `core_num` is dynamic it references a body-local `tensor.dim` scalar (e.g. `t_dim // 16`) emitted as an earlier statement.

`EmitBatchedAllocTensors` hoisted that alloc to the top of `PTO2_SCOPE()` because the placeholder's constant `[1]` IR shape hid the dependency from `ShapeDependsOnLocalVars`. The generated orchestration C++ then used the local before its declaration:

```cpp
uint32_t gm_pipe_buffer_0_ci_shapes[1] = {static_cast<uint32_t>((4096) * ((t_dim / 16)))};  // uses t_dim
...
int64_t t_dim = (int64_t)orch_args.tensor(0).shapes[0];   // declared too late
```

→ `error: 't_dim...' was not declared in this scope`.

## Fix

In `EmitBatchedAllocTensors`, re-check the resolved `core_num` expression against the same `locally_defined` set that `ShapeDependsOnLocalVars` uses (via the shared `ExprRefsAnyOf`). When `core_num` reads a body-local, route the create out of the hoisted batch into the per-op path so it is emitted **after** that local. The size override is still keyed by emit name, which the body-order visit reuses. Static `core_num` (constant size) hoists as before.

Only the combination triggers the bug: single-scope cube→vec fusion (⇒ GM pipe buffer injected) × dynamic dim (⇒ pipe size references a body-local). Static dim and multi-scope layouts were already fine.

## Testing

- New codegen UT `test_dynamic_gm_pipe_buffer_alloc_follows_its_size_local` asserts the sizing local is declared before the alloc; verified it fails on the pre-fix code path.
- New Ascend910B ST `test_spmd_dynamic_gm_pipe.py` covers the single-scope cube→vec fusion with a dynamic token dim end-to-end against a torch golden.
- `tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py` + `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_inject_gm_pipe_buffer.py` (136 tests) pass; clang-tidy clean.

## Related Issues

Fixes #1768

title: feat(reporter): add per-buffer breakdown to AllocateMemoryAddr memory report
body:
## Summary

The memory report written after `AllocateMemoryAddr`
(`build_output/<case>/report/memory_after_AllocateMemoryAddr.txt`) previously
showed only per-function, per-space totals (`Used / Limit / Usage% / MemRefs`).
Planning a kernel fusion required hand-estimating which buffers consume a space.

This adds a per-buffer breakdown under each space's summary — one row per base
allocation with its name, slot size, address range, and live range (statement
indices):

```
  Buffers (Vec)  -- base allocations making up Used (gaps between ranges = alignment)
    Name              |  Size       |  Address range            |  Live range
    ------------------+-------------+-------------------------+------------
    mem_vec_2         |      256 B  |  [0, 256)               |  [5, 7]
    mem_vec_3         |      256 B  |  [256, 512)             |  [6, 7]
    mem_vec_4         |      256 B  |  [512, 768)             |  [7, 8]
```

The detail is organized around the existing `Used` high-water value (the real
reserved footprint): buffers are aggregated by `base_` Ptr (view MemRefs fold
into their base's slot), sorted by address, and their sizes account for `Used`,
with alignment padding visible as gaps between consecutive address ranges. The
compact summary table is unchanged.

## Implementation

- `report.h`: new `BufferDetail` struct + `FunctionMemoryUsage.buffers`.
- `memory_report_generator.cpp`: `MemoryUsageCollector` extended with a
  monotonic statement counter (live-range proxy) and an ordered per-base map;
  stays O(N log N).
- `report.cpp`: renders the `Buffers (<space>)` block.

title: feat(pass): plumb pl.split slot_num through automatic mixed-kernel pipe
body:
## Summary

Resolves the reopened part of #1472: the cross-core ring depth (`slot_num`) was only tunable on the **manual** `pl.aic/aiv_initialize_pipe` path (PR #1584). The **automatic** cube→vector split path — `pl.spmd(..., optimizations=[pl.split(mode)])` and `pl.at(level=CORE_GROUP, optimizations=[pl.split(...)])` — hardcoded the depth (8 unidirectional / 4 bidirectional) in `BuildAutomaticPipeSetup`, so growing a vector tile past the default-8-slot ceiling required a full manual-pipe rewrite of the scope.

This adds an optional `slot_num=` keyword to `pl.split`, plumbed end-to-end.

## Usage

```python
# Shrink the auto-inserted cube->vector ring to free buffer for a larger vec tile
with pl.spmd(4, optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN, slot_num=4)]):
    ...

with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP,
           optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN, slot_num=16)]):
    ...
```

## Changes

- **DSL** (`optimizations.py`): `pl.split(mode, slot_num=N)` with positive-int validation.
- **Parser** (`ast_parser.py`): `slot_num` recorded on the InCore/AutoInCore scope attrs across the `pl.at`, spmd with-tid, and spmd for-loop forms; rejected unless the scope enables a cross-core split (`UP_DOWN` / `LEFT_RIGHT`), and unless positive.
- **Outliner** (`scope_outline_utils.h`): propagates the `slot_num` scope attr to the outlined function attr.
- **ExpandMixedKernel / `BuildAutomaticPipeSetup`**: when set, `slot_num` drives **both** the reserved buffer (`slot_size * slot_num`) and the emitted `initialize_pipe` `slot_num` attribute, so PTOAS and the auto-reserved buffer stay consistent. Omitting it keeps the PTOAS-derived default.
- **Printer**: round-trips `slot_num` via the `optimizations=[pl.split(...)]` form across all scope shapes.

## Design notes

`slot_num` drives the buffer multiplier on **both** a3 (local footprint = `slot_num` when `local_slot_num` is omitted) and a5, so **no arch-dependent sizing is needed**. Decoupling logical depth from a smaller local resident window (`local_slot_num < slot_num`, a2/a3 only) remains a manual-path-only optimization.

Pure-incremental and backward-compatible: no IR node / op / codegen / verifier changes (reuses the `slot_num` op kwarg already wired by #1584); the default 8/4 behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

- End-to-end: `slot_num=16` → reserved buffer `65536 = 4096×16`, both `initialize_pipe` calls carry `slot_num=16`.
- New tests: parser attrs / round-trip / 3 negatives (`test_scope_parsing.py`); pass before/after output (`test_expand_mixed_kernel_a2a3.py`).
- Regression: `ut/language` + `ut/ir/transforms` + `ut/codegen` + `ut/ir/statements` all green (4000+ tests).
- Docs updated (en + zh-cn).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Cross-core system tests on device (a3 / a5)
