title: [EXPERIMENT - DO NOT MERGE] Disable LegalizePTOBufferReuse to map CI dependencies
body:
## Purpose (throwaway experiment — DO NOT MERGE)

Temporarily removes `LegalizePTOBufferReuse` from the Default pipeline to **empirically determine which CI cases actually depend on it**. The CI failures on this PR are the deliverable.

## Hypothesis

`MemoryReuse` only coalesces tile variables with identical dtype **and** structural shape (`AreTileTypesCompatible` requires `shape_` equality; 2D tiles may differ only in `valid_shape`). Every difference it permits is already PTO-materializable, so the **signature-incompatible-split path** in `LegalizePTOBufferReuse` looks unreachable on real pipeline output — its unit tests construct the illegal sharing by hand.

The one behaviour `MemoryReuse` cannot model is the **Ascend910B split-AIV `tile.load` + `tile.tpop_from_aic` hardware hazard**, which this pass force-splits regardless of signature compatibility.

## Expected outcome

- If only `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_legalize_pto_buffer_reuse.py` (and any 910B-hazard codegen cases) fail → confirms the signature-split path is effectively dead and the live job is the hazard split.
- If unrelated end-to-end / codegen cases fail → the pass is load-bearing beyond the hazard, hypothesis is wrong.

## Change

Comments out the single pipeline entry in `python/pypto/ir/pass_manager.py`. Nothing else.

title: [Feature] One L1 load -> two L0B textracts (transposed + non-transposed) for QK+PV on shared KV
body:
### Summary

Support end-to-end **one GM->L1 load feeding two L0B `textract`/move** for a
single Mat tensor/parameter consumed by both a `b_trans=True` and a
`b_trans=False` `pl.matmul` in the same scope: the KV is loaded into L1 **once**,
then extracted to L0B **twice** -- once non-transposed, once transposed.

The pto-isa `textract` (Mat->L0B) already implements the transpose-extraction
path, so the L1 tile can physically serve both matmuls; this is purely a pypto
lowering gap.

Follow-up to the closed #1532 (same root cause; still reproduces on current main).

### Motivation / Use Case

dsv4 decode (`models/deepseek/v4/decode_sparse_attn.py`, `qk_pv`) uses one
`sparse_kv` tensor as both the K operand (QK, `b_trans=True`) and the V operand
(PV, `b_trans=False`). Because pypto pins a single K-orientation per SSA
tensor / InCore param, the two uses must currently be kept as **two separate
GM->L1 loads of byte-identical data**:

    qk_kv_k = sparse_kv[..., 0:HEAD_DIM]   # QK, b_trans=True
    qk_kv_v = sparse_kv[..., 0:HEAD_DIM]   # PV, b_trans=False   (identical slice)

Inspecting the generated `qk_pv.pto`, this emits **two** `pto.tload` of the same
KV per sparse block (one 512x128 row_major, one 128x512 col_major). The goal is a
single `tload` into L1 followed by two `textract` to L0B. This also blocks the
FlashAttention-style QK+PV fusion (the PV output must round-trip through GM
instead). qwen3 avoids this only because its `k_cache`/`v_cache` are separate
params; MLA/dsv4 share one KV.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Unifying the two slices into one variable:

    qk_kv = sparse_kv[..., 0:HEAD_DIM]                              # ONE L1 load
    qk_raw = pl.matmul(qk_q,  qk_kv, b_trans=True,  out_dtype=pl.FP32)  # textract #1 (transpose)
    qk_oi  = pl.matmul(qk_exp, qk_kv,                out_dtype=pl.FP32)  # textract #2 (non-transpose)

should compile and lower to **one** GM->L1 `tload` + **two** L0B `textract` with
per-use transpose. Today it fails in ConvertTensorToTileOps:

    ValueError: The operator tile.matmul requires matching inner dimensions,
    but got lhs K=128 and rhs K=512    (matmul.cpp:78, qk_oi site)

Desired lowering: keep one Mat tile (one fractal) in L1; emit two `textract`s,
one non-transpose and one transpose, instead of fixing a single K-orientation on
the SSA tensor and forcing two GM loads.

### Alternatives Considered

- Two slice vars on the same tensor -> same error (per-tensor K-orientation).
- `pl.load(target_memory=Vec)` then matmul -> matmul drops `b_trans` (per #1532).
- Status quo: two GM->L1 loads + GM round-trip for PV (current dsv4 workaround).

### Additional Context

ISA support is already present -- see pto-isa
`include/pto/npu/a2a3/TExtract.hpp`:

- `TExtractToRight` / `TExtractToLeft` accept src fractal `(ColMajor && isRowMajor)`
  **or** `(RowMajor && !isRowMajor)`; when `Dst.SFractal != Src.SFractal` it
  dispatches the transpose path `TExtractToB<...,true>` -> `TExtractToBTranspose`
  (Load3DV2 for bf16/fp32, Load2D-transpose for b8).

So one Mat tile of a fixed fractal can be extracted to L0B in either orientation;
the missing piece is pypto emitting the transpose-textract for the
opposite-`b_trans` use rather than rejecting it.

Related: #1532 (closed 2026-05-26, same root cause, still reproduces).

Environment (analysis basis): pypto `533d629d` (main), pypto-lib `56c01e1d`,
pto-isa `109c9f72`.

title: refactor(pass): fold Ascend910B load+tpop hazard into MemoryReuse, remove LegalizePTOBufferReuse
body:
## Summary

Removes the `LegalizePTOBufferReuse` pass and folds its one load-bearing job — the Ascend910B split-AIV `tile.load` + `tile.tpop_from_aic` in-place hazard split — into `MemoryReuse`, which already owns every buffer-coalescing decision.

## Motivation

`LegalizePTOBufferReuse` ran right after `MemoryReuse` to undo illegal PTO buffer sharing. An experiment (disabling the pass and reading CI) showed:

- Its **signature-legalisation path is unreachable in practice**: `MemoryReuse` only coalesces tiles with identical dtype *and* shape (`AreTileTypesCompatible`), so every sharing it produces is already PTO-materialisable. The pass's own unit tests constructed the illegal sharing by hand.
- The **only real dependency** was a single system test, `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_trans.py::TestTransposeColumnOperations::test_nd3d_transpose[a2a3]`, which silently produced wrong numerics on Ascend910B (cube transpose → `tpop_from_aic`) without the pass. Ascend950 was unaffected.

Rather than coalesce-then-split, `MemoryReuse` now never forms the hazardous sharing.

## What changed

**MemoryReuse** (`src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp`)
- Collects load-derived and tpop-consuming vars in one IR walk — only when the function is Ascend910B split-AIV (gated by `RequiresSplitLoadTpopWorkaround()`).
- In the reuse decision, blocks a writer from in-place-reusing a load buffer it reads when the writer also consumes a `tile.tpop_from_aic` value. This reuses the existing in-place "buffer still occupied at def" detection, so the guard is precise. Off-910B the inputs are empty and reuse behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Removal**
- `LegalizePTOBufferReuse` pass + factory + binding + stub + pipeline entry + CMake source + dedicated test, all deleted.
- `FoldNoOpReshape` / `BackendHandler` doc comments updated to point at `MemoryReuse`.

**Tests**
- Hazard coverage migrated to `test_memory_reuse.py`: Ascend910B split-AIV blocks the `tile.add(load, tpop)` output from reusing the load buffer; Ascend950 still reuses it.
- `test_pass_manager` strategy assertions updated.

**Docs**
- Deleted the pass doc, added an "Ascend910B load + tpop_from_aic hazard" section to the MemoryReuse doc, renumbered the passes-doc sequence, and synced zh-cn + the pass-doc-ordering rule.

## Testing

- Build: clean (`pypto_core` builds).
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/`: **1262 passed, 25 skipped** (incl. the new hazard tests).
- pre-commit: clang-format, cpplint, ruff, pyright all pass.
- The end-to-end `test_nd3d_transpose[a2a3]` regression runs on CI (Ascend sim).

title: tests(st): add L3 ring allreduce ST (monolithic InCore, RS+AG schedule)
body:
## Summary

Add L3 distributed ST `test_l3_ring_allreduce.py` — PyPTO DSL port of the **chunked ring allreduce** (reduce-scatter + allgather) from simpler PR [#975](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/pull/975) (`allreduce_ring_distributed/`).

Ring uses 2(P−1) per-round barriers with O(N/P) remote traffic per step; mesh uses a single global barrier with O(N) remote reads.

### Design

- **Monolithic InCore kernel** — single AIV task dispatch per rank. Stage-in → RS loop → AG loop → stage-out all in one `pl.range`-based kernel. PTOAS v0.45 MTE drain ([#718](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/pull/718)) makes multi-round barriers safe.
- **Fixed-P factory** `_build_ring_allreduce_program(n_ranks)` — separate programs for P=2 and P=4 with static chunk sizes.
- **Flat scratch window `[1, SIZE]`** — chunking via Scalar offsets, matching simpler's pointer-arithmetic approach.
- **No exchange buffer** — reads directly from peer's chunk slot via `pld.tile.remote_load`.
- **Notify-all / wait-all per round** — signal matrix `[2(P−1), P]` int32, zero-initialized by `alloc_window_buffer`. Python `int` shapes avoid SSA variable renaming inside `pl.range` loop bodies.

### Algorithm (matching `allreduce_ring_kernel.cpp` @ `9c2236ac`)

| Phase | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Stage-in | Partition rank input → `NR` equal chunks in scratch |
| Reduce-scatter | `(NR−1)` ring steps: barrier → `remote_load` left neighbour → `pl.add` into local |
| Allgather | `(NR−1)` ring steps: barrier → `remote_load` left neighbour → store into local |
| Stage-out | Concatenate chunks → output |

Golden: `output[i] = P·i + 100·P·(P−1)/2` — same as mesh allreduce.

### Verification

- **P=2**: `test_l3_ring_allreduce.py -k "2" --platform=a2a3 --device=0,1 --forked` — ✅ PASS (32s)
- **P=4**: `test_l3_ring_allreduce.py -k "4" --platform=a2a3 --device=0-3 --forked` — ✅ PASS (31s)
- **Regression**: `tests/st/distributed --device=0,1 --forked` — ✅ 33/33 passed, 0 failures

### Dependencies

- [#1758](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/1758) (scalar `__rfloordiv__`/`__rtruediv__`) — merged 2026-06-12
- PTOAS ≥ v0.44 (MTE drain [#718](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/pull/718)) — v0.45 in CI/Docker

### Files changed

- `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_ring_allreduce.py` — new file, ~254 lines

No C++/IR/pass/binding changes.

title: fix(incore-profiling): support single-kind ptoas kernels
body:
## Summary

The `incore-profiling` skill's testcase generator and symbol resolver had only ever been exercised on **mixed cube+vector** kernels (e.g. `qk_pv`), whose merged `__global__` dispatcher is synthesized by the tool as plain C++ (mangled symbol). Profiling the first **pure single-kind** kernel (`merge_norm`, vector-only) failed, because ptoas emits pure kernels as `extern "C" __global__` (unmangled symbol):

1. **Link failure** — `emit_launch_cpp` forward-declared the kernel **without** `extern "C"`, so the `<<<>>>` launch call mangled and failed to link:
   `ld.lld: error: undefined reference ... merge_norm(...)`.
2. **Symbol-resolution failure** — `resolve_symbol` only matched the demangled `name(...)` form, so it could never find a bare unmangled `extern "C"` symbol (`c++filt` leaves it as just `merge_norm`, no parens):
   `failed to resolve kernel symbol for ['merge_norm']`.

## Fix

- `gen_profiling_case.py` — emit `extern "C"` on **both** the `launch.cpp` forward declaration and the synthesized mixed dispatcher, so the launch-ABI symbol is always unmangled, uniform with the ptoas pure-kernel convention.
- `incore_profile.py` — `resolve_symbol` also accepts an exact unmangled match (`demangled == name`), in addition to the existing `name(...)` prefix match.

13 insertions, 3 deletions across the two helper scripts.

## Testing

Verified end-to-end with `msprof op simulator` (camodel, cann-8.5.1, Ascend910B1):

- `merge_norm` (pure vector) — now builds, resolves, and collects: `EXPORTED 1/1`.
- `qk_pv` (mixed cube+vector) — still `EXPORTED 1/1` (its symbol is now the unmangled `qk_pv`; no regression).

These are `.claude/skills/` tooling scripts (not shipped library code), so the cross-layer-sync / type-stub / `tests/` policies don't apply; both files pass the repo pre-commit hooks (ruff, pyright).

title: feat(runtime): Add per-task ring sizing to RunConfig
body:
## Summary

The runtime recently added per-task ring sizing via `CallConfig.runtime_env`
(runtime #1042). This wires it through to PyPTO's `RunConfig` so callers can
size the per-task rings per invocation.

- Add three optional overrides to `RunConfig`: `ring_task_window`, `ring_heap`,
  `ring_dep_pool`. `None` (default) leaves the field unset so the runtime falls
  back to its `PTO2_RING_*` env var / compile-time default.
- `_build_call_config` transcribes each into `CallConfig.runtime_env` **only
  when set**, leaving the field at its `0` default otherwise — matching the
  precedence the runtime expects (per-task value > env var > compile-time
  default). Both `CompiledProgram.build_call_config` paths forward `run_config`
  unchanged, so the new fields propagate automatically.
- `RunConfig` validates the values early (power-of-2 ≥ 4 for the task window,
  power-of-2 ≥ 1024 bytes for the heap, `[4, INT32_MAX]` for the dep pool),
  mirroring the runtime's `RuntimeEnv::validate()` so callers get a clear error
  at construction rather than a deep failure inside the runtime.

`RunConfig` is per-invocation, which maps exactly onto the runtime's "per L2
submission" granularity — no IR / pass / codegen changes are required.

## Testing

- [x] Added unit tests in `tests/ut/runtime/test_run_config.py`: field
  defaults, valid/boundary values, the three validation rules, and
  `_build_call_config` transcription (set / unset / partial) via a spy
  `CallConfig` so they run without the optional `simpler` package. 20 new tests
  pass; `ruff` clean.
- [x] Code review completed.

## Related Issues

Adapts PyPTO to runtime per-task ring sizing (`CallConfig.runtime_env`).

title: feat(ir): add DimExpr IR node for composite dynamic dimensions
body:
### Summary

Add `DimExpr` — a first-class compile-time IR expression node (`ObjectKind::DimExpr`) that wraps composite dimension expressions like `NR * SIZE` with `IgnoreField` semantics on `body_`. This prevents passes (ConvertToSSA, InitMemRef, SSAVerify) from walking into type-annotation Vars inside composite dims, which would otherwise fatally break tile allocation when composite shapes appear at the InCore body level.

### Motivation

PR #1765 (already merged) stores composite dims as bare `Mul(Var, ConstInt)` directly in `TensorType` shapes. While sufficient for parametric types (function signatures), it breaks when composite dims appear in InCore body expressions like `pl.create_tensor([NR * SIZE, 1])` — ConvertToSSA renames the `Var("NR")` inside the type-annotation Mul, and InitMemRef then rejects the tile because it can't find NR's definition in scope.

`DimExpr` solves this by wrapping the arithmetic in a node that every visitor/verifier/serializer treats as opaque by default (via `IgnoreField`), while expression functors (arith analyzers) auto-unwrap for free (via a non-pure-virtual default).

### What's in this PR

**Phase 1 — IR Foundation:**
- C++ `DimExpr` class (`include/pypto/ir/scalar_expr.h`) with `body_` as `IgnoreField`
- Visitor (no-op), Mutator (identity), ExprFunctor (auto-unwrapping default)
- Structural equality: DimExpr(Mul) ⇔ bare Mul
- Python printer: unwraps `DimExpr` to print its body
- Codegen: unwrap in `GenerateExprString`, `CollectVarsFromShapeExprImpl`, `GetExprAsCode`
- SSA verifier: register Vars inside `DimExpr` bodies in outermost scope

**Phase 2 — Python Bindings + Parser:**
- `nb::class_<DimExpr, Expr>` binding + `ir.dim_expr()` factory
- Type stubs in `ir.pyi`
- Parser auto-wraps composite Scalar dims in `_validate_dim_value` and `python_value_to_ir`

**Tests (differentiating from #1765):**
- `test_composite_dim_is_wrapped_in_dimexpr`: parser produces `DimExpr`, not bare `Mul`
- `test_dimexpr_survives_print_parse_roundtrip`: round-trip preserves structure
- `test_bare_dynvar_not_wrapped_in_dimexpr`: bare `pl.dynamic()` stays as `Var`
- `test_dimexpr_collect_vars_from_shape`: codegen correctly finds Vars inside `DimExpr`

### What's NOT in this PR (deferred to follow-up)

- Distributed ST generalization (allgather, reduce_scatter, broadcast → N-rank with `NR * SIZE`)
- Host orchestration codegen (`EmitShapeDimVarDefs` for DimExpr bodies)
- Dev docs for DimExpr

### Design decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| `body_` is `IgnoreField` | Prevents ConvertToSSA from renaming type-annotation Vars |
| ExprFunctor default recurses into `body_` | Arith analyzers auto-unwrap with 0 changes |
| IRVisitor is no-op, IRMutator is identity | Default traversal doesn't descend into composite dims |
| DimExpr is NOT a `VarLike` | Same rationale as MemRef (compile-time vs runtime semantics) |
| Compile-time only — fully resolved before codegen reaches NPU | Zero runtime impact |

title: feat(distributed): add pld.tensor.barrier, broadcast, allgather, reduce_scatter composite intrinsics
body:
### Summary

Add four new composite collective intrinsics to the `pld.tensor.*` family, completing the window-bound distributed collective API established by `pld.tensor.allreduce` (#1746). Each op follows the same composite-op pattern: register a C++ type deducer, write a lowering rule in `LowerCompositeOps` (pass 14), add access-analysis entries in `ConvertTensorToTileOps` (pass 12), expose raw IR builders and DSL wrappers, and cover with P=2/P=4 ST tests + unit tests.

### New intrinsics

| Op | Signature | Phases | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pld.tensor.barrier` | `barrier(signal) → signal` | 2 (notify-all / wait-all) | `DistributedTensor` rebind |
| `pld.tensor.broadcast` | `broadcast(target, signal, root=k) → target` | 3 (notify / wait / tile.create + pld.tile.get from root) | `DistributedTensor` rebind |
| `pld.tensor.allgather` | `allgather(local_data, target, signal, out) → out` | 4 (load / stage-in / notify / wait / per-peer pld.tile.get) | `Tensor [1, NR*SIZE]` — writes directly into user-provided `out` |
| `pld.tensor.reduce_scatter` | `reduce_scatter(target, signal, op=Sum) → target` | 5 (same 5-phase shape as allreduce) | `DistributedTensor` rebind |

All ops use `kGe` wait predicates and carry the single-shot signal-buffer discipline. `reduce_scatter` lowers the same 5-phase post-reduce-barrier recipe as `allreduce` to prevent the WAR race.

**Allgather lowering** is aligned with the simpler `allgather_distributed` reference (`simpler/examples/workers/l3/allgather_distributed/`): each rank stores at local `[0,0]` in its private HCCL window. Phase 3 uses a shared `[1, SIZE]` VEC staging tile and `pld.tile.get` to transfer each peer's chunk directly into the output Tensor at column offset `[0, r*SIZE]` for all ranks including self (HCCL `CommRemotePtr` returns identity for `peer == my_rank`). No `tile.concat` accumulation — each intermediate Tile is only `[1, SIZE]` and fits in UB for any SIZE or NR. Fully N-rank general.

**Broadcast lowering** similarly emits `tile.create` + `pld.tile.get` directly (the tensor-level get has no codegen and `ConvertTensorToTileOps` runs before this pass). The VEC staging tile is sized from the target's compile-time shape; `pld.tile.get(target, peer=root, target, stage)` transfers root's data into every rank's window slot via HCCL identity mapping for self.

### Files changed (20 files, ~2228 insertions)

- **C++ op deducers**: `src/ir/op/distributed/collective.cpp` — 4 deducers consolidated per review feedback
- **Lowering rules**: `src/ir/transforms/lower_composite_ops_pass.cpp` (+506) — 4 `Lower<Op>Rule` functions + kRules entries
- **Access analysis**: `src/ir/transforms/convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp` (+83) — `GetWriteTargetExpr` + `AnalyzeCallAccess` + barrier alias origin
- **Build**: `CMakeLists.txt` (+1) — add `collective.cpp`
- **Python IR builders**: `python/pypto/ir/op/distributed/tensor_ops.py` (+101)
- **DSL wrappers**: `python/pypto/language/distributed/op/tensor_ops.py` (+160)
- **Re-exports**: `python/pypto/ir/op/distributed/__init__.py` (+16)
- **Docs**: `docs/en/dev/passes/14-lower_composite_ops.md` (+62), `docs/zh-cn/dev/passes/14-lower_composite_ops.md` (+62)
- **ST tests** (4 new files): `tests/st/distributed/collectives/test_l3_tensor_{barrier,broadcast,allgather,reduce_scatter}_intrinsic.py` — P=2/P=4 parametrized, deferred construction, rank-aware goldens
- **UT tests**: `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_lower_composite_ops.py` (+306), `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.py` (+139)
- **ST reorg**: moved existing hand-written tests into `collectives/` subdirectory

### Review feedback addressed

- ✅ Consolidated 4 separate op files → single `collective.cpp` ([review](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/1782#discussion_r1953012347))
- ✅ Allgather 2-arg → 3-arg → 4-arg `allgather(local_data, target, signal, out)` returning `Tensor`. Replaced `tile.concat` UB bottleneck with per-peer `pld.tile.get` writing directly into output at column offset `[0, r*SIZE]` via a single shared VEC staging tile. Each transfer is `[1, SIZE]` — scales to any NR/SIZE.
- ✅ Allgather lowering aligned with simpler HCCL window reference (store at `[0,0]`, `pld.tile.get` for all ranks, HCCL identity mapping for self)
- ✅ Broadcast lowering emits `tile.create` + `pld.tile.get` directly, no `remote_load` / `tile.store`
- ✅ Barrier `GetWriteTargetExpr` returns `args_[0]` for alias-origin propagation ([review](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/1782#discussion_r1953012355))
- ✅ ST tests reorganized into `collectives/` subdirectory ([review](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/1782#discussion_r1953012356))

### Verification

- **Sim Docker UT**: 4/4 allgather tests, 25/25 full collective UTs ✅
- **Sim Docker ST**: 9/9 distributed sim tests (P=2) ✅
- Latest commit: `c6581649` on `georgebisbas:feat/composite-collectives`

title: fix(SplitVectorKernel): per-subblock slice for reshape of a full tile
body:
## What

`SplitVectorKernel` mishandles a `tile.reshape` that lifts a **full,
un-split** source tile onto the cross-core split axis. The generic
op-halving only shrinks the reshape's result type; since reshape is an
offsetless view, **both AIV subblocks read the first half of the full
buffer** and lane 1 silently reuses lane 0's data.

The common trigger is a rank-1 load (which legitimately bypasses the
split-specific load rewrite, having no split axis) immediately reshaped
into a `[1, N]` row that spans the full split width.

## Why it's a bug

In DeepSeek-V4 decode `proj_b` (INT8 GEMM + per-channel dequant epilogue,
run with `pl.split(SplitMode.LEFT_RIGHT)`) the per-channel scale is
`wo_b_scale[n0:n0+B_N_TILE]` -> rank-1 `[B_N_TILE]` load -> `reshape([1, B_N_TILE])`.
After the split, lane 1 correctly pops its half of the matmul result and
stores to columns `n0 + subblock_idx*half`, **but multiplies by the wrong
half of the scale** (it reads `scale[n0 : n0+half]` instead of
`scale[n0+half : n0+B_N_TILE]`), corrupting ~half the output channels.

It only shows on device: `__CPU_SIM` does not override `get_subblockid()`
(single-lane), and the standalone golden's synthetic `wo_b_scale` is
near-uniform across channels so the wrong half is numerically close. With
realistic (`torch.randn`) weights the decode `swa` / `hca` / `csa` attention
outputs regress -- ~22% of `x_out` elements out of tolerance on a2a3.

## Fix

For a `tile.reshape` under a vector split whose input is **not** already
lane-split and whose split dim is non-singleton, emit the reshape at full
width, then a per-subblock `tile.slice [.., subblock_idx*half : +half]` on
the split axis so each lane reads its own half. Reshapes whose input is
already split fall through to the existing result-halving unchanged.

## Validation

- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_split_vector_kernel.py` -- 26 passed.
- DeepSeek-V4 `decode_attention_swa/hca/csa` on a2a3: **FAIL -> PASS**
  (broken baseline: `swa x_out` 22.2% mismatch; with fix all three pass).
- Repo scan: no other `pl.split` scope hits the changed path (other
  split-scope reshapes are non-split or `[1, N]` singleton on the UP_DOWN
  axis, which the singleton guard skips).

title: [experiment][do-not-merge] memory-reuse: disable AreTileTypesCompatible to map its CI coverage
body:
## ⚠️ EXPERIMENT — DO NOT MERGE

This PR is a **data-gathering experiment**, not a feature. It exists only to let CI tell us **exactly which cases depend on the `AreTileTypesCompatible` reuse gate** in `MemoryReuse`.

## What it does

Forces `AreTileTypesCompatible()` to `return true`, so `MemoryReuse` no longer blocks buffer reuse on **shape / dtype / TileView** differences. (Single-file change in `src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp`.)

## Why

PTO codegen now emits a **per-variable** `pto.alloc_tile` — each tile var gets its **own address + own type** (`EmitAllocTileForVar`). The "same shape required" gate was added back when codegen bound **one `alloc_tile` per buffer** and used it for all ops on that buffer (#331). The L0 cross-shape reuse exception (#1601) already relies on the per-var model. So the general shape constraint *may* be over-conservative — this run measures its real coverage.

## What to look at in CI

- **Unit tests**: locally, 5 `test_memory_reuse.py` cases flip by design (cross-dtype, fillpad ×3, 3D `valid_shape`) — these assert the gate's behavior.
- **The signal we actually want**: `st` / codegen / **ptoas** jobs. Local UT codegen passes (simple kernels don't trigger conflicting reuse); the real correctness impact (e.g. the paged-attention scenario behind #331) only surfaces at the ptoas/system-test layer. Those failures map the gate's true necessity.

## Next steps (not in this PR)

Depending on which jobs fail, decide whether to (a) keep the gate, (b) relax only `shape` (keep `dtype`/layout), or (c) extend the L0-style byte-reuse to more spaces with a proper codegen audit. Then close this PR.

title: feat(ir): add pl.create_tensor(init_value=) for AICPU buffer pre-fill
body:
## Summary

Wire the runtime's `TensorCreateInfo::set_initial_value()` into pypto so a runtime-allocated output can be **pre-filled on the AICPU before any kernel writes it**. This exposes the runtime's existing AICPU fill/zeroing capability — previously reachable but unconnected from pypto (only the runtime's own examples used it).

New DSL parameter:

```python
# Zero a runtime-allocated buffer (valid for every dtype)
c = pl.create_tensor([16, 16], dtype=pl.FP32, init_value=0)

# Non-zero fill (integer / 32- or 64-bit float dtypes)
c = pl.create_tensor([16, 16], dtype=pl.FP32, init_value=2.5)
```

Generated orchestration code:

```cpp
TensorCreateInfo c_ci(c_ci_shapes, 2, DataType::FLOAT32);
c_ci.set_initial_value(0);                           // zero: dtype-agnostic uint64 overload
// non-zero fp32: c_ci.set_initial_value(static_cast<float>(2.5));
```

## Design

- `tensor.create` op gains a `double init_value` attr; DSL/IR `create` gain an `init_value: int | float | None` parameter, normalized to `float`.
- Codegen emits the fill right after the `TensorCreateInfo`:
  - **zero** → `set_initial_value(0)` (default `uint64_t` overload — zero packs to zero bytes for every dtype/element size, so no `half`/`bfloat16` type is needed).
  - **non-zero** → typed `static_cast<ctype>(value)` with full round-trippable precision.
  - **non-zero sub-32-bit float (fp16/bf16)** → rejected with a clear `CHECK`: the orchestration translation unit has no `half`/`bfloat16` type to pack the element bytes.
  - **fractional value into an integer dtype** → rejected to avoid silent truncation.
- The Submit synth-output `TensorCreateInfo` path carries a comment explaining it intentionally has no `init_value` (no user-facing `create` to honour).

The fill applies only to runtime-allocated outputs and is cheaper than `pl.full` (which materializes a constant via a kernel).

## Testing

- [x] 6 new tests in `tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py` (zero fp32, non-zero float, non-zero int, fractional-int reject, fp16 non-zero reject, fp16 zero allowed)
- [x] Broader codegen + tensor-op sweep: 628 passed
- [x] Full Default pass pipeline verified end-to-end (init_value survives to codegen)
- [x] clang-tidy clean on the C++ diff
- [x] Docs updated (en + zh-cn operation reference)

title: feat(ir): forbid_output_alias marker + remove tile-type reuse gate in MemoryReuse
body:
## Summary

Replace the coarse tile-type reuse-compatibility gate in MemoryReuse with a precise, op-semantic no-alias mechanism, and close every in-place hazard the removal exposed.

1. **Add per-operand `forbid_output_alias(arg_index)`** (`OpRegistryEntry`): an op declares a specific input whose buffer its output must not reuse — finer than `not_inplace_safe()` (forbids aliasing *any* input). `tile.sel` marks its mask (arg 0) and tmp scratch (arg 3).

2. **Remove `AreTileTypesCompatible`** (shape/dtype/TileView match + L0 byte-reuse exception). PTO codegen binds a per-var `alloc_tile` to each tile, so tiles sharing a MemRef may carry different shape/dtype/TileView. Enables cross-dtype / cross-shape / divergent-`valid_shape` reuse.

3. **Unify the no-alias guard**: `not_inplace_safe()` and `forbid_output_alias(i)` feed one per-output forbidden-input set (`ForbidAliasCollector`).

4. **Resolve operands to their physical buffer** in the guard (`TileMemRefBase` + `base_remap`), so a forbidden operand reached via VIEW inheritance or coalesced onto another buffer by an earlier reuse is still caught.

5. **Mark the ops whose in-place the gate had been incidentally hiding** (found by on-device replay-bisecting qwen3-14B decode, rank-3 gather, and DeepSeek-V4 SWA):
   - `tile.row_sum/row_max/row_min` — read input row + tmp scratch → `not_inplace_safe`.
   - `tile.rsqrt` — high-precision path reads input + tmp (like `tile.recip`) → `not_inplace_safe`.
   - `tile.{row,col}_expand{,_mul,_add,_sub,_div}` — broadcast vector (arg 1) re-read per row/col → `forbid_output_alias(1)`.
   - `tile.cast` — a *widening* cast (output dtype wider than input) cannot run in place (write cursor outruns read cursor); forbid output↔input aliasing only in the widening direction.

## Testing (Ascend a2a3, on device)
- qwen3-14B decode: **PASS**
- DeepSeek-V4 `decode_attention_swa`: **PASS** (kv_cache + x_out)
- gather (`TestGatherIndex`) + cmp (tile/tensor): **PASS**
- memory_reuse UT: **52 passed** (incl. `TestForbidOutputAlias`: sel / row_sum / view-reached / widening-cast / col_expand_mul); full `tests/ut`: **6101 passed, 2 skipped**

## Docs
- `docs/{en,zh-cn}/dev/passes/30-memory_reuse.md` updated (reuse conditions + no-alias guard + test coverage).

title: [Bug] Removing a vector op (pl.transpose) from a fused cube+vec spmd reallocates the MTE3→V fence EVENT_ID and deadlocks at runtime (AICPU 507018)
body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto** (codegen + runtime) — The fault is in the AIV pipe-fence / sync-event (EVENT_ID) allocation during codegen. A mathematically-equivalent, cleanly-compiling kernel deterministically deadlocks at runtime (AICPU 507018). 507018 originates in the pypto `runtime` submodule but the trigger is the codegen fence-event assignment.

### Description

In `models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py` (pypto-lib, DSv4 `hc_pre` fused into a single `pl.spmd` scope: cube RMS+matmul → GM scratch `mixes_gm`, read back in-task for the pre/post/mix_x/comb vector epilogue), the `mix_x` step builds 4 per-head scalar columns `pre0..pre3`.

Two **mathematically-equivalent** ways to build them:

**(A) via transpose — PASSES**
```python
pre_eps_t = pl.transpose(pre_eps, axis1=0, axis2=1)      # [HC_PAD, T_TILE]
pre0 = pl.mul(pl.reshape(pre_eps_t[0:1, 0:T_TILE], [T_TILE, 1]), 1.0)
pre1 = pl.mul(pl.reshape(pre_eps_t[1:2, 0:T_TILE], [T_TILE, 1]), 1.0)
pre2 = pl.mul(pl.reshape(pre_eps_t[2:3, 0:T_TILE], [T_TILE, 1]), 1.0)
pre3 = pl.mul(pl.reshape(pre_eps_t[3:4, 0:T_TILE], [T_TILE, 1]), 1.0)
```

**(B) via direct column slices — DEADLOCKS (AICPU 507018, 5/5 deterministic on a2a3)**
```python
pre0 = pl.mul(pre_eps[:, 0:1], 1.0)
pre1 = pl.mul(pre_eps[:, 1:2], 1.0)
pre2 = pl.mul(pre_eps[:, 2:3], 1.0)
pre3 = pl.mul(pre_eps[:, 3:4], 1.0)
```

Both produce identical `[T_TILE,1]` contiguous tiles. (B) compiles cleanly (pypto + ptoas), then hangs on device:
```
sync_run_streams: aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
```
Reproduced 5/5; variant (A) passes every time. Repro = the single 5-line swap above, nothing else changed.

**Root cause (localized to codegen).** Diffing the two generated `hc_pre_1spmd_aiv.cpp`, the *only* difference is the hardware sync-event (`EVENT_ID`) allocation for the `MTE3→V` pipe fences. Removing the benign `pl.transpose` vector op makes the fence allocator move the `mix_x` loop's double-buffer fence off `EVENT_ID3` onto `EVENT_ID2`, and rearrange the local fences:

| | mix_x loop double-buffer fence (MTE3→V) | transpose-local fence |
|---|---|---|
| (A) transpose, PASS | `EVENT_ID3` (prime → wait → set → drain) | `EVENT_ID2` (set/wait pair) |
| (B) colslice, DEADLOCK | `EVENT_ID2` (prime → wait → set → drain) | — (removed); new `EVENT_ID3` pair |

Per-`EVENT_ID` static `set_flag`/`wait_flag` counts stay balanced in both, and per-event program order looks alternating — so it is **not a missing fence**. The deadlock appears to be an event liveness/reuse hazard in the allocator that only manifests under this kernel's `split=0` dual-AIV-subblock replay (cf #1761) combined with the cube→GM-scratch (`mixes_gm`) self-RAW (cf #1650). Giving the allocator one extra distinct event (what the transpose incidentally does) avoids it.

This makes `pl.transpose` a load-bearing workaround in `hc_pre.py`, which is surprising and fragile.

Related (same 507018 family, different root cause): #1761, #1650, #1592.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `6f0304d` (the `mix_x` transpose has existed since the hc_pre single-spmd fusion, PR pypto-lib#533, on `main`) |
| pypto | `a18c4cf9` (branch: main) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `48980572` |
| pto-isa | `8e436661` (branch: main) |
| ptoas | `0.45` |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Repro variants (differ only in the `pre0..pre3` block above): `hc_pre_transpose.py` (PASS) / `hc_pre_colslice.py` (deadlock) — will attach.
- Generated-code evidence: build dirs `_jit_hc_pre_test_20260616_163200` (transpose) vs `_20260616_163215` (colslice); diff isolated to the `EVENT_ID2`/`EVENT_ID3` reassignment in `kernels/aiv/hc_pre_1spmd_aiv.cpp`.
- Run on `a2a3` real device (`--mode decode`, T=128).
- A minimal standalone repro was not extracted; per prior experience this 507018 class only manifests in the fuller fused scope (cube + GM self-RAW + multi-consumer vec). The 5-line swap on `hc_pre.py` is a deterministic trigger.

title: [Bug] SplitVectorKernel (pl.split UP_DOWN) rescales reshape result TYPE but not its shape ARGUMENT → memory_reuse OOB abort (size 64 into 32)
body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto** (compile-time codegen) — `SplitVectorKernel` (the `pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)` lowering) row-splits a vector scope by halving tile **types**, but leaves the explicit shape **argument** of `pl.tile.reshape` un-rescaled. A later `memory_reuse` pass then sizes the reshape output from the stale (un-split) argument and aborts when it cannot fit that into the split-sized reuse slot.

### Description

Adding `optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)]` to the fused single-`pl.spmd` scope in `models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py` (DSv4 `hc_pre`) aborts at **compile time** (a2a3sim `--compile-only`, deterministic 6/6):

```
pypto.InternalError: Internal error: sharing-group member offset 0
rebased to rel=0 size=64 falls outside reuse target (size 32)
Check failed: rel >= 0 && (uint64_t)rel + old->size_ <= (*source_memref)->size_
  at src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp:1328
C++ traceback: memory_reuse_pass.cpp:1859 -> fuse_create_assemble_to_slice_pass.cpp:124 (x3) -> memory_reuse_pass.cpp:1361
```

**Root cause (from the pass IR dump `30_after_InitMemRef.py`, i.e. after `SplitVectorKernel` at pass 24).** The `mix_x` epilogue builds 4 per-head scalar columns via transpose + reshape:

```python
pre_eps_t = pl.transpose(pre_eps, axis1=0, axis2=1)          # [HC_PAD, T_TILE]
pre0 = pl.mul(pl.reshape(pre_eps_t[0:1, 0:T_TILE], [T_TILE, 1]), 1.0)   # T_TILE == 16
pre1 = pl.mul(pl.reshape(pre_eps_t[1:2, 0:T_TILE], [T_TILE, 1]), 1.0)
pre2 = pl.mul(pl.reshape(pre_eps_t[2:3, 0:T_TILE], [T_TILE, 1]), 1.0)
pre3 = pl.mul(pl.reshape(pre_eps_t[3:4, 0:T_TILE], [T_TILE, 1]), 1.0)
```

After UP_DOWN the dumped IR shows the reshape **result type halved to `[8,1]`** (32 B) while the reshape **shape argument stays `[16, 1]`** (64 B):

```python
# 30_after_InitMemRef.py
t__tmp_v15: pl.Tile[[8, 1], pl.FP32, pl.MemRef(mem_vec_40, 0,   32), pl.Mem.Vec] = pl.tile.reshape(t__tmp_v14, [16, 1])
t__tmp_v17: pl.Tile[[8, 1], pl.FP32, pl.MemRef(mem_vec_40, 64,  32), pl.Mem.Vec] = pl.tile.reshape(...,        [16, 1])
t__tmp_v19: pl.Tile[[8, 1], pl.FP32, pl.MemRef(mem_vec_40, 128, 32), pl.Mem.Vec] = pl.tile.reshape(...,        [16, 1])
t__tmp_v21: pl.Tile[[8, 1], pl.FP32, pl.MemRef(mem_vec_40, 192, 32), pl.Mem.Vec] = pl.tile.reshape(...,        [16, 1])
pre0_inline10: pl.Tile[[8, 1], pl.FP32, pl.MemRef(mem_vec_51, 0, 32), pl.Mem.Vec] = pl.tile.reshape(..., [16, 1])
# ... pre1/pre2/pre3 identical
```

`memory_reuse` computes the reshape output size from the argument `[16, 1]` = **64 bytes**, but the split allocated a `[8, 1]` = **32-byte** slot → `64 > 32` → the assert (`size=64 falls outside reuse target (size 32)`). The `64` and `32` in the error map exactly to the stale `[16,1]` shape vs the split `[8,1]` type.

So `SplitVectorKernel` halves `reshape`'s result tile type but does not halve the `[T_TILE, 1]` literal it carries (because `T_TILE` is a Python constant baked into the op argument).

**Reproduction**
- File: `models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre_updown_draft.py` (the committed `hc_pre.py` with one line changed: `optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)]` added to the `pl.spmd(...)`). Will attach.
- `python models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre_updown_draft.py -p a2a3sim --mode decode --compile-only` → aborts as above (compile-only, no device needed).
- Removing the transpose+reshape (using `pre_eps[:, h:h+1]` column slices instead, no `reshape(_, [T_TILE,1])`) makes this compile pass — confirming the `reshape` shape-argument is the trigger.

**Related**
- #839 — same class (SplitVectorKernel mishandling a `reshape` under split), but manifests as a runtime precision error rather than this compile-time memory_reuse abort. Likely the same underlying weakness in how the split rewrites `reshape`.
- #1789 — the column-slice workaround (which sidesteps *this* bug) hits a separate **runtime** 507018 fence-allocation deadlock on the same kernel.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `6f0304d` (branch `perf/dsv4-hc-pre-sinkstack-mixx`; repro = `hc_pre_updown_draft.py`) |
| pypto | `a18c4cf9` (branch: main) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `48980572` |
| pto-isa | `8e436661` (branch: main) |
| ptoas | `0.45` |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- The crash is in `memory_reuse_pass` reached via `fuse_create_assemble_to_slice_pass`; the offending allocs are `mem_vec_40/51/52/53/54` (the transposed `pre_eps_t` rows and `pre0..pre3`).
- Pass dump used: enable via `run_jit(..., compile_cfg=dict(dump_passes=True))`; inspect `build_output/.../passes_dump/30_after_InitMemRef.py` (last dump before the failing pass).
- Fix direction: when `SplitVectorKernel` rescales a `reshape`'s result tile type, it must also rescale the op's target-shape argument (and any baked-in `T_TILE`-derived literal) consistently.

title: feat(runtime): L2 swimlane two-pass dep_gen capture + dfx name_map
body:
## Summary

Makes the L2 swimlane usable again after the runtime bump, where the converter
now needs a dep_gen task graph (`deps.json`) plus a name map to render
dependency arrows and resolved kernel names instead of anonymous `task(rXtY)`
lanes. Two changes:

- **Two-pass swimlane execution.** Enabling `enable_l2_swimlane` on an onboard
  platform runs the kernel twice: a dep_gen graph capture, then a clean
  in-process timing pass (dep_gen perturbs timing, so the graph and the timing
  are captured separately — the converter's documented workflow). The graph
  pass runs in a **subprocess** because the runtime's per-run finalize does not
  reliably reclaim the SVM host-register mappings the DFX collectors allocate,
  so a second DFX run in the *same* process hits the registration cap
  (`halHostRegister` rc 8); a child process reclaims that state on exit. The
  capture is best-effort and never fatal, bounded by a timeout, and uses a
  per-run uuid so concurrent captures don't collide. The subprocess rebuilds
  orch args from `golden.py` (harness) or a saved spec (compiled-program API) —
  host tensors are serialized with real data so data-as-control inputs route
  the same graph; only device-resident tensors fall back to zeros. Simulator
  platforms stay single-pass.
- **dfx name_map synthesis** so the profiling tools render readable kernel names.

> The orchestration-level `ArgDirection` signature change that was previously
> bundled on this branch has been dropped — it surfaced a separate, deterministic
> direction-aware host↔device staging bug in the a2a3-onboard / a5 runtimes and
> will be reworked in its own PR alongside the runtime fix.

## Testing

- [x] Onboard end-to-end on a2a3 (qwen3-14b decode_layer, `--enable-l2-swimlane`): `deps.json` + `l2_swimlane_records.json` produced, `merged_swimlane_*.json` renders dependency arrows + resolved kernel names; golden passes

title: feat(distributed): pl.nranks_dim — first-class DSL primitive for distributed rank-count dimensions
body:
### Why

Distributed kernels express per-rank buffer shapes in terms of the world size — `signal: DistributedTensor[[NR, 1], INT32]` where `NR` is the number of ranks.  Before this PR, the only way to express that dimension was `pl.dynamic("NR")`, a string-keyed general-purpose mechanism that carries no semantic distinction between rank-count dimensions and ordinary dynamic axes.
This created three problems:

1. **No compiler awareness.** The compiler had no way to distinguish "this dimension is the rank count" from "this dimension is an arbitrary runtime value."  Downstream passes and codegen had to resort to fragile name matching (`"NR"` substring heuristics) that silently broke on any deviation.
2. **Leaky abstraction.** The rank count is a first-class distributed concept — it should be a named DSL primitive, not a string argument to a generic dynamic-dimension function.
3. **No misuse detection.** Writing `pl.load(data, [NR, 0], ...)` in a tile expression would silently produce broken IR because `NR` resolved like any ther dynamic dimension, leaking into tile shapes where only `ConstInt` is legal.

### What

This PR introduces `pl.nranks_dim` — a singleton `DynVar` that is semantically distinct from `pl.dynamic()`:

```python
NR = pl.nranks_dim  # singleton — no parentheses, not a function call

@pl.function
def kernel(self,
    signal: pld.DistributedTensor[[NR, 1], INT32],  # ← type annotations only
) -> ...:
    nranks = pld.nranks(ctx)
    for peer in pl.range(nranks):   # ← dynamic loop bound (runtime value)
        chunk = pl.load(..., [1, SIZE])  # ← tile shapes always ConstInt
```



Contract:

- pl.nranks_dim must only appear in type annotations (parameter shapes, return types). It carries an is_nranks_dim_ flag on the underlying ir::Var.

- Tile shapes (pl.load / pl.store / pld.tile.remote_load) remain ConstInt — the rank count only controls how many times the static-tile loop body runs, never what the tile looks like.
- The compiler rejects misuse in expression position with a clear error:
"pl.nranks_dim must only appear in type annotations, not in expressions."
- Resolution is structural — no name matching. The is_nranks_dim_ flag
is the single source of truth across all layers.

title: feat(ir): Add window externalization policies
body:
## Summary

- Add dense-access region analysis for orchestration tensor window externalization.

title: refactor(codegen): extract CollectBodyAliases for ForStmt iter-arg analysis
body:
The ForStmt visitor currently does three jobs in one place: walk the body for assigns/nested loops, run the alias fixpoint for iter-args, then emit the carry lowering. That’s why every TaskId array-carry or rebind tweak means wading through ~450 lines of codegen, and you can’t test the analysis without dragging the whole emitter along. AliasingNodeCollector being a nested class inside the visitor was basically admitting the analysis isn’t a real module yet — it’s buried in emission code.

Next up: IterArgCarryAnalyzer (alias fixpoint + rebind/array-size planning), then the broader orch-codegen cleanup (carry emission helpers, OrchestrationCodegen class) — Planning each as small, reviewable PRs.

## Summary

Extract the inline `AliasingNodeCollector` from `OrchestrationStmtCodegen::VisitStmt_(ForStmtPtr)` into `orchestration_analysis` as `BodyAliases` + `CollectBodyAliases()`.

The ForStmt visitor now calls `CollectBodyAliases(for_stmt->body_)` and uses `body_aliases.assigns` / `body_aliases.nested_fors` in the existing alias-equivalence fixpoint.

## Changes

- `orchestration_analysis.h` — add `BodyAliases` struct and `CollectBodyAliases()` declaration
- `orchestration_analysis.cpp` — implement collector (same IR walk as before)
- `orchestration_codegen.cpp` — remove ~15-line nested class; wire through `CollectBodyAliases()`

title: fix(passes): halve tile.reshape shape arg for already-split input in SplitVectorKernel
body:
## Summary

`SplitVectorKernel` (the `pl.split(UP_DOWN)` lowering) halves a vector scope by halving tile **types**. For `tile.reshape` over an **already-split** input, it fell through to the plain result-halving path, which halved the result `TileType` but only patched the explicit shape argument for `tile.full` / `tile.create` — leaving `tile.reshape`'s target-shape literal (`args[1]`) stale.

This made the stale shape (e.g. `[16, 1]`, 64 B) disagree with the halved result type (`[8, 1]`, 32 B). `memory_reuse` then sized the reshape output from the un-split shape and aborted at compile time:

```
sharing-group member offset 0 rebased to rel=0 size=64 falls outside reuse target (size 32)
  at src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp:1328
```

## Fix

In the plain result-halving path, halve `tile.reshape`'s shape argument (`args[1]`) on the split axis alongside the result type, reusing the existing `HalveTupleElement` helper so the type and the shape literal stay consistent.

## Tests

- Added `test_reshape_of_already_split_input_halves_shape_arg` to `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_split_vector_kernel.py`, covering a reshape whose input is already split. Verified it **fails without the fix** (reproduces the bug) and **passes with it**.
- Full `test_split_vector_kernel.py` (31 tests) passes; worktree rebuilt clean.
- Updated the EN/ZH pass docs (`23-split_vector_kernel.md`) to describe the shape-arg halving on the already-split fall-through path.

Fixes #1790

title: feat(distributed): materialize host tensor allreduce builtin
body:
## Summary

This PR completes the host tensor allreduce builtin path for distributed PyPTO.

- Materialize `builtin.tensor.allreduce` as a generated `next_levels/` callable during compile
- Add builtin variant mangling for `builtin.tensor.allreduce__sum__fp32`
- Render builtin allreduce kernel, entry wrapper, and kernel config from package templates
- Dispatch host-level `pld.tensor.allreduce(src, signal, op=pld.ReduceOp.Sum)` through the existing `submit_next_level` / `chip_callables` runtime path
- Keep the user-facing API as `pld.tensor.allreduce`; no new host namespace or runtime helper is introduced
- Use explicit user-provided signal tensors, matching the current host collective design
- Add unit and system coverage for builtin materialization, generated host dispatch, and L3 host tensor allreduce execution

## Motivation

PR1 added the tensor allreduce API, IR plumbing, and host lowering infrastructure. This PR adds the remaining builtin materialization and execution path so host orchestrators can lower `pld.tensor.allreduce` into per-device builtin chip dispatches using the same `next_levels/` mechanism as user chip callables.

The implementation avoids a parallel collective registry or host-side helper. Builtin collectives are compiled, registered, and dispatched through the existing distributed runtime flow.

## Scope

This PR implements the first supported host tensor allreduce variant:

- `op = pld.ReduceOp.Sum`
- `dtype = FP32`

Other reduce ops and dtypes remain reserved for follow-up support.

title: fix(ir): allow pl.split slot_num with SplitMode.NONE
body:
## Summary

`pl.split(pl.SplitMode.NONE, slot_num=N)` was rejected by the DSL front-end even though the lowering already supports it. A `SplitMode.NONE` mixed kernel still drives a cube→vector cross-core pipe (on Ascend910B via dual-AIV dispatch), and `ExpandMixedKernel` already reads the `slot_num` attr and sizes that ring from it regardless of split mode. The restriction lived only in the parser and printer, making the feature unreachable for the NONE case.

This was confusing because `SplitMode.NONE` does **not** mean "non-split kernel" — it is a valid mixed-kernel configuration that still carries a cube→vector pipe.

## Changes

- **Parser** (`ast_parser.py`): drop the "`slot_num` is only valid with a cross-core split mode" rejection.
- **Printer** (`python_printer.cpp`): emit `optimizations=[pl.split(mode, slot_num=N)]` whenever `slot_num` is set — including `SplitMode.NONE` — across the InCore, AutoInCore, and both SPMD scope forms. Adds a small `ScopeHasSplitInfo` helper to share the emission gate. Previously the printer silently dropped `slot_num` for NONE, breaking round-trip.
- **Docstring + pass docs (en/zh)**: correct the false claim that `slot_num` only applies to `UP_DOWN` / `LEFT_RIGHT`.
- **Tests**: flip the old rejection test (`test_split_slot_num_requires_split_mode`) to `test_split_slot_num_allowed_with_none_mode`, and add an SPMD-form NONE round-trip test (`test_for_spmd_split_none_slot_num_roundtrips`).

title: feat(runtime): per-task ring sizing for L3 distributed dispatch
body:
## Summary

Extends per-task ring sizing (`ring_task_window` / `ring_heap` / `ring_dep_pool`) from the L2 single-chip path to the **L3 distributed** path. Previously the `config` argument on the L3 dispatch entry points was discarded (`del config`), so every task on a `DistributedWorker` reused one fixed `CallConfig` and ring sizes could only be set process-wide via `PTO2_RING_*` env vars.

A per-dispatch `RunConfig` now sizes that dispatch's runtime ring buffers, with the same precedence as L2:

```
per-dispatch RunConfig.ring_*  (highest)
  └─ program DistributedConfig baseline (block_dim / aicpu_thread_num)
       └─ runtime PTO2_RING_* env / compile-time default
```

When a `config` is supplied, `_run_compiled` builds a **fresh** `CallConfig` for that dispatch only (from the program's `DistributedConfig` baseline plus the ring overrides), leaving the prepared, shared `call_config` untouched. With no `config` the prepared baseline is reused with zero extra allocation. This lets consecutive dispatches — and, in multi-program serving, different programs (e.g. prefill vs. decode) — each use their own ring sizes.

## Changes

- **Wire the per-dispatch `RunConfig`** through `DistributedWorker.__call__` / `run`, `execute_distributed`, `execute_distributed_compiled`, and `DistributedCompiledProgram.__call__`.
- **DRY**: extract `_apply_ring_overrides()` so L2 (`_build_call_config`) and L3 (`_make_call_config`) transcribe ring sizing identically.
- **Type hints**: `config: Any` → `config: RunConfig | None` across the affected signatures.
- **Docs**: document the L3 per-dispatch path in the EN and zh-CN `05-runtime-ring-sizing.md` (both stay under the 500-line limit).

No C++/binding/stub changes are needed — `RunConfig.ring_*` and `CallConfig.runtime_env` already exist and are reused from the L2 path.

## Usage

```python
from pypto.runtime import RunConfig

with compiled.prepare() as rt:                       # setup once
    prefill = RunConfig(platform="a2a3", ring_task_window=256)
    decode  = RunConfig(platform="a2a3", ring_task_window=64)
    rt(host_x, weight, host_out, config=prefill)     # large window
    rt(host_x, weight, host_out, config=decode)      # smaller window

compiled(a, b, c, config=RunConfig(platform="a2a3", ring_heap=8 * 1024 * 1024))  # one-shot
```

On the L3 path only the `ring_*` fields of `RunConfig` are consumed; compile-side / DFX fields are ignored (they are set at compile / prepare time).

## Testing

- [x] New `TestPerTaskRingSizing` (3) in `test_distributed_worker.py`: no-config reuses the prepared baseline; a per-dispatch `RunConfig` rebuilds the `CallConfig`; `run()` forwards the same override.
- [x] New `TestMakeCallConfigRing` (3) in `test_run_config.py`: L3 `_make_call_config` leaves ring fields at 0 with no config, transcribes overrides, and preserves the `DistributedConfig` baseline under a partial overlay.
- [x] All ring-sizing tests pass (9) and the full `test_distributed_worker.py` suite passes (56).
- [x] `ruff` clean; pre-commit `pyright` / `markdownlint` pass.

## Related Issues

N/A

title: feat(pass): share one L1 load across opposite-b_trans matmuls via tile.transpose_view (#1776)
body:
## Summary

A single Mat tensor consumed by both a `b_trans=True` and a `b_trans=False` `pl.matmul` now loads to L1 **once**; the transposed use is realized as a zero-copy `tile.transpose_view` (NZ↔ZN) view aliasing the same buffer, instead of two byte-identical GM→L1 loads.

- **New `tile.transpose_view` op**: swaps trailing dims and maps the block/scatter layout to its transpose dual (NZ↔ZN, NN↔ZZ, ND↔DN). It inherits the input `MemRef` so `InitMemRef`/`AllocateMemoryAddr` place the view at the source address; codegen emits no data movement (the two same-address `alloc_tile` declarations are the whole mechanism).
- **ConvertTensorToTileOps**: the consumer-driven load is always natural; the matmul-operand bridge wraps a 2D `b_trans`/`a_trans` operand in `tile.transpose_view`. `batch_matmul` (ND) keeps the legacy transpose-at-load path.

## Testing

- `tile.transpose_view` layout-duality unit tests (all 6 layouts)
- Shared-KV conversion test (one load + one view)
- Real-NPU shared-KV numerics st test (non-square kv, b_trans=True + b_trans=False sharing one sliced buffer)

title: fix(passes): track split axis through transpose/reshape in SplitVectorKernel
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1790. `SplitVectorKernel` (`pl.split` UP_DOWN / LEFT_RIGHT) assumed a single global split axis (dim0 for UP_DOWN) in every rewrite branch. When a vector scope transposes/reshapes the split (token) axis into the free axis — RMS `row_sum -> [1,N]` row vector, `tile.transpose`, sinkhorn row-major reshapes — the pass halved the wrong axis, producing numel-inconsistent tiles (an already-split `[8,1]` reshaped to a `[1,16]` claiming 16 elems) and a mis-halved transpose (`[8,8] -> [4,16]`). Those oversized views then aborted `memory_reuse`:

```
sharing-group member offset 0 size=64 falls outside reuse target (size 32)
  at src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp:1461
```

The DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre` fused cube+vec kernel hits exactly this. #1796 patched only the already-split plain result-halving reshape path and did not cover the migrating reshapes this kernel actually hits, so #1790 stayed open.

## Fix

Resolve a **per-tile split axis** before rewriting:

- A fixpoint analysis (`SplitAxisAnalysis`) seeds `tile.load` / `tpop_from_aic` at the default axis and propagates it across `transpose` (swap), `reshape` (axis map), reduce and elementwise ops.
- Input-less accumulators (`tile.full` / `tile.create` / pipeline `iter_arg`) take their axis from their consumer; `init` / `iter_arg` / `yield` are unified.
- `ProcessStmt` halves each tile on its **resolved** axis instead of the global one, dropping the full-width-reshape + per-lane-slice workaround.
- A numel-consistency `INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN` on split view ops fails fast in this pass instead of deep in `memory_reuse`.

**Safety invariant:** a tile that never crosses a migrating transpose/reshape resolves to the default axis, so existing UP_DOWN / LEFT_RIGHT codegen is byte-identical (verified: `qwen3` scope3 post-pass IR unchanged; the 31 existing UTs unchanged).

## Tests

- New UT `test_reshape_migrates_split_axis_for_full_accumulator` (before/after structural).
- New self-contained ST `test_split_vector_kernel_axis_migration` reproducing the `memory_reuse` abort: crashes on the original pass, compiles on the fixed pass (compile-only on `a2a3sim`).
- Local: `hc_pre` repro compiles (decode + prefill); 32 split UTs pass; new ST passes.

## Validation

On-device numerical validation (real `a2a3`) is deferred to CI.

title: fix(backend): cap safe AIV Vec UB below physical size (pto-isa#170)
body:
## Summary

Lower the **safe** usable AIV Vec unified buffer (UB) below its physical size so the allocator rejects over-budget kernels at compile time, instead of letting them silently corrupt on device (workaround for hw-native-sys/pto-isa#170).

- **Ascend910B (A2/A3):** Vec UB `192KB → 184KB`
- **Ascend950 (A5):** Vec UB `248KB → 240KB`

**Why:** PTO-ISA reserves ~8KB at the top of the Vec UB that silently corrupts (NaN on device) any tile placed there. A kernel whose Vec high-water lands in that top region compiles cleanly today and then produces NaNs at runtime — the physical-size budget never subtracted the reserved region.

**How:** No new check is needed. The `AllocatedMemoryAddr` verifier already raises an error when the Vec high-water exceeds `backend->GetMemSize(Vec)`, which now returns the capped safe size. `soc.cpp` is the single source of truth (every consumer reads it dynamically via `GetMemSize`). Each lowered constant carries a `TODO(pto-isa#170)` to restore the physical size once PTO-ISA stops reserving the top region.

## Testing

- [x] Full unit suite passes (`tests/ut`, 6062 passed / 2 skipped)
- [x] Updated 910B/950 backend memory-size tests (184KB / 240KB)
- [x] New regression test: `AllocatedMemoryAddr` verifier errors when a Vec footprint sits **above the safe cap but below the physical size** (e.g. a 192512-byte tile on 910B), guarding against silently raising the cap back to the physical size

## Note

This is a PyPTO-side mitigation. The root cause is the PTO-ISA reservation (hw-native-sys/pto-isa#170); once that is fixed, revert the two `soc.cpp` constants to their physical sizes (the `TODO`s mark them).

title: feat(ir): global largest-first packing for MemoryReuse buffer reuse
body:
## Summary

Replaces the definition-order greedy in `IdentifyReuseOpportunities` (MemoryReuse pass) with a **global first-fit-decreasing packer**: within each memory space, intervals are placed **largest-first**, and every later interval joins the first existing buffer all of whose members it can share with. A buffer's size is fixed by its first (largest) member, so a later, larger tile can now host an earlier, smaller one — which the prior one-directional size gate (`source.size >= target.size`) could never capture.

### What changed

- **`src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp`** — rewrite `IdentifyReuseOpportunities`:
  - Sort each memory space's intervals largest-first (ties by definition order for determinism), pack into buffers; the representative each member rebases onto is the buffer's largest member.
  - Fold the pairwise reuse constraints into a `can_share` predicate over the **current** constraint model — lifetime overlap, the Ascend910B `load + tpop_from_aic` in-place hazard, and the per-operand `forbid_output_alias` / `not_inplace_safe` no-alias guard. Because the packer no longer runs in program order, every directional gate is checked **both ways**.
  - The representative's `tile.alloc` dominates the whole function (InitMemRef hoists every alloc to the function-body head), so a representative defined after some of its members is safe; `reuse_map` stays flat (member → representative).
  - Drop the now-dead `LifetimeInterval::def_op_name` field.
- **docs** (`docs/{en,zh-cn}/dev/passes/30-memory_reuse.md`) — describe the largest-first packing and drop the explicit byte-size condition.
- **tests** (`tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_memory_reuse.py`):
  - `TestL0CrossShapeReuse` — the smaller, earlier `la` now reuses the larger `lc`'s L0A buffer (bidirectional cross-shape L0 reuse).
  - `TestTopDownRetargeter` not-inplace-safe test — largest-first packing coalesces two 8 KB tiles onto `merged`'s 16 KB buffer (3 Vec allocs instead of 4); the mrgsort hazard guard and the inserted `tile.move` are unchanged.

### Benefit

Bidirectional reuse lowers peak buffer usage where a smaller live range is defined before a larger, lifetime-disjoint one (e.g. cross-shape L0 cube inputs, and the retargeter test's 8 KB → 16 KB coalescing).

## Testing

- [x] Full unit suite: `tests/ut/` — 6123 passed, 2 skipped
- [x] Codegen system tests: `tests/st/codegen/` — 29 passed (incl. qwen3 golden comparisons)
- [x] `clang-format` clean; `check_english_only` clean; `clang-tidy` introduces no new findings on changed lines
- [x] Code review completed
- [x] Documentation updated (en + zh-cn)
