title: Feature: indexed GM-row gather with loop-local / per-iteration indices (paged_gather #1644 is single-shot only)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Summary

We need an indexed GM-row gather (gather scattered rows of a paged KV pool into UB/L1) that can be driven by **loop-local / per-iteration indices** — usable inside an `spmd` or `pl.range` / `CORE_GROUP` loop where each iteration gathers a different set of rows. The recently merged `pl.paged_gather` (#1644) is exactly the right primitive conceptually, but it is **single-shot only**: its `indices` must be a kernel-input (or otherwise tile-lowering-surviving) tensor used in one call with no enclosing runtime loop. That does not fit per-token sparse attention.

## Motivation

In the DeepSeek-V4 unified decode sparse-attention kernel (`models/deepseek/v4/decode_sparse_attn.py`), the compressed-KV gather is ~half the decode wall. Per token it does a paged lookup `phys = block_table[idx // block_size] * block_size + idx % block_size` and gathers the selected rows — byte-for-byte what `paged_gather` does internally. Fusing it (gather straight into L1, feed the QK/PV matmul, drop the ~84 MB `sparse_kv` GM round-trip) is the single biggest remaining decode optimization.

## What we tried (all rejected)

Calling `pl.paged_gather` with a per-(token, block) index, three index forms:

1. a runtime slice `cmp_logical_idx[g_t:g_t+1, off:off+128]` inside an AIV `pl.spmd`
2. the same slice inside `pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP)` + `pl.range`
3. a freshly **materialized** index — `pl.create_tensor([1, 128], INT32)` written from the slice — inside the CORE_GROUP loop

All three fail at lowering with:

```
pypto.InternalError: tensor.paged_gather: indices must be TensorType
Check failed: idx_type at src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp:1482
```

## Root cause

`paged_gather`'s lowering (op_conversion) runs **after** the tile-lowering passes, so any tensor created or sliced inside a runtime loop has already become a tile / `partition_view` by then and is no longer a `TensorType`. Only tensors that survive tile-lowering (kernel inputs, or top-level tensors used whole with no per-iteration indexing) stay `TensorType`. The ST test (`tests/st/runtime/ops/test_paged_gather.py`) passes precisely because it calls `paged_gather` once, outside any loop, on a kernel-input `idx`.

## Request

Either of:

- **(A)** Extend `paged_gather` so `indices` (and `block_table`) may be **loop-local / per-iteration** tensors — e.g. lower the per-row scalar load loop to read the index from a tile / `partition_view`, or run the conversion before tile-lowering / re-materialize the index at the call site.
- **(B)** Add a tile-level `mgather` (GM-row indexed gather into UB/L1) intended for use **inside** `spmd` / `pl.range`, taking a UB index tile.

Either unblocks fusing the gather into per-token attention. (A) preserves the paged semantics; (B) is the lower-level building block.

## Environment

- pypto `main` (e.g. `3c92d01c`), target a2a3 (Ascend 910B/C).

title: fix(passes): reject unsplittable transpose kernels with an actionable error (#1790)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1790. A `pl.split` request is **rejected with a `ValueError`** when the kernel contains a `tile.transpose` that **swaps the split axis** — instead of being silently downgraded to the no-split path.

## Root cause

`tile.transpose` swaps two axes, so the per-lane split data migrates to the *other* dimension while `SplitVectorKernel` still halves the *original* split axis — it cannot type such a transpose correctly, so the result would be mis-shaped and miscompute. This is independent of split mode (UP_DOWN dim 0 / LEFT_RIGHT dim 1) and dtype. (Separately, the pto-isa FP transpose also miscomputes on device for split-shrunk source rows — the original #1790 device symptom — to be filed as a pto-isa defect.)

## Why reject instead of downgrade

The split is a **performance decision the user owns**. Silently stripping it compiles a slower kernel than asked for and hides the regression behind a `LOG_WARN`. And the no-split kernel is one the user can already request directly (`SplitMode.NONE`), so downgrading adds no convenience — it only masks the problem. The pass now fails loud and hands the choice back to the user.

## Fix

`TransposeSplitHazardFinder` runs at the start of `ExpandMixedFunction` and flags the first `tile.transpose` whose source is **non-singleton on the split axis** (a singleton-on-split-axis source carries no split data — the no-op broadcast case — and is left split; a dynamic, non-`ConstInt` extent is treated as non-singleton and flagged conservatively). On a hit it raises a `ValueError` (`CHECK_SPAN`, with IR source location) pointing at the offending transpose, with two fix directions:

1. **Drop the split** — `attrs={"split": pl.SplitMode.NONE}` (or remove the `pl.split(...)` optimization).
2. **Eliminate the transpose** — e.g. replace a transpose-then-row-index with a direct column slice such as `pre[:, h:h+1]`. This keeps the split (so the kernel still gets the requested speedup) and also avoids the pto-isa FP transpose tail-path miscompute.

## Verification

- C++ builds clean in-worktree.
- Regression tests in `test_expand_mixed_kernel_a2a3.py`: the three hazard cases (UP_DOWN / LEFT_RIGHT / int8) assert the `ValueError` is raised and that the message surfaces both fix directions; the singleton-split-axis case still compiles with the split preserved.
- EN/ZH pass docs updated.

## Note

The underlying `[8,8]` FP32 `TTRANS` tail-path miscompute is a pto-isa defect (to be filed separately); once fixed, such transposes could be split rather than requiring the user to remove them.

title: feat(ir): pl.create_l1 + pl.gather_row — kernel-driven paged gather into L1
body:
## Summary

Adds two tensor-level ops — the flexible, **kernel-driven** counterpart to `tensor.paged_gather` — that let a kernel build an on-chip (L1/`Mem.Mat`) matmul B-operand row by row while computing each physical source row itself (block-table lookups, multi-source selection, invalid-row clamping):

| Op | Lowers to (`ConvertTensorToTileOps`) | Role |
| -- | ------------------------------------ | ---- |
| `pl.create_l1(shape, dtype, transpose=…)` | `tile.create(target_memory=Mat, transpose=…)` | seed the loop-carried L1 accumulator |
| `pl.gather_row(acc, src, dst_off, src_off, shapes, transpose=…)` | `tile.gather_row` (DPS) | DMA one caller-addressed GM row into `acc` (per-row `GM→L1` tload, no `tmov`) |

Both deduce a `TensorType`, so the gathered result composes with tensor-level `pl.matmul` / softmax; both are registered self-loading so `src` stays in GM.

### Transpose (ZN) for a `b_trans` matmul operand

`transpose=True` makes the gathered tile a transposed B-operand with no GM round-trip:

- `tile.create` gains a `transpose` attr → allocates the transposed Mat (ZN) fractal (`blayout=row_major`, `slayout=col_major`).
- `tile.gather_row` codegen presents `src` as a **DN-strided** `make_tensor_view` so `pto.tload` runs `DN→NZ` — the actual transpose. A straight `ND→NZ` tload scrambles the fractal layout (wrong results / AICore 507018 at scale). `paged_gather(is_trans=True)` shares this path.
- The `transpose` kwarg was missing from the `tile.create` **DSL** layer; without it the printed IR (`transpose=…`) failed to re-parse, breaking the print→parse roundtrip verifier. Now wired through both DSL layers with a `None` default, so existing `tile.create` output is unchanged.

## Testing

- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_gather_row.py` — convert-only lowering, ZN transpose layout, type validation (dtype mismatch / non-positive shape), full-pipeline survival (parametrized over `transpose`).
- [x] `tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen_gather_row.py` — asserts the transpose path emits the `#pto.layout<dn>` source view, and the non-transpose path does not.
- [x] No regressions across operators / parser / language / printing / convert / paged-attn suites (~1900 tests).
- [x] Docs updated in `docs/en` + `docs/zh-cn` (`12-convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.md`).

title: feat(ir): pl.submit allow_early_resolve hint for speculative early-dispatch
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in **frontend interface** for the runtime's per-task speculative early-dispatch hint ([simpler#1065](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1065)) — the issue explicitly lists codegen-side emission of `set_allow_early_resolve()` as "future work", which this implements.

Marking a task launch:

```python
out, tid = pl.submit(self.kernel, x, scratch, allow_early_resolve=True)
out, tid = pl.spmd_submit(self.kernel, x, y, core_num=8, allow_early_resolve=True)
```

opts that task in as a producer whose consumers the scheduler may **pre-stage** onto idle cores before it completes (released by a doorbell the instant it finishes). It lowers to `Arg::set_allow_early_resolve(true)` on the producer task's `Arg`. Pure scheduling optimisation — no effect on results; pays off on critical paths built from many short tasks.

## Design

`allow_early_resolve` is a **first-class `Submit` field** (sibling to `sync_start_`), but **independent of the SPMD launch spec** so it works on a plain `pl.submit` too. It's user-authored launch intent (not compiler metadata), so it does not live in `attrs_`.

## Cross-layer changes

| Layer | Change |
|---|---|
| IR (`expr.h`) | New `Submit.allow_early_resolve_` field + ctor param + reflection descriptor; `SubmitToCallView` surfaces it as the `allow_early_resolve` Call-view attr |
| Bindings / stub | nanobind ctor arg + auto-exposed read prop; `ir.pyi` field + overload |
| Parser | Accept the bool kwarg on `pl.submit` / `pl.spmd_submit`; reject non-bool literals and use on plain fire-and-forget calls |
| Printer | Round-trips `allow_early_resolve=True` (independent of `core_num`) |
| Passes + serialization | Thread the field through every Submit-rebuilding pass (mutator, derive-call-directions, SSA, phase-fence, materialize-strides, tensor→tile, auto-derive-deps, optimize-orch-tensors, flatten-call-expr) and the deserializer — same handling as `sync_start`, so the flag survives the pipeline to codegen |
| Codegen | `EmitEarlyResolveHint` emits `set_allow_early_resolve(true)` on the producer `Arg` before its `rt_submit_*` at all three submit sites |
| Docs | `scope.py` docstrings, `python_syntax` (en + zh), IR hierarchy |

## Testing

- New `test_submit_allow_early_resolve.py`: parser / IR / printer / structural-equal coverage (both submit forms, default-false, explicit-false, non-bool rejection, plain-call rejection, print round-trip).
- New orchestration codegen golden tests: positive emission + opt-in negative (no flag ⇒ no emission).
- [x] All new tests pass (12); broad regression green (submit / serialization / codegen + all 9 threaded passes, ~772 tests).
- [x] Build clean; pre-commit (clang-format / cpplint / ruff / pyright) clean.

title: [Bug] codegen: manual_scope TaskId can't be loop-carried into Array[TASK_ID]
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

A `TaskId` captured inside `pl.manual_scope()` cannot be loop-carried into a `pl.array(pl.TASK_ID)` across a `pl.range` loop. Orchestration codegen fails with an `INTERNAL_CHECK`:

```
Internal error: scalar yield to array carry must resolve to a TaskId variable registered in manual_task_id_map_
Check failed: tid_binding != nullptr at src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:1389
```

**Root cause.** When a `pl.range` loop carries an `Array[TASK_ID]` whose slots are filled per-iteration by a `pl.parallel` block (the "scalar yield to array carry" path), codegen resolves each yielded tid through `manual_task_id_map_`. A tid produced **inside `pl.manual_scope()`** is not registered there, so the lookup fails. The identical kernel compiles cleanly when the producer runs in the ordinary auto-dep region (no `manual_scope`) — see the contrast below, where the *only* difference is the `with pl.manual_scope():` wrapper.

This looks like the same family as the (closed) #1577 "TaskId array element scalar deps are not registered in auto-scope codegen", but the complementary direction: #1577 was the **read** path (`array.get_element(Array[TASK_ID]) -> Scalar[TASK_ID]` used in `deps=`); this is the **write / loop-carry** path (a `manual_scope` tid yielded into a carried `Array[TASK_ID]`), and it still fails on latest `main` (`3ec5e838`).

**Secondary issue:** `compile_for_test()` *prints* the error but does not raise — the failure only becomes fatal (`PartialCodegenError`) in the device/codegen path. Ideally the frontend would reject this earlier with a clear user-facing diagnostic instead of an `INTERNAL_CHECK`.

**Real-world impact:** in the qwen3-14b decode (`models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py`), `dcr_xgamma`'s `DOWN_ON` sliced writers of `out` / `normed_out` WAW-serialize on one core when emitted in the auto-dep region (the `OutWindowExternalizer` Pattern-5 that should keep them parallel bails because the task writes two outputs). Moving the writer **into** `manual_scope` removes the WAW (parallel writers), but is blocked by this codegen limitation because the per-layer dcr tids are loop-carried (`prev_out_tids` / `prev_normed_tids`). We had to fall back to a single `pl.spmd` dispatch instead.

### Steps to Reproduce

Compile-only, no device needed:

```python
import sys
import pypto.language as pl
import torch
from pypto.backend import BackendType, set_backend_type

N, LOOP, ROWS, COLS = 4, 2, 16, 256
TILE = COLS // N

@pl.jit.inline
def layer(
    x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
    y: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
    prev_tids: pl.Array[N, pl.TASK_ID],
    out_tids: pl.Array[N, pl.TASK_ID],
) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]:
    # consumer of the PREVIOUS iteration's carry -> makes `carry` truly loop-carried
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="consumer",
               deps=[prev_tids[i] for i in range(N)]):
        y[0:ROWS, 0:COLS] = pl.add(y[0:ROWS, 0:COLS], 1.0)
    # produce N tids INSIDE manual_scope and yield them into the carried array
    with pl.manual_scope():                       # <-- remove this wrapper -> compiles fine
        for n in pl.parallel(N):
            with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="prod",
                       deps=[prev_tids[n]]) as prod_tid:
                c0 = n * TILE
                y[0:ROWS, c0:c0 + TILE] = pl.add(y[0:ROWS, c0:c0 + TILE], 1.0)
            out_tids[n] = prod_tid                # <-- scalar yield to array carry
    return y

@pl.jit
def repro(x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32], y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]]):
    carry = pl.array.create(N, pl.TASK_ID)
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="seed") as seed_tid:
        y[0:ROWS, 0:COLS] = pl.add(x[0:ROWS, 0:COLS], 0.0)
    for s in pl.unroll(N):
        carry[s] = seed_tid
    for _i in pl.range(LOOP):                     # LOOP > 1 forces cross-iteration carry
        y = layer(x, y, carry, carry)
    return y

if __name__ == "__main__":
    set_backend_type(BackendType.Ascend910B)
    repro.compile_for_test(torch.randn([ROWS, COLS]), torch.empty([ROWS, COLS]))
```

**Contrast (compiles clean):** delete the `with pl.manual_scope():` line and de-indent the `for n in pl.parallel(N):` block by one level (producer in the auto-dep region). The kernel is otherwise identical and compiles without error — isolating `pl.manual_scope()` as the trigger.

### Expected Behavior

Either:
1. codegen supports loop-carrying a `manual_scope`-produced `TaskId` into an `Array[TASK_ID]` (register such tids in `manual_task_id_map_` / honor C++ lexical scope lifetime, in line with the #1577 fix discussion), or
2. the frontend rejects this pattern with a clear, user-facing error — not an `INTERNAL_CHECK` (`Internal error: ...`).

### Actual Behavior

Orchestration codegen aborts:

```
Failed to generate orchestration 'repro': Internal error: scalar yield to array carry
must resolve to a TaskId variable registered in manual_task_id_map_
Check failed: tid_binding != nullptr at src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:1389
```

(Via `compile_for_test` the error is printed but not raised; via the normal device/codegen path it surfaces as a fatal `PartialCodegenError`.)

### Git Commit ID

3ec5e838 (pypto, main)

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1577 (closed — complementary "read" direction of the same `manual_task_id_map_` registration gap).

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `3ec5e838` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `2668be5a` |
| pypto-lib | `556f615` |
| pto-isa | `b9122ec` |
| ptoas | `v0.45` |
| CANN | not detected |

title: feat(op): add tile.mgather (GM-row indexed gather-load into VEC tile) [#1807]
body:
## Summary

Adds `tile.mgather` (`pto.mgather`) — indexed gather-load from a GM table into a fresh VEC tile, usable with a loop-local index inside `spmd` / `pl.range` (route B for #1807). Two modes via `coalesce`:

- **row** (default): `dst[r, j] = mem[idx[r], j]`, `idx` a `[1, R]` index vector, output `[R, mem_cols]`.
- **elem**: `dst[i, j] = mem[idx[i, j]]`, output = `idx` shape.

Implemented across all layers: C++ op (`src/ir/op/tile_ops/memory.cpp`), IR wrapper, DSL (`pl.tile.mgather` / `pl.mgather`), codegen (`MakeTileMgatherCodegenPTO`), UT, and en/zh docs.

## Key fix — row-mode 507018 hang (`not_inplace_safe`)

`tile.mgather` initially defaulted to in-place-safe, so `MemoryReuse` could place the output tile at the **same UB address as the index tile** (both at offset 0). Row-mode gather reads the whole `idx` vector across its per-row DMA loop while writing `dst`, so an aliased `dst` corrupts indices mid-loop → garbage GM addresses → intermittent AICPU **507018** hangs that worsen with gathered row count (16 rows clean, 32 rows ~always hung).

Fix: mark the op `.not_inplace_safe()` (mirroring `tile.gather` / `tile.scatter`) so `dst` gets its own buffer. Verified on a2a3 (pto-isa e722679b + PTOAS 0.47): the case that deterministically hung (32×32) now passes 5/5 with zero hangs across repeated runs; index/dst tiles allocate at disjoint UB offsets.

## Also included

- Derive the output tile's `valid_shape` from the index tile's effective valid (`DeduceTileMgatherType`), with UTs.
- Row regression ST cases (`16×64`, `32×32`) that reproduced the hang before the fix.
- Doc note: PTOAS requires the index tile row byte size to be 32-byte aligned (`none_box` constraint) — INT32 index width a multiple of 8; pad + `valid_shapes` for other counts.

## a2a3 ST is skipped pending a toolchain bump

`TestMgatherRow` / `TestMgatherElem` are `@pytest.mark.skip`. a2a3 `tile.mgather` needs a toolchain newer than CI currently pins (ptoas v0.45, pto-isa 016396b5 via runtime 09f1546f):

- **PTOAS 0.47** for the row-mode `MTE2→S` index sync (PTOAS#861) — not yet officially released.
- a **pto-isa with the templated `MGATHER<Coalesce>`** (e722679b) and its **matching runtime** (SDMA layout). These move in lockstep via `runtime/pto_isa.pin`; overriding the pto-isa alone regresses the distributed SDMA path, so it can't be done piecemeal.

The op and the in-place fix are verified locally on that toolchain (row + elem pass). Un-skip once CI's ptoas / pto-isa / runtime are bumped together.

Refs #1807.

title: refactor(codegen): extract IterArgCarryAnalyzer from ForStmt visitor
body:
Extracts iter-arg carry analysis from the monolithic `OrchestrationStmtCodegen::VisitStmt_(ForStmtPtr)` (~400 lines) into a standalone `IterArgCarryAnalyzer` class.

## Summary

Decomposes `OrchestrationStmtCodegen::VisitStmt_(ForStmtPtr)` — the most complex method in PyPTO codegen — by extracting the iter-arg carry **analysis** into a standalone `IterArgCarryAnalyzer` class. The visitor shrinks from a monolith mixing three concerns (alias fixpoint, rebind classification, array-carry sizing) to a pipeline that consumes pre-computed `IterArgCarryPlan` structs.

| Concern | Before | After |
|---------|--------|-------|
| Alias-equivalence fixpoint | ~140 lines inline | `ComputeAliasClasses()` in analyzer |
| Rebind detection | Inline in visitor | `Analyze()` -> `IterArgCarryPlan::is_rebind` |
| Array-carry sizing | Inline in visitor | `Analyze()` -> `IterArgCarryPlan::array_size` |
| Dynamic compiler-dep collection | Inline in visitor | `IterArgCarryPlan::dynamic_compiler_dep_collection` |
| Emission (unchanged) | ~200 lines | Same code, now purely mechanical from plans |

### Files

| File | Change | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| `iter_arg_carry_analyzer.h` | **new** (82 lines) | `IterArgCarryPlan` struct (4 fields) + `IterArgCarryAnalyzer` class with full design doc |
| `iter_arg_carry_analyzer.cpp` | **new** (298 lines) | `Analyze()`, `ComputeAliasClasses()`, `ResolveArrayCarrySize()` — with restored design comments |
| `orchestration_analysis.h` | +25 lines | `EvalConstInt`, `EvalConstTripCount`, `UnwrapAutoScope` exposed as shared helpers with full doc comments |
| `orchestration_analysis.cpp` | +35 lines | Shared helper implementations; `UnwrapAutoScope` handles `kAttrCompilerAutoManualScopeCandidate` |
| `orchestration_codegen.cpp` | +220 / −402 lines | ForStmt visitor shrinks; calls analyzer; uses `carry_plans` throughout |
| `CMakeLists.txt` | +1 line | Add new `.cpp` to codegen library |
| `test_orchestration_task_deps.py` | +65 lines | Regression test for compiler-dep carry outer-loop sizing |

### More details

- **Nearly pure extraction** of the alias fixpoint and carry-sizing logic from the ForStmt visitor, with design documentation preserved.
- `EvalConstInt` / `EvalConstTripCount` are now shared helpers in `orchestration_analysis.h` (deduplicated from anonymous-namespace copies).
- `UnwrapAutoScope` now co-located with `CollectBodyAliases` in `orchestration_analysis` — updated to handle `kAttrCompilerAutoManualScopeCandidate`-tagged scopes (upstream change) so the analyzer and IfStmt handler share one implementation.
- `compiler_dep_collection` logic from #1759 preserved via post-analysis pass in codegen. The post-process calls `EvalConstTripCount` **unconditionally** for compiler-dep carries — `ResolveArrayCarrySize` cannot override the outer loop's trip count with an inner loop's (YunjiQin review).
- `dynamic_compiler_dep_collection` integrated into `IterArgCarryPlan` — Parallel ForStmt compiler-dep carries without a const trip count use a dynamic `std::vector<PTO2TaskId>` instead of a fixed stack array. `compiler_dep_collection` is gated on `array_size > 0`, matching the old pre-refactor logic.
- `IsOp(call, "tensor.assemble")` used instead of bare `call->op_->name_ ==` for operator identity check (Copilot review).

### Noted for reviewer

1. **`ComputeAliasClasses()`** is a verbatim move of the ~140-line fixpoint loop from `VisitStmt_(ForStmtPtr)` with one safety improvement: a bounds guard on `return_vars_[k]` dereference. The four alias rules (TupleGetItemExpr, tensor.assemble, output_existing/inout calls, nested ForStmt return-var propagation) are unchanged. Full design comments restored in the new location.

2. **`ResolveArrayCarrySize()`** is the recursive Parallel/Sequential array-threading logic, moved verbatim from the codegen class.

3. **Compiler-dep post-processing** is the only logic that is not a pure move. It applies `NeedsCompilerDepTaskId` (which lives on the codegen class) to the analyzer's plans. The sizing uses the shared `EvalConstTripCount` unconditionally — no fallback that would let `ResolveArrayCarrySize` override the outer loop's trip count. `compiler_dep_collection` is gated on `array_size > 0`, matching the old code. The `is_rebind` field is left as set by `Analyze()` (inside the yield guard), matching the old code's behavior.

4. **`UnwrapAutoScope`** was an anonymous-namespace function in the codegen file. It is now a named function in `orchestration_analysis` so both the analyzer and the IfStmt handler can call it. Updated to handle `kAttrCompilerAutoManualScopeCandidate` (upstream change from #1932).

title: fix(codegen): loop-carry manual_scope TaskId into Array[TASK_ID]
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1811.

Orchestration codegen restored `array_carry_vars_` wholesale on every `PTO2_SCOPE(MANUAL)` exit. A `pl.parallel` array carry registered **inside** a `manual_scope` reuses the **enclosing** `pl.range` loop's backing array, but the wholesale restore wiped that registration. The enclosing loop's `YieldStmt` — emitted *after* the manual-scope block — then could not resolve the carry and tripped an `INTERNAL_CHECK`:

```
Internal error: scalar yield to array carry must resolve to a TaskId variable
registered in manual_task_id_map_
```

The identical kernel without the `with pl.manual_scope():` wrapper compiles cleanly — the loop-body AUTO scope restores *after* the yield, not before it.

## Fix

The wholesale restore is correct only for scope-local C++ identifiers (a `PTO2TaskId` local declared inside the block dies at the closing brace — issue #1577). An array carry whose backing array was declared in the enclosing scope survives the brace and is legitimately referenced after it.

On `MANUAL`-scope exit, codegen now preserves array carries whose backing storage is **enclosing-scope-valid** (named by an identifier not in the scope's local set) and reverts only the scope-local ones. The matching per-slot dep names in `manual_task_id_map_` are kept in sync. The pass remains O(N) over the carry map.

## Testing

- [x] New regression test `test_manual_scope_tid_loop_carried_into_array_carry` (confirmed it crashes without the fix and emits correct single-backing-array threading with it)
- [x] `tests/ut/codegen/` — 466 passed
- [x] Full UT suite — 6181 passed, 2 skipped
- [x] Code review completed
- [x] Documentation updated (EN + zh-CN orchestration codegen docs)

## Related Issues

Fixes #1811. Complementary to #1577 (the read-path direction of the same `manual_task_id_map_` registration gap).

title: feat(ir): M/N output tiling in AutoTileMatmulL0
body:
## Summary

`AutoTileMatmulL0` lowered an oversized `tile.matmul` to a pipelined K-loop but only handled **K-tiling**. When `ChooseL0Tile` returned `m < M` or `n < N` (the `[M, N]` output Acc exceeds L0c) it emitted `PH-AT-006` and left the matmul untouched — so the full `[M, N]` accumulator overflowed L0c at `AllocateMemoryAddr`.

This PR implements **M/N output tiling**. The operands are already Mat-resident, so only the output overflows. For a plain `tile.matmul` whose result is consumed by exactly one 2D `tile.store(c, base, out)`, the pass now tiles the output:

- unrolls into a `ceil(M/m) × ceil(N/n)` grid of `[m, n]` sub-tiles (partial on the boundary via **static** extents — `m`/`n` need not divide `M`/`N`),
- computes each with the existing pipelined K-loop,
- stores each `[m, n]` Acc sub-tile straight to `out[mi:, ni:]` (the direct-store / DDR-output path),
- chains the output tensor through the per-sub-tile stores in SSA form.

Every Acc tile is then ≤ L0c, so the matmul lowers through `AllocateMemoryAddr` with no overflow.

## Why

A cross-core matmul scheduler emits per-tile `[w, h]` output regions whose per-tile InCore kernels must fit L0c for any tile size. We deliberately do not bound that scheduler by L0c (it would distort the L1 + cross-core region balance), so on-core M/N tiling here is the mechanism that lets oversized output tiles lower.

## Design notes

- **Unrolled static sub-tiles, not a runtime loop.** `ChooseL0Tile` optimizes L1↔L0 traffic and picks `m`/`n` that rarely divide `M`/`N` (e.g. 256×256 → `m=192, n=160`), so partial boundary tiles are the norm. Unrolling with static partial extents handles boundaries cleanly — no `valid_shape` masking, no runtime `min()` — and is trivially correct.
- The K-loop builder is parameterized by sub-tile offset `(mi, ni)` + extent `(m, n)`; the **K-only path (`mi = ni = 0`, `m = M`, `n = N`) emits byte-identical IR** (existing structural tests unchanged).
- A per-`SeqStmts` use-count + store-consumer index is built lazily so M/N folding stays **O(N)**.

## Deferred (still `PH-AT-006`, left untouched)

`tile.matmul_acc` (needs per-sub-tile slicing of the caller's `[M, N]` accumulator), a Vec left operand (PV path), a single K block (`K/k < 2`), and non-store consumers (need the Mat-scratch / `tile.assemble` path for on-chip downstream ops).

## Testing

- **End-to-end acceptance** — 256×256 FP32 on Ascend910B (output 256 KB > 128 KB L0c) compiles through the full pipeline (passes `AllocateMemoryAddr` with no L0c overflow) and matches `torch.matmul` (`rtol=atol=1e-3`).
- Pass-level numeric checks via `torch_codegen` for clean (512×512) and **partial-boundary** (384×384) tiles.
- Structural before/after for the 2×2 grid; deferred-case and idempotency coverage.
- Full suite green (`tests/ut/ir/transforms`, `tests/ut/jit`, `tests/ut/debug`: 2025 passed).

A `tile.extract` handler was added to `debug.torch_codegen` (a 2D slice) so tiled matmuls — K-only and M/N — can be numerically validated; the op was previously never exercised through `torch_codegen`.

Docs updated (`docs/en` + `docs/zh-cn`).

## Note: separate prerequisite commit

`fix(backend): import Traversable from importlib.resources.abc on Python 3.11+` — `importlib.abc.Traversable` was deprecated in 3.12 and removed in 3.14, breaking all pypto imports on a 3.14 interpreter. Required for the test suite to run; kept as its own focused commit.

title: feat(profiling): auto-provision msopprof + bundle raw sim trace
body:
## Summary

Two cohesive robustness improvements to the in-core profiling workflow.

**1. Auto-provision the `msopprof` worker (`incore-profiling` skill)**

`msprof op simulator` is only a launcher — it execs
`$ASCEND_TOOLKIT_HOME/tools/msopprof/bin/msopprof`. Some CANN 9.0 toolkit drops
ship the launcher but omit that worker binary, so every collect died deep in the
run with `Cannot find msopprof`. `incore_profile.py` now:

- Probes `msprof op simulator --help` up front (classifying on output, since
  msprof returns rc 0 even on its error lines).
- When the worker is missing, provisions one by **copying** (not symlinking —
  msprof rejects symlinks) a `msopprof` from another local CANN install into the
  expected path, handling both the 9.x (`tools/msopprof/bin`) and 8.x
  (`tools/msopt/bin`) layouts, then re-probes.
- Also provisions the worker's companion injection lib: `msprof op simulator`
  `LD_PRELOAD`s `<toolkit>/tools/msopprof/lib64/libmsopprof_injection.so`, so a
  drop shipping neither worker nor lib (e.g. CANN 9.0.0) otherwise dies in the
  app's `aclInit` with error 500000 "init soc version failed" (the missing
  preload is silently ignored). The lib is copied from the source worker's
  sibling `lib64` to the exact `LD_PRELOAD` path, idempotently.
- Fails early with precise remediation (naming the expected path) when no worker
  exists or `--no-auto-msopprof` is set.
- New flags: `--msopprof <path>` and `--auto-msopprof/--no-auto-msopprof`.
- A cross-version fallback is warned; a bad collect is still flagged
  `collect_failed`, never silently accepted. Filesystem probes are hardened
  against `PermissionError`.

**2. Bundle the raw binary trace with the cleaned trace (`clean_sim_trace`)**

`clean_sim_trace` writes `trace.clean.json` + `instr_metrics.json` but left the
raw `visualize_data.bin` behind, so deliverable folders weren't self-contained.
New `--copy-raw/--no-copy-raw` (default on): with `-o <target>`, the raw binary
trace (`visualize_data.bin` + per-core data) is copied into
`<target>/raw_simulator/`; the source `OPPROF_*` dir is left intact (copy, not
move). No-op when writing next to the input.

## Testing

- `tests/ut/tools/test_clean_sim_trace.py`: 3 new tests (copy-into-target with
  source-intact assertions, `--no-copy-raw` skip, no-`-o` no-op) — 26/26 pass.
- `clean_sim_trace` validated end-to-end against a real `OPPROF_*/simulator/`
  dump; the worker preflight/provision logic validated against a live CANN 9.0
  install (detect-missing → provision from 8.5.1 → re-probe usable → idempotent).
- Injection-lib provisioning validated for the 8.x→9.0 cross-layout case: the
  lib lands byte-identical at `tools/msopprof/lib64/libmsopprof_injection.so`
  (the `LD_PRELOAD` path), and with it present the op-simulator runs the kernel
  to completion where it previously failed in `aclInit`.
- Pre-commit hooks (ruff, pyright, headers, markdownlint) pass.

## Notes

- Tooling-only change — no C++/bindings/IR, no `.pyi`.
- Docs updated in both `docs/en/dev/` and `docs/zh-cn/dev/04-simulator-trace-cleaning.md`.

title: refactor(language): retire deprecated InCore-scope DSL APIs
body:
## Summary

Retire the deprecated ways to declare InCore/AutoInCore scopes in favor of the unified `pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP[, optimizations=[...]])` form:

- **`pl.chunked_loop_optimizer`** sentinel + the legacy `pl.at(optimization=, split=)` keyword arguments.
- **`pl.incore()` / `pl.auto_incore()`** scope context managers.

## Changes

- **Parser** (`ast_parser.py`): drops the legacy kwarg/scope handling; removed kwargs/scopes now fall through to the generic "unknown keyword argument / unsupported context manager" error.
- **DSL** (`dsl_api.py`, `language/__init__.py`): removes the sentinel and the `IncoreContext`/`AutoIncoreContext` context-manager classes plus their exports.
- **Printer** (`python_printer.cpp`): always emits the `optimizations=[...]` form. Previously it still emitted the deprecated `optimization=`/`split=` forms when `slot_num` was unset, so removing parser support without this would have broken print→parse round-trips.
- **JIT specializer** (`specializer.py`): emits entry functions as `Orchestration` directly and drops the now-dead `pl.incore` scope detector; `OutlineIncoreScopes` still outlines `pl.at(CORE_GROUP)` scopes into per-core kernels (verified against the existing `pl.at`-based JIT tests).

All call-sites across tests, examples, and docs (en + zh-cn) are migrated; deprecation and backward-compat tests for the removed forms are deleted.

## Migration

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `pl.at(..., optimization=pl.chunked_loop_optimizer)` | `pl.at(..., optimizations=[pl.auto_chunk])` |
| `pl.at(..., optimization=pl.chunked_loop_optimizer(split=pl.SplitMode.X))` | `pl.at(..., optimizations=[pl.auto_chunk, pl.split(pl.SplitMode.X)])` |
| `pl.at(..., split=pl.SplitMode.X)` | `pl.at(..., optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.X)])` |
| `with pl.incore():` | `with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP):` |
| `with pl.incore(split=pl.SplitMode.X):` | `with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.X)]):` |
| `with pl.auto_incore():` | `with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, optimizations=[pl.auto_chunk]):` |

## Testing

- [x] Full `tests/ut/jit/` suite + parser / transform / codegen UT (specializer classification verified)
- [x] Cross-core codegen golden tests
- [x] Runtime ST tests on a2a3 device (cross-core split + slot_num, dump-tag, qwen3 scope3-mixed)
- [x] All 13 migrated examples compile
- [x] clang-tidy / ruff / pyright clean (pre-commit)

title: [RFC] Explicit AIV split: pl.split_aiv + aiv_shard/aic_gather replacing SplitVectorKernel auto-analysis
body:
### Summary

Introduce an **explicit, user-driven AIV-split DSL** for mixed cube+vector (AIC/AIV) kernels, replacing the compiler-inferred splitting in the `SplitVectorKernel` pass. The surface is three constructs: a `for aiv_id in pl.split_aiv(2):` SPMD loop that binds the sub-core index, and two boundary ops that mark every full↔half transition across the cube↔vector boundary — `pl.aiv_shard(tile, mode)` (full→half, AIC→AIV) and `pl.aic_gather(tile, mode)` (half→full, AIV→AIC). The split **mode** (`UP_DOWN`/`LEFT_RIGHT`) is declared on the transfer ops in 2D-tile vocabulary and **validated**, not inferred. This deletes the brittle index-space analysis that currently miscompiles split-axis sub-slice stores, and lands on existing, already-correct codegen (`tpop_from_aic` halves, `tpop_from_aiv` keeps full) so codegen/PTOAS need no changes.

Related: #1034 (split-axis reduction / GM-mediated semantics), #1447 (SplitVectorKernel odd-`N` validation), #1789 (cross-core split dual-AIV deadlock).

### Motivation

**The concrete blocker.** A distilled flash-attention inner step (`qk_pv`: QK^T → online-softmax → PV) at `M_TILE=64, HEAD_DIM=512, K_TILE=128` hits a progression of compiler blockers:

1. **L0C (Acc) overflow** — two co-resident FP32 matmul accumulators, QK `[64,128]` (32 KB) + PV `[64,512]` (128 KB) = 160 KB > 128 KB. *Fixed* by #1805 (global largest-first packing now reuses the dead QK slot).
2. **Vec overflow** — the `[64,128]` softmax intermediates hit 197632 B > 188416 B. *Worked around* by adding `optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)]`, which halves the row axis across the two AIV sub-cores.
3. **[CURRENT] ptoas codegen failure** — with the `UP_DOWN` split active, the strided `H_TILE`-row stores (`mi[r0:r0+16] = qk_mi[r0:r0+16]`) produce:
   ```
   'pto.tstore' op expects dst static element count (8) to match src valid_shape static element count (16)
   ```

**Root cause.** `SplitVectorKernel` is a *syntactic, per-statement shape-halver with no model of the index space*. It halves a `tile.slice`'s **result type** (`[16,1]`→`[8,1]`) but leaves its **shape/offset args** (`[16,1]`), manufacturing the mismatched `tstore(subview<16>, partition<8>)`. The failing pattern (strided sub-slice stores along the split axis) is **structural to online-softmax**, so the failure is endemic under buffer pressure, not incidental. The pass is a per-op whitelist (`load/store/full/create/reshape` get arg rewrites; `tile.slice` and everything else fall through to result-type-only halving), which is fragile and unbounded as new ops appear.

**Why explicit beats fixing the auto-pass.** When the user authors the partition, the slice shapes and result types are self-consistent by construction, so the entire mismatch class disappears. The compiler stops doing index-space inference and instead just *validates declared intent* and *stamps the per-transfer `split`*. Kernel authors already write explicit tile offsets, `get_subblock_idx`, and cross-core handoffs — this is idiomatic, not new burden.

### Design

#### API (three constructs)

```python
def split_aiv(n: int = 2) -> SplitAivIterator: ...
    # for aiv_id in pl.split_aiv(2):  -> body runs once per AIV sub-core.
    #   aiv_id = pl.tile.get_subblock_idx(); n is HW-fixed at 2 (validated).

def aiv_shard(tile: T, mode: SplitMode) -> T: ...
    # AIC->AIV scatter: this lane's half of a full cube tile.
    # result type = input with the split axis HALVED.

def aic_gather(tile: T, mode: SplitMode) -> T: ...
    # AIV->AIC gather: reassemble per-lane halves into the full tile the cube consumes.
    # result type = input with the split axis DOUBLED.  (inverse of aiv_shard)
```

`mode` is `SplitMode.UP_DOWN` (split rows / axis 0) or `SplitMode.LEFT_RIGHT` (split cols / axis 1), expressed in **2D-tile vocabulary**.

#### Worked example (the `qk_pv` kernel)

```python
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="qk_pv"):
    qk_raw  = pl.matmul(q, k, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32)         # AIC, full [M, K]
    for aiv_id in pl.split_aiv(2):
        qk_h    = pl.aiv_shard(qk_raw, pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)           # [M//2, K]  full->half
        qk_sc   = pl.mul(qk_h, SOFTMAX_SCALE)
        qk_mi   = pl.row_max(qk_sc)                                    # [M//2, 1]
        qk_exp  = pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(qk_sc, qk_mi))
        qk_li   = pl.row_sum(qk_exp)
        qk_bf16 = pl.cast(qk_exp, target_type=pl.BF16)                 # [M//2, K]
        qk_full = pl.aic_gather(qk_bf16, pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)         # [M, K]    half->full
        qk_oi_f = pl.matmul(qk_full, v, out_dtype=pl.FP32)            # [M, HEAD] cube sees FULL, deduce ok
        qk_oi   = pl.aiv_shard(qk_oi_f, pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)          # [M//2, HEAD] full->half
        base = aiv_id * (M_TILE // 2)
        for sub in pl.unroll((M_TILE // 2) // H_TILE):
            r0 = sub * H_TILE
            oi[base + r0 : base + r0 + H_TILE, :]  = qk_oi[r0:r0+H_TILE, :]   # GM store: lane's owned rows
            mi[base + r0 : base + r0 + H_TILE, 0:1] = qk_mi[r0:r0+H_TILE, 0:1]
            li[base + r0 : base + r0 + H_TILE, 0:1] = qk_li[r0:r0+H_TILE, 0:1]
```

The user makes **one annotation per full↔half transition**. Everything else flows by type.

#### Semantic model — closed under two boundary ops

A tile is either **full** (AIC vocabulary, `[M,…]`) or **half** (AIV-lane vocabulary, `[M//2,…]`). `aiv_shard` is the only full→half edge; `aic_gather` is the only half→full edge. The type itself (`[M]` vs `[M//2]`) encodes which — **no split-state analysis or propagation is needed**, and cube ops always see full operands so their shape deduction is unchanged. This is what makes `qk_oi_f = matmul(qk_full, v)` type-check: `qk_full` is full `[M,K]` (post-gather), so the matmul deduces `[M,HEAD]` normally. Feeding a half into a cube op is rejected by the verifier (see below).

#### Mode is declared, not inferred

The split direction is a property of the **2D tile at the transfer** — `tile.tpush_to_aiv`/`tpop_from_aic` carry a `split` int attr (`None=0/UpDown=1/LeftRight=2`), and tiles are already 2D by `ExpandMixedKernel` time (`FlattenTileNdTo2D` is pass 15, `ExpandMixedKernel` 21, `SplitVectorKernel` 23). A *generic high-dim slice* cannot reliably name "row" vs "col" because the high-dim→2D-tile axis mapping (flatten/layout/transpose) is decided by passes that run after the user's source. So the user declares the mode in 2D-tile vocab on the shard/gather op, and the compiler **validates** it at the 2D-tile boundary rather than guessing.

#### Lowering — onto existing, already-correct paths

```
aiv_shard(x, mode)  ->  cube  tile.tpush_to_aiv(x, split=N)  +  AIV  tile.tpop_from_aic(split=N)   # HALVES (existing)
aic_gather(x, mode) ->  AIV   tile.tpush_to_aic(x, split=N)  +  cube tile.tpop_from_aiv(split=N)    # KEEPS FULL (existing)
```

From `split_vector_kernel_pass.cpp:400-406`: *"`tpop_from_aic`: AIV consumes from cube — halve the popped tile … `tpop_from_aiv`: AIC consumes from vector — keep full tile shape."* The two new ops are exactly the two existing pop behaviors surfaced to the user; orchestration codegen (`RequiresDualAivDispatch` is already boolean) and the `.pto`/PTOAS layer (per-transfer `split`) are unchanged.

#### Compiler-side changes, by pass

- **Frontend** (`language/dsl_api.py`, `parser/ast_parser.py`): add `split_aiv` to `_VALID_ITERATORS`; `_parse_split_aiv_for_loop` (mirror `_parse_spmd_for_loop`) opens an `InCore` scope with attr `{"split_aiv": True}` and binds `aiv_id = tile.get_subblock_idx()`. Reject `n != 2`, loop kwargs (`init_values/chunk/stage/deps`), and a scope that also carries `optimizations=[pl.split(...)]`.
- **New IR ops** `tile.aiv_shard` / `tile.aic_gather` (`src/ir/op/tile_ops/`): one `tile` arg + `split` int attr; type inference halves / doubles the mode axis (`CHECK_SPAN` even extent).
- **`ExpandMixedKernel`** (pass 21): lower `aiv_shard`/`aic_gather` to their `tpush`/`tpop` pairs with `split = int(mode)` from the op (today `MakeSplitKwargs()` stamps the `split=0` placeholder; now it carries the declared mode).
- **`SplitVectorKernel`** (pass 23): for `split_aiv` functions, **skip the per-op halving entirely** (tiles already half via the shard type). Retain only `dual_aiv_dispatch` stamping.
- **New `AivSplitVerifier`** (registered in `PropertyVerifierRegistry`): the validation below.

#### Validation (pass-time, span'd)

| Check | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| even extent | `aiv_shard`: split-axis even; `aic_gather`: result extent even |
| **full-operand pairing** | a cube op may only consume *full* tiles; a half must pass through `aic_gather` first (this is the check that catches the `matmul(half, …)` mistake) |
| mode consistency | a half from `aiv_shard(_, a)` later `aic_gather`'d must use axis `a` (def-use link) |
| `get_subblock_idx` scope | only valid inside a `split_aiv` function (else it silently returns 0 and both lanes write the same rows) |
| GM offset ↔ mode axis | a `Split(a)` tile's GM store must address axis `a` by `aiv_id` |
| slot-size | `GetCommonSlotSizeBytes` succeeds across all transfers |
| mode policy | conservative single-mode gate (see Open Questions) — one deletable `CHECK` |

#### Multi-mode finding (ISA fact, corrects an earlier assumption)

We verified that **per-transfer split modes are mechanically supported** by the runtime/PTOAS, *not* limited to one mode per kernel: the pipe `pipe_key` (`FlagID|DirType|SlotNum|LocalSlotNum|SlotSize`) does **not** encode the split mode; `CreateInitializePipe` fixes only slot *size*/direction/depth (`GetCommonSlotSizeBytes` = max); the split is realized per-`tpop` ("AIC pushes one full tile, both AIV0/AIV1 consume their halves from the same slot", `runtime/.../tpush-tpop-sim.md`); and `RequiresDualAivDispatch` is a boolean. The existing "conflicting cross-core split modes" error in `SplitVectorKernel` is therefore a **software simplification** tied to its one-`split_dim`-per-function rewrite, not a hardware law. The explicit model removes that coupling, so mixed modes become structurally possible (subject to a PTOAS confirmation probe — see Open Questions).

### Affected Files

- `python/pypto/language/dsl_api.py` — **Modify** — `split_aiv`, `aiv_shard`, `aic_gather`
- `python/pypto/language/parser/ast_parser.py` — **Modify** — `_VALID_ITERATORS` + `_parse_split_aiv_for_loop` + double-decl reject
- `python/pypto/language/__init__.py`, `op/__init__.py`, `pypto_core/*.pyi` — **Modify** — exports + stubs
- `src/ir/op/tile_ops/aiv_shard.cpp` (+ `aic_gather`) — **New** — `tile.aiv_shard` / `tile.aic_gather` ops + type inference
- `python/bindings/modules/*.cpp` — **Modify** — bindings for the new ops
- `src/ir/transforms/expand_mixed_kernel_pass.cpp` — **Modify** — lower shard/gather to `tpush`/`tpop` with `split=N`
- `src/ir/transforms/split_vector_kernel_pass.cpp` — **Modify** — bypass per-op halving for `split_aiv` functions
- `src/ir/transforms/aiv_split_verifier.cpp` — **New** — validation + registry entry
- `docs/{en,zh-cn}/dev/passes/` + DSL docs — **New/Modify** — pass doc + `pl.split_aiv`/`aiv_shard`/`aic_gather`

### Testing Plan

`tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_aiv_shard.py` (before/after, `ir.assert_structural_equal`):

1. The `qk_pv` case: `aiv_shard(UP_DOWN)` + `H_TILE` sub-slice store **compiles through ptoas** (the original regression).
2. `LEFT_RIGHT` column shard → `split=2`, even-`N` validated.
3. Type check: `aiv_shard([M,K], UP_DOWN)` → `[M//2,K]`; `aic_gather([M//2,K], UP_DOWN)` → `[M,K]`.
4. Full-operand pairing: `matmul(half, …)` without `aic_gather` raises a span'd error.
5. Error cases: odd extent; reduce-on-split-axis; `get_subblock_idx` outside `split_aiv`; GM offset on the wrong axis; double-declaration with `pl.split`.
6. Single-mode gate fires on two differing modes (until lifted).
7. Codegen parity: post-lowering IR matches the legacy `pl.split` path for an equivalent whole-tile kernel.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Fix the auto-pass (`SplitVectorKernel`) systematically** — add a `SplitState` (FullAxis/SubRegion) model + coordinate-transform rewrite + keep split-axis loops rolled. Rejected as the primary path: it re-implements the index-space reasoning the pass keeps getting wrong; the unrolled strided store leaves the iteration structure unrecoverable (offsets `32,48` index a 32-row tile). Worth retaining as the *legacy* path for simple whole-tile kernels.
- **Generic slice as the transfer marker** (`qk_raw[aiv_id*half:…]`) — rejected: a high-dim source slice can't be mapped to the 2D-tile row/col mode (flatten/layout/transpose intervene), so the compiler can't reliably check `UP_DOWN` vs `LEFT_RIGHT`.
- **`mode=` on the `split_aiv` loop** — rejected: the mode is a property of each AIC↔AIV transfer, not of the SPMD loop; multiple transfers may differ.
- **Remove the loop entirely** (infer dual-AIV from shard ops, use `get_subblock_idx()` directly) — rejected: the GM output store needs the lane index, so a bound `aiv_id` + a scoped per-lane region is cleaner than scattered `get_subblock_idx()` calls.

### Rollout / Migration

- `pl.split_aiv` (explicit) and `pl.split(mode)` (auto) **coexist in parallel**, converging on byte-identical post-detection IR (`split` Function attr + `dual_aiv_dispatch`, `tpush`/`tpop` carrying `split=N`), so codegen and PTOAS need zero changes.
- Explicit is the recommended path for index-space-aware kernels; auto is retained as the simple on-ramp. **Do not** make auto lower to explicit (synthesizing correct `aiv_id`-indexed slices for arbitrary kernels is exactly the inference the auto path lacks).
- No backward-incompatible change: existing `pl.split` users are untouched; new ops are additive.

### Security Considerations

None. This is a compiler-internal DSL/IR change with no new external input surface, network, or secret handling. The added verifier strictly *tightens* validation (turns silent miscompiles into pass-time errors).

### Open Questions

1. **Region boundary / cube roundtrip.** How the cube assembles two lanes' halves for an intermediate `matmul` (via `aic_gather` → `tpop_from_aiv` full path) needs a prototype to confirm against PTOAS on a small two-lane example before the pass is written.
2. **PTOAS mixed-mode probe.** Hand-author a `.pto` with two `tpop`s (`split=1`, `split=2`) and run `ptoas` to definitively decide whether the conservative single-mode gate can be deleted.
3. **Naming.** `aic_gather` (scatter/gather symmetry) vs `aic_merge` / `aic_assemble`. Feedback welcome.
4. **Pure-AIV split (no cube transfer).** Has no shard op to trigger dual-dispatch; out of scope here, or add a thin `with pl.dual_aiv()` marker only if a real case appears.

title: [Pass Bug] MemoryReuse global largest-first packing (#1805) drops PIPE_MTE3<->PIPE_V sync -> stale read, ~17.5% wrong output
body:
### Pass Name

MemoryReuse (`src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp`)

### Description

PR #1805 (commit `035359b9`, "global largest-first packing for MemoryReuse
buffer reuse") introduces a numerical-correctness regression. After this
commit the MemoryReuse pass repacks tile buffers into tighter/overlapping
offsets, but a required `PIPE_MTE3 <-> PIPE_V` synchronization at the new
reuse boundary is **not** inserted (the flags present before the commit are
dropped). A vector op then reads a tile before the MTE3 store that fills it
completes -> stale read -> corrupted output.

Reproduces with the dsv4 `prefill_sparse_attn` kernel (pypto-lib):
`python models/deepseek/v4/prefill_sparse_attn.py -p a2a3 -d <dev>`
=> `attn_out` fails `ratio_allclose(atol=1e-4, rtol=1/128)` with
error_count ~= 92000/524288 (~17.5%), deterministic every run.

Bisect (each step rebuilt with `cmake --build build --parallel`):

| pypto commit | result |
|---|---|
| #1759 `1217e0c1` (cross-scope deps) | PASS |
| #1810 `2cd14c2c` (parent of #1805) | PASS |
| **#1805 `035359b9` (MemoryReuse global largest-first packing)** | **FAIL ~17.5%** |
| HEAD `d2471cbb` (main) | FAIL ~17.5% |

The only file recompiled at the culprit commit is `memory_reuse_pass.cpp`.

A minimal `@pl.program` reproducer has not yet been isolated; the Before/Actual
below are the codegen-level manifestation (kernel
`prefill_hca_attn_qk_softmax_tile`) captured by comparing the PASS-era vs
FAIL-era `build_output`.

### Git Commit ID

d2471cbb (culprit: 035359b9 / PR #1805)

### Before IR (Input)

```python
# No minimal @pl.program reproducer isolated yet.
# Repro: models/deepseek/v4/prefill_sparse_attn.py (pypto-lib @ e36b94d1)
#
# Codegen evidence (PASS-era, pypto @ 2cd14c2c, parent of #1805):
#   kernel prefill_hca_attn_qk_softmax_tile holds 8 PIPE_MTE3<->PIPE_V flags,
#   e.g. an MTE3 store guarded by:
#       set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID0)
#       ... (vector consumer) ...
#       wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID0)
#   buffer offsets: v25..v29 = 81920 / 73728 / 65536 / 81984 / 90176
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

```python
# After MemoryReuse, the cross-pipe sync guarding the reused buffer must be
# preserved: every MTE3 store into a reused tile that a vector op later reads
# keeps its matching set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V)/wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V).
# Tighter packing is fine ONLY if the reuse boundary still emits the sync.
```

### Actual IR or Error

```shell
# FAIL-era (pypto @ 035359b9 / d2471cbb): kernel prefill_hca_attn_qk_softmax_tile
# keeps only 4 of the 8 PIPE_MTE3<->PIPE_V flags (net loss of 4 across ALL
# kernels: 404 -> 400). Both a set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID0) and its
# matching wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID0) are removed.
#
# buffer offsets repacked into overlapping ranges:
#   v25..v29 = 69696 / 65536 / 69760 / 65600 / 77952
#
# runtime validation:
#   'attn_out' FAIL (ratio_allclose(atol=0.0001, rtol=0.0078125, max_error_ratio=0.005))
#   ratio_allclose fail: error_count=92186/524288 (ratio=17.5831%, allowed<=0.5000%)
```

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

Ascend 910C (observed on-device; root cause is in the pass and likely not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform (if relevant)

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1475 (a different MemoryReuse hazard — WAR serialization of
independent matmuls — not the same root cause). Repro kernel lives in
pypto-lib (`models/deepseek/v4/prefill_sparse_attn.py`, commit `e36b94d1`).

title: feat(ir): allow_early_resolve hint on pl.spmd dispatch forms
body:
## Summary

Extends the speculative early-dispatch opt-in `allow_early_resolve` — already supported on `pl.submit(...)` and `pl.at(...)` — to all three `pl.spmd(...)` dispatch forms:

- plain with-form: `with pl.spmd(N, allow_early_resolve=True): kernel(...)`
- capture form: `with pl.spmd(N, allow_early_resolve=True) as tid: ...`
- loop form: `for i in pl.spmd(N, allow_early_resolve=True): ...`

The flag is recorded as an `allow_early_resolve` attr on `SpmdScopeStmt`. The existing scope outliner already reads this attr generically and threads it onto the synthesised `ir.Submit` (forcing the Submit shape even without `as tid`), where orchestration codegen emits `Arg::set_allow_early_resolve(true)` — so no new IR node fields, bindings, or type stubs were needed.

## Changes

- **DSL** (`dsl_api.py`): `spmd()` / `SpmdContext` gain an `allow_early_resolve: bool = False` parameter.
- **Parser** (`ast_parser.py`): parses the kwarg (boolean-literal validated via a shared `_parse_spmd_bool_literal_kwarg` helper reused by `sync_start=`); threads it onto the `SpmdScopeStmt` attrs for all three forms; rejects it on a `pl.cluster()`-nested `pl.spmd` (`_reject_spmd_early_resolve_in_cluster`), since such a scope is unwrapped into the Group function and never produces a Submit.
- **Printer** (`python_printer.cpp`): emits `allow_early_resolve=True` in all three `SpmdScopeStmt` rendering paths so print→reparse round-trips.
- **Pass guard** (`outline_cluster_scopes_pass.cpp`): `UnwrapNestedSpmd`'s `INTERNAL_CHECK` also covers `allow_early_resolve` (defensive, for hand-built/deserialized IR).
- **Docs**: English + Chinese DSL syntax references updated.

## Testing

- [x] Parser / IR-attr / print round-trip tests for all three forms (`test_scope_parsing.py`)
- [x] Outliner threads the flag onto `ir.Submit`, incl. force-Submit-without-`as tid` (`test_outline_cluster_scopes.py`)
- [x] End-to-end codegen emits `set_allow_early_resolve(true)` + negative case (`test_spmd_scope_tid_codegen.py`)
- [x] Cluster-nesting rejection + non-bool-literal rejection
- [x] Full local regression (language + ir/transforms + printing + codegen) green; rebuilt against rebased base

title: test(ops): Add tile-op ST coverage for previously untested ops
body:
## Summary

Adds **a2a3 System Tests** for tile ops that previously had **no ST coverage**, and fixes one codegen bug surfaced along the way. **90 a2a3 tests** (from an initial 22) under `tests/st/runtime/ops/`.

Each op is swept across coverage dimensions (per a per-op audit):
- **shape** — square `16×16`, tall `32×64`, wide `8×128`
- **valid_shape** — aligned, narrow-both `[8,12]`, narrow-rows `[8,16]`, narrow-cols `[16,8]` (store writes only the valid region; the rest of the zero-init output must stay 0)
- **dtype** — FP16 (sqrt/relu/lrelu/muls/divs/col_expand_add), BF16 (matmul_bias), uint16 (not_)
- **op args** — lrelu slopes `{0, 0.1, 1, -0.5, 2}`; muls/divs scalars incl. negative/zero/identity/fractional; sin/cos signed multi-period (±2π); sqrt 0-boundary; matmul_bias M/K/N + K-split
- **offset** — non-zero store offset into a larger output

a2a3-only via `@pytest.mark.platforms("a2a3")` (no platform param; `TestCase()` relies on the `--platform` default); a5 coverage will follow in a separate PR.

CI: all checks green (system-tests, system-tests-a5sim, unit-tests ubuntu+macos, codegen-tests, dist-system-tests, pypto-lib-model, pre-commit, clang-tidy).

## Ops covered (passing on a2a3)

`t`/`a`/`b` are `pl.Tile`, `s` a scalar.

| File | Op | Semantics | Usage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_unary_math.py` | `sin` | element-wise sine, radians, FP32: `out = sin(t)` | `pl.tile.sin(t)` |
| | `cos` | element-wise cosine, radians, FP32: `out = cos(t)` | `pl.tile.cos(t)` |
| | `sqrt` | element-wise square root (FP32/FP16): `out = sqrt(t)` | `pl.tile.sqrt(t)` |
| `test_activation_ops.py` | `relu` | `out = max(0, t)` | `pl.tile.relu(t)` |
| | `lrelu` | **leaky** ReLU: `out = t if t > 0 else slope*t` | `pl.tile.lrelu(t, 0.1)` |
| `test_vector_misc.py` | `muls` | tile × scalar: `out = t * s` | `pl.tile.muls(t, 2.5)` |
| | `divs` | tile ÷ scalar: `out = t / s` | `pl.tile.divs(t, 2.0)` |
| | `col_expand_add` | broadcast `col[1,N]` down rows + tile: `out[i,j] = t[i,j] + col[0,j]` | `pl.tile.col_expand_add(t, col)` |
| `test_gemv.py` | `matmul_bias` | `C[M,N] = A[M,K] @ B[K,N] + bias[1,N]` (Mat-resident; layout passes insert L0 extracts) | `pl.tile.matmul_bias(a, b, bias)` |
| `test_bitwise.py` | `not_` | bitwise NOT, int16/uint16: `out = ~t` | `pl.tile.not_(t)` |

```
sqrt:            [[1,4],[9,16]]               -> [[1,2],[3,4]]
relu:            [-2,-1,0,3]                  -> [0,0,0,3]
lrelu(0.1):      [-2,-1,0,3]                  -> [-0.2,-0.1,0,3]
col_expand_add:  t=[[1,2],[3,4]], col=[10,20] -> [[11,22],[13,24]]
matmul_bias:     A=[[1,2]], B=I2, bias=[[10,20]] -> [[11,22]]
narrow valid_shape: physical [16,16], valid [8,12]: out[:8,:12]=op(in); rest = 0
```

## Codegen fix — `trem` / `trems` / `txor` / `txors` `tmp` operand

ptoas's `TRem/TRemS/TXor/TXorS` take a scratch `tmp` tile as a third `ins` operand (`src0, src1, tmp`), but the PTO op table (`src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp`) registered arity 2 and `tile.rem`/`tile.rems` had no `tmp` param, so the emitted `.pto` was missing the operand (ptoas: `expected ','`). Fix: add a `tmp` to `tile.rem`/`rems` across the DSL, IR builder and op registration (mirroring `xor`/`xors`; `rems` uses the dtype-permissive `DeduceTileOpTileScalarTileType`), and bump the table arity to 3. The `test_tile_rem`/`rems` UTs are updated to pass `tmp`. Verified the regenerated `.pto` matches ptoas's `PTOOps.td` assemblyFormat.

## Tolerances (kept strict; relaxed only where FP16/accumulation requires it)

Almost everything uses the strict `rtol=atol=1e-5` default — including **sin/cos**, which are accurate to 1e-5 on a2a3 (16×16/32×64/narrow all pass). The only relaxations are forced by representable precision, not by masking error:
- **FP16 `lrelu` → 2e-3**: FP16 machine epsilon ≈ 9.8e-4, so a 1e-5 comparison is below FP16's representable precision; 2e-3 ≈ 2 ULP. (relu/muls/divs FP16 stay strict — they are exact in FP16.)
- **`matmul_bias` → 1e-3**: K-reduction reorder vs torch — same bar as the existing `test_matmul` AutoL0 cases.
- **`lrelu` golden** is true leaky-relu (`x>0 ? x : slope*x`), confirmed from device values; FP32 lrelu stays at strict `1e-5`. This was a correctness fix to the reference, not a tolerance relaxation.

An earlier revision loosened sin/cos to 1e-2; that was reverted once CI showed the wide-tile failure is a **codegen defect** (below), not approximation error.

## Codegen / ISA defects discovered (candidates for follow-up issues)

Writing this coverage surfaced real on-device defects (not test issues). They are
skipped/omitted here and tracked locally:

1. **sin/cos miscompute columns ≥ 64 on a width-128 tile (ptoas/pto-isa)** —
   `[8,128]` FP32 `tile.sin`/`tile.cos` return garbage for cols ≥ 64 (64/1024
   grossly wrong), while `[16,16]`/`[32,64]`/narrow are correct at the strict
   1e-5 default and `tile.sqrt` at `[8,128]` is fine. Root cause confirmed to be
   **below pypto**: the generated `.pto` is correct — every op in the
   `LowerSinCos` chain (`tcvt` FP32↔INT32, binary `tmul`/`tadd`/`tsub`, scalar
   `tmuls`/`tadds`) is emitted uniformly at `rows=8, cols=128`, identical
   metadata to the passing `relu` path. So ptoas/pto-isa miscompiles one of these
   vector ops on the second 64-wide segment of a width-128 tile. **Not fixed in
   this PR (pypto codegen is correct); the wide sin/cos case is omitted (removed,
   not skipped) and this will be followed up on the ptoas/pto-isa side.**
2. **`matmul_bias` narrow-N** — the cube does not zero the `[:, VALID_N:]` output
   region (narrow-M and narrow-K are correct).
3. **Cube 1-row / acc paths** — `gemv`/`gemv_bias` hit pto-isa `TExtract`
   `static_assert(dstRow % 16 == 0)`; `gemv_acc` hits an unsupported acc→acc
   `pto.tmov`.
4. **`tsubc` miscompute** — `addc`/`subc`/`addsc`/`subsc` produce wrong `a-b-c`.
5. **Integer bitwise/remainder ISA gaps** — `rem`/`rems` (int32 wrong / alloc
   error), `xor`/`xors` (need int16/uint16), `and_`/`or_`/`shl`/`shr` (ptoas
   rejects). The `tile.rem`/`rems` DSL+codegen tmp-operand fix in this PR is kept
   so they are ready to re-enable.

## Ops deliberately given NO ST (not skipped — simply not added)

These tile ops are **registered in the pypto front-end but have no working a2a3 ptoas/pto-isa path**, so an ST cannot pass. Rather than carry `@pytest.mark.skip` placeholders, **no ST is added for them at all** — the suite contains zero skipped tests of its own. Each will get ST once the pto path exists; status is tracked in `docs/zh-cn/dev/ptoas-op-status.md`.

| Op(s) | Why ST cannot be added on a2a3 yet |
|---|---|
| `gemv` / `gemv_bias` | pto-isa `TExtract` `static_assert(dstRow % 16 == 0)` rejects the 1-row vector |
| `gemv_acc` | ptoas has no acc→acc `pto.tmov` |
| `addc` / `subc` / `addsc` / `subsc` | `pto.tsubc` miscomputes `a - b - c` on device |
| `rem` / `rems` | `TREM` returns wrong values on int32; `TREMS` `alloc_tile` element-type error (codegen `tmp`-operand fix is kept, ready to re-enable) |
| `xor` / `xors` | `TXOR`/`TXORS` require int16/uint16 — int32 unsupported |
| `and_` / `or_` / `shl` / `shr` (+ scalar `ands`/`ors`/`shls`/`shrs`) | ptoas rejects `pto.tand`/`tor`/`tshl`/`tshr` (`invalid kind of type specified`) |
| `prelu` | the 3-arg DSL form does not match codegen `pto.tprelu` |
| `expands` / `sum` / `sels` | no codegen registered / undocumented semantics — not assemblable |
| `sin` / `cos` at width-128 (`8×128`) | ptoas/pto-isa miscomputes columns ≥ 64 (`16×16`/`32×64`/narrow are covered and pass at strict 1e-5; only the wide shape is left out) |
| `matmul_bias` narrow-N | the cube does not zero the `[:, VALID_N:]` output region (narrow-M and narrow-K are covered) |

## Incidental
- Renamed `test_activation.py` → `test_activation_ops.py` (the original basename collided with `tests/st/examples/02_intermediate/test_activation.py`, aborting a2a3 pytest collection).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(ops): add product-reduction (row/col_prod) and expand max/min/expdif ops
body:
