title: [RFC] Move LowerCompositeOps before ConvertTensorToTileOps
body:
## Summary

Propose moving `LowerCompositeOps` (slot 14) to run **before** `ConvertTensorToTileOps` (slot 12), so composite collectives can emit clean tensor-level primitives like `pld.tensor.get`/`pld.tensor.put` and let the existing conversion registry handle flattening + VEC staging tile allocation uniformly.

## Problem

`LowerCompositeOps` currently runs **after** `ConvertTensorToTileOps`. Because tensor-to-tile conversion has already run, composite lowerings cannot emit tensor-level ops — they must duplicate the conversion logic: compute `[rows, cols]` from N-D shapes, allocate a `tile.create`, and emit `pld.tile.get`/`pld.tile.put` directly.

This duplication bit us in [feat/relax-get-dst](https://github.com/georgebisbas/pypto/tree/feat/relax-get-dst): relaxing `pld.tile.get`'s dst to accept plain `Tensor` required fixing the verifier, codegen, and DSL wrappers — but the reviewer pointed out the same fix was missing in `op_conversion_registry.cpp`. The duplicated flattening logic in `LowerCompositeOps`'s `LowerTensorBroadcastRule` must now also be kept in sync with any future type-constraint changes.

## Current pass ordering

| Slot | Pass |
|------|------|
| 12 | `ConvertTensorToTileOps` |
| 13 | `OptimizeOrchTensors` |
| 14 | `LowerCompositeOps` |

`LowerCompositeOps` has **empty PassProperties** — requires nothing, produces nothing — suggesting no hard dependency on the output of passes 12-13.

## Proposed

| Slot | Pass |
|------|------|
| ~12 | `LowerCompositeOps` ← moved earlier |
| 12 | `ConvertTensorToTileOps` ← runs after, picks up tensor-level get/put |

With this, composites could emit `pld.tensor.get(dst, peer, src)` and let `ConvertTensorToTileOps` handle the `tile.create` + `pld.tile.get` uniformly.

## Open questions

1. Does `LowerCompositeOps` depend on any `IRProperty` or IR shape from `ConvertTensorToTileOps`? The allreduce lowering emits `tile.load`/`tile.store` — those would need rewriting to tensor-level ops.

2. What does `OptimizeOrchTensors` do to orchestration-level variables? Does `LowerCompositeOps` need its output?

3. Composite ops currently use `tile.remote_load` directly. Full benefit requires rewriting all composite lowerings to emit tensor-level primitives.

## References

- `src/ir/transforms/lower_composite_ops_pass.cpp` — all lowering rules
- `src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp` — `pld.tensor.get`/`put` → `tile.create` + `pld.tile.get`/`put`
- `docs/en/dev/passes/12-convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.md`
- `docs/en/dev/passes/14-lower_composite_ops.md`
- Notes: [`pypto-3.0-notes/pr_plans/36-move-lower-composite-ops-before-convert-tensor-to-tile.md`](https://github.com/georgebisbas/pypto-3.0-notes/blob/main/pr_plans/36-move-lower-composite-ops-before-convert-tensor-to-tile.md)

title: ci: single source of truth for pto-isa/ptoas; derive pto-isa from runtime submodule
body:
## Problem

pto-isa and ptoas versions were duplicated across `ci.yml`/`daily_ci.yml` (9 inline `--pto-isa-commit` literals, 3 `git checkout <sha>`, ptoas pins in 5 job envs) and drifted. More broadly, **pypto, pypto-lib and the runtime each pinned pto-isa independently** with nothing keeping them consistent.

## What this does

**1. Centralize (de-dup).** `toolchain/versions.env` + a `toolchain` lead job feed every device job via `needs.toolchain.outputs.*`. A guard step fails CI if a pto-isa/ptoas literal reappears inline.

**2. Make the runtime the source of truth for pto-isa.** The runtime now publishes `runtime/pto_isa.pin` (simpler #1134). This PR:
- bumps the runtime submodule `fcc33bcb -> fb28fd71` (picks up #1134 + runtime-internal changes; pypto builds clean, `tests/ut/runtime` 308 pass, no source adaptation), and
- **derives** pto-isa from `runtime/pto_isa.pin` instead of declaring it — the `toolchain` job reads the pinned submodule. `versions.env` keeps only the pypto-owned ptoas pins.

Bumping the runtime submodule now moves pypto's pto-isa in lockstep with the runtime it builds against.

**Net pto-isa change:** `016396b5 -> ddafa8da` (the runtime's pin). The device jobs in this run validate the bumped runtime + this pto-isa.

## Follow-up

pypto-lib derives the same toolchain from the pypto it builds (drops its own `b9122ec5` + ptoas literals).

title: feat(ir): role-aware pipeline-stage buffer separation in MemoryReuse
body:
## Summary

`pl.pipeline(stage=F)` replicates a loop body F times for ping-pong buffering, but `MemoryReuse` coalesced the sibling-clone tiles into one buffer because their program-order lifetimes are disjoint — serializing the stages and defeating the pipeline. The prior safeguard was a fragile *side effect* of `CanonicalizeIOOrder` clustering loads to induce lifetime overlap, which breaks when the dependency graph or nested structure prevents that clustering.

This makes stage separation an explicit, **role-aware** reuse constraint:

- **LowerPipelineLoops** tags every tile-producing `Call` in clone `k` with a `pipeline_membership="group:stage"` attr (one pair per enclosing replicated region, so nested same-core pipelines stay separated at every level).
- **MemoryReuse** reads it and blocks a cross-stage buffer share (same group, different stage) **when at least one tile is a load** (`tile.load`/`tile.read`). Only load buffers need per-stage privacy so iteration `i+1`'s prefetch overlaps iteration `i`'s compute; compute intermediates of different stages may still coalesce.

### Why role-aware (not depth=F)

Forbidding *all* cross-stage reuse (depth=F) is physically infeasible — F full copies of every intermediate overflow the on-chip budget (e.g. `stage=4` RMSNorm needs 4×67KB > 188KB UB). The L0 matmul spaces (Left/Right/Acc/Bias) are exempt entirely — their buffering is owned by `AutoTileMatmulL0` / `CanonicalizeIOOrder` extract clustering and is capacity-bound.

### Op-call attr round-trip

`pipeline_membership` is the first op-call attr that must survive across passes. Added generic op-call attr round-trip: the python printer emits an allowlisted `attrs={...}` for op-calls and the parser re-attaches it via a new `ir.set_call_attrs` binding, so the attr survives the print→parse round-trip the test harness runs after every pass.

## Testing

- [x] New regression tests (`TestPipelineStageSeparation`): load separation, role-aware compute coalescing (buffers < depth=F), and a non-pipeline control.
- [x] Full `tests/ut/ir`, `tests/ut/codegen`, `tests/ut/language`, `tests/ut/jit` suites pass.
- [x] Previously-broken real kernels now pass: `test_pipeline_matmul_acc_no_acc_to_acc_tmov`, `test_qwen3_decode`.
- [x] Documentation updated (passes 26/30, en + zh), correcting the inaccurate "MemoryReuse cannot merge" claim.

title: fix(st): enlarge paged-attention task ring window to avoid flaky 507018 (#1840)
body:
## Summary

`test_dynamic_paged_attention[256-64-128-64-8192-32768]` intermittently fails on a2a3 with AICore error **507018** (issue #1840). This PR pins the root cause to **runtime task-ring sizing** and applies a front-end (RunConfig) workaround so the ST passes deterministically.

## Root cause (device-verified)

The dynamic paged-attention pipeline emits **~525K tasks** for this config:

```
batch * q_loop * kv_blocks * inner_kernels  +  init
  256 *   4     *   128     *      4         + (256*4)  ≈ 525,312
```

That far exceeds the default per-ring task window `PTO2_TASK_WINDOW_SIZE = 16384`. The AICPU **orchestrator** (producer) fills the task ring and spins in `alloc()` waiting for the **scheduler** (consumer) to drain it. Under producer/consumer back-pressure timing it hits the alloc spin limit (`PTO2_ALLOC_SPIN_LIMIT = 100000`) and a *normal full ring* is misreported as a fatal:

```
[pto_ring_buffer.h] FATAL: Task Allocator Deadlock - Task Ring Full!
[scheduler_cold_path.cpp] Fatal error (code=3) ... total_tasks=0
[aicpu_executor.cpp]      PTO2 runtime failed with rc=-3   -> host 507018
```

It is flaky because it is a timing race — volume-sensitive and diff-independent (matches the ~1/3 CI rate and the report that it reproduces on an unrelated Python-only PR).

This is **not** codegen, scheduler-dispatch, AICore compute, or the orchestration `.so` — those were investigated and ruled out on-device.

## Fix

Set `ring_task_window` / `ring_dep_pool` via `RunConfig` for this test (≥ the program's task count) so the orchestrator never blocks. The ST harness dispatches through `runner._execute_on_device`, which bypasses the `program.run` `_apply_ring_overrides` path, so it didn't forward ring sizing — this PR forwards `RunConfig.ring_*` as `runtime_env` overrides through that path.

Files:
- `python/pypto/runtime/runner.py` — `_execute_on_device` accepts + forwards a `runtime_env` dict.
- `tests/st/harness/core/test_runner.py` — builds `runtime_env` from `RunConfig.ring_*` (case config first, else runner config).
- `tests/st/runtime/.../test_dynamic_paged_attention.py` — sets `ring_task_window=1048576, ring_dep_pool=1048576` (1048576 = smallest power-of-2 ≥ ~525K task count).

## Verification (device A/B, a2a3)

| Config | Result |
| --- | --- |
| default window (16384) | **5/9 runs hit 507018** |
| enlarged window | **12/12 pass** (6 via env var + 6 via this RunConfig path) |

## Note — final solution still under discussion

This is a **front-end workaround** that unblocks CI and demonstrates the root cause lives in the runtime task-ring sizing. A larger window trades memory for headroom (it holds the whole task graph). The proper runtime-side fix — auto-size the window to the task count, or make a full ring legitimately back-pressure/block instead of false-deadlocking (and avoid the orchestrator busy-spin starving the scheduler) — is intentionally **not** in this PR and should be decided separately.

Refs: #1840

title: [Bug] pl.split(UP_DOWN) scope producing a GM tensor for a following unsplit scope 507018-deadlocks
body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto** (codegen/runtime) — a kernel that compiles cleanly emits code that 507018-deadlocks at runtime on a2a3. The trigger is a purely structural property of the UP_DOWN split + a cross-scope GM dependency; there is no compile-time error.

### Description

A heavy `pl.spmd(optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)])` scope that writes a GM scratch tensor which is then consumed by a **following UNSPLIT** `pl.spmd` scope **507018-deadlocks at runtime**:

```
ERROR sync_run_streams: aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
ERROR recover_device_or_mark_unusable: Device unrecoverable after AICore error 507018 ...
RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
```

It **compiles cleanly** (no error/warning). UB high-water in the generated IR is only ~44KB, so this is **not** a UB-budget overflow.

#### Isolating controls (every one of these PASSes — only the combination deadlocks)

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| Heavy UP_DOWN scope writes comb result to a scratch consumed by a following **unsplit** scope | **507018 deadlock** |
| Same scope writing **final outputs** (no following consumer scope) | PASS |
| Bare `UP_DOWN producer → scratch → unsplit consumer` with **trivial** ops (`load/mul/store`) | PASS |
| **Opposite direction**: unsplit producer → GM → `UP_DOWN` consumer | PASS |
| The heavy vector work alone under UP_DOWN (mix_x-style FP32 D-loop, OR comb softmax/sinkhorn) | PASS |
| Whole kernel **unsplit** | PASS |

So the deadlock requires BOTH: (a) a heavy UP_DOWN scope, AND (b) it produces a GM tensor consumed by a following unsplit scope. The bare directional dependency alone (trivial work) does not trigger it, and the reverse direction (unsplit→UP_DOWN) is fine.

#### Reproduction

`python models/deepseek/v4/_tmp_updown_combo.py -p a2a3` (in pypto-lib). Self-contained kernel:

```python
import pypto.language as pl

T = 128; HC_MULT = 4; HC_PAD = 8; W = HC_MULT * HC_PAD
D = 4096; T_TILE = 16; D_TILE = 256; ITERS = 4; EPS = 1e-6

@pl.jit
def combo_split(
    xb: pl.Tensor[[T, HC_MULT * D], pl.BF16],
    xp: pl.Tensor[[T, W], pl.FP32],
    xc: pl.Tensor[[T, W], pl.FP32],
    out_x: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[T, D], pl.BF16]],
    out_c: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[T, W], pl.FP32]],
):
    comb_scratch = pl.create_tensor([T, W], dtype=pl.FP32)
    # ---- SPLIT (UP_DOWN) producer scope: mix_x D-loop + comb softmax/sinkhorn ----
    for ob in pl.spmd(T // T_TILE, name_hint="combo", optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)]):
        t0 = ob * T_TILE
        rs = pl.create_tile([T_TILE, 1], dtype=pl.FP32, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        mx = pl.create_tile([T_TILE, 1], dtype=pl.FP32, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        ph0 = pl.load(xp, [t0, 0], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, 1], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        ph1 = pl.load(xp, [t0, 1], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, 1], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        ph2 = pl.load(xp, [t0, 2], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, 1], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        ph3 = pl.load(xp, [t0, 3], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, 1], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        pre0 = pl.row_sum(pl.recip(pl.add(pl.exp(pl.neg(ph0)), 1.0)), rs)
        pre1 = pl.row_sum(pl.recip(pl.add(pl.exp(pl.neg(ph1)), 1.0)), rs)
        pre2 = pl.row_sum(pl.recip(pl.add(pl.exp(pl.neg(ph2)), 1.0)), rs)
        pre3 = pl.row_sum(pl.recip(pl.add(pl.exp(pl.neg(ph3)), 1.0)), rs)
        for db in pl.range(D // D_TILE):
            d0 = db * D_TILE
            y = pl.row_expand_mul(pl.cast(pl.load(xb, [t0, 0 * D + d0], [T_TILE, D_TILE], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), target_type=pl.FP32), pre0)
            y = pl.add(y, pl.row_expand_mul(pl.cast(pl.load(xb, [t0, 1 * D + d0], [T_TILE, D_TILE], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), target_type=pl.FP32), pre1))
            y = pl.add(y, pl.row_expand_mul(pl.cast(pl.load(xb, [t0, 2 * D + d0], [T_TILE, D_TILE], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), target_type=pl.FP32), pre2))
            y = pl.add(y, pl.row_expand_mul(pl.cast(pl.load(xb, [t0, 3 * D + d0], [T_TILE, D_TILE], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), target_type=pl.FP32), pre3))
            pl.store(pl.cast(y, target_type=pl.BF16, mode="rint"), [t0, d0], out_x)
        p0 = pl.fillpad(pl.load(xc, [t0, 0 * HC_PAD], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, HC_MULT], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), pad_value=pl.PadValue.min)
        p1 = pl.fillpad(pl.load(xc, [t0, 1 * HC_PAD], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, HC_MULT], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), pad_value=pl.PadValue.min)
        p2 = pl.fillpad(pl.load(xc, [t0, 2 * HC_PAD], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, HC_MULT], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), pad_value=pl.PadValue.min)
        p3 = pl.fillpad(pl.load(xc, [t0, 3 * HC_PAD], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, HC_MULT], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), pad_value=pl.PadValue.min)
        g0 = pl.fillpad(pl.add(pl.row_expand_div(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p0, pl.row_max(p0, mx))), pl.row_sum(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p0, pl.row_max(p0, mx))), rs)), EPS), pad_value=pl.PadValue.zero)
        g1 = pl.fillpad(pl.add(pl.row_expand_div(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p1, pl.row_max(p1, mx))), pl.row_sum(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p1, pl.row_max(p1, mx))), rs)), EPS), pad_value=pl.PadValue.zero)
        g2 = pl.fillpad(pl.add(pl.row_expand_div(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p2, pl.row_max(p2, mx))), pl.row_sum(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p2, pl.row_max(p2, mx))), rs)), EPS), pad_value=pl.PadValue.zero)
        g3 = pl.fillpad(pl.add(pl.row_expand_div(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p3, pl.row_max(p3, mx))), pl.row_sum(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p3, pl.row_max(p3, mx))), rs)), EPS), pad_value=pl.PadValue.zero)
        for it in pl.range(ITERS):
            g0 = pl.row_expand_div(g0, pl.add(pl.row_sum(g0, rs), EPS))
            g1 = pl.row_expand_div(g1, pl.add(pl.row_sum(g1, rs), EPS))
            g2 = pl.row_expand_div(g2, pl.add(pl.row_sum(g2, rs), EPS))
            g3 = pl.row_expand_div(g3, pl.add(pl.row_sum(g3, rs), EPS))
            cs = pl.add(pl.add(pl.add(g0, g1), pl.add(g2, g3)), EPS)
            g0 = pl.div(g0, cs); g1 = pl.div(g1, cs); g2 = pl.div(g2, cs); g3 = pl.div(g3, cs)
        # comb -> GM SCRATCH (consumed by the following UNSPLIT scope) == TRIGGER
        pl.store(g0, [t0, 0 * HC_PAD], comb_scratch)
        pl.store(g1, [t0, 1 * HC_PAD], comb_scratch)
        pl.store(g2, [t0, 2 * HC_PAD], comb_scratch)
        pl.store(g3, [t0, 3 * HC_PAD], comb_scratch)
    # ---- UNSPLIT consumer scope: reads the scratch the split scope wrote ----
    for ob in pl.spmd(T // T_TILE, name_hint="combo_consume"):
        t0 = ob * T_TILE
        for g in pl.range(HC_MULT):
            grp = pl.load(comb_scratch, [t0, g * HC_PAD], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, HC_MULT], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
            pl.store(pl.set_validshape(grp, T_TILE, HC_MULT), [t0, g * HC_MULT], out_c)
    return out_x
```

Redirecting the four `comb_scratch` stores to a final output (`out_c`) and deleting the consumer scope makes it PASS — that one change is the difference between hang and pass.

Note: the device run also occasionally fails earlier with `halMemCtl rc=13 (EACCES)` on some cards (an unrelated PMU/register-permission issue) — retry until a good card runs the kernel; the 507018 is deterministic on a good card.

Related (distinct root causes): #1789 (within-scope event-allocation 507018, not cross-scope), #1840 (flaky paged-attention 507018), #1820 (AIV split DSL RFC), hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#362 (UP_DOWN precision drift).

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `f658207` |
| pypto | `94db6529` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `fcc33bcb` |
| pto-isa | `a1d60eb0` |
| ptoas | `0.46` |
| CANN | not detected |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

title: feat(ir): full-K M/N direct-store pipelined tiling in AutoTileMatmulL0
body:
## Summary

Adds **full-K M/N direct-store pipelining** to `AutoTileMatmulL0`. When a Mat-resident `tile.matmul`'s `[M, N]` output exceeds L0c and its sole consumer is a 2D `tile.store`, the pass tiles the output and — for the full-K case (`k == K`) — emits **nested `ForKind::Pipeline` loops** so `LowerPipelineLoops` double-buffers the moving-operand `tile.extract` behind the cube.

This is the direct-store (DDR-output) path. The on-chip-consumer / Mat-scratch (L1 `tile.assemble`) path is **deferred** to a separate follow-up (see Scope).

## What it does

- **Moving-operand double buffering** — the inner-loop `tile.extract` is hoisted (Load tier) so `LowerPipelineLoops` produces an L0A/L0B ping-pong, hiding the L1→L0 prep behind the cube matmul (the pto-isa A2A3 cost model's TEXTRACT-overlap win).
- **One L0C accumulator** — the inner loop carries `pipeline_overlap_stores=false`, so `CanonicalizeIOOrder` keeps each store adjacent to its matmul (`matmul_i, store_i, matmul_{i+1}`) instead of floating both stores below both matmuls. The floated schedule co-lives two `[m, n]` Acc results (`2·m·n·bytes_c`) while the chooser budgets one L0C buffer → an L0C overflow. (e.g. 320×320 @ 64 BF16 previously overflowed at 204800 = 2× the 100 KB C tile; now allocates.)
- **Exact row/column traversal** — the stationary (outer) axis minimises total interior extract traffic, `T_row = P·A + P·Q·B` vs `T_col = P·Q·A + Q·B`, rather than the `A ≥ B` panel-size heuristic (which mis-picks on rectangular grids).
- **Interior + tail boundary handling** — the divisible `[0, full_m) × [0, full_n)` interior pipelines with exact trip counts; the L-shaped partial boundary is peeled into straight-line tiles. No exact-divisor constraint on `M`/`N`, so e.g. `M = 272 = 16·17` does not collapse to a 16×16 tile and non-16-aligned dims are handled.

Split-K M/N (`K` spanning ≥ 2 L0 blocks) keeps the existing unrolled per-sub-tile K-loop grid. Both paths drive a shared `SubtilePlacer` (direct-store placement).

## Scope / deferred

Scoped to **full-K M/N direct-store pipelining**. The **Mat-scratch / L1-assembly** path (keep the `[M, N]` intermediate on-chip via `tile.assemble` for a downstream matmul) is deferred: the Acc→Mat assemble cannot lower to a config-identical `pto.subview` (Acc and Mat have different tile configs — fractal 1024 vs 512) and needs a converting `tmov`. On-chip consumers are left untouched with a `PH-AT-006` perf hint.

## Testing

- Row-stationary and column-stationary full-K paths (stationary-operand choice pinned).
- Partial-boundary tail peeling (272×272), numerically exact incl. the corner.
- Full Default-pipeline allocation with no L0C overflow (the one-accumulator regression).
- Post-lowering `matmul/store` interleaving (the one-accumulator schedule).
- **PTOCodegen smoke test** — direct-store full-K generates valid PTO MLIR (clean 320×320 + tail 272×272).
- Full `ir` / `jit` / `codegen` unit suite passes.

title: feat(ops): add tile.gatherb and tile.tri (byte-offset gather + triangular mask)
body:
## Summary

Continues the "add PTOAS-supported-but-missing ops" work (after #1824, #1845).
Adds two tile-only ops, both verified to assemble through ptoas, plus a status-doc fix.

### `tile.gatherb` — `pto.tgatherb` (byte-offset gather)
`dst[i, j] = *(src_base + offset[i, j])` — gather by per-element **byte** offset.
Mirrors `tile.gather` but takes raw `UINT32` byte offsets and needs no scratch
tile. Output is shaped like `offset` with the src dtype; src dtype in
{I8/U8, I16/U16, I32/U32, FP16, BF16, FP32}, dst row-major. The kSimpleOps
codegen mapping already existed; this wires the op registration + type
deduction, Python IR/DSL wrappers, both export registries, UT, an on-device ST
(FP16/FP32/INT32 × reverse/roll offset patterns), and op-reference docs.

### `tile.tri` — `pto.ttri` (triangular mask generator)
Generate a lower/upper triangular 0/1 mask over a 2D destination with diagonal
offset `d` — lower `dst[i,j]=1` iff `j<=i+d`, upper iff `j>=i+d` (matches
`torch.tril`/`torch.triu`). Mirrors the `tile.ci` generator: `diagonal` scalar
(INT32) + static 2D shape plus `dtype`/`upper` attributes; dtype in
{INT16, INT32, UINT16, UINT32, FP16, FP32}, dst row-major.

Codegen emits the **generic** MLIR op form
`"pto.ttri"(%diag, %dst) {upperOrLower = N : i32} : (i32, dst_type) -> ()`
because ptoas only exposes the compile-time upper/lower selector via the generic
syntax — the pretty `ins/outs` form hard-codes the lower variant. Both variants
were confirmed to assemble through ptoas to `TTRI<Tile, 0|1>(dst, diag)`.

### Docs
`part_add`/`part_mul`/`part_max`/`part_min` (merged in #1845, a2a3 system-tests
green) status-matrix remarks updated from "a2a3 真机待 CI" to "a2a3 真机已过".

## Testing
- Full `tests/ut/ir/operators/test_tile_ops.py` green (incl. new gatherb/tri UT).
- CPU host passes + codegen clean; emitted `.pto` for both ops assembles through
  ptoas to the expected `TGATHERB` / `TTRI` intrinsics.
- On-device ST added for both ops — relies on a2a3 system-tests for device numerics.

title: [Feature] Surface simpler's RunTiming through pypto's ChipWorker/RegistrationHandle so callers can reuse simpler's --rounds benchmark mode
body:
### Summary

simpler **already has** a rounds-based benchmark mode (`runtime/simpler_setup/scene_test.py`): `--rounds N` registers the callable once (`worker.register(...)`, scene_test.py:1201), loops `for round_idx in range(rounds)` (:1222), and each round does `timing = worker.run(handle, chip_args, config=config)` (:1243) — where `simpler.Worker.run` **returns a `RunTiming`** — collecting `(host_wall_us, device_wall_us)` (:1245) and reporting per-round averages via `_log_round_timings` (:328). `runtime/tools/benchmark_rounds.sh` drives this across ST examples.

The problem: pypto's wrapper around the same simpler worker **discards** that `RunTiming`. `pypto.runtime.worker.ChipWorker.run` (`python/pypto/runtime/worker.py:402`, `:409-412`) receives the `RunTiming` from `_run_chip` (`:443-458`, which returns `self._impl.run(cid, ...)` = simpler's `RunTiming`) but returns tensor outputs only; `RegistrationHandle.__call__` (`:556-566`) delegates to it and likewise drops timing. So any caller going through pypto's public Worker path — rather than `simpler.Worker` directly — cannot reuse simpler's benchmark mode.

Please surface the `RunTiming` that simpler already returns through pypto's register-once path, so pypto callers can run the same `--rounds` benchmark (register once, run N cheap launches, read per-round `device_wall_us`).

### Motivation / Use Case

We want a benchmark mode in pypto-lib's daily CI that measures each kernel's **on-device** time (~1 ms range). pypto-lib's golden harness dispatches through pypto (`execute_compiled` / `ChipWorker`), not `simpler.Worker`, so it cannot tap simpler's existing `scene_test` `--rounds` benchmark. The only public timed pypto entry is `execute_compiled` (#1679), which is **one-shot** (`register` → `run` → `close` per call), so looping it re-pays host register/load every iteration (hundreds of ms/round), swamping device time.

The infrastructure to do this correctly already exists end-to-end in simpler (`prepare_callable` + `run_prepared(..., out_timing)` cheap repeated launches with per-invocation `PtoRunTiming`; `simpler.Worker.run` returns it; `scene_test` consumes it). The one missing link is that pypto's wrapper hides it. Closing that gap lets pypto-lib reuse simpler's benchmark mode instead of reinventing it.

- One-shot timing (#1679, CLOSED) covers `execute_compiled` / `execute_on_device` only.
- Worker init/run/close lifecycle (#1155, CLOSED) exposes register-once reuse but never returns `RunTiming` from the repeated calls.
- simpler's `scene_test` `--rounds` mode is the prior art to mirror — it just needs the pypto Worker layer to stop swallowing `RunTiming`.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Mirror what `scene_test` does with `simpler.Worker`, but through pypto's public Worker. In rough order of preference:

1. A timing-returning variant on the handle / worker so the register-once + rounds loop can read it:

```python
h = worker.register(compiled)
for _ in range(rounds):
    outputs, timing = h.run_timed(a, b)        # or worker.run_timed(compiled, ...)
    samples.append(timing.device_wall_us)
```

2. A high-level benchmark helper that owns the loop + aggregation (the pypto equivalent of `scene_test --rounds` + `_log_round_timings`):

```python
stats = pypto.runtime.benchmark(compiled, args, rounds=100, warmup=3,
                                platform="a2a3", device_id=0)
# stats.device_wall_us_min / _median / samples ...
```

3. At minimum, stop discarding the `RunTiming` already produced by `_run_chip` so it is reachable from the public register-once path.

Keep `RegistrationHandle.__call__` / `ChipWorker.run`'s existing tensor-return contract intact (timing is opt-in via the new entry point) for backward compatibility.

### Additional Context

- simpler benchmark mode (prior art): `runtime/simpler_setup/scene_test.py` — `--rounds`, register-once (`:1201`), rounds loop (`:1222`), `worker.run` returns `RunTiming` (`:1243`), collect `(host_wall_us, device_wall_us)` (`:1245`), `_log_round_timings` (`:328`); driver `runtime/tools/benchmark_rounds.sh`.
- simpler C API already supports per-invocation timing on cheap launches: `run_prepared(..., PtoRunTiming *out_timing)` (`runtime/src/common/worker/pto_runtime_c_api.h:202-208`).
- pypto gap: `ChipWorker.run` discards timing (`python/pypto/runtime/worker.py:402`, `:409-412`); `_run_chip` already returns it (`:443-458`); `RegistrationHandle.__call__` (`:556-566`).
- `execute_compiled` is one-shot (`python/pypto/runtime/runner.py:1183`).
- For L3+ DAG runs `device_wall_us` is currently 0 (only L2 single-task runs carry a real device wall) — a benchmark helper should document / handle this.
- Related: #1679, #1155
- Repo HEAD at filing: `05b1b852`

title: docs(ops): correct scatter_mask ISA framing; document mask patterns for gather + scatter
body:
## Summary

Corrects a **codebase-wide inaccurate claim** that mask-pattern *scatter* is a real `pto.tscatter` ISA instruction that "A5 rejects" — and rewrites the operator-doc "Mask patterns" section to cover **both** gather and scatter directions.

### Verified ground truth (pto-isa + PTOAS)

| Form | Reality |
| ---- | ------- |
| Mask-pattern **gather** (`gather_mask`) | A real ISA op — `pto.tgather` maskPattern form, implemented via `MaskSelect`, supported on **A2/A3 and A5** (the `1..7` values match the hardware `VREDUCEv2` pattern modes) |
| Mask-pattern **scatter** (`scatter_mask`) | **Not a distinct ISA instruction on any backend.** pto-isa exposes a `maskPattern` form only for `tgather`; PTOAS `TScatterOp` accepts only the index form `ins(%src, %indexes) outs(%dst)` (no `maskPattern` attribute). `tile.scatter_mask` / `tensor.scatter_mask` are PyPTO **codegen-level** forms lowered to a `pto.tscatter` mask emission. |

So "A5 rejects this form" is not an ISA/hardware limitation — the form is not an ISA instruction at all (and gather-mask actually *does* run on A5).

## What changed (documentation only)

- **Docs (`ir/05-operators.md`, EN + zh-cn):** rewrote the **Mask patterns** section to explain both directions — `gather_mask` *selects & compacts* (`out_cols = cols / stride`, a real ISA op) and `scatter_mask` *places & expands* (`dst_cols = cols * stride`, a PyPTO codegen form). Retitled the gather-only "Output width" table column to a direction-neutral "Stride", added scatter cross-references, and added worked examples for both.
- **Docstrings** (`{ir,language}/op/{tile,tensor}_ops.py`) and **op descriptions** (`src/ir/op/{tile,tensor}_ops/scatter.cpp`): dropped the unsupported "A5 rejects this form" claim and the "Maps to PTOAS `pto.tscatter` mask form" wording.
- **Codegen / conversion comments** (`pto_ops_common.cpp`, `op_conversion_registry.cpp`): fixed an in-file self-contradiction and removed a reference to a non-existent `TScatterMaskImpl` symbol.

All changes are comment / docstring / string-literal only — **no behavioral change**. Verified no test asserts the changed strings; EN/zh-cn stay synchronized and within the 500-line doc limit.

## Deliberately out of scope / follow-up

- `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_scatter.py` (`TestScatterMaskForm`) still pins to `Ascend910B` on the same premise. Its comments and pinning behavior are a coherent unit; correcting the premise needs a runtime check (a behavioral change), so it is left for a separate change.
- Separately worth investigating: the `scatter_mask` codegen emits `pto.tscatter ins(%src, {maskPattern=…})`, which the current PTOAS `TScatterOp` (index-form only) does not parse — so the end-to-end `scatter_mask` path may be non-functional, masked by the hardware-gated ST cases. Tracked for follow-up.

title: feat(codegen): lower Acc->Mat tile.assemble as a converting pto.tmov
body:
## Summary

Lower a cross-space **`Acc→Mat` `tile.assemble`** (a matmul L0C result drained into an L1/Mat scratch) as a **converting `pto.tmov`**, instead of a config-identical `pto.subview`. Previously the subview was always typed from the **source** tile, so an `Acc` (fractal 1024) → `Mat` (fractal 512) assemble tripped `CheckSubviewTileCompat` and `PTOCodegen` aborted. Masked because the existing assemble tests are same-config and `torch_codegen` never exercises `PTOCodegen`.

## Fix

In `MakeTileAssembleCodegenPTO`:

- **Type the `pto.subview` entirely from the result tile** (the base it is a view of). `SubViewOp::verify` requires the view to match its base in element type, address space, *and* the whole `TileBufConfigAttr`; building from the result and overriding only the source's physical window makes every field match by construction — no field-by-field patching, and forward-compatible if the IR ever permits a requantising Acc→Mat. (`CheckSubviewTileCompat` stays strict for every other, pure subview; gate is on the **result** space.)
- **Skip the out-of-window preservation copy for a full-window Acc→Mat insert** (offset 0 and source physical shape == result physical shape). That copy is a dead write the subview `tmov` immediately overwrites, and would otherwise be an unsupported **Mat→Mat** `tmov` (`okPair` has no Mat→Mat). Scoped to the Acc→Mat path so same-config assemble codegen is untouched.
- **Fail loud (`CHECK_SPAN`) on a partial, non-merged Acc→Mat** — its out-of-window copy *is* an unsupported Mat→Mat. This is only reachable when the Mat target is not reused in-place as the result; the Mat-scratch autotiler's in-place iter-arg chain makes `target == result`, dissolving the path (a self-removing guard).
- Preserve `CheckSubviewTileCompat`'s **pad** invariant (`CHECK_SPAN`); the dtype invariant is already enforced upstream by `DeduceTileAssembleType` (`source.dtype == result.dtype`), so no codegen assert is needed.

## Validation

Built the current PTOAS (commit **`e9ef590d`**, 2026-06-24) from source on stock **LLVM/MLIR 19.1.7** (its codegen path needs Huawei's patched LLVM, but the dialect + verifier build on stock MLIR) and ran its verifier on a whole-tile Acc→Mat module:

```
$ pto-verify acc_mat_fullwindow.pto
RESULT: PARSE + VERIFY OK
```

with **no Mat→Mat tmov and no stripping** — the emitted `pto.subview … -> <loc=mat, fractal=512>` + `pto.tmov ins(<loc=acc, fractal=1024>) outs(<mat view>)` is accepted as-is (`TMovOp::isAccToMat` only constrains the Mat dst fractal to 512). PyPTO-only fix; no PTOAS change.

## Scope

**Codegen only** — independent of the M/N direct-store tiling PR and of the Mat-scratch autotiler. Whole-tile Acc→Mat (the representative Mat-scratch drain) is valid and tested; partial-non-merged Acc→Mat is rejected with a clear in-place message and lands with the autotiler's in-place merging in a follow-up. This removes the PTOCodegen/PTOAS lowering blocker; Mat-scratch scheduling, L0C capacity, and whole-function memory-legality remain separate follow-ups.

## Testing

- Positive: full-window Acc→Mat — subview `loc=mat`/`fractal=512`, tmov source `loc=acc`/`fractal=1024`, and **no Mat→Mat pre-copy**.
- Negative: partial non-merged Acc→Mat — rejected with the in-place message.
- Same-config assemble test unchanged (partial, pre-copy retained); full `tests/ut/codegen/` suite passes.

title: feat(runtime): surface RunTiming and add register-once benchmark helper
body:
## Summary

Closes the gap that prevented pypto callers from reusing simpler's
`scene_test --rounds` benchmark mode (issue #1858). pypto's public Worker
received simpler's per-launch `RunTiming` but discarded it on the
register-once path, so the only timed entry was the one-shot
`execute_compiled` (re-pays compile/register every round).

**Phase 1 — surface RunTiming (proposal #1):**
- `ChipWorker.run_timed` / `RegistrationHandle.run_timed` return
  `(outputs, RunTiming)`. `run()` / `__call__` keep their tensor-return
  contract — timing is opt-in. `run()` is refactored to share a private
  `_dispatch` core with `run_timed`.
- `Worker` ABC gains a default `run_timed` that raises a clear error for
  L3+ (no aggregated device wall), so `DistributedWorker` handles surface a
  helpful message instead of `AttributeError`.

**Phase 2 — benchmark helper (proposal #2):**
- `pypto.runtime.benchmark(compiled, args, rounds=, warmup=, platform=,
  device_id=, config=)` registers once, dispatches `warmup+rounds` cheap
  launches via `run_timed`, and returns `BenchmarkStats` (per-launch
  `device_wall_us` samples + min/median/mean/max/stdev). `platform=`/
  `device_id=` and `config=` are mutually exclusive.
- `BenchmarkStats` exposes issue-aligned `device_wall_us_*` / `samples` and
  shorter `device_us_*` names, plus `all_zero_device` for the
  non-`PTO2_PROFILING` / L3 (`device_wall_us == 0`) case.

## Testing
- [x] Unit tests: `tests/ut/runtime/test_run_timing_plumbing.py` (run_timed
      plumbing) and `tests/ut/runtime/test_benchmark.py` (loop / warmup /
      aggregation / kwargs / aliases) — all pass.

title: fix(passes): localize tile.set_validshape operand in SplitVectorKernel
body:
## Problem

A vector-side `pl.tile.set_validshape` inside an `UP_DOWN`/`LEFT_RIGHT` split scope fails PTOAS assembly:

```
'pto.set_validshape' op expects row operand <= shape dim (16)
```

## Root cause

`SplitVectorKernel`'s generic AIV branch (`ProcessStmt`) halves the **result type** of every TileType-producing op, but only adjusts the explicit shape operands of `tile.full`/`tile.create` and `tile.reshape`. `tile.set_validshape`'s row/col operands were left at their full pre-split extent, so on the split axis the operand exceeded the halved physical shape:

```
# after SplitVectorKernel (UP_DOWN, [32,8] -> [16,8] per lane)
set_validshape(s, 32, 4)   # result type [16,..] but row operand still 32  -> 32 > 16
```

`set_validshape` only relabels the valid extent of the *same* tile, so localizing the operand is exactly correct (and matches how `HalveTileShape` already localizes the result type's `valid_shape`).

## Fix

Localize the split-dim valid operand via `LocalizeValidDimForSplit`. `operand_idx = 1 + split_dim` covers both `UP_DOWN` (row) and `LEFT_RIGHT` (col).

## Tests

- **UT** (device-free, `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_split_vector_kernel.py`): before/after structural check — `set_validshape(z_vec, 16, 64)` → `set_validshape(z_vec, 8, 64)`.
- **ST** (`tests/st/runtime/cross_core/test_cross_core_tpush_valid_shape.py`, a2a3): a cross-core kernel calling `set_validshape` on the **vector** side, where the tile is halved.

Full `test_split_vector_kernel.py` (32 tests) passes; both new tests host-compile clean and the emitted `.pto` shows the localized operand (`set_validshape %popped, %c8_index, %c8_index` on a `rows=8` tile).

## Out of scope (follow-up)

`tile.extract` (index_row/col + `shape` kwarg) and `tile.assemble` (offset) have a *related but different* gap in the same branch: they are windowing ops, so "halve the result type + localize one operand" is the wrong model (the explicit `shape`/window must be partition-aware). Pass-level reproduced but deliberately deferred to a separate issue; the generic branch also lacks a fail-loud guard for unhandled split-axis operands.

title: feat(pass): per-kernel windowize=True opt-in for tensor window externalization
body:
## Summary

This is a reduced follow-up to the closed #1844 attempt. Instead of introducing
global windowing policy knobs, this PR adds one explicit IR-level opt-in:
an outlined InCore-type function (`InCore`, `AIC`, or `AIV`) may carry
`windowize = true`, and Pattern 5 in `OptimizeOrchTensors` only considers
functions with that attr.

The Python DSL currently exposes this opt-in through `pl.at(...)`:

```python
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, windowize=True):
    ...
```

Tests, tools, or handwritten DSL/IR may also attach the same function attr
directly:

```python
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore, attrs={"windowize": True})
def kernel(...):
    ...
```

Only outlined InCore-type kernels whose source scope explicitly sets
`windowize=True` are eligible for local tensor window externalization. Kernels
without the attr keep the existing behavior. The transform itself is keyed on
the function attr rather than on `pl.at` specifically, so other frontends or
hand-written IR can use the same attr without adding another pass option.
After lowering, both forms are equivalent because Pattern 5 reads only the
function attr.

The intended review shape is deliberately narrow:

- No global window policy API.
- No default automatic windowization.
- No carrier parameter system.
- No broad codegen/runtime surface change.
- Windowization is reachable only through explicit per-function opt-in.

## What Changed

### API and IR plumbing

- Adds `windowize: bool = False` to `pl.at(...)`.
- Parses `windowize` as a boolean literal.
- Prints `windowize=True` in Python IR round-trips.
- Propagates the scope attr to outlined InCore-type function attrs.
- Also supports direct function attrs such as
  `@pl.function(..., attrs={"windowize": True})` for tests/tools that construct
  IR without going through `pl.at`.

### OptimizeOrchTensors

- Adds an optional Pattern 5 module for local tensor window externalization.
- Skips Pattern 5 entirely unless at least one InCore-type function has
  `windowize=True`.
- Rewrites only explicitly opted-in kernels.
- Uses conservative safety checks before rewriting callsites:
  - materializable tensor view types,
  - dynamic parent/window compatibility,
  - submit ABI argument limits,
  - overlapping/sibling output writers,
  - `Submit` call preservation.
- Leaves unsupported cases on the baseline path instead of partially rewriting
  them.

## Validation

### Unit Tests

```bash
pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_optimize_orch_tensors.py -q
```

Result:

```text
64 passed
```

Coverage includes parser/outliner propagation of `windowize=True`, Python
printer round-trip, default-off behavior, positive windowed rewrites, structural
baseline fallback checks, and submit-aware ABI/safety edge cases.

### Compile-only Smoke Test

I also ran a local compile-only smoke test using
`pypto-lib/models/qwen3/14b/prefill_fwd.py`. The model source was copied to a
temporary report directory before injecting `windowize=True`; `pypto-lib` itself
was not modified.

Generated orchestration:

```text
reports/pypto-window-externalization-v7/local_prefill_compile_check_20260625_170820/
  v7_windowize_prefill_compile_only_clean2/orchestration/prefill_fwd.cpp
```

Result summary:

```text
windowed kernels: 15
.view(...) count: 34
add_inout/add_input/add_output/add_scalar: 31/51/3/54
carrier: 0
runtime_current/barrier: 0
```

The generated C++ contains the expected `__windowed` tasks and `.view(...)`
window arguments for the annotated kernels.

### Hardware Swimlane Evidence

Hardware swimlane measurements were run on Ascend NPU with model-local
`windowize=True` annotations. These annotations are not part of this PR; they
are validation evidence that the explicit opt-in exposes narrower runtime
windows for selected kernels.

| Case | Baseline (us) | v7 windowize (us) | Improvement |
| ---- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `qwen3/14b/prefill_fwd.py` | 9768.78 | 5741.77 | **41.22%** |
| `deepseek/v3_2/deepseek_v3_2_decode_back.py` | 2091.66 | 1760.36 | **15.84%** |
| `deepseek/v4/hc_head.py` | 160.54 | 135.98 | **15.30%** |
| `deepseek/v3_2/deepseek_v3_2_decode_front.py` | 113589.20 | 96718.16 | **14.85%** |

`qwen3/14b/prefill_fwd.py` is the primary evidence. The local runner annotated
15 kernels:

```text
rmsnorm
q_proj
kv_proj
q_norm
k_norm
attention_writeback
out_proj
out_proj_residual
post_rmsnorm
gate_proj
up_proj
silu
down_proj
down_proj_residual
final_rmsnorm
```

All 15 produced `__windowed` clones. The generated orchestration used explicit
local views and kept the submit ABI at:

```text
add_inout/add_input/add_output/add_scalar = 31/51/3/54
```

No carrier parameters and no runtime-current barriers were produced.

`deepseek/v3_2/deepseek_v3_2_decode_back.py` is the clearest DeepSeek swimlane
example: 7 `__windowed` clones, 10 `.view(...)` calls, and visible overlap
improvement in the swimlane.

`deepseek/v4/hc_head.py` is small but clean: 3 `__windowed` clones
(`hc_head_linear`, `hc_head_reduce`, `hc_head_rms`) and a consistent runtime
reduction.

`deepseek/v3_2/deepseek_v3_2_decode_front.py` is a larger supplementary case:
21 `__windowed` clones and a clean end-to-end reduction, though its swimlane is
less visually direct than `decode_back`.

## Notes

- #1844 is closed and should be treated as the previous broader attempt, not as
  the implementation shape of this PR.

title: [Bug] pl.split(UP_DOWN) silently miscompiles a scope containing a row reduction (row_sum) — wrong numerics, no error
body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto** — `pl.split(SplitMode.UP_DOWN)` codegen. A scope whose body contains a row reduction (`pl.row_sum`) compiles cleanly and runs without error but produces WRONG output under UP_DOWN. The same scope with `SplitMode.NONE` is correct. Most likely the split pass fans the reduction's free-axis across the two AIV subblocks, yielding partial sums with no cross-subblock combine. Critically it is NOT rejected at compile time — it silently miscompiles. (Related #1034 / #1820 note split-axis reductions are meant to be *rejected*; this case slips through and corrupts results instead.)

### Description

Repro: per-token row-normalize `y[i,:] = x[i,:] / sum_j x[i,j]`. A tiny dummy matmul is present only to *engage* UP_DOWN (a pure-vector scope does not trigger the split otherwise). `T_TILE=16` so the `[T_TILE,1]` FP32 reduction tile splits to `[8,1]`=32B and does NOT hit the separate col-major 32B-align wall — isolating the reduction bug alone.

On-device (a2a3), comparing each output `y` against torch golden:

| scope | split | `y` result |
|---|---|---|
| direct: `row_sum -> [T,1] -> recip -> row_expand_mul` | NONE | PASS |
| direct (same body) | UP_DOWN | **FAIL (wrong numerics)** |
| reshape: `row_sum -> [1,T] -> recip -> [T,1]` (rms_norm pattern) | NONE | PASS |
| reshape (same body) | UP_DOWN | **FAIL (wrong numerics)** |

Both reduce forms fail under UP_DOWN and pass under NONE → it is the `row_sum` reduction itself, not the reshape.

Minimal self-contained repro (also at `models/deepseek/v4/_tmp_updown_reduce_repro.py` in pypto-lib):

\`\`\`python
import pypto.language as pl

T_TILE, C, NTASK = 16, 512, 8
T = NTASK * T_TILE
MM_M = MM_K = 128 ; MM_N = 32   # dummy-mm dims only

# split mode is the ONLY difference between PASS and FAIL:
#   NONE -> PASS,  UP_DOWN -> FAIL
@pl.jit
def repro(x: pl.Tensor[[T, C], pl.BF16],
          y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[T, C], pl.BF16]],
          dummy_out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[NTASK * MM_M, MM_N], pl.BF16]]):
    for t in pl.spmd(NTASK, optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)]):  # vs NONE
        t0 = t * T_TILE
        acc = pl.matmul(x[0:MM_M, 0:MM_K], x[0:MM_N, 0:MM_K], b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
        dummy_out[t*MM_M:t*MM_M+MM_M, 0:MM_N] = pl.cast(acc, target_type=pl.BF16, mode="rint")
        xc = pl.cast(x[t0:t0+T_TILE, 0:C], target_type=pl.FP32)
        inv = pl.recip(pl.row_sum(xc))            # [T_TILE,1]  <-- reduction
        yc = pl.row_expand_mul(xc, inv)
        y[t0:t0+T_TILE, 0:C] = pl.cast(yc, target_type=pl.BF16, mode="rint")
    return y
\`\`\`

Expected: UP_DOWN either produces correct `y` (combine partial sums across subblocks) or is rejected at compile time. Actual: silent wrong output.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | \`9f31b7e\` |
| pypto | \`c3e362ba\` (branch: \`main\`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | \`95197fd7\` |
| pto-isa | \`1ba8f54b\` (branch: \`main\`) |
| ptoas | \`0.46\` |
| CANN | \`9.0.0\` |

### Host Platform

\`Linux (aarch64)\`

### Additional Context

Related: hw-native-sys/pypto#1034, hw-native-sys/pypto#1820 (split-axis reduction should be rejected), hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#362 (reduction-order drift under split in a matmul scope). Surfaced while testing the dummy-mm→UP_DOWN trick on DeepSeek-V4 decode `rms_norm`; the production hc_pre work already avoids this by keeping `row_sum`/RMS out of split scopes.

title: feat(ir): tile chained-matmul output into an L1/Mat scratch (Mat-scratch AutoTileMatmulL0)
body:
> **📦 Self-contained PR.** This includes the **2 iter-arg inference fixes** (`tile.assemble` TileView-optionality inheritance + `InferTileMemorySpace` inherit-input for loop `IterArg`s — the bottom 2 commits) that the full-K (pipelined) Mat-scratch path requires; without them the loop-carried scratch fails structural verification (`TileView presence mismatch in ForStmt`). These were previously offered separately as [#1868](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/1868), now **closed in favor of this single PR** — cross-fork base-retargeting made the merge-order stack awkward, so the prerequisite fixes are folded in here.

## Summary

Tile an oversized `[M, N]` `tile.matmul` output into an **L1/Mat scratch** (Acc→Mat `tile.assemble`) when the result is consumed **entirely as a matmul operand** (a chained matmul), keeping it on-chip for the consumer instead of round-tripping through DDR. Both grid shapes: **split-K** (unrolled) and **full-K** (pipelined). This is the Mat-scratch placement the `AutoTileMatmulL0` doc previously marked "deferred."

On **A2/A3 (Ascend 910B)** the offset Acc→Mat writeback is a cube **FIXPIPE `pto.tinsert`**, which *requires* an `f32 → bf16/f16` downcast (ptoas rejects same-precision A2/A3 tinsert). So the on-chip scratch is **bf16**, written directly by the cube — no Vector round-trip. On **A5 (Ascend 950)** tinsert accepts `dst=f32`, so the f32 scratch path is kept. The choice is made through a `BackendHandler::RequiresLowPrecisionMatScratch()` query — no arch branch in the pass.

## What it does

- **Consumer detection** — `SiblingUseCounter` counts matmul-operand reads (`tile.matmul` args {0,1}, `matmul_acc` args {1,2}; arg 0 is the accumulator, correctly excluded). `TryFoldMatScratch` selects Mat-scratch when *every* use of the result is a matmul-operand read.
- **bf16 fold** — the autotiler recognizes `c = matmul(a, b, out_dtype=FP32); cb = cast(c, BF16); d = matmul(cb, e)` and folds the cast into the scratch dtype: the `[M, N]` Mat scratch is created as **bf16**, both the result and the cast remap to it, and the now-dead `tile.cast` is dropped.
- **Backend gate** — `RequiresLowPrecisionMatScratch()` returns `true` on 910B (an f32 scratch is left on the deferred path with `PH-AT-007`) and `false` on 950 (f32 scratch kept). No `if (arch == ...)` in the pass.
- **L1-capacity gate** — Mat-scratch is selected only when the packed `[M, N]` scratch fits the backend's Mat/L1 capacity; otherwise the chain stays on the DDR path with a clear hint, instead of overflowing at allocation.
- **`MatScratchPlacer`** — plugs into the `SubtilePlacer` interface; `Init` creates the Mat scratch, `PlaceAt` assembles each sub-tile in place. Both `BuildSplitKGrid` (constant offsets) and `BuildFullKPipelined` (loop-variable offsets) drive it.
- **Codegen** — a bf16/f16 Acc→Mat `tile.assemble` lowers to `pto.tinsert` (`loc=acc,dtype=f32 → loc=mat,dtype=bf16`); the f32 Acc→Mat path falls through to the converting subview + `tmov` (A5). The assemble result aliases the target buffer when memory reuse merged them, so the chain writes one buffer with no Mat→Mat copy.
- **Layout / type** — `DeduceTileAssembleType` permits the `f32→bf16/f16` FIXPIPE downcast and inherits the target's TileView optionality, so the aliased chain shares one Mat NZ operand layout.

## Validation

- **ptoas v0.45 (on-device toolchain)** — both split-K and full-K chained matmuls assemble + verify green; codegen emits real `pto.tinsert` into a bf16 Mat scratch (0 Mat→Mat, 0 Vector cast ops — the downcast is the cube FIXPIPE).
- **Real Ascend 910B (`--platform a2a3`)** — `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_auto_tile_matmul.py` runs the bf16 split-K + full-K chains on hardware: **2 passed**. The golden applies the same `(a@b)→bf16→@e` FIXPIPE rounding and is matched by Frobenius relative error (rtol/atol 2e-2).
- **Unit** — autotiler dispatch (split-K + full-K, K=32) + PTOCodegen e2e (4× `pto.tinsert`, `loc=mat, dtype=bf16`) + numerical (Frobenius rel-err < 5e-2). Full suite: 2856 unit tests pass; ruff clean.

## Example

`examples/kernels/11_auto_tile_matmul.py` — the DDR/Mat × full-K/split-K matrix (`ddr_full_k`, `ddr_split_k`, `mat_full_k`, `mat_split_k`); the `mat_*` kernels exercise the on-chip bf16 scratch chain.

## Commits

1. `fix(ir)` — inherit TileView optionality in `tile.assemble`
2. `fix(ir)` — `InferTileMemorySpace` inherit-input from `IterArg` loop iter-args
3. `feat(ir)` — the Mat-scratch autotiler (consumer detection, `MatScratchPlacer`, split-K + full-K dispatch)
4. `feat(codegen)` — alias in-place Acc→Mat `tile.assemble` result to the target buffer
5. `feat(ir)` — gate Mat-scratch selection on backend Mat/L1 capacity
6. `test(ir)` — full-K Mat-scratch tests exercise true full-K (K=32)
7. `example+st(ir)` — compiler-tiled matmul examples (DDR/Mat × full-K/split-K)
8. `fix(ir)` — lower chained-matmul Mat-scratch as bf16 `pto.tinsert`
9. `docs(st)` — fix Mat-scratch s-test header (910B is the bf16 `pto.tinsert` path)

Rebased onto current `main` (`4946aac7`).

## Remaining (follow-ups, not blockers)

- **Deferred M/N regimes** — `tile.matmul_acc` M/N and a Vec left operand (PV) M/N stay deferred (`PH-AT-006`); orthogonal to placement.
- **Full-window f32 Acc→Mat (fits-L0c) `tmov` path** — the inverse-kernel chained-matmul pattern (cube→cube, no offset, keeps f32) is a separate placement, not covered here.

title: refactor(matmul): zero-copy transpose_view for 2D mixed-kernel + ND batch_matmul
body:
## Summary

Migrate matmul `b_trans`/`a_trans` off the legacy transpose-at-load path onto the zero-copy `tile.transpose_view` model — for both the 2D mixed-kernel case (a Vec compute result feeding a `b_trans` matmul) and ND `tile.batch_matmul` (extends #1776 to ND). The tile-level op is now transpose-agnostic; a transpose is just one extra zero-copy view (no `pto.ttrans` data copy).

**2D (Vec-sourced mixed kernel)**
- A Vec compute result feeding a `b_trans` matmul is moved whole to Mat and reinterpreted by a `tile.transpose_view` over the buffer-less cross-core tpop result (emits `pto.treshape`, no copy), instead of a real per-operand transpose.

**ND `tile.batch_matmul`**
- **convert**: ND operands load natural to Mat + one whole `tile.transpose_view` (drops the `!is_nd` gate and transpose-at-load baking).
- **flatten**: unified per-operand handling — each operand (lhs/rhs, transposed or not, load- or move-sourced) is brought whole into L1 and per-batch sliced (row slice for plain, column slice for `transpose_view`); broadcast reused. A capacity gate (`BatchOperandsWholeFit`) falls back to a per-batch load (+ per-batch `transpose_view`) when the whole operands exceed L1. A natural 3D Mat load (batch>1) collapses its source window to 2D so the hardware ND2NZ path sees a 2-dim GlobalTensor.
- **codegen**: emit a matching 2D `make_tensor_view` for the collapsed load.
- The dead whole load/view is dropped when the per-batch fallback is taken.

**Deprecation** — `refactor(language): deprecate load transpose param`
- `pl.load(..., transpose=True)` now emits a `DeprecationWarning`; the load-time transpose is replaced by `tile.transpose_view`. The parameter still works (`LowerTransposeLoadParamLayout`) and will be removed later.

## Testing

- [x] Full unit-test suite green (`tests/ut/`, 6274 passed).
- [x] NPU (Ascend910B / a2a3) end-to-end: GM `b_trans`/`a_trans` (batch=1, multi-batch, non-aligned N/K), V2C mixed-kernel, broadcast, `matmul_acc`, dsv4 grouped-slice (proj_a), and the `!fit` per-batch path (22 passed).
- [x] Code review + clang-tidy + pre-commit hooks pass.
- [x] Docs updated (pass 15, EN + ZH).

## Related Issues

Extends #1776 (zero-copy `tile.transpose_view`) to the 2D mixed-kernel and ND `tile.batch_matmul` paths.

## Follow-ups (deferred)

A move-sourced (V2C mixed-kernel) operand that does not fit L1 still uses the whole-slice path — correct only while the moved tile fits the fixed cross-core ring; a per-batch V2C move is a follow-up (documented in `BatchOperandsWholeFit`).

title: fix(codegen): source get_subblock_idx from runtime signature param
body:
## Summary

`tile.get_subblock_idx()` previously lowered to a `pto.get_subblock_idx`
instruction (the ccec `get_subblockid()` register). Under the
`tensormap_and_ringbuffer` dispatch that register returns a stale value, and it
was only corrected on dual-AIV paths via the `get_subblockid()` macro bridge —
so non-bridged paths (e.g. a5/950) could read the wrong lane id.

This routes `get_subblock_idx` through the **synthetic signature-parameter**
channel already used by `get_block_idx` / `get_block_num`:

- `PTOCodegen` appends a `%__pypto_spmd_subblock_idx: i32` param to the
  `func.func` signature, and the op lowers to `arith.index_cast` of it (no more
  `pto.get_subblock_idx`).
- The kernel wrapper resolves it from `intrinsic.h::get_sub_block_id(args)` —
  the runtime per-core lane id stored in `GlobalContext.sub_block_id` — and
  forwards it as a trailing call arg.
- Identity params are appended in canonical order `block_idx, block_num,
  subblock_idx`, each gated independently per function on both the C++ emission
  and Python call-forwarding sides.

The `get_subblockid()` macro bridge (`pypto_runtime_subblock_id`) is **retained**
— it serves ptoas-*internal* pipe-slot offsets, which are unrelated to this op
and coexist with the new param (both source the same runtime lane id).

Emitted unconditionally (no `__CPU_SIM` fork) because
`GlobalContext.sub_block_id` is populated by the scheduler on every platform;
`get_sub_block_id(args)` is defined for both a2a3 and a5.

## Testing

- [x] C++ rebuilds clean; full `tests/ut/codegen/` suite passes (473)
- [x] `test_split_vector_kernel`, `test_convert_tensor_to_tile_ops`,
      `test_torch_codegen`, `jit/test_spmd` pass
- [x] Two new tests: MLIR-signature (`%__pypto_spmd_subblock_idx` appended, op
      lowers to `index_cast`, `pto.get_subblock_idx` gone) and wrapper
      (`get_sub_block_id(args)` local + trailing call arg)
- [x] Code review completed; docs (en + zh-cn) updated in sync

title: fix(ir): correct tile.assemble type & memory-space inference for loop iter-args
body:
> **📚 Stack base — merge this first.** [#1865](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/1865) (Mat-scratch `AutoTileMatmulL0`) is built on top of these two fixes. The same two commits sit at the base of #1865's branch (identical patches), so they are reviewed here. Once this PR merges to `main`, #1865's diff automatically reduces to just the Mat-scratch feature. (A true base-retarget stack isn't possible — cross-fork PRs can't point their base at a fork branch.)

## Summary

Two coupled `tile.assemble` type/memory-space **inference** fixes. Both are general correctness fixes (independent of any pass that emits `tile.assemble`); together they unblock `AutoTileMatmulL0`'s **full-K Mat-scratch** path, which threads a Mat scratch through a pipeline loop and assembles Acc sub-tiles into it.

## Fixes

1. **`DeduceTileAssembleType` inherits the target's TileView optionality** (`transform.cpp`). It previously built the struct-default TileView (`row_major/none_box`) even when the target carried an *implicit* view (e.g. a `tile.create`'d Mat scratch, whose effective layout is the Mat NZ implicit). That split a loop-carried assemble chain's type (create: no view vs assemble: default view); once aliased, the layouts collided. Now an implicit-view target yields an implicit-view result.

2. **`InferTileMemorySpace` inherits the input space from an `IterArg` target** (`infer_tile_memory_space.cpp`). `InheritFromInput` used `As<Var>`, which does **not** match an `IterArg` (kind-traits). So an inherit-input op whose first argument is a loop iter-arg — notably `tile.assemble`'s Mat-scratch target — skipped it and fell through to the Acc **source**, forcing the whole scratch chain into Acc (L0c overflow). Fix: seed each TileType iter-arg's space from its init before analysing the body, and match IterArg args via `AsVarLike`.

## Why coupled

The natural trigger — a Mat scratch carried through a loop and assembled into — won't even **parse** without fix 1 (the loop-carried reassignment sees mismatched TileViews), and infers the **wrong memory space** without fix 2.

## Test

`test_assemble_into_mat_iter_arg_keeps_scratch_mat` builds exactly that pattern and asserts the scratch chain stays Mat. It **fails with only fix 1** and passes with both. 2217 transform + codegen tests pass.

title: feat(runtime): support per-ring list config for RunConfig ring sizing
body:
## Summary

Extend the three `RunConfig` ring-sizing overrides — `ring_task_window`, `ring_heap`, `ring_dep_pool` — from `int | None` to `int | list[int] | None`, so callers can size each scope-depth ring independently instead of broadcasting a single value to all of them.

- **Scalar** → broadcast to all 4 rings (unchanged behavior, fully backward compatible).
- **`list[int]` of exactly 4 entries** → sizes rings 0..3 independently. A `0` entry means "leave that ring at its env/compile-time default" (matching the runtime's `value != 0` guard).
- **`None`** → unset (unchanged).

The underlying runtime `RuntimeEnv` binding already accepts both a scalar (broadcast) and a 4-element list, so the shared `_apply_ring_overrides` transcription helper is unchanged — lists flow through to both the L2 and L3 dispatch paths untouched. This lets a multi-program L3 worker dispatch each program with its own ring sizes (e.g. a wider task window for prefill than decode).

## Changes

- `runner.py`: field types → `int | list[int] | None`; `_validate_ring_overrides` validates the scalar-or-list contract (length must be `_RING_DEPTH` = 4; per-entry pow2/range checks; `0` sentinel; rejects bool/float entries). Prior scalar error messages preserved verbatim.
- `distributed_runner.py`: docstrings updated to describe the scalar-or-4-list contract.
- `test_run_config.py`: new coverage for valid lists, the `0` sentinel, wrong lengths, out-of-range entries, non-int (bool/float) entries, and L2/L3 list transcription.

## Testing

- [x] `tests/ut/runtime/test_run_config.py`: 77 passed (incl. all pre-existing scalar tests)
- [x] Verified the real runtime binding accepts a 4-list, broadcasts a scalar, and rejects wrong lengths
- [x] Code review completed (PASS)

title: backend: resolve pl.dynamic dims in the distributed host orchestrator
body:
> Draft / WIP — companion to a still-in-progress DeepSeek V4 packed
> chunked-prefill change in pypto-lib. The fix itself is self-contained, but
> it is gated on that consuming feature and is posted here for review/visibility.

## Problem

The distributed host orchestrator generated for an `@pl.jit.host` wrapper
slices per-rank inputs, e.g.

```python
tensors["x_hc__ssa_v0"][rank, 0:DEEPSEEK_PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, 0:4, 0:4096]
```

When the host function carries `pl.dynamic()` dims, the dim symbol
(`DEEPSEEK_PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN`) is a runtime-only value that is never bound
anywhere in the generated `orchestration/host_orch.py`, so executing the
orchestrator fails with `NameError: name '...DYN' is not defined`.

The device-side codegen already recovers dynamic dims from runtime tensor
shapes (`_append_dynamic_dim_unpacking`); the Python host orchestrator had
no equivalent. No existing distributed kernel combines `@pl.jit.host` with
`pl.dynamic`, so this path was previously untested.

## Fix

Add a post-processing step in `_generate_with_distributed`
(`python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py`) that, for each orchestrator function,
emits at the top of the body — once per dynamic-dim symbol —

```python
<DIM> = tensors["<key>"].shape[<dim>]
```

derived from the first generated slice that uses the symbol (so it is robust
to the symbol's emitted name).

## Scope / risk

- Additive; operates on the generated host-orchestration source string.
- No-op when the orchestrator has no `pl.dynamic()` dims (the common case),
  so existing distributed kernels are unaffected.

## Validation

Built locally; the generated `host_orch.py` now defines the dynamic dims and
the distributed program dispatches across ranks. Exercised end-to-end by the
companion pypto-lib packed chunked-prefill kernel on a2a3 (2-card EP2).

title: feat(distributed): wire DFX diagnostics into the L3 dispatch path
body:
## Summary

The single-chip (L2) path drives all five runtime DFX diagnostics, but the L3
`DistributedWorker` path silently dropped them. This wires DFX through the L3
dispatch so all five work per rank, isolated per chip:

- **Driver** (`_make_call_config`): thread `enable_dump_tensor` / `enable_pmu` /
  `enable_dep_gen` / `enable_scope_stats` / `enable_l2_swimlane` + `output_prefix`
  from the per-dispatch `RunConfig` onto the shared `CallConfig`.
- **Codegen** (`distributed_codegen.cpp`): route each rank-pinned (`device=r`)
  chip dispatch through a new `_submit_chip` helper that namespaces the DFX
  `output_prefix` per rank (`<base>/rank{worker}`), so per-chip artifacts
  (`pmu.csv`, `deps.json`, `l2_swimlane_records.json`, …) don't overwrite each
  other. The comm-less single-dispatch path is byte-compatible (bare
  `submit_next_level`).
- **Swimlane**: enabled on L3 and run as a clean **two-pass** dispatch on the
  one-shot path (pass 1 dep_gen → `deps.json`, pass 2 swimlane → records with
  unperturbed timing), then converted per rank to `merged_swimlane_*.json`. Each
  pass re-forks the chip workers, so the per-pass DFX collectors (resident in the
  forked children) get clean SVM state — no `halHostRegister` cap (rc 8), so
  unlike the in-process L2 path no subprocess is needed.

Commits:
1. `wire DFX diagnostics into the L3 dispatch path` (Phase 1+2)
2. `support L2 swimlane on the L3 dispatch path` (Phase 3, single-pass)
3. `run L3 swimlane as a clean two-pass dispatch` (Phase 3 follow-up)

## Testing

- Unit: `tests/ut/runtime/test_run_config.py`, `test_distributed_worker.py`
  (DFX flag wiring, `_submit_chip` suffix/restore, swimlane co-enable) — 120 passed.
- ST: `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_dfx_per_rank.py` (per-rank DFX dirs +
  swimlane), sim + onboard a2a3.
- Onboard a2a3: per-rank ST (2/4 dev) and the real DeepSeek-V4 MoE (`--ep 4`,
  HCCL dispatch/combine) pass for `dep_gen` / `scope_stats` / `l2_swimlane`,
  with the two passes surviving HCCL teardown/re-init and producing clean
  per-rank `merged_swimlane_*.json`.

Note: DFX collection on comm-heavy L3 models adds tasks/deps to the rings, so
size them up via `PTO2_RING_*` / `RunConfig.ring_*` (the per-task ring overrides
this branch already plumbs through L3).

title: [Code Health] Resolve pl.dynamic dims generally in distributed host orchestration codegen (replace regex post-process)

labels.name: code health
labels.description: Technical debt, robustness concerns, code quality improvements

body:
### Category

Robustness (potential edge-case failure)

### Component

Codegen

### Description

**Problem (general — not specific to any model).** The native C++ `DistributedCodegen` lowers every HOST orchestrator (`@pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)`) into Python (`orchestration/host_orch.py`). When that host function carries `pl.dynamic()` dimensions that flow into **host-side per-rank tensor slicing**, the generated code references the dynamic-dim *symbol* but never binds it anywhere in the emitted module, so executing the orchestrator raises `NameError` at runtime. This affects **any** distributed HOST orchestrator that slices with a dynamic dim — DeepSeek packed prefill is merely the case that first exercised it.

Two manifestations of the **same** root cause:

1. **Tensor-shape-derived dim** (e.g. packed / chunked prefill):

   ```python
   tensors["x__ssa_v0"][rank, 0:PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, 0:4, 0:4096]
   #                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ never bound -> NameError
   ```

   The value is recoverable from a runtime tensor shape (`tensors["x"].shape[1]`).

2. **Composite / world_size-derived dim** (see #1803, an allgather mesh):

   ```python
   tensors["out__ssa_v0"][r, 0:1, 0:(NR * 64)]   # NR = pl.dynamic("NR")
   #                                  ^^ never bound -> NameError
   ```

   Here the symbol appears inside an affine/composite expression, and the natural binding is `NR = world_size` — a comm-domain quantity the orchestrator already knows.

**Why it matters.** The device-side codegen already solves the equivalent problem *generally*: `_append_dynamic_dim_unpacking` walks each tensor param's shape, collects dynamic-dim Vars via the C++ helper `collect_vars_from_shape_expr`, and inverts affine forms (`var`, `var±c`, `var*c`, `var//c`) back into a runtime value (`_invert_shape_dim_for_var`). The host-orchestration path has no equivalent, so a whole class of otherwise-valid distributed programs silently fails at runtime.

### Minimal Reproduction

The bug reproduces on a clean `origin/main`. The smallest trigger is a HOST orchestrator that slices a per-rank sub-tensor whose **slice bound uses a `pl.dynamic` dim**:

```python
import pypto.language as pl
from pypto import ir
from pypto.ir.distributed_compiled_program import DistributedConfig

M = pl.dynamic("M")            # runtime-only dynamic dim
N = pl.dynamic("N")
NRANKS = 2

@pl.program
class L3DynSliceRepro:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def add_one(self, x: pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32],
                y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]:
        return pl.store(pl.add(pl.load(x, [0, 0], [128, 128]), 1.0), [0, 0], y)

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
    def chip(self, x: pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32],
             y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]:
        return self.add_one(x, y)

    @pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
    def host_orch(self, x: pl.Tensor[[NRANKS, M, N], pl.FP32],
                  y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[NRANKS, M, N], pl.FP32]]):
        # Per-rank host slice whose stop bound uses the dynamic dim M:
        for r in pl.range(NRANKS):
            self.chip(x[r, 0:M, 0:N], y[r, 0:M, 0:N], device=r)

compiled = ir.compile(
    L3DynSliceRepro,
    platform=...,                                  # a2a3 / 910B
    distributed_config=DistributedConfig(device_ids=[0, 1], num_sub_workers=0),
)
```

The generated `orchestration/host_orch.py` contains a slice that references `M` without ever binding it:

```python
for r in range(0, NRANKS, 1):
    tensors["y__ssa_v0"][r, 0:M, 0:N] = ...   # NameError: name 'M' is not defined
```

This is a one-line delta from the **passing** upstream baseline `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_composite_shape_dim.py`, whose own docstring notes it carries the dynamic dim **only in parameter types** and does **no per-rank slicing** — which is exactly why it does not hit this path. #1803 carries a confirmed end-to-end runnable repro of the composite (`NR * SIZE`) form; its actual failure is:

```text
tensors["t__tmp_v3"] = tensors["outputs__ssa_v0"][r__idx_v0, 0:1, 0:(NR * 64)]
                                                                      ^^
NameError: name 'NR' is not defined
```

The host-side per-rank slice form follows `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_rank_slice_dispatch.py` (`for r in pl.range(...): self.child(x[r], ...)`); the only addition here is a **dynamic** dim in the slice bound.

### Current Workaround (to be replaced)

PR #1871 papers over manifestation (1) only, with a regex post-process over the *generated source string* (`_resolve_host_orch_dynamic_dims`, added by that PR — **not on `main`**). For a foundational repo this is fragile:

- It parses generated Python text, so it is coupled to the exact codegen output format and silently no-ops (→ the `NameError` returns) if that format ever changes.
- Its pattern matches only `^0:<symbol>$`, so it cannot handle composite slices like `0:(NR * 64)` (#1803) or non-zero slice starts.
- It recovers only from tensor shapes; it has no notion of world_size / comm-domain-derived dims.
- It lives in the backend post-processing layer, not at the codegen source where the IR — and therefore the param→dim and comm-domain mappings — is directly available.

### Location

Proper-fix site (where `host_orch.py` is emitted), on `origin/main`:

- `src/codegen/distributed/distributed_codegen.cpp:263` — `DistributedCodegen::EmitFunction` (emits the signature, then `RegisterParamsAndEmitScalarBindings(func)` at `:293`, then visits the body at `:313`). The dynamic-dim recovery preamble should be emitted here for HOST orchestrators.
- `src/codegen/distributed/distributed_codegen.cpp:347` — `GetCommSlotSizeAsCode`, i.e. world_size / comm-domain quantities are already resolved at this layer.

Device-side reference to mirror, on `origin/main`:

- `python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py:346` — `_append_dynamic_dim_unpacking`
- `python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py:319` — `_invert_shape_dim_for_var` (affine inversion)
- `python/bindings/modules/codegen.cpp:101` — `collect_vars_from_shape_expr` (C++ helper, already bound; callable directly from C++)

Interim stopgap to remove once codegen emits the preamble: `_resolve_host_orch_dynamic_dims` in `python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py` (lives on PR #1871's branch only).

### Proposed Fix

Emit the dynamic-dim recovery preamble directly in `DistributedCodegen` for HOST orchestrators, driven by the IR (not by parsing generated text), covering all forms:

1. In `EmitFunction` (host-orch path), after `RegisterParamsAndEmitScalarBindings`, walk `func->params_`. For each `TensorType` param, for each shape dim, collect dynamic-dim Vars with the existing `collect_vars_from_shape_expr` — the **same** helper the device side uses, so host and device stay in lockstep by construction.
2. For each dynamic-dim Var, emit one binding at the top of the body:
   - bare tensor dim → `<DIM> = tensors["<param>"].shape[<dim>]`
   - affine/composite of a tensor dim (`var*c`, `var±c`, `var//c`) → invert it the same way `_invert_shape_dim_for_var` does (e.g. `(tensors["<param>"].shape[<dim>]) // c`)
   - dims that are comm-domain / world_size quantities (e.g. `NR`, #1803) → bind from the orchestrator's `world_size` / comm-domain info already available at this layer, rather than from a tensor shape.
3. Dedup across params by `Var.unique_id` (as the device side already does), preferring an invertible source when a symbol appears in multiple dims.
4. Remove the `_resolve_host_orch_dynamic_dims` regex post-process once the codegen emits the preamble.

This subsumes #1803 (composite `NR * SIZE`) and supersedes #1871's stopgap with a single, format-independent mechanism. No public API / IR change — internal codegen output only — so no Python binding or type-stub change is required; it needs a C++ rebuild and a regression test for HOST-orchestrator + `pl.dynamic` codegen (assert the preamble is emitted and the dynamic symbol is no longer a free name).

**Related:** #1803 (concrete composite-dim failure this would fix), #1871 (interim regex stopgap this would replace).

### Priority

Medium (minor risk, should fix in next few releases)

title: feat(ops): add row/col argmax/argmin reductions (tile + tensor)
body:
## What

Add `row_argmax` / `row_argmin` / `col_argmax` / `col_argmin` across all layers (C++ tile + tensor, IR/DSL wrappers, unified dispatch, codegen, tensor→tile conversion, UT, a2a3 ST, docs), mapping to `pto.trowargmax` / `pto.trowargmin` / `pto.tcolargmax` / `pto.tcolargmin`.

Each op takes `(src, tmp)` and produces an **int32 index** tile:
- row variants reduce the last axis → `[M, 1]` (column index of the per-row extremum)
- col variants reduce axis 0 → `[1, N]` (row index of the per-column extremum)

## Notes

- Output dtype is **int32**, not the source dtype — implemented via an `out_dtype` override on the shared reduction deducers (DRY, no new deduce functions).
- All four require a **tmp scratch tile**, including the column variants (unlike `col_max`/`col_min` which are 1-arg).
- The tensor→tile conversion sizes the tmp tile **exactly like the source**. Unlike the `row_sum`-style scratch, the tmp last dim must **not** be padded to 128 — the column argmax reads the column count from the tmp/src extent, so a wider tmp returns the last-row index for every column.
- `kSimpleOps` codegen entries + `SplitVectorKernel` reduce-axis guard added for the four new ops.

## Testing

- Unit tests: tile op, tensor op (int32 output + shape), and tensor→tile conversion (tmp injection).
- System tests (`tests/st/runtime/ops/test_argmax_reduction.py`): row/col × argmax/argmin, FP32 + FP16 src, tile + tensor level.
- **Verified on real a2a3 hardware — all ST cases pass.**

title: feat(distributed): isolate L3 DFX artifacts per dispatch, not per card
body:
## Summary

L3 distributed DFX artifacts were namespaced only by card (`rank{worker}`). When one card receives **multiple L2 dispatches** in a single `host_orch` run — pipeline stages, expert kernels, or different chip programs all pinned to the same `device` — the runtime re-inits and finalizes its per-run collector to a **fixed filename** each dispatch (`pmu.csv`, `deps.json`, `l2_swimlane_records.json`), so every dispatch but the last was silently overwritten.

This change namespaces by card **and** the card's k-th dispatch: `rank{worker}/d{k}`.

- **Counter lifecycle:** the per-card dispatch counter lives on `orch`, reset at the top of every run in `_dispatch.orch_fn`. Both dispatch paths (one-shot `execute_distributed` and the reused `DistributedWorker.run()`) route through `_dispatch`, so it resets per run. The swimlane two-pass reissues dispatches in the same order after the reset, so pass 1 (`deps.json`) and pass 2 (records) land in the same `d{k}` dir for the converter to join.
- **`_submit_chip`:** appends `/rank{worker}/d{k}` to `output_prefix` for the submit, then restores (safe — `submit_next_level` copies the `CallConfig` synchronously). DFX-off and unconstrained (`worker < 0`) dispatches are forwarded unchanged.
- **`_collect_l3_swimlane`:** scans `rank{r}/d*/` subdirs and converts each independently (3.10-safe `glob("d*") + is_dir()`).
- Docstrings updated across `distributed_runner.py` and `distributed_compiled_program.py` to the new `rank{r}/d{k}/` layout.

Pure-Python runtime change — no codegen / C++ touched.

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests (122 passed): adds `test_multiple_dispatches_same_card_get_distinct_dirs` (the bug this fixes) and `test_counter_resets_when_orch_dispatch_idx_cleared` (two-pass reset semantics); existing `TestSubmitChip` / DFX-wiring updated to the `d{k}` layout.
- [x] ST `test_l3_dfx_per_rank.py` updated to expect `rank{r}/d0/`.
- [x] Sim probe: two dispatches to one card produce separate `rank0/d0/` and `rank0/d1/` records (no overwrite).
- [x] **a2a3 hardware — deepseek/v4 `moe` ep4** (one dispatch/card): `x_next` PASS, artifacts under `rank{r}/d0/` with `merged_swimlane`.
- [x] **a2a3 hardware — deepseek/v4 `decode_fwd` ep2** (multiple dispatches/card): PASS, `rank{r}/d0` **and** `rank{r}/d1` each with a separate `merged_swimlane` — the real multi-dispatch case that previously overwrote.
- [x] Code review completed.
