title: feat(backend): complete codegen for tile.col_expand_div / col_expand_sub
body:
## What

`tile.col_expand_div` and `tile.col_expand_sub` (column-broadcast arithmetic) had complete front-end support — C++ op + type deducer, Python IR, DSL, `tensor.* → tile.*` conversion, `torch_codegen`, and front-end UTs — but **no device codegen**, so any kernel using them failed to assemble. This completes the codegen and adds the missing tests.

## Changes

- **`pto_ops_common.cpp`**
  - Register both ops in `kSimpleOps` (`tile.col_expand_div → pto.tcolexpanddiv`, `tile.col_expand_sub → pto.tcolexpandsub`, arity 2).
  - Add them to the col-expand subview eager-materialization set in `MakeNaryCodegenPTO`, matching the existing `mul/add/max/min/expdif` handling (these ops can't consume a `pto.subview` operand).
- **`canonicalize_tile_slice_pass.cpp`** — align `IsColExpandMaterializingOp` with the codegen materialization set. It previously listed only `col_expand_mul/add`, so a dynamic-offset Vec `tile.slice` feeding `div/sub/max/min/expdif` was not rewritten to a fresh `tile.extract` and could re-trigger the #1640 source-aliasing hazard.

## Tests

- **UT** (`test_pto_codegen_ops.py`): div/sub lowering assertions + the #1640 slice-materialization regression extended to div/sub. Full UT suite (201) green locally.
- **ST** (`test_col_expand_arith.py`, new): tile + tensor tracks, full and narrowed `valid_shape` (both/rows/cols), FP32 + FP16. **12 cases, all PASS on real a2a3 hardware** (device run, 36.3s).
- Status doc updated.

title: [Code Health] Restore real per-run timing (RunTiming) via [STRACE] markers after runtime PR #1177

labels.name: code health
labels.description: Technical debt, robustness concerns, code quality improvements

body:
### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Python Bindings

### Description

The runtime submodule was bumped from `09f1546f` to `393d0211`. Runtime PR #1177 (`feat(dfx): [STRACE] host/device timing markers; single source of truth`) is an explicitly **BREAKING** change:

- `simpler.Worker.run` / `run_prepared` / `ChipWorker::run` now return `None`.
- The native `RunTiming` nanobind type and the `PtoRunTiming` C-ABI struct (+ `out_timing` param) were removed.
- Per-stage run timing (host wall, on-NPU device wall + AICPU phase breakdown) is now emitted as `[STRACE]` log markers and parsed offline via `simpler_setup.tools.strace_timing` (runtime `docs/dfx/host-trace.md`).

**Stopgap already in place** (landed with the submodule bump): pypto defines a *zeroed* `RunTiming` shim dataclass in `python/pypto/runtime/task_interface.py` (`host_wall_us=0.0`, `device_wall_us=0.0`). The dispatch layers call `run()` and then return `RunTiming()` so the public contract keeps working — but **all timing values are now `0.0` / meaningless**. This unblocks the import/runtime break without restoring real numbers.

This issue tracks the real migration: consume the `[STRACE]` markers so `RunTiming` carries actual host/device wall times again, restoring the functionality from #1679 (timing plumbing) and #1858 (register-once benchmark).

Related: #1679, #1858

### Location

Stopgap shim and the dispatch points that need real timing wired in:

- `python/pypto/runtime/task_interface.py` — zeroed `RunTiming` dataclass shim
- `python/pypto/runtime/worker.py` — `ChipWorker._run_chip` / `run_timed` (returns `RunTiming()` shim)
- `python/pypto/runtime/device_runner.py` — `execute_on_device` one-shot `Worker` path
- `python/pypto/runtime/distributed_runner.py` — `_dispatch` (L3)
- `python/pypto/runtime/bench.py` — `benchmark` aggregates `run_timed().device_wall_us` (currently always `0.0`; `is_profiling_disabled()` heuristic may need revisiting)

On-device ST tests still asserting real timing (require hardware; not adapted in the stopgap):

- `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_run_timing.py`
- `tests/st/distributed/test_l2_multi_orch.py`
- `tests/st/runtime/framework_and_models/test_run_timing_st.py`
- `tests/st/harness/core/test_runner.py`

### Proposed Fix

1. Parse `[STRACE]` markers via `simpler_setup.tools.strace_timing` into a pypto `RunTiming` with real `host_wall_us` / `device_wall_us`.
2. Wire that into `ChipWorker._run_chip` / `run_timed`, `device_runner.execute_on_device`, and `distributed_runner._dispatch` instead of the zeroed shim.
3. Make `pypto.runtime.bench.benchmark` read the real numbers; revisit `is_profiling_disabled()`.
4. Re-enable / fix the on-device ST tests listed above.
5. Clean up the stopgap shim once real timing is plumbed (or keep the dataclass but populate it).

### Priority

Low (no impact today, good to fix eventually)

title: feat(ops): add class-A tile/tensor ops a2a3 ST; fix expands/sels codegen; configurable ptoas timeout
body:
## Summary

Add a2a3 system tests for a batch of "class A" tile/tensor ops that had front-end + codegen but no dedicated ST, and fix two genuine codegen/deducer defects that the device runs surfaced.

**New ST (all validated on real a2a3):** `div`/`divs`, `log`, `adds`, `subs`, `expands`, `row_min`, `row_expand_add`, `sels`, and `mrgsort` 3-way/4-way (added to `test_sort.py`). Each op gets tile + tensor coverage where applicable, scalar/dtype sweeps, and narrowed `valid_shape` cases on the tile path.

## Codegen / deducer fixes (surfaced by the device runs)

- **`tile.expands` deducer**: output dtype now follows the target tile instead of promoting against the scalar. The old `PromoteDataTypes(tile, scalar)` widened FP16 tile + FP32 scalar → FP32, breaking the `pto.tstore` src/dst bitwidth match on A2/A3.
- **`MakeFullCodegenPTO`**: re-emit the `texpands` scalar constant at the dst tile dtype, so `pto.texpands` sees `scalar type == dst element type` (FP16 was emitting an `f32` scalar into an `f16` tile).
- **Register `tile.expands` PTO codegen** (reuses the `texpands` path) — it was previously an orphan with no `f_codegen`, so `tensor.expands → tile.expands` lowering would have crashed codegen.
- **Redefine `tile.sels`** to the real TSELS semantics `(mask, src, tmp, scalar) -> dst = mask ? src : scalar`, replacing the bogus `(lhs, rhs, select_mode)` promote form. Updates the C++ deducer + codegen, IR/DSL wrappers, debug `torch_codegen`, UT, and en/zh operation-reference docs.

## Testing

- All new ST **pass on real a2a3** (final consolidated run: 120 passed, 1 skipped).
- `tile_ops` UT updated for the new `sels(mask, src, tmp, scalar)` form; UT green.
- Tensor-level `div`/`log` tests use full-shape configs only (tensor ops have no per-tile `valid_shape`).
- `test_sels_int32` is skipped pending a fix to integer `cmps` scalar codegen (the mask builder emits the integer threshold as MLIR `index` instead of the tile dtype; pre-existing and unrelated to `tile.sels` — integer `cmps` has never been ST-covered).

## Notes

`docs/zh-cn/dev/ptoas-op-status.md` updated to mark these ops as ST-covered.

title: [Feature] In-kernel put-fence / TPUT-quiesce primitive to enable multi-core parallelized cross-rank push (combine_push / dispatch)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### Summary

The MoE `combine_push` (and the symmetric `dispatch` payload push) in the DeepSeek-V4 kernels is a **serial, put-issue-bound** task that **cannot be parallelized across cores today** because pypto has no in-kernel primitive to guarantee a rank's outbound `TPUT`s have **landed at the peer** before a subsequent cross-rank `notify`.

We need either:
- **(A)** an in-kernel **put-fence / TPUT-quiesce** op (per-rank drain of outbound TPUTs), usable mid-kernel between a multi-core push scope and a single-core barrier scope; and/or
- **(B)** formal support + validation for a **multi-core `pl.spmd` cross-rank `pld.tensor.put` followed by a `deps`-ordered single-core `notify`/`wait` barrier**, with the semantics that the `deps` edge implies remote-landing (not just task-completion).

### Motivation / Use Case

`combine_push` (`pypto-lib/models/deepseek/v4/combine.py:92-153`) is one `pl.at(CORE_GROUP)` serial task: one scalar core builds ~48 scattered `pld.tensor.put` descriptors (~0.5 us each), then a cross-rank `combine_done` `notify`/`wait` barrier. Measured **~24 us** on a2a3 EP=2, and **during its window all 71 other cores are idle**.

It is **put-ISSUE-bound, not transfer-bound**:
- 384 KB / 24 us = **16 GB/s ≈ 17% of the ~96 GB/s link (6× headroom)** — a transfer-bound kernel would sit near peak.
- 24 us / 48 puts ≈ **0.5 us/put** = one scalar core serially building scatter descriptors. Scattered `dst_offsets=[r_route, 0]` forbid coalescing, so each row is its own descriptor.

The hardware **already supports parallel issue**: each core's TPUT selects `channelGroupIdx = get_block_idx()` → its **own** SDMA SQ/CQ among `kSdmaMaxChannel = 48` channels. Distributing the put-issue across the idle cores would cut `combine_push` to a **~5-6 us floor** (transfer + barrier), saving **~16-18 us per call**. Because it is on the **fully-serial MoE tail**, that converts **1:1 to wall-clock** and **multiplies across the model's MoE layers** per decode step.

### Proposed API / Behavior

**Option A — explicit in-kernel put-fence** (preferred; minimal new surface):

```python
with pl.spmd(EP_WORLD_SIZE * N_LOCAL_EXPERTS, name_hint="combine_push") as push_tid:
    bucket = pl.tile.get_block_idx()
    ...                                  # each core issues its own bucket's puts on its own SDMA channel
    pld.tensor.put(dst=routed_y_buf, peer=dst, src=recv_y_flat, ...)

with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, deps=[push_tid], name_hint="combine_done") as barrier_tid:
    pld.system.put_fence()               # NEW: block until ALL of this rank's outbound TPUTs have LANDED at peers
    pld.system.notify(target=combine_done, ...)   # now guaranteed to follow the data
    pld.system.wait(signal=combine_done, ...)
```

**Option B — make `deps` imply TPUT-landing:** define that a scope with `deps=[push_tid]`, where `push_tid` issued cross-rank puts, is guaranteed to start only after `push_tid`'s outbound TPUTs have **landed** (not merely been issued to SDMA), and add an ST test mirroring this `combine_push` pattern.

Either way the deliverable is: a kernel author can split put-issue across cores and still get correct cross-rank ordering before the done-`notify`.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Flat static-bound form** (serial route-table build + `pl.spmd` over `N_ROUTES` with a per-lane mask): retires the dynamic-loop-bound `507018` class, but keeps the **same push/barrier split** → same cross-core ordering hazard → expected to deadlock identically. Not a fix.
- **Per-expert streaming** (push inside `expert_routed`'s per-expert `pl.parallel` to hide under the expert cloud): needs the **exact same** cross-core put→notify ordering guarantee plus an all-experts join, with larger blast radius — strictly worse than fixing the primitive.
- **Keep push+notify atomic (status quo):** correct, but leaves ~16-18 us/layer of put-issue serialized on one core with 71 cores idle.

### Additional Context

**Empirical result.** We implemented the 3-scope split (`with pl.spmd(EP*N_LOCAL) as push_tid` → `pl.at(CORE_GROUP, deps=[push_tid])` barrier → `pl.spmd(deps=[barrier_tid])` reduce, capture-form with `pl.tile.get_block_idx()`). It **compiles**, but on **a2a3 EP=2 it DEADLOCKS (300 s timeout, killed)** on the first run. This multi-core cross-rank put + `deps`-separated barrier pattern is **not exercised anywhere** in pypto tests.

**Why it breaks.** The current code deliberately keeps the structure atomic — `combine.py:88`: *"keep TPUT + notify/wait in one atomic task"*. In one `InCore` task, the puts and the `notify` share the **same SDMA channel + program order**, so the `notify` is guaranteed to follow the puts. After the split, the barrier's `notify` runs on a **different** SDMA channel than the puts (`channelGroupIdx = get_block_idx()`), with **no hardware ordering** between this rank's puts-landing and its notify-to-peer. `deps=[push_tid]` only guarantees **task-completion** of the push scope, **not remote-landing** of its TPUTs. There is no in-kernel "drain my outbound TPUTs" primitive (`comm_barrier` is host-side all-rank, unusable mid-kernel).

**Hardware path references:** per-core channel selection `channelGroupIdx = get_block_idx()` (`pto-isa .../comm/async/sdma/sdma_async_intrin.hpp:514-532`), `kSdmaMaxChannel = 48` (`sdma_types.hpp:30`); TPUT emit is `pto.barrier<PIPE_ALL>` + `pto.comm.tput` with **no** post-put completion/quiesce barrier (`src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp:2913-2919`).

**Affected kernels:** `pypto-lib/models/deepseek/v4/combine.py:92-153` (combine_push), `dispatch.py:209-235` (symmetric payload push).

**Versions:** pypto `55fdd38` (main), pypto-lib `1a23bd3`. Target: a2a3 EP=2. Blocks a measured **~16-18 us/layer** MoE-tail win.

title: fix(runtime): make `CoreCallable.build` `arg_index` optional for simpler #1181
body:
### Problem
The runtime's #1181 ("replace `arg_index` with positional dump + func_id array")
removed the `arg_index` parameter from `CoreCallable.build` — the binding is now
`build(signature, binary)`. pypto unconditionally passes `arg_index=…`, so
against #1181+ runtimes it fails with:

`TypeError: build(): incompatible function arguments` (unexpected `arg_index`)

This breaks running pypto on current simpler `main`. Dropping `arg_index`
outright isn't an option either: pre-#1181 runtimes (including the pinned one)
**require** it parallel to `signature`.

### Fix
Feature-detect `arg_index` support once from the nanobind signature
(`CoreCallable.build.__doc__`) and pass it only when accepted, via a small
`_build_core_callable` helper shared by both kernel-compile paths in
`compile_and_assemble` (`python/pypto/runtime/device_runner.py`).

pypto now drives **both** runtime generations with no pin bump:
- pre-#1181 runtimes (e.g. the current pinned `runtime`): `arg_index` passed (identity slot map when the kernel config omits it).
- #1181+ runtimes (current simpler `main`): `arg_index` omitted.

### Testing
- `qwen3-14b` `decode_layer.py -p a2a3` compiles, runs, and validates **PASS**
  against current simpler `main` (post-#1181).
- The pinned (pre-#1181) runtime path is unchanged and still works.
- `ruff` clean.

### Notes
No public API change; no pin bump. One-file change in
`pypto/runtime/device_runner.py`.

title: [Feature] AllocateMemoryAddr: liveness-aware offset-packing for differently-shaped disjoint-lifetime L0 buffers
body:
### Summary

`AllocateMemoryAddr` (`src/ir/transforms/allocate_memory_addr_pass.cpp`) is a pure **bump allocator**: it gives each `MemoryReuse` base-Ptr group its own non-overlapping address range (`current_addr = AlignAddress(current_addr + slot_size, space)` per group) with no awareness of cross-group lifetime disjointness, and **never subdivides a freed region**. Replace it with **liveness-aware offset-packing** — place each buffer at the lowest offset free for its *entire lifetime* (first-fit-by-lifetime / interval coloring) — so a freed region can host differently-shaped, lifetime-disjoint co-live buffers.

### Motivation / Use Case

Surfaced by the roofline-chooser work (AutoTileMatmulL0 operand-stationary + Mat-scratch chained matmuls). A chained matmul `(a@b)@c` kept on-chip in an L1/Mat scratch is **fully sequential** — the producer computes `d` into L1, then the consumer reads `d` from L1 — so the producer's L0A operand buffer and the consumer's L0A double-buffers are used in sequence and *should* reuse the same space (peak 64 KB).

But when the producer is **A-stationary** (one monolithic 64 KB held-A buffer) and the consumer is **double-buffered** (two 32 KB buffers), MemoryReuse reuses the producer's 64 KB buffer for *one* of the consumer's 32 KB buffers (wasting 32 KB) and allocates a *fresh* 32 KB for the other → `64 + 32 = 96 KB > 64 KB` L0A → **overflow**. The freed 64 KB region cannot be re-subdivided into the consumer's `2×32 KB`.

The current workaround (in the roofline-chooser PR) constrains chained-matmul (Mat-scratch) producers to **output-stationary** so their buffer shapes match the consumer's double-buffer and pack. That gives up A/B-stationary for chained producers. Offset-packing would **retire the workaround** and is **symmetric** — it fixes producer-A-stationary, consumer-A-stationary, and fragmentation alike.

### Proposed API / Behavior

In `AllocateMemoryAddr`, replace the per-group bump with **first-fit-by-lifetime**: compute each base-Ptr group's lifetime interval (the union of its members' `[def, last_use]` from `MemoryReuse`), then place each group at the lowest offset where `[off, off+slot_size)` is free for that group's whole lifetime. PTOAS's own `PlanMemory` already does this (it splits a freed region into `head | e | tail`); pypto's allocator does not.

### Additional Context

- **Repro:** a chained matmul producer `256x256x128` (A-stationary) feeding a consumer → the full Default pipeline raises `Left buffer usage 98304 bytes exceeds platform limit (65536 bytes)` at `AllocateMemoryAddr`.
- **Avoided in tests today:** `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_auto_tile_matmul_l0.py::test_chained_matmul_uses_mat_scratch` deliberately uses dims (`256x256x256`) where the chooser picks output-stationary for both matmuls so their L0 buffers pack.
- **Documented as a follow-up** in `docs/en/dev/passes/14-auto_tile_matmul_l0.md` (the Mat-scratch placement section).
- This is part of the broader pypto/PTOAS memory-planning rework.

Related: #1475 (a *different* MemoryReuse problem — over-aggressive reuse introducing a WAR hazard that serializes independent matmuls; this issue is the orthogonal offset-assignment/packing gap).

title: fix(ir): repoint cross-half GM tensor refs to base param in ExpandMixedKernel
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1894. Fixes a PTO codegen crash — `Tensor view not found for parameter: <t>__phi_v<N>` (also `__rv_v<N>` / `__tile`) at `pto_codegen.cpp` `GetOrCreateTensorView` — when a GM tensor is written on one lane of a mixed `pl.split_aiv` InCore function and consumed on the other lane (e.g. a vector `tile.store` producer feeding a cube `matmul` consumer, across a `pl.system.syncall`).

**Root cause.** `ExpandMixedKernel` splits a mixed function into `_aic` and `_aiv` siblings whose params come only from `func->params_`. A GM write on the producing lane yields a fresh SSA *version* of the tensor — straight-line `<t>__tile` (tile.store result), loop `<t>__rv` (ForStmt return_var), or conditional `<t>__phi` (IfStmt phi return_var). The consuming lane references that version, but it is defined only on the producing lane, so after the split it is an unbound free var on the consumer (`__FREE_VAR`) that codegen cannot map to a tensor view.

**Fix.** The pass already repaired the symmetric AIV-side case via an origin map; this generalizes it and applies it to both lanes:
- `BuildGmOriginMap` — built once from the original body; traces each Var to its origin `Out`/`InOut` param. Now also propagates origins through **IfStmt phi `return_vars`** (the one form the inline map missed; loops and straight-line stores were already covered).
- `RemapDanglingGmRefsToParam` — repoints every dangling cross-lane GM reference (origin is an `Out`/`InOut` param) onto that lane's shared base parameter before `DeepClone`. Applied symmetrically to AIC (new) and AIV (replacing the prior inline block).

Conservative by omission: a reference whose origin cannot be resolved to an `Out`/`InOut` param is left unchanged. `O(N log N)`, `IsOp`-based operator checks, deterministic iteration order.

## Testing

- [x] Full `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` suite: **1721 passed**
- [x] Existing `test_expand_mixed_kernel_{a2a3,split_aiv,a5}` suites pass (AIV refactor behavior-preserving)
- [x] 3 new regression tests (straight-line store / IfStmt phi / ForStmt loop) assert the AIC consumer no longer references a free var and loads resolve to a function parameter
- [x] 3 minimal repros (the three SSA-version forms) reach PTO codegen without the view-resolution crash

## Notes

Repointing resolves only the *name*. Cross-lane ordering for the AIV→AIC (V2C) direction still relies on an explicit barrier (`pl.system.syncall`), which the affected kernels already use. A fenceless V2C GM read-after-write is a separate, pre-existing synchronization concern — the automatic tpush/tpop fence covers only the C2V direction — and is out of scope for this view-resolution fix.

title: test: speed up qwen3 UT and split orchestration-codegen tests
body:
## Summary

Two local unit-test latency fixes found via profiling the `tests/ut` suite — the two slowest spots.

### 1. `tests/ut/jit/test_qwen3_decode.py`: ~76s → ~3s
- **Drop `torch.normal_()` from `_make_args`.** `compile_for_test` reads only tensor *shape/dtype* (via `_bind_args`), never the values, so filling the Qwen3-32B weights + 512K-row KV cache (916M elements) with RNG was ~37s/test of pure overhead. Now uses bare `torch.empty(...)`.
- **Share one memoized `post_pass` compile** across both tests (they assert on the same post-pass program). Uses a function-scoped + module-cached fixture rather than `scope="class"` so the compile stays inside the per-test `PYPTO_PROG_BUILD_DIR` redirect (a class-scoped fixture would set up before that autouse fixture and leak `build_output/` dirs into the repo).

### 2. Split `tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen.py` (7566 lines)
CPython's `inspect.findsource()` AST-parses the **whole containing file once per `@pl.program` class**, so a large multi-program test file pays `O(classes × file_size)`. The 139 program classes each re-parsed all 7566 lines (~33s, ~39% of the file's wall time).

Split into 6 focused files plus `_orchestration_codegen_common.py` for the shared helpers + `SELF_ALIAS_RE`:

| File | Tests |
| ---- | ----- |
| `test_orchestration_codegen.py` (`TestOrchestration` pt1) | 31 |
| `test_orchestration_codegen_more.py` (`TestOrchestrationMore`) | 32 |
| `test_orchestration_manual_scope.py` | 29 |
| `test_orchestration_tensor_rw.py` | 18 |
| `test_orchestration_misc.py` (9 small classes) | 17 |
| `test_orchestration_task_deps.py` (module-level fns) | 21 |

Smaller files cut per-class `getsourcelines` ~85% (33s → 5s); file wall 86s → 54s serial, ~14.5s under `-n auto`. **No test logic changed** — a faithful code move verified by an AST bijection (164 functions/methods, identical bodies) and unchanged collection count (148).

## Testing
- [x] Full `tests/ut -n auto`: **6358 passed, 2 skipped** (test count unchanged)
- [x] Split orchestration files: 148 tests pass (serial and xdist); `ruff check`/`pyright` clean
- [x] qwen3: 2 tests pass; verified no `build_output/` repo leakage and no verification-coverage loss
- [x] Code review completed

title: [Feature] Auto-fence AIV->AIC (V2C) cross-lane GM read-after-write in ExpandMixedKernel
body:
### Summary

`ExpandMixedKernel` splits a mixed `pl.split_aiv` InCore function into AIC + AIV lanes and, via `CollectGmCrossLaneSyncs`, inserts a `tpush`/`tpop` fence for a GM tensor written on the **cube** lane and read on the **vector** lane (C2V). The reverse direction — a GM tensor written on the **vector** lane (AIV) and consumed on the **cube** lane (AIC), i.e. **V2C** — is intentionally left **unfenced** (`CollectGmCrossLaneSyncs`: `if (store.side != CoreSide::AIC) continue;`, `src/ir/transforms/expand_mixed_kernel_pass.cpp` ~line 616) because V2C transport needs V->C fractal adaptation.

Request: automatically synchronize the V2C direction too — either by emitting a V2C `tpush`/`tpop` fence (with the fractal adaptation), or by injecting a `pl.system.syncall` when a V2C cross-lane GM dependency has no established fence/barrier — so producer/consumer ordering is guaranteed by the compiler rather than by a hand-written barrier.

### Motivation / Use Case

Follow-up to #1909, which fixed the PTO codegen crash where a GM tensor written inside a `split_aiv` region and consumed by a cube matmul left a dangling `__FREE_VAR` (the fix repoints the cross-half reference to the shared base parameter). That fix makes the V2C produce/consume pattern **compile**, but it does **not** add a happens-before edge for the V2C direction.

Consequently, a fenceless V2C GM read-after-write can let the cube lane read the GM scratch **before** the vector lane writes it → a **silent wrong result** rather than a loud failure. Today, correctness for these kernels (e.g. the in-kernel rope->attn fusion) relies on the author placing an explicit `pl.system.syncall` barrier between the producer and consumer phases. Auto-fencing would make the safe behavior automatic and prevent a future fenceless V2C kernel from compiling into a race.

An automated reviewer flagged this as **P1** on #1909 (left as an open follow-up thread at `src/ir/transforms/expand_mixed_kernel_pass.cpp:1243`).

### Proposed API / Behavior

Three candidate directions (to be decided during design):

- **(a) Full fix — V2C fence.** Extend `CollectGmCrossLaneSyncs` to also handle `store.side == AIV` with the consumer on AIC, emitting the V2C `tpush`/`tpop` fence with the required V->C fractal adaptation (`tile.move` to NZ/ZN before `tpush_to_aic`, fractal-typed `tpop_from_aiv`).
- **(b) Auto-barrier.** When a V2C cross-lane GM dependency is detected and no fence/barrier is already established, auto-insert a `pl.system.syncall` (or equivalent cross-core barrier) covering the producer->consumer ordering.
- **(c) Safety net.** Detect a genuinely fenceless V2C GM RAW and reject it with an actionable diagnostic (e.g. "insert `pl.system.syncall` between the producing `split_aiv` region and the cube consumer"), instead of compiling a racy kernel.

Pointers:
- `src/ir/transforms/expand_mixed_kernel_pass.cpp` — `CollectGmCrossLaneSyncs` (C2V-only gate at ~line 616: `if (store.side != CoreSide::AIC) continue;`).
- The #1909 repoint path (`BuildGmOriginMap` / `RemapDanglingGmRefsToParam`) is what now makes V2C compile.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Status quo:** require the kernel author to place an explicit `pl.system.syncall` barrier between the producing `split_aiv` region and the cube consumer. This works (and is what the shipped fusion kernels do), but it is easy to omit, and omission produces a silent race rather than a diagnostic.

### Additional Context

- Follow-up to #1909 (fix: repoint cross-half GM tensor refs to base param in `ExpandMixedKernel`).
- Related: #1894 (first-class `SplitAivScopeStmt`), #1820 (explicit AIV-split DSL), #1034 (GM-mediated split-axis reduction).
- Severity: medium — no wrong results in the shipped `syncall`-fenced kernels; the risk is a future fenceless V2C kernel compiling into a race.

title: feat(ir): roofline cost-model L0 tile chooser + non-aligned-K peel + operand-stationary
body:
## Summary

Rewrites `ChooseL0Tile` from an ad-hoc bytes-traffic heuristic to an **exhaustive
roofline cost-model search** over the design space `(m, n, k, stationarity, dbC)`,
**op-sim work-calibrated against the a2a3 device**, and adds the two emit paths it
enables in `AutoTileMatmulL0`:
- **non-divisor-K boundary peel** (16-aligned k + 16-aligned tail),
- **operand-stationary** (A/B-stationary: held operand single-buffered in the full
  L0 buffer via a `Sequential` outer loop).

dbC=2 (L0C double-buffer) is scored but gated off — emitter not implemented (follow-up).

## Cost model — what it is, what it reads from the backend

Roofline wall in core cycles: `wall = max(C_load, C_mad) + C_drain` (drain exposed).
- **C_load**: L1→L0A/L0B traffic under the chosen loop order, scaled by per-buffer
  bandwidths; op-sim-fit **~200 / ~132 B/cyc** (~1.5:1, not the datasheet 2:1).
- **C_mad**: cube MAD (per-`TMATMUL` issue overhead × K-fractal count); op-sim-accurate,
  unchanged.
- **C_drain** is **per output tile**: `⌈M/m⌉·⌈N/n⌉ · (drain_fixed + bytes_c·m·n / bw_drain)`.
  The drain count is invariant to K-splitting (partial sums accumulate in one L0C) but
  rises with M/N-splitting, so the per-drain fixed overhead stops the chooser
  over-splitting the output on shallow-K shapes.

The chooser reads from the active `BackendHandler`: **L0 capacities** (per-backend),
**fractal alignment** (16), and the **`L0CostModel`** (the bandwidths + MAD/drain
constants above). See the a5 note under Follow-ups — the cost-model constants are
currently a2a3-only.

## Measured impact

**Two regimes, measured separately: isolated GEMMs where the choosers pick different
tiles (wins), and real end-to-end models (neutral — no regression).**

### 1. Isolated GEMMs where the two choosers diverge — physical 910B

Every sweep-5/7 forced tile (new-pick vs old-pick) run on a **real NPU 910B2** via the
swimlane harness (warmup + min-of-3, parallel devices; 65/70 OK, the 5 FAILs are the
L1-overflow shapes). This isolates the tile-choice effect on the shapes where the two
choosers actually pick differently — silicon, not the simulator.

**Wins (device cube-exec, new vs old):**

| shape (bf16) | device | op-sim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 768×768×64 | **2.28×** | 1.89× |
| 512×512×64 | **1.75×** | 2.48× |
| 512×512×128 | **1.38×** | 2.14× |
| 256×256×64 (anchor) | **1.27×** | 1.67× |
| 128×512×128 | **1.25×** | 1.57× |
| 256×256×256 | **1.23×** | 1.41× |

- **18/21 op-sim wins are faster on silicon; 17/21 still ≥ 1.05×.** Every big
  drain-cliff win holds — the old byte-minimizer's misaligned-N tiles pay the FIXPIPE
  drain penalty on real hardware too.
- **Magnitude rule: device ≈ 1 + 0.5·(op-sim − 1).** Silicon retains ~half the op-sim
  excess-over-1.0 — a fixed host launch/staging floor dilutes small-matmul ratios (256²×64
  ≈ 12 µs device vs 3.3 µs op-sim). But the **largest drain-bound shapes preserve or
  exceed op-sim** (768×768×64: device **2.28×** > op-sim 1.89×). So op-sim cube-cycle
  ratios are drain-exposed **upper bounds**; treat the silicon reality as the rule above.
- **No real regression.** The 3 sub-1.0 device results are op-sim-marginal shapes (≤1.16×)
  collapsing into ±device-noise (~±3–4%); worst is 0.962× on the wider-M `512×256×256`
  already flagged marginal in sweep-4. The old `320×320×64` −2% never reproduces (0.997×).
  WIDERM is safe (0.995–1.062×); SANITY deterministic (64³ = 2.94 µs, 128³ = 6.42 µs).
- The FLIPPED drain-count fix confirms on silicon where it matters (mid/large:
  `64×256×256` 1.14×, `128×192×512` 1.10×); on the smallest shallow-K shapes its benefit
  sits below the device launch floor (neutral) — there it is a correctness/no-regression
  fix, not a speedup.

### 2. End-to-end on real models (pypto-lib `golden` harness, physical 910B, torch-validated) — NEUTRAL

Multi-sample with per-kernel variance (the device is noisy; single-sample deltas are **not**
separable — an early min-of-2 pass produced a phantom ~2% prefill "regression" that
vanished under 4-sample variance):

- **qwen3-14b decode** (M=16): neutral — every matmul within ±1% (5 samples). The chooser is
  **bypassed** (decode matmuls are DSL hand-tiled to single-L0 16×64 shapes).
- **qwen3-14b prefill** (M=512, the reworked #662 SPMD kernels): **neutral** — 4 samples/build,
  for every projection/MLP matmul the old↔new mean gap is below the combined per-kernel std
  (gate 90.9±2.9 vs 90.8±1.6 µs, up 89.4±2.2 vs 91.2±2.1, out_proj 102.7±4.7 vs 103.1±2.1).
- **DeepSeek-V4 MoE**: every expert GEMM (routed gate/up/down + shared-expert + gate) picks the
  **identical L0 tile** old-vs-new — the choosers do not diverge on the dsv4 path.

The §1 divergent-shape wins **do not appear** in these models — their GEMMs are either
chooser-bypassed (hand-tiled) or picked identically by both choosers — so e2e is a **no-op
with zero measured regression**. (The example models in this repo — FFN, llama-mini — are
likewise 64×64 single-L0 no-ops, verified byte-identical.) The full-K OS
**hoist-consistency fix** (`os_holds_a`: the emit obeys the chooser's bandwidth-weighted hoist
instead of a raw-byte heuristic) is included and, as a latent-correctness fix, is e2e-neutral —
its loop-order change is behavior-verified by a unit test (`320×320×64` → hold B), correctly
invisible to wall-clock.

**Net.** The new chooser's value is (1) a principled roofline + drain-count model that avoids
the old byte-minimizer's FIXPIPE drain-cliff tiles on shapes where they diverge (up to 2.28×
on isolated silicon), plus (2) the non-aligned-K peel and operand-stationary emit paths — with
**zero measured e2e regression** on the real workloads exercised.

## Validation

- 41 chooser unit tests (every emit path + all four cost terms) + a brute-force
  oracle proving the solver finds the model's global wall-minimum; auto-tile pass
  tests re-pinned to the new optima.
- Op-sim sweeps 1–7 fitting the constants + validating the drain-count fix
  (FLIPPED / GAIN / WIDERM / SANITY axes all pass).
- `pypto-lib-model` CI job green; FFN / paged-attention / llama-mini clear every
  pypto pass locally.

## Known limitation (does not block this PR)

This PR is **self-contained** — its CI is green **without #1924**. The on-kernel
chained mat-scratch stest uses full-K (K=64) so both matmuls in the chain stay
**output-stationary**, sharing one algorithm: no #1908 incompatible-mode L0
packing and no #1924 accumulator-coalesce is needed to pass.

Separately, a production split-K matmul with a large loop-carried L0C accumulator
(e.g. `512×512×192`) selects a split-K tile; `LowerPipelineLoops` peels the K-loop
into accumulator if-phis whose reconciliation emits a phantom Acc→Acc `tile.move`
→ a second co-live L0C → **`AllocateMemoryAddr` overflow**. This is a **pre-existing
`MemoryReuse` gap, independent of this PR's merge**, and is fixed by **#1924**
(`MemoryReuse::CoalesceAccumulatorIfPhis`). The current model examples (FFN,
paged-attention, llama-mini) do **not** hit it.

## Follow-ups (not blocking)

- **a5 cost-model calibration.** `Backend950` does **not** override `GetL0CostModel()`,
  so a5 uses the a2a3-calibrated bandwidths/MAD/drain constants. a5 picks already
  differ correctly via its larger **L0C (256 KB vs 128 KB)** — it fits bigger
  accumulators, fewer M/N splits — but the *ranking constants* are not a5-calibrated.
  Add a `Backend950::GetL0CostModel()` override once an a5 op-sim sweep is run.
- **N%32 drain-alignment cliff** — op-sim over-weights it (~3.3×); not modelled
  (ranking-neutral within a problem), a candidate refinement.
- **dbC=2 two-accumulator emitter** — re-enable `allow_double_buffer_c` once implemented.

title: [Bug] Spmd task submission omits the DistributedTensor CommContext arg → cross-rank notify/wait/put from a pl.spmd scope deadlocks (AICore 507015)
body:
### Component

**pypto** — orchestration codegen (`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`).

### Description

Cross-rank distributed signalling (`pld.system.notify` / `pld.system.wait`, and `pld.tensor.put`) issued from inside a **multi-core `pl.spmd` scope** fails at runtime with `AICore error 507015 / 507018 "bounded device drain failed"`. The **identical** ops in a single-core `pl.at(pl.Level.CORE_GROUP)` (InCore) scope work correctly.

**Root cause:** the orchestration codegen for an Spmd task (`GenerateSpmdCallCode`) does **not** thread the per-`DistributedTensor` **CommContext** scalar into the task's `L0TaskArgs`, whereas the InCore path (`GenerateFunctionCallCode`) does (via `EmitDistTensorCtxScalars`). The L1 kernel (PTOCodegen) still emits and reads a trailing `!pto.ptr<i64>` CommContext arg per DistributedTensor, so the Spmd kernel reads an **out-of-bounds / garbage** value for it → wrong peer address → the notify writes to garbage → the wait spins forever → device drain timeout.

### Steps to Reproduce

Minimal barrier, 2 ranks EP=2 on a2a3: each rank does mutual cross-rank `pld.system.notify(op=AtomicAdd)` + `pld.system.wait(cmp=Ge)` on a `pld.DistributedTensor` counter, once per lane, threshold = lanes. Only the scope differs:

- `pl.at(pl.Level.CORE_GROUP)` (single core) → **PASS**
- `pl.spmd(2)` and `pl.spmd(32)` → **507015 `bounded device drain failed`** (deterministic; fails even at 2 lanes)

Repro script: pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/min_barrier_draft.py --mode single|spmd --lanes N` (can be ported to `tests/st/distributed/` as a minimal case — happy to send a PR).

**Generated-code evidence (the smoking gun).** Both kernels read the CommContext at `args[3]`:
```cpp
// kernel_entry, BOTH single and spmd:
__gm__ int64_t* done__ssa_v0_ctx = reinterpret_cast<__gm__ int64_t*>(args[3]);
barrier(done, [out,] my_rank, [expected,] done__ssa_v0_ctx);   // v4 used by CommRemoteOffset_i32(v4, peer)
```
InCore orchestration (works) — passes the ctx as args[3]:
```cpp
params_t0.add_input(ext_done);
params_t0.add_output(ext_out);
params_t0.add_scalar(my_rank);
params_t0.add_scalar(ext_done_ctx);        // <-- CommContext -> args[3]
rt_submit_aiv_task(0, params_t0);
```
Spmd orchestration (fails) — ctx **missing**, only 3 args:
```cpp
params_t0.add_input(ext_done);
params_t0.add_scalar(my_rank);
params_t0.add_scalar(expected_inline3);
params_t0.launch_spec.set_block_num(32);   // NO add_scalar(ext_done_ctx)
rt_submit_aiv_task(0, params_t0);
```
So the spmd kernel reads `args[3]` out of bounds → `CommRemoteOffset_i32(garbage, peer)` → invalid peer GM address → `TNOTIFY` writes to garbage (the peer's counter never increments) → every block's `TWAIT` never reaches the threshold and spins → `aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU)` times out → 507015.

**Source location + fix.** In `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`:
- `EmitDistTensorCtxScalars()` (~line 2306) emits `add_scalar(ext_<name>_ctx)` per DistributedTensor formal.
- `GenerateFunctionCallCode` (InCore) calls it (~line 2699).
- `GenerateSpmdCallCode` (~line 2714) emits the task params + `EmitLaunchSpec(...set_block_num...)` but **never calls `EmitDistTensorCtxScalars`** (the InCore path early-returns into `GenerateSpmdCallCode` at ~line 2668, skipping the 2699 call).

**Suggested fix:** call `EmitDistTensorCtxScalars(...)` inside `GenerateSpmdCallCode` too, resolving the DistributedTensor formals through the Spmd wrapper (they're already reordered via `BuildWrapperReorderedParams`), so Spmd tasks thread the CommContext scalars exactly like InCore tasks.

### Expected Behavior

Cross-rank `notify`/`wait`/`put` issued from a `pl.spmd` scope should address the peer correctly and run, the same as from `pl.at(pl.Level.CORE_GROUP)`.

### Actual Behavior

`AICore error 507015 / 507018 "bounded device drain failed"` — the Spmd kernel reads a garbage CommContext and hangs. Deterministic, even at 2 lanes.

### Impact

Blocks parallelizing MoE `combine_push` / the symmetric `dispatch` payload push across the (otherwise idle) cores — the motivation for #1906, which is really just this missing codegen arg rather than a new capability.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `55fdd38` |
| pypto runtime (simpler) | `09f1546` |
| pypto-lib | `1a23bd3` |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Related

#1906 (feature framing of the same blocker), #1789 (different spmd 507018 — EVENT_ID fence), #1803 (different distributed-codegen bug).

title: feat(runtime): add StackedDeviceTensor for per-card resident weight sharding
body:
## Summary

Adds `DistributedWorker.alloc_stacked_tensor` to upload a leading-dim-stacked `[B, *tail]` tensor **once** and keep each shard resident on its own card, reused across dispatches — the multi-card analogue of the single-card resident `DeviceTensor`.

When a HOST orchestrator slices a `[B, N, M]` weight along its leading dim and dispatches a per-rank child (`for r in range(world_size): child(x[r], device=r)`), passing the whole host tensor re-uploads each `x[r]` slice to its card on every dispatch. A `StackedDeviceTensor` makes `x[r]` resolve to a resident shard, so the runtime skips the per-dispatch H2D upload through the existing `child_memory` path — **no codegen or C++ changes**.

### Changes
- **`StackedDeviceTensor`** — a `[B, *tail]` wrapper whose `__getitem__` returns shard `i`'s `DeviceTensor`; validates shard count/shape/dtype and whole-shard slicing.
- **`alloc_stacked_tensor(host, worker_ids=None)`** — shard `i` → worker `worker_ids[i]` (default `range(B)`, matching `device=r`). Pass `worker_ids` to match the program's `device=` for permuted/subset placements (e.g. `[1, 0]`). Adds `free_stacked_tensor` + auto-free on `close()`.
- **Relaxed `Worker.alloc_tensor`/`free_tensor`** to any `worker_id`; owned tensors are now tracked by `(worker_id, ptr)` so per-card buffers free against the right worker. This also lets a single resident `DeviceTensor` be placed on any card.
- Validates `StackedDeviceTensor` args against the parameter shape on dispatch.

## Testing
- [x] Unit tests: coverage for `StackedDeviceTensor` (construction/indexing/validation) and `alloc_stacked_tensor` (identity/permuted/free/auto-free/rollback). Existing worker-memory unit tests updated to the new `(worker_id, ptr)` tracking and the now-supported non-zero `worker_id`.
- [x] On-device st (`tests/st/distributed/test_l3_stacked_device_tensor.py`): **2 passed** on 2 cards via `task-submit` — `test_identity` and `test_permuted` (`worker_ids=[1, 0]`), each proving residency by zeroing the host source after upload and still computing `a + b`.
- [x] `ruff` + `pyright` clean; docs updated.

## Documentation
Getting-started (en + zh-cn) gains an `alloc_stacked_tensor` section.

title: [Feature] Support tensor-level aiv_shard / aic_gather in @pl.jit split_aiv regions
body:
### Summary

Extend `pl.aiv_shard` / `pl.aic_gather` to accept **high-level tensors**, so explicit AIV-split boundaries can be written in `@pl.jit` / `pl.spmd` kernels (where `pl.matmul` and elementwise ops return `Tensor`), not only in tile-ISA `@pl.program` / `@pl.function(Opaque)` kernels (where they return `Tile`).

Today `pl.aiv_shard(t)` requires `t` to be a `Tile`. In a high-level kernel the natural producers return `Tensor`, so an explicit shard fails at parse:

```
The operator tile.aiv_shard requires argument to be a TileType, but got TensorType
```

### Motivation / Use Case

Fusing rope + attention + online-softmax into one `fa_fused` root in the qwen3-14b decode layer (pypto-lib), I wanted per-head **explicit** `aiv_shard` / `aic_gather` inside the `gp` pipeline of a `pl.split_aiv(2, UP_DOWN)` region — cube QK/SV outside the region, vector softmax on the sharded half — mirroring the tile-ISA `SplitAivQkPvProgram` example (`tests/st/codegen/torch/test_torch_codegen_cross_core.py`).

In the `@pl.jit` / `pl.spmd` kernel this is impossible: `raw_scores = pl.matmul(q_padded, k_tile, ...)` is a `Tensor`, so `pl.aiv_shard(raw_scores)` fails with the `TensorType` error above.

The only way to get a data-parallel AIV split at the `@pl.jit` level today is the **AUTO** `pl.split_aiv(mode=UP_DOWN)` region — the compiler inserts `aiv_shard`/`aic_gather` at the C→V / V→C boundaries during lowering. That works and is correct, but gives the author **no explicit control** over shard placement or which ops are sharded, and forces a full tile-ISA `@pl.program` rewrite of the kernel if explicit control is wanted — inconsistent with an otherwise high-level kernel.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Accept a high-level `Tensor` argument to `pl.aiv_shard` / `pl.aic_gather` inside a `for aiv_id in pl.split_aiv(...)` region, lowering to the same tile-ISA `tile.aiv_shard` / `tile.aic_gather` (split axis from the region mode) that the auto path already produces — just under explicit user placement:

```python
raw = pl.matmul(q, k, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32)      # Tensor (cube), OUTSIDE the region
for aiv_id in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN):
    h = pl.aiv_shard(raw)          # Tensor -> this lane's row-half (C->V)
    s = softmax(h)                 # vector work on the half
    full = pl.aic_gather(s)        # half -> full (V->C)
oi = pl.matmul(full, v, out_dtype=pl.FP32)                  # Tensor (cube), OUTSIDE the region
```

### Alternatives Considered

- **Auto `pl.split_aiv(mode=UP_DOWN)`** (current): works, but no explicit control over shard granularity/placement.
- **Rewrite phase-1 in tile-ISA `@pl.program`/`@pl.function(Opaque)`**: enables explicit shard/gather but is a large change and inconsistent with the surrounding `@pl.jit` kernel.

### Additional Context

- Related: #1820 (the RFC that introduced `pl.split_aiv` + `aiv_shard`/`aic_gather`). This request is the tensor-level extension of those ops.
- pypto main commit at time of filing: `ff8028d`.
- Downstream: pypto-lib qwen3-14b decode `fa_fused` fusion (per-region `pl.split_aiv`: rope `NONE` -> attn `UP_DOWN` -> softmax `NONE`). The auto `UP_DOWN` region already emits per-head shard/gather correctly; this is purely about explicit tensor-level control.

title: fix(codegen): thread DistributedTensor CommContext into Spmd/Group tasks
body:
## Summary

Cross-rank signalling (`pld.system.notify` / `pld.system.wait` / `pld.tensor.put`) issued from a multi-core `pl.spmd` (or multi-core Group) scope deadlocked at runtime (`AICore 507015/507018 "bounded device drain failed"`), while the same ops from a single-core `pl.at(CORE_GROUP)` InCore scope worked.

**Root cause:** the L1 kernel appends one trailing `!pto.ptr<i64>` CommContext arg per `DistributedTensor` formal, but only the InCore orchestration path (`GenerateFunctionCallCode` → `EmitDistTensorCtxScalars`) threaded the matching `add_scalar(ext_<name>_ctx)` into the task. The wrapper paths (`GenerateSpmdCallCode` and all `GenerateGroupCallCode` branches) built task params via `BuildWrapperReorderedParams` and never emitted the ctx scalar, so the kernel read an out-of-bounds garbage CommContext → wrong peer address → notify wrote to garbage → wait spun forever → drain timeout.

## Changes

- `BuildWrapperReorderedParams` now also returns, per `DistributedTensor` formal (in inner-kernel param order), the resolved `ext_<name>` to emit as a trailing ctx scalar. This reuses its existing bridge-aware inner-kernel → wrapper → outer-arg mapping, so the **Spmd**, **AIV-only Group**, **MixedKernels Group**, and **Spmd-wrapped-Group bridge** paths are all fixed uniformly.
- New `EmitCtxScalars` helper emits the ctx scalars after the params, mirroring the InCore ordering.
- The InCore `EmitDistTensorCtxScalars` is unchanged.

## Testing

- [x] New orchestration-text regression tests for the plain-Spmd (AIV) path and the MixedKernels-Group-bridge path (`tests/ut/codegen/test_spmd_scope_tid_codegen.py`), asserting `add_scalar(ext_<name>_ctx)` is threaded.
- [x] `tests/ut/codegen/` full suite: 494 passed.

## Related Issues

Fixes #1913

Also relates to #1906 (feature framing of the same blocker).

title: fix(jit): round-trip pl.InOut params through the specializer
body:
## Problem

`pl.InOut[pl.Tensor[...]]` parameters are silently dropped when the JIT specializer regenerates a function's signature into the intermediate `@pl.function` source. The generated param comes out **bare** (no annotation) and downstream codegen fails:

```
Error: Parameter 'kv_cache' missing type annotation
  --> <jit:attention_swa_test>:...
    ... kv_cache, block_table: pl.Tensor[[4, 1], pl.INT32], ...
             ^^^^^^^^ Parameter 'kv_cache' missing type annotation
```

This happens on both `@pl.jit.inline` sub-kernels and orchestration entries, even though `pl.Out[...]` round-trips fine and the `type_resolver` already maps `InOut` → `ir.ParamDirection.InOut` correctly. The loss is purely in the specializer's source round-trip.

## Root cause (`pypto/jit/specializer.py`)

- `_classify_params` only recognised the `Out` wrapper (`outer.attr == "Out"`). An `InOut[...]` param matched neither the Out branch nor the plain-Tensor branch (its outer node is `InOut`, not `Tensor`), so it was classified as **nothing** — never added to `tensor_params`.
- `_build_params` only annotates params in `tensor_params`; everything else hits the final `else: result.append(name)` → emitted bare.
- `_build_tensor_annotation` could only produce `pl.Out[...]` or plain, never `pl.InOut[...]`.

## Fix

- `_classify_params`: recognise the `InOut` wrapper, collect `inout_params`, and add such params to `tensor_params` (now returns a 5-tuple).
- `_build_tensor_annotation`: emit `pl.InOut[...]` when `is_inout`.
- `_build_params`: thread `is_inout` (stripped for inline helpers, same as `Out` — inline params are in-place aliases with no calling-convention boundary).
- Update the two `_classify_params` call sites and the inline-deprecation warning to cover both wrappers.

## Tests

- `TestClassifyParams`: `test_inout_param`, `test_inout_param_subscripted_tensor`.
- `TestSpecializer`: `test_inout_annotation_filled` — specializes an entry with `pl.InOut[...]` and asserts the wrapper survives into the generated source (the exact regression).
- Updated existing `_classify_params` / `_build_params` call sites for the new signature.

`tests/ut/jit` — 274 passed. Verified end-to-end on device: a kernel whose orch entry declares `kv_cache: pl.InOut[pl.Tensor[...]]` now compiles and passes golden (previously failed with "missing type annotation").

title: Feature/a8w8 matmul dequant fusion
body:
## Summary

This PR adds PyPTO compiler support for the Qwen3-14B A8W8 decode path by introducing the `pl.a8w8_matmul_dequant_acc` tensor op and lowering it into existing tile/PTO primitives.

The op represents the common A8W8 projection pattern:

```text
INT8 activation x INT8 weight
  -> INT32 accumulator
  -> FP32
  -> activation-scale multiply
  -> weight-scale multiply
  -> FP32/BF16 output
```

## What Changed

### A8W8 matmul-dequant-acc op

- Adds the Python DSL / IR entry points for `pl.a8w8_matmul_dequant_acc`.
- Registers the C++ tensor op and validates:
  - `INT32` accumulator input
  - `INT8` lhs/rhs inputs
  - floating-point activation and weight scales
  - `[M]` / `[M, 1]` activation scale shapes
  - `[N]` / `[1, N]` weight scale shapes
  - `FP32` / `BF16` outputs
  - `a_trans` / `b_trans` dimension inference

### Tensor-to-tile lowering

- Lowers the tensor op to existing tile primitives:
  - `tile.matmul_acc` for general `M > 1`
  - `tile.gemv_acc` for `M == 1` decode
  - `tile.cast`
  - row/column scale multiplication
- Keeps the M=1 decode path lighter by using scalar activation-scale read plus vector multiply.

### Codegen and compiler support

- Extends tile move/type handling needed by the lowered IR.
- Adds PTO codegen support for the generated tile operation patterns.
- Fixes compiler pass edge cases triggered by the A8W8 decode lowering shape:
  - SSA handling for static constant branches with return values
  - mixed AIC/AIV expansion aliases
  - backend layout repair before tile store/load
  - cross-core pipe/split-id handling

### Tests

Adds focused unit coverage for:

- A8W8 matmul-dequant-acc type/lowering behavior
- M=1 decode lowering to `tile.gemv_acc`
- PTO codegen output for lowered tile patterns
- `tile.move(target_type=...)`
- backend layout repair behavior

## Validation

### PyPTO focused tests

Run from the `pypto` repository root:

```bash
source <venv>/bin/activate
PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" \
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_a8w8_matmul_dequant.py \
  tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen_ops.py \
  tests/ut/ir/operators/test_op_registry.py
```

Result:

```text
180 passed, 5 warnings
```

### Qwen3-14B A8W8 smoke generation

After rebuilding the native extension with:

```bash
source <venv>/bin/activate
pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
```

8-token generation using the matching `pypto-lib` / `pypto-serving` branches completed successfully:

```text
text: 的建筑风格和历史背景。
北京

prefill/TTFT: 8.256s
decode: 0.498s over 7 steps
TPOT: 71.1 ms/token
```

A previous 48-token smoke run also produced coherent Chinese text with TPOT around 73.9 ms/token.

## Notes

This PR contains PyPTO-side compiler functionality only. The model-level Qwen3-14B A8W8 decode/prefill kernels live in the companion `pypto-lib` PR and depend on `pl.a8w8_matmul_dequant_acc` being available.

title: feat(ops): support tensor-level aiv_shard/aic_gather in @pl.jit split_aiv regions
body:
## Summary

Closes #1915. Extends `pl.aiv_shard` / `pl.aic_gather` to accept high-level **`Tensor`** operands (not only `Tile`) inside a `for aiv_id in pl.split_aiv(...)` region in `@pl.jit` / `pl.spmd` kernels, giving authors **explicit** AIV-split shard/gather placement — lowering to the same `tile.aiv_shard` / `tile.aic_gather` the AUTO `split_aiv` path already produces.

Before, `pl.aiv_shard(matmul_result)` failed at parse:
```
The operator tile.aiv_shard requires argument to be a TileType, but got TensorType
```

## Approach

New `tensor.aiv_shard` / `tensor.aic_gather` ops → lowered 1:1 to `tile.*` at `ConvertTensorToTileOps` (pass 10). From pass 10 onward the IR is identical to the AUTO path, so downstream passes (LowerAutoVectorSplit / ExpandMixedKernel / SplitVectorKernel) need **no changes**.

- **Op + deducer** — rank-2 `TensorType` deducer sharing `ReshapeSplitAxis` / `ReadSplitAttr` with the tile deducer. **2D-only**: `UP_DOWN`/`LEFT_RIGHT` are only well-defined on the 2D physical tile view (an N-D tensor flattens to `[product(leading), last]`), so N-D is rejected with a reshape hint rather than silently miscompiling.
- **Frontend** — parser type-dispatches the emitted op namespace by operand type; the tensor form is **region-only** and `DistributedTensorType` is rejected (out of scope). DSL wrappers use a constrained `TypeVar` (`Tile→Tile`, `Tensor→Tensor`).
- **Verifier + affinity** — `AivSplitValid` and the core-affinity classifier recognize the `tensor.*` variants in the pre-pass-10 window.
- **Conversion** — re-attaches the vector-side (`Vec`) memory the deducer drops, verified structurally identical to the AUTO path (used as an oracle).

## Testing

- Unit tests across all layers: op deducer, parser, printer round-trip, verifier, and pass-10 conversion (incl. an AUTO-vs-explicit type-equality oracle test).
- End-to-end `@pl.jit TensorSplitAivQkPvProgram` (issue #1915's exact use case) compiled through the Default pipeline on Ascend910B — **torch golden matches (max abs diff 0.0)**, no `tile.aiv_shard`/`tensor.aiv_shard` survives `ExpandMixedKernel`, both AIC/AIV lanes emitted.
- Consolidated cross-suite sweep green; the tile-ISA path is untouched.
- Docs added for pass 10 (en + zh-cn).

title: fix(ir): coalesce peeled loop-carried accumulator if-phis in MemoryReuse
body:
## Summary
Fixes a pre-existing MemoryReuse bug that **halves the usable L0C capacity for pipelined-K matmuls**. Reproduces on `main`; not chooser-specific.

`LowerPipelineLoops` peels the `stage=2` K-loop into `if`-phis whose live branch is an in-place `matmul_acc` (on the accumulator buffer) and whose dead `if k==0` branch is a fresh `matmul` seed on a *different* Acc buffer. `YieldFixupMutator` reconciled them by copying the accumulator onto the seed's buffer via an `acc->acc tile.move`. Two consequences:

1. **Only half of L0C is usable.** The reconciliation copy is the same size as the accumulator and **co-live** with it, so a single pipelined-K accumulator can occupy at most **half** of L0C — the other half is the phantom duplicate. On a2a3 (128 KB L0C) that caps the accumulator at 64 KB (e.g. `128×128` fp32); the `512×512×192 bf16` case wants the full 128 KB tile (`256×128` fp32 = 131072 B) and fails to compile with `Acc buffer usage (262144 bytes) exceeds platform limit (131072 bytes)` — **exactly 2×**. This directly bounds matmul tiling: the L0 roofline tiler (#1912) sizes L0C tiles against the *full* L0C, so without this fix its larger tiles overflow and it is forced into smaller, less efficient ones (more M/N sub-tiles → more accumulator drains and operand reloads).
2. **ptoas rejects the move.** Acc->Acc `tmov` has no legal address-space pair on any target (no legal Acc->Acc pair), so the peeled K-loop path fails to compile even when the duplicate would fit.

## Fix (`src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp`)
- **`TopDownRetargeter::CoalesceAccumulatorIfPhis`** (Step 3.75): identifies the in-place-accumulator branch by its `reuses_input` producer and retargets the *other* branch's seed onto the accumulator buffer, so both branches share it and no move is emitted (matches `mad_acc`'s shared-`%dst` semantics). The retarget is **mandatory** — a declined retarget is an `INTERNAL_CHECK`, never a move, since no legal Acc->Acc move exists. A single coalesced accumulator can then use the **full** L0C.
- **Branch-locality + branch-scoped liveness guard.** The `check_liveness=false` bypass is sound only when (a) the seed producer is a `Call` lexically *inside* the non-accumulator branch — a pre-`if` value yielded through the branch runs unconditionally and would clobber the accumulator the sibling branch reads — and (b) the accumulator buffer is dead *within the branch* after the seed. A branch-scoped `IsTargetDeadAtAssign` (new `stop_at` param halts the scan at the enclosing `if`) enforces (b) while ignoring the mutually-exclusive sibling and the legitimate post-`if` phi consumers; when either (a) or (b) fails the phi is left to `YieldFixup`. The branch-tail scan rejects a later **read _or_ write-only clobber** of the accumulator base (`SubtreeWritesBase`, the dual of the reads-only collector) — a fresh producer aliasing the base without reading it would otherwise overwrite a retargeted seed before the phi consumes it.
- **`NormalizeIdentityCopyBuffersMutator`** (Step 4.5): reconciles a downstream bare-`Var` SSA identity copy of the retargeted return_var (which otherwise keeps the pre-coalesce buffer), and re-anchors an in-place op's output onto its reused input's new buffer when the input was retargeted (`ReanchorInplaceOutput`) — see below.

## Non-divisor K-peel
When the K tile does not divide K, `AutoTileMatmulL0` pipelines the full K-blocks and peels a straight-line `matmul_acc` tail. After `CoalesceAccumulatorIfPhis` retargets the loop accumulator, that tail's output — an in-place op aliasing the accumulator — stayed declared on the pre-coalesce buffer, orphaning it on a never-written Acc base (compiles, but reads a stale buffer → wrong result). `ReanchorInplaceOutput` re-anchors the tail onto the accumulator's coalesced buffer, mirroring the existing bare-`Var` and view-input rename handling.

## Testing
- **Unit:** structural before/after (`assert_structural_equal`) on a minimal accumulator if-phi (verified to regress pre-fix: 2 Acc buffers + phantom Acc->Acc move); a gating test proving the Acc-only scope (a Vec `fillpad_inplace` if-phi is left to the legal Vec->Vec move path); a branch-locality test (a pre-`if` seed stays on a distinct buffer); and a write-only-clobber test (a later write-only def of the accumulator base blocks the seed retarget). Full MemoryReuse suite **64 pass**; transforms **1778** unaffected.
- **Device (a2a3):**
  - `512x512x192 bf16` matmul — compiles through the full pipeline with **one `loc=acc` buffer of the full 128 KB L0C and zero `tmov`** in the emitted `.pto`; on-device numerics vs an f32 golden (Frobenius rel_err < 2e-2). Pre-fix this same shape overflowed at 2× (262144 > 131072).
  - Non-divisor K-peel `128x688x128 bf16` (k=128 peel: 5 full K-blocks + 48 tail) — **compiles and is numerically correct: 0 / 16384 mismatches** at rtol=atol=2e-3 (residuals at pure fp32-accumulation rounding, ~1e-5 abs), versus a compile-but-wrong 16378 / 16384 without the `ReanchorInplaceOutput` fix.
  - Broader AutoL0 sweep (the `_AUTOL0_SHAPES` set, bf16, A-/B-stationary, chained mat-scratch, both K-peels) — 11 / 11 pass, no regression.

## Docs
Updated `docs/en|zh-cn/dev/passes/29-memory_reuse.md` (Algorithm + Implementation).

title: feat(ci): borrow NPU per case via task-submit, free CI from card pinning
body:
## Summary

Frees device CI jobs from holding a fixed NPU for their whole run. The slow
part (IR→kernel/orch C++→binary compile + golden) needs no card, so it now
runs card-free on a CPU pool while each case borrows an NPU per run from the

- **feat(ci): borrow NPU per case via task-submit** — device-side

  path untouched; sim never borrows a card). Batches artifacts into one hot
  process per batch to amortize device init.
- **fix(pr): address review feedback** — INFRA marker distinguishes
  reconstruction/setup failures from device failures; per-batch first-rebind
  attribution; watchdog scaled by batch length; inline work_dir routed
  through host-visible `build_output`; shlex-quoted `--run` payload; rc=1
  triage.
- **refactor(runtime): dedup task-submit execute/reconstruct helpers** —
  extract shared `_reconstruct_artifact` / `_run_on_device` (execute_artifact)
  and `_build_execute_artifact_cmd` / `_exec_task_submit` (harness) between the

- **ci: kill orphaned task-submit tasks and re-enable device jobs** — every
  card-borrowing job gets an `always()` cleanup step that kills its own
  detached task-submit tasks (scoped by checkout dir) on cancel/kill; re-enable
  `dist-system-tests` and `pypto-lib-model`.

title: fix(runtime,backend): bound device compile fan-out; configurable ptoas timeout
body:
## What

Runtime/backend half of the `system-tests` (a2a3) compile-stability work,
split out from #1926 per review. The paired CI workflow tuning
(`--precompile-workers`, step `timeout-minutes`) lives in a separate PR.

Under the `system-tests` job, each case's per-kernel compile fan-out spun up
many `ccec` subprocesses, and heavy kernels could be killed by a hardcoded 60s
ptoas wall-clock under high compile-pool concurrency (spurious timeouts, not
real work limits).

## Changes

- **`device_runner.py`** — cap per-case device compile fan-out at
  `min(16, available_cpus)` (overridable via `PYPTO_DEVICE_COMPILE_WORKERS`) so
  it composes with the outer precompile pool instead of multiplying into
  process/thread exhaustion (libgomp thread-creation failures / segfaults). The
  affinity probe also tolerates `OSError` (restricted containers/sandboxes),
  falling back to `os.cpu_count()`.
- **`pto_backend.py`** — make the per-kernel ptoas compile timeout configurable
  via `PYPTO_PTOAS_TIMEOUT`, default raised 60s → 120s.

## Test

Python-only; no behavior change on the default (unset-env) local path other
than the higher default timeout. Validated end-to-end alongside the CI tuning
PR (system-tests a2a3 stabilized).

title: feat(ci): tune system-tests compile concurrency (workers 128->64, timeout 15->20min)
body:
## What

CI workflow half of the `system-tests` (a2a3) compile-stability work, split out
from #1926 per review. The paired runtime/backend changes (per-case fan-out cap,
configurable ptoas timeout) are in #1928.

## Changes

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `Test system tests` step:

- `--precompile-workers` 128 → 64 — the outer precompile pool multiplied with
  each case's kernel-compile fan-out to spawn ~100 concurrent ccec subprocesses,
  exhausting process/thread limits and segfaulting mid-compile. Halving it lets
  the outer pool compose with the per-case cap in #1928.
- `timeout-minutes` 15 → 20 — the lower concurrency reduces compile throughput,

within the 20min budget.

Best paired with #1928: `--precompile-workers=64` is calibrated to compose with
that PR's per-case fan-out cap. Landing this alone still lowers concurrency
safely, but the two are designed to work together.

## Summary

Enables **bf16 atomic-add** for `tile.store` / `tensor.assemble` (split-K accumulation) on the Ascend910B (A2/A3) profile, and broadens atomic-add test coverage across all hardware atomic dtypes and both core types.

title: [Bug] dep_gen (DFX) instrumentation breaks full-occupancy pl.system.syncall -> AICore timeout 507018
body:
### Component

Backend (runtime `dep_gen` / DFX dependency-capture instrumentation)

### Description

`dep_gen` (the DFX dependency-capture runtime instrumentation, `enable_dep_gen=True`, on by default) perturbs AICore/AIV core occupancy and breaks the **full-occupancy contract** of `pl.system.syncall(core_type="mix")`.

An in-kernel `syncall(core_type="mix")` is a hard FFTS cross-core barrier: **every** dispatched block must reach it (on 910B that is all 24 AIC + 48 AIV lanes). With `dep_gen` enabled, the extra instrumentation work changes which cores are occupied / when they arrive, so some cores never reach the barrier and the AICore side times out.

The kernel is functionally correct: with `dep_gen` disabled the exact same program passes golden validation on device. Only the DFX instrumentation flips it from PASS to a hang/timeout, so `dep_gen` is altering scheduling/occupancy behavior it should be transparent to.

### Steps to Reproduce

```markdown
1. Take a mixed cube+vector `@pl.jit` kernel that dispatches all NUM_CORES
   blocks so every AIC (24) + AIV (48) lane participates, and uses an in-kernel
   `pl.system.syncall(core_type="mix")` barrier (full-occupancy contract: every
   dispatched block must arrive at the barrier).
2. Run it on a 910B device with dep_gen ENABLED (the default, enable_dep_gen=True).
   Concrete downstream repro — pypto-lib qwen3-14b fused decode kernel:
     python models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py -p a2a3 -d 0     # dep_gen on
3. Observe the run hang, then abort with AICore timeout 507018.
4. Re-run the SAME kernel with dep_gen disabled:
     python models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py -p a2a3 -d 0 --no-dep-gen
   -> golden PASS.
```

### Expected Behavior

`dep_gen` (DFX dependency capture) instrumentation must be transparent to scheduling/occupancy: enabling it must not change the set of cores that reach a full-occupancy `syncall(core_type="mix")` barrier. The kernel should PASS regardless of the `dep_gen` setting.

### Actual Behavior

With `dep_gen` enabled the run hangs, then fails:

```
[ERROR] validate_runtime_impl: [runtime_maker.cpp:623] PTO2 runtime failed: orch_error_code=0 sched_error_code=100 runtime_status=-100
RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
```

Disabling `dep_gen` (`--no-dep-gen` / `enable_dep_gen=False`) makes the identical kernel PASS. The instrumentation appears to occupy cores / add work such that not all AIC+AIV blocks arrive at the `syncall` barrier, producing the AICore timeout (507018).

### Git Commit ID

80bac774e64f55c5e7b336d4184f9222ff43073d

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Downstream kernel / PR exercising this: hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#656 (fused rope+attn+softmax qwen3-14b decode; in-kernel `syncall` barriers between rope / attn / online-softmax phases).
- Worked around downstream in pypto-lib CI with a per-file `# ci: no-dep-gen` directive that appends `--no-dep-gen` for kernels using a full-occupancy `syncall`. That workaround should be removable once this is fixed.
- Related (same AICore error code 507018, but different root cause): #1840 (intermittent paged-attention device fault), #1789 (fence EVENT_ID reallocation hazard).

title: chore(runtime): bump simpler to 4d5fbe4c; adapt STRACE span rename (supersedes #1907)
body:
### Problem
Bumping the `runtime` submodule to current simpler `main` (`4d5fbe4c`) requires two pypto adaptations, one of which fails silently:

1. **simpler #1181** dropped `arg_index` from `CoreCallable.build` (`build(signature, binary)`), while pre-#1181 runtimes still *require* it. pypto passes `arg_index=` unconditionally → `TypeError` on #1181+ runtimes.
2. **simpler #1210** renamed the `[STRACE]` span-tree root `run_prepared` → `simpler_run` (device emitters + `strace_timing._ROUNDS_TABLE_NAMES`). pypto's `bench.py` hardcoded the old names in `_parse_stats_from_strace`, so on a #1210+ runtime `by_name().get(...)` returns `None` and every host/device wall sample is **silently `0.0`** (no error).

### Fix
- **`arg_index` (device_runner.py)** — feature-detect support once from `CoreCallable.build.__doc__` and pass `arg_index` only when accepted, via a shared `_build_core_callable` helper. Drives both runtime generations with no branch on the pin. *(This commit is @noabauma's from #1907, cherry-picked to keep the two adaptations together in one coherent bump; this PR supersedes #1907.)*
- **STRACE span names (bench.py)** — drop the hardcoded `_SPAN_HOST` / `_SPAN_DEVICE`; derive the keys from the installed runtime's `_ROUNDS_TABLE_NAMES` inside `_parse_stats_from_strace`. Works against both `run_prepared` (pre-#1210) and `simpler_run` (#1210+) runtimes.
- **runtime submodule** — `02bd0c4f` → `4d5fbe4c`.

### Adaptation audit (02bd0c4f → 4d5fbe4c)
The rest of pypto's consumed surface is **unchanged**:
- Public `Worker` API — #1210 renamed only internal `_ChipWorker`/binding methods (`prepare_callable` → `register_callable`), not `Worker.register/run/...`.
- `Tensor` struct + orchestration API headers — comment-only diff; `host_api.h` additions are internal.
- `simpler_setup` tools consumed by pypto (`torch_interop`, `strace_timing`, `swimlane_converter`, `log_config`, `KernelCompiler`) — signatures intact.

### Testing
- `tests/ut/runtime/test_benchmark.py` — **17 passed** against the `4d5fbe4c` runtime (parse tests exercise the real `strace_timing`, resolving to `simpler_run`). The fixture now sources the span root from `_ROUNDS_TABLE_NAMES`, keeping the tests generation-agnostic.
- `ruff` clean.
- `test_benchmark_st.py` (asserts `device_wall_us > 0`) is the on-device regression guard for the span rename — not yet run on-device here.

### Notes
No public API change. Distributed L3/L2 and SPMD paths are not device-validated post-#1210 (larger separate surface).

title: feat(codegen): add memory_planner switch to hand allocation to ptoas
body:
## Summary

Adds a `MemoryPlanner {PYPTO, PTOAS}` option to `ir.compile()` that selects who plans on-chip buffer memory:

- **`PYPTO`** (default, behavior unchanged): run `MemoryReuse` + `AllocateMemoryAddr`, bake physical addresses into `pto.alloc_tile addr = ...`, and run ptoas at `--pto-level=level3` (ptoas trusts the pre-baked addresses).
- **`PTOAS`**: skip both PyPTO allocation passes, omit the `pto.alloc_tile addr` operand, and run ptoas at `--pto-level=level2` so its `PlanMemory` pass owns on-chip allocation — letting callers escape the PyPTO allocator and its budget verifier.

### How it works

- The switch lives on `PassContext` (per the pass-context-config rule) and is read by `PassManager` to conditionally skip `MemoryReuse` + `AllocateMemoryAddr`.
- It is also threaded through `generate()` to codegen (new `PTOCodegen::Generate(emit_tile_addr=...)` flag, gating the three `addr` emission sites) and to the ptoas flag builder (`--pto-level` selection).
- `InitMemRef` runs in both modes — it creates the MemRefs / alloc ops that ptoas `PlanMemory` plans over. Buffer aliasing is preserved through shared alloc SSA identity, not through addresses, so dropping `addr` is safe for `level2`.
- `pto_rebuild` (debug `.pto` splice path) infers the ptoas level from whether the `.pto` carries an `addr` operand, staying in sync with whichever mode produced it.

### Caveat (surfaced at compile time)

`PTOAS` mode also defers the Ascend910B `load + tpop_from_aic` in-place hazard legalisation and reserve-buffer base resolution (normally done by `MemoryReuse` / `AllocateMemoryAddr`) to ptoas. `compile()` emits a `logger.warning` so callers verify affected kernels on-device.

## Testing

- [x] New `tests/ut/codegen/test_memory_planner_switch.py` (6): PassContext round-trip; PTOAS skips `MemoryReuse` + `AllocateMemoryAddr`; codegen emits/omits `addr` per mode.
- [x] `tests/ut/backend` + `tests/ut/codegen` — 550 passed (2 existing tests adapted for the internal-helper signature change).
- [x] `tests/ut/pass` — 15 passed.
- [x] Built with GCC 15; clang-tidy clean on the changed C++ (pre-existing findings elsewhere untouched).
- [ ] On-device validation of `PTOAS` mode (level2 PlanMemory) — recommended follow-up per the caveat above.

## Notes

- Cross-layer sync: C++ enum → nanobind → type stubs → Python.
- Docs updated (en + zh-cn) in `docs/*/dev/codegen/00-pto_codegen.md`.
- Default path (`PYPTO`) is unchanged.

title: [Bug] hard-form pl.system.syncall deadlocks (AICore 507018) at partial core occupancy — no compile-time check
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

A kernel using the **hard (FFTS) form** of `pl.system.syncall` deadlocks on device with `RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018` (AICore timeout) when the enclosing `pl.spmd(N)` launch does **not fill all physical cores** of the barrier's `core_type`. The hard barrier (`SYNC_AIV_ONLY_ALL` / mix) waits for *every* physical core of that type to arrive; the unlaunched cores never reach the barrier, so the FFTS wait never completes.

There is **no compile-time diagnostic** — the mistake only surfaces at runtime as a timeout, and it leaves the device draining/reset (subsequent runs on that device fail with `code 13` until reset). The compiler already knows both the launch block count (`pl.spmd(N)`) and the target SoC's physical core count per core type, so this is statically checkable.

### Steps to Reproduce

Minimal on-device repro (Ascend 910B = 48 physical AIV cores): a SPMD elementwise add with a hard `pl.system.syncall(core_type="aiv_only")` between the loads and the add, launched at partial occupancy. Mirrors `tests/st/runtime/cross_core/test_syncall.py` (whose docstring already documents that hard SYNCALL needs full AIV occupancy).

```python
TR = TC = 128
N = 24  # < 48 physical AIV  -> PARTIAL occupancy (set N = 48 for the passing control)

@pl.program
class PartialSyncAll:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def add(self, a: pl.Tensor[[N*TR, TC], pl.FP32], b: pl.Tensor[[N*TR, TC], pl.FP32],
            out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N*TR, TC], pl.FP32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[N*TR, TC], pl.FP32]:
        i = pl.tile.get_block_idx(); o = i * TR
        ta = pl.load(a, [o, 0], [TR, TC]); tb = pl.load(b, [o, 0], [TR, TC])
        pl.system.syncall(core_type="aiv_only")          # HARD barrier
        out = pl.store(pl.add(ta, tb), [o, 0], out); return out

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
    def orchestrator(self, a, b, out):
        with pl.spmd(N):                                  # N=24 < 48 -> partial
            out = self.add(a, b, out)
        return out
```

Run on `a2a3`. `pl.spmd(24)` (partial) → 507018. Changing **only** `pl.spmd(24)` → `pl.spmd(48)` (full occupancy) → **PASS**. Occupancy is the sole variable.

### Expected Behavior

The compiler rejects a hard-mode `syncall` whose enclosing `pl.spmd` launch does not fill all physical cores of the barrier's `core_type`, with a clear compile-time error, e.g.:

> `hard pl.system.syncall(core_type="aiv_only") requires the spmd launch to fill all 48 AIV cores, but pl.spmd(24) launches 24 blocks. Use mode="soft" (GM-polling) for partial occupancy.`

At minimum, a documented static diagnostic instead of a silent runtime 507018 + device reset.

### Actual Behavior

Compiles silently; on device the run hangs until the FFTS wait times out and the device is force-reset:

```
[ERROR] sync_run_streams: aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
[ERROR] recover_device_or_mark_unusable: AICore error 507018: bounded device drain failed (force reset will follow in finalize)
RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
```

The device is left unusable afterwards (later runs fail with `code 13` until it recovers).

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `d598b41b` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `02bd0c4f` |
| pto-isa | `e722679` |
| ptoas | `0.48` |
| CANN | not detected |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Additional Context

- The **soft** form already works at partial occupancy: `pl.system.syncall(mode="soft", core_type="aiv_only", gm_workspace=ws, used_cores=N)` (see the `*Soft*` case in `tests/st/runtime/cross_core/test_syncall.py`). A compile-time check for the hard form would make the hard-vs-soft occupancy contract explicit and catch the footgun early.
- Related: hw-native-sys/pypto#1931 (dep_gen instrumentation perturbing a *full*-occupancy syncall → 507018) — a distinct root cause; this issue is specifically the **missing compile-time occupancy guard** for the hard form.
