Each lane owns 4 disjoint items.""" with pl.spmd(16, name_hint="sa"): for aiv in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.NONE): lane = pl.get_block_idx() * 2 + aiv for it in pl.range(IPL): g = lane * IPL + it out = pl.assemble(out, pl.reshape(src[g : g + 1, 0 : ROWS * COLS], [ROWS, COLS]), [g * ROWS, 0]) return out @pl.jit def plain_spmd_arm( src: pl.Tensor[[SRC_ROWS, ROWS * COLS], pl.FP32], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[OUT_ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]], ): """CONTROL: identical work partition, 32 spmd blocks, no split_aiv.""" with pl.spmd(LANES, name_hint="ps"): lane = pl.get_block_idx() for it in pl.range(IPL): g = lane * IPL + it out = pl.assemble(out, pl.reshape(src[g : g + 1, 0 : ROWS * COLS], [ROWS, COLS]), [g * ROWS, 0]) return out if __name__ == "__main__": ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("-p", "--platform", default="a2a3") ap.add_argument("-d", "--device", type=int, default=0) args = ap.parse_args() torch.manual_seed(1) src = torch.randn(SRC_ROWS, ROWS * COLS, dtype=torch.float32) want = src.reshape(OUT_ROWS, COLS) cfg = RunConfig(platform=args.platform, device_id=args.device) failed = [] for tag, fn in (("CONTROL plain pl.spmd(32), no split_aiv", plain_spmd_arm), ("BROKEN pl.spmd(16) + pl.split_aiv(2, NONE)", split_aiv_arm)): out = torch.zeros(OUT_ROWS, COLS, dtype=torch.float32) fn(src, out, config=cfg) o = out.view(ITEMS, ROWS, COLS) w = want.view(ITEMS, ROWS, COLS) bad = [g for g in range(ITEMS) if not torch.equal(o[g], w[g])] err = float((out - want).abs().max()) print(f"[split_aiv] {tag:<46} {'PASS' if not bad else 'FAIL'} " f"max_err={err:8.5f} wrong items = {len(bad):3d}/{ITEMS}", flush=True) if bad: failed.append(tag) lanes_bad = sorted({g // IPL for g in bad}) print(f"[split_aiv] wrong lanes ({len(lanes_bad)}/{LANES}): {lanes_bad}") g0 = bad[0] print(f"[split_aiv] want[{g0}][0,:4] = {w[g0][0, :4].tolist()}") print(f"[split_aiv] got [{g0}][0,:4] = {o[g0][0, :4].tolist()}") print(f"\n[split_aiv] {'BUG REPRODUCED' if failed else 'no bug on this build'}", flush=True) raise SystemExit(1 if failed else 0) ```
The two arms have the **identical work partition**, identical inputs, identical golden. The only difference is `pl.split_aiv(2, NONE)` vs a plain `pl.spmd(32)`. ## Ablation — `pl.split_aiv` is the only necessary ingredient Bisected from qwen3's real phase-0 body (an in-register QK-norm) down to the repro above. Each row removes exactly ONE ingredient; work partition, inputs and golden are identical throughout. | variant | `split_aiv`? | result | |---|:---:|---| | full chain, `spmd + split_aiv + lane-guard + pl.pipeline` | ✅ | **FAIL** 64/128 | | `pl.range` instead of `pl.pipeline` | ✅ | **FAIL** 64/128 | | lane guard removed | ✅ | **FAIL** 64/128 | | **`split_aiv` removed (plain `pl.spmd(32)`)** | ❌ | **PASS** 0/128 | | all QK-norm arithmetic removed (`concat`+`reshape` only) | ✅ | **FAIL** 64/128 | | **`pl.concat` removed too (slice + reshape only)** | ✅ | **FAIL** 64/128 | | `pl.full` hoisted out of the loop | ✅ | **FAIL** 64/128 | So it needs **no** `pl.concat`, **no** reduction, **no** arithmetic, **no** lane guard, and **no** `pl.pipeline`. Only `pl.split_aiv`. The same chain in a plain `pl.at(pl.Level.CORE_GROUP)` task is **bit-exact** against torch (`max_abs_err = 0.000000`, 0/128 items wrong). ## Suspected mechanism (not verified — for the fix's author) The body updates a loop-carried SSA tensor: ```python for aiv in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.NONE): ... out = pl.assemble(out, tile, [row, 0]) # both lanes produce a new `out` ``` Both lanes write, so both produce a new version of `out`. The dropped rows come back as **exact zeros — never written**, which is what one would expect if only ONE lane's `out` survives into the enclosing scope and the other lane's SSA chain is discarded. The block-parity alternation of *which* lane survives suggests the surviving version is selected by something that flips with the block index. Per the docstring, the region is consumed and erased by **`LowerAutoVectorSplit` (pass 20)** and "never reaches ExpandMixedKernel or codegen" — so that is where I would look first. ## Blast radius `pl.split_aiv(2, SplitMode.NONE)` with an `aiv_id`-dispatched `pl.assemble` is exactly the pattern qwen3-14b's fused decode uses in **both** its rope phase and its online-softmax phase. Measured consequence, grading the fused kernel against the un-fused one (a different kernel, and the one that passes the serving e2e) on a fixture where every batch row shares one `seq_len`: | seq_len | max_abs_err | argmax agreement | |---|---|---| | 6 (a real serving prompt) | **1.65** | **11/16** | | 31 | 0.62 | 15/16 | | 128 | 0.19 | 16/16 | | 1024 | 0.03 | 16/16 | Logit scale is ~7, so at a short prompt the kernel is 23 % of scale off and flips 5 of 16 tokens; the error decays with context length, so long fixtures hide it entirely. The qwen3-14b **serving e2e fails**. pypto-lib previously REVERTED the whole fused-decode feature (pypto-lib#703, "Revert Qwen3 decode changes causing incorrect serving output") — this is one of the reasons why. ## Ruled out Each was tested and falsified, so please don't re-chase them: - **Not `pl.concat`.** Removing it entirely still fails (ablation row 6). (The separate `tile.concat` missing-`.not_inplace_safe()` defect is real and already fixed; this reproduces on top of that fix.) - **Not the orchestration forwarded-tuple mis-bind** (#2003 / PR #2004). Reproduces with that patch applied. - **Not the lane guard** (`if lane < N`), **not `pl.pipeline`**, **not `pl.full` placement**, **not the arithmetic** — every one removed independently, still fails. - **Not `pl.reshape`** — the same reshape in a plain `pl.spmd` control is bit-exact. - **Not pto-isa, not the ring arena, not a race** — deterministic across runs. ## Suggested direction If the "both lanes run the full body for disjoint work" contract is meant to hold, then `LowerAutoVectorSplit` must merge (not select) the two lanes' writebacks to a carried tensor. If instead that pattern is **not** supported — i.e. a carried tensor may not be `pl.assemble`d from both lanes of a `NONE` region — then the DSL should **reject it at parse time** rather than silently dropping half the work. `pto.alloc_multi_tile` already takes exactly that stance for a comparable silent-overlap hazard ("...adjacent slots would silently overlap. `pto.alloc_multi_tile` therefore rejects `compact = row_plus_one` slot layouts"). Silent wrong data is the worst possible outcome, and in this case it cost a shipped feature a revert.

title: [Bug] pl.concat silently returns wrong data: tile.concat is missing .not_inplace_safe(), so MemoryReuse aliases dst onto a src
body:
## Background `pl.concat` **silently returns wrong data** on device. It compiles clean, raises nothing, produces no NaN — the destination just contains the wrong values. `MemoryReuse` coalesces the `tile.concat` output onto one of its own source buffers, and `pto.tconcat` is not in-place safe. Found while debugging qwen3-14b's fused decode (`models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py`), which uses `pl.concat` to build the QK-norm reduction tile. The kernel returns wrong tokens; the in-repo golden cannot see it because that golden is a second on-device dispatch of the same code path. Reproduction environment: | Component | Version | |---|---| | pypto | `8ebddcb8` (`main`) — also reproduces on `a655a5a7` | | simpler | `c94aa9f3` | | ptoas | `0.48` | | pto-isa | `83d01313` (the pin) | | CANN | `9.0.0` | | NPU | Ascend 910B (`a2a3`), and `a2a3sim` | Independent of the two other pypto defects found in the same investigation — the orchestration forwarded-tuple mis-bind (#2003 / PR #2004) and `pl.split_aiv(2, NONE)` dropping half its work (#2006). This reproduces with both of those fixed. ### Component IR / MemoryReuse ## Root cause `tile.concat` is registered **without `.not_inplace_safe()`** (`src/ir/op/tile_ops/transform.cpp:763`), so `MemoryReuse` is free to coalesce its output buffer onto one of its inputs. But `pto.tconcat` **cannot be done in place**: ``` dst[i, 0 : C0) = src0[i, 0 : C0) dst[i, C0 : C0 + C1) = src1[i, 0 : C1) ``` `dst`'s row stride is `C0 + C1`, which differs from **both** sources' row strides. It copies row by row, forward. So as soon as `dst` shares a base address with a src, writing `dst`'s row *j* lands on source rows that have **not been read yet** — and they are then read back as the data that just clobbered them. `tile.transpose` is already marked `.not_inplace_safe()` for exactly this reason. `tile.concat` was missed. Confirmed in the generated `.pto` — compile the same kernel at a passing and a failing shape and diff the `alloc_tile` addresses: ```mlir // PASSES — concat([1,128], [1,896]) -> [1,1024] %t__tile = pto.alloc_tile addr = 0 valid_col = 128 (src0) %0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = 512 valid_col = 896 (src1) %1 = pto.alloc_tile addr = 512 valid_col = 1024 (dst) <-- dst aliases src1 // SILENTLY CORRUPTS — concat([1,640], [1,896]) -> [1,1536] %t__tile = pto.alloc_tile addr = 0 valid_col = 640 (src0) %0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = 2560 valid_col = 896 (src1) %1 = pto.alloc_tile addr = 2560 valid_col = 1536 (dst) <-- dst aliases src1 ``` Both alias; whether the aliasing actually corrupts depends on the sizes and on the copy pipeline's read-ahead, which is why there is an apparent "size threshold" and why small cases got away with it. ## Actual behaviour Two forms, both reproduced on real hardware with `randn` inputs: **Form A — single-row operands: `src1` is dropped entirely and replaced by a verbatim copy of `src0`.** ``` CASE A concat([1,640], [1,896]) -> [1,1536] FAIL src0 half correct : True src1 half is a VERBATIM COPY of src0: True expected src1[:6] = [7.0, 7.0, 7.0, 7.0, 7.0, 7.0] got src1[:6] = [0.001, 0.002, 0.003, 0.004, 0.005, 0.006] CTRL A concat([1,128], [1,896]) -> [1,1024] PASS ``` **Form B — multi-row operands: rows of the `src0` half receive other `src0` rows.** ``` CASE B concat([16,64], [16,64]) -> [16,128] FAIL rows of src0 half that are wrong : [10, 12, 14] first bad element at [row 10, col 0]: expected 0.64100, got 0.32100 CTRL B concat([8,64], [8,64]) -> [8,128] PASS ``` Independently measured on a single-kernel `randn` test, same code, before vs after the fix: | | before | after | |---|---|---| | `a2a3sim` | 31/32 rows wrong; `row1.left = b[0]` | all correct | | `a2a3` (device) | 7 rows wrong (18, 20, …, 30); `row18.left = a[9]`, `row20.left = a[10]` | all correct | `row18.left = a[9]` is the self-clobber signature: writing `dst` row 9 landed `a[9]` on `src0`'s row-18 address, and iteration 18 then read it back. **The device only corrupts the back half** — the first 17 rows' reads were hoisted by the copy pipeline — which makes it *more* insidious than sim, not less. ## Why CI was green `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_concat.py` **does** run on device (the system-tests direct-device step). It passed because its inputs are **constant**: `torch.full(1.0)` / `torch.full(2.0)`. The corruption's shape is "overwrite one row of `src0` with **another row of `src0`**". If every row of `a` is `1.0`, overwriting one with another is a no-op. **Constant test data is structurally blind to a row-permutation defect.** The ST is updated to use random data in the PR. ## Steps to reproduce Standalone; imports only `pypto.language` + `pypto.runtime`. No pypto-lib, no golden harness. ```bash python pypto_concat_bug_repro.py -d # exits 1 on the bug ```
pypto_concat_bug_repro.py — two broken cases + two passing controls ```python import argparse import torch import pypto.language as pl from pypto.runtime import RunConfig A_W, A_PAD, A_TOT = 640, 896, 1536 # Form A: single-row, numel(src0) >= 608 B_R, B_H, B_F = 16, 64, 128 # Form B: multi-row, R >= 12 C_W, C_PAD, C_TOT = 128, 896, 1024 # control A: numel(src0) below threshold D_R, D_H, D_F = 8, 64, 128 # control B: R below threshold @pl.jit def case_a(x: pl.Tensor[[1, A_W], pl.FP32], p: pl.Tensor[[1, A_PAD], pl.FP32], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[1, A_TOT], pl.FP32]]): with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="a"): out[0:1, 0:A_TOT] = pl.concat(x[0:1, 0:A_W], p[0:1, 0:A_PAD]) return out @pl.jit def case_b(lo: pl.Tensor[[B_R, B_H], pl.FP32], hi: pl.Tensor[[B_R, B_H], pl.FP32], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[B_R, B_F], pl.FP32]]): with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="b"): out[0:B_R, 0:B_F] = pl.concat(lo[0:B_R, 0:B_H], hi[0:B_R, 0:B_H]) return out @pl.jit def ctrl_a(x: pl.Tensor[[1, C_W], pl.FP32], p: pl.Tensor[[1, C_PAD], pl.FP32], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[1, C_TOT], pl.FP32]]): with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="c"): out[0:1, 0:C_TOT] = pl.concat(x[0:1, 0:C_W], p[0:1, 0:C_PAD]) return out @pl.jit def ctrl_b(lo: pl.Tensor[[D_R, D_H], pl.FP32], hi: pl.Tensor[[D_R, D_H], pl.FP32], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[D_R, D_F], pl.FP32]]): with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="d"): out[0:D_R, 0:D_F] = pl.concat(lo[0:D_R, 0:D_H], hi[0:D_R, 0:D_H]) return out if __name__ == "__main__": ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("-p", "--platform", default="a2a3") ap.add_argument("-d", "--device", type=int, default=0) args = ap.parse_args() cfg = RunConfig(platform=args.platform, device_id=args.device) bad = [] # Form A: a distinct-valued src0, a constant src1 -> a dropped src1 is unmissable. x = (torch.arange(A_W, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(1, A_W) + 1) * 0.001 p = torch.full((1, A_PAD), 7.0) out = torch.zeros(1, A_TOT) case_a(x, p, out, config=cfg) ok = torch.equal(out, torch.cat([x, p], 1)) print(f"CASE A concat([1,{A_W}], [1,{A_PAD}]) -> [1,{A_TOT}] {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}") if not ok: bad.append("A") print(f" src1 half is a VERBATIM COPY of src0: " f"{torch.equal(out[0, A_W:A_W + A_W], x[0])}") print(f" expected src1[:6] = {p[0, :6].tolist()}") print(f" got src1[:6] = {out[0, A_W:A_W + 6].tolist()}") # Form B: distinct value per (row, col) -> a permuted row is unmissable. lo = (torch.arange(B_R * B_H, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(B_R, B_H) + 1) * 0.001 hi = lo + 100.0 out = torch.zeros(B_R, B_F) case_b(lo, hi, out, config=cfg) ok = torch.equal(out, torch.cat([lo, hi], 1)) print(f"CASE B concat([{B_R},{B_H}], [{B_R},{B_H}]) -> [{B_R},{B_F}] {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}") if not ok: bad.append("B") wrong = [r for r in range(B_R) if not torch.equal(out[r, :B_H], lo[r])] print(f" rows of src0 half that are wrong : {wrong}") r = wrong[0] print(f" expected lo[{r},:6] = {lo[r, :6].tolist()}") print(f" got lo[{r},:6] = {out[r, :6].tolist()}") for tag, fn, (r, w0, w1) in (("CTRL A", ctrl_a, (1, C_W, C_PAD)), ("CTRL B", ctrl_b, (D_R, D_H, D_H))): a = torch.randn(r, w0) b = torch.randn(r, w1) o = torch.zeros(r, w0 + w1) fn(a, b, o, config=cfg) print(f"{tag} concat([{r},{w0}], [{r},{w1}]) -> [{r},{w0 + w1}] " f"{'PASS (expected)' if torch.equal(o, torch.cat([a, b], 1)) else 'FAIL (unexpected!)'}") print(f"\n{'BUG REPRODUCED — failing cases: ' + str(bad) if bad else 'no bug on this build'}") raise SystemExit(1 if bad else 0) ```
## Blast radius Any kernel using `pl.concat` where `MemoryReuse` chooses to coalesce the output onto a source is silently wrong, with no signal. In qwen3-14b's fused decode this corrupts the Q QK-norm tile (real Q rows off by up to **6.59** on a scale of 4.66; the zero-pad rows of `all_q_padded` come back non-zero), which is one of the reasons pypto-lib previously REVERTED the whole fused-decode feature (pypto-lib#703, "Revert Qwen3 decode changes causing incorrect serving output"). ## Ruled out - **Not `pl.reshape`** — correct at every shape tested, including `[1, N] -> [R, C]`. - **Not a `pl.full` materialisation artifact** — a real input tensor as `src1` gives the identical wrong answer. - **Not the orchestration mis-bind (#2003)** or **`pl.split_aiv` (#2006)** — reproduces with both fixed. - **Not pto-isa, not the ring arena, not a race** — deterministic. ## A contract gap worth closing separately `PTOAS/docs/PTO_IR_manual.md`'s `pto.tconcat` section (and pto-isa's `docs/isa/TCONCAT.md`) say **nothing** about whether `dst` may overlap a `src` — neither permitted nor forbidden. Meanwhile: - `pto.ttranspose` carries a **required `tmp` operand** precisely because a permuting op cannot be done in place; - `pto.alloc_multi_tile` **rejects** `compact = row_plus_one` slot layouts specifically because "adjacent slots would silently overlap". So the codebase clearly knows this class of hazard — but `tconcat` has neither a `tmp` nor a stated no-overlap contract, and its implementation neither handles the overlap nor rejects it. We are fixing this conservatively on the pypto side (`.not_inplace_safe()`), but if the ISA owner intends `dst`/`src` overlap to be forbidden, that should be **written into the ISA doc** — otherwise the next shifted/permuting op will hit exactly the same thing.

title: fix(ir): mark tile.concat not_inplace_safe so MemoryReuse cannot alias dst onto a src
body:
Fixes #2007.

## The bug

`pl.concat` **silently returned wrong data on device**. It compiled clean, raised nothing, produced no NaN — the destination just held the wrong values.

`tile.concat` was registered **without `.not_inplace_safe()`**, so `MemoryReuse` was free to coalesce its output buffer onto one of its own inputs. But `pto.tconcat` cannot be done in place:

```
dst[i, 0 : C0)       = src0[i, 0 : C0)
dst[i, C0 : C0 + C1) = src1[i, 0 : C1)
```

`dst`'s row stride is `C0 + C1`, which differs from **both** sources' row strides, and the copy runs row by row, forward. So once `dst` shares a base address with a src, writing `dst`'s row *j* lands on source rows that have **not been read yet** — and they are then read back as the data that just clobbered them.

`tile.transpose` is already marked `.not_inplace_safe()` for exactly this reason. `tile.concat` was missed.

## Observed

Single kernel, `randn` inputs, same code before vs after:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `a2a3sim` | 31/32 rows wrong, `row1.left = b[0]` | all correct |
| `a2a3` (device) | 7 rows wrong (18, 20, …, 30), `row18.left = a[9]`, `row20.left = a[10]` | all correct |

`row18.left = a[9]` is the self-clobber signature: writing `dst` row 9 landed `a[9]` on `src0`'s row-18 address, and iteration 18 then read it back. **The device only corrupts the back half** — the first 17 rows' reads are hoisted by the copy pipeline — which makes it *more* insidious than sim, not less.

Also reproduced standalone with single-row operands, where the whole `src1` half of the output comes back as a **verbatim copy of `src0`**:

```
concat([1,640], [1,896]) -> [1,1536]   FAIL — src1 half == src0 (expected 7.0, got src0's values)
concat([1,128], [1,896]) -> [1,1024]   PASS (below the size at which it bites)
```

## Why CI did not catch it

`tests/st/runtime/ops/test_concat.py` **does** run on device (the system-tests direct-device step). It passed because its inputs were **constant**: `torch.full(1.0)` / `torch.full(2.0)`.

The corruption's shape is *"overwrite one row of `src0` with **another row of `src0`**"*. If every row of `a` is `1.0`, overwriting one with another is a no-op. **Constant test data is structurally blind to a row-permutation defect.**

## Changes

- **`src/ir/op/tile_ops/transform.cpp`** — add `.not_inplace_safe()` to `tile.concat`.
- **`tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_memory_reuse.py`** — regression UT in `TestInplaceOps`: concat's output buffer base must differ from **both** src bases. Runs on CPU, so it guards the regression in CI without hardware.
- **`tests/st/runtime/ops/test_concat.py`** — switch the ST to random data. This changes a test **input** to strengthen detection; **no assertion was weakened**.

## Verified

- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` + `tests/ut/codegen/` — **2719 passed**.
- ST on device (`--platform=a2a3`, pinned pto-isa) — passed.
- `examples/kernels/04_concat.py` — now passes on sim; its own assert was failing before this fix.
- An independent standalone reproducer (single-row + multi-row forms, plus two passing controls) goes from `exit 1` to `exit 0`.

## Contract gap, worth closing separately

`PTOAS/docs/PTO_IR_manual.md`'s `pto.tconcat` section (and pto-isa's `docs/isa/TCONCAT.md`) say **nothing** about whether `dst` may overlap a `src` — neither permitted nor forbidden. Meanwhile `pto.ttranspose` carries a **required `tmp` operand** precisely because a permuting op cannot be done in place, and `pto.alloc_multi_tile` **rejects** slot layouts where "adjacent slots would silently overlap".

So the codebase knows this class of hazard, but `tconcat` has neither a `tmp` nor a stated no-overlap contract, and its implementation neither handles the overlap nor rejects it. This PR fixes it conservatively on the pypto side; if the ISA owner intends `dst`/`src` overlap to be forbidden, that belongs in the ISA doc — otherwise the next shifted/permuting op will hit the same thing.

title: [Bug] t[:, a:b] on a multi-row tile silently returns wrong data — pl.tile.slice encodes a dense MemRef over its own live source
body:
## Background **`t[:, a:b]` — a column slice of a MULTI-ROW tile — silently returns wrong data.** It compiles clean, raises nothing, produces no NaN. `ROWS = 1` is correct; every `ROWS >= 2` is corrupted. This is about as basic as a DSL operation gets, and it is the fourth silent data-corruption defect found in this same investigation (after #2003, #2007, #2006). Found in qwen3-14b's fused decode (`models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py`), whose RoPE step column-slices a `[16, 128]` tile into halves. The kernel returns wrong tokens; the in-repo golden cannot see it because that golden is a second on-device dispatch of the same code path. Reproduction environment: | Component | Version | |---|---| | pypto | `8ebddcb8` (`main`) + the fixes for #2003 / #2007 / #2006 — reproduces with all three applied | | simpler | `c94aa9f3` | | ptoas | `0.48` | | pto-isa | `83d01313` (the pin) | | CANN | `9.0.0` | | NPU | Ascend 910B (`a2a3`) | ### Component IR / MemRef (`pl.tile.slice`) ## Root cause pypto lowers `t[:, a:b]` to `pl.tile.slice` -> `MemRef(parent_buf, byte_offset = a * esize, size = rows * cols_slice * esize)` — a **flat byte offset into the parent with a DENSE size**. That encoding is only coherent when `rows == 1`. Generated `.pto` for the qwen3 case (`q_heads` is `[16, 128]` f32, row pitch 512 B): ```mlir %q_heads @76032 16x128 f32 (row pitch 512 B) %q_lo @76032 16x 64 f32 pad=0 (row pitch 256 B) <-- base == q_heads %q_hi @76288 16x 64 f32 pad=0 (row pitch 256 B) <-- base == q_heads + 256 B pto.textract ins(%q_heads, 0, 0) outs(%q_lo) pto.textract ins(%q_heads, 0, 64) outs(%q_hi) ``` `textract` must repack **strided (pitch 128) -> dense (pitch 64)**, and its destination lands **on top of its own still-live source**: - `q_lo`'s extract trashes `q_heads`; - `q_hi`'s extract then reads the already-trashed `q_heads` **and** overwrites `q_lo` — which is read again afterwards. - Only **row 0** survives, because for row 0 the dense destination address happens to equal its source address. This was simulated byte-for-byte on the host from the kernel's own inputs: the simulation predicts the device's `q_heads` **and** the downstream `q_rot` with **max|diff| = 0.000000 across all 2048 rows**. **Why `ROWS = 1` is safe** (and why the qwen3 K path is unaffected while Q is destroyed): with one row, source and destination pitches coincide, so the repack is an identity copy. qwen3's K path row-slices to 1 row *first* (`k_normed[0:1, :]`) and only then column-slices; its Q path column-slices the full 16-row tile. A Q/K bisect on the real kernel isolated the bug to Q exactly along that line. ## Actual behaviour ``` ROWS max_abs_err wrong elems wrong rows verdict -------------------------------------------------------------------- 1 0.000000 0/128 0/1 PASS 2 3.602502 64/256 1/2 *** WRONG *** 4 7.598506 128/512 2/4 *** WRONG *** 8 7.048662 256/1024 4/8 *** WRONG *** 16 9.420689 512/2048 8/16 *** WRONG *** ``` Signature at `ROWS = 16` — `out[0, 64:68]` comes back holding **row 1's lower half**: ``` device out[0, 64:68] = [-0.5881, -0.3706, -0.3759, -0.3649] correct x[0, 64:68] * w[:4] = [-0.3789, 0.8139, 0.5189, -0.8323] x[1, 0:4] * w[0:4] = [-0.5881, -0.3706, -0.3759, -0.3649] <-- what actually lands ``` Exactly the dense-repack-over-live-source signature. ## Steps to reproduce Standalone; imports only `pypto.language` + `pypto.runtime`. No pypto-lib, no golden harness. ~100 lines. **No `pl.spmd`, no `pl.system.syncall`, no `pl.split_aiv`, no `pl.create_tensor`** — a column slice of a multi-row tile is sufficient on its own. ```bash python repro_colslice.py -d # exits 1 on the bug ```
repro_colslice.py ```python """STANDALONE repro — pypto only (pypto.language + pypto.runtime). No pypto-lib, no golden harness. A COLUMN slice of a MULTI-ROW tile is silently miscompiled. t = x[0:ROWS, :] # [ROWS, 128] f32 tile in UB, row pitch 128 floats lo = t[:, 0:64] # -> pto.textract into a DENSE [ROWS,64] tile (pitch 64) hi = t[:, 64:128] # ALLOCATED AT t's OWN BASE ADDRESS (+0 / +64 floats) pypto lowers each column slice to a `pto.textract` that repacks strided(pitch 128) -> dense(pitch 64), and the memory allocator gives the destination the *subview's* address, i.e. INSIDE the still-live source tile. The repack is therefore performed IN PLACE over its own input: * lo's extract overwrites t (dest row r lands at t+64r, source row r sits at t+128r); * hi's extract then reads the ALREADY-TRASHED t, and its dest (t+64 .. t+64+64*ROWS) overwrites lo as well. Only row 0 survives (its destination address equals its source address). For ROWS == 1 the whole thing degenerates to an identity copy, so a single-row tile is unaffected — which is why the same construct is harmless elsewhere. Run: python repro_colslice.py -d 3 """ import argparse import torch import pypto.language as pl from pypto.runtime import RunConfig COLS = 128 HALF = 64 ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("-d", "--device", type=int, default=3) args = ap.parse_args() import pypto.pypto_core as _c # noqa: E402 print(f"[pypto] {_c.__file__}\n") cfg = RunConfig(platform="a2a3", device_id=args.device, enable_dep_gen=False) def build(rows): @pl.jit def k( x: pl.Tensor[[rows, COLS], pl.FP32], w: pl.Tensor[[1, HALF], pl.FP32], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[rows, COLS], pl.FP32]], ): with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP): t = x[0:rows, :] # [rows, 128] tile lo = t[:, 0:HALF] # column slice <-- the defect hi = t[:, HALF:COLS] # column slice <-- the defect a = pl.col_expand_mul(lo, w) # lo * w b = pl.col_expand_mul(hi, w) # hi * w out = pl.assemble(out, pl.concat(a, b), [0, 0]) return out return k print(f"{'ROWS':>5} {'max_abs_err':>12} {'wrong elems':>14} {'wrong rows':>12} verdict") print("-" * 68) fails = [] for rows in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16): torch.manual_seed(0) x = torch.randn(rows, COLS, dtype=torch.float32) w = torch.randn(1, HALF, dtype=torch.float32) out = torch.zeros(rows, COLS, dtype=torch.float32) build(rows)(x, w, out, config=cfg) ref = x * torch.cat([w, w], dim=1) # golden: every column scaled by w err = (out - ref).abs() bad = int((err > 1e-5).sum()) badr = int((err.max(dim=1).values > 1e-5).sum()) ok = bad == 0 if not ok: fails.append(rows) print(f"{rows:>5} {float(err.max()):>12.6f} {bad:>6}/{rows*COLS:<7} {badr:>5}/{rows:<6} " f"{'PASS' if ok else '*** WRONG ***'}") print() if fails: print(f"REPRODUCED: column-slicing a multi-row tile is miscompiled for ROWS = {fails}.") print("ROWS = 1 passes (source and destination addresses coincide), which is exactly why") print("a single-row RoPE is unaffected while a 16-row one is destroyed.") # Show the signature on the largest failing case. rows = fails[-1] torch.manual_seed(0) x = torch.randn(rows, COLS, dtype=torch.float32) w = torch.randn(1, HALF, dtype=torch.float32) out = torch.zeros(rows, COLS, dtype=torch.float32) build(rows)(x, w, out, config=cfg) print(f"\nSignature (ROWS={rows}): out[0, 64:68] should be x[0, 64:68]*w[0,0:4]; the dense") print("repack instead leaves it holding row 1's LOWER half:") print(f" device out[0, 64:68] = {[round(v, 4) for v in out[0, HALF:HALF+4].tolist()]}") print(f" correct x[0,64:68]*w[:4] = " f"{[round(v, 4) for v in (x[0, HALF:HALF+4] * w[0, 0:4]).tolist()]}") print(f" x[1, 0:4]*w[0:4] = " f"{[round(v, 4) for v in (x[1, 0:4] * w[0, 0:4]).tolist()]} <-- what actually lands") raise SystemExit(1) print("NOT reproduced.") ```
## Blast radius `t[:, a:b]` on a multi-row tile is a routine DSL construct. Any kernel doing it is silently wrong, with no signal — and it is used identically by the *working* K path in the very same kernel, which is what made this so hard to see. Measured consequence in qwen3-14b's fused decode, grading against the un-fused kernel (a different kernel, and the one that passes the serving e2e) on a fixture where every batch row shares one `seq_len`: | | `all_q_padded` vs a host oracle | bad rows | err@6 | argmax@6 | |---|---|---|---|---| | as-is | **5.765625** | **640/640** | 1.42 | 13/16 | | with the Q RoPE forced to slice one row at a time | **0.000977** (a bf16 quantum) | **0/640** | 0.084 | **16/16** | qwen3-14b's **serving e2e fails**. pypto-lib previously REVERTED the whole fused-decode feature (pypto-lib#703, "Revert Qwen3 decode changes causing incorrect serving output") — this is one of the reasons why. ## Suggested fix The bad `MemRef` is already present at `29_after_InitMemRef`, i.e. **before** `MemoryReuse` and `AllocateMemoryAddr` — so this is not a memory-reuse aliasing bug like #2007; the slice's shape is mis-encoded at construction. Options: 1. **Give the sliced tile the parent's row pitch** (`pad = cols_parent - cols_slice`), making it a true strided view. `textract` then becomes a no-op and nothing is repacked. This looks like the right fix. 2. Or allocate a **genuinely disjoint** destination, so the strided -> dense repack is out-of-place. 3. Failing either, **reject it** — the precedent is `pto.alloc_multi_tile`, which refuses slot layouts that "would silently overlap". Silent wrong data is the worst possible outcome. ## Ruled out Each was tested and falsified: - **Not #2003 / #2007 / #2006** — reproduces with all three fixes applied. - **Not `MemoryReuse`** — the mis-encoded MemRef exists before that pass runs. - **Not UB over-subscription** — `fa_fused`'s report says Vec 98.5 KB / 184 KB = 53.5 %. - **Not float reassociation, not the reduction tile shape, not the publish mechanism, not the fa_fused task structure** — each removed independently in the real kernel; none moved the error. - **Not the K path** — proven bug-neutral by a Q/K bisect (unfolding K alone changes nothing; unfolding Q alone fixes it).

title: fix(ir): a column slice of a multi-row tile must not materialize over its own source
body:
Fixes [#2010](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/2010)

`t[:, a:b]` on a multi-row tile feeding a `col_expand_*` op silently returned wrong data. `ROWS = 1` was correct; every `ROWS >= 2` case was corrupted, with no error, no NaN.

## Root cause

`tile.slice` inherits its source's memory, so the slice's result buffer is a **dense `[rows, slice_cols]` window sitting inside the still-live source**. The `pto.tcolexpand*` family cannot read a `pto.subview` operand, so codegen lazily materializes the slice with a `pto.textract` into that buffer — repacking *strided* (source row pitch) into *dense* (slice row pitch) **on top of its own input**.

Only row 0 survived, because its dense destination happens to equal its source address. That is exactly why a single-row slice was unaffected while a 16-row one was destroyed.

Generated `.pto` before the fix (`[16, 128]` f32 column-sliced into halves):

```mlir
%t   = pto.alloc_tile addr = 0     rows=16, cols=128     // source, still live
%lo  = pto.alloc_tile addr = 0     rows=16, cols=64      // SAME base as %t
%hi  = pto.alloc_tile addr = 256   rows=16, cols=64      // %t + 256 B
pto.textract ins(%t, 0,  0) outs(%lo)   // strided -> dense repack ON TOP OF %t
pto.textract ins(%t, 0, 64) outs(%hi)   // reads the already-trashed %t, overwrites %lo
```

## Fix

`CanonicalizeTileSlice` already rewrote *dynamic-offset* Vec slices into a `tile.extract` with a fresh buffer (#1640), but its guard tested the wrong property. A const offset only guarantees the destination **address** is right; the destination **layout** must match too, and it does so only for a **contiguous** window — a single row, or one spanning every column.

`IsDynamicSliceOffset` is replaced by `MaterializationCorruptsSource`, which rewrites whenever the lazy textract would not be an identity copy. Contiguous const-offset slices are still left untouched, so they keep sharing the source buffer rather than paying for a duplicate allocation.

Two supporting changes close the same hole from the other side:

* **`tile.extract` is now registered `not_inplace_safe()`.** Without it, `MemoryReuse` coalesced the freshly allocated extract buffer straight back onto the source it reads from, restoring the in-place repack the rewrite exists to avoid. (Verified: with the pass fix alone, the device still returned wrong data.)
* **The codegen materialization path hard-fails on a non-contiguous window** (`INTERNAL_CHECK`) instead of emitting the source-corrupting repack, so any slice that escapes the pass (e.g. a 4-arg slice carrying `valid_shape`) is rejected loudly rather than producing silently wrong data — option 3 in the issue.

## Note: the issue's repro also needs the `tile.concat` fix

The repro in #2010 trips **two independent defects**. Isolating them on device (`[16, 128]`, Ascend 910B):

| Variant | This PR | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Column slices, **no** concat | **PASS** (was wrong for every `ROWS >= 2`) | #2010 itself — fixed here |
| Concat, **no** column slice anywhere | still wrong | needs the separate `tile.concat` `not_inplace_safe()` fix |
| The issue's repro (both) | needs both | green once both land |

The second defect is `pto.tconcat` writing its wider-pitch `[R, C0+C1]` destination onto one of its own live inputs; it is already fixed on the `fix/concat-not-inplace-safe` branch, so it is deliberately **not** duplicated here. With both changes applied together, the issue's repro passes for every `ROWS` (max|diff| = 0).

## Verification

* **Device (Ascend 910B)**: a `[16, 128]` tile column-sliced into halves through `col_expand_mul` now matches the host oracle exactly (max|diff| = 0 over all rows), where it previously diverged on 11 of 16 rows.

title: fix(codegen): dispatch dual_aiv_dispatch AIV kernels on both vector lanes
body:
## Summary

A `pl.split_aiv` region is task-parallel: both AIV lanes run the body on disjoint work selected by `aiv_id`. `SplitVectorKernel` stamps such an AIV kernel `dual_aiv_dispatch`, but only the mixed-kernel Group submit honoured it. The three single-kernel dispatch paths — direct call, Spmd wrapper, and AIV-only Group — all built their submit through `CoreTypeToSubmitPrefix()`, which unconditionally yields `rt_submit_aiv_task` for VECTOR.

`rt_submit_aiv_task` fills only the AIV0 slot of `MixedKernels`, so the runtime schedules a single-AIV task: one AIV core per block. The second lane never launches, and the lone lane that does reads a `get_sub_block_id()` the runtime leaves undefined for single-AIV tasks, so its `aiv_id` is really its physical cluster position. **Half the work is silently dropped** — the destination rows come back as exact zeros, with no error, no NaN, and a block-parity pattern for which lane survives. A pure-vector kernel (no cube work) hits this on the Spmd-wrapper path.

### Changes

1. **`fix(language)`: make `split_aiv` IR survive print → parse unchanged.** Two parser-side asymmetries made `python_print` → parse lossy for a function carrying a `pl.split_aiv` region, failing the roundtrip verifier on every pass over such IR:
   - An explicit `attrs={"split": pl.SplitMode.NONE}` was dropped on parse while the printer emits it. Store every mode instead — behaviour-preserving, since `Function::GetSplitMode()` maps `split == 0` to `nullopt` and is the attr's sole reader.
   - A `pl.split_aiv` loop directly in an InCore function body was wrapped in a synthesized `InCoreScopeStmt`. An InCore function is already a core function — nothing is left to outline — and it is the shape post-outline IR prints as. Emit the region in place there too.

2. **`fix(codegen)`: dispatch `dual_aiv_dispatch` AIV kernels on both vector lanes.** Route the three single-kernel paths through a shared `BuildSingleKernelSubmitExpr()`, which emits `MixedKernels{INVALID_KERNEL_ID, id, id}` + `rt_submit_task` for a `dual_aiv_dispatch` VECTOR kernel. Two active AIV slots make it a MIX-shape task, so the scheduler places both lanes of one cluster under the same `block_idx` and gives them `sub_block_id` 0 and 1; the cluster's AIC core is unused. **No runtime change is needed.**

A plain vector kernel carries no `dual_aiv_dispatch` and keeps `rt_submit_aiv_task`, so it retains its full independent-AIV parallelism. Mixed kernels are untouched.

## Testing

- [x] New roundtrip tests (`tests/ut/ir/printing/test_split_aiv_roundtrip.py`) guard both parser arms.
- [x] New orchestration codegen UT (`tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen_more.py`) covers the `dual_aiv_dispatch` submit shape.
- [x] The existing NONE-region codegen ST compiled this exact shape but only asserted a `.pto` was emitted — which is why the defect shipped. It now also asserts the submit launches both lanes.
- [x] Documentation updated (`docs/en/dev/codegen/01-orchestration_codegen.md` + zh-cn).

## Related Issues

Fixes #2006

title: feat(jit): compile @pl.jit kernels straight from the signature (#1996)
body:
JITFunction.compile() now accepts zero positional arguments: when no sample tensors are passed, the shape/dtype contract is read directly from the kernel's own parameter annotations. This drops the throwaway torch.empty(...) dummies that callers with large kernel signatures had to hand-build purely to be introspected for shape/dtype, and removes the duplicated shape declarations between compile time and runtime allocation.

title: test(st): run the L0C matmul K-reduction accumulator under memory_planner=PTOAS
body:
## What

Parametrize `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_memory_reuse_acc_coalesce.py` by memory planner (`pypto`, `ptoas`) so the peeled `176x176` fp32 L0C accumulator if-phi — a `512x512x192` bf16 matmul that split-K peels into a `matmul` seed + `matmul_acc` K-reduction — is validated **on device under both planners**.

## Why

This test is the on-device numeric check for the L0C accumulator coalescing, but it only ran under the default **PyPTO** planner. The **PTOAS** side of that same accumulator handoff (the cb4181e8 must-alias lineage that #1995 built on) had solid codegen-level unit coverage (`test_if_phi_handle_ptoas`, `test_memory_planner_switch`, `test_ptoas_planner_views`) but **no on-device numeric guard**.

Under `memory_planner=PTOAS` the reuse/allocation passes are skipped and `MaterializeSemanticAliases` alone must keep the peeled accumulator if-phi on one addr-less `tile_buf` handle. If it doesn't, ptoas PlanMemory allocates two L0C buffers and the K-reduction silently drops accumulation — a wrong-result miscompile that compiles clean. This is exactly the class of defect that only an on-device numeric test catches.

## Verification

On device (a2a3), both variants pass; PTOAS `rel_err = 9.45e-08`, identical to PyPTO.

```
test_512x512x192_bf16_compiles_and_runs[pypto] PASSED
test_512x512x192_bf16_compiles_and_runs[ptoas] PASSED
```

title: feat(passes): add HoistScopeLocalAllocs to mark manual-scope hoistable allocs
body:
## Summary

Moves the manual-scope allocation-hoist decision (issue #1697) out of orchestration codegen's emit-time indent arithmetic and into an explicit IR fact, honoring the "strict 1-to-1 codegen" contract.

A `pl.manual_scope` is a **scheduling** region, not a **storage** region: a `tensor.create` inside it may be read by a task placed *after* the block, so its generated C++ declaration must be hoisted one scope out — otherwise the local dies at the closing brace and the after-scope reader fails to compile.

The new **`HoistScopeLocalAllocs`** pass stamps `hoistable_alloc` on every `tensor.create` that sits **directly** in a `RuntimeScopeStmt(manual=true)` body and whose result shape references no `Var` defined inside that body (i.e. is enclosing-scope-valid). Nested manual scopes are handled; only `Orchestration` functions are touched. Orchestration codegen's batched-alloc hoist gate now reads this attr instead of `IsAtManualScopeBodyIndent()` + an on-the-fly `ShapeDependsOnLocalVars` scan.

Threaded through every layer following the `ClassifyIterArgCarry` template:

- `IRProperty::HoistableAllocsMarked` + `PassProperties` + string mapping
- `PropertyVerifier` (`verify_hoistable_allocs_marked`) + registry entry
- `GenerateOrchestration` codegen precondition (guards against a skipped pass)
- `passes.h` factory, nanobind binding, `.pyi` stub, `pass_manager` insertion (after `MaterializeRuntimeScopes`)
- `python_printer` op-attr allowlist so the bool attr round-trips print → parse (binary `.pto` handles it generically by value type)
- docs `43-hoist_scope_local_allocs` (en + zh) + pass-manager overview

## Testing

- New pass unit tests (`test_hoist_scope_local_allocs.py`): static-marked, outside-scope-unmarked, for-nested-unmarked, shape-local-unmarked, idempotency, metadata, end-to-end pipeline
- Broad UT sweep green (transforms + codegen + printing + parser + serialization)
- End-to-end verified: `alloc_tensors(...)` is emitted before the `PTO2_SCOPE(MANUAL) {` header (the #1697 behavior), now driven by the IR attr

## Notes

- Orchestration-only in this PR. The distributed `_alloc_intermediates` (POSIX-shm pre-fork) hoisting is a distinct emission target and can adopt the same `hoistable_alloc` attr in a follow-up.

title: fix(jit): guard un-inferrable tuple/scalar return elements (#2016 follow-up)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #2016 (`b2f347fd`). That PR taught `_infer_return_type` to fill
un-inferrable tuple-return elements — a local with no `TensorMeta` (a TASK_ID
from `pl.spmd`, or `logits` unpacked from a dep call) — from the function's
**explicit** return annotation, copied **verbatim** (`ast.unparse`). Two cases
were unguarded and started failing at parse time (surfaced when kernels adopted
`jit_fn.compile(...)` for host wrappers, e.g. pypto-lib qwen3 decode):

- **Bare** element (`pl.Tensor`, no shape) → `ParserTypeError: Incomplete type annotation: pl.Tensor`.
- **Symbolic-shaped** element (`pl.Tensor[[BATCH, VOCAB], pl.FP32]`) → `NameError: name 'BATCH' is not defined`.

## Fix

- **Copy an explicit element only when it is a *complete* (subscripted) type**
  (`pl.Scalar[pl.TASK_ID]`, `pl.Tensor[[...], ...]`), folding module
  int/float/bool constants in its shape to literals (`[BATCH, VOCAB]` →
  `[16, 152064]`) so symbolic dims become concrete extents.
- **Drop the whole annotation only when it is dispensable** — a bare element is
  present AND no sibling element *requires* the annotation.

### Why dropping is safe (and when it is not)

A plain tensor return is re-inferable by the parser from its IR value once the
annotation is gone — the pre-#2016 behavior that worked for years. A **TASK_ID**,
by contrast, the parser **cannot** re-derive from a value; that is exactly why
#2016 added the copy. So the drop is gated:

| Return | Behavior |
| ------ | -------- |
| all-tensor bare tuple (qwen3 host wrapper) | annotation dropped → parser re-infers → compiles |
| Out-param + `pl.Scalar[pl.TASK_ID]` (#2016) | kept (TASK_ID preserved) |
| bare tensor-local + `TASK_ID` (the risky mix) | **not** dropped — TASK_ID kept; the bare element surfaces as a clear `Incomplete type annotation` the author must shape, instead of silently stripping the TASK_ID |

## Testing

- New unit tests in `tests/ut/jit/test_specializer.py`: bare element → dropped;
  bare element next to a TASK_ID → annotation kept; subscripted element with
  symbolic module constants → folded to literals; no `py_globals` → left symbolic.
- `test_specializer.py`: 104 passed. Full `tests/ut/jit/` passes (2 pre-existing
  `test_split_k` numerical failures reproduce on `main` without this change).
  ruff clean.

## Impact

Once merged, host-orchestrator kernels that return locals with (bare) tuple
annotations — e.g. pypto-lib qwen3 `qwen3_decode_host`, which blocks
pypto-serving #53 and pypto-lib #765 — compile again with **no kernel change**.

## Related

- Regression introduced by #2016 (`b2f347fd`, 2026-07-13).

title: [Feature] Support dynamic DistributedTensor context merges in PTO control flow
body:
### Summary

Support dynamically selecting a `DistributedTensor` across control-flow branches by carrying its base pointer and `CommContext` as synchronized SSA results. Until this is implemented, PTO codegen should continue rejecting merges whose branches yield different communication contexts.

### Motivation / Use Case

A direct alias of a distributed tensor can safely inherit the source tensor view, base pointer, and communication context. The same is true for loop carriers and `if` branches that refer to the same distributed allocation.

A genuinely dynamic selection is different:

```python
result = lhs
if cond:
    result = rhs
pld.tile.remote_load(result, peer=peer, offsets=[0, 0], shape=[16, 16])
```

When `lhs` and `rhs` belong to different communication domains, selecting only one static context can address the wrong remote window. Current PTO codegen therefore rejects this merge instead of silently miscompiling it.

Supporting the use case requires the selected data pointer and selected context to follow the same control-flow edge.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Keep the DSL unchanged. Lower a conflicting distributed-tensor merge conceptually as a paired control-flow result:

```mlir
%base, %ctx = scf.if %cond -> (!pto.ptr<i32>, !pto.ptr<i64>) {
  scf.yield %rhs_base, %rhs_ctx
} else {
  scf.yield %lhs_base, %lhs_ctx
}
%view = pto.make_tensor_view %base ...
```

The implementation should:

- Select the tensor base pointer and `CommContext` together.
- Reconstruct the statically typed tensor view after the merge.
- Preserve tensor offsets and view metadata for aliases of subviews.
- Extend the same paired-carry model to loops if loop iterations may switch allocations.
- Diagnose any path where only the tensor or only the context is merged.
- Retain the current same-context fast path and conservative rejection until the paired lowering is complete.

### Alternatives Considered

- Keep one branch context unconditionally: unsafe because it can route remote access through the wrong communication window.
- Select only the context: insufficient because the base pointer must follow the same branch.
- Yield the tensor view directly through `scf.if`: currently loses static dimensions needed by `pto.partition_view`; see #1533.
- Permanently prohibit cross-allocation merges: safe but prevents useful runtime selection patterns.

### Additional Context

Related: #1533, #1956

PR-03 establishes the conservative invariant: aliases and same-allocation control-flow carriers preserve their context, while conflicting contexts fail with an actionable internal diagnostic. This issue tracks the larger paired base/context control-flow design separately.

title: fix(codegen): Preserve distributed alias communication context
body:
## Summary

- Preserve each `DistributedTensor` communication-context binding through direct aliases, `if` merges that retain one allocation, and `for` / `while` carriers.
- Fail early with construct-specific internal diagnostics when distributed tensor metadata loses its `CommContext`.
- Reject `if` branches that merge different context SSAs, because choosing either static context can pair the other branch data pointer with the wrong remote-window table.
- Add regression coverage for direct alias propagation and conflicting-context rejection.
- Apply the configured brace style to existing single-line loops in the touched control-flow file so diff-scoped clang-tidy passes.

## Why

PTO codegen represents a distributed tensor with three coordinated pieces of state: its tensor view, backing base pointer, and a side-table mapping to the runtime `CommContext` pointer. Alias and structured-control-flow lowering already propagated the view and base pointer, but context propagation was optional on several paths. Losing that binding makes later remote or synchronization operations unable to resolve the correct communication domain.

A dynamic merge of tensors from different allocations cannot safely retain one branch context. Supporting that case requires selecting the base pointer and context together, then rebuilding the static tensor view. That larger design is tracked separately in #2027; this PR keeps the conservative rejection.

## User impact

Aliases and same-allocation control-flow carriers now remain valid inputs to distributed PTO operations. Invalid or unsupported metadata flows fail at the point where context is lost or conflicts, instead of silently selecting an incorrect communication window or failing later with a less actionable error.

## Testing

- `cmake --build build --parallel`
- `cmake --build build-pypto --parallel` using the existing Python 3.12 test environment
- `python -m pytest tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_distributed_pto_codegen.py -n auto --maxprocesses 8 -q` — 28 passed
- `pre-commit run --files src/codegen/pto/pto_codegen.cpp src/codegen/pto/pto_control_flow_codegen.cpp tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_distributed_pto_codegen.py`
- `python tests/lint/clang_tidy.py --diff-base HEAD`
- Full unit suite — 7,134 passed, 2 skipped, 1 unrelated environment failure in `test_no_dfx_without_output_prefix_is_ok`: the installed `_task_interface.CallConfig` lacks `enable_dump_args`

## Related issues

title: [Feature] Verify DistributedTensor CommContext provenance through PTO aliases
body:
### Summary

Make `DistributedTensor` communication-context provenance a fully verified PTO codegen invariant. Every distributed tensor alias and structured-control-flow carrier should preserve the same coordinated triple: tensor view, backing base pointer, and `CommContext` SSA. Missing metadata must fail at the point where it is lost, and conflicting `if` branches must remain rejected until paired base/context selection is supported.

### Motivation / Use Case

Cross-rank PTO operations use the tensor pointer together with the matching runtime `CommContext` to resolve peer window addresses. Retaining the view or base pointer without proving that the corresponding context follows the same allocation creates a correctness risk: later `remote_load`, `remote_store`, `put`, `notify`, or `wait` lowering may lack the communication domain or could be paired with the wrong remote-window table.

The happy paths currently depend on side-table propagation spread across direct assignments, `YieldStmt`, `IfStmt`, `ForStmt`, and `WhileStmt`. These paths should be validated explicitly rather than treating a missing context as an optional condition.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Keep the DSL and public API unchanged. In PTO codegen:

- Direct aliases inherit the source tensor view, base pointer, and `CommContext`.
- Same-allocation `if` results and `for` / `while` carriers retain the initialization context.
- Any distributed alias or yield with no context produces an actionable internal diagnostic.
- An `if` whose branches provide different contexts is rejected with an explanation that selecting one context could address the wrong communication window.
- Dynamic cross-allocation selection remains a separate design tracked by #2027; it requires selecting the base pointer and context together and rebuilding the static tensor view.
- Regression coverage includes direct aliases, consistent `if`, `for`, `while`, and conflicting-context rejection.

### Alternatives Considered

- Continue allowing an empty context side-table entry: defers the failure and obscures the metadata-loss source.
- Keep either branch context when an `if` conflicts: unsafe because the selected tensor data may belong to the other communication window.
- Implement dynamic paired selection in the same change: larger control-flow design with PTOAS static-view constraints; tracked separately in #2027.

### Additional Context

PR #2028 prototyped the conservative invariant and passed toolchain, pre-commit, clang-tidy, codegen, Linux/macOS unit, model, a5sim, and general system checks. Its distributed-system job failed `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_remote_store.py::TestL3RemoteStore::test_subview_halves`, leaving one remote-store half unwritten. That InCore test contains no alias or structured control flow and passed on `main` shortly before, so causality is unproven; nevertheless, distributed address-routing changes warrant dedicated hardware revalidation before reopening the implementation.

Closed prototype: #2028

Related dynamic-selection design: #2027

title: fix(lint): enforce pinned clang-tidy in CI and fix hidden findings
body:
## Summary

CI has been running **clang-tidy 14.0.0** while the project requires **21.1.0**, and `clang_tidy.py` only *warned* on the mismatch. An older clang-tidy silently ignores checks it does not know, so `misc-include-cleaner` (added in LLVM 17) **has never actually run in CI** — the check enabled by #215 / #219 was inert, and its findings accumulated behind a green check.

Root cause: the `clang-tidy` job runs in `localhost:5000/ci-py310:latest`, whose Ubuntu 22.04 base provides apt clang-tidy 14. The repo's `github_ci.Dockerfile` does pin `clang-tidy==21.1.0`, but it builds a different, amd64-only image (`ghcr.io/.../github-ci`) that only `system-tests-a5sim` uses, so the pin never reached the arm64 runner.

## Changes

**Make the pin real**
- `ci.yml`: the clang-tidy job installs the pinned clang-tidy, reading the version from `REQUIRED_VERSION` so the pin has a single source of truth, and passes the new `--strict-version`.
- `clang_tidy.py`: `--strict-version` fails when the version is mismatched *or* unparseable, so drift can never silently under-lint again. Local runs keep the soft warning, so a contributor with a different clang-tidy is not blocked.
- `clang_tidy.py`: cap the *default* worker count (CI passes `--jobs` explicitly and is unaffected).

**Fix the 193 findings the pinned version reports** (0 remain)
- 178 mechanical: 160 `misc-include-cleaner` (60 includes added, 89 removed), plus `braces-around-statements`, `use-emplace`, `raw-string-literal`, `loop-convert`, `use-nodiscard`, `unnecessary-value-param`.
- 15 by hand:
  - `unchecked-optional-access` x6 — added the missing `INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN`, or bound a reference so the guard and the dereference refer to the same object.
  - `performance-move-const-arg` x3 — `std::move` into a `const&` parameter never moved; dropped it (the by-value `attrs` correctly keeps its move).
  - `bugprone-optional-value-conversion` — stop unwrapping an optional just to re-wrap it.
  - `deadcode.DeadStores` — removed a write-only variable.
  - `bugprone-narrowing-conversions` — explicit `static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>`.
  - `bugprone-nondeterministic-pointer-iteration-order` x3 — `NOLINTNEXTLINE` with rationale. Each loop's effect is order-invariant (a set read only via `.count()`, a copy of unique keys, an any-match early return), so converting core pass containers to ordered ones would cost performance for no behavioral change.

## Testing

- [x] Full clang-tidy under 21.1.0: **0 project findings** (was 193)
- [x] Build green (223/223)
- [x] `pre-commit run` — all hooks pass (clang-format, cpplint, ruff, pyright)
- [x] Unit tests: 7132 passed, 2 skipped
- [x] `--strict-version` verified against a simulated clang-tidy 14 and an unparseable version (both exit 1); real 21.1.0 passes

## Notes for reviewers

- The fixes were produced with **openEuler GCC 12.3.1**, while CI uses **Ubuntu GCC 15**. `misc-include-cleaner` derives its symbol→header mapping from the libstdc++ on disk, so the 89 *removals* are the toolchain-sensitive part. This PR validates itself: because `clang_tidy.py` is in the diff, the script forces a **full** check, now on the pinned version, against CI's real toolchain.
- The runner image still ships clang-tidy 14 and is disconnected from the repo's Dockerfile. The pip-install step makes the job correct regardless, but refreshing `localhost:5000/ci-py310` is still worth doing separately.

title: refactor(ir): dedup BufferRootCollector into shared util
body:
## Summary

Consolidates the `BufferRootCollector` buffer-root analysis, which existed in three places with two divergent behaviours, into a single shared implementation.

- **Delete dead code**: `GenerateOrchestration` (orchestration codegen) constructed a `BufferRootCollector`, initialized it and visited the body, but never read its `buffer_roots` result — three lines of pure wasted work, now removed.
- **Add shared analysis** `include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/buffer_root_collector.{h,cpp}` (namespace `ir::buffer_root`), based on the more correct copy that previously lived inside `FuseCreateAssembleToSlice`. Its `SelectReturnRoot` matches a call's single (non-tuple) return value to the Out/InOut arg with the same shape+dtype, so a differently-typed InOut scratch is never mistaken for the real output buffer; ambiguous matches record no root (skipping an alias is always safe).
- **`FuseCreateAssembleToSlice`** drops its local copy and uses the shared class.
- **`DeriveCallDirections`** switches from the codegen copy to the shared class. Single-return root selection now goes through `SelectReturnRoot` instead of naively taking the first Out/InOut root.
- **Remove the naive `BufferRootCollector`** from codegen `orchestration_analysis.{h,cpp}`. Both remaining users are `ir::` transforms, so this also removes the `ir -> codegen` dependency for this analysis.

## Testing

- [x] `cmake --build build` clean
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_derive_call_directions.py` + `test_fuse_create_assemble_to_slice.py` — 46 passed

title: fix(codegen): Preserve distributed alias communication context
body:
## Summary

PTO codegen describes a `DistributedTensor` with three coordinated pieces of state: its tensor view, its backing base pointer, and a side-table mapping to the runtime `CommContext` pointer. Alias and structured-control-flow lowering already propagated the view and the base pointer, but `CommContext` propagation was **optional** on several paths — a missing binding was silently tolerated. A later `remote_load` / `remote_store` / `put` / `notify` / `wait` could then lose its communication domain, or pair a data pointer with the wrong remote-window table.

This makes the binding a verified invariant instead:

- Direct `AssignStmt` aliases inherit the source tensor view, base pointer, and `CommContext`.
- `YieldStmt`, `IfStmt`, `ForStmt`, and `WhileStmt` carriers retain the initialization context when they keep the same allocation.
- A `DistributedTensor` alias or yield that loses its context now fails **at the point where the metadata is lost**, with a construct-specific internal diagnostic, rather than surfacing later as a less actionable error.
- An `IfStmt` whose branches yield different context SSAs is rejected. The tensor result stays outside `scf.if` and aliases one backing SSA, so selecting either branch's context could pair the other branch's data pointer with the wrong remote-window table.

The DSL and public API are unchanged.

## Why the conflicting-`if` case is rejected rather than merged

Supporting a dynamic cross-allocation merge requires selecting the base pointer and the `CommContext` **together** and then rebuilding the static tensor view — a larger control-flow design under the PTOAS static-view constraints. That is tracked separately in #2027; this PR keeps the conservative rejection with an explanatory diagnostic.

## Testing

- `cmake --build build --parallel`
- `python -m pytest tests/ut/codegen/ -q` — 571 passed (including all 28 distributed PTO codegen tests)
- Full unit suite — 7,169 passed, 2 skipped. The single failure, `tests/ut/runtime/test_run_config.py::TestExecuteOnDeviceDfxValidation::test_no_dfx_without_output_prefix_is_ok`, reproduces identically on a clean `main` with these changes stashed: the installed `_task_interface.CallConfig` lacks `enable_dump_args`. It is a pre-existing environment issue, not a regression.
- `pre-commit run --files src/codegen/pto/pto_codegen.cpp src/codegen/pto/pto_control_flow_codegen.cpp tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_distributed_pto_codegen.py`
- `python tests/lint/clang_tidy.py --diff-base HEAD --strict-version` (pinned clang-tidy 21.1.0) — clean

## Regression coverage

New: direct-alias `CommContext` propagation, and conflicting-context `IfStmt` rejection. Consistent `if` / `for` / `while` carriers were already covered by the existing `test_tensor_view_preserves_*_distributed_metadata` tests.

## Notes

This re-lands the closed prototype #2028. Its brace-style cleanup in `IsDefinedInBranch` is no longer part of the diff — that formatting landed on `main` independently via #2030, so only the functional changes remain here.

## Related issues

Fixes #2029

- #2027 tracks dynamic paired base-pointer / `CommContext` selection across control flow.
- #1533 and #1956 describe the static-view and PTOAS constraints behind the current conservative lowering.

title: feat(ir): Verify valid shape bounds
body:
## Summary

- add tri-state proof utilities for symbolic valid-extent equality and ordering
- validate explicit valid-shape rank and provable `0 <= valid[i] <= shape[i]` bounds
- recursively enforce the invariant for tensor, tile, distributed, tuple, signature, local, loop-carried, and call-result types
- add focused verifier coverage for constant, symbolic, composite, and canonical full-shape cases

## Why

A shaped value can represent padded storage where only part of the physical shape is valid. Without a standing verifier invariant, malformed metadata such as a `[64, 68]` valid shape on `[64, 64]` storage can survive until a later compiler pass and fail far from its source. This change reports provable violations at the normal type-verification boundary while preserving genuinely unknown symbolic bounds.

## Impact

There is no new user-facing API. Compiler passes that create or propagate valid-shape metadata now receive early diagnostics for definite rank and bounds errors, providing the safety foundation for later valid-shape propagation work.

## Validation

- `cmake --build build --parallel`
- `python -m pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_type_check_pass.py tests/ut/ir/test_tensor_view_semantics.py tests/ut/ir/verifier/test_valid_shape_bounds.py -n auto --maxprocesses 8 -q` (67 passed)
- `pre-commit run --files include/pypto/ir/type_inference.h src/ir/op/type_inference.cpp src/ir/verifier/type_check_pass.cpp tests/ut/ir/verifier/test_valid_shape_bounds.py`

title: fix(ci): orphaned-task cleanup via task-submit --find + raise --timeout to 3600s
body:
## Summary

This PR bundles two related CI reliability changes to the device-job workflows.

### 1. Fix orphaned-task cleanup (`.github/actions/kill-orphaned-tasks`)
- The cleanup action matched task-submit output with `task-submit --list`, whose human-facing view truncates the command column to 77 chars. The full `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$CHECKOUT_PATH` grep never matched, so the cleanup was silently a no-op. Switch to `task-submit --find "$target"`, which matches against the untruncated COMMAND and prints bare task-ids.
- Pass `checkout-path` via an `env:` var (`CHECKOUT_PATH`) instead of inlining `${{ inputs.checkout-path }}` into the `run:` script, so a path with spaces or shell metacharacters cannot break the command or inject into it (`${{ }}` is textual pre-substitution before bash sees the script).
- Add observability: report the killed count, and surface `--find`/`--kill` failures with `::error::`/`::warning::` instead of failing silently.

### 2. Raise `task-submit --timeout` to 3600s (`ci.yml`, `daily_ci.yml`)
- Bump every `task-submit --timeout` from `1800s` to `3600s` (12 invocations in `ci.yml`, 2 in `daily_ci.yml`).
- `--timeout` governs the device-acquisition **queue wait** — raising it gives device jobs more tolerance for runner contention before task-submit gives up waiting for a card.
- `--max-time` (the run wall-clock cap: 1800 / 900 / 600) is deliberately **left unchanged**, so this only grants more queue-wait headroom, not longer executions. The `--timeout 60` in the kill-orphaned-tasks path and `--task-queue-timeout=1800` in the batched system-tests step are different flags and are intentionally untouched.

## Testing
- [ ] CI config change — validated by the CI runs on this PR.

## Notes
- `--find` requires `task-submit >= 2026-07-14` on the runner. The cleanup step now `exit 1`s if `--find` is unavailable ("fail safe rather than sorry"), so the runner-side tool update should land in lockstep with this merge.

title: [Performance] Qwen3-14B decode: native fa_fused ~2.3x slower than CANN FAI (paged_attention_cce) — A2/A3 C2V/V2C GM round-trip
body:
## Background

In pypto-lib (`models/qwen3/14b`), the Qwen3-14B **decode** path originally used a
pypto-native fused flash-attention, `fa_fused` (introduced in pypto-lib #656,
reapplied in #756). In pypto-lib **#765** it was **replaced** by an external CANN
`FusedInferAttentionScore` (FAI) kernel, `paged_attention_cce`, because the native
kernel was slower on A2/A3 (910B). This issue asks pypto to analyze the codegen-level
root cause of that gap.

Data source: the controlled TraCR/PMU profiling in **pypto-lib#622**
(CCE `spmd_paged_attention_highperf` vs in-layer `fa_fused`), plus an in-decode
makespan measurement (`fa_fused` ≈ 100µs slower than the `paged_attention_cce` that
replaced it). Numbers below are from those runs, not a fresh local reproduction.

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `de953d1` (branch: `test/ptoas-matmul-kreduction-st`) |
| simpler | `c94aa9f` (matches pin) |
| ptoas | `0.48` (matches pin) |
| pto-isa | local `016396b`; pypto pin `83d0131` — **off pin** (`PTO_ISA_ROOT` unset, active clone ambiguous) |
| CANN | npu-smi 26.0.rc1 |

Diagnosis: **pypto** — codegen/lowering. On A2/A3 the fused cube+vector root's
C2V/V2C boundary still routes through a GM pipe buffer (`InjectGMPipeBuffer` is
backend-gated off for 910B), so fusion buys load-balance but not GM-traffic savings.

Related: pypto-lib#622, pypto-lib#765, pypto-lib#656, simpler#899, simpler#986.

---

### Summary

At the Qwen3-14B decode attention shape (**batch 16, 40 q-heads, 8 KV heads (5:1
GQA), head_dim 128, context 4096, block 128**), the pypto-native fused decode
attention `fa_fused` — QK→softmax→SV fused into **one mixed cube+vector root**,
grid-strided over a compacted seq-block work table (`fa_work_build` → `fa_fused` →
`online_softmax`) — is materially slower than the hand-written CANN
`FusedInferAttentionScore` (`paged_attention_cce`) that replaced it in pypto-lib
#765.

**Suspected pypto-side root cause (A2/A3, 910B):** the fused root's C2V/V2C boundary
**still routes through a GM pipe buffer** because `InjectGMPipeBuffer` is
backend-gated (disabled on 910B). So each fused block pays an **AIC↔AIV GM
round-trip** — the fusion delivers the intended load-balance win (~1.25× of ideal)
but **not** the AIC↔AIV GM-traffic elimination it was meant to provide. On A5 the
L2-swimlane path keeps this boundary on-chip; on A2/A3 it does not. This is
consistent with pypto-lib#622's PMU finding that the gap is **MTE2-pipe idle from
cross-core synchronization stalls**, not an HBM bandwidth ceiling.

The ask: confirm whether the A2/A3 C2V/V2C GM round-trip is the dominant cost, and
whether `InjectGMPipeBuffer` (or an equivalent on-chip C2V/V2C path) can be enabled
for 910B so a pypto-native fused attention can reach FAI/CCE parity.

### Git Commit ID

`de953d105f8fddaa4ab37a1c7d3669abc0eafee2`

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B (a2a3)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Reproduction Script

The native `fa_fused` was removed from pypto-lib `main` by #765, so reproduce from
its parent commit, or use the controlled setup from pypto-lib#622.

**A) In-context (pypto-lib), against the parent of #765:**
```bash
# pypto-lib @ 4ee8cf4~1 (fa_fused still present)
python models/qwen3/14b/decode_fwd.py -p a2a3 -d 0 --enable-l2-swimlane
# read fa_fused on-core / makespan contribution from the L2 swimlane
```

**B) Isolated like-for-like (pypto-lib#622 method, TraCR on 910B):**
- CCE: `spmd_paged_attention_highperf` case `b16_h40_kv8_s4096_bs128_fp16`
  (simpler#899).
- pypto: in-layer `fa_fused` from the Qwen3-14B decode layer, `--max-seq`.
- Build simpler with `BUILD_TRACR=ON`, `_DEFAULT_RUNTIME = "tensormap_and_ringbuffer"`,
  post-process with `tracr_process`, view in Perfetto. Full recipe in pypto-lib#622.

### Expected Performance

Parity (within a few %) with the CANN FAI / CCE kernel. Per pypto-lib#765, the CANN
`paged_attention_cce` runs **~235µs @ 98% core occupancy** on the B16 decode shape;
a pypto-native fused attention should land in the same envelope rather than +100µs.

### Actual Performance

- **On-core attention busy time (pypto-lib#622, TraCR):** CCE ~**548µs** vs pypto
  `fa_fused` ~**1263µs** → **~2.3×** (~715µs overhead).
- **In-decode makespan contribution:** `fa_fused` ≈ **100µs slower** than the
  `paged_attention_cce` that replaced it in #765 (the earlier "on par ~233µs vs
  ~235µs" claim in #765 did not hold up under this measurement).

### Profiling Data (Optional)

See pypto-lib#622 for the TraCR Perfetto traces (`cce_b16_h40_kv8_s4096_bs128_fp16.json`,
`qwen3_14b_decode.json`) and the PMU MTE2-idle analysis. The pre-#765 `fa_fused`
design note in `decode_fwd.py` states the A2/A3 GM round-trip explicitly:

> "the fused root's C2V/V2C boundary still routes through a GM pipe buffer on 910B
> (`InjectGMPipeBuffer` is backend-gated), so fusing does NOT avoid the AIC↔AIV GM
> round-trip on A2/A3 — the win here is load balance, not GM savings. (On A5 the
> L2-swimlane path keeps it on-chip.)"

### Additional Context

- This is the pypto-codegen-side counterpart to the measurement-focused
  pypto-lib#622; filed here per request to route the `InjectGMPipeBuffer` /
  C2V/V2C-boundary question to the pypto codegen team.
- Note the pto-isa version divergence in the table above; the reported numbers come
  from pypto-lib#622's controlled TraCR runs and the in-decode measurement, not a
  fresh reproduction on this exact local toolchain.

title: refactor(ir): dedup IsBuiltinOp into ir::op_predicates
body:
## Summary

The IR layer duplicated the builtin-op classifier and reverse-`#include`d a codegen header — a layering violation, since codegen depends on IR, never the reverse. This PR removes both.

- **Dedup `IsBuiltinOp`.** The `tile.`/`tensor.`/`system.`/`array.` namespace-family predicate had four copy-pasted implementations: the canonical one in codegen `orchestration_analysis.cpp`, plus file-local copies in `return_lineage_utils.cpp`, `verify_orchestration_references.cpp`, and `buffer_root_collector.cpp` (the latter two even carried a "if a third reader appears, promote to a shared util" comment — the third reader already existed). Promoted to a single canonical home in `ir::op_predicates`, next to the other string-based op predicates. codegen keeps its unqualified call sites via a thin inline forward.
- **Remove the reverse dependency.** With the predicate in the IR layer, five IR passes/verifiers (`derive_call_directions`, `auto_derive_task_dependencies`, `materialize_runtime_scopes`, `window_externalization`, `verify_call_directions`) no longer `#include "pypto/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_analysis.h"`. IR→codegen includes are now zero.

This is the follow-up that #1994 explicitly deferred — after moving the wrapper-direction and return-to-param analyses out of codegen, its notes read: *"derive_call_directions_pass.cpp still imports the codegen layer for BufferRootCollector / IsBuiltinOp ... closing it properly is its own change."* This PR is that change (rebased on top of #1994).

Behavior-preserving: `name.find(x) == 0` and `name.rfind(x, 0) == 0` are equivalent prefix checks.

## Testing

- Build: full `cmake --build` green (188/188 targets, `pypto_core` relinked).
- IR transforms + verifier + codegen UTs: **2811 passed** (rebased on #1994, includes its new tests).
- Code review: pass. clang-tidy: no new findings attributable to this diff.

title: feat(ir): Preserve type metadata across calls and control flow
body:
## Summary

- recursively substitute dynamic shape and view metadata through Tensor, DistributedTensor, Tile, and nested Tuple call returns
- preserve authoritative in-scope metadata through SSA aliases and `if`/`for`/`while` carriers
- enforce strict control-flow boundary agreement for kind, dtype, physical shape, effective valid shape, tensor padding, and distributed window identity
- reject symbolically unknown joins when no runtime guard is emitted

## Why

Valid-region inference is only sound when its metadata survives function calls and control-flow joins. Previously, call substitution covered only a subset of type metadata, SSA could revive stale variable identities, and joins did not consistently validate effective valid regions.

This follows PR #2037 and implements the “Preserve type metadata across calls and control flow” step of the unified valid-shape plan.

## Testing

- `cmake --build build --parallel`
- `python -m pytest tests/ut --ignore=tests/ut/runtime -n auto --maxprocesses 8 -q` — 6763 passed, 2 skipped
- focused parser/SSA/verifier/codegen suite after rebase — 153 passed
- `python tests/lint/clang_tidy.py --diff-base HEAD`
- `pre-commit run --files <changed-files>`

## Scope

No public API, operator propagation, codegen behavior, or documentation changes.
