title: fix(language): preserve Call attrs when an annotation overrides the call type
body:
## Summary

The DSL parser silently dropped **every attr** on a call to a function declared *later* in the same `@pl.program` class.

An annotated assignment whose call type is less precise than the annotation rebuilds the `Call` to carry the annotated type (`ast_parser.py`, `visit_AnnAssign`). That rebuild used the `Call(op, args, kwargs, type, span)` overload — which has no `attrs` slot — so the attrs were simply not carried over.

A forward-referenced callee hits this on *every* call: `gvar_to_func` is filled incrementally in declaration order, so a callee declared below the caller is still unknown → the call's return type infers to `UnknownType` → the annotation always overrides it → the rebuild fires.

Two programs differing only in the order of the two `def`s therefore parsed differently:

```python
r: pl.Tensor[[64], pl.FP32] = self.kernel(
    x, dst, attrs={"arg_directions": [pl.adir.input, pl.adir.output_existing]}
)
```

| declaration order | parsed result |
| ----------------- | ------------- |
| `kernel` above `main` (backward ref) | `attrs=['arg_directions']`, `dirs=[Input, OutputExisting]` |
| `kernel` below `main` (forward ref) | `attrs=[]`, `dirs=[]` — silently empty |

### Impact

Everything carried in `Call.attrs` was affected on a forward-referenced call, not just `arg_directions`:

- `arg_direction_overrides` — a user's `pl.no_dep(arg)` was silently ignored, so `DeriveCallDirections` had nothing to override and the slot took the very dependency the user opted out of.
- `dump_vars` — a requested `pl.dump_tag` / `dumps=` silently did not dump.
- `device` — the per-dispatch device subset was lost.

It also broke `print -> reparse` for any program whose call graph cannot be emitted callee-first — e.g. mutually recursive Group wrappers, where whichever wrapper is printed first loses its call attrs on reparse.

## Fix

Carry `attrs` through the rebuild by using the attrs-taking overload, matching what the sibling rebuild on the tile-subscript path already does:

```python
 value_expr = ir.Call(
-    value_expr.op, value_expr.args, value_expr.kwargs, override_type, value_expr.span
+    value_expr.op,
+    value_expr.args,
+    value_expr.kwargs,
+    value_expr.attrs,   # <- was dropped
+    override_type,
+    value_expr.span,
 )
```

`Submit` is unaffected: it derives from `Expr`, not `Call`, so `isinstance(expr, ir.Call)` never matches a `Submit` and this path cannot lower one (pass-submit-awareness rule 3).

## Testing

New `TestForwardReferencedCallee` in `tests/ut/language/parser/test_call_arg_directions_dsl.py`:

- `test_attrs_survive_regardless_of_declaration_order` — parametrized `backward_ref` / `forward_ref` over the *same* program, so the test pins the asymmetry itself.
- `test_no_dep_override_attr_survives_forward_reference` — the `pl.no_dep` marker attr survives too.

Both were confirmed to **fail without the fix** (`forward_ref` fails, `backward_ref` passes) and pass with it.

- [x] Full unit suite green: 7198 passed, 2 skipped
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format` / pyright / header + english-only lints clean

title: test(ir): convert DeriveCallDirections tests to Before/Expected style
body:
Rebased onto `main` now that #2045 has merged, so this is a single test + docs commit with no parser changes in the diff.

## Summary

The transform tests in `test_derive_call_directions.py` were split between two styles. Most used the project-standard Before/Expected + `assert_structural_equal` pattern, but two classes asserted the pass output by reaching into the IR:

```python
# TestNoDepOverride
assert _dirs(calls[0]) == [ir.ArgDirection.Input, ir.ArgDirection.NoDep, ir.ArgDirection.OutputExisting]

# TestMaterializeWrapperDirections
assert self._dirs_of(After, "group") == [ir.ParamDirection.In, ir.ParamDirection.Out]
```

Both are now Before/Expected, so every transform test states the whole expected IR rather than the one field the author happened to check:

- **`TestNoDepOverride`** — the derived vector and the surviving `pl.no_dep` marker are spelled as `attrs={"arg_directions": [...], "arg_direction_overrides": [...]}`, which is exactly the printer's rendering of the marked call.
- **`TestMaterializeWrapperDirections`** — the materialized signature is spelled as `pl.Out` / `pl.InOut` on the wrapper's own parameter, where `Before` declared a bare tensor.

The `TestVerify*` classes keep `pytest.raises`: they feed deliberately ill-formed IR to the verifier, and a rejection has no "Expected IR" to compare against.

## This widens coverage

`Expected` pins call-site consequences the old assertions never looked at:

- never-demote case: `main`'s first arg stays `output_existing` (it would silently degrade to `input` if the monotone merge regressed) — the old test only checked the wrapper signature.
- mutually-recursive case: the R-prior promotion *inside* the cycle (`self.z(...)` first-writer `output_existing`, then `self.kern(...)` promoted to `inout`) — previously unchecked.

## Cleanups

- Dropped the now-dead `_UserCallCollector` / `_user_calls` / `_dirs` / `_dirs_of` helpers.
- Removed the class-level fixture that downgraded `TestNoDepOverride` to property-verification-only. It was working around test kernels that declared no return annotation (the reparsed call's type degraded to `UnknownType`); annotating them lets the class run under the default print -> reparse roundtrip instrument instead.
- Removed the empty `PassContext([])` on the mutually-recursive test — with #2045 merged the cyclic program round-trips, so it too runs under full roundtrip verification.
- Two stale comments deleted: the claim that the printer never emits `arg_direction_overrides` (it does, generically via `PrintAttrValue`), and the claim that the cyclic roundtrip failure was a printer dependency-order limitation (it was the parser bug fixed in #2045).

## Testing

- [x] `test_derive_call_directions.py`: 41 passed, now all Before/Expected and all under the default roundtrip instrument
- [x] Full unit suite green after rebase: 7217 passed, 2 skipped
- [x] `ruff` / pyright / markdownlint / header + english-only lints clean
- [x] Docs updated (`34-derive_call_directions.md`, en + zh-cn)

title: [RFC] IR cannot express scalar aliasing: two IR names for one runtime extent
body:
### Summary

PyPTO's IR has no way to state that two scalar expressions denote the **same runtime value**. A `pl.dynamic("M")` symbol lives only in *types* (as a shape placeholder); a runtime scalar such as `pl.tensor.dim(x, 0)`, a `pl.Scalar` parameter, or a `pl.tensor.read(...)` lives only in *values*. Nothing in the IR relates the two. Scalar equality is decided by `structural_equal` plus an arithmetic analyzer that can only prove *algebraic* identities, so two distinct `Var`s that hold the same number at runtime are, to the compiler, two different extents. Every "same extent, two names" program is therefore a latent parse/verify failure, and type inference has to paper over the gap with heuristics.

Related: #1285 (structural `var.type == value.type` on every AssignStmt — the check that trips on an alias), #594.

### Motivation

This is not hypothetical: it is the root cause of the Qwen3-14B prefill regression from #2043.

Caller and callee share one module-level symbol, `PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN = pl.dynamic("PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN")`:

```python
def prefill_layer(hidden_states: pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, HIDDEN], pl.BF16],
                  ..., out: pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, HIDDEN], pl.BF16], layer_idx)
                  -> pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, HIDDEN], pl.BF16]: ...

def prefill_fwd(hidden_states: pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, HIDDEN], pl.BF16], ...):
    prefill_tokens = pl.tensor.dim(hidden_states, 0)          # a SECOND name for the same extent
    for layer_idx in pl.range(num_layers_actual):
        with pl.scope():
            layer_next_hidden = pl.create_tensor([prefill_tokens, HIDDEN], dtype=pl.BF16)
            hidden_states = prefill_layer(hidden_states, ..., layer_next_hidden, layer_idx)
```

`DeduceCallReturnType` binds the callee placeholder `PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN -> prefill_tokens` (from the `out` argument), so the call's return type comes back as `pl.Tensor[[prefill_tokens, 5120]]` while `hidden_states` is declared `pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, 5120]]`. The parser rejects the reassignment:

```
ParserTypeError: Cannot reassign 'hidden_states' with a different type:
  was pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, 5120], pl.BF16],
  got pl.Tensor[[prefill_tokens, 5120], pl.BF16]
```

Both types denote the *same* extent — `prefill_tokens` is *defined as* dim 0 of `hidden_states`, whose type says that dim is `PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN`. The compiler simply cannot say so.

Dropping the binding heuristic does not help; it just moves the failure, and the new error text is itself an admission of the gap:

```
Dynamic type variable 'TOKENS_DYN' has conflicting bindings TOKENS_DYN and n
that are not provably equal ...; cross-function calls do not emit a runtime shape guard
```

That symbols are *type-level only* is explicit in codegen — `src/codegen/tensor_op_codegen.cpp` (the `tensor.dim` orchestration op) notes that for a dynamic dim `GenerateExprString` returns the symbol name, "which is not a valid C++ identifier in the orchestration scope", and therefore reads the TaskArg descriptor instead.

**Consequences today**

- `DeduceCallReturnType` carries an ad-hoc preference order between a self-bound placeholder, a constant actual, and a symbolic alias. That preference *is* the bug above.
- `InlineFunctions` performs no symbol substitution, so a callee's placeholder can never be soundly resolved to the caller's actual extent.
- Any pass that compares extents structurally is one alias away from a false mismatch.

### Design

This RFC asks for a **general** mechanism; it does not propose one implementation. Three directions, roughly in increasing order of ambition:

**(1) Bind dyn symbols as first-class SSA values at the function boundary.**

Give a function a signature-level binding list, so the symbol *is* the extent of the argument that declares it:

```
func prefill_fwd(hidden_states: Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, 5120], BF16], ...)
  where PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN := dim(hidden_states, 0)          # <-- new: symbol has a definition
```

The analyzer can then substitute, `tensor.dim(x, i)` becomes redundant (it folds to the symbol), and codegen has something to emit. This is analogous to TVM's `PrimFunc.buffer_map` / `T.match_buffer`, which is exactly what makes `A.shape[0] == n` *known* rather than *assumed*.

**(2) An explicit equality/assume constraint node.**

```python
pl.assume(n == PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN)     # feeds the arith analyzer; no code emitted
```

Cheap and local, but it puts the burden on the user and is unchecked.

**(3) A canonical scalar-alias structure (union-find) consulted by `ProveValidExtentEqual`.**

Passes union scalars they know to be equal (`n := tensor.dim(x, 0)` with `x : [M, ...]` unions `n` and `M`); extent proofs consult the representative. Keeps the IR unchanged, but the alias set must survive passes and serialization.

### Affected Files

Indicative, for direction (1):

- `include/pypto/ir/function.h` — **Modify** — signature-level symbol bindings
- `src/ir/op/type_inference.cpp` — **Modify** — `DeduceCallReturnType` unifies against bound symbols instead of guessing a preferred actual
- `src/ir/transforms/inline_functions_pass.cpp` — **Modify** — substitute callee symbols with caller actuals
- `src/ir/arith/analyzer.cpp` — **Modify** — teach `ProveValidExtentEqual` about symbol bindings
- `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp` — **Modify** — emit symbol definitions from the declaring argument
- `docs/en/dev/ir/` + `docs/zh-cn/dev/ir/` — **Modify** — document the value/type duality of dynamic dims

### Testing Plan

- Parser: a caller and callee sharing a `pl.dynamic` symbol, with a temp sized from `pl.tensor.dim`, reassigned into a loop-carried var (the Qwen3 prefill shape) — must type-check and round-trip.
- Type inference: an extent supplied by two different arguments (identity, constant, and symbolic alias) must resolve without a heuristic preference order.
- Analyzer: `ProveValidExtentEqual(tensor.dim(x, 0), M)` where `x : Tensor[[M, ...]]` must return `kTrue`.
- Codegen: every symbol referenced as a value must be defined before first use in the emitted host code.
- Inline: an inline callee declaring a symbol must behave correctly when called with a statically-shaped tensor *and* with a symbolic one.

### Alternatives Considered

**Fold `pl.tensor.dim(x, i)` onto the declared extent in Orchestration bodies** (the fix now landing for the Qwen3 regression). It removes the most common alias source and makes the symbol a real host value in orchestration codegen, but it is a *narrowing*, not a solution. Still uncovered:

- a scalar **parameter** that is semantically a tensor's extent — `def f(n: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32], x: pl.Tensor[[N_DYN, H]])` cannot state `n == N_DYN`;
- a caller symbol and a callee symbol known equal at runtime;
- an extent read at runtime (`pl.tensor.read(seq_lens, [b])`);
- Inline/InCore callees, where folding is *unsound* — the callee's placeholder is not the caller's, and `InlineFunctions` does not substitute it;
- any extent derived through arithmetic the analyzer cannot invert.

### Open Questions

- Should a symbol binding be part of the **function signature** (checked at every call site) or a body-level statement?
- What happens when two arguments declare the same symbol with genuinely different runtime extents? Today this is silently accepted (no runtime shape guard is emitted). Should the signature imply a guard, a verifier error, or stay unchecked?
- Do `Tile` extents need the same treatment, or is the tensor/host boundary sufficient?

title: feat(ir): Intersect valid regions for load, slice, and extract
body:
## Summary

Implements [brief 08 — Intersect valid regions for window reads](docs/en/dev/proposals/unified_valid_shape_prs/08-window-reads.md) of the unified `valid_shape` series (follows #2043).

A window read could return a full-valid result even when its window lay over the source's invalid padding, or ran off the physical edge of the source — exposing garbage as real data. `tensor.slice`, `tile.slice`, `tile.load` and `tile.extract` now share one rule, per dimension:

```text
available    = clamp(source_valid - offset, 0, window)
result_valid = min(requested_valid, available)
```

so a read never widens past the source valid region, the requested valid region, or the result window. An explicit `valid_shape` is now a **request** that narrows the result and can no longer widen it.

The rule lives in one place — `InferWindowReadValidShape` in `type_inference.h/cpp` — so tensor and tile get identical semantics and diagnostics.

## The non-clamping contract

A read without `clamp` **asserts** that its window lies inside the source: `offset + extent <= source_physical`. Provable violations are rejected; relations that stay symbolic are trusted, because that inequality *is* the operator's precondition, not a guess.

Under it a fully-valid source keeps a fully-valid window, so no guard expression is built and **in-bounds reads of unpadded sources are unchanged**. The intersection only bites when the source is genuinely partially valid, or when a read opts into clamping.

This reading is forced by the brief's own `drop_dims` requirement (an erased axis must be provably valid). The alternative — emitting a guard whenever in-bounds is unprovable — would give `x[i, :]` a validity of `min(max(N-i,0),1)`, not provably 1, and reject scalar indexing across the tree (e.g. `src[phys, :size]` in the paged-gather tests).

Expressions are built proof-first: a `min`/`max`/`sub` term is emitted only when the arithmetic analyzer cannot already settle the comparison, so constant arithmetic folds and no redundant nesting survives into a type.

## `clamp=True`

Sanctions a ragged read: the window may overhang and the valid region is cut back to the source edge.

| Op | `clamp` | Why |
| -- | ------- | --- |
| `tensor.slice` | ✅ | The emitted view shape is clamped (`min(shape, parent - offset)`) and the strided-Tensor runtime enforces the bound. |
| `tile.load` | ✅ | The DMA only fetches the valid extent; the destination tile is free to overhang. |
| `tile.slice` | ❌ | `pto.subview` is a pure view (`CheckSubviewTileCompat` does no bounds work) and the Mat/Vec fold in `CanonicalizeTileSlice` turns the window into a `tile.extract`, whose ISA TEXTRACT bounds are hard. |
| `tile.extract` | ❌ | Same — TEXTRACT bounds are hard. |

**Nothing can clamp an on-chip window**, so `tile.slice` rejects an overhang and the diagnostic says why, rather than naming a flag it cannot honour. Threading `clamp` into `tile.extract` would have silenced the ISA check and emitted an out-of-bounds TEXTRACT — a loud compile error traded for a silent hardware fault.

## Behavior change

**A fixed-width read whose overhang is statically provable is now a hard error** rather than silently full-valid. Three in-tree call sites declared the intent they already relied on:

- `test_pto_codegen_paged_attn_multi_config.py` — the motivating real case: a 64-wide unroll read of a **2-element** block table. Only the first `n_blocks` entries are ever addressed and the runtime already clamped it; now says `clamp=True`.
- `test_torch_codegen.py::test_tensor_slice_out_of_bounds_is_padded` — rows 64–128 of a 96-row source; now says `clamp=True`, still asserts the tail is padded.
- `test_pto_codegen.py::test_dynamic_tensor_unary_expr_var_is_collected_and_non_invertible` — loaded 16 rows from a tensor whose dim is `Neg(V_NEG)`, i.e. provably ≤ 0. The impossible load was incidental scaffolding; the test's subject (a `Neg` dim reaching the arg-unpacking inverter as non-invertible) is unchanged.

Symbolic offsets stay trusted, so the common dynamic-loop idiom still compiles unchanged.

Also: `drop_dims` now requires the erased axis to be **provably valid**, since rank reduction leaves the axis nothing left to say.

## Deviations from the brief (recorded per the series rules)

1. **`clamp` is scoped to `tensor.slice` + `tile.load`**, not slicing generally — for the hardware reason above. Tensor/tile parity of the *valid-region rule* is preserved (one shared helper); only the physical-overhang sanction differs, because the substrate genuinely does.
2. **Lower-rank windows are not intersected.** `tensor.slice` and `tile.load` both accept a window of lower rank than the source (e.g. a 2D window over a 3D parent). `OptimizeOrchTensors` materializes those as *strides*, so they are not a rectangle in source coordinates and intersecting them would target the wrong axes; they keep the validity they are given. Rank mismatch between `valid_shape` and the window still rejects.
3. **Docs are deferred** to the series' final documentation PR (brief 04), per the plan's series-wide rules. This description is the auditable source.

## Testing

- **+35 focused tests** across `tests/ut/ir/operators/test_tensor_ops.py` and `test_tile_ops.py`: full and partial sources, explicit validity (intersect, not replace), nonzero offsets, static folding, symbolic offsets, static OOB, negative offsets, rank mismatch, clamp at each edge, drop-dim success/failure, pad inheritance, lower-rank fallback, and print/parse round trips for both `tensor.slice(clamp=True)` and `tile.load(clamp=True)`.
- Full unit suite: **7272 passed**, 2 skipped (pre-existing environmental skips), 0 failed.
- `pre-commit` all hooks pass; diff-based `clang-tidy` clean; `pyright` clean.

title: feat(runtime): Allow inherited immutable host tensors

## Summary

This PR adds support for passing immutable host tensors to `DistributedWorker` through inherited process memory.

It is the PyPTO runtime companion for [pypto-serving#70](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-serving/pull/70).

## Changes

- Add the `inherited_host_tensors` argument to `DistributedWorker`.
- Retain registered CPU tensors before worker processes are forked.
- Allow registered tensors to be used as read-only `In` arguments without shared-memory staging.
- Continue requiring shared memory for `Out` and `InOut` arguments.
- Validate that registered objects are contiguous CPU tensors.
- Add unit tests for supported and rejected cases.
- Document the behavior in both English and Chinese.

## Motivation

Large immutable serving weights can be inherited by forked worker processes through copy-on-write mappings. This avoids copying those tensors into shared memory before worker creation.

title: fix(language): Fold tensor.dim onto its dyn-dim symbol; add Qwen3 prefill CI
body:
## Problem

A tensor's declared extent **is** its runtime extent, so reading it back with `pl.tensor.dim` minted a *second* scalar naming the same quantity. Nothing downstream can prove that copy equal to the `pl.dynamic()` symbol the tensor types carry, so every shape built from the copy disagreed structurally with the shapes built from the symbol.

That is what broke Qwen3-14B prefill in pypto-serving after #2043 (which turned on the cross-function return-type substitution that had, until then, been a silent no-op — `As<ShapedType>` never matched a `TensorType`, so `DeduceCallReturnType` returned the callee's declared types verbatim):

```python
PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN = pl.dynamic("PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN")

def prefill_fwd(hidden_states: pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, HIDDEN], pl.BF16], ...):
    prefill_tokens = pl.tensor.dim(hidden_states, 0)          # a SECOND name for the same extent
    for layer_idx in pl.range(num_layers_actual):
        with pl.scope():
            layer_next_hidden = pl.create_tensor([prefill_tokens, HIDDEN], dtype=pl.BF16)
            hidden_states = prefill_layer(hidden_states, ..., layer_next_hidden, layer_idx)
```

The callee declares the *same* symbol, so `DeduceCallReturnType` bound `PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN -> prefill_tokens` from the `out` argument and returned `pl.Tensor[[prefill_tokens, 5120]]`, while `hidden_states` is declared `pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, 5120]]`:

```
ParserTypeError: Cannot reassign 'hidden_states' with a different type:
  was pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, 5120], pl.BF16],
  got pl.Tensor[[prefill_tokens, 5120], pl.BF16]
```

Both types denote the same extent. The compiler simply cannot say so — see RFC #2047 for the general gap.

## Fix

**Parser** — in an Orchestration body, `pl.tensor.dim(x, i)` folds to the extent `x`'s type already names, and the Python name binds *straight to that symbol* instead of copying it into a `Let`. The direct binding is the point: a copy would be what lands in every shape built from the name, recreating the alias immediately. One runtime extent, one IR name.

**Codegen** — orchestration entry now defines each symbol the emitted body references, once, from the task-arg descriptor of the first parameter declaring it:

```cpp
    // Dynamic-dim symbols (extent of the declaring argument)
    int64_t PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN = (int64_t)orch_args.tensor(0).ref().shapes[0];
```

This also fixes a **pre-existing** bug: `pl.create_tensor([M, N])` emitted `{static_cast<uint32_t>(M), ...}` with `M` undefined — host C++ that does not compile. Any model sizing a temp with a dyn symbol was silently broken.

The fold is **Orchestration-only**, which is exactly where the symbol is a value. An Inline/InCore callee's placeholder is not the caller's — `InlineFunctions` does not substitute callee symbols, and the callee may be reached with a statically-shaped actual — so there `tensor.dim` stays a genuine runtime read (pinned by a test).

## CI

Adds a Qwen3-14B **prefill** step to the `pypto-lib-model` job, mirroring the existing decode step. Prefill exercises the dynamic-shape host path decode does not (a `pl.dynamic` token axis, a temp sized from `pl.tensor.dim`, and a layer result reassigned into a loop-carried var), which is why this regression reached pypto-serving unseen.

## Tests

`tests/ut/ir/parser/test_cross_function_call_return_type.py` (5 new):
- the fold itself, and the Qwen3 loop-carried-reassignment regression;
- reassigning a folded name must never write **through** the alias into the symbol (the symbol names an argument's extent — it is immutable). Scopes are a stack, so the guard tests the Var the name is bound to rather than tracking names;
- every axis spelling folds (`dim(x, axis=0)`, a named constant) — the printer normalizes them all to `dim(x, 0)`, so a spelling that did not fold would fold on reparse and break the round-trip;
- an Inline callee keeps `tensor.dim` as a runtime read.

`tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen_more.py` (1 new): each symbol is read once from the declaring argument's descriptor, and is defined before the use that needs it.

Full `tests/ut/`: **7240 passed, 2 skipped**. ruff / clang-format / clang-tidy / pyright clean.

## Notes

title: feat(ir): preserve valid regions through unary and reduction ops
body:
Implements brief 11 of the unified `valid_shape` series (*Preserve valid regions through unary and reduction operations*). Follows #2031 (canonicalization), #2037 (proof/bounds), and #2043 (type boundaries).

## Summary

- **Tensor unary + cast now preserve the input's valid region.** `neg`, `abs`, `recip`, `exp`, `log`, `sqrt`, `rsqrt`, `sin`, `cos` and `cast` each returned a bare `TensorType(shape, dtype)`, so a partial region silently widened back to the full allocation and padding became indistinguishable from real data. They now carry the input's effective valid shape onto a **fresh** result — default layout, empty stride, null padding, no source memref. Tile unary already did this (#1370).
- **Tensor reductions now preserve validity on the surviving axes** and collapse the reduced axis, matching what tile already did (#1401).
- **New guard: a reduction over a provably *empty* valid region is rejected** at type deduction instead of asserting on device.
- **Fixes an out-of-bounds read reachable from ordinary DSL code** (details below).
- Shared helpers land in `type_inference.h`: a `GetValidShape` overload for `TensorType` (the tensor dual previously existed only as a file-local duplicate), `MakeFreshTensorType`, and `CheckReductionInputNonEmpty`.

A fully valid input still yields a fully valid, view-less result — the type constructors canonicalize redundant full validity away — so no existing program changes shape.

## Deviation from the brief: reductions do *not* reject a partially valid reduced axis

The brief asks for this rejection, but conditions it on *"if a kernel consumes the full physical reduced axis"*. **That premise does not hold here.** The backend reduction kernels bound their loops by the *source tile's valid extent*:

```cpp
// pto-isa: TRowSum.hpp
uint16_t m = srcTile.GetValidRow();
uint16_t n = srcTile.GetValidCol();   // reduced axis extent, read from the source
TRowSum<TileDataOut, TileDataIn>(dstTile.data(), srcTile.data(), m, n);
```

`TColSum` likewise bounds the reduced first axis by `GetValidRow()`, and the NPU a2/a3 and a5 paths do the same. The kernels fold exactly the real cells and **never read padding**, so the reduced axis collapses to a fully valid output axis and the result is the reduction over real data. Rejecting it would forbid a hardware-supported, numerically correct path and force a redundant `fillpad`.

This is not merely a reading of the ISA — it is already load-bearing behavior. `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_prod_reduction.py` and `test_argmax_reduction.py` contain ~25 on-device cases that deliberately narrow the **reduced** dim and assert numeric correctness (*"Narrowing the reduced dim exercises the partial-reduction tail"*). Implementing the brief's rule literally would have required deleting them.

**What the kernels genuinely cannot handle is an empty input** — they assert `validCol != 0 && validRow != 0`, and an empty region also leaves `max`/`min` with no value to return. So the rejection this PR adds is for a *provably zero* valid extent, which converts a hardware assert into a compile-time error. An unproved symbolic extent is still accepted, matching the standing verifier rule for unknown symbolic bounds.

```text
row_sum(tile[128,128], valid=[128,40])   accepted -> result [128,1], fully valid
row_sum(tile[128,128], valid=[128,vlen]) accepted -> vlen is never proved; kernel clamps at runtime
row_sum(tile[128,128], valid=[128,0])    rejected -> would trip PTO_ASSERT(validCol != 0)
row_sum(fillpad(t, min))                 accepted -> unchanged (paged-attention path)
```

## Bug fix: SIGBUS on a rank-mismatched `valid_shape`

A `valid_shape` whose rank differs from the physical shape made consumers index past the end of the vector. This crashed the process with **SIGBUS and no Python exception** (exit 135), and was reachable from ordinary DSL code:

```python
x: pl.Tensor[[64, 128], pl.FP32, pl.TensorView(layout=..., valid_shape=[40])]  # rank 1 vs rank 2
pl.tensor.col_sum(x)   # reduces axis 0, reads the missing axis-1 extent
```

`GetValidShape` now rejects it with a clear `ValueError` naming the two ranks. The check sits at the one place every consumer resolves an effective valid shape, so it **also closes the same pre-existing hazard on the tile path** (present since #1401). `ValidateValidShapeBounds` already reported this as `kRankMismatch`, but only over an already-built program — the type is constructed long before the verifier runs.

## Diagnostics added

| Condition | Error |
| --------- | ----- |
| Reduction input with a provably zero valid extent | `<op>: input valid extent on axis N is 0 (valid_shape [...]), so the reduction has no real data to consume...` (carries the input's span) |
| `valid_shape` rank != physical rank | `<Tensor\|Tile>Type valid_shape rank (N) must match the physical shape rank (M): valid_shape [...] vs shape [...]` |

## Deliberately out of scope

- **Fresh tile results still inherit the source's `pad`.** This is wrong in principle (a unary op writes only the valid region, so after `exp` a zero-padded source's padding is not zero), but it **cannot be fixed one op family at a time**: `InheritTileViewLayout` has 27 call sites across unary, elementwise, broadcast, gather and sort, and the DSL compares types across families at reassignments. Dropping `pad` in unary alone makes `row_expand_sub` -> `exp` fail to type-check (`ParserTypeError: Cannot reassign 'pij_tile' with a different type`). The elementwise brief owns both the "never inherit padding on a fresh result" rule and the elementwise/broadcast files, and can change all families atomically.
- **Tensor scalar-binary** (`tensor.adds` / `subs` / `muls` / `divs` / `fmods`) still drop validity. They live in `tensor_ops/elementwise.cpp`, which the elementwise brief owns and audits; tile's equivalents already preserve it. `tile.move` already preserves validity.
- **User-facing documentation** is deferred to the series' final documentation PR, per the series rules.

## Testing

- 20 new tests in `tests/ut/ir/operators/{test_tensor_ops,test_tile_ops}.py`: fully valid canonicalization, partial static + symbolic propagation, casts, row/column reductions, non-reduced-axis preservation, partial-reduced-axis collapse, empty-extent rejection (row/col/axis forms), rank-mismatch rejection, scalar results, and "fresh result carries no source alias metadata".
- Full unit suite: **7254 passed, 2 skipped**.
- `pre-commit` and the diff-based `clang-tidy` gate are clean.

title: WIP: Add experimental DSA memory-planner adapter
body:
## Summary

- add an optional `MemoryPlanner.DSA` path that exports unmerged physical
  allocations, invokes a standalone C++ DSA solver, independently validates
  the placement, and writes offsets back to PyPTO `MemRef`s
- solve standard buffer-level DSA geometry: lifetime conflicts and explicit
  separations are address-disjoint; lifetime-disjoint buffers may reuse and
  subdivide freed regions
- preserve mandatory aliases, pools, capacities, reservations, alignment,
  target/no-alias constraints, and pipeline-stage separations
- add schema-v1 corpus export, capability checks, PassContext/system-test
  planner selection, and focused adapter tests

## Status

This is a **draft/WIP implementation** for RFC #1980 and #1908. It does not yet
close either issue.

The external [`tonibohnlein/dsa-solver`](https://github.com/tonibohnlein/dsa-solver)
dependency is temporary research scaffolding. PyPTO pins
[`0af3c08`](https://github.com/tonibohnlein/dsa-solver/commit/0af3c08a5e7ff152bcacc16da9fdf985cba1204b)
(package version 0.8.0). Once a production heuristic is selected and validated,
it should be ported into PyPTO and the external dependency removed.

## Architecture

```text
InitMemRef
  -> MaterializeSemanticAliases
  -> collect unmerged physical allocations
  -> standalone DSA solver
  -> independent validation
  -> write offsets back to MemRefs
```

The DSA path skips opportunistic `MemoryReuse` coalescing but reuses its
phi/loop-aware lifetime and constraint analysis. Each physical allocation is
exported with one conservative lifetime hull; unproven gaps between SSA aliases
are not exposed as reusable memory.

## Standard DSA geometry

The former global whole-slot restriction is disabled. A freed region may be
subdivided among smaller co-live buffers, which is the geometry required by
#1908.

PyPTO contributes constraints and provenance:

- fixed pools, capacities, reservations, and alignment
- mandatory alias classes
- target and semantic no-alias separations
- hard separation of pipeline stages that must coexist

The uncalibrated `pipeline_serialization` cost proxy is research-only and is not
used by the production first-fit path.

## Validation

Current exact pins:

- PyPTO: `27ceb9f6`
- dsa-solver: `0af3c08a`
- PyPTO-Lib: `6e897cd9`

Host and CI gates:

- dsa-solver CTest: **17/17 passed**
- focused DSA-enabled PyPTO tests: **53/53 passed**
- all PR CI checks pass, including DSA integration, clang-tidy, Linux/macOS
  unit tests, system/simulator tests, and PyPTO-Lib models
- the synthetic #1908 geometry places one expired 64 KiB producer and two
  co-live 32 KiB consumers at a **64 KiB peak**
- previous device investigations fixed unsafe multi-interval export and missing
  if-phi/loop-carry writebacks

### Current device blocker: partial-overlap dependency

The blocking 910B2 gather gate fails deterministically under DSA on four
devices while PyPTO passes:

`test_gather.py::TestGatherIndex::test_gather_tile_input_source_unchanged[a2a3]`

The standard DSA placement reuses part of an expired 4 KiB allocation:

```text
assemble_src       [4096, 8192)  last read by pto.tmov
gather_idx_row     [4608, 4640)  later written by pto.tload
```

The placement is valid against the exported sequential lifetimes. However,
PTOAS v0.48 does not emit the required cross-pipe WAR synchronization for this
partial overlap. The later 32-byte load can overwrite data still being consumed
by the move, producing exactly eight corrupted FP32 elements. Equal-base reuse
is handled, but arbitrary range overlap is not currently represented safely
through the PyPTO fixed-address path.

This is not the earlier multi-interval-hole defect and not a standalone-solver
feasibility bug. The remaining design work is to preserve standard DSA
subdivision while making partial-overlap reuse dependency-safe, either through
range-aware downstream dependency handling or a narrowly grounded PyPTO
constraint/repair. Reintroducing the former global whole-slot rule would hide
the defect but would also remove the #1908 subdivision capability.

Until this blocker is fixed and rerun, this PR makes no end-to-end correctness
or performance claim for standard partial-overlap placement.

## Remaining WIP

- fix or safely constrain partial-overlap reuse across asynchronous pipes
- rerun gather, if-phi, transposed-matmul, planner-switch, and pipeline gates
- complete broader PyPTO and PyPTO-Lib DeepSeek/Qwen DSA regression sweeps
- run the original #1908 A-stationary chained-matmul case and remove its
  output-stationary workaround
- calibrate synchronization/pipeline costs before enabling a structured
  objective
- select and port an in-tree production heuristic

## Corpus and research

The standalone repository contains **452 unique checked-in PyPTO/PyPTO-Lib
instances** after structural deduplication, plus the MiniMalloc benchmark
family. Benchmark reports keep standard DSA peak/runtime separate from
PyPTO-specific research objectives.

## Related

- RFC and research tracking: #1980
- fragmentation acceptance case: #1908
- pipeline false-dependency motivation: #1949

title: refactor(ir): move TileBufSignature out of codegen into ir
body:
## Summary

`TileBufSignature` (a normalized view of a tile's buffer layout: memory space, dtype, physical shape, layout, fractal, pad, valid-shape) is a **pure function of `ir::TileType`** — it has zero codegen dependencies — yet it lived in `namespace pypto::codegen` under `include/pypto/codegen/pto/tile_buf_signature.h`. Its **only** consumer is the IR pass `FoldNoOpReshape`, which therefore had to reverse-`#include` a codegen header from the IR layer: the same layering inversion (IR must not depend on codegen) as the recent `IsBuiltinOp` / wrapper-direction / return-to-param cleanups.

- Move the header to `include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/tile_buf_signature.h` and change its namespace `pypto::codegen` → `pypto::ir` (include guard updated to match).
- Update `fold_no_op_reshape_pass.cpp`: fix the include path and drop the `codegen::` qualifier.
- No codegen `.cpp` referenced the type (it maintains parallel string-based logic in `PTOCodegen`), so codegen is unaffected.

Behavior-preserving: the header-only struct is moved verbatim (git detects a 97% rename).

## Relation to #2041

This is the second of two independent layering cleanups. Together they bring the IR layer's dependency on codegen to **zero**:

| PR | Reverse-dependency removed |
| --- | --- |
| #2041 | `orchestration_analysis.h` / `IsBuiltinOp` |
| this PR | `codegen/pto/tile_buf_signature.h` / `TileBufSignature` |

title: refactor(ir): dedup runtime facade, shared helpers, and dead code
body:
## Summary

Removes duplication across the IR Python layer, in three independent groups (combines what were PRs #2054 and #2055).

### 1. Compiled-program runtime facade
`CompiledProgram`, `_SubChipCallable`, and `DistributedCompiledProgram` each re-maintained the same runtime facade.
- **Unify param-metadata extraction.** `distributed_compiled_program._extract_param_infos_from_func` was a verbatim copy of `compiled_program._extract_func_param_infos` that had drifted to a bare/untyped signature and a shorter error message. Deleted it; the distributed path reuses `_extract_func_param_infos`. Only observable change: the distributed `TypeError` gains the richer `". Expected ShapedType or ScalarType."` wording.
- **Share the debug-runner emitter.** The byte-identical `_emit_debug_runner` bodies become one module-level `_write_debug_runner(output_dir, platform, get_metadata)`.
- **Light runtime-facade mixin.** `load` / `chip_callable` / `runtime_name` / `runtime_config` / `_ensure_runtime_loaded`, duplicated between `CompiledProgram` and `_SubChipCallable`, move into a `_RuntimeFacade` mixin. `CompiledProgram`'s multi-orch guard is preserved via an overridable `_check_runtime_access()` hook. `DistributedCompiledProgram` has no such facade and is untouched — no `__call__` / execution semantics are merged.

### 2. Small shared helpers
- **`_to_int32_scalar`** (RNG seed normalizer) was copy-pasted byte-for-byte in `op/tensor_ops.py` and `op/tile_ops.py`; moved to the shared `ir/utils.py`.
- **Builder `output()` / `outputs()`** — identical across `ForLoopBuilder` / `WhileLoopBuilder` / `IfStmtBuilder` (differing only in the "for loop" / "while loop" / "if statement" message label) — extracted into a `_ReturnVarsAccessor` mixin; each builder sets `_result_kind`.

### 3. Dead code
- `jit/specializer._collect_dep_names` had no callers anywhere — deleted.

### Review feedback addressed
- Builder `output()`/`outputs()` raise `RuntimeError` (not `assert`, which `-O` strips).
- `_write_debug_runner` wraps the script write in its best-effort try/except so a debug-file I/O error never crashes compilation.
- `_RuntimeFacade._ensure_runtime_loaded` publishes the `_chip_callable` sentinel last, after `_runtime_name` / `_runtime_config`.

## Not in scope
- Two items from the original review were already resolved by #2035 (ST fuzz framework removal): `_analyze_input_usage` and the Torch golden op-conversion duplication.
- `DistributedCompiledProgram`'s static `_build_full_args` near-duplicates the module-level one but intentionally omits an in-place-style hint in its `ValueError`; merging it would change a user-facing message, so it is left as a follow-up.

title: refactor(ir): Remove axis-based tile reductions tile.sum/max/min
body:
## What

Removes the axis-parameterized tile reductions `tile.sum` / `tile.max` / `tile.min` from the IR registry and every layer that depended on them. The direction-specific `row_*` / `col_*` reduction families remain and are now the only tile reductions.

## Why

These three ops were DSL-reachable but had **no path to the device**:

- No backend codegen entry (contrast every `row_*`/`col_*` op → `pto.trowsum` / `pto.tcolsum` / …).
- No composite-lowering rule (unlike `tile.sin` / `tile.cos`, which decompose in `LowerCompositeOps`).
- No production users — every working kernel already uses `pl.row_sum(t, tmp)` / `pl.col_max(t)`.

The PTO ISA exposes only **direction-specific** reduction intrinsics, and the tensor layer already encodes that convention (there is no `tensor.sum`). The axis form was the sole place in the stack that broke it. Its type deducer also admitted shapes the ISA can never produce — `keepdim=False` rank-drop, full-reduce-to-`Scalar`, and ND mid-axis reductions — so it could type-check and survive the pass pipeline only to fail at codegen.

An axis-parameterized reduction is not a useful IR abstraction here: the axis is compile-time-constant by construction (shape inference reads it), so any lowering would be a fixed `axis==last ? row_sum : col_sum` switch on a literal the frontend already knows — a naming convention, not a deferred decision. If the numpy-like spelling is wanted later, it belongs in the DSL as a helper, not as an IR op.

## Scope

Removed across all layers:
- C++ registrations for `tile.sum/max/min`, plus the now-dead `DeduceTileReductionType` and its file-local `GetKwarg` (`reduction.cpp`).
- The axis-remap special cases in `FlattenTileNdTo2D` (analysis + rewrite) and the axis branch of `IsReduceOnSplitAxis` — all existed only to service the `axis` kwarg. The `row_*`/`col_*` guard in `IsReduceOnSplitAxis` is unchanged.
- Python IR builders, DSL wrappers, top-level `pl.*` re-exports, and the torch debug reduction handlers.

## API impact

- **`pl.sum` is removed** (no scalar meaning, no users).
- **`pl.min` / `pl.max` survive as scalar-pair min/max** — these are load-bearing (`pl.max(pl.min(remaining, block_size), 0)` in the paged-attention examples and JIT tests). The Tile-reduction overload is dropped; the two are now symmetric scalar-only functions routing to the `ir::Min`/`ir::Max` builtins, exactly as the scalar branch did before.
- Reductions are now `pl.tile.row_sum` / `row_max` / `row_min` / `row_prod` (collapse last axis) and `col_*` (collapse axis 0).

## Tests

- Deleted tests that only exercised the removed ops.
- **Ported** `test_reduce_on_split_axis_rejected` to `col_sum` (which collapses axis 0 = the split axis under `UP_DOWN`), so the miscompile guard on the pass-side `IsReduceOnSplitAxis` call stays covered.
- **Rewrote** `test_compile_writes_orchestration_on_partial_codegen_failure` to fault-inject at the per-kernel emit seam instead of relying on an unlowerable op — it now exercises the real per-function error collection and `PartialCodegenError` file-preservation path without depending on any op lacking codegen.

Docs updated (EN + ZH): IR operator reference, `FlattenTileNdTo2D` pass doc, `src/ir/op` README, and the user-facing operation reference.

## Verification

- Clean build (`RelWithDebInfo`).
- Full unit suite: **7223 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed**.
- `ruff` + `clang-format` + `cpplint` + `markdownlint` + `pyright` + header/English checks all pass (pre-commit).

Net: **+88 / −722** across 23 files.

title: feat(codegen): lower Tile SSA to explicit PTO target IR
body:
## Summary

- introduce `PTOTileBufType` so mutable PTO destination buffers are explicit SSA handles rather than codegen-recovered state
- add and default-enable `MaterializePTOTileHandles` plus `LowerTileToPTOIR` at the codegen boundary
- lower supported Tile operations, structured `ForStmt`/`IfStmt`, scalar carries, Tile phi/carry handles, SPMD parameters, and rank-N tensor transfers to destination-passing PTO target IR
- select the target or legacy printer independently per function, so mixed fully lowered/deferred programs remain valid
- defer unsupported functions as whole units to the legacy path, never as partially bufferized functions
- preserve post-pipeline performance hints on `pto.tload`/`pto.tstore` and provide a logical-IR-only debug path for consumers such as `torch_codegen`
- add synchronized English and Chinese design/pass documentation

## Design

```text
Logical Tile SSA
  -> MaterializePTOTileHandles
  -> verified logical-value / mutable-buffer plan
  -> LowerTileToPTOIR
  -> destination-passing PTO target IR
  -> PTOIRPrinter
```

The resulting IR remains SSA: each `PTOTileBufType` handle has one definition, while target operations explicitly read or mutate the referenced storage through registered operand roles and memory effects. Tile arithmetic target ops are void destination-passing operations in `EvalStmt`.

Orchestration remains C++ codegen and is not lowered by these passes. Unsupported PTO surfaces—including cross-core pipes, dynamic-shape Tensor parameters, general reductions, `WhileStmt`, and remaining Tile families—mark the complete InCore function `pto.target_lowering_deferred` before mutation.

## Current coverage

- rank-N Tensor views/transfers with physical rank-2 Tile buffers
- static or dynamic rank-2 valid shapes
- load/store, create/full, slice, alloc-backed reshape, basic unary/binary/tile-scalar elementwise ops, move/fillpad, and row sum

title: [Feature] Detect lost WAR (write-after-read) dependencies in task scheduling and fix via inout rewrite or explicit error
body:
### Summary

The runtime task scheduler drops **WAR (write-after-read) anti-dependencies** for loop-carried buffers, which silently produces data races and precision/accuracy errors. PyPTO currently has no mechanism to detect or guard against this. We should add **WAR analysis** to the task-dependency derivation path so that, when a WAR hazard is detected, PyPTO either:

1. rewrites the reading task's `Input` argument to `InOut` so the runtime tracks it as a new writer version and emits the missing edge, **or**
2. raises a clear compile-time error instructing the user to construct the WAR dependency explicitly via the manual-dependency mechanism (`pl.submit(..., deps=[...])`).

Related runtime bug: hw-native-sys/simpler#1306. Related PyPTO RFC on automatic dependency derivation: #1368.

### Motivation / Use Case

The runtime dependency generator emits RAW and WAW edges but **omits WAR edges** in loop-carried buffer scenarios. Concretely, for a buffer allocated once and carried across loop iterations:

- Iteration N: `writer(N)` modifies the buffer (`inout`), then `reader(N)` reads it (pure `input`).
- Iteration N+1: `writer(N+1)` modifies the buffer again.

The runtime generates:
- RAW: `writer(N) -> reader(N)` (same iteration), and
- WAW: `writer(N) -> writer(N+1)` (loop-carried),

but **not** the required WAR edge `reader(N) -> writer(N+1)`. Because the reader produces no new version of the buffer, the loop carries the *writer's* output forward, so `writer(N+1)` depends only on `writer(N)` — never on `reader(N)`. The scheduler is then free to run `writer(N+1)` concurrently with `reader(N)`, overwriting the buffer while it is still being read → data race.

**Impact (from the runtime issue):** in a minimal reproducer ~35% of one band's output contained another band's data; in production (Qwen3-14B prefill) ~10% of logits were corrupted due to shared gate/accumulator buffers racing across MLP bands.

**Why this needs a PyPTO-side fix:** the corruption is silent — no crash, just wrong numbers — and is extremely hard to diagnose because the generated orchestration looks correct (all directions/annotations are right; only the dependency edge is missing). PyPTO owns argument-direction assignment (`DeriveCallDirections`) and compiler dependency derivation (`AutoDeriveTaskDependencies`), so it is the right layer to detect the hazard and either encode the missing constraint or fail loudly. Today PyPTO has neither WAR analysis nor a diagnostic for this case, so users hit silent precision errors with no guidance.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Add WAR-hazard analysis to the dependency-derivation path (candidate home: `AutoDeriveTaskDependencies`, pass 35, which already builds a storage-location/alias map for tensor Vars and tracks loop-carried roots). For each storage root that is:

- read as pure `Input` by a task in iteration N, and
- written (`inout`/output) by a task in iteration N+1 through the loop carry,

detect the missing `reader(N) -> writer(N+1)` WAR edge and resolve it via one of:

```text
Option A (automatic):  rewrite the reader's Input arg on that slot to InOut
                       so the runtime versions the buffer and derives the edge.
Option B (diagnostic): raise a clear compile-time error naming the buffer and
                       the two tasks, instructing the user to add the WAR edge
                       explicitly:

    # reader(N) must complete before writer(N+1) overwrites `buf`
    _, tid_read  = pl.submit(self.reader, buf, ...)
    _, tid_write = pl.submit(self.writer, buf, ..., deps=[tid_read])
```

Behavior should be scoped to AUTO runtime scopes (MANUAL scopes already require explicit `deps=[...]` and must keep their scheduling contract untouched). A conservative default of Option B (error out) is acceptable as a first step so correctness is never silently violated; Option A (automatic `Input -> InOut` rewrite) can follow as an optimization once the analysis is proven sound.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Fix only in the runtime scheduler** (hw-native-sys/simpler#1306): necessary but not sufficient — PyPTO should still surface/guard the hazard so users on current runtime versions are not silently miscompiled, and so the constraint is expressed in the IR/orchestration.
- **Always require manual `deps=[...]`**: too burdensome and easy to forget; the whole point of AUTO scopes is automatic dependency derivation. A detect-and-guard/auto-fix approach preserves that ergonomics.
- **Do nothing (status quo)**: unacceptable — produces silent, hard-to-debug precision errors in real models.

### Additional Context

- Runtime issue: hw-native-sys/simpler#1306 (WAR dependency loss in the runtime task scheduler).
- Related PyPTO work: #1368 (RFC: automatic manual-scope dependency derivation), #1744, #1939.
- Relevant PyPTO code: `AutoDeriveTaskDependencies` (pass 35, `docs/en/dev/passes/35-auto_derive_task_dependencies.md`) and `DeriveCallDirections` (pass 34); manual mechanism `pl.submit(..., deps=[...])`.

title: [Feature] Wire runtime dispatch-predicate into the pypto frontend (pl.spmd(predicate=...))
body:
### Summary

Expose the runtime's **dispatch-predicate** mechanism through the pypto frontend so a statically-materialized SPMD task can be conditionally retired (never dispatched to a core) based on a value only a prior task produces — evaluated by the scheduler at the dispatch point, not in orchestration.

The runtime side already shipped this in [hw-native-sys/simpler PR #1314](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/pull/1314) (currently pinned at `cddf2b6c`): `L0TaskPredicate` / `L0PredicateOperand` / `PredicateOp{NONE,EQ,NE,GT,LT,GE,LE}` and `Arg::set_predicate(...)`, evaluated in the scheduler via `DispatchPredicate::pass()`. **pypto codegen does not emit any of it yet** — that PR's description explicitly notes "Frontend (pypto `pl.spmd(predicate=...)`) lands separately." This issue tracks that frontend wiring.

### Motivation / Use Case

**DeepSeek-V4 expert-routed MoE — skip empty experts.** Each expert's per-expert `row_count` is runtime data only known after the router/gather stage, written into a tensor. pypto's AOT orchestration only has the tensor *address*, not the *value*, so "skip experts with `row_count == 0`" cannot be a constant known at submit:

- Reading the value in orchestration stalls on `wait_for_tensor_ready` (the producer must finish first) — serializing the pipeline.
- Submitting all experts and branching inside the kernel still pays the full launch + core-occupancy + data-movement cost per empty expert (in decode, most of 256 experts are empty).
- Making the expert count dynamic breaks the static task-graph model the whole runtime is built on.

A dispatch predicate resolves this: submit all expert tasks statically (no orchestration stall, graph stays static); each carries `predicate = row_count[e] > 0` and depends on the gather producer; the scheduler reads `row_count[e]` at the dispatch point (value already current, no wait) and dispatches only non-empty experts. A FALSE predicate retires the task inline via the dep-only path — it still settles fanin/fanout so the downstream combine unlocks (it does NOT vanish from the graph).

### Proposed API / Behavior

Constructor-first surface (comparison-expression sugar `row_count[e] > 0` is a follow-up):

```python
for e in pl.range(NUM_EXPERTS):          # static loop
    with pl.spmd(num_blocks,
                 deps=[gather_tid],                        # producer of row_count MUST be a dep
                 predicate=pl.dispatch_pred(row_count, [e], ">", 0)):
        self.expert_ffn(tokens[e], out[e])
```

Predicate shape is fixed to `tensor[indices] OP const` with `OP in {==, !=, >, <, >=, <=}` — mirroring the runtime `{operand, op, target}` triple. Scope is **`pl.spmd` only** for the first cut (the closest analog `allow_early_resolve` also lives there; `pl.submit`/`pl.at` can follow later).

Planned layering (mirrors the `allow_early_resolve` path, simpler #1065):

1. **DSL** — `predicate=` param on `pl.spmd` + new `pl.dispatch_pred(tensor, indices, op, target)` constructor.
2. **Parser** — parse/validate the kwarg (operand is a tensor Var, op in the 6 comparisons, target is an integer literal), store as a scope attr.
3. **IR** — new first-class `Submit::predicate_` field. Unlike `allow_early_resolve_`, it carries SSA values (operand tensor Expr + index Exprs), so passes MUST walk it (visitor/mutator), same as `deps_`/`core_num_`.
4. **SubmitToCallView** — surface it as a Call-view attr for codegen.
5. **Codegen** — emit `L0TaskPredicate` + `Arg::set_predicate(...)` in orchestration codegen (operand/op/target only; the runtime derives `elem_size` from the tensor dtype).
6. **Verifier** — a `SubmitVerifier` enforcing the contract that the predicate tensor's producer is one of the task's deps (else the dispatch-point read races an unwritten value).

### Alternatives Considered

- **Read the value in orchestration and branch on submit** — stalls on `wait_for_tensor_ready`, serializes the pipeline. Rejected.
- **Submit all experts, branch inside the kernel** — still pays launch/core/data-movement per empty expert. Rejected.
- **Dynamic task count (submit only non-empty experts)** — breaks the static task-graph / AOT-orchestration model. Rejected.

### Additional Context

- Runtime feature: [hw-native-sys/simpler PR #1314](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/pull/1314), commit `7d526e12`; runtime currently pinned at `cddf2b6c`.
- Reference test on the runtime side: `tests/st/{a2a3,a5}/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/predicated_dispatch/` (gate=0 skips, gate=1 dispatches; passes on a2a3sim and onboard a2a3).
- Frontend precedent to mirror end-to-end: `allow_early_resolve` (simpler #1065) — same `pl.spmd → Submit → SubmitToCallView → orchestration codegen` chain, emitting `Arg::set_allow_early_resolve(true)`.

title: feat(ir): add system.cacheinvalid cache-line invalidate op
body:
## Summary

Adds a `system.cacheinvalid` SyncOp that invalidates the cache lines backing a tensor sub-region. The op carries a uniform N-D `(shapes, offsets)` region (both matching the tensor rank), and codegen picks one of two lowerings by the region size — covering both a scalar write and a tile store.

- **IR registration** (`src/ir/op/sync_ops/sync.cpp`): `SyncOp` category, args `tensor`, `shapes`, `offsets`, `DeduceUnknownType`.
- **Python IR wrapper** (`python/pypto/ir/op/system_ops.py`): builds the `shapes`/`offsets` tuples; validates that both match the tensor rank and carry integer coordinates.
- **DSL** (`python/pypto/language/op/system_ops.py`): unwraps the `Tensor`/`Scalar` args; exported in `__all__`.
- **Codegen** (`src/backend/common/pto_ops_memory.cpp`): two-form dispatch (see below), reusing the existing `GetFlatOffsetSSA` and partition-view helpers (`EmitPartitionViewPTO` / `MakePartitionTensorViewType`).
- **Torch reference** (`python/pypto/debug/torch_codegen.py`): registered as a no-op alongside `system.fence`.
- **Docs**: EN + ZH operator tables.

## Two codegen forms

Dispatch is on `shapes`: an all-1 region is a single element (scalar write) and lowers through a raw pointer; any larger (or dynamic) dimension is a tile store and lowers through a `partition_tensor_view`, matching `tile.store`'s `outs()` operand.

**Scalar write — `shapes` all 1** (`pl.system.cacheinvalid(t, [1, 1], [0, 8])`):

```mlir
%0 = pto.addptr %arg1, %c8_index : !pto.ptr<f32> -> !pto.ptr<f32>
pto.cmo.cacheinvalid %0 single_cache_line
```

The N-D `offsets` are flattened over the tensor shape (supports a dynamic offset, e.g. a loop variable).

**Tile store — larger region** (`pl.system.cacheinvalid(t, [128], [0])`):

```mlir
%payload_view = pto.partition_view %t_view, offsets = [%c0_index], sizes = [%c128_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<128xf32>
pto.cmo.cacheinvalid %payload_view single_cache_line : !pto.partition_tensor_view<128xf32>
```

## API

```python
pl.system.cacheinvalid(tensor, shapes, offsets)   # shapes first, then offsets; both N-D, matching tensor rank
```

## Testing

- [x] Parser round-trip for both the scalar (all-1 shapes) and region forms
- [x] Codegen: scalar write emits the ptr-form `pto.cmo.cacheinvalid` (no partition-view annotation)
- [x] Codegen: region emits `pto.partition_view` + a `!pto.partition_tensor_view<...>` cmo
- [x] Codegen: dynamic (loop-variable) offset reaches the flattened ptr offset
- [x] IR wrapper rejects rank mismatch (`ValueError`) and non-integer coordinates (`TypeError`)
- [x] Full unit suite passes (no regressions)
- [x] Code review, clang-tidy, pre-commit hooks clean

title: [WIP] Wire runtime dispatch-predicate into the pypto frontend (pl.spmd_submit(predicate=...))
body:
> **Status: WIP / Draft.** Core frontend is complete and validated end-to-end on onboard a2a3; see *Deferred* for what is intentionally out of scope for this PR.

Tracks [hw-native-sys/pypto#2059](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/2059). Depends on the runtime `DispatchPredicate` struct + `Arg::set_predicate(...)` from [hw-native-sys/simpler#1314](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/pull/1314). That runtime is **already on `upstream/main`** (bumped to `a756969c`, a descendant of `cddf2b6c`, in [hw-native-sys/pypto#2061](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/2061)), so **this PR no longer bumps the submodule** — it is pure frontend on top of the current runtime. That runtime PR explicitly deferred the frontend ("Frontend (pypto `pl.spmd(predicate=...)`) lands separately") — this is it.

## What this does

Exposes the runtime **dispatch predicate** through the DSL: a statically-materialized SPMD task can be **conditionally retired** (never dispatched to a core) based on a value only a *prior* task produces. The condition is evaluated by the scheduler **at the dispatch point** — after the task's dependencies are satisfied, so the value is current — **not** in orchestration (which would stall on `wait_for_tensor_ready`). A false predicate retires the task inline via the dep-only path, still settling fanin/fanout so downstream consumers unlock; it does **not** vanish from the graph.

### Motivating use case — MoE skip-empty-experts

DeepSeek-V4 expert-routed MoE computes each expert's `row_count` at runtime (written into a tensor). Orchestration only has the tensor *address*, not the *value*, so "skip experts with `row_count == 0`" cannot be a constant known at submit. Alternatives and why they fail:

| Approach | Problem |
| --- | --- |
| Read the count in orchestration, branch on submit | Stalls on `wait_for_tensor_ready` → serializes the pipeline |
| Submit all experts, branch inside the kernel | Still pays launch + core-occupancy + data-movement per empty expert |
| Make the expert count dynamic | Breaks the static task-graph / AOT-orchestration model |

The dispatch predicate resolves this: submit all experts statically (graph stays static, no orchestration stall); each carries `predicate = row_count[e] > 0` and depends on the gather producer; the scheduler reads `row_count[e]` at the dispatch point (no wait) and dispatches only non-empty experts.

## Frontend usage (the writing form)

Constructor-first surface — a new `pl.dispatch_pred(...)` passed as `predicate=` to `pl.spmd_submit` / `pl.submit`:

```python
out, tid = pl.spmd_submit(
    self.kernel, *args, core_num=N,
    deps=[producer_tid],                               # see Contract below
    predicate=pl.dispatch_pred(tensor, [i0, i1, ...], "op", target),
)
```

`pl.dispatch_pred(tensor, indices, op, target)` maps 1:1 onto the runtime `operand[indices] <op> target`:

| Arg | Meaning | Constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tensor` | operand tensor read at the dispatch point | must be a tensor |
| `[indices]` | element locator | **list literal**; each element a `ConstInt` or loop `Var`; non-empty |
| `"op"` | comparison spelling | one of `==` `!=` `>` `<` `>=` `<=` (string literal) |
| `target` | right-hand side | **integer literal** (may be negative) |

MoE example (the shape validated end-to-end):

```python
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
def main(self, x, out, rc):                            # rc = row_count tensor
    with pl.manual_scope():
        rc, g_tid = pl.spmd_submit(self.gate, rc, core_num=1)      # producer of rc
        out, _ = pl.spmd_submit(
            self.expert, x, out, core_num=1,
            deps=[g_tid],                                          # producer is a dep
            predicate=pl.dispatch_pred(rc, [0, 0], ">", 0),        # rc[0,0] > 0
        )
    return out
```

Generated orchestration C++ (mirrors the runtime's hand-written form):

```cpp
L0TaskPredicate params_t1_pred;
params_t1_pred.operand.tensor = &ext_rc;
params_t1_pred.operand.ndims = 2;
params_t1_pred.operand.indices[0] = 0;
params_t1_pred.operand.indices[1] = 0;
params_t1_pred.op = PredicateOp::GT;
params_t1_pred.target = 0;
params_t1.set_predicate(params_t1_pred);
```

Parse-time validation rejects malformed predicates (non-tensor operand, non-list indices, bad op spelling, non-literal target, a non-`dispatch_pred` value).

### Contract

**The predicate operand tensor's producer MUST be one of the submit's `deps=`** so the dispatch-point read observes the current value. In this WIP only the *structural* well-formedness is enforced (operand present & a tensor, indices non-empty, op in range) in the `Submit` constructor; the *dataflow* "producer ∈ deps" check is deferred (see below), so the author is currently responsible for `deps=`.

## Design approach

Mirrors the existing `allow_early_resolve` path (simpler#1065) end-to-end: `pl.spmd_submit → Submit → SubmitToCallView → orchestration codegen`.

- **IR (`Submit`)** — four first-class fields: `predicate_operand` (`optional<ExprPtr>`), `predicate_indices` (`vector<ExprPtr>`), `predicate_op` (`int64`, a `DispatchPredicateOp`), `predicate_target` (`int64`). The operand/indices are SSA-bearing IR-node fields; op/target are stored as `int64` **leaves on purpose** — the reflection system requires an explicit `VisitLeafField` overload per leaf type (structural-equal / hash / serializer / deserializer), so a dedicated enum leaf would cost 4+ touchpoints; `int64` + `optional<ExprPtr>` + `vector<ExprPtr>` are all already supported, keeping reflection zero-cost. A `DispatchPredicateOp` enum is used at the API boundary; the int is an internal encoding whose values match the runtime `PredicateOp`.
- **Pass safety** — the operand + indices are part of the use-def chain, so the C++ visitor/mutator walk them (like `deps_` / `core_num_`), and **all 13 `Submit` reconstruction sites** across the passes preserve the predicate via a new `Submit::GetPredicateInit()` helper. Verified: the predicate survives inline / SSA / outline / materialize and resolves to `&ext_<name>` at codegen.
- **Cross-layer** — nanobind `Submit` ctor gains the predicate args; `DispatchPredicateOp` enum is bound (the `None`/int-0 member is not exposed to Python — `None` is a keyword; "no predicate" = pass none); `ir.pyi` updated.
- **Codegen** — `EmitPredicateHint` emits the `L0TaskPredicate` + `set_predicate` block on the task's `L0TaskArgs` before `rt_submit_*`. `elem_size` is intentionally left for the runtime to derive from the tensor dtype.
- **Printer / deserializer** — round-trip the four fields (`predicate=pl.dispatch_pred(...)` prints and reparses).

### Why `pl.spmd_submit` (not the scope form) for this cut

`pl.spmd_submit` builds a `Submit` directly at parse time (before SSA), so the Submit-level pass-walk fully covers it with **zero scope-attr plumbing**. The `with pl.spmd(predicate=...)` scope form is outlined *after* SSA (pass 8-9), so its operand/index Vars would live on scope attrs during SSA and need extra `VisitScopeAttrs`/`MutateScopeAttrs` Expr-walking + scope serializer/printer handling — deferred to keep this PR tight.

## Scope / deferred

Out of scope for this WIP (each a clean follow-up; all share the same IR fields + codegen):

1. **Dataflow verifier** — "predicate operand producer must be a dep" (only the structural check is in).
2. **`with pl.spmd(predicate=...)` scope form** (needs scope-attr Expr-walking).
3. **Comparison-expression sugar** — `predicate=(row_count[e] > 0)` instead of the constructor.

Predicate expressiveness is deliberately limited to `tensor[indices] OP const` — this matches the runtime's single-comparison `DispatchPredicate`. Multiple conditions / boolean combination / arithmetic are not expressible; the pattern is to reduce them to one gate value in a prior kernel.

## Testing

- `tests/ut/language/parser/test_submit_predicate.py` — parse/IR field population, all 6 op spellings, negative-target, 5 negative cases, print→parse round-trip.
- `tests/ut/codegen/test_predicate_codegen.py` — full Default pipeline → asserts the `set_predicate` block (and its absence without a predicate).
- `tests/st/runtime/scheduling/test_predicated_dispatch.py` — end-to-end: `x_producer → clobber(predicate=gate[0,0]>0, deps=[xp]) → consumer(deps=[clobber_tid])`. gate=0 → clobber skipped → sentinel(42) survives; gate=1 → clobber dispatched → poison(999); consumer unlocks in **both** cases (proving inline-retire still settles fanout). **Passes on onboard a2a3.**
- Regression: 2808 transforms + codegen UTs green.

title: ci: split system-tests into two balanced jobs
body:
## Problem

The `system-tests` job's batched `Test system tests` step dominated its wall-clock: measured at ~7–15 min across recent `main` runs (60–75% of all test time) and unbounded on heavy runs. Because that one step was the long pole, the job could not be shortened by rearranging the lighter direct-device / DFX steps around it.

Per-step timings from three recent `main` runs (seconds):

| Step | run A | run B | run C |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Setup NPU (build) | 133 | 206 | 142 |
| **Test system tests** (batched) | **426** | **455** | **932** |
| direct-device + paged + multi-orch + swimlane + dump-args | 276 | 424 | 283 |

## Change

Split the batched `device_batch` load **by directory** across two jobs that run in parallel:

- **`system-tests`** — batched shard 1: the heavy dirs `runtime/ops` + `runtime/cross_core` (~68% of the batched load).
- **`system-tests-direct`** — batched shard 2: `device_batch` on the remaining dirs, plus **all** `-m 'not device_batch'` direct-device tests and the DFX steps (paged-attention, multi-orch L2, swimlane, dump-args).

The ~68/32 batched split balances shard 1 against the extra direct + DFX load carried by the second job, so the critical path is roughly the heavier of the two rather than their sum. Heavy-run estimate: **~18 min → ~12.5 min**, with the two jobs finishing at about the same time.

## Coverage (unchanged)

- shard-1 dirs ∪ shard-2 (rest) exactly reconstruct the original batched scope; shard 2 `--ignore`s `ops`/`cross_core` so nothing runs twice.
- The direct-device step still runs `-m 'not device_batch'` over all of `tests/st`, so direct tests living under `ops`/`cross_core` are not dropped.
- `distributed` / `codegen` / `dump_tag` exclusions are preserved.
- The second job checks out under `./st-direct-checkout` to avoid colliding with `system-tests`' `./st-checkout` on the shared self-hosted host, and cleans up its own orphaned task-submit tasks.

## Notes

- The 68/32 partition is estimated from the count of `test_runner.run` files per directory; the directory allocation may need a small tweak once real per-job timings are observed (documented in the job comments).
- Both jobs run their own build (ccache-shared, usually a cache hit) — the fixed cost of parallelizing.
- The existing required check name `system-tests` is unchanged. To gate merges on the new job too, add `system-tests-direct` to the branch protection required status checks.

title: fix(runtime): Recover interleaved [STRACE] records in L3 bench parse
body:
## Summary
- L3 benchmark parsing (`distributed=True`) forks one chip worker per rank, all sharing the capture fd. Their concurrent writes can interleave two complete `[STRACE]` records onto a single physical line.
- simpler's `parse_spans` reads at most one record per line (`search` + greedy `attrs=.*`), so it silently drops the second record — losing that dispatch's orch/sched spans and making the affected `(round, rank)` read as **0**.
- Fix: in `_parse_stats_from_strace`, re-split the captured log on the `[STRACE]` marker (`log_text.replace("[STRACE]", "\n[STRACE]")`) so every record gets its own line before handing the text to the **unmodified** simpler parser. Each record's payload is intact on the wire — only the line boundary was lost. A prefix left on a marker-less line simply fails the regex and is skipped, as before.

## Testing
- [x] Added L3 regression test `test_parse_l3_recovers_interleaved_records_on_one_line` mashing two records onto one physical line; asserts both invocations survive. Verified it **fails without the fix** (round1 host reads `0.0`) and passes with it.
- [x] `tests/ut/runtime/test_benchmark.py` — 28 passed.
- [x] Full `tests/ut/` suite run; no new regressions from this change.

title: feat(distributed): add shape+dtype overload to alloc_window_buffer
body:
## Summary

Adds `pld.alloc_window_buffer(shape, *, dtype=...)` — a convenience overload
that computes the per-rank byte size from the shape and dtype, eliminating
manual `product(shape) * dtype.get_byte()` arithmetic. Normalizes to the
existing IR op — no C++ changes, no new IR surface.

Implements option 5 of RFC #1968.

## Before / After

```
# Canonical byte form (preserved)
data_buf   = pld.alloc_window_buffer(nr * SIZE * pl.FP32.get_byte())
signal_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(nr * pl.INT32.get_byte())

# Shape+dtype overload (new)
data_buf   = pld.alloc_window_buffer([nr, SIZE], dtype=pl.FP32)
signal_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer([nr], dtype=pl.INT32)
```

The canonical form is unchanged. The two-phase `alloc -> window` design
remains first-class — a single buffer can still back multiple `window()`
views across loop iterations.

## Changes (2 files, DSL-only)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `tensor_ops.py` | `_compute_window_buffer_bytes` helper, two `@overload` signatures, dispatch on first-arg type |
| `test_alloc_window_buffer.py` | 2 new tests, 2 error-match strings updated |
