title: [Tracking] Dispatch-predicate frontend — phased rollout
body:
Umbrella tracking issue for landing the runtime **dispatch predicate** in the pypto frontend, in phases. Origin feature request: [hw-native-sys/pypto#2059](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/2059). Runtime mechanism: [hw-native-sys/simpler#1314](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/pull/1314) (`DispatchPredicate` / `Arg::set_predicate`), already on `upstream/main` via the runtime bump to `a756969c`.

> **Status (2026-07-26):** Phases 1–3 are merged to `main`; Phase 4 (`pl.at`) is up for review in [hw-native-sys/pypto#2151](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/2151). The frontend is now feature-complete — the dispatch predicate is authorable on the call form (`pl.spmd_submit` / `pl.submit`), the `with pl.spmd(...)` scope form (all three spellings), and `with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, ...)`. Only the **optional** Phase 5 polish remains.

### Background

A dispatch predicate lets a statically-materialized SPMD task be conditionally retired (never dispatched to a core) based on a value only a prior task produces — evaluated by the scheduler at the dispatch point, not in orchestration. Motivating use case: MoE "skip empty experts" (`row_count[e] > 0`). See #2059 for the full rationale.

### Surface

```python
# Call form (Phase 1)
out, tid = pl.spmd_submit(self.expert, x, out, core_num=N,
                          deps=[gather_tid],              # operand's producer
                          predicate=(row_count[e] > 0))

# Scope form (Phase 3)
with pl.spmd(N, deps=[gather_tid], predicate=(row_count[e] > 0)) as tid:
    out = self.expert(x, out)

# pl.at scope form (Phase 4) — CORE_GROUP only
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP,
           deps=[gather_tid], predicate=(row_count[e] > 0)) as tid:
    out = self.expert(x, out)
```

The comparison is parsed as an **ordinary expression but never evaluated** — `rc[e]` is the DSL's usual sugar for `pl.read`, so it lowers to plain IR (`Gt(Cast(tensor.read(..)), 0)`) reusing the existing comparison nodes. It rides on `Submit.predicate` and is never in a statement position, so the read does not execute in orchestration. Expressiveness is fixed to `tensor[indices] OP int-literal`.

### Phases

- [x] **Phase 1 — Core frontend** — `pl.spmd_submit` / `pl.submit` `predicate=(t[i] > 0)`. **PR: [hw-native-sys/pypto#2067](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/2067)** (merged).
  - IR: a single `Submit.predicate` field holding the comparison Expr — reuses the existing `Eq/Ne/Lt/Le/Gt/Ge` nodes over `tensor.read` instead of a bespoke encoding, so reflection needs no new leaf type and the shape stays open for a future multi-condition runtime. Decomposition into the runtime's `operand OP target` triple lives in orchestration codegen.
  - Pass safety: visitor/mutator walk + all Submit reconstruction sites preserve the predicate.
  - Cross-layer: nanobind ctor takes one optional `predicate` Expr + `ir.pyi` (no enum needed).
  - Codegen: `EmitPredicateHint` → `L0TaskPredicate` + `Arg::set_predicate(...)`.
  - Printer / deserializer round-trip; `NoNestedCall` verifier exempts the predicate (a declarative spec, not an evaluated expression — flattening it would turn the read into a real orchestration load).
  - Parser validation: operand is a tensor subscripted to one element, integer-scalar indices, index count == rank, integer-literal target, single (unchained) comparison; mirrored `0 < t[i]` normalized to `t[i] > 0`.
  - **Producer∈deps contract enforced at the parser boundary** (see Phase 2).
  - Tests: parser/IR + codegen UTs, onboard **a2a3** end-to-end ST; DSL docs (en + zh-cn).
- [x] **Phase 2 — Producer∈deps contract** — ~~a `SubmitVerifier` with use-def analysis~~ → **landed in Phase 1 at the parser boundary** (PR #2067): each submit's result Vars are tracked against its producer TaskId, and a predicate whose operand producer is absent from `deps=` is rejected. Without it the scheduler could evaluate the predicate before the producer wrote the tensor and dispatch on stale data. **Extended in Phase 3** to cover scope-produced operands (see below).
  - Residual (accepted, author's responsibility — not statically provable): an operand with no tracked producer (e.g. a function parameter), and `Array[N, TASK_ID]` dep entries which do not name their producers individually.
  - Optional follow-up: an IR-level verifier would additionally cover hand-built / deserialized IR, which the parser check does not see. Low priority — the DSL is the only way to author a predicate today.
- [x] **Phase 3 — `with pl.spmd(predicate=...)` scope form** — **PR: [hw-native-sys/pypto#2092](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/2092)** (merged). Accepted on **all three** spmd spellings: plain `with`, `with ... as tid`, and `for i in pl.spmd(...)`. Same expression, validation, lowering, and runtime ABI as the call form. `pl.at(..., predicate=...)` was deliberately **out of scope** here — the C++ side is shared, so a later cut is parser + `dsl_api` only. **Done in Phase 4 below**, and that prediction held.
  - The scope outlines only at `OutlineSpmdScopes`, so between parse and outline the predicate rides on `SpmdScopeStmt.attrs_` as the **first Expr-valued scope attr**, carrying live SSA Vars (operand tensor + indices).
  - **Correction to the original plan:** this needed **four** attr walkers, not the two anticipated (`VisitScopeAttrs` / `MutateScopeAttrs`) — also `ConvertToSSA::SubstScopeAttrs` (versions the operand; mirrors the `kAttrDevice` ExprPtr handling on `Call`) and **DCE `FindLiveRoots`** (else the operand's feeding assignment looks dead, and its removal leaves a dangling attr ref — the same failure class as #1456). Missing any one produces a silently-wrong dangling reference, so a `kAttrPredicate` constant was introduced to make the set greppable.
  - **Serialization needed no change** — the `ExprPtr` attr branch already existed; only a new printer method (`PrintScopePredicateAttr`) was added, narrower than the "scope serializer/printer handling" originally anticipated.
  - `ScopeOutliner` moves the attr onto `Submit.predicate` and forces the Submit shape (synthesising a TaskId Var when the scope has no `as tid`), exactly like `allow_early_resolve`. `NoNestedCall` exempts the scope predicate via a new `ShouldVisitScopeAttr(key)` hook (same rationale as the Submit-field exemption in Phase 1; the hook keeps the base walker the single source of truth).
  - **Scope-producer tracking** so the Phase-2 contract genuinely applies to the scope form — a tensor produced by `with pl.spmd(...) as tid:` was previously untracked, so a missing `deps=` was silently certified. The deps-remediation hint is tailored per form (the plain / `for` forms cannot take `deps=`, so they are pointed at the `as tid` capture form instead of at a kwarg that would itself be rejected).
  - Cluster nesting rejects `predicate=` at parse time, and `UnwrapNestedSpmd` asserts it for hand-built / deserialized IR (such a scope is unwrapped into the Group function and never produces a `Submit`, so the predicate would be silently dropped).
  - **Drive-by fix:** `structural_hash` now **skips** Var-/Expr-valued scope attrs instead of throwing — a latent bug that already made every `with pl.spmd(...) as tid:` (`task_id_var`) un-hashable, which this change would otherwise have extended to any scope predicate.
  - Tests: parser (all three forms, canonical attr order, print round-trip, cluster + deps rejection, per-form hint), transforms (SSA versions the operand to the producing scope's result, DCE liveness, `structural_hash` regression), codegen (full `Default` pipeline → `set_predicate`), and an on-board **a2a3** ST proving the scope and submit forms skip/dispatch identically on hardware.
- [x] **Phase 4 — `pl.at(..., predicate=...)` scope form** — **PR: [hw-native-sys/pypto#2151](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/2151)**. The cut Phase 3 deferred ("the C++ side is shared, so a later cut is parser + `dsl_api` only"). Confirmed accurate: every scope-attr walker (`VisitScopeAttrs` / `MutateScopeAttrs` / `ConvertToSSA::SubstScopeAttrs` / DCE `FindLiveRoots` / `structural_hash` / `NoNestedCall`) and `ScopeOutliner` were already scope-kind agnostic, so no new plumbing was needed.
  - **Placement restricted to where the scope becomes an independently submitted L0 task**, since anywhere else the predicate has no runtime carrier: `level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP` only (a Hierarchy `pl.at` inside an Orchestration function survives the whole `Default` pipeline un-outlined — `OutlineHierarchyScopes` is `Opaque`-only — and never produces a `Submit`), and not nested inside `pl.cluster()` / `pl.spmd()` / another `pl.at` (the inner dispatch is folded into the enclosing Group / Spmd wrapper; codegen emits `set_predicate` from the *outer* call only). Both rejected at parse time; `ScopeOutliner` and a new `AssertNoInnerDispatchPredicate` in `OutlineClusterScopes` re-assert them for hand-built / deserialized IR.
  - **Scope-producer tracking extended to `with pl.at(...) as tid:`**, so the Phase-2 contract genuinely applies. Unlike `pl.spmd`, `pl.at` accepts `deps=` on *every* form, so the remediation hint always offers it rather than redirecting to the `as tid` capture form.
  - **Outliner bug found and fixed (also affected the Phase-3 `pl.spmd` form):** `ScopeOutliner` read `kAttrPredicate` raw, bypassing its own `store_target_renames_` substitution. A `pl.at` body typically writes its tensor with `pl.store`, so the attr names a scope-local post-store alias that outlining drops — the emitted `Submit` then referenced a dangling Var (caught by `UseAfterDefCheck`). The operand is now resolved exactly as the synthesised call's args are. Latent for `pl.spmd` too, whenever a predicate operand was written by an earlier sibling `pl.at` scope.
  - Tests: parser (attr landing, canonical order, print round-trip, no-`as tid` form, level + three nesting rejections, shared shape validation, scope-producer contract, hint wording), transforms (SSA versioning, outliner rebinding, DCE liveness), codegen (`set_predicate` block, operator/operand-order, emission order, plus a `windowize=True` case — `windowize` is `pl.at`-only and is the only DSL path reaching the predicate entry in `WindowExternalization`'s view-synthesised key filter). On-board **a2a3** ST gains a `pl.at` variant: **6/6 pass** across all three authoring forms. Full UT suite 7791 passed, 2 skipped. Docs updated (en + zh-cn).
- [ ] **Phase 5 (optional) — polish** — remaining:
  - Orchestration-codegen doc note for `set_predicate`.
  - A runnable MoE "skip empty experts" example under `examples/`.
  - ~~Broader ST parity vs the runtime `predicated_dispatch` case~~ → **done in Phase 3**, extended in Phase 4: `tests/st/runtime/scheduling/test_predicated_dispatch.py` is the frontend counterpart of the runtime's hand-written scene test and now covers the submit, `pl.spmd` scope and `pl.at` scope forms on a2a3.

> **Dropped: comparison-expression sugar.** Originally planned as a separate phase on top of a `pl.dispatch_pred(tensor, indices, op, target)` constructor. Per review feedback the expression is strictly constrainable *and* extends better (a future runtime multi-condition predicate maps naturally onto `a[0] > 0 and b[0] > 0`, whereas the constructor would need a combinator API). The constructor was therefore removed entirely rather than shipped and later deprecated — `predicate=(t[i] > 0)` is the only surface, and `pl.dispatch_pred` never ships.

### Carried constraints

- **Expressiveness** is fixed to `tensor[indices] OP const` (one comparison), matching the runtime's single-comparison `DispatchPredicate`. Chained comparisons, arithmetic, boolean combination, and non-literal right-hand sides are rejected at parse time; reduce anything richer to a single gate value in a prior kernel. Native multi-condition would require a runtime-side change.
- **Contract**: predicate operand producer ∈ `deps=` — enforced at the parser where statically provable (Phase 2), extended to scope-produced operands in Phase 3.

title: feat(ir): dispatch-predicate frontend — Phase 1 (pl.spmd_submit(predicate=...))
body:
> **Phase 1 of [hw-native-sys/pypto#2066](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/2066)** — dispatch-predicate phased rollout. This PR is the core frontend, complete and validated end-to-end on onboard **a2a3**. The remaining phase (`with pl.spmd(...)` scope form) is tracked in #2066 and lands separately.

_(Reopened from the closed WIP #2062 — same branch/commits, now tracker-scoped and non-draft.)_

Tracks [hw-native-sys/pypto#2059](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/2059). Depends on the runtime `DispatchPredicate` struct + `Arg::set_predicate(...)` from [hw-native-sys/simpler#1314](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/pull/1314). That runtime is **already on `upstream/main`** (bumped to `a756969c`, a descendant of `cddf2b6c`, in [hw-native-sys/pypto#2061](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/2061)), so **this PR no longer bumps the submodule** — it is pure frontend on top of the current runtime. That runtime PR explicitly deferred the frontend ("Frontend (pypto `pl.spmd(predicate=...)`) lands separately") — this is it.

## What this does

Exposes the runtime **dispatch predicate** through the DSL: a statically-materialized SPMD task can be **conditionally retired** (never dispatched to a core) based on a value only a *prior* task produces. The condition is evaluated by the scheduler **at the dispatch point** — after the task's dependencies are satisfied, so the value is current — **not** in orchestration (which would stall on `wait_for_tensor_ready`). A false predicate retires the task inline via the dep-only path, still settling fanin/fanout so downstream consumers unlock; it does **not** vanish from the graph.

### Motivating use case — MoE skip-empty-experts

DeepSeek-V4 expert-routed MoE computes each expert's `row_count` at runtime (written into a tensor). Orchestration only has the tensor *address*, not the *value*, so "skip experts with `row_count == 0`" cannot be a constant known at submit. Alternatives and why they fail:

| Approach | Problem |
| --- | --- |
| Read the count in orchestration, branch on submit | Stalls on `wait_for_tensor_ready` → serializes the pipeline |
| Submit all experts, branch inside the kernel | Still pays launch + core-occupancy + data-movement per empty expert |
| Make the expert count dynamic | Breaks the static task-graph / AOT-orchestration model |

The dispatch predicate resolves this: submit all experts statically (graph stays static, no orchestration stall); each carries `predicate = row_count[e] > 0` and depends on the gather producer; the scheduler reads `row_count[e]` at the dispatch point (no wait) and dispatches only non-empty experts.

## Frontend usage (the writing form)

A plain comparison expression passed as `predicate=` to `pl.spmd_submit` / `pl.submit`:

```python
out, tid = pl.spmd_submit(
    self.kernel, *args, core_num=N,
    deps=[producer_tid],                               # see Contract below
    predicate=(tensor[i0, i1, ...] > 0),
)
```

> **The comparison is parsed as an ordinary expression, but never evaluated.** `rc[0, 0]` is already the DSL's sugar for `pl.read`, so the kwarg lowers to plain IR — `Gt(Cast(tensor.read(rc, [0, 0])), 0)` — reusing the IR's existing comparison nodes rather than any bespoke encoding. It is stored on `Submit.predicate`, never in a statement position, so the `tensor.read` is **not** executed in orchestration: doing so would stall on `wait_for_tensor_ready`, exactly what the predicate exists to avoid.

It maps 1:1 onto the runtime `operand[indices] <op> target`:

| Part | Meaning | Constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tensor` | operand tensor read at the dispatch point | a **signed 8/16/32/64-bit integer** tensor, subscripted to one element (the runtime sign-extends what it reads, so an unsigned operand could compare as negative and silently invert the decision; sub-byte dtypes have no addressable single-element read) |
| `[indices]` | element locator | one integer-scalar index per operand dimension (`ConstInt`, loop `Var`, or integer arithmetic); constants must be non-negative and there must be at most `MAX_TENSOR_DIMS` of them — the runtime array is a fixed `uint32_t[]` |
| `<op>` | comparison | one of `==` `!=` `>` `<` `>=` `<=`, single (unchained) |
| `target` | right-hand side | **integer literal** (may be negative) |

The mirrored order is accepted and normalized: `0 < rc[e]` records the same predicate as `rc[e] > 0` (the operator flips so the tensor is the operand).

MoE example (the shape validated end-to-end):

```python
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
def main(self, x, out, rc):                            # rc = row_count tensor
    with pl.manual_scope():
        rc, g_tid = pl.spmd_submit(self.gate, rc, core_num=1)      # producer of rc
        out, _ = pl.spmd_submit(
            self.expert, x, out, core_num=1,
            deps=[g_tid],                                          # producer is a dep
            predicate=(rc[0, 0] > 0),
        )
    return out
```

Generated orchestration C++ (mirrors the runtime's hand-written form):

```cpp
L0TaskPredicate params_t1_pred;
params_t1_pred.operand.tensor = &ext_rc;
params_t1_pred.operand.ndims = 2;
params_t1_pred.operand.indices[0] = 0;
params_t1_pred.operand.indices[1] = 0;
params_t1_pred.op = PredicateOp::GT;
params_t1_pred.target = 0;
params_t1.set_predicate(params_t1_pred);
```

Parse-time validation rejects everything the runtime cannot express. Because the kwarg is now parsed as an ordinary expression, most of these are caught by the DSL's own typing with better messages than a bespoke check would give:

| Rejected | Reported as |
| --- | --- |
| `rc > 0` | `must be ScalarExpr or Var with ScalarType` — a predicate locates one *element* |
| `rc[0] > 0` on a rank-2 `rc` | same — a partial index yields a view, not an element |
| `rc[0, 0] > 1.5` | `requires same numeric dtype category` (int32 vs fp32) |
| `rc[0, 0] > u[0, 0]` | same — the RHS must be a constant, not another element |
| `0 < rc[0, 0] < 8` | `Only simple comparisons supported` — the runtime evaluates exactly one |
| `rc[0, 0] in x` | `Unsupported comparison` |
| `rc[x, 0] > 0` | `index element 0 must be ScalarType` |
| `rc[0, 0] % 8 == 0`, `a[0] > 0 and b[0] > 0` | not a bare comparison — `predicate must be a single comparison` |

### Contract

**The predicate operand tensor's producer MUST be one of the submit's `deps=`** so the dispatch-point read observes the current value. Without it the scheduler may evaluate the predicate before the producer has written the tensor and dispatch on stale data — a silent wrong result.

The parser makes a **best-effort spot check**, not a guarantee — a clean parse means "no obvious mistake found", not "proven correct". It tracks the result variables a submit binds via tuple unpacking and rejects a predicate whose operand producer is missing from `deps=`. It does **not** see through, and silently accepts:

| Not covered | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `rc2 = rc` then `rc2[0, 0]` | the alias is a fresh variable with no recorded producer |
| a tensor passed as `pl.Out` and rebound under a new name | only the returned binding is tracked, not the argument alias |
| `rc3 = self.helper(rc)` | any intervening call launders the association |
| `res = pl.spmd_submit(...)` (single-target form) | that path records nothing |
| any `deps=` containing an `Array[N, TASK_ID]` entry — **including the common `deps=[tids[i]]`** | array entries do not name producers individually, so the check is skipped for that submit |
| a producer written *later*, e.g. a loop-carried `rc` from the previous iteration | the lookup runs while parsing the predicate |

One case that previously **falsely certified** a submit is now caught: strict SSA reuses one `ir.Var` object across same-named rebindings, so `deps=[tid]` matched by identity even when `tid` had been rebound to a different task in between. A per-Var binding generation detects that.

Getting `deps=` right remains the author's responsibility.

## Design approach

Mirrors the existing `allow_early_resolve` path (simpler#1065) end-to-end: `pl.spmd_submit → Submit → SubmitToCallView → orchestration codegen`.

- **IR (`Submit`)** — a single first-class field, `std::optional<ExprPtr> predicate_`, holding the comparison Expr as written (e.g. `Gt(Cast(tensor.read(rc, [0, 0])), 0)`). No new IR vocabulary: it reuses the existing `ObjectKind::{Eq,Ne,Lt,Le,Gt,Ge}` nodes over `tensor.read`, so reflection needs no new leaf type and the node's shape stays open — a future runtime accepting `And(Gt(...), Gt(...))` needs no IR or frontend change. It is SSA-bearing, so visitor/mutator walk it exactly like `core_num_`, and the 13 Submit reconstruction sites pass it through.

  *Decomposition into the runtime's `operand OP target` triple lives in orchestration codegen*, the layer that owns the runtime ABI — deliberately not baked into the IR node.
- **Pass safety** — the predicate Expr is part of the use-def chain, so the C++ visitor/mutator walk it (like `deps_` / `core_num_`) and **all 13 `Submit` reconstruction sites** pass it through. Verified end-to-end: it survives inline / SSA / outline / materialize and resolves to `&ext_<name>` at codegen.

  One deliberate exemption: the **`NoNestedCall` verifier skips `Submit::predicate_`**. That invariant flattens *evaluated* expressions into temporaries, but the predicate is a declarative spec the scheduler evaluates at dispatch, so it is inherently nested (`Gt(Cast(tensor.read(..)), 0)`). Flattening it would be actively wrong — hoisting the read into an orchestration statement makes it a real load that stalls on `wait_for_tensor_ready` (the very stall the predicate exists to avoid) and strips the operand/indices codegen needs. `FlattenCallExpr` already leaves the field alone (it only walks `args_`). Everything else on the Submit is still checked.
- **Cross-layer** — the nanobind `Submit` ctor takes one optional `predicate` Expr; `ir.pyi` updated. No enum is bound (none is needed).
- **Codegen** — `EmitPredicateHint` decomposes `Cmp(Cast?(tensor.read(t, MakeTuple(i...))), ConstInt)` (either operand order, flipping the operator when the constant is on the left) into the `L0TaskPredicate` + `set_predicate` block, emitted on the task's `L0TaskArgs` before `rt_submit_*`. Anything not in that shape is reported as a user error. `elem_size` is intentionally left for the runtime to derive from the tensor dtype.
- **Printer / deserializer** — round-trip the single Expr; the comparison prints itself, so there is no bespoke syntax (`predicate=(rc[0, 0] > 0)` prints and reparses).

### Why `pl.spmd_submit` (not the scope form) for this cut

`pl.spmd_submit` builds a `Submit` directly at parse time (before SSA), so the Submit-level pass-walk fully covers it with **zero scope-attr plumbing**. The `with pl.spmd(predicate=...)` scope form is outlined *after* SSA (pass 8-9), so its operand/index Vars would live on scope attrs during SSA and need extra `VisitScopeAttrs`/`MutateScopeAttrs` Expr-walking + scope serializer/printer handling — deferred to keep this PR tight.

## Scope / deferred

Out of scope for this PR (tracked in #2066; shares the same IR fields + codegen):

1. **`with pl.spmd(predicate=...)` scope form** — that scope outlines *after* SSA, so its operand/index Vars would live on scope attrs during SSA and need `VisitScopeAttrs` / `MutateScopeAttrs` Expr-walking plus scope serializer/printer handling. `pl.spmd_submit` builds a `Submit` at parse time (pre-SSA), so the Submit-level pass-walk covers it with zero scope plumbing.
2. **Optional polish** — an orchestration-codegen doc note, a runnable MoE example under `examples/`.

Two items that were originally planned as separate phases are **already in this PR**: the producer∈deps dataflow check (see Contract), and the comparison-expression surface — the `pl.dispatch_pred(...)` constructor was removed rather than shipped and later deprecated, so `predicate=(t[i] > 0)` is the only surface and the constructor never ships.

Predicate expressiveness is deliberately limited to `tensor[indices] OP const` — this matches the runtime's single-comparison `DispatchPredicate`. Multiple conditions / boolean combination / arithmetic are not expressible; the pattern is to reduce them to one gate value in a prior kernel. Native multi-condition would require a runtime-side change.

## Testing

- `tests/ut/language/parser/test_submit_predicate.py` — parse/IR field population, all 6 op spellings, negative-target, 5 negative cases, print→parse round-trip.
- `tests/ut/codegen/test_predicate_codegen.py` — full Default pipeline → asserts the `set_predicate` block (and its absence without a predicate).
- `tests/st/runtime/scheduling/test_predicated_dispatch.py` — end-to-end: `x_producer → clobber(predicate=gate[0,0]>0, deps=[xp]) → consumer(deps=[clobber_tid])`. gate=0 → clobber skipped → sentinel(42) survives; gate=1 → clobber dispatched → poison(999); consumer unlocks in **both** cases (proving inline-retire still settles fanout). **Passes on onboard a2a3.**
- Regression: 2808 transforms + codegen UTs green.

title: perf(runtime): prewarm the prebuilt runtime arena at worker init
body:
## Summary

The first dispatch with a given ring sizing pays a **~800 ms cold build** of the prebuilt runtime arena. That cost previously landed inside the first (usually timed) dispatch, inflating benchmarks and first-token latency. Workers now build it eagerly at `init`, so the cold build lands in setup instead.

- **L3**: `DistributedWorker.__init__` and `execute_distributed`'s one-shot path. `DistributedWorker`'s `config` (previously `del`'d as reserved) is now the `RunConfig` whose ring sizing is prewarmed; its `CallConfig` is built through `_make_call_config` — the same construction `run()` uses — so the prewarmed arena's sizing key matches the dispatch's.
- **L2**: `ChipWorker.init` and `execute_on_device`'s one-shot path. L2 dispatch takes ring sizing from the per-call `RunConfig`, never from the worker's own `config`, so `ChipWorker` prewarms a bare `CallConfig` (the runtime's default sizing) — transcribing its config's rings would build an arena no dispatch asks for.
- `benchmark()` now forwards its dispatch config to `prepare()`, which otherwise prewarmed the baseline sizing that the first dispatch immediately discarded.

The arena cache is keyed on the full per-ring sizing vector and is **single-slot per worker**, so dispatches that alternate ring sizings rebuild on each switch. Guidance (keep the sizing constant across a worker's dispatches; per-ring differences within one dispatch are fully covered) is documented in `docs/en/dev/05-runtime-ring-sizing.md` and its zh-cn mirror.

**Dependency:** requires the simpler runtime's `Worker.init(prewarm_config=...)` parameter, landed via the runtime bump to `a756969c` (upstream/main `chore(runtime): bump runtime to a756969c (#2061)`).

## Testing

- [x] Runtime unit tests pass (`tests/ut/runtime/`), including new mock-based prewarm assertions: `test_distributed_worker.py::TestArenaPrewarm` (baseline + ring-sized `config` branches) and `test_worker_reuse.py::test_init_prewarms_arena_cache`; `test_benchmark.py` asserts `benchmark()` forwards its config to `prepare()`.
- [x] Code review completed; `ruff` + `pyright` + `markdownlint` clean.
- [x] Documentation updated (en + zh-cn `05-runtime-ring-sizing.md`).
- [ ] New end-to-end ST `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_ring_sizing_prewarm.py` (functional `f = a + b` under an explicit prewarmed ring sizing) — needs an onboard run; not verified locally due to a pre-existing pto-isa/build_output mismatch that breaks all L3 sim STs in the dev env.

title: [Performance] Recreating CommDomain per L3 dispatch adds ~124 ms lifecycle overhead
body:
## Background

In pypto-lib, `models/deepseek/v4/decode_fwd.py` on Ascend 910B (`a2a3`, EP=2) has a severe performance problem outside the existing runtime STRACE window: every prepared L3 dispatch recreates and releases its communication domain/window buffers.

Across 100 measured rounds after 5 warmup rounds, CommDomain allocation plus backend release costs 123.80 ms on average, while the kernel's STRACE effective time is only 47.78 ms.

Reproduce with:

    PYPTO_BENCH=1 python tools/comm_domain_timing.py \
        models/deepseek/v4/decode_fwd.py \
        -p a2a3 --ep 2 -d 0,1

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `2e6cc68a2b43fb7748769b10fb6976619ec43971` (branch: `temp`) |
| pypto | `7759b264a0327735cb2ff6dccb2e0c1c9f937c31` (branch: `main`) |
| simpler | `a756969cfb4b25756792e6fbcb198d08beb6eea0` (detached) |
| ptoas | `0.48` |
| pto-isa | `83d01313d9bfc247c4b7c8bcf969d1019f0d106f` (detached) |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |
| Driver | `26.0.rc1` |

All simpler, ptoas, and pto-isa versions match the pins from the current pypto checkout.

Diagnosis: **pypto/simpler L3 communication lifecycle** — PyPTO lowers the window-buffer declarations into `with orch.allocate_domain(...)` inside the generated orchestration entry. Therefore every call through a prepared `DistributedWorker` performs a fresh collective allocation and release. The bundled simpler runtime implements the dynamic-domain handshake using file-based IPC announcement and barriers with 100 ms and 50 ms polling intervals, respectively.

### Summary

Prepared L3 programs should be able to reuse their communication domain and window buffers across dispatches. Currently, `decode_fwd` allocates and releases a 2,523,416-byte window per rank on every benchmark round.

The communication lifecycle overhead is approximately 2.59x the measured kernel execution time and accounts for about 72% of the combined lifecycle-plus-kernel time.

### Git Commit ID

`7759b264a0327735cb2ff6dccb2e0c1c9f937c31`

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Reproduction Script

Save the following as `tools/comm_domain_timing.py` in a pypto-lib checkout:

```python
import atexit
import runpy
import statistics
import sys
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

from simpler.worker import Worker

WARMUP = 5
samples = defaultdict(list)


def wrap(method_name, phase):
    original = getattr(Worker, method_name)

    def timed(self, *args, **kwargs):
        start = time.perf_counter_ns()
        result = original(self, *args, **kwargs)
        elapsed_us = (time.perf_counter_ns() - start) / 1_000
        samples[phase].append(elapsed_us)
        print(
            f"[COMM_TIMING] phase={phase} "
            f"seq={len(samples[phase]) - 1} us={elapsed_us:.3f}",
            flush=True,
        )
        return result

    setattr(Worker, method_name, timed)


wrap("_allocate_domain", "alloc")
wrap("_release_domain_now", "free")


def report():
    for phase in ("alloc", "free"):
        values = samples[phase][WARMUP:]
        print(
            f"[COMM_TIMING_SUMMARY] phase={phase} samples={len(values)} "
            f"min_us={min(values):.3f} "
            f"median_us={statistics.median(values):.3f} "
            f"mean_us={statistics.fmean(values):.3f} "
            f"max_us={max(values):.3f}",
            flush=True,
        )

    paired = [
        alloc_us + free_us
        for alloc_us, free_us in zip(
            samples["alloc"][WARMUP:],
            samples["free"][WARMUP:],
        )
    ]
    print(
        f"[COMM_TIMING_SUMMARY] phase=alloc_plus_free samples={len(paired)} "
        f"min_us={min(paired):.3f} "
        f"median_us={statistics.median(paired):.3f} "
        f"mean_us={statistics.fmean(paired):.3f} "
        f"max_us={max(paired):.3f}",
        flush=True,
    )


atexit.register(report)

target = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
sys.argv = [str(target), *sys.argv[2:]]
sys.path[:0] = [str(target.parent), str(Path.cwd())]
runpy.run_path(str(target), run_name="__main__")
```

Run:

    PYPTO_BENCH=1 python tools/comm_domain_timing.py \
        models/deepseek/v4/decode_fwd.py \
        -p a2a3 --ep 2 -d 0,1

### Expected Performance

The communication domain/window should be allocated once per prepared worker or compiled-program lifetime and reused across benchmark and serving dispatches.

Steady-state dispatches should not pay collective VMM allocation, IPC handle exchange/import, file barriers, and collective teardown on every invocation.

### Actual Performance

EP=2, 2,523,416-byte window per rank, 100 measured rounds:

| Phase | Median | Mean | P95 | Min | Max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| CommDomain allocate | 103.26 ms | 85.36 ms | 107.52 ms | 2.13 ms | 153.84 ms |
| Backend release | 51.66 ms | 38.44 ms | 53.65 ms | 1.42 ms | 57.35 ms |
| Allocate + release | 154.64 ms | 123.80 ms | 158.86 ms | 3.57 ms | 205.91 ms |
| Kernel effective | 48.43 ms | 47.78 ms | — | 45.60 ms | 49.91 ms |

The latency is strongly quantized:

- Allocation: 80/100 rounds took at least 75 ms; 19/100 took less than 10 ms.
- Release: 73/100 rounds took at least 10 ms; 27/100 took less than 10 ms.
- One-time base communicator initialization took 1.428 seconds and was excluded by warmup.

The quantization matches the current implementation:

- `domain_read_announce` retries every 100 ms.
- `file_barrier` retries every 50 ms.

This means the observed number is the complete end-to-end dynamic CommDomain lifecycle, not isolated `aclrtMalloc` latency.

### Profiling Data

STRACE reports:

    effective_us (100 rounds) min=45604.6 median=48431.4 mean=47780.2 max=49913.1

Parent-side instrumentation reports:

    phase=alloc median_us=103264.900 mean_us=85358.586
    phase=free median_us=51664.668 mean_us=38442.592
    phase=alloc_plus_free median_us=154636.000 mean_us=123801.193

### Additional Context

Potential directions:

1. Hoist CommDomain/window allocation into `DistributedCompiledProgram.prepare()` and release it when the prepared worker closes.
2. Cache domains by program/domain identity, worker set, window size, and buffer layout.
3. If per-dispatch allocation must remain supported, replace file polling with event-driven synchronization or substantially shorter waits.
4. Preserve fresh logical state between dispatches by explicitly resetting counters/buffers rather than physically reallocating the window.

Related: #1189, #1968

title: [Feature] Front-end DSL primitive for cross-core (cube↔vector) sync — expose pto.sync.set / pto.sync.wait
body:
## Summary

Expose a user-facing pypto Python DSL primitive that emits the existing PTO IR cross-core synchronization ops `pto.sync.set` (`SyncSetOp`) / `pto.sync.wait` (`SyncWaitOp`), so kernel authors can hand-write cube↔vector (AIC↔AIV) producer/consumer pipelines. The IR ops and their lowering already exist in PTOAS — only the front-end entry point is missing.

## Motivation / Use Case

Reimplementing hand-written CANN Ascend-C attention kernels natively in pypto (e.g. `models/qwen3/14b/kernels/paged_attention_cce`) requires expressing the cube–vector rendezvous. The CCE version drives it with `AscendC::CrossCoreSetFlag<MODE, PIPE>(id)` / `CrossCoreWaitFlag(id)` and three flags (`qkReady` / `softmaxReady` / `pvReady`) to pipeline **QK (cube) → online-softmax (vector) → PV (cube) → rescale (vector)** with a 2-stack lookahead (`PRE_LAUNCH=2`) and a 3-slot GM workspace.

There is currently no pypto DSL way to place such a rendezvous by hand. Automatic sync insertion (GraphSyncSolver) covers dependency-driven fencing, but a hand-authored software pipeline needs **explicit, pipe-precise control**:
- trigger the flag on a specific pipe's completion (`PIPE_FIX` / `PIPE_MTE3`) — i.e. exactly when the producer's store lands in GM;
- a chosen static or dynamic event id;
- the flag decoupled from data movement, so the author controls buffer depth / lookahead.

The plumbing is already wired downstream:
- PTO IR: `SyncSetOp` (`pto.sync.set`) / `SyncWaitOp` (`pto.sync.wait`) — `include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td:2769`; args: `pipe`, `event_id` (static) / `event_id_dyn`, `ffts_mode` (0..2).
- Lowering: `lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp:1313` → `ffts_cross_core_sync` (A3) / `set_intra_block` (A5), building the FFTS message via `getFFTSMsg`; `sync.wait` → `wait_flag_dev`.
- Event-id allocation: `GraphSyncSolver` has a `CROSS_CORE_SYNC` mode with 16 cross-core event ids (2 reserved) — `include/PTO/Transforms/GraphSyncSolver/Utility.h:31`.

So this request is only for the **DSL front-end** that reaches these ops.

## Proposed API / Behavior

Illustrative (names TBD):

```python
# producer (cube) side, after the result store to GM
pl.sync.set(pipe=pl.PIPE_FIX, event_id=1)     # or pl.PIPE_MTE3
# consumer (vector) side, before the read
pl.sync.wait(pipe=pl.PIPE_MTE2, event_id=1)
```

- `pipe`: which pipe's completion triggers / is awaited (maps to `SyncSetOp.pipe`).
- `event_id`: static int **or** a dynamic index value (`SyncSetOp` already supports both via `event_id` / `event_id_dyn`).
- optional `ffts_mode` (0..2, A3) → `SyncSetOp.ffts_mode`.
- Lowers 1:1 to `pto.sync.set` / `pto.sync.wait`. Should interoperate with (or cleanly opt out of) GraphSyncSolver's automatic event-id allocation so manual and auto sync do not collide on ids.

## Alternatives Considered

- **tpush / tpop** (queue primitives that package GM buffer + FFTS flag): fine for simple producer/consumer, but a queue abstraction may not expose the pipe-precise trigger point, the chosen buffer depth (3 slots), or the decoupled lookahead needed to match a hand-tuned pipeline. An explicit `sync.set/wait` is the low-level escape hatch.
- **Keep authoring these kernels as CCE externs** (status quo): defeats the goal of a native pypto implementation + apples-to-apples perf comparison.

## Additional Context

- Concrete driver: pypto-lib todo "用 pypto 接口重新实现 5 个子 kernel" (`models/qwen3/14b/kernels/paged_attention_cce/todo.md`). `BlockMmadQK` is already reimplemented in pypto; the cube–vector epilogue pipeline is blocked on these primitives.
- Related: hw-native-sys/pypto#1911 (auto-fencing V2C GM deps), hw-native-sys/pypto#1906 (put-fence cross-rank), hw-native-sys/pypto#1820 (explicit AIV-split DSL).

title: ci: run only a smoke subset of unit tests on macOS
body:
## Problem

The `unit-tests` matrix ran the full `tests/ut` suite (~6.7k cases) on **both** `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest`. The second OS re-validates the same pure-Python / IR logic, roughly doubling unit-test CI cost for little added signal (macOS unit-tests ≈ 8.5 min).

## Change

Keep the full suite on Linux; run a small foundational **smoke subset** on macOS:

| OS | pytest target | cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ubuntu-latest | `tests/ut` (full) | ~6700 |
| macos-latest | `tests/ut/core` + `tests/ut/ir/core` | 243 |

The C++ extension's macOS compilation is already validated by the `pip install -v .[dev]` build step, so macOS only needs to confirm the built module **imports and executes**. The chosen dirs cover the core object system (dtype / error / logging) and basic IR node construction — the layers where a macOS-specific binding or compile/execute break would surface.

## Implementation

Uses matrix `include` entries that attach a per-OS `ut_paths` to the existing `os × python-version` matrix. This adds **no new jobs**, so the required-check names `unit-tests (ubuntu-latest, 3.10)` and `unit-tests (macos-latest, 3.10)` are unchanged.

```yaml
matrix:
  os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
  python-version: ["3.10"]
  include:
    - os: ubuntu-latest
      ut_paths: tests/ut
    - os: macos-latest
      ut_paths: tests/ut/core tests/ut/ir/core
```

## Verification

- `pytest tests/ut/core tests/ut/ir/core` locally on macOS: **242 passed, 1 skipped in 3.4s**.
- Matrix expansion checked: still exactly 2 jobs with the original names; Linux → full, macOS → smoke.

## Note

macOS no longer catches macOS-only failures outside the smoke dirs (e.g. codegen / language layers). Linux still runs everything; widen `ut_paths` for macOS if a macOS-specific regression slips through.

title: fix(ir): allow INT16 indices in gather index form on A5
body:
## Problem

The `tile.gather` and `tensor.gather` type deducers hard-coded the A2/A3-only index-form constraints (**indices `INT32`**; **`tmp` `INT32` with matching rank) for *all* backends. As a result, valid A5 (Ascend950) programs — which permit `i16` indices and impose no `tmp` dtype/shape relation (PTO IR manual, `pto.tgather` A5 index-form checks) — were rejected at IR type deduction, before ever reaching the backend.

## Fix

Type deduction is backend-agnostic and runs **before** arch selection, so it now accepts the **union** of per-target constraints and leaves the arch-specific rules to the PTOAS verifier (which already implements them per arch):

- **indices**: accept `INT32 | INT16` (was `INT32`-only)
- **`tmp`**: require only that it is a Vec tile operand (dropped the `INT32` dtype + matching-rank checks)

### Changes
- `src/ir/op/tile_ops/gather.cpp` — relax `DeduceTileGatherType` (indices `INT32|INT16`; drop `tmp` dtype + rank checks)
- `src/ir/op/tensor_ops/gather.cpp` — relax `DeduceTensorGatherType` (mirrors `tensor.scatter`, which already accepts `INT16` indices)
- Updated gather docstrings across the DSL/IR tile and tensor wrappers
- `tests/ut/ir/operators/test_gather.py`, `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_gather.py` — A5 INT16 index-form regression tests

## Testing
Local UT + system/runtime tests for the A5 INT16 gather index form pass.

title: [New Op] Add PyPTO frontend for pto.tprefetch_async (async GM→L2 prefetch)
body:
### Operation Level

**Other** — a comm/system-level **asynchronous memory-prefetch primitive**, not a tensor/block compute op. It starts an SDMA-backed async prefetch from GM into **L2 cache** and returns an async event/session pair for completion tracking.

### Proposed Name & Signature

PTOAS now implements the full op family (see **Additional Context**), but PyPTO has **no frontend at all** for it. The op family needs four coordinated pieces exposed at the DSL, plus three new IR value types (`PrefetchAsyncContext`, `AsyncEvent`, `AsyncSession`).

Proposed DSL surface (final namespace is a design decision for the implementer — a dedicated `pl.prefetch.*` module is suggested since this is neither a plain `pl.tile.*` compute op nor a `pld.*` distributed op):

```python
# 1. Build an async-prefetch context from a GM workspace buffer (i8 scratch)
ctx: pl.PrefetchAsyncContext = pl.prefetch.make_context(workspace)

# 2. Kick off an async GM -> L2 prefetch of a flat contiguous 1D GM region;
#    returns an async completion event
event: pl.AsyncEvent = pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(src, ctx)

# 3. Project the session bound to the context
session: pl.AsyncSession = pl.prefetch.session(ctx)

# 4. Wait for the prefetch to complete
done: bool = pl.prefetch.wait(event, session)
```

Mapping to the PTOAS ops:

| PyPTO frontend (proposed) | PTOAS op |
| --- | --- |
| `pl.prefetch.make_context(workspace)` | `pto.make_prefetch_async_context` |
| `pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(src, ctx)` | `pto.tprefetch_async` → `TPREFETCH_ASYNC(src, ctx)` |
| `pl.prefetch.session(ctx)` | `pto.get_prefetch_async_session` |
| `pl.prefetch.wait(event, session)` | `pto.comm.wait_async_event` |

### Semantics Description

- **`make_context(workspace)`**: materializes a first-class `PrefetchAsyncContext` from a GM workspace pointer (i8 scratch region used by the SDMA path).
- **`async_prefetch(src, ctx)`**: starts one asynchronous prefetch from GM into **L2 cache** via SDMA CMO. Returns an `AsyncEvent`. Does **not** block.
  - **Constraint (mirrors PTOAS `verify()`):** `src` must be a **flat contiguous logical-1D GM** region (view-like / GM memref). Non-1D or non-GM sources must be rejected at PyPTO IR verification time, matching the PTOAS op's input checks.
- **`session(ctx)`**: pure projection of the async session tied to `ctx` (used to wait on the returned event).
- **`wait(event, session)`**: waits for the async prefetch to complete; yields a boolean/`i1` done flag.

The op is a **cache hint / latency-hiding primitive**: it does not change any tensor values, only warms L2. Unlike most PTO intrinsics, `TPREFETCH_ASYNC` does not carry implicit wait-event synchronization — completion is explicit via the event/session.

### Example Usage

```python
@pl.program
class PrefetchExample:
    @pl.function
    def main(self, x: pl.Tensor[[4096], pl.FP32], ws: pl.Tensor[[1024], pl.INT8]) -> pl.Tensor[[4096], pl.FP32]:
        # Warm L2 with x while other work proceeds
        ctx = pl.prefetch.make_context(ws)
        evt = pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(x, ctx)
        session = pl.prefetch.session(ctx)

        # ... unrelated compute overlaps the prefetch ...

        pl.prefetch.wait(evt, session)   # ensure x is resident in L2 before the hot loop
        # ... consume x from the now-warm cache ...
        return x
```

### Hardware Support Considerations

- Maps directly to the Ascend PTO-ISA intrinsic `TPREFETCH_ASYNC(src, ctx)`, implemented over **SDMA CMO** (cache-management ops).
- Effective only on **A3 / A5**. On platforms where `SdmaWorkspaceManager::Init` is unavailable, PTOAS falls back to a **no-op prefetch** (with a runtime warning); PTOAS also exposes `PTO_DISABLE_SDMA_WORKSPACE_INIT=1` as an A3/A5 runtime fallback. The PyPTO frontend should degrade gracefully (functional no-op) on unsupported targets rather than error.
- Since it only warms cache, correctness is target-independent; only performance benefits are hardware-specific.

### Motivation / Use Case

`pto.tprefetch_async` is the only PTOAS primitive that lets a kernel **proactively pull GM data into L2 cache asynchronously**, overlapping the fill latency with unrelated compute. This is a key latency-hiding lever for memory-bound kernels (large GEMM operands, attention KV, MoE expert weights) where the working set exceeds on-chip capacity but fits in L2.

Today PyPTO cannot express this at all:
- The status matrix (`docs/zh-cn/dev/ptoas-op-status.md`, updated 2026-06-23) still marks `pto.tprefetch_async` as *"ptoas未实现 (ISA_ONLY)"* — but **PTOAS has since implemented the full op family** (op defs + verifiers + EmitC lowering to `TPREFETCH_ASYNC(...)` + runnable samples). The status doc row should also be corrected to reflect this.
- The related `pto.tprefetch` (prefetch into a local **tile** buffer, not L2) is likewise unimplemented in PyPTO (marked *MISSING (infra, skip)*), but is out of scope for this request — this issue is specifically about the **L2 async** path.

Exposing this unblocks manual latency-hiding in hand-written kernels and gives passes a target for future auto-prefetch insertion.

### Additional Context

Reference implementation in the PTOAS repo (sibling checkout `../PTOAS`):

- Op definitions: `include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td`
  - `TPrefetchAsyncOp` — *"Asynchronously prefetch global data into L2 cache via SDMA CMO"*
  - `MakePrefetchAsyncContextOp`, `GetPrefetchAsyncSessionOp`
- Verifiers: `lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp` (`TPrefetchAsyncOp::verify()` — enforces flat-contiguous-1D GM `src`)
- EmitC lowering: `lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp` → emits `TPREFETCH_ASYNC(...)` / `pto::PrefetchAsyncContext`
- Manual: `docs/PTO_IR_manual.md` § *`pto.tprefetch_async` - Asynchronous GM Prefetch into L2*
- Runnable samples: `test/samples/TPrefetchAsync/` (`tprefetch_async_binding.py` / `.pto` / compare script) and lit tests `test/lit/pto/tprefetch_async_*.pto`

Implementation will be a cross-layer effort: register the three IR value types + four ops in C++ (`include/pypto/ir/`, `src/ir/`), add nanobind bindings + `.pyi` stubs, build the `pl.prefetch.*` DSL surface, wire codegen to the PTOAS ops, and add unit + (A3/A5) system tests.

Related PyPTO op-status tracking: `docs/zh-cn/dev/ptoas-op-status.md` (row `pto.tprefetch_async`).

title: feat(passes): InsertCommFence — cacheinvalid + fence for data-before-signal
body:
## Summary

ptoas 0.50 pushes the *data-before-signal* obligation onto the compiler: a
cross-rank publishing write must be visible to the peer before the
`pld.system.notify` that releases it, and a value read after `pld.system.wait`
must not come from a stale cache line. This PR adds the `InsertCommFence` pass
plus the codegen changes ptoas 0.50 requires.

**1. Add the InsertCommFence pass** (runs last in the Default/DebugTile
pipelines). It is a single **stateless, purely-local** IR traversal — no
control-flow analysis and no cross-statement state. It classifies each leaf
statement and appends markers immediately after it:

- **Local publishing write** — a window-bound `tile.store`, or a `get` into a
  local window destination: a whole-tensor region
  `system.cacheinvalid(target, shape, offsets)` followed by a GM `system.fence`.
  The target is trivially in scope at the write site (window params, aliases,
  loop-carried `iter_arg`s, and branch-local values all invalidate correctly).
  Whole-tensor for now; narrowing to the precise sub-region is a follow-up.
- **Remote write** — `remote_store` / `put`: only a GM `system.fence`. The paired
  peer-region `cacheinvalid` lands at a peer-offset address (`local_ptr +
  delems(peer)`) that is not yet IR-expressible, so its codegen emits it — a
  workaround pending a first-class IR form for the peer address. The release
  fence is inserted here (not embedded in codegen) so ordering stays IR-visible.
- **Opaque write** — a `Submit`, or a call to an unregistered user function whose
  body is not analysed here: a conservative whole-GM `system.cacheinvalid()`
  (no args) + `system.fence`.
- **After a wait**: a whole-GM `system.cacheinvalid()` before the next cacheable
  GM read.
- **notify: nothing.** ptoas ties the release fence to the *write's*
  cacheinvalid, not to the notify — so a pure barrier notify (no data) and a
  notify releasing data written in an earlier loop both need no marker of their
  own. Established empirically on ptoas 0.50.

The pass is idempotent (re-running inserts nothing) and runs after all
statement-reordering passes so each marker stays adjacent to its write through
codegen.

**2. Inline `CommRemoteOffset`** (`fix(codegen)`). The distributed remote-op
codegen computed the peer offset via a `func.call @CommRemoteOffset_<dtype>`
helper. ptoas' `pto-memory-consistency` pass rejects that `func.call` (the callee
holds CommContext `pto.load_scalar` reads), demanding they live in the caller.
The offset arithmetic is now inlined at each call site; the now-dead helper
machinery is removed (net −118 lines). This is an independent, pre-existing
blocker for **all** distributed remote-op kernels on the latest ptoas —
baseline `main` failed identically.

**3. ptoas 0.50 toolchain + TPUT drain.** Bump the ptoas toolchain to 0.50.
`put` (TPUT) codegen keeps a tail `pto.barrier <PIPE_ALL>` between the tput and
its peer cacheinvalid: TPUT is a DMA, and the GM fence orders *memory* but does
not drain the MTE pipe that issued the DMA, so without the barrier the following
notify can fire before the (possibly atomic) DMA has landed at the peer.
Device-verified: an MTE3-scoped barrier is **not** enough — only PIPE_ALL is
stable (PTOAS#872 workaround; remove once ptoas drains the tput itself).

## Verified end-to-end on ptoas 0.50

A distributed ring `remote_store`+`notify` kernel compiles end-to-end through
ptoas 0.50 to final C++. The generated `.pto` for a remote write is
`pto.tstore → pto.cmo.cacheinvalid … single_cache_line (codegen) →
pto.fence.barrier_all #pto.fence_scope<gm> (pass) → pto.comm.tnotify`, and the
inline offset (`pto.load_scalar` reads + `arith.divsi`) replaces the rejected
`func.call`.

## Testing

- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_insert_comm_fence.py` — Before/Expected structural
  tests: local-window `cacheinvalid`+`fence`, remote-write `fence`-only,
  opaque-write whole-GM marker, wait-side whole-GM `cacheinvalid`,
  notify-needs-nothing, straight-line / if-branch / loop / back-edge / two-phase
  and ring-allreduce combos, and idempotency.
- `tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_distributed_pto_codegen.py` — asserts the
  inline offset (no `func.call @CommRemoteOffset`) and the
  `store < cacheinvalid < fence < tnotify` lowering (plus the `put` tail
  `PIPE_ALL` barrier).
- `tests/ut/codegen` + `tests/ut/ir/transforms` sweep green.
- Docs updated (en + zh; pass slot 43; distributed-ops helper table).

title: [Feature] Tensor API: keep matmul operands resident in L1 (Mat) across a loop (load-once / stationary operand)
body:
### Summary

At the **tensor API** level (`pl.matmul`), there is no way to keep a matmul operand **resident in L1 (`Mem.Mat`)** across a user-written loop. When the same operand (typically a small, stationary left matrix) is reused inside a `pl.range` loop, the compiler emits that operand's `tile.load(..., target_memory=Mem.Mat)` **inside the loop body**, so it is re-loaded from GM on every iteration instead of being loaded once and kept resident.

We would like a tensor-level mechanism to express "this operand stays resident in L1/Mat across the loop" (load-once / stationary operand), so users don't have to drop to the tile API to get it.

### Motivation / Use Case

A very common GEMM shape is a **small stationary left matrix multiplied against a large / streamed right matrix**: e.g. a resident weight or query tile swept across many KV / activation tiles. The intended hardware behavior is:

- load the small left operand into L1 (and on to L0A) **once**, keep it resident;
- **loop** over the large right operand, bringing on-chip only the right sub-matrix each iteration.

This is exactly the pattern users reach for when the right matrix is too large to fit L1 all at once and must be streamed. Today it cannot be expressed on the tensor API:

- The tensor API is otherwise the recommended, compiler-managed path (no manual `load`/`move`), but it silently reloads the stationary operand every iteration — redundant GM→L1 DMA traffic proportional to the loop trip count.
- `AutoTileMatmulL0` does **not** help: it only tiles the K-dimension of a *single* `tile.matmul`; it has no notion of cross-iteration operand residency for a user-written loop.
- A single wide `pl.matmul(lhs, rhs_wide)` only works when the *entire* right operand fits L1 (Mat ≤ 512KB on Ascend910B). A genuinely large right matrix overflows L1, because there is no L1-level streaming/tiling for one tensor-level matmul.

Net effect: for this whole class of kernels, users must abandon the tensor API and hand-manage memory spaces at the tile level.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Two possible directions (either would solve the use case):

**Option A — explicit residency hint** on the operand or the matmul:

```python
# left operand pinned to L1/Mat for the lifetime of the loop
lhs_resident = pl.resident(lhs, space=pl.Mem.Mat)
for n in pl.range(0, N, N_TILE):
    b_n = rhs[:, n : n + N_TILE]
    c_n = pl.matmul(lhs_resident, b_n, out_dtype=pl.FP32)  # loaded once, reused
    out = pl.assemble(out, c_n, [0, n])
```

**Option B — compiler LICM (loop-invariant code motion)**: when an operand and all of its `tile.load` arguments are loop-invariant, hoist the generated `tile.load(..., Mem.Mat)` out of the loop automatically. No API change; `pl.matmul(lhs, b_n)` inside a loop would "just work" (left loaded once).

### Alternatives Considered

- **Tile-level manual hoist (works today, verified):** load `lhs` to `Mem.Mat` + move to `Mem.Left` once *outside* the loop, reuse inside. This produces exactly the desired IR (see below). Downside: forces users off the tensor API and onto manual memory-space management for an otherwise-simple kernel.
- **Single wide `pl.matmul` + AutoTileMatmulL0 A-stationary:** only viable when the whole right operand fits L1; does not scale to a large/streamed right matrix.

### Additional Context

Verified on commit `aff862ba` by running the Default pass pipeline with `dump_ir` and inspecting the final IR.

**Naive tensor-level loop — left operand reloaded every iteration** (`ConvertTensorToTileOps` places the `lhs` load inside the loop, and no later pass hoists it out through all 44 passes):

```python
for n in pl.range(0, 2048, 128, init_values=(out,)):
    b_n     = pl.tile.load(rhs, [0, n], [128, 128], target_memory=pl.Mem.Mat)
    lhs_mat = pl.tile.load(lhs, [0, 0], [16, 128],  target_memory=pl.Mem.Mat)  # reloaded every iteration
    c_n     = pl.tile.matmul(lhs_mat, b_n)
    out     = pl.tile.store(c_n, [0, n], out)
```

**Tile-level manual hoist — left operand resident** (dedicated L0A allocation, loaded once outside the loop — the behavior we want the tensor API to be able to express):

```python
mem_left = pl.tile.alloc(pl.Mem.Left, 4096)
lhs_l1   = pl.tile.load(lhs, [0, 0], [16, 128], target_memory=pl.Mem.Mat)  # once, outside loop
lhs_left = pl.tile.move(lhs_l1, target_memory=pl.Mem.Left)                  # once, resident
for n in pl.range(0, 2048, 128, init_values=(out,)):
    b_l1    = pl.tile.load(rhs, [0, n], [128, 128], target_memory=pl.Mem.Mat)
    b_right = pl.tile.move(b_l1, target_memory=pl.Mem.Right)
    c       = pl.tile.matmul(lhs_left, b_right)  # reuses resident lhs_left
    out     = pl.tile.store(c, [0, n], out)
```

Related: #1595 (AutoTileMatmulL0 limitations).

title: feat(dsl): expose tile.gather_row as a first-class DSL interface
body:
## Summary

`tile.gather_row` was previously reachable only through the parser's IR-builder fallback (`_dispatch_ir_builder_op`): the C++ printer emits `pl.tile.gather_row(...)`, but the language layer had no matching wrapper, so the op carried no type-checked signature, docstring, or IDE surface and was handled like a pass-internal lowering op.

This PR promotes it to a first-class DSL interface:

- Add a `gather_row` wrapper to `pypto.language.op.tile_ops` (mirroring `load` / `store` / `assemble`), exposing `pl.tile.gather_row(dst, src, dst_offset, src_offset, shapes, transpose=...)` with `Tile` / `Tensor` typing and a docstring.
- The parser now dispatches `pl.tile.gather_row` through the DSL-wrapper path (`_dsl_tile.gather_row`) instead of the raw IR-builder fallback. Printed IR round-trips identically (structurally equal).

No IR / op-registry or C++ changes — the `tile.gather_row` op itself is unchanged.

## Testing

- Added a round-trip regression test (`test_tile_gather_row_dsl_interface_roundtrips`) exercising a hand-authored tile-level kernel that calls `pl.tile.gather_row` directly.
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_gather_row.py` — 10 passed.
