- add codegen unit tests for all three barrier ops
- update English and Chinese IR operator docs with the exact lowering forms

## Testing

Added unit tests covering:

- `pl.system.bar_all()` emits `pto.barrier <PIPE_ALL>`
- `pl.system.bar_v()` emits `pto.barrier <PIPE_V>`
- `pl.system.bar_m()` emits `pto.barrier <PIPE_M>`

title: [Bug] Orchestration verification fails when passing a rebound DistributedTensor
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

After MaterializeDistTensorCtx, orchestration functions that thread DistributedTensor context can contain synthesized `pld.system.*` ops such as `pld.system.get_comm_ctx`. However, `IsBuiltinOp()` in [`pypto/src/ir/transforms/utils/op_predicates.cpp`](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/blob/bd4f3563c818dc995977d4631aab461a15f02426/src/ir/transforms/utils/op_predicates.cpp#L72) currently only recognizes these prefixes as builtins: `tile.`, `tensor.`,  `system.` `array.`
It does not treat `pld.system.*` as builtin, even though those ops are registered IR builtins and are introduced by passes.

As a result, transformed IR like this:
```python
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration, level=pl.Level.CHIP, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
def chip_orch(self, signal__ssa_v0: ..., signal_ctx: pld.CommCtxType) -> ...:
    signal__ssa_v1 = self.func_1(signal__ssa_v0, signal_ctx, attrs={...})
    signal_ctx_1: pld.CommCtxType = pld.system.get_comm_ctx(signal__ssa_v1)
    signal__ssa_v2 = self.func_2(signal__ssa_v1, signal_ctx_1, attrs={...})
    return signal__ssa_v2
```
contains a builtin `pld.system.get_comm_ctx(...)` call that `IsBuiltinOp()` misclassifies as non-builtin / user-level.
This can confuse downstream transforms/utilities that use `IsBuiltinOp()` to distinguish builtin ops from user calls.

### Proposed Fix

Extend `IsBuiltinOp()` (https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/blob/bd4f3563c818dc995977d4631aab461a15f02426/src/ir/transforms/utils/op_predicates.cpp#L72) to include the distributed system prefix:
```cpp
return op_name.rfind("tile.", 0) == 0 || op_name.rfind("tensor.", 0) == 0 ||
       op_name.rfind("system.", 0) == 0 || op_name.rfind("array.", 0) == 0 ||
       op_name.rfind("pld.tile.", 0) == 0 || op_name.rfind("pld.tensor.", 0) == 0 ||
       op_name.rfind("pld.system.", 0) == 0;
```

### Steps to Reproduce

```markdown
python orch_verf_failed.py -p a2a3 -d 0,1


[orch_verf_failed.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30587160/orch_verf_failed.py)
```

### Expected Behavior

Should run normally. And verification can pass for this case:
```
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration, level=pl.Level.CHIP, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
    def chip_orch(
        self, signal__ssa_v0: pl.InOut[pld.DistributedTensor[[2, 1], pl.INT32, pl.MemRef("mem_ddr_0", pl.const(0, pl.INT64), 8)]], signal_ctx: pld.CommCtxType
    ) -> pld.DistributedTensor[[2, 1], pl.INT32]:
        signal__ssa_v1: pld.DistributedTensor[[2, 1], pl.INT32, pl.MemRef("mem_ddr_1", pl.const(0, pl.INT64), 8)] = self.func_1(
            signal__ssa_v0, signal_ctx, attrs={"arg_directions": [pl.adir.inout, pl.adir.scalar]}
        )
        signal_ctx_1: pld.CommCtxType = pld.system.get_comm_ctx(signal__ssa_v1)
        signal__ssa_v2: pld.DistributedTensor[[2, 1], pl.INT32, pl.MemRef("mem_ddr_2", pl.const(0, pl.INT64), 8)] = self.func_2(
            signal__ssa_v1, signal_ctx_1, attrs={"arg_directions": [pl.adir.inout, pl.adir.scalar]}
        )
        return signal__ssa_v2
```

### Actual Behavior

```
  Function   | Error
  -----------+--------------------------------------------------------------
  chip_orch  | Verification failed after 'GenerateOrchestration
             | preconditions' for properties {SplitIncoreOrch,
             | OrchestrationReferencesResolved, RuntimeScopesMaterialized,
             | ReturnParamsExplicit, IterArgCarryClassified}:
  -----------+--------------------------------------------------------------
```

### Git Commit ID

bd4f3563c818dc995977d4631aab461a15f02426

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (x86_64)

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: Ring allreduce: unaligned-data handling (dcci flush tail + 32B transfer alignment)
body:
Two alignment gaps in the ring allreduce kernel template that the mesh allreduce kernel already handles but the ring kernel currently does not.

### 1. dcci flush loop misses the chunk tail

**File:** `python/pypto/runtime/builtins/collectives/allreduce_ring/templates/kernel.cpp.in`

The dcci flush loop in both the Reduce-Scatter and AllGather phases steps by 16 elements (`i += 16`), which only covers the full chunk when `chunk_elems % 16 == 0`. Compile-time validation only guarantees `numel % NR == 0`, so a tail cache-line spanning the chunk end goes unflushed.

**Counter-example:** `numel = 18, NR = 2` → `chunk_elems = 9` (36 bytes). Chunk 1 starts at byte 36 and spans two cache lines; the 16-element stride misses the second one.

### 2. 32-byte transfer alignment is missing

The mesh allreduce kernel explicitly rounds ragged spans up to `kTransferAlignmentBytes` = 32 bytes (in `collectives/allreduce/templates/kernel.cpp.in`), aligning `tile_elems` to avoid partial-vector load/store. The ring kernel feeds `tile_elems` raw into `ShapeDyn` / `StrideDyn` with no such rounding.

### 3. `kRecvTileDebugValue` rename

The constant name at the top of the kernel reads like leftover debug scaffolding. The `TASSIGN` call is legitimate (it binds `recv_tile` to its buffer as a placeholder, overwritten by the subsequent `TLOAD`), but the constant should be renamed to something like `kRecvTileInitFill` with a one-line comment.

### Suggested approach

- Extract a shared alignment helper used by both mesh and ring kernel templates.
- For the dcci flush: step by 16 elements but emit one additional flush for the final partial cache-line.
- Add an ST case where `chunk_elems % 16 != 0` (e.g. `numel=18, NR=2`).
- Rename `kRecvTileDebugValue` → `kRecvTileInitFill`.

### Context

Raised in review of PR #2094 by @YunjiQin.

title: feat(distributed): add HOST-orchestrated builtin.tensor.all_to_all_v
body:
## Summary

Closes the last gap in host-orchestrator support for variable-size all-to-all. `pld.tensor.all_to_all_v` (variable-size all-to-all, MPI_Alltoallv pattern) merged as #2112, but only as an InCore composite — calling it from a `host_orch` function hit an explicit "not supported in a HOST orchestration function" rejection. This adds the missing HOST dispatch path, cloning the proven `builtin.tensor.all_to_all` pattern (#1997) across every layer:

- **Op registration** (`collective.cpp`): `builtin.tensor.all_to_all_v`, narrowing `input` and `send_counts` to strict window-bound `DistributedTensor` — forced by `EmitBuiltinWindowCollectiveDispatch`, which has no dispatch path for a plain `Tensor` arg at this layer (same narrowing the existing `builtin.tensor.all_to_all` already applies to its own `input`).
- **Lowering rule** (`lower_host_tensor_collectives_pass.cpp`): `MakeBuiltinAllToAllV`, deriving `MAX_RECV = target.shape[0] / signal.shape[0]` and forwarding it as a kwarg/attr alongside `dtype`.
- **Codegen** (`distributed_ops_codegen.cpp`): the variant string mangles both `max_recv` and `dtype` (`builtin.tensor.all_to_all_v__maxrecv<N>__fp32`) — `MAX_RECV` is baked into the kernel as a compile-time `constexpr`, and codegen's `MarkBuiltinEmitted`/`RecordBuiltinNextLevel` state is program-global, so two call sites with different `MAX_RECV` would otherwise silently mis-share one kernel instantiation.
- **Runtime templates**: new `all_to_all_v/` builtin package. The kernel always transfers the full `MAX_RECV`-row block per destination — matching `LowerTensorAllToAllVRule`'s compile-time `transfer_shape` exactly, for bit-for-bit InCore/HOST parity on the wire — and publishes the runtime-clamped count into peer `recv_counts` via `TNOTIFY` inline with the push.
- **Comm-domain analysis** (`materialize_comm_domain_scopes_pass.cpp`): device-coverage inheritance for both `signal` and `recv_counts` (two `CollectiveConsumer` entries sharing the same data alloc), plus a HOST-side loop-use guard (`repeating_scope_depth_`, tracked for both `ForStmt` and `WhileStmt`) mirroring the InCore path's `CheckAllReduceLoopUse` — the HOST path had **no** equivalent protection before this change, so a caller could previously reuse a single-use signal across loop iterations undetected.
- Removed the explicit `IsInCoreOnlyCollective` rejection in `LowerCompositeOps` now that a HOST rule exists for this op.
- Docs (EN+ZH): documents the new HOST path and corrects a pre-existing inaccuracy — the InCore lowering always transfers the full `MAX_RECV` block; only the *published count* was ever runtime-gated, not the transfer itself.

## Design notes for reviewers

- `send_counts` must be staged through a window buffer at the HOST layer even though it's logically pure-local, per-rank data (never cross-rank-published) — this is a real ergonomic cost of the narrowing above, not a bug. The new HOST system test documents this with an explicit `fill_counts_step`/`fill_counts_orch` staging pair.
- Kept the barrier as the existing single-use `Set(1)`/`wait≥1` protocol, matching every other HOST builtin and the InCore `all_to_all_v` rule this clones — the reusable credit-barrier rework (#2175) is unmerged and out of scope here.
- Kept FP32-only (`CheckSupportedFp32BuiltinVariant`), matching every HOST builtin except `allreduce`. Adding FP16 across all HOST builtins is a separate, broader gap.
- `all_to_all`/`allgather`/`barrier` share the same single-use-signal exposure to `host_orch` loops and have no equivalent guard today — pre-existing, out of scope for this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] Full C++ rebuild in the sim Docker image (`pypto3-hw-native-sys:sim`) — clean.
- [x] Full unit test suite: **8539 passed, 13 skipped, 0 failed** (includes new/updated tests across all 5 touched layers, zero regressions elsewhere).
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files`: clean (headers, English-only, EN/ZH docs parity, docs-nav, clang-format, cpplint, markdownlint, ruff check/format, pyright).
- [x] **Distributed system tests not run in this environment.** `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_host_tensor_all_to_all_v.py` (new) plus the InCore/HOST `all_to_all` regression STs all hit `ImportError: cannot import name 'RunTiming' from '_task_interface'` — a pre-existing local-environment mismatch (the `runtime` submodule checkout is ahead of what the sim image's `simpler` runtime was built against), reproducing identically on unmodified, already-shipped sibling tests. Unrelated to this change, but means the actual distributed exchange logic has not been exercised end-to-end here.
- [x] NPU verification pending.

title: [Feature] Allow pl.aiv_shard on a vector-produced Vec tile so a per-lane scattered gather_row can be expressed inside pl.split_aiv
body:
## Background In pypto-lib, `models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_sparse_attn.py` (`qk_pv`) on `a2a3` has a **compile** problem: there is no way to express, at tensor level, "the two AIV lanes each gather half of a scattered row set into UB, then hand the assembled tile to the cube as a matmul B-operand". `qk_pv` assembles each `[ATTN_K_TILE, HEAD_DIM]` sparse KV tile with 128 single-row `pl.gather_row` calls on the **cube**. Measured on 910B1, the cube's per-row `GM->L1` ND2NZ sustains only ~3.5 scattered 1 KB loads in flight (~21 us for the tile) while a vector lane reaches ~13 (~5 us), and `qk_pv` is 73% MTE2-occupied while its two AIV lanes idle at ~7%. Moving the gather to the AIV lanes is worth ~4% end-to-end on the layer. That works today only via a GM staging buffer plus hand-written `pl.system.set_ffts` + `sync_set`/`sync_wait` (the author-side barrier that #1911 describes). The tensor-level `split_aiv` + `aic_gather` formulation, which needs neither, is blocked. Reproduce with: python repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py --fix 0 # the original rejection python repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py --fix 1 # "derive from aiv_shard" python repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py --fix 3 # "let the implicit path halve it" The repro case is **not committed** — save the file below at the pypto-lib repo root to run it. Files required: `repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py` (self-contained; imports only `pypto.language` and pypto-lib's `golden` harness).
Reproduction case — repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py (save at the pypto-lib repo root) ```python """Repro: no tensor-level way to split a scattered GM->UB gather across the two AIV lanes. Goal: the two AIV lanes each gather half of a scattered row set into UB, then the assembled [ROWS, HEAD_DIM] tile is handed to the cube as a matmul B-operand. The scattered row indices are runtime values (a paged KV top-k list), so the gather must accept arbitrary per-row source offsets. `pl.paged_gather(space=Vec)` is the only tensor-level op that produces a UB-backed Tensor, but it cannot be given a per-lane sub-range of the index list: * a sliced index tensor (static or dynamic) -> "indices must be TensorType" * a pl.aiv_shard(...) result -> "indices must be TensorType" * a [2, n/2] per-lane layout -> "requires 2D indices to have shape [1, n]" `pl.gather_row` does take arbitrary runtime offsets, and `pl.full` gives it a UB-backed Tensor accumulator. But putting that inside `pl.split_aiv` is rejected, and each of the three fixes LowerAutoVectorSplit suggests is itself blocked. Run each variant from the pypto-lib repo root: python repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py --fix 0 # the original rejection python repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py --fix 1 # "derive from aiv_shard" python repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py --fix 3 # "let the implicit path halve it" """ import pypto.language as pl POOL_ROWS = 16384 HEAD_DIM = 512 ROWS = 128 HALF = ROWS // 2 Q_ROWS = 16 @pl.jit def fix0_half_extent( pool: pl.Tensor[[POOL_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], pl.BF16], idx: pl.Tensor[[ROWS], pl.INT32], q: pl.Tensor[[Q_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], pl.BF16], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[Q_ROWS, ROWS], pl.FP32]], ): """Half-extent UB accumulator; the gather's SOURCE offset references aiv.""" with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="fix0", allow_early_resolve=True): for aiv in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN): ub = pl.full([HALF, HEAD_DIM], dtype=pl.BF16, value=0.0) for k in pl.range(HALF): src = pl.cast(pl.read(idx, [aiv * HALF + k]), pl.INDEX) ub = pl.gather_row(ub, pool, [k, 0], [src, 0], [1, HEAD_DIM]) kv = pl.aic_gather(ub) out[0:Q_ROWS, 0:ROWS] = pl.matmul(q, kv, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32) return out @pl.jit def fix1_aiv_shard( pool: pl.Tensor[[POOL_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], pl.BF16], idx: pl.Tensor[[ROWS], pl.INT32], q: pl.Tensor[[Q_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], pl.BF16], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[Q_ROWS, ROWS], pl.FP32]], ): """Fix (1): derive the accumulator from a pl.aiv_shard result.""" with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="fix1", allow_early_resolve=True): for aiv in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN): ub_full = pl.full([ROWS, HEAD_DIM], dtype=pl.BF16, value=0.0) ub = pl.aiv_shard(ub_full) for k in pl.range(HALF): src = pl.cast(pl.read(idx, [aiv * HALF + k]), pl.INDEX) ub = pl.gather_row(ub, pool, [k, 0], [src, 0], [1, HEAD_DIM]) kv = pl.aic_gather(ub) out[0:Q_ROWS, 0:ROWS] = pl.matmul(q, kv, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32) return out @pl.jit def fix3_implicit( pool: pl.Tensor[[POOL_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], pl.BF16], idx: pl.Tensor[[ROWS], pl.INT32], q: pl.Tensor[[Q_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], pl.BF16], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[Q_ROWS, ROWS], pl.FP32]], ): """Fix (3): no explicit boundary ops; both offsets reference the lane index.""" with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="fix3", allow_early_resolve=True): for aiv in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN): ub = pl.full([ROWS, HEAD_DIM], dtype=pl.BF16, value=0.0) for k in pl.range(HALF): src = pl.cast(pl.read(idx, [aiv * HALF + k]), pl.INDEX) ub = pl.gather_row(ub, pool, [aiv * HALF + k, 0], [src, 0], [1, HEAD_DIM]) kv = ub out[0:Q_ROWS, 0:ROWS] = pl.matmul(q, kv, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32) return out VARIANTS = {0: fix0_half_extent, 1: fix1_aiv_shard, 3: fix3_implicit} def golden(tensors): tensors["out"][:] = ( tensors["q"].float() @ tensors["pool"][tensors["idx"].long()].float().t() ).to(tensors["out"].dtype) def build_tensor_specs(): import torch from golden import TensorSpec return [ TensorSpec("pool", [POOL_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], torch.bfloat16, init_value=lambda: torch.randn(POOL_ROWS, HEAD_DIM)), TensorSpec("idx", [ROWS], torch.int32, init_value=lambda: ((torch.arange(ROWS, dtype=torch.int64) * 977) % (POOL_ROWS - ROWS)).to(torch.int32)), TensorSpec("q", [Q_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], torch.bfloat16, init_value=lambda: torch.randn(Q_ROWS, HEAD_DIM) / HEAD_DIM ** 0.5), TensorSpec("out", [Q_ROWS, ROWS], torch.float32, is_output=True), ] if __name__ == "__main__": import argparse from golden import run_jit parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument("--fix", type=int, default=0, choices=sorted(VARIANTS)) parser.add_argument("-p", "--platform", type=str, default="a2a3") parser.add_argument("-d", "--device", type=int, default=0) args = parser.parse_args() result = run_jit( fn=VARIANTS[args.fix], specs=build_tensor_specs(), golden_fn=golden, runtime_cfg=dict(platform=args.platform, device_id=args.device), rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2, ) print("PASS" if result.passed else f"FAIL {result.error}") ```
Reproduction environment: | Component | Version | |---|---| | pypto-lib | `14f3863` (branch: `perf/assemble-swa-decode-window-in-l1-drop-gm-gather`) | | pypto | `6234d0e9` (branch: `main`) | | simpler | `9922afdb` (detached) | | ptoas | `0.54` | | pto-isa | `83d01313` | | CANN | `8.5.1` (runs), `8.3.RC1.alpha003` at `ascend-toolkit/latest` | Version mismatch (off pinned): **simpler** expected `dccb8379080b43173744b9981de2542b3d025e19`, actual `9922afdb08cc6f203eaf39328661e2f2648d333d`. This is a **compile-time** failure in `LowerAutoVectorSplit` / `ConvertTensorToTileOps`; simpler is the runtime and takes no part in those passes, so the divergence is not believed to affect the result. ptoas and pto-isa are on their pins. Diagnosis: **pypto** — all three failures are raised by pypto compiler passes and verifiers. ### Summary `pl.gather_row` is the only op that gathers scattered GM rows at arbitrary **runtime** offsets, and `pl.full` is the only tensor-level way to give it a UB-backed `Tensor` accumulator. That pair cannot be placed inside a `pl.split_aiv` region: `LowerAutoVectorSplit` classifies `tile.gather_row` as full-width and names three fixes, and **each of the three is independently blocked**. | variant | what it does | result | |---|---|---| | `--fix 0` | half-extent `pl.full`, gather's **source** offset references `aiv_id`, `aic_gather` | `LowerAutoVectorSplit: a pl.split_aiv region mixes explicit tile.aiv_shard/tile.aic_gather boundary ops with plain full-width vector op(s) [tile.gather_row] ...` | | `--fix 1` | full-extent `pl.full` -> `pl.aiv_shard` -> gather -> `aic_gather` | `AivSplitValid`: *"'tile.aiv_shard' operand is in Vec, but it transfers a cube-produced value across the cross-core boundary and requires Acc. ... A Vec operand is vector-produced (pl.load / pl.full) and already lives on the AIV lane — drop the pl.aiv_shard and let the implicit affinity-gated split halve it."* | | `--fix 3` | full-extent `pl.full`, **both** offsets reference `aiv_id`, no boundary ops | `AllocatedMemoryAddr`: `Function 'fix3_aic': Mat buffer usage (1064960 bytes) exceeds platform limit (524288 bytes)` | Two observations: 1. In `--fix 0` the gather's **source** offset already references `aiv_id`, which is what fix (2) asks for ("an op whose arguments reference `aiv_id` is per-lane by construction and is accepted"). It is still rejected — the check appears to consider only the destination/accumulator, not the source. 2. Fix (1) is not applicable to this shape at all: `aiv_shard` is specified for a **cube-produced** (`Acc`) value crossing C2V, but the accumulator here is vector-produced (`Vec`). The diagnostic itself redirects to fix (3), which then overflows L1. The net effect is that a per-lane scattered gather has no tensor-level spelling, and the only working formulation is a GM staging buffer with hand-written `set_ffts` + `sync_set`/`sync_wait`. ### Motivation / Use Case DeepSeek-V4-Flash CSA decode. `qk_pv` is 29.7% of the layer's machine core-time and 73% MTE2-occupied on the cube, gathering 128 scattered 1 KB KV rows per tile; its AIV lanes are ~7% occupied. Micro-benchmarks on 910B1 (same binary, disjoint index sets, ordering-controlled): | path | us for one 128x512 BF16 tile | |---|---| | cube, 128 x `gather_row` (today) | 20.90 | | AIV pair, UB accumulate + coalesced store | 3.26 | The GM-staging workaround lands ~4% end-to-end on the layer, but it costs a 4 MB scratch buffer, triples the bytes moved (scattered read + write + read), and needs the manual barrier. `aic_gather` returning a `Tensor` in `Mat` — verified: with a `Tensor` input it returns `pl.Tensor[[256, 512], pl.BF16]` — would remove the staging buffer, the extra traffic, and the barrier in one step. ### Proposed API / Behavior Preferred (this is fix (1) made applicable): let **`pl.aiv_shard` accept a vector-produced `Vec` operand**, sharding a locally-built UB tile into per-lane halves. Today it is restricted to `Acc` (cube-produced, C2V). Accepting `Vec` would let a `pl.full` accumulator be sharded and then filled by per-lane `gather_row` calls, with `aic_gather` carrying the assembled tile to the cube: ```python for aiv in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN): ub = pl.aiv_shard(pl.full([ROWS, HEAD_DIM], dtype=pl.BF16, value=0.0)) # -> [ROWS/2, HEAD_DIM] for k in pl.range(ROWS // 2): src = pl.cast(pl.read(idx, [aiv * (ROWS // 2) + k]), pl.INDEX) ub = pl.gather_row(ub, pool, [k, 0], [src, 0], [1, HEAD_DIM]) kv = pl.aic_gather(ub) # -> [ROWS, HEAD_DIM] in Mat out = pl.matmul(q, kv, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32) ``` Alternatives that would also unblock it: - **Honour fix (2) for DMA ops** — accept `tile.gather_row` as per-lane when *any* of its offsets (source included) references the region's lane index, not only the destination. - **Let `paged_gather` take a per-lane index range** — a sliced/sharded index tensor, or an explicit index-offset argument. Today `pl.paged_gather` is the only tensor-level op producing a UB `Tensor`, but it rejects a sliced index tensor (static *or* dynamic) with `indices must be TensorType`, rejects a `pl.aiv_shard` result with the same error, and rejects a `[2, n/2]` per-lane layout with `requires 2D indices to have shape [1, n], but got first dim 2`. Any one of these would make the `paged_gather` + `aic_gather` form work directly. ### Alternatives Considered - **GM staging + explicit barrier (what pypto-lib ships today).** The AIV lanes coalesce chunks into a GM scratch and the cube reloads them contiguously, ordered by `pl.system.set_ffts` + `sync_set(pipe=MTE3, core_type="aiv")` / `sync_wait(pipe=MTE2, core_type="aic")`. Correct and ~4% faster end-to-end, but needs a 4 MB scratch, triples bytes moved, and relies on the hand-written barrier that #1911 wants automated. Without the barrier the kernel passes 9/9 uninstrumented runs and fails 3/3 under `--enable-l2-swimlane 1` — a silent race, exactly the failure mode #1911 describes. - **Rewrite the qk_pv consumer chain at tile level.** `pl.tile.gather_row` accepts a `Vec` destination and arbitrary runtime offsets, so a `create_tile` + `tile.gather_row` + `aic_gather` chain works — but `aic_gather` then returns a `Tile`, and `pl.matmul` rejects mixed `Tensor`/`Tile` operands, so the whole QK/softmax/PV chain (~25 lines) has to move to tile level. Possible today; avoided because it makes the kernel materially harder to read for what should be an operand-plumbing detail. ### Additional Context Related: - #1911 — auto-fence AIV->AIC (V2C) GM read-after-write. The barrier this issue is trying to avoid needing is exactly the one #1911 proposes to automate; the shipped pypto-lib workaround is the "status quo" alternative listed there. - #2203 — `LowerAutoVectorSplit` halves a vector op's result without sharding its full-width operand. Same pass, adjacent defect family (that one is about elementwise ops with un-sharded operands; this one is about a DMA op being classified full-width). - #1820 — RFC for the explicit `pl.split_aiv` + `aiv_shard`/`aic_gather` DSL this issue exercises. - #2130 — `pl.pipeline` cannot generate skewed cross-core schedules without manual `sync_set`/`sync_wait`. Consistent with what was measured here: `pl.pipeline(stage=2)` over the staging chunks gave no overlap (349.8 vs 348.8 us) because the manual per-chunk handover already serialises the pair. - #2006 — `pl.split_aiv(2, SplitMode.NONE)` silently drops half the work. Measurements above are from 910B1, CANN 8.5.1, `--start-pos 8192`, `B=4 S=2 T=8`.

title: fix(ir): Admit a lane-localized tile.gather_row in a split_aiv region
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2244 — a per-lane scattered `pl.gather_row` had no tensor-level spelling inside `pl.split_aiv`, forcing a GM staging buffer plus a hand-written `pl.system.set_ffts` + `sync_set`/`sync_wait` barrier.

Two independent causes, one of them a genuine defect:

**1. `AddressArgs` did not know `tile.gather_row` (the blocker).**

`ValidateMixedExplicitRegion` admits a vector op into the per-lane half-width dataflow when its *address* args reference the region's `aiv_id`. The table in `LowerAutoVectorSplit` listed only `tile.load` / `tile.slice` / `tile.extract`, so a gather's address was never consulted and the op was always reported full-width. The pass's own suggested fix — *"localize it yourself with the region's lane index … an op whose arguments reference `aiv_id` is per-lane by construction and is accepted"* — was therefore **unreachable** for the only op that reads GM at an arbitrary runtime offset.

Added, keyed on `src_offset` (arg 3) **only**. `tile.gather_row` is DPS and carries two offsets, but just the READ window decides whether the lanes do different work:

| shape | meaning | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lane-derived `src_offset` | each lane pulls its own scattered rows | admitted |
| lane-derived `dst_offset`, lane-invariant `src_offset` | both lanes fetch the *same* rows into different slots of a full-width accumulator | still reported |

**2. The unblocked kernel then overflows L1 on the cross-core pipe ring.**

The ring is a `system.reserve_buffer`, not a MemRef — tiles are allocated *above* it, so it is counted in the high-water mark yet invisible in the per-tile accounting an author can inspect. A `[128, 512]` BF16 tile crossing V2C reserves `131072 x 8 = 1 MB` of a 512 KB L1, and the diagnostic was a bare byte count that said nothing about where the bytes went:

```
Function 'qk_pv_aic': Mat buffer usage (1064960 bytes) exceeds platform limit (524288 bytes)
```

Now:

```
… exceeds platform limit (524288 bytes). 1048576 of those bytes are reserved by
system.reserve_buffer, not by tiles — this function's cross-core pipe ring. Lower its
depth with optimizations=[pl.cross_core_slot(slot_num=N)] on the enclosing pl.at(...),
or shrink the tile that crosses the cube/vector boundary
```

The `pl.cross_core_slot` remediation is appended **only** when the buffer really is one of the pipe rings, so a hand-authored `pl.reserve_buffer` gets its bytes attributed but is not pointed at a knob that cannot shrink it. The figure is read from the same `ResolveReserveBufferBases` result the allocator used as its floor (rather than an independent re-sum), and is resolved lazily so a green build pays nothing.

## Result

The natural spelling now lowers end-to-end:

```python
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="sparse_kv", allow_early_resolve=True,
           optimizations=[pl.cross_core_slot(slot_num=2)]):
    for aiv in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN):
        ub = pl.full([64, 512], dtype=pl.BF16, value=0.0)       # per-lane HALF extent
        for k in pl.range(64):
            src = pl.cast(pl.read(idx, [aiv * 64 + k]), pl.INDEX)
            ub = pl.gather_row(ub, pool, [k, 0], [src, 0], [1, 512])
        kv = pl.aic_gather(ub)                                  # V2C -> [128, 512] in Mat
    out[0:16, 0:128] = pl.matmul(q, kv, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
```

Each AIV lane gathers its own 64 scattered rows into UB and pushes its half; the cube pops the reassembled `[128, 512]` L1 tile. No GM staging buffer, no manual barrier.

## Notes on what was *not* changed

- **`pl.aiv_shard` still rejects a `Vec` operand.** The issue's preferred API asks to relax this, but `tile.aiv_shard` *is* the C→V cross-core transfer (it folds into `tpush_to_aiv`/`tpop_from_aic`), and `Acc` is the only space the c2v pipe can push. A `pl.full` accumulator never crosses that pipe, so there is nothing to shard across it — and writing the accumulator at the half extent expresses the same thing with no new IR.
- **Ring depth is not auto-capped to fit.** Depth is the cross-core pipelining depth, so silently shrinking it would turn a loud compile error into a quiet throughput regression.
- **`paged_gather` with a sliced/sharded index range** (the issue's third alternative) stays open as a separate convenience item; it is not needed to unblock this kernel.

## Testing

- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_lower_auto_vector_split.py` — `test_region_admits_lane_localized_gather_row`, `..._nested_in_loop` (the real shape: gather inside a `pl.range`, so the lane-scalar set must survive the scan's loop recursion), and `test_region_rejects_gather_row_localized_only_on_dst` (pins `AddressArgs` to `src_offset` alone).
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_allocate_memory_addr_pass.py` — attribution fires with the right bytes and knob; omitted for a hand-authored buffer; omitted for an unrelated memory space.
- `tests/st/codegen/dsl/test_split_aiv_gather_row_codegen.py` (new) — the kernel lowers to the expected AIV/AIC split, compiles through PTO codegen to a `.pto`, and without `cross_core_slot` produces the attributed overflow message.
- Full `tests/ut`: 8464 passed, 2 skipped. One pre-existing unrelated failure (`test_ir_trace.py::test_installed_console_script_preserves_main_exit_codes`) reproduces identically on a clean tree.
- clang-format, clang-tidy, cpplint, ruff, pyright, markdownlint, docs EN/ZH parity: all pass.

## Documentation

- `docs/{en,zh}/dev/passes/19-lower_auto_vector_split.md` — address-arg acceptance table extended; new "Per-lane scattered gather" section covering the two authoring rules (half-extent accumulator, ring sizing).
- `docs/{en,zh}/dev/passes/32-allocate_memory_addr.md` — new "Capacity verification" section documenting the high-water check and the reserve-buffer attribution.

## Related Issues

Fixes #2244

title: fix(distributed): close window-aliasing gap and O(N²) pass complexity in HOST collectives
body:
## Summary

A review of the distributed collectives stack (allreduce, barrier, broadcast, reduce_scatter, allgather, all_to_all, and — after the rebase onto #2243 — all_to_all_v) surfaced one real correctness gap and one real complexity-budget violation, both silent today. This PR fixes both.

### 1. Window aliasing was unchecked for most HOST collectives — a real silent-corruption risk

Before this PR, `LowerHostTensorCollectives`'s `CheckDistinctInputTargetWindows` was wired into only 2 of 6 collectives (`allgather`, `all_to_all`), and even there it only checked `input` vs `target` — never vs `signal`. `allreduce`, `barrier`, `broadcast`, `reduce_scatter` had **no aliasing check at all**.

Concretely: nothing stopped a user from writing

```python
pld.tensor.allreduce(data, signal, op=pld.ReduceOp.Sum)
```

where `data` and `signal` are two different `pld.window()` views over the **same** `alloc_window_buffer`. That's a real cross-process race — the reduce's data write and the barrier's notify/wait control write land in the same memory — and it would compile cleanly and fail silently or corrupt data at runtime instead of raising a clear compile-time error.

**Fix**: `HostCollectiveRule::scope_buffers` already enumerates every window operand for every op (it existed to resolve the enclosing `CommDomainScopeStmt`) — this PR reuses that same list to run a new, generic `CheckPairwiseDistinctWindows` helper once, in `LowerCollective`, covering all 7 HOST collectives uniformly. One shared helper instead of one-off per-op checks that get missed. Rebased onto #2243, this also replaces #2243's bespoke `CheckAllToAllVDistinctWindows` with the same generic path — all 10 operand pairs of `all_to_all_v` (input/target/signal/send_counts/recv_counts) are now checked by the shared helper. The plain/unbound-tensor guard is folded into the same generic path: `HostCollectiveRule::host_bound_args` lists the args whose public deducer accepts a plain `Tensor` (allgather/all_to_all `input`, all_to_all_v `input` + `send_counts`), checked with `CHECK_SPAN` before window lookup — so a plain `Tensor` on the HOST path is a user error, not an internal one.

### 2. O(N²) pass complexity — a direct violation of this repo's own `pass-complexity.md`

`MaterializeCommDomainScopes`'s domain-clustering phase did a **linear scan of the `pending` domains list per allocation** to find a matching descriptor. For a program with many independently-scoped comm domains, this is O(allocations × domains) = O(N²).

**Fix**: `DeviceDescriptor` already has `operator<`, so this PR adds a `std::map<DeviceDescriptor, size_t>` index alongside `pending`, turning the lookup into O(log domains) — squarely within the project's own "ordered map/set lookups are fine" complexity allowance. No behavior change; a new 3-domain regression test pins the clustering order and exercises the map hit at a nonzero index. `DeviceDescriptor::operator<` is aligned with `operator==` for all-device descriptors (`subset` is meaningless when `is_all`), which the map makes load-bearing.

### 3. `broadcast`'s `root` was never bounds-checked against the device count

Only `root >= 0` was validated. `root=100` on a 4-rank job compiled cleanly and would fail at runtime as an out-of-bounds remote read. This PR adds a `root < participating_devices` check on the explicit static-device-subset domain (mirroring the existing signal-capacity check's scope — the fully-dynamic "all device" domain is left as a documented limitation, same as the existing signal-capacity gap there, since there's no compile-time device count to check against in that case).

## Signal / mode validation: superseded by main's lowering passes

The original version of this PR also unified signal-shape validation into the public deducers (a `CheckSignalDistributedTensor` helper called from every public op). Since then, main moved signal and `mode` validation into the lowering passes — `LowerHostTensorCollectives::IsRingAllReduce` (HOST) and `LowerCompositeOps` (InCore) — which enforce the same contract at lowering time for every collective. This PR was rebased onto that architecture and no longer duplicates the checks in the deducers.

## What's intentionally *not* in this PR

Several other findings were evaluated and deliberately deferred — a `CollectiveOpBuilder` abstraction (premature without an 8th collective) and a runtime-assert IR primitive for the dynamic-domain gaps mentioned above (real gap, but new IR/runtime infra, out of scope here). Happy to open tracking issues for these if useful.

## Test plan

- Window-aliasing rejection for all 7 HOST collectives via the generic pairwise path (data-vs-data, data-vs-signal, and control-vs-control pairs), plain-tensor HOST-input rejection for allgather/all_to_all/all_to_all_v, broadcast `root`-out-of-range rejection, and a 3-domain clustering regression for the complexity fix.
- Host-lowering signal success-path tests (rank-1 signals through the builtin validators).
- Agent gate `host_collectives_ut_sim` (sim Docker): the full `test_lower_host_tensor_collectives.py` + `test_materialize_comm_domain_scopes.py` + `test_host_orch_distributed.py` + `test_lower_composite_ops.py` suite — 258 tests pass.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`, `clang-format --dry-run --Werror`, and the repo lint scripts (en/zh parity, headers, English-only, no-broad-raises) clean on all touched files.

title: feat(verifier): register RuntimeScopesMaterialized property verifier
body:
## Summary

Orchestration codegen emits `PTO2_SCOPE()` **only** from explicit `RuntimeScopeStmt` nodes inserted by `MaterializeRuntimeScopes` — it no longer wraps `for`/`if` bodies implicitly. The compiler already listed `IRProperty::RuntimeScopesMaterialized` on the orchestration codegen precondition path, but **no `PropertyVerifier` was registered**, so `VerifyProperties` silently skipped the check.

This PR closes that gap by:

1. Registering a `RuntimeScopesMaterialized` property verifier (checks `auto_scope == false` on all `FunctionType::Orchestration` functions in the program).
2. Adding the property to `GetVerifiedProperties()` so `PassPipeline` auto-verifies it after `MaterializeRuntimeScopes`.
3. Hardening `VerifyOrchestrationCodegenPreconditions` to reject **stale `Function` handles** — the `func` passed to `generate_orchestration` must be the instance currently stored in `program` after transform passes.
4. Adding negative-path unit tests, updating hand-built codegen test helpers, and updating verifier / pass-42 documentation (EN + zh-CN).

No change to orchestration codegen emission logic or to `MaterializeRuntimeScopes` pass behavior — verification and precondition wiring only.

## Motivation

Orchestration codegen is a **printer**, not a smart wrapper. If scopes were never materialized in IR, codegen used to run anyway and could produce wrong or missing `PTO2_SCOPE()` regions — failures show up as overlap-map bugs, wrong task dependencies, or device hangs rather than a clean compile-time error.

**Minimal failing example (before this PR):** an orchestration function with a `for` loop and `pl.submit` inside, run through `convert_to_ssa` + `derive_call_directions` but **without** `materialize_runtime_scopes`, then passed to `generate_orchestration`. The function still has `auto_scope=True` and no `RuntimeScopeStmt` nodes; codegen omits scopes silently.

**After this PR:** compile-time error directing the author to run `MaterializeRuntimeScopes`.

A second hole found during review: program-level verification could pass while codegen emitted a **stale `Function` pointer** left over from before `MaterializeRuntimeScopes` replaced the function node. Codegen entry now rejects that mismatch.

### Invariant (v1)

For every orchestration function `f`:

- `Materialized(f)` ⟺ `f.GetAttr("auto_scope", default=true) == false`
- Satisfied when pass 42 ran (default path) or the user declared `@pl.function(auto_scope=False)`

We use the `auto_scope` marker (same idempotency flag the pass sets) rather than a structural `RuntimeScopeStmt` tree walk in v1, to avoid false positives on user opt-out with zero hand-placed scopes.

## What changed

### C++

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/ir/verifier/verify_runtime_scopes_materialized.cpp` | **New** — property verifier |
| `include/pypto/ir/verifier/verifier.h` | Factory declaration + Doxygen |
| `src/ir/verifier/property_verifier_registry.cpp` | Register verifier |
| `src/ir/transforms/ir_property.cpp` | Add to `GetVerifiedProperties()` |
| `src/codegen/codegen_preconditions.cpp` | Reject stale `func` handle vs `program`; `CHECK_SPAN` for missing-function API contract |
| `CMakeLists.txt` | Build new source file |

### Tests

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `tests/ut/codegen/test_verify_runtime_scopes_materialized.py` | **New** — verifier + codegen precondition + stale-handle cases |
| `tests/ut/codegen/test_codegen_preconditions.py` | Smoke test runs `materialize_runtime_scopes` before codegen |
| `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_pass_pipeline.py` | `GetVerifiedProperties()` regression assertion |
| `tests/ut/codegen/_orchestration_codegen_common.py` | `_finalize_handbuilt_for_codegen`, `_orch_func_from_program` |
| `tests/ut/codegen/test_array_codegen.py` | Hand-built IR runs MRS before codegen |
| `tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_misc.py` | Re-fetch orch func after finalize |
| `tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_codegen_more.py` | Re-fetch orch func after finalize |
| `tests/ut/ir/operators/test_mx_scale_memspace.py` | MX precondition test runs MRS before codegen |
| `tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_host_orch_distributed.py` | Host collective next-level tests run MRS before `pto_backend.generate` |

**Test matrix:**

1. **Registry rejection** — `PropertyVerifierRegistry.verify_or_throw` fails when MRS skipped.
2. **Codegen precondition rejection** — `generate_orchestration` fails (not silent).
3. **Stale handle rejection** — finalized `program` + pre-finalize `func` pointer rejected.
4. **Positive path** — full finalize chain passes verifier.
5. **User opt-out** — `@pl.function(auto_scope=False)` passes without running MRS.
6. **`GetVerifiedProperties()`** — property present in pipeline auto-verify set.

### Docs

- `docs/en/dev/passes/99-verifier.md` — built-in rule row + `GetVerifiedProperties()` set
- `docs/zh/dev/passes/99-verifier.md` — parity
- `docs/en/dev/passes/42-materialize_runtime_scopes.md` — verifier cross-link
- `docs/zh/dev/passes/42-materialize_runtime_scopes.md` — parity

## Verification surfaces (after merge)

| Surface | Behavior |
|---------|----------|
| `PropertyVerifierRegistry` | Verifier runs on demand |
| `VerifyOrchestrationCodegenPreconditions` | Program properties enforced; `func` must match `program` instance |
| `PassPipeline` post-pass verify | Auto-check after `MaterializeRuntimeScopes` (deduped if re-produced later) |

title: fix(ir): Derive tile.move's result fractal from the destination space
body:
## Summary

`DeduceTileMoveType` copied `blayout`/`slayout` from the source tile's effective view but left `fractal` at the `TileView` default (512). For an `Acc` (L0C) destination — whose implicit fractal is 1024 — the deduced view matched neither the implicit view for no-space nor the one for `Acc`, so `CanonicalizeTileViewInPlace` could not collapse it to `nullopt` even after `OpRegistry::Create` stamps `memory_space` onto the type.

That made a pass-synthesized move self-inconsistent. `MemoryReuse`'s YieldFixup types the assigned `Var` by cloning the source (view absent) while the `Call` carried the explicit wrong-fractal view:

```text
after MemoryReuse : acc_mv  VAR tile_view=None   CALL tile_view=SET(fractal=512)
after print->parse: acc_mv  VAR tile_view=SET    CALL tile_view=SET(fractal=512)

RuntimeError: [RoundtripInstrument] Structural equality failed after pass 'MemoryReuse'.
  Error: Structural equality assertion failed at: ['main'].body[8].else_body[1].var
  Reason: TileType tile_view presence mismatch
```

The printer emits only the Var's annotation, and the parser refills the view from the Call (`ast_parser.py`: `merged_tv = ann_tv if ann_tv is not None else inf_tv`), so the program failed the print→parse roundtrip after `MemoryReuse`.

## Fix

`fractal` describes how the *destination* buffer is boxed, not a property carried from the source, so it is now seeded from the destination space via a new `tile_view_semantics::GetImplicitFractal` helper. `GetImplicitTileView` delegates to the same helper so the two cannot drift, which also lets the duplicated `fractal = 32` literals in the scale branches go.

Behavior across all source→destination pairs:

| destination | before | after |
| ----------- | ------ | ----- |
| `Vec`, `Mat`, `Left`, `Right` | 512 | 512 (unchanged) |
| `LeftScale` / `RightScale` | 32 | 32 (unchanged, now via the helper) |
| `Acc` | 512 (wrong) | 1024 |

`Acc→Vec` is unchanged at 512 — the cube→vec pipe un-fractalizes during transfer. `Vec→Acc` and `Right→Acc` now report 1024 instead of a wrong 512; their views were already explicit for other reasons, so only the number changed.

The fix is deliberately in the op's type deduction rather than in `MemoryReuse::CreateTileMove`. Typing the LHS Var from the op's deduction alone would have made both sides agree on `fractal=512` for an Acc tile, which breaks the same-address elision in `pto_ops_elementwise.cpp` (it compares `src_view.fractal == dst_view.fractal`, and the elision exists for #1310) and feeds a wrong fractal into the emitted tile-buffer type string via `pto_type_utils.cpp`.

## Testing

- [x] All tests pass — `tests/ut/`: 8552 passed, 2 skipped; `tests/st/codegen`: 42 passed
- [x] Code review completed
- [x] clang-tidy clean on the changed TU and header
- [x] Documentation updated (`docs/en` + `docs/zh`)

New coverage:

- `TestTileMoveOp` in `tests/ut/ir/operators/test_tile_ops.py` — parametrized over Vec/Mat/Acc pinning the destination fractal and that a same-space move's view is stored canonically as `None`, plus the `Acc→Vec` case.
- `test_synthesized_acc_move_var_and_call_agree_on_tile_view` in `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_memory_reuse.py` — pins the underlying invariant so a regression names the actual defect instead of surfacing as an opaque roundtrip diff.

This also **removes two `PassContext([], VerificationLevel.NONE)` bypasses** in `TestTopDownRetargeter` that existed only to hide this roundtrip failure; those tests now run under full verification. The divergent-Acc-phi program they shared with the new test is extracted into `_divergent_acc_phi_program()`.

title: fix(ir): Carry the SPMD launch spec on the dispatch, not the callee
body:
## Summary

A `pl.spmd` block count is an expression evaluated in the **dispatching** function's scope, but scope outlining stored it on the outlined **callee**'s `attrs_` as `attrs={"core_num": <ExprPtr>}`. A `Function` is a closed scope, so this made the callee reference Vars it does not bind.

Two consequences followed from that one carrier choice:

- **Print → parse was broken.** Function attrs print as a Python decorator, which is evaluated at class-body time — before any function body binds the name. Any program with a dynamic `pl.spmd` count failed the roundtrip instrument from `OutlineClusterScopes` onward (37 of 46 passes), with `NameError: name 'm__ssa_v0' is not defined`.
- **The use was invisible to per-function analyses.** The visitor and mutator walk one function at a time, so a scalar consumed only by a launch width looked dead — which is why `Simplify` carried a program-wide `CollectCoreNumReferencedVars` shield.

This moves the spec to the launch site, where its Vars are actually in scope:

| Dispatch shape | Carrier |
| -------------- | ------- |
| plain `Call` (`with pl.spmd(...)`) | `attrs["core_num"]` (`ExprPtr`) + `attrs["sync_start"]` (`bool`, only when true) |
| `Submit` (`with pl.spmd(...) as tid`) | first-class `Submit::core_num_` / `sync_start_` |
| `Group` from `pl.cluster(): with pl.spmd(...)` | the dispatch, same as above |

```python
# before — free variable in the callee's decorator
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Spmd, attrs={"core_num": m__ssa_v0 // 16})
def hc_spmd(...): ...
    out = self.hc_spmd(a, b, out)

# after — in scope at the call site
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Spmd)
def hc_spmd(...): ...
    out = self.hc_spmd(a, b, out, attrs={"core_num": m__ssa_v0 // 16})
```

No printer or parser change was needed: the generic Call-attr codec already round-trips an `ExprPtr`, and orchestration codegen's `EffectiveLaunchSpec` already preferred the dispatch's own attrs.

The `pl.cluster()`-nested case needs one extra step — its spec is lifted from *inside* an already-outlined Group, where the count references a Group **param**, so `LaunchSpecStamper` maps `params_[i] → args_[i]` back through the dispatch. The Group keeps a self-contained `spmd_unwrapped` bool so the occupancy verifier can still distinguish a launch wrapper from a mixed-kernel Group.

## Supporting changes

- **`IsExprValuedCallAttr`** — one definition of which Call attrs hold an `ExprPtr`, consumed by the visitor, mutator and SSA pass. These were three hand-maintained key lists that had already drifted (`convert_to_ssa_pass.cpp` knew only `device`).
- **Occupancy verifier** — memoizes its per-function callee walk. The spec is now read once per launch *site* rather than once per *function*, which without a cache is the nested-scan shape `pass-complexity.md` forbids. Also adds a launch-site check so scope-based `pl.spmd` is still verified.
- **Removals** — `CollectCoreNumReferencedVars` and the now-unused `protected_vars` overload of `EliminateDeadScalarAssignments`; the use is local and ordinary once the spec rides the dispatch.

## Testing

- [x] Full suite: 8551 passed, 2 skipped
- [x] New regression tests for both paths: the outlined function carries no `core_num`, the dispatch does, the cluster-nested spec is translated into caller Var space, and both programs survive print → parse
- [x] Verified end-to-end that `NameError` is gone across all 46 passes
- [x] clang-tidy clean on changed files
- [x] Docs updated (en + zh)

## Note

The function-level `core_num` read paths in `EffectiveLaunchSpec` and the occupancy verifier are kept for hand-written / deserialized IR, but no pass produces them any more. A follow-up could delete them and add a verifier rule rejecting `core_num` on a `Function`, which would close the remaining way to construct the invalid state.

title: refactor(parser): Remove the deprecated pl.Tensor[..., pl.DN] shorthand
body:
## Summary

**BREAKING CHANGE:** the DN layout-only shorthand on a tensor type annotation now raises `ParserTypeError` instead of emitting a `DeprecationWarning`.

```python
b: pl.Tensor[[K, N], pl.FP32, pl.DN]   # was: DeprecationWarning -> now: ParserTypeError
```

Writing `pl.Tensor[..., pl.DN]` forces the reader to hold two coordinate systems at once (IR-logical post-view shape vs. runtime row-major shape) — exactly the ambiguity RFC #1300 supplementary 1 set out to remove. The shorthand was deprecated for that reason; this removes it.

- `_warn_on_user_facing_dn_layout` -> `_reject_user_facing_dn_layout` in `python/pypto/language/parser/type_resolver.py`. The error carries a span and quotes the annotation's **source spelling**, so a layout passed through a variable (`MY = ir.TensorLayout.DN; pl.Tensor[..., MY]`) reports `MY` rather than a `pl.DN` the user never wrote.
- The hint lists the three migration patterns: drop the marker and write the runtime shape, derive DN at the use site via `pl.transpose`, or inherit it through a slice/reshape of a DN-producing op.
- Drops the now-unused `warnings` import.

## Scope — what is *not* affected

`TensorLayout.DN`, the `pl.DN` constant, and `pl.TensorView(stride=..., layout=DN)` all stay valid. Only the bare layout marker in slot 3 of a `Tensor` / `DistributedTensor` annotation is rejected — the explicit view carries its own stride and so has no implicit coordinate flip.

Print/reparse round-trip is unaffected: `IRPythonPrinter::PrintTensorView` only ever emits the full `pl.TensorView(stride=..., layout=...)` form, never the bare shorthand.

No production use of the shorthand remained in this repo or in `pypto-lib`.

## Testing

- [x] `tests/ut` full suite: 8426 passed, 2 skipped
- [x] `tests/ut/language/parser/test_type_resolver.py`: rewrote the two `pytest.warns` cases as `pytest.raises`; added coverage for the variable-held DN layout and a positive case locking in that `pl.TensorView(stride=..., layout=DN)` still resolves
- [x] ruff check / ruff format / pyright clean
- [x] Code review completed
- [x] Documentation updated — `docs/en|zh/user/01-language_guide.md` (Deprecated -> Rejected) and `docs/en|zh/dev/passes/28-materialize_tensor_strides.md` (example prose no longer refers to the removed spelling)

title: fix(ir): Restore the print→parse roundtrip for a loop-carry init parameter
body:
## Summary

`tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_declared_memref.py::TestSlots::test_runtime_slot_index_reaches_the_address`
is currently **red on `main`** (e.g. CI run `30776101637` on `a20e884f`: `1 failed, 8499 passed`), so every
PR branched off it inherits the failure through the merge-commit CI.

The test itself is fine. It runs the pass pipeline under the autouse `RoundtripInstrument`
(print → parse → structural compare after each pass), and its program — a `pl.range` loop whose
`init_values` is a `pl.Tile` parameter — makes `InitMemRef` place that parameter in a
compiler-allocated buffer. Two separate defects made the resulting IR unprintable. #2238 removed
the `VerificationLevel.NONE` bypass that had been hiding both.

### 1. A signature MemRef base printed as an unbound forward reference

`IRPythonPrinter::PrintMemRef` chose between a bare variable reference and a quoted string by asking
only whether the base `Ptr` is defined in the function body — never *where* the MemRef was being
printed. A parameter annotation is emitted before the body binds any name, so the base allocated by
the body printed as a forward reference:

```python
def main(self, ..., seed__ssa_v0: pl.Tile[..., pl.MemRef(mem_ddr_1, ...), pl.Mem.DDR], ...):
    mem_ddr_1: pl.Ptr = pl.tensor.alloc(pl.Mem.DDR, 16384)   # bound only here
```

```
NameError: name 'mem_ddr_1' is not defined
```

The comment above the branch already documented the intended behaviour ("forward references in
parameter annotations ... use a string literal"); the implementation just did not honour it. A
`printing_signature_` flag now forces the string form across the parameter list and return types,
leaving body annotations — where the base *is* in scope — on the bare-name form.

### 2. A cross-memory-space retarget left the bound Call's type stale

With the printer fixed the test advanced one pass and failed structural equality after
`MaterializeSemanticAliases`:

```
at ['main'].body[3].body[1].value.type   →   TileType memory_space mismatch
```

A retarget rewrites the LHS `Var`'s type but leaves the RHS `Call`'s type as the op inferred it.
That is harmless while the retarget stays inside one memory space (only the MemRef base moves, and a
`Call` type carries no MemRef) — which is why this went unnoticed. The pass already declines
cross-space retargets for ops encoding output memory in a `target_memory` kwarg (`tile.create` /
`move` / `load`), but `tile.add` has no such kwarg, so the Vec compute result gets folded onto the
DDR loop-carry buffer:

| | `var.type` | `value.type` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | `MemRef("mem_ddr_1"), Mem.DDR` | `Mem.Vec` ← stale |
| after | `MemRef("mem_ddr_1"), Mem.DDR` | `Mem.DDR` |

That pair cannot be spelled in the DSL: the printer emits one annotation (the `Var`'s) and the parser
then retypes the `Call` to match it (`ast_parser` `override_type`), so the roundtrip necessarily
compared unequal. The memory space is now carried onto the `Call`; the MemRef stays `Var`-only,
matching what `structural_equal` and the parser's `_types_match` already assume.

## Testing

- [x] `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_declared_memref.py` — **51 passed** (was 1 failed / 48 passed)
- [x] Full unit suite from the worktree build: **8551 passed, 2 skipped**. The one remaining
      failure, `tests/ut/tools/test_ir_trace.py::test_installed_console_script_preserves_main_exit_codes`,
      asserts a pip-installed `pypto-ir-trace` console script that this source-tree run has no
      way to provide; CI installs the package, so it passes there.
- [x] `cmake --build build --parallel` clean, zero warnings
- [x] clang-tidy on the changed C++ (project `tests/lint/clang_tidy.py --diff-base=origin/main`): clean
- [x] clang-format / cpplint / ruff on every changed file: clean
- [x] `tests/lint/` scripts (headers, English-only, EN↔ZH parity, doc nav, no-broad-raises): all pass

New `TestLoopCarryRoundtrip` covers both defects directly rather than leaving them guarded only
incidentally by the slots test: one asserts the parameter annotation quotes a body-allocated base
and the printed program reparses, the other asserts the retargeted binding's `Call` and `Var` agree
on memory space.

title: docs(ir): Document TileView::fractal as a byte size
body:
## Summary

`TileView::fractal` is a **byte** count, but `batch_matmul.cpp` documented it as an element count — "`fractal=1024`: 32x32 sub-tile fractal size". The two readings disagree: 1024 bytes of FP32 is a **16x16** box (`1024 / 4 / 16 = 16`), not 32x32.

The authoritative consumer divides by the element width to recover the geometry:

```cpp
// src/backend/common/pto_ops_datamove.cpp
// NZ fractal granularity: M0 = 16 rows; the C0 lane count along columns is
// fractal_bytes / dtype_bytes / M0 (both collapse to 16 for fp16/bf16).
box_cols = view_info.fractal / dtype_bytes / kNZFractalRows;
```

`docs/en/dev/passes/10-convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.md` likewise names the field `fractal_bytes`. The declaration itself said only "Fractal size" with no unit, so neither reading was anchored — a reader taking the matmul comment at face value computes the wrong box geometry.

## Changes

Comments and docstrings only — no behavior change.

- **`include/pypto/ir/type.h`** — state the unit on the field and on both `TileView` constructor `@param` docs, plus a note deriving the box geometry, the two matmul-path values (`512` Mat/Left/Right operand, `1024` Acc accumulator — both 16x16 boxes), and the MX scale value (`32`, where the 1-byte scale dtype makes bytes and elements coincide).
- **`src/ir/op/tile_ops/matmul.cpp` / `batch_matmul.cpp`** — replace the "32x32 sub-tile" reading with the byte reading; the accumulator is 4-byte (FP32/INT32).
- **`python/bindings/modules/ir.cpp`, `python/pypto/pypto_core/ir.pyi`, `python/pypto/ir/builder.py`** — carry the unit across all three layers per `cross-layer-sync.md`.
- **`docs/{en,zh}/dev/codegen/00-pto_codegen.md`** — fix the same unit-less wording.

## Testing

- [x] Full build clean (`cmake --build build`, 211/211)
- [x] `tests/ut/ir/core` + `tests/ut/ir/operators` — 1214 passed, 1 skipped
- [x] clang-tidy on the diff — clean
- [x] All 15 pre-commit hooks pass (clang-format, cpplint, ruff, pyright, markdownlint, en/zh doc parity)

title: [Feature] Allow pl.MemRef on reshape-derived intermediate tiles (row-vector softmax terms)
body:
## Background In pypto-lib, tuning `models/qwen3/14b/bench_attention_swpipe_best_performance.py` (decode attention) on `a2a3`, we use `pl.MemRef("name")` declared allocations to break false WAR dependencies that MemoryReuse introduces by folding independent tiles onto one buffer (this is the intended use of #2171, and it wins ~2.3% on the cube-side K/V loads). We then tried to apply the same fix on the **vector** side — pinning the online-softmax intermediates (`d = exp(m - hm)`, a `[16,1]` decay column vector) so MTE2's next score load stops waiting on the vector reading the current one. This is rejected at trace time. Reproduce with: python repro_memref_intermediate.py -p a2a3sim The repro case is **not committed** — save the file below and run it.
Reproduction case — repro_memref_intermediate.py ```python """Minimal repro: pl.MemRef on a reshape-derived intermediate tile is rejected. The online-softmax decay d = exp(m - hm) is a [N,1] column vector; sub reshapes its operands, so exp(...) lands in its source tile's allocation and cannot be given its own buffer — even though pinning it is exactly how you'd break a false WAR that serialises the vector pipe.""" import pypto.language as pl import torch from golden import TensorSpec, run_jit N, K = 16, 128 @pl.jit def probe(x: pl.Tensor[[N, K], pl.FP32], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N, K], pl.FP32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[N, K], pl.FP32]: for _t in pl.spmd(1, name_hint="probe"): tmp = pl.create_tile([N, K], dtype=pl.FP32, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec) xt = pl.load(x, [0, 0], [N, K], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec) m = pl.row_max(xt, tmp) lm = pl.row_max(pl.tile.muls(xt, 0.5), tmp) hm = pl.maximum(lm, m) # We want d in its OWN Vec buffer to break the WAR against the next score # load. But exp(sub(...)) inherits its source (reshape) allocation: d: pl.Tile[[N, 1], pl.FP32, pl.MemRef("d_buf"), pl.Mem.Vec] = pl.exp(pl.sub(m, hm)) p = pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(xt, hm)) out = pl.store(pl.row_expand_mul(p, d), [0, 0], out) return out def main(): specs=[TensorSpec("x",[N,K],torch.float32,init_value=lambda:torch.randn([N,K])), TensorSpec("out",[N,K],torch.float32,is_output=True)] r=run_jit(fn=probe, specs=specs, golden_fn=None, runtime_cfg={"platform":"a2a3sim","device_id":0}, compile_only=True) print("passed=",r.passed) if __name__=="__main__": main() ```
Fails at trace time with: ``` ValueError: Tile 'd__ssa_v0' is produced by 'tile.reshape', which lands in its source tile's allocation, so it cannot be given one of its own. Bind the source tile instead. [repro_memref_intermediate.py:25:8] ``` Reproduction environment: | Component | Version | |---|---| | pypto-lib | `fd91568` (branch: main) | | pypto | `06fdbfc3` (branch: main) | | simpler | `9922afdb` | | ptoas | 0.54 | | pto-isa | `83d01313` | | CANN | not detected | Diagnosis: **pypto** — the `pl.MemRef` allocation binding (InitMemRef / MemoryReuse) refuses reshape-derived tiles. Related: pypto#2131, pypto#1475 (same family — false-dependency buffer folding), but distinct: this is a specific applicability gap in the #2171 `pl.MemRef` feature. ### Summary `pl.MemRef("name")` cannot be attached to a tile that is produced by a `tile.reshape` (i.e. any row/column-vector result of `sub` / `row_expand_*` / an `exp` fed by them). The error says "Bind the source tile instead", but the source is an anonymous reshape with no DSL-level name to annotate, so the guidance is not actionable. This blocks using `pl.MemRef` to break false WAR dependencies among the online-softmax column-vector intermediates (`lm`, `hm`, `d`, `m`, `l`) — exactly the terms whose buffer folding serialises the vector pipe. ### Motivation / Use Case `pl.MemRef` (#2171) is the sanctioned way to break MemoryReuse's false WAR folds. It works for full-width tiles produced by `load` / `exp(row_expand_sub(...))`, and gives real wins (cube-side K/V double-buffering, ~2.3% on qwen3-14b decode attn). But the online-softmax recurrence is dominated by `[N,1]` column-vector terms that are all reshape-derived, and those are precisely the ones MemoryReuse coalesces (one vec buffer held 22–26 tiles in our kernel). Being unable to pin them leaves a class of false vector-pipe dependencies with no user-level escape hatch, so the `pl.MemRef` win stops at the cube side. ### Proposed API / Behavior Allow `pl.MemRef` on a reshape-derived tile by giving the reshape *view* its own declared allocation (the reshape is a no-copy view; the request is to place the underlying storage in the named slot). If that is infeasible, at minimum make the diagnostic actionable: name the concrete source tile the user must bind, or accept the annotation on the reshape result and propagate it to the source alloc. ### Alternatives Considered - Binding the source: the "source" is an unnamed `pl.sub(...)` / `pl.reshape(...)` intermediate with no DSL variable to annotate. - Pinning only the full-width tiles we *can* pin (score, prob): verified — removes some V→MTE2 WAR flags (8→5) but not the column-vector folds, and does not move wall time in our case (those WARs happen to be masked by the cross-core QK_READY wait). The column-vector terms remain unaddressable.

title: [Feature] Allow pl.prefetch.async_prefetch to prefetch a sub-region (offset + size), not only a whole tensor
body:
### Summary

`pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(src, ctx)` can only prefetch a **whole** tensor: the IR
verifier requires `src` to be a `Var`/`IterArg` with a fully static shape that is
logically 1D (every dimension except the last must be 1), and codegen always emits a
`pto.partition_view` covering the entire tensor.

Please allow prefetching a **sub-region** — a base offset plus a length — so a caller
can warm only the slab it is about to consume.

### Motivation / Use Case

Trying `pl.prefetch` on the Qwen3-14B decode kernel (`models/qwen3/14b/decode_fwd.py`
in pypto-lib) showed the whole-tensor restriction makes the op inapplicable to the one
case it seems designed for — hiding weight-load latency behind unrelated compute.

**1. The region we want to warm is a slice, and slices are rejected.**
In the fused multi-layer decode, weights are stacked across layers: `wq` is
`[NUM_LAYERS * HIDDEN, HIDDEN]` = `[204800, 5120]` BF16 ≈ 2 GB, and layer `L` reads only
the row slab `wq[L*HIDDEN : (L+1)*HIDDEN, :]` (≈ 52 MB). There is no way to express that
slab: passing `wq[a:b, :]` fails with

```
prefetch.async_prefetch expects src to be a Var or IterArg
```

and passing `wq` itself fails with

```
prefetch.async_prefetch expects src to be a flat contiguous logical 1D GM region
(all dimensions except the last must be 1), but dimension 0 is 204800;
reshape the tensor to [N] or [1, ..., N] before prefetching
```

`pl.reshape(wq, [1, N])` is accepted, but it reshapes the *whole* tensor, so the only
thing that can be issued is a 2 GB prefetch — not what the layer needs.

**2. Whole-tensor is over L2 capacity even in the single-layer case.**
A2/A3 L2 is ~192 MB. One Qwen3-14B decode layer's weights total ≈ 660 MB
(wq 52 + wk 10.5 + wv 10.5 + wo 52 + w_gate 178 + w_up 178 + w_down 178 MB). Only the
smaller matrices fit, and the ones that dominate the memory traffic (`w_gate` / `w_up` /
`w_down`, 178 MB each) can never be prefetched whole. Sub-region prefetch would let a
kernel warm a tile-sized window that actually fits and actually stays resident.

**3. The underlying SDMA path already takes a base pointer and a length.**
This looks like a PyPTO-side restriction rather than a hardware or PTO-ISA one:

- pto-isa's `SdmaCmoPrefetch(__gm__ uint8_t *src, uint64_t messageLen, ...)`
  (`include/pto/comm/async/sdma/sdma_cmo_intrin.hpp`) is already expressed as
  base + length, and `TPrefetchAsyncIsFlatContiguous1D` only needs the region to be
  one packed contiguous run;
- PyPTO codegen already builds a `pto.partition_view`, but hardcodes it to the whole
  tensor — `EmitWholeTensorPartitionView` in `src/backend/common/pto_ops_prefetch.cpp`
  fills `offset_codes` with zeros and `size_codes` with the full shape.

A row slab `w[a:b, :]` of a packed row-major tensor **is** a single flat contiguous run
(base `= data + a * row_stride`, length `= (b - a) * row_stride`), so presenting it as a
`[1, len]` partition view should satisfy the existing pto-isa check without any change
below PyPTO.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Either an explicit offset/size pair:

```python
ctx = pl.prefetch.make_context()
# Warm just layer L's slab of the stacked weight.
evt = pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(wq, ctx, offset=layer_idx * HIDDEN * HIDDEN, size=HIDDEN * HIDDEN)
pl.prefetch.wait(evt, pl.prefetch.session(ctx))
```

or accepting a contiguous slice expression directly:

```python
evt = pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(wq[layer_idx * HIDDEN : (layer_idx + 1) * HIDDEN, :], ctx)
```

Notes on what would make it usable for the decode case:

- **A dynamic offset matters.** In a layer loop the slab base is `layer_idx * stride`
  with `layer_idx` a loop induction variable, so the offset should be allowed to be a
  scalar expression. Only the *size* needs to be a compile-time constant (it is what
  sets the byte extent).
- Keeping the "one flat contiguous run" requirement for the resulting region is fine —
  a full-width row slab of a packed tensor already satisfies it. Rejecting a
  non-contiguous region (e.g. a column slice) at IR-construction time with the current
  style of message would be the right behavior.

### Alternatives Considered

- **`pl.reshape(w, [1, N])` then prefetch** — accepted by the verifier, but it can only
  express the whole tensor, which is either the wrong region (stacked multi-layer
  weights) or larger than L2 (single-layer `w_gate`/`w_up`/`w_down`).
- **Passing each layer's weight slab as its own kernel parameter** — would make the
  region static, but needs `NUM_LAYERS × 7` extra parameters (280 for Qwen3-14B) and
  gives up the stacked-weight layout the rest of the kernel depends on.
- **Doing nothing and relying on the natural MTE2 stream** — this is the current state;
  it is what the request is trying to improve on.

### Additional Context

Measured on device (a2a3), Qwen3-14B single decode layer, batch 16, seq 4096, task
makespan from the L2 swimlane. The prefetch is numerically transparent as documented
(the golden check passed in every configuration) — this is purely about placement and
cost:

| Config | prefetch task exec | layer makespan | vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (no prefetch), 6 runs | — | 989 / 1024 / 1029 / 1034 / 1035 / 1072 µs | — |
| whole `wk` (10.5 MB) | 414 / 423 / 494 µs | 1291 / 1326 / 1384 µs | +29% |
| whole `wk` + `wv` (21 MB) | ~415 µs each | 1317 / 1342 µs | +29% |
| whole `wq` (52 MB) | 423 / 501 µs | 1331 / 1395 µs | +32% |
| whole `wo` (52 MB) | 456 µs | 1347 µs | +31% |

The form that is expressible today, for reference — a standalone head task that issues
the pull and waits, which nothing else depends on:

```python
wo_flat = pl.reshape(wo, [1, HIDDEN * HIDDEN])
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="prefetch_wo"):
    pf_ctx = pl.prefetch.make_context()
    pf_evt = pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(wo_flat, pf_ctx)
    pl.prefetch.wait(pf_evt, pl.prefetch.session(pf_ctx))
```

**A second, separable problem:** the prefetch task carries a large fixed cost that is
nearly independent of the transferred size, so even with sub-region support a small warm
would not pay for itself. Isolated microbenchmark (one prefetch task plus one trivial
task, per-task `Avg Exec` from the swimlane):

| prefetched bytes | task exec |
|---|---|
| 0.52 MB | 533.7 µs |
| 8.39 MB | 400.3 µs |
| 67.1 MB | 733.9 µs |
| 4 × 0.52 MB, concurrent tasks | 489–577 µs each |

Dropping the `pl.prefetch.wait` does not help (8.39 MB, no wait: 386.6 µs), so the cost
is on the issue path (`make_context` / `tprefetch_async`), not in the wait; and four
concurrent tasks each pay it, so it is per-task rather than one-time SDMA setup. For
scale, a whole Qwen3-14B decode layer is ~1030 µs. Happy to split this into its own
performance issue if you'd prefer to track it separately.

In this particular kernel the regression above has a second cause worth flagging: the
fused attention is a full-occupancy `pl.spmd(..., sync_start=True)` dispatch, so a
~0.5 ms prefetch task holding one AIV pushed its head overhead from 24.4 µs to 352.3 µs
while its exec time was unchanged (309 → 313 µs). That is a scheduling interaction, not a
prefetch defect, but it means a long-running hint task is expensive next to a
full-occupancy dispatch.

Environment for the measurements above:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `fd91568` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto | `06fdbfc3` (branch: `main`) |
| simpler | `9922afdb` (detached) |
| ptoas | `0.54` |
| pto-isa | `83d01313` |
| Host | Linux (aarch64) |

Related: #2075 (added the `pl.prefetch` frontend and introduced the flat-1D constraint),
#2166 (ST coverage tracker, batch B19 lists the flat-contiguous-1D limit as a constraint
to cover).

title: fix(ir): Revert unrelated valid shape changes
body:
## Summary

## Motivation

PR #2233 bundled behavior changes with the parameter rename. The matmul result propagation can place dynamic valid-shape SSA values outside their defining scope, causing PTOAS compilation failures in pypto-lib a2a3 cases. This PR narrows #2233 back to the requested naming migration.
