title: [Feature] Lower pld.tensor.put to remote_store when src is a tile, so computed values are pushable from @pl.jit
body:
### Summary A value computed inside a kernel lives in UB and lowers to a `TileType`. Today it cannot be pushed cross-rank: `pld.tensor.put` requires a GM source, and the one op that does take a tile — `pld.tile.remote_store` — is tile-level and rejects the tensor-level value a `@pl.jit` kernel produces. The value is rejected from both directions, so the only way to push a computed result is to store it back to GM first and push from there. Proposal: dispatch `pld.tensor.put` on the kind of its `src` — GM tensor → `TPUT` (today's path), tile → `remote_store`. ### Motivation / Use Case `pld.tensor.put`'s source must be a readable local GM region, because codegen emits `TPUT(remote_gm_view, local_gm_view, staging_tile)` and a UB tile has no GM address to build the second operand from (`src/backend/common/pto_ops_distributed.cpp:584`). That is a real property of the instruction, not an oversight — TPUT's staging tile is internal to it. But the UB→remote path **does** exist in the ISA and is already exposed: `pld.tile.remote_store` lowers to `pto.tstore` straight from a tile into a peer's window. It is simply unreachable from a `@pl.jit` tensor-level kernel, because its operand check demands a `TileType` at authoring time while tensor-level values are `TensorType` until `ConvertTensorToTileOps` runs. So a kernel that computes something and wants to push it must today write: ```python scratch[...] = computed # UB -> GM pld.tensor.put(src=scratch, ...) # GM -> UB staging -> TPUT -> peer ``` which costs an extra GM round-trip, and makes ordering the author's problem: the store and the put are different engines touching the same GM addresses. In a kernel where those land on different pipes with nothing between them, a fraction of each tile is read stale. We hit exactly this while fusing the DeepSeek-V4 LM-head projection with its outgoing all-to-all (the `combine_push` in [#1906](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/1906)): a few hundred wrong values per vocab shard out of 517120, with the count varying run to run. (Observed in a mixed cube+comm kernel on an unmerged branch, so the corruption figure is context-specific — the structural point is that the round-trip exists and its ordering is unspecified.) With a tile-source lowering the round-trip disappears and so does the hazard: the computed tile goes straight to the peer. ### Proposed API / Behavior No new user-facing op. `pld.tensor.put` gains a second lowering target, chosen by the kind of `src`: ```python pld.tensor.put(dst=win, peer=p, src=gm_tensor, ...) # -> TPUT (unchanged) pld.tensor.put(dst=win, peer=p, src=computed, ...) # -> remote_store (new) ``` Two reasons this fits the existing design rather than adding a mechanism: - `pld.tensor.put` is *already* lowered — `ConvertTensorToTileOps` rewrites it into a `tile.create`-allocated VEC staging tile plus `pld.tile.put`. This adds a second target to a pass that already exists. - Operand-kind dispatch is already the house pattern: `pl.aiv_shard` accepts a Tile (`@pl.program`) or a Tensor (`@pl.jit`) and picks `tile.aiv_shard` / `tensor.aiv_shard` accordingly. Drain semantics no longer diverge between the two targets, which is what would otherwise make this dispatch a silent trap: `remote_store` codegen emits `pto.cmo.cacheinvalid` on the written peer region, and `InsertCommFence` inserts the paired GM `system.fence` after each publishing write — its header states that this satisfies "any later `pto.comm.tnotify` that releases that data, including a notify in a different loop". #### Risk: the two argument surfaces do not match ``` pld.tensor.put(dst, peer, src, dst_offsets, src_offsets, shape, *, atomic, chunk_rows, chunk_cols, pipeline) pld.tile.remote_store(src_tile, target, peer, offsets) ``` `remote_store` writes **the whole tile** at one destination offset. It has no `src_offsets`, no `shape`, no `atomic`, and no staging knobs. Every other `put` argument is therefore either lowered by slicing the tile first, or is meaningless — and most failure modes are silent rather than loud: | `put` argument | Tile-source lowering | Risk if unverified | | --- | --- | --- | | `shape` smaller than the tile | must slice to a sub-tile | **silent corruption** — writes the full tile over the peer's neighbouring region | | `src_offsets` | must slice the tile | wrong rows pushed. Dynamic offsets may not be sliceable at all — see [#2213](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/2213) for the related static-partition-view constraint | | `atomic=AtomicType.Add` | no lowering exists | **silently degrades to a plain store** — a combine loses contributions | | `chunk_rows` / `chunk_cols` / `pipeline` | meaningless (already in UB) | silently ignored; the author believes double-buffering is on | | `dst_offsets` | maps to `offsets` | rank rules differ: `remote_store` requires a 2-D tile `valid_shape` and `target rank >= 2`, padding leading dims with 1s. A >2-D tile has no lowering | | tile memory space | must be Vec | an Acc operand (a raw `pl.matmul` result) is not a legal `tstore` source | | dtype | must equal `target.dtype` | currently checked at tile level only | #### Required: verify in the tensor-level op, before lowering These checks belong in `pld.tensor.put`'s verifier, not after `ConvertTensorToTileOps` has picked a target: 1. **Silence.** Most rows above are accept-and-do-the-wrong-thing, not fail. `atomic=Add` and an undersized `shape` are correctness bugs that no existing check can catch, because `remote_store` never receives those arguments — they are dropped at the call boundary. 2. **Diagnostics.** The failure today already surfaces as `pld.tile.put src must be a Tensor or DistributedTensor, got TileType`, naming an op the author never wrote. Post-lowering checks inherit that problem. Concretely, when `src` is tile-typed, `pld.tensor.put` should reject `atomic != None_`, reject non-zero `chunk_rows`/`chunk_cols`/`pipeline`, require a 2-D Vec tile whose dtype matches `dst`, and require that `src_offsets`/`shape` either be expressible as a tile slice or be absent. Each diagnostic should name the tile-source form, so the author knows which lowering they landed in. ### Alternatives Considered - **Expose a tensor-level `pld.tensor.remote_store`** instead of overloading `put`. Makes the choice of instruction visible at the call site rather than implied by operand type. Now that `InsertCommFence` equalizes the ordering semantics, the difference is an implementation detail, so overloading `put` seems preferable — but this is a reasonable alternative if the argument-surface mismatch above is judged too wide to hide behind one entry point. - **Let `pld.tile.put` accept a tile `src`.** This fights the instruction: TPUT needs two `GlobalTensor` descriptors, and the staging tile it takes is its own bounce buffer, not a data source. - **Keep staging through GM and add a barrier.** Works, but pays an extra GM round-trip per tile and re-serializes what the fusion was trying to overlap. ### Additional Context Reproduction — compile-only, needs pypto alone (no device, no pypto-lib). Save and run: ``` python repro_put_tile_src.py ``` ``` pld.tensor.put(src=): ValueError: pld.tile.put src must be a Tensor or DistributedTensor, got TileType pld.tile.remote_store(): InvalidOperationError: pld.tile.remote_store src_tile must be a TileType, got TensorType ```
Reproduction case — repro_put_tile_src.py (not committed; save locally to run) ```python """pld.tensor.put / pld.tile.remote_store: a computed (UB) value is pushable by neither. Compile-only; needs pypto alone — no device, no pypto-lib. python repro_put_tile_src.py """ import torch import pypto.language as pl import pypto.language.distributed as pld from pypto.ir.distributed_compiled_program import DistributedConfig from pypto.runtime import RunConfig N_RANKS = 2 ROWS = 16 COLS = 256 @pl.jit def put_computed( src: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32], win: pld.DistributedTensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32], peer: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32], ): with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="push_put"): # A computed value: lives in UB, lowers to a TileType. scaled = pl.mul(src[0:ROWS, 0:COLS], 2.0) pld.tensor.put( dst=win, peer=peer, src=scaled, dst_offsets=[0, 0], src_offsets=[0, 0], shape=[ROWS, COLS], ) @pl.jit def remote_store_computed( src: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32], win: pld.DistributedTensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32], peer: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32], ): with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="push_rs"): scaled = pl.mul(src[0:ROWS, 0:COLS], 2.0) pld.tile.remote_store(scaled, win, peer, [0, 0]) @pl.jit.host def l3_put_computed(src: pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]): win_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer([ROWS, COLS], dtype=pl.FP32) for r in pl.range(pld.world_size()): win = pld.window(win_buf, [ROWS, COLS], dtype=pl.FP32) put_computed(src[r], win, r, device=r) @pl.jit.host def l3_remote_store_computed(src: pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]): win_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer([ROWS, COLS], dtype=pl.FP32) for r in pl.range(pld.world_size()): win = pld.window(win_buf, [ROWS, COLS], dtype=pl.FP32) remote_store_computed(src[r], win, r, device=r) def try_compile(host, label): cfg = RunConfig( platform="a2a3", distributed_config=DistributedConfig(device_ids=list(range(N_RANKS)), num_sub_workers=0), ) try: host.compile(torch.zeros(N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS, dtype=torch.float32), config=cfg) print(f"{label}: COMPILED") except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - the message is the report first = str(exc).strip().split("\n")[0] print(f"{label}: {type(exc).__name__}: {first}") if __name__ == "__main__": try_compile(l3_put_computed, "pld.tensor.put(src=)") try_compile(l3_remote_store_computed, "pld.tile.remote_store()") ```
Environment (all components on their pins): | Component | Version | |---|---| | pypto | `9d329a11` (branch: `main`) | | simpler | `3165cc89` (detached) | | ptoas | `0.57` | | pto-isa | `83d01313` | | CANN | `9.0.0` | | pypto-lib | `6741e82` (branch: `main`) | Related: #1906 (put-fence / TPUT-quiesce for the same `combine_push` push path), #2213 (PTOAS static partition-view shapes, relevant to whether a dynamic `src_offsets` can be lowered to a tile slice).

title: feat(runtime): replay an already-compiled single-chip program from build_output
body:
## Summary

`execute_compiled(work_dir, ...)` is directory-driven, but `benchmark()` needs
a live `CompiledProgram`, so the `--runtime-dir` tuning loop — edit the
generated orchestration cpp / `.pto`, then re-measure — silently loses timing
for L2 programs. Correctness still replays; only the numbers, which are usually
the point of the edit, are unobtainable.

The asymmetry comes down to one missing input. `benchmark`'s L2 branch reaches
`build_orch_args` / `build_call_config` / `output_indices`, all derived from
`_extract_param_infos(self._program)`. Every other member it touches —
`platform`, `runtime_name`, `runtime_config`, `chip_callable` — already rebuilds
from the build directory through `compile_and_assemble`.

L3 closed this gap in #1749 with a `distributed_meta.json` sidecar plus
`DistributedCompiledProgram.from_dir()`. This adds the single-chip counterpart,
so the edit-and-re-measure loop closes for L2 kernels as well:

    compiled = CompiledProgram.from_dir(work_dir, platform="a2a3")
    stats = benchmark(compiled, args, rounds=100)

## Changes

- `python/pypto/ir/compiled_program.py`: a `compiled_meta.json` sidecar
  recording the orchestration param metadata, return-type count, platform, and
  backend; `CompiledProgram.from_dir()` reconstructs from it with no recompile
  and no pass re-run. `__init__` accepts `program=None` plus pre-derived
  metadata and writes neither the sidecar nor `debug/run.py` on that path, so a
  hand-edited runner survives a reload. A multi-orch build gives each
  `next_levels/<name>/` sub-build its own sidecar — each is a complete build
  directory in its own right, and that is what the parent's error message
  points at.
- **Which layout a build is** — one top-level program or one sub-build per
  orchestration — now comes from the codegen that just ran
  (`pto_backend.multi_chip_orch_names`, the single source of truth `generate()`
  also dispatches on), never from scanning the output directory.
- **Reusing an `output_dir` is safe in every direction.** `ir.compile()` never
  clears it, so each fresh compile drops what it does not itself write: a
  sidecar it declines to record, and the build-kind markers of the *other* kind
  (top-level `kernel_config.py` / `compiled_meta.json` vs
  `orchestration/host_orch.py` / `distributed_meta.json`). Those markers are how
  `replay()` and `from_dir()` decide what a directory holds, so a leftover would
  re-point the whole directory at an older build rather than merely age out.
  Only markers are removed; artifact trees are left alone.
- **Sidecar loading is treated as untrusted input.** One shared loader validates
  every field of both sidecars — JSON shape, param entries, directions, dtypes,
  return count, backend, platform, and the L3 `distributed_config` block —
  reporting each failure as a single `ValueError` naming the file and the
  recompile that regenerates it. Enum fields resolve through `__members__`, not
  `getattr`, so a name like `"mro"` cannot pass as a `ParamDirection` or
  `BackendType`. Both sidecars are written atomically (temp file + `os.replace`).
- `python/pypto/ir/distributed_compiled_program.py`: the L3 sidecar gains the
  same three guarantees (stale removal, atomic write, full validation) through
  the shared helpers, and `DistributedConfig` enforces the constraints its own
  docstring declares — non-empty, distinct, non-negative `device_ids`, a
  non-negative `num_sub_workers`, and an `aicpu_thread_num` of 0 (architecture
  default) or at least 2 — on the dataclass, so a reloaded config is held to the
  same bar as a live one.
- `CompiledProgram.program` widens to `Program | None`. No in-repo consumers;
  downstream code doing `compiled.program.get_function(...)` needs a guard.
- `tests/ut/ir/test_compiled_program.py` (91 tests) and
  `tests/ut/ir/test_distributed_compiled_program.py` (18): sidecar contents,
  metadata round-trip (including the packed-FP4 x2 carrier shape), dispatch,
  override precedence, every malformed-payload path, the no-clobber guarantees,
  the full member surface `benchmark()` touches, and directory reuse in each
  direction — multi-orch → single-orch driven by two real `ir.compile()` runs,
  plus L2 → L3 and L3 → L2.
- `tests/st/runtime/framework_and_models/test_benchmark_st.py`: on-device
  confirmation that a directory-reloaded program produces correct output and
  real per-launch `device_wall_us`.
- `docs/{en,zh}/dev/03-runtime-replay.md`: new page. `03-runtime-dfx.md` was
  already at the 500-line documentation limit, so both replay sections (L2 and
  L3) move here and the DFX page keeps a pointer. Nav, the dev index, and the
  affected cross-references are updated alongside.

## Verification

`tests/ut/` is green (9664 passed / 8 skipped). On a2a3 hardware, via
`task-submit`: `test_benchmark_st.py` L2 cases including the new
`from_dir`-replay one, the L3 per-rank benchmark case on two cards, and
`test_l2_multi_orch.py` end to end including its real device dispatch.

Issue: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/2344
Prior art: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/1749 (the L3 counterpart this mirrors)

title: feat(ir): make pl.split_aiv authoritative for AIV placement
body:
## Summary

A mixed cube+vector kernel that also carries a distributed comm op did not build, and `pl.split_aiv` did not help. This makes the region authoritative for AIV placement and fixes the codegen defect behind the build failure.

- **Inline the peer-offset arithmetic.** PTO codegen emitted a module-level `@CommRemoteOffset_<dtype>` helper. A mixed kernel is one MLIR module compiled into one `.cpp` per core, and the helper carried no `pto.kernel_kind`, so ptoas wrapped its body in `#if defined(__DAV_VEC__)` while leaving the value-returning `return` outside the guard — the AIC compile failed on undeclared identifiers. The arithmetic is now emitted inline at each call site, so no value-returning function without a kernel kind reaches a mixed module.
- **`pl.split_aiv` is explicit manual mode.** A function holding at least one region opts in: `LowerAutoVectorSplit` stamps `core_placement` on the region's no-duplicate calls before erasing the wrapper, `ClassifyCallAffinity` consumes it, and a comm op written inside a region stays off the cube lane.
- **The verifier enforces the division.** Cube compute is rejected in any region (extending the existing check to `mode=NONE`); vector compute outside every region is rejected in a manual-mode function; and a tile crossing a region edge must say so through `pl.aiv_shard` / `pl.aic_gather`, which are now legal in a `mode=NONE` region and preserve the shape there.
- **Declare what the ISA actually constrains.** `VECTOR` on the put/get family, whose staging tile ptoas requires to be in VEC. A new `set_no_duplicate()` registry axis marks an op that must not run on a second core.

## Why the affinity declarations are shaped this way

`pld.system.notify` and `pld.system.wait` are **core-agnostic** and are deliberately left undeclared. Their pto-isa implementations are pure scalar/GM (`st_atomic`, `dcci`, `dsb`), ptoas imposes no core or section constraint, and pto-isa's own cube-built `allgather_gemm_compute_kernel.cpp` calls `TWAIT`. Declaring `VECTOR` would be a false claim about the ISA.

`notify` carries `set_no_duplicate()` for **both** `NotifyOp` forms, because the cube-lane hazard is not double-counting but **premature release from the wrong lane**: the AIC copy can publish the signal before the AIV lane's TPUT has landed the data it releases. `wait` is deliberately unmarked — it *blocks*, and its presence on the cube lane is load-bearing; pinning it to AIV would let the matmul race past the peer data it exists to wait for.

## What stays the author's responsibility

Two things are documented rather than diagnosed, because the compiler cannot distinguish the correct form from the incorrect one:

1. **A `mode=NONE` region body runs on both AIV sub-lanes.** A once-only side effect must be sharded by `aiv_id` or guarded to one lane. Both forms compile to one statement in the AIV body with `dual_aiv_dispatch=True`; they differ only in whether `aiv_id` reaches the call's arguments.
2. **AIC and AIV are asynchronous.** Ordering GM traffic across the boundary needs `pl.system.syncall(core_type="mix")`. No boundary op can express a GM crossing, since `pld.tensor.put` takes GM by signature.

Both are covered in `docs/en/user/language/04-scopes.md`, the `pl.split_aiv` docstring, and the distributed primitives chapter, with the failure each prevents spelled out.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/ut/` — **9380 passed, 3 skipped**
- Full pre-commit suite green: pyright, ruff, clang-format, cpplint, markdownlint, and the repository lint checkers (en/zh doc parity, english-only, op-name literals, doc nav, symbol coverage)
- End to end: the generated `.cpp` for a mixed matmul + `put` + `notify` kernel compiles under `ccec` for **both** `dav-c220-cube` and `dav-c220-vec`. A positive control reproduced the original guard defect and confirmed the cube compile fails on it, so the check is not vacuous.

## Known limitations

- `pld.tile.remote_load` still classifies `SHARED`. Benign today — the duplicated cube copy produces a `Vec` tile no cube statement consumes, so DCE removes it. Neither obvious fix is safe: declaring `VECTOR` is a false ISA claim, and classifying from the result tile makes `LowerAutoVectorSplit` treat the op as halvable when its `offsets` / `shape` tuples have no rewrite in the halving path. A real fix teaches the halving path about the op. Characterised by tests in `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_core_affinity.py`.
- The crossing checks record only `AssignStmt`-bound definitions, so a crossing laundered through a loop-carried value (`IterArg`, `return_vars`) is not detected. This under-approximates — false negatives, never false positives.
- `docs/en|zh/dev/passes/20-lower_auto_vector_split.md` and `21-expand_mixed_kernel.md` now exceed the 500-line guidance in `.claude/rules/documentation-length.md` and want condensing.

title: [Bug] Assigning an operator result to a pl.Out parameter silently writes nothing
body:
### Component

Parser

### Description

Assigning a tensor-op result directly to a `pl.Out` parameter compiles cleanly, runs to
completion, and **never writes the output buffer**. The caller receives uninitialised
memory. Nothing reports a problem at any stage — not the parser, the passes, codegen,
ptoas, or the runtime.

```python
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP):
    out = pl.add(a, b)          # compiles, runs, writes nothing
```

The form that does write is:

```python
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP):
    out = pl.assemble(out, pl.add(a, b), [0, 0])
```

There are two problems here, and the second is why the first keeps happening.

**1. It is a silent wrong answer.** A rebinding that produces garbage should not be
accepted without a diagnostic.

**2. The correct form is awkward.** `out = pl.assemble(out, expr, [0, 0])` names `out`
twice and adds a `[0, 0]` offset just to say "this result is the whole output". The
natural spelling is the one that silently fails, so the mistake is easy to make and
invisible once made.

This is not hypothetical: every complete example in the user manual was written the
natural way and therefore produced NaN — 15 sites across the quickstart, the
programming-model page, the language chapter and the tasks chapter. They compiled, so
review and the docs example gate both passed them. PR #2347 rewrites all of them.

Related: #889 — same class of defect (an `Out` parameter rebound so the caller's buffer is
never written), but its root cause is `pl.create_tensor` shadowing, and the validation
added for it does not cover an operator-result assignment.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Save as `repro.py`:

```python
import pypto.language as pl
import torch
from pypto.runtime import RunConfig

@pl.jit
def add(
    a: pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.FP32],
    b: pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.FP32],
    out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.FP32]],
):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP):
        out = pl.add(a, b)
    return out

torch.manual_seed(0)
a = torch.randn(128, 128)
b = torch.randn(128, 128)
out = torch.zeros(128, 128)
add(a, b, out, config=RunConfig(platform="a2a3sim"))
print("max diff:", (out - (a + b)).abs().max().item())
print("has NaN :", torch.isnan(out).any().item())
```

2. Run `python repro.py`.

3. Replace the body with `out = pl.assemble(out, pl.add(a, b), [0, 0])` and run again to
   see the contrast.

### Expected Behavior

Either of the following would be acceptable; the first is preferable.

**Option A — desugar the assignment.** When the assignment target is an `Out` parameter
and the value's shape matches it, treat

```python
out = <tensor-expr>
```

as

```python
out = pl.assemble(out, <tensor-expr>, [0, 0])
```

This makes the natural spelling correct and removes the boilerplate. A partial write still
needs an explicit `pl.assemble` with a real offset, which is exactly when the offset
carries information.

**Option B — reject it at parse time.** Raise a `CHECK`-style error naming the parameter
and the required form, e.g.

```
out = pl.add(...): assigning an operator result to the Out parameter 'out' does not
write it. Use out = pl.assemble(out, pl.add(...), [0, 0]) to write the whole tensor.
```

Either way, the current behaviour — accept it, run it, and hand back uninitialised memory
— should not survive.

### Actual Behavior

The program compiles and runs to completion with no diagnostic, and the output buffer is
never written:

```
max diff: nan
has NaN : True
```

Verified against the `pl.assemble` form on the same commit and inputs, which gives
`max diff: 0.0`.

### Git Commit ID

71020585278b68f56c72c40d5570f07dbb20bc8b

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Reproduced on `a2a3sim` with `PTOAS_ROOT=/usr/local/ptoas/0.54` (the version pinned in
  `toolchain/versions.env`) and the `runtime` submodule at its pinned `3165cc89`.
- The same silent-write behaviour occurs inside `@pl.jit.incore`, not just inside
  `pl.at` in an orchestration body.
- Every write site under `examples/` already uses the explicit form — `pl.store` ×156,
  `pl.assemble` ×28, zero bare assignments — so the working code in the repository is
  consistent with today's semantics. The gap is that the natural spelling is accepted
  instead of rejected or desugared.
- `docs/en/dev/language/00-python_syntax.md` documents the intended mechanism
  ("a captured tensor that the scope body mutates via `pl.assemble`"), which supports
  Option A being a surface-syntax change rather than a semantic one.
- Filed while writing the user manual; the docs-side repair is PR #2347.

title: docs(user): add the Tutorials chapter
body:
## What

Adds `docs/{en,zh}/user/tutorials/` — seven task-oriented walkthroughs (B3), plus the three examples they needed.

**Writing operators**

| Page | Ends in |
| ---- | ------- |
| `00-elementwise.md` | An element-wise kernel, tensor level → tile level → chunked → checked |
| `01-reduction-softmax.md` | A numerically stable softmax |
| `02-matmul.md` | A K-blocked matmul, and what split-K costs |
| `03-mixed-kernel.md` | Cube and vector overlapping in one scope |

**Shaping the schedule**

| Page | Ends in |
| ---- | ------- |
| `04-task-graph.md` | A program whose dependency graph you control |
| `05-scheduling-tuning.md` | A measurement loop over the four DFX observation points |

## The mixed-kernel gap

`03-mixed-kernel.md` closes the gap #2120 flagged as larger than distributed. There was no standalone mixed-kernel example anywhere — the only real one is inside `examples/models/qwen3_jit/kernels/projection.py`, and `examples/intermediate/01_fused_linear.py`-style "fused" kernels are two sequential InCore functions, which is the form a mixed kernel replaces.

The page documents the cross-core ring sizing that every non-toy mixed kernel runs into:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Tile crossing the boundary | `[128, 128]` FP32 = 64 KB |
| Default ring depth | 8 slots → **512 KB** |
| Vector budget | **184 KB** |

So `pl.cross_core_slot(slot_num=2)` is mandatory rather than decorative — and the error, which names a byte count and not the tile, is quoted verbatim so a reader can match it.

## New examples

- `examples/advanced/03_mixed_kernel.py` — three modes (staged / UP_DOWN / LEFT_RIGHT)
- `examples/intermediate/07_task_graph.py` — an inferred edge and the same edge declared
- `examples/beginner/02_elementwise.py` — extended with `chunked_add`, the step from one tile to a tensor that needs a loop

## Verification

Every runnable example was **executed on a2a3sim**, not just compiled:

```
19 runnable example(s), 0 failed
```

Examples carrying their own `torch.allclose` have that assertion run as part of the check, so the softmax, matmul, mixed-kernel and task-graph pages are golden-checked, not merely non-NaN.

This branch predates #2347. Its examples already use `pl.assemble` throughout, so there is no overlap in content, only in subject.

title: [Bug] Advancing the Simpler pin onto the Buffer API stalls DeepSeek V4 decode after the first token (TENSOR_WAIT_TIMEOUT)
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Update 2026-08-13:** this is **not** caused by the port in #2355 — it reproduces identically on #2345's own head (`75e4bcc4`) with our code absent, 3 runs. The "look in pypto / the port" narrowing below is withdrawn; see [this comment](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/2354#issuecomment-5278994812). The four exclusions still stand.

### Summary

Advancing pypto's `runtime/` (Simpler) pin onto the Buffer device-memory API makes DeepSeek V4 Flash W8A8 serving **start and upload correctly but stall in decode after the first generated token**. Startup is clean (346.6 GB of resident weights uploaded, 0 faults, `model loaded` in 74.0s); the first token comes out; the second decode step dies with a tensor-wait timeout.

This is filed to record what has already been **excluded**, so the next person does not re-pay for it.

### Symptom

```
AICore error 507901: bounded device drain failed
Device[0] fault, ret=0x7110011
PTO2 runtime failed: orch_error_code=8 sched_error_code=100 runtime_status=-8
  orch_error_code=8 TENSOR_WAIT_TIMEOUT - waiting for tensor data timed out: the producing
  task never completed, or a consumer never released its fanout reference
  sub_class=S1:running-stalled (detail=1) completed=71/9 running=3 ready=0 waiting=0
  stuck_task_id=4294967357 stuck_core=41
→ finalize_native_run failed with code -8 (run_id=2 slot=0 generation=2 dispatch_id=3 run_epoch=3)
```

`stuck_task_id` decodes as `(ring 1 << 32) | 61`. Note `run_id=2` / `generation=2`: the **second** run of the persistent program, not the first.

Inference harness: `req 0: TRUNCATED 1/32`, then zero tokens on `req 1`. Both the streaming and non-streaming completion paths are affected identically, so it is not an API-surface problem.

### Environment

| Component | Value |
|---|---|
| pypto | `08f6c70f` + the pin-advance port (7 layers, see below) |
| Simpler | `8a82bf9e` |
| pypto-lib | `f0d352e` |
| pypto-serving | `71fd275` |
| PTOAS | v0.57 (as pinned by `toolchain/versions.env`) |
| Hardware | 8 × 910B2, driver 25.5.1, kernel cache freshly built for this stack |

### Control: the old pin does not stall

Same serving tree (`71fd275`), same pypto-lib (`f0d352e`), same model, same warm kernel cache, same harness — only pypto/Simpler/PTOAS older (`08d3b231` / `3165cc89` / v0.54):

```
req   0: 32 tok in 5.162s (cum=32)
req   1: 32 tok in 1.530s (cum=64)
RESULT no_fault_in=2 cumulative_tokens=64      faults: 0
```

Startup there is 73.7s vs 74.0s on the advanced pin, so the pin is performance-neutral; the difference is purely functional.

### Excluded, with evidence

1. **The pre-existing 507018 decode fault** — excluded by the control above.
2. **The window view losing `child_memory=True` semantics.** `src/common/task_interface/buffer.h`'s capability matrix *requires* `address_space == DEVICE` for a `VMM_WINDOW` backend, so the materialized `ChipTensor` reports `is_device_memory()` and `runtime_maker.cpp` takes the pass-through branch. Semantics are preserved by construction.
3. **Reuse of the port's POSIX-shm staging Buffers.** With a fresh Buffer per copy and no memoization at all, the stall reproduces identically.
4. **An upstream regression in Simpler's window path.** Simpler's own `tests/st/worker/collectives/{allreduce,all_to_all}` pass on `8a82bf9e` on this node (with `--platform a2a3 --device 0-7`; without those flags every case skips or the phase aborts while still exiting 0).

### Narrowing

Diffing the **generated** decode `orchestration/host_orch.py`, old pin vs advanced pin: 215 of 227 lines are byte-identical. The port changes only the 12 comm-window task args, from

```python
_ta_0.add_tensor(Tensor.make(data=__comm_d0[r].buffer_ptrs["arrived_buf__ssa_v0"],
                             shapes=(8, 1), dtype=DataType.INT32, child_memory=True), ...)
```

to

```python
_ta_0.add_tensor(__comm_d0[r].buffers["arrived_buf__ssa_v0"].tensor((8, 1), DataType.INT32), ...)
```

Those 12 include the synchronisation flags `arrived_buf`, `data_arrived_buf`, `combine_arrived_buf`, `lm_head_hidden_done_buf`, `lm_head_logits_done_buf` — i.e. exactly the objects a consumer can wait on forever.

### Sharpest untested hypothesis

`pypto-serving` allocates and frees the per-step decode inputs **per token**: `_TransientDeviceTensor` → `worker.alloc_tensor(...)` (`npu_runner.py:3767`), released in the `finally` at `:3686`. Under the Buffer ABI that mints *and releases* a Buffer identity on every decode step inside a persistent run, where the old path moved raw pointers through `rtMalloc`/`rtFree` with no identity or registry. Simpler#1751 ("reject Buffer release while an in-flight run still references it") shows this lifetime edge is real. `hw-native-sys/pypto-serving#44` already asks for those four tensors to be pooled/owned by L3 — doing that would also test this hypothesis.

Adjacent, probably distinct: `hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#929` reports that the same MoE protocol **corrupts** results after persistent worker reuse with changing inputs, on the *old* stack. Different symptom (corruption, not a hang), but it establishes the persistent-reuse path as already fragile.

### A caution on the obvious next tool

`hw-native-sys/pypto#1931` records that `dep_gen` instrumentation itself provokes AICore 507018 at full occupancy. Resolving `stuck_task_id` via a dependency dump may manufacture the very fault it is meant to explain — cross-check against a non-instrumented run.

title: Advance the Simpler pin onto the Buffer device-memory API (port, not a bump)
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Update 2026-08-13 — this PR is being superseded in part, and reduced on purpose.**
> #2345 does the same pin advance (it moves `runtime` to `e4ab544a`, 16 commits *ahead* of the `8a82bf9e` used here) and covers the same renames, emitters and the `tests/ut/runtime` rewrite this PR lists as a gap. So the port below is no longer the contribution.
> What survives is one measured thing: **#2345's H2D path copies, and this one does not.** Once #2345 merges, this PR will be reduced to the `copy_to` / `copy_from` in-place host-buffer naming (see *What is still worth merging* below) rather than rebased whole.
> Still a draft, but no longer because of us: #2354 reproduces on #2345's own head with our code absent, so the decode stall is a blocker for that PR too.

Advances pypto's `runtime/` (Simpler) pin onto the Buffer device-memory API and ports pypto across it.

### What is still worth merging

`DistributedWorker.copy_to` in #2345 stages every H2D through a freshly created POSIX-shm Buffer plus a full host→host `ctypes.memmove` of the payload, and `alloc_tensor` is `malloc` + `copy_to`, so all 346.6 GB of DeepSeek V4's resident weights pay an extra copy. This PR instead *names* the mapping the caller already holds — `wrap_fork_inherited(ptr, nbytes, …)` per shard, with the backend classified by the caller (`FORK_SHM` when `tensor.is_shared()`, `FORK_COW` read-only otherwise, per the capability matrix in `src/common/task_interface/buffer.h`) — and stages through shm **only** for host memory allocated after the fork, which cannot be named at all.

Measured 2026-08-13, one node, one session, single-variable: `pypto-serving` `71fd275`, `pypto-lib` `f0d352e`, PTOAS v0.57 both sides, 8 × 910B2, `--dp 8 --ep 8`, warm kernel cache, 346.6 GB resident:

| stack | resident upload | `model loaded` |
|---|---|---|
| #2345 alone | 497.7s | 518.1s |
| #2345 + #2292 | 98.9s | 119.3s |
| **this PR + #2292** | **25.6s** | **33.0s** |
| this PR alone | 66.5s | 74.0s |

**These absolutes are setup-dependent and should not be quoted as properties of either branch.** `pypto-serving`#134 measured the same class of host-copy cost at ~492s on this node and ~62s on another (page-cache state, mount, driver all matter — see that PR's discussion). What transfers is the mechanism and the direction: one extra full copy of the whole weight set, removed rather than parallelised. On a setup where the copy is cheap the gap will be much smaller.

497.7s is essentially the pre-`pypto-serving`#134 number (492.8s) *on this node*, i.e. here #2345 gives back the win of the loader change that maps the prepacked sidecar `MAP_SHARED` precisely so the upload need not copy. Cold runs agree independently: isolating the upload as `kernel-cache STORED` → `resident main weights uploaded` (both stacks pay the same ~150s of kernel compile) gives ~484.6s on #2345 vs ~20.6s here, with `model loaded` 731.3s vs 263.4s. Reported on #2345 with the code pointers.

### Why the pin had to move

Simpler #1702 removed the last of three serializers on the device-memory path (process-wide `_child_prov_lock`, run admission, and the GIL on the four bindings). pypto pinned `3165cc89`, which predates it, so #2292's concurrent shard upload was a **no-op** on that pin. #2345 now carries the pin advance instead; #2292 applies to its head with zero conflicts (two hunks, offsets only) and is worth 5.03× there (497.7 → 98.9s) versus 2.84× on this pin — it parallelises the extra memcpy too, which is why the copy still has to go.

| DeepSeek V4 Flash W8A8, 8 cards, 346.6 GB, warm cache | without #2292 | with #2292 |
|---|---|---|
| resident-weight upload | 66.5s (3 runs, ±0.6) | **23.4s / 23.8s** |
| `model loaded` total | 74.0s | **31.0s / 31.2s** |
| effective bandwidth | 5.2 GB/s | **14.8 GB/s** |

The old pin reaches `model loaded` in 73.7s, so the pin itself is performance-neutral — the 2.84× is #2292's, unlocked by the pin.

### What the port turned out to be

Not a bump. Seven layers, each found only by running the next step — recorded here because #2345 solves the same problems and the traps are worth having written down:

1. `L2TaskArgs` → `ChipTaskArgs` (Simpler #1681) — 74 sites in codegen and the collectives templates.
2. `Tensor` → `ChipTensor` at chip level, including every AIV kernel's `__gm__` preamble. Note the trap: `simpler.task_interface` exports **both** names — the plain `Tensor` is #1729's wire ABI and stays valid, so `Tensor.make(...)` on the Python path must *not* be renamed.
3. `AccessMode.READWRITE`, not `READ_WRITE`.
4. Host memory allocated **after** the fork cannot be named with `wrap_fork_inherited` at all; it stages through `create_buffer` (POSIX shm).
5. `make_tensor_arg` now takes `(worker, tensor)`; generated code has no worker in scope, so the submitter binds one via ContextVar.
6. `Tensor.make` is gone — a `DeviceTensor` is named from its allocating Buffer, which forces the owning chip onto the handle (equal-sized shards share the same numeric address on every chip).
7. Comm windows moved from `ctx.buffer_ptrs[name]` (addresses) to `ctx.buffers[name]` (Buffers).

### Verified

- 8-chip hardware check: shard uploads through the Buffer API, bogus free refused, write into a COW mapping refused, registry frees — 4/4.
- DeepSeek V4: 346.6 GB uploaded, 0 faults, `model loaded`, prefill produces a token.
- `tests/ut/{codegen,ir,language,jit,debug}`: 8441 passed, 2 skipped.

### Known gaps

- **#2354** (the decode stall) — now attributed to the ABI adoption itself, not to this port: it reproduces on #2345's head with our code absent, 3 runs, same `stuck_task_id=4294967357`.
- ~44 `tests/ut/runtime` tests still mock the old contract (`malloc(nbytes, worker_id) -> int`, `Tensor.make(child_memory=True)`). #2345 rewrites these, which is one reason to reduce this PR rather than rebase it.
- `execute_compiled`'s one-shot path builds task args before its worker exists, which the Buffer ABI cannot support; it now raises with an explanation. Fixing it has to decide what the two-pass DFX path does.

title: fix(ir): check innermost dim on GM->cube tile loads
body:
## Summary

The `TileInnermostDimGranularity` perf hint (PH001) returned early for any tile
in a cube-private memory space, so it never fired on a GM→Mat load. That skip
was reasoned from L2 locality, which holds for chip-internal movement but not
for the only two ops this check inspects: `tile.load` and `tile.store` have a
`TensorType` on their non-tile side, which is always off-chip, so both are
GM↔chip transfers whose GM side crosses L2 at the innermost-dim granularity
regardless of where the tile lands. The genuinely cube-private moves
(`tile.move` / `tile.extract`, Mat→L0) are never visited by this check, so the
skip could only ever suppress true positives. It is now removed, and each hint
additionally reports how much traffic the flagged transfer carries.

The concrete shape it hid (issue #2309): `pl.matmul(..., b_trans=True)` loads
the caller's `[N, K]` weight window verbatim, so a `[64, 1024]` GM read becomes
a `[1024, 64]` one — the same bytes moved as 16× the DMA descriptors, 128 B per
row against the backend's own 512 B recommendation. Users now get a compile-time
line naming it instead of silence.

No behavior change to compilation or generated code: PH001 is advisory, written
to `perf_hints.log` with a one-line stderr summary, and suppressible via
`disabled_diagnostics`.

## Changes

- `src/ir/verifier/perf_hint_tile_innermost_dim.cpp`: drop the cube-memory-space
  early return, so GM↔chip transfers are checked in every space. Add a transfer
  volume clause to the message (`moves <total>B as <rows> x <innermost>B rows`),
  where `rows` is the number of separate short bus transactions the transfer
  issues, and add `transfer_bytes` to the dedup `SiteKey`. Without the latter, a
  hot weight panel and an incidental activation load that share span, op, dtype,
  innermost size and memory space collapsed into one hint whose occurrence count
  named neither. The clause is omitted when an outer dim is symbolic.
- `tests/ut/ir/verifier/test_perf_hint_tile_innermost_dim.py`: replace
  `test_cube_memory_space_not_flagged_a5`, which asserted the incorrect premise
  and whose fixture never reached the code path it described, with
  `test_gm_to_mat_load_is_flagged_a5` (the #2309 regression guard, including the
  volume clause) and `test_chip_internal_move_not_flagged_a5` (the half of the
  old rule that survives: `tile.move` is never inspected).
- `docs/en/dev/passes/92-diagnostics.md`, `docs/zh/dev/passes/92-diagnostics.md`:
  document the corrected scope and the volume clause, note that kernels staging
  many small GM→Mat panels will see more lines, and regenerate the example block
  from a real run.

## Hint volume

Measured across the example corpus, comparing hints on cube spaces (new) against
Vec (unchanged): the whole of `examples/beginner`, `examples/intermediate` and
`examples/advanced` gains **3** hints, all in `intermediate/05_assemble.py`, a
teaching kernel that deliberately stages 16×16 panels. The tuned cube kernels —
`beginner/05_matmul`, `intermediate/01_fused_linear`, `intermediate/04_matmul_acc`,
`advanced/01_split_k`, `advanced/02_auto_tile_matmul` — and all five
`examples/models` kernels, including both attention models, stay silent.

No absolute volume gate was added: an absolute byte cutoff would be invented
policy, and the check cannot see loop trip counts.

## Verification

- `cmake --build build --parallel 32`: exit 0, `Built target pypto_core`.
- `python -m pytest tests/ut/ir/verifier/test_perf_hint_tile_innermost_dim.py
  tests/ut/pass/test_diagnostic_instrument.py -q`: exit 0, 30 passed.
- `python -m pytest tests/ut tests/lint -q -n 8 --maxprocesses 8`: exit 0,
  9451 passed, 3 skipped.

All three ran through the push transaction's validation runner at the pushed
commit, on a checkout rebased onto `upstream/main`.

title: feat(distributed): add pld.tensor.remote_store for computed values
body:
## Summary

A value computed inside a kernel lives on-core and lowers to a `TileType`, which made it unpushable cross-rank from both directions: `pld.tensor.put` requires a GM source, and `pld.tile.remote_store` rejects the tensor-level value a `@pl.jit` kernel actually holds. Pushing a computed result meant storing it back to global memory and pushing from there — an extra round trip, with the store and the transfer landing on different pipes with nothing ordering them.

This adds `pld.tensor.remote_store`, the tensor-level twin of `pld.tile.remote_store`: same four arguments, same single `pto.tstore`, one IR level up. `ConvertTensorToTileOps` lowers it 1:1 (mirroring `tensor.aiv_shard -> tile.aiv_shard`), so a computed value now goes straight from on-core memory to the peer's window. The short form `pld.remote_store` dispatches between the two levels on its operand, so user code reads the same at either level.

Resolves the need described in #2349. That issue proposed overloading `pld.tensor.put` on the kind of its `src`; this implements the alternative the issue itself lists — see *Design note* below.

## Changes

- `src/ir/op/distributed/remote_store.cpp`: register `pld.tensor.remote_store`; share one contract between both forms covering target/peer/offsets/dtype, the 2-D push shape, static bounds, and `atomic`. Each form's src-type diagnostic names the sibling entry point, so an author writing at the wrong level is pointed at the right op.
- `src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp`: lower `pld.tensor.remote_store` 1:1 via `RegisterSimple`. Its `InputSpaceReq{Vec}` makes the op **total** on its argument surface — `BridgeInputSpaces` only rewrites `TensorType` operands, so a computed value passes through as a tile keeping its space, while a `src` still resident in GM is auto-bridged with a natural `tile.load`. Also rejects a tile `src` on `pld.tensor.put` at the op the author wrote, replacing an error that named the internal `pld.tile.put`.
- `src/backend/common/pto_ops_distributed.cpp`: emit `pto.tstore`'s `atomicType` for `AtomicType.Add`, under the same bf16/Ascend910B guard `tile.store` carries. Emitted only for `kAdd`, so plain pushes stay byte-identical.
- `src/ir/op/distributed/comm_op_utils.h`: add the shared push bounds check and atomic-value check (`put` now uses the latter too).
- `python/pypto/{ir,language}/...`: IR builders and DSL wrappers for the new op; `atomic` on the tile form; `pld.remote_store` becomes a type dispatcher instead of a re-export.
- `docs/{en,zh}/`: document the new op, the namespacing rationale, atomic semantics, and the bounds rule; both dev references were condensed alongside the additions.

### Behavior changes beyond the new op

- **`pld.tile.remote_store` gains `atomic`.** `pto.tstore` already accepts `atomicType` and `tile.store` already emits it; `atomic=AtomicType.Add` makes the push a combine (`peer_region += src`). This is what an all-to-all combine needs to sum every rank's contribution in place.
- **Both forms now bounds-check the push.** `remote_store` carries no transfer `shape` of its own to clamp against, so an oversized or badly-offset push silently overwrote the peer's neighbouring region; the `remote_load` mirror already checked this. Statically out-of-bounds pushes that previously compiled now fail with a message naming the dimension.
- **`pld.tile.remote_store` declares `set_input_memory(0, {Vec, Acc})`** (matching `tile.store`) in place of `no_memory_spec`, so `InferTileMemorySpace` can pull a producer into a legal space. This records a demand; it does not reject.
- The push contract admits an N-D source whose leading dims are all `1`, because the deducer also runs *before* `FlattenTileNdTo2D` collapses N-D tiles. Only a leading extent > 1 is rejected — that would fold into the row count and overrun the target.

No migration is required: every existing call site keeps its meaning, and non-atomic `remote_store` codegen is unchanged.

## Design note

`pld.tensor.put` is deliberately **not** overloaded on the kind of its `src`. Doing so would make five of its arguments (`src_offsets`, `shape`, `atomic`, `chunk_rows`/`chunk_cols`, `pipeline`) conditionally meaningless depending on how the value was produced upstream — a property invisible at the call site — and it contradicts the documented rule that a `pld` namespace encodes the IR level an op lives at. `put` remains the GM→GM bulk (TPUT) path, which stages through a bounce buffer and is therefore not bounded by what fits on-core; `remote_store` moves what is already on-core, in one write.

## Verification

Run in this worktree at the pushed commit (`7c99550d`), rebased onto `upstream/main`:

- `cmake --build build --parallel`: exit 0
- `python -m pytest tests/ut/ --ignore=tests/ut/runtime --ignore=tests/ut/core/test_error.py -n auto --maxprocesses 8`: exit 0 — **8846 passed, 4 skipped**
- `ruff check python/ tests/`; `ruff format --check python/ tests/`: exit 0
- `clang-format --dry-run --Werror` on the 5 touched C++ files: exit 0
- `tests/lint/clang_tidy.py --diff-base HEAD`: exit 0
- `markdownlint-cli2 --config tests/lint/.markdownlint.yaml "docs/**/*.md"`: 0 issues
- `tests/lint/{check_headers,check_op_name_literals,check_no_broad_raises,check_docs_en_zh_parity,check_docs_nav,check_english_only,check_docs_symbol_coverage}.py`: all exit 0

New coverage: 42 tests across the deducer (`tests/ut/ir/test_distributed_ops.py`), printer round-trip (`tests/ut/ir/parser/test_remote_store.py`), the conversion pass (`tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.py`), and codegen (`tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_distributed_pto_codegen.py`) — including that the computed-value path emits `pto.tstore` with no `pto.comm.tput` and no staging tile.

**Two exclusions above are pre-existing environment failures, not regressions**, and reproduce identically on `upstream/main`: `tests/ut/runtime/` fails at import with `GLIBCXX_3.4.30 not found` from the prebuilt `simpler` module, and `tests/ut/core/test_error.py`'s `(?:^|/)(?:src|include/pypto)/` regex matches this conda interpreter's own `/usr/local/src/conda/python-3.13.5/...` frames.

**Not run:** `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_remote_store.py::test_tensor_level_push_of_computed_value` — the ST added here needs 2 devices. Its program was verified to compile end-to-end through the full pipeline, but its numeric golden has not executed.

title: fix(ir): attribute synthesized tile ops to their own source spans
body:
## Summary

Two InCore lowering passes stamped the enclosing function's span on the tile ops
they synthesize, so those `Call` nodes reported the `def` line instead of the
statement they came from. `FlattenTileNdTo2D` is the dominant one — it hands
`func->span_` to `TransformBody` and reuses it for every node it re-creates, and
`ResolveBackendOpLayouts` then inherits the coarsened spans for the
`tile.reshape` ops it inserts. `ConvertTensorToTileOps` has the same defect on a
smaller scale, on the entry `tile.load` it synthesizes per converted tensor
parameter and the exit `tile.store` it synthesizes per returned tile.

Each synthesized op is now attributed to the node that motivated it: the
statement being rewritten, the parameter an entry load reads, or the `return` an
exit store serves. Only nodes that genuinely belong to the whole function (the
rebuilt `Function` and its body `SeqStmts`) keep the function span. Nothing
about IR structure, types, or op selection changes — only which source location
each op carries.

This matters beyond diagnostic quality. Every consumer that reads a span off a
`Call` was degraded: `CHECK_SPAN` / `INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN` failures raised by any
later pass, IR trace reports, and MLIR `loc()` in the generated `.pto`. It also
produced an outright wrong result in one place — the PH001 perf hint
deduplicates by source site, so an entry load and a loop load on two different
source lines merged into a single `(2 occurrences at this source location)` hint
describing two unrelated transfers.

Measured over post-pipeline IR, counting `Call` spans nested inside their own
statement. `PagedAttention` was measured on both builds; the other two were
measured only after the fix.

| Program | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_pto_codegen_paged_attn.py` `PagedAttention` | 34/99 | 99/99 |
| `test_pto_codegen_paged_attn.py` `UnalignedPagedAttention` | not measured | 20/20 |
| Tensor-level InCore kernel (entry-load / exit-store path) | not measured | 9/9 |

Per-pass measurement on `PagedAttention` locates the loss precisely: spans stay
100% precise through `ConvertTensorToTileOps`, drop to 2/46 at
`FlattenTileNdTo2D`, and lose a further 22 at `ResolveBackendOpLayouts`.

## Changes

- `src/ir/transforms/flatten_tile_nd_to_2d/rewrite.cpp`: the rewrite loop binds
  `span` from the statement it is rewriting, so every re-created op and the
  batch-matmul / transpose lowering helpers it delegates to inherit the precise
  location. The function-span parameter became unused and was removed;
  `Rewrite` still spans the body `SeqStmts` wrapper with the function span.
- `src/ir/transforms/convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp`: the entry `tile.load`
  carries the parameter declaration's span; the exit `tile.store` and the `Out`
  param it writes carry the `return`'s span. Body-op conversion already threaded
  `call->span_` and is unchanged.
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_flatten_tile_nd_to_2d.py`,
  `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.py`: regression tests
  pinning the attribution. Both were confirmed to fail against the pre-fix build.
- `tests/ut/ir/verifier/test_perf_hint_tile_innermost_dim.py`:
  `test_dedup_collapses_repeated_site_a3` asserted the `(N occurrences)` collapse
  that only the coarsened spans produced — its `pl.range(4)` loop is not
  unrolled, so there is one transfer per site and the collapse it observed was
  the two unrelated loads described above. That assertion is dropped; the test
  keeps its per-source-site distinctness check, which this fix is what makes
  meaningful. **Follow-up:** no test now covers the dedup collapse path itself. A
  `pl.unroll(4)` variant does exercise it correctly (4 genuinely identical loads
  at one source line collapse to one counted hit, entry load staying separate) if
  that coverage is wanted back.
- `docs/en/dev/02-error-handling.md`, `docs/zh/dev/02-error-handling.md`: a
  "Span attribution in passes" section documenting the rule, since the same
  `func->span_` shortcut is available in every pass.

## Verification

Run at the pushed head `b431a84`, after rebase onto `upstream/main`:

- `cmake --build build --parallel`: exit 0, no errors or warnings.
- `pytest tests/ut/ -n auto --maxprocesses 8`: exit 0, 9442 passed, 3 skipped.
- `ctest` (in `build/`): exit 0, 1/1 passed.
- `tests/lint/{check_headers,check_english_only,check_docs_en_zh_parity,check_docs_nav,check_op_name_literals,check_no_broad_raises,check_docs_symbol_coverage}.py`:
  exit 0 each.
- `clang-format --dry-run --Werror` on both changed `.cpp` files: exit 0.
- `ruff check tests/` and `ruff format --check`: exit 0, 89 files already formatted.

Regression coverage was validated in both directions: the two new span tests
were run against a build with the fix reverted and both failed, then passed with
it restored.

title: fix(codegen): compile loop carries seeded by a literal
body:
## Summary

An Orchestration loop that carries a scalar seeded from a constant failed to compile, aborting with `Internal error: ForStmt iter_arg initValue must be a variable, got non-variable expr`. Writing `acc: pl.Scalar[pl.INT64] = 0` before a `pl.range` loop that accumulates into `acc` is legal DSL and traces fine, so the failure surfaced only at codegen and named an IR-internal concept the user never wrote. Two independent defects combined to produce it, and both are fixed here. Loop carries can now be seeded from a literal directly, instead of peeling the first iteration into an `if`/`else` phi to bind a real variable.

## Changes

- `src/codegen/orchestration/`: orchestration codegen no longer requires an `IterArg::initValue_` to be a `Var`. The IR permits any expression there — `docs/en/dev/ir/02-types.md` uses a `ConstInt` init in its canonical loop example, and `Simplify` propagates a constant scalar binding into the iter_arg — so a legal program was reaching an `INTERNAL_CHECK`. The init expression is now emitted directly (`int64_t acc__rv_v1 = 0;`), and a carry the body never rebinds aliases straight to that expression. The one path that still needs the init to *name* something is the `ArrayType` carry copy-in, which indexes it slot-by-slot; that keeps an internal check with a specific message.
- `python/pypto/language/parser/`: an annotated scalar assignment no longer binds a Var to a constant of a different dtype. A bare int literal parses as the untyped placeholder `ConstInt(v, INDEX)`, so `acc: pl.Scalar[pl.INT64] = 0` produced `AssignStmt(Var[INT64], ConstInt[INDEX])` and violated `AssignTypeSymmetry`. The mismatch stayed invisible until `Simplify` moved the constant into a loop's iter_arg init, where `TypeCheck` reported a carry dtype mismatch. The parser now re-stamps the placeholder with the annotated dtype.
- `examples/models/05_paged_attention_batch.py`: drops the peel workaround and its comment, which stated that a loop carry "must be seeded from a bound variable". `max_bn` is now seeded from `0` and the loop runs over the full batch range. The two forms are equivalent (`bn_b >= 0`, so folding batch 0 into the `max` changes nothing).
- `tests/ut/`: three regression tests — a rebinding literal-seeded carry and a trivial (never-rebound) one in the orchestration codegen tests, and an `AssignTypeSymmetry` test pinning the annotated-literal dtype.
- `docs/`: the orchestration codegen doc states the `IterArg` init contract, in both `en` and `zh`.

Only the codegen defect is reachable without verification enabled, which is why the original report showed just the internal error. Both fixes are needed for the program to compile under the default `PYPTO_VERIFY_LEVEL=roundtrip` the test suite runs with.

No interface change and no migration step. The peel idiom remains valid; it is simply no longer required. `examples/models/09_paged_attention_spmd.py` still uses it and was left alone.

## Verification

- `cmake --build build --parallel && python -m pytest tests/ut/ -n auto --maxprocesses 8 -q`: exit 0 — 9499 passed, 3 skipped. Run by the push transaction's validation runner against the pushed commit.
- `ctest -j8` (in `build/`): exit 0 — 1/1 passed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed Python files: exit 0.
- `tests/lint/check_english_only.py`, `check_headers.py`, `check_no_broad_raises.py`, `check_op_name_literals.py`, `check_docs_nav.py`, `check_docs_en_zh_parity.py`: exit 0 each.
- End-to-end: `python examples/models/05_paged_attention_batch.py` compiles through the Default pipeline (Ascend910B) and emits `int64_t max_bn__rv_v2 = 0;` in the generated orchestration C++.

title: feat(ir): warn when rebinding an Out param drops the write (#2352)
body:
## TL;DR

- **Bug (#2352):** `out = pl.add(a, b)` on an `Out`/`InOut` parameter writes nothing. It rebinds the Python name, compiles, runs, and hands the caller back uninitialised memory — with no diagnostic from the parser, the passes, codegen, PTOAS, or the runtime.
- **Fix:** report it as an `OutParamWriteDropped` warning naming the parameter and the `out[:] = <expr>` form that does write. The compiler does **not** synthesize the write — see below for why it cannot.
- **Detection is data-flow, not syntax:** a value can reach the parameter without naming it, and that is a genuine write-through that must stay silent.
- **Wiring:** a `DiagnosticCheck` at `DiagnosticPhase::PrePipeline`, alongside `UnusedVariable`; opt-out via the existing `disabled_diagnostics` set.

Supersedes #2359, which tried to desugar the bare assignment into a whole-tensor write. That approach was withdrawn — the reasoning is below, since it is the main design decision here.

## Why the compiler does not write it for you

The obvious fix is to rewrite `out = <expr>` into `out = pl.assemble(out, <expr>, [0, 0])`. That does not work, and the reason is a pre-existing property of the IR rather than anything this PR introduces.

`tensor.assemble` has no codegen of its own. It survives lowering only when `ConvertTensorToTileOps` can fuse its value operand into a `tile.store`. When the value is an already-materialised tensor, nothing fuses and the op reaches codegen unlowered. On `main`, both of these fail identically:

```text
out[0:256, 0:64] = <tensor var>          -> No codegen registered for operation: tensor.assemble
pl.assemble(out, <tensor var>, [0, 0])   -> No codegen registered for operation: tensor.assemble
```

An inserted whole-tensor write is therefore unlowerable for exactly the values a rebind tends to carry: an already-materialised tensor, a user-function result, a distributed collective. #2359 demonstrated this concretely — desugaring turned 30 previously-passing `dist-system-tests` cases red with that error.

Writing through the parameter has to stay the user's explicit act. The compiler's job here is to say so, loudly.

## How the check decides

A syntactic "does the value mention the parameter?" test is wrong, because a value can reach the parameter through a loop carry:

```python
for col, (d,) in pl.range(0, n, chunk, init_values=(data,)):
    d = pl.store(local, [0, col], d)
    staged = pl.yield_(d)
data = pld.tensor.allreduce(staged, signal, ...)
```

`staged` never names `data`, yet it *is* `data` threaded through the carry, so the rebind is a real write-through. This is the shape in the ring-allreduce InCore kernels, and it is covered by a regression test.

The check therefore taints each `Out`/`InOut` parameter forward through the function's definition graph and reports a rebind only when its value shares nothing with that taint. Every approximation leans the same way — a Var with several definitions accumulates their union, and loop/branch results union all of a region's init and yielded values — so an imprecise edge can only ever *suppress* a warning, never invent one on correct code.

All parameters are tainted in one shared pass over one shared reverse index, each carrying its own bit in a `uint64_t` mask, so the analysis is linear in the size of the function body rather than `O(params × body)`.

### Deliberate false negative

A value that merely *reads* the parameter — `out = pl.add(out, b)` — is tainted too and is **not** reported, even though it also drops the write. Telling "reads the parameter" from "writes through the parameter" needs per-op write semantics the operator registry does not record (`pld.tensor.allreduce` is `.no_memory_spec()`, for one). A false warning on correct collective code costs more than a missed one. This is documented in the code, the docs, and a test.

## Behaviour

| Code | Warns |
| ---- | ----- |
| `out = pl.add(a, b)` (the #2352 repro) | yes |
| `out = tmp` (freshly computed local) | yes |
| `acc = pl.add(a, b)` on an `InOut` parameter | yes |
| `out[:] = pl.add(a, b)` | no |
| `out[0:64, 0:128] = a` | no |
| `out = pl.assemble(out, <expr>, [0, 0])` | no |
| `out = pl.store(local, offset, out)` | no |
| `data = pld.tensor.allreduce(staged, sig)` (loop-carry alias) | no |
| `out = pl.add(out, b)` (reads only — see above) | no |

```text
[warning] [OutParamWriteDropped] (pipeline_input) Assigning to Out parameter 'out'
in function 'main' rebinds the name only — the caller's buffer is never written.
Use 'out[:] = <expr>' to write the whole tensor, or 'out[<slices>] = <expr>' for
a sub-window. at repro.py:12:9
```

The check is scoped to shaped (Tensor / Tile) parameters, because the suggested remedy has no scalar spelling.

## Changes

| Area | File |
| ---- | ---- |
| Check | `src/ir/verifier/warning_out_param_write_dropped.cpp` (new) |
| Registration | `include/pypto/ir/verifier/diagnostic_check_registry.h`, `src/ir/verifier/diagnostic_check_registry.cpp`, `CMakeLists.txt` |
| Bindings + stubs | `python/bindings/modules/passes.cpp`, `python/pypto/pypto_core/passes.pyi` |
| Tests | `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_out_param_write_dropped_warning.py` (new, 17 cases) |
| Docs | `docs/en/dev/language/00-python_syntax.md`, `docs/zh/dev/language/00-python_syntax.md` |

## Validation

- Full CI green at `9e90e767`, including `dist-system-tests` — the job #2359 broke, and the one that had been skipped on the previous commit because `clang-tidy` gated it.
- Local full UT suite: 9438 passed; the failure set is identical to the `origin/main` baseline (19, all local runtime/simpler environment issues).
- 17 new unit tests: the reported cases, every write-through spelling, plain-tensor and distributed loop-carry aliasing, the documented false negative, multi-parameter taint isolation, and the registration/opt-out wiring.
- `clang-tidy` clean on all three touched C++ files; `clang-format`, `ruff`, `ruff format`, and `pyright` clean.
- Verified the check is silent across the repository's own code: zero warnings over the full codegen and IR unit-test suites.

## Not in this PR

The English guide is 1,147 lines against the repository's 500-line documentation limit, and was already 1,085 lines at the base commit. Splitting it means re-pointing at least eight references across both language trees, several with deep anchors, so it is tracked separately as #2365 rather than bundled here.

title: fix(language): forward pad_value through pl.slice
body:
## Summary

`pl.tensor.slice` and `pl.tile.slice` both accept `pad_value`, but the unified `pl.slice` dispatcher never declared it, so the parameter was unreachable through the facade on either path — `pl.slice(x, shape, offset, pad_value=0)` raised `TypeError: slice() got an unexpected keyword argument 'pad_value'`, and callers had to drop to the level-specific spelling to set a padding mode. `pl.slice` now declares and forwards it.

This needs no cross-path guard. Unlike `clamp`, which only a Tensor can honour, `pad_value` exists at both levels, so forwarding is the whole fix.

Forwarding alone would have degraded a diagnostic, so the second half of the change repairs that — see below. Callers that omit `pad_value` are unaffected, and the Tensor-only `clamp` rejection on the Tile path is unchanged.

## Changes

- `python/pypto/language/op/unified_ops.py` — `pl.slice` declares `pad_value` and forwards it on both dispatch branches, in the same positional slot both callees already use: after `drop_dims`, before the Tensor-only `clamp`. An AST sweep of `tests/`, `examples/`, `python/`, and `docs/` found all 253 existing `pl.slice` call sites pass exactly three positional arguments, and the three that use `clamp` spell it as a keyword, so moving `clamp` one slot rebinds nothing.

- `python/pypto/ir/utils.py` — new `caller_warning_stacklevel()`, which walks out to the first stack frame outside the `pypto` package.

- `python/pypto/language/op/tensor_ops.py`, `python/pypto/language/op/tile_ops.py` — the two `slice` "pad_value has no effect" warnings take their `stacklevel` from that helper instead of a literal `2`.

  A literal `2` names the *immediate* caller, which was always user code before — and is the dispatcher once `pl.slice` forwards. The consequence is worse than a misleading filename: Python's default filter dedupes on `(text, category, lineno)` recorded in the frame named by `stacklevel`, so a fixed library line collapses every distinct call site onto one record. Measured on the unfixed branch, three distinct user call sites produced **1** warning instead of 3 — a kernel with twenty misused `pl.slice` calls would have seen one warning pointing into `unified_ops.py` and nineteen silent drops. Walking to the first non-`pypto` frame restores one warning per real call site and stays correct through any depth of forwarding.

- `tests/ut/language/test_unified_ops.py` — `TestUnifiedSlicePadValue` (15 tests): forwarding on both paths, the `0`/`inf` literal sugars, positional binding, `pad_value` alongside `clamp`, `None`/omitted staying byte-identical to the previous IR, and both DSL-parser paths (the parser reaches the wrapper dynamically, so kwarg resolution is a separate risk from the direct call).

  Every forwarding test pairs its structural match against the explicit `pl.tensor.*` / `pl.tile.*` call with a negative assertion that the no-`pad_value` IR differs, so the test fails rather than passing vacuously if both sides drop the kwarg. Two tests cover the warning defect specifically — attribution and per-call-site dedup — because `pytest.warns` checks neither `filename` nor `lineno` and installs `simplefilter("always")`, which defeats the dedup it needs to observe. Both were confirmed to fail against a reverted `stacklevel=2`.

## Verification

Run against the pushed commit `12e1cfcd`, rebased onto `main`:

- `ruff check` (5 changed files): exit 0, all checks passed
- `ruff format --check` (5 changed files): exit 0, already formatted
- `cmake --build build --parallel`: exit 0
- `pytest tests/ut/language/test_unified_ops.py`: exit 0, 160 passed
- `pytest tests/ut/ -n auto --maxprocesses 8`: exit 0, **9511 passed, 3 skipped** in 2:40

Separately, the two warning-regression tests were run against a reverted
`stacklevel=2` to confirm they are not vacuous: 4 failed, with the dedup test
reporting `assert 1 == 3`.

No behaviour change for existing callers, no interface removal, and no
migration step.

title: feat(ir): align GM-store destination dtype gates with the pinned toolchain
body:
## Summary

Two GM-store destination-dtype gates were each wrong in opposite directions, and
both are corrected here against the pinned toolchain (ptoas v0.57, pto-isa
`83d01313`).

**Missing gate.** A bf16 atomic-add is only honoured by the A2/A3 store pipe, and
that check lived in the PTO `tile.store` emitter — so it covered one of six
atomic sites. The distributed paths had no backend guard at all: a bf16 remote
atomic-add on Ascend950 compiled through PyPTO and failed later on a pto-isa
`static_assert`, in generated `.pto` the user never wrote. Nothing downstream
catches it, since ptoas' `TPutOp::verify` checks element-type agreement and
shapes but never the atomic dtype. These are not separate mechanisms — pto-isa's
comm `TPut` lands each chunk through `TSTORE_IMPL<..., AtomicAdd>` and
`remote_store` emits a `pto.tstore` directly — so one `AtomicAddDtypeValid`
property verifier now governs all six, rejecting at pipeline input with the
user's own source span.

**Over-strict gate.** `SupportsAccToGmDtype(Ascend950)` omitted BF16 while
claiming to "mirror ptoas exactly". Both pinned layers accept
`i32/f32/f16/bf16` as a non-quant A5 acc-tstore destination, and pto-isa's a5 ST
suite stores into a bf16 destination directly, so `AccToGmStoreValid` was
rejecting an A5 cube matmul that the toolchain accepts and forcing a needless
`pl.cast` through the vector unit.

**Behavior change.** On Ascend950: a bf16 atomic-add is now a PyPTO error at
pipeline input rather than a downstream failure, and a bf16 Acc→GM store now
compiles instead of being rejected. Ascend910B is unaffected, as is every
non-bf16 hardware atomic-add dtype. Because the atomic check moved out of
codegen it is now skippable under `PYPTO_VERIFY_LEVEL=none` — the same trade the
sibling `AccToGmStoreValid` already makes.

## Changes

- `src/ir/verifier/verify_atomic_add_dtype.cpp` (new): flags an atomic-add whose
  GM destination dtype the target backend's store pipe cannot combine, keyed on
  `BackendHandler::SupportsBf16AtomicAdd`. Covers `tile.store`,
  `tensor.assemble`, `pld.tensor.put`, `pld.tile.put`,
  `pld.tensor.remote_store` and `pld.tile.remote_store`. Modelled on
  `verify_acc_to_gm_store.cpp`: skips when no backend is configured, and is
  Submit-aware via `SubmitToCallView`.
- `IRProperty::AtomicAddDtypeValid`: listed in `GetStructuralProperties()` and
  `GetVerifiedProperties()` rather than produced by a pass. Nothing here depends
  on lowering — the atomic kwarg and the destination dtype are in the user's own
  IR — so `PassPipeline` verifies it at `pipeline_input`.
- `src/backend/common/pto_ops_memory.cpp`: the ad-hoc bf16 guard in the
  `tile.store` emitter is deleted, leaving one predicate for every atomic site.
- `src/ir/op/distributed/put.cpp`: `ValidatePutContract` now calls the shared
  `comm_op::ValidateAtomicAddDtype` that `remote_store` already uses, so the
  backend-neutral hardware allow-list (fp32/bf16/fp16/int32/int16/int8) cannot
  drift between the two distributed paths. This closes a second gap on put: an
  INT64 remote atomic-add used to compile.
- `include/pypto/backend/950/backend_950_handler.h`: `SupportsAccToGmDtype` gains
  BF16, matching both pinned layers. The hook stays per-backend because the two
  arches' sets are independent facts about each pinned target.
- Comment corrections: the `SupportsBf16AtomicAdd` docs cited the a5
  `SetAtomicAdd<T>` `static_assert` as evidence that bf16 atomic-add is
  unsupported there. That helper lists `bfloat16_t` on both arches, so it is no
  evidence either way — and misreading it is what produced the wrong conclusion
  about the neighbouring Acc→GM table. The real evidence is the pinned ST suite:
  a2a3 runs `tstore_acc2gm` case 60 with `atomicType=1` into a bf16 destination,
  while a5 runs that identical case with `atomicType=0`.
- Cross-layer wiring: `ir_property.h/.cpp`, the `verifier.h` factory,
  `PropertyVerifierRegistry`, `CMakeLists.txt`, the nanobind enum, and the
  `passes.pyi` stub.

## Tests

- `tests/ut/ir/verifier/test_atomic_add_dtype.py` (new, 22 cases): bf16 rejected
  on Ascend950 and accepted on Ascend910B across four authoring surfaces, fp32
  accepted on both profiles, plain non-atomic bf16 unaffected, plus two
  end-to-end pipeline cases.
- `tests/ut/jit/test_split_k.py`: a cube matmul stored straight into a bf16
  target, parametrized over `a2a3` / `a5`, asserting a `loc=acc` store into a
  bf16 partition view. Deliberately non-atomic so it isolates the Acc→GM
  whitelist from the still-A2/A3-only atomic gate.
- Deducer negatives in `tests/ut/ir/test_distributed_ops.py`; a bf16-put positive
  in the distributed codegen tests; the pre-existing A5 store test retargeted
  from the codegen call to the pipeline run.

## Verification

- `cmake --build build --parallel`: exit 0, no errors or new warnings.
- `pytest tests/ut/ -n auto --maxprocesses 8`: **9524 passed, 3 skipped**. Run by
  the push transaction's validation runner at the exact pushed OID
  (`e645a4da`).
- Focused pass ahead of the broader suite (verifier, distributed ops,
  distributed codegen, PTO codegen ops), same runner.
- `pre-commit`: all hooks pass (clang-format, cpplint, ruff check/format,
  pyright, markdownlint, check-docs-en-zh-parity, check-op-name-literals).
- `ctest` in `build/`: 1/1 passed.

No device or CA-model run: the added coverage is structural, and the existing
device coverage for atomic-add (`tests/st/`) is unchanged by this range. The
Ascend950 conclusions are read off the pinned toolchain sources cited above
rather than measured on hardware.

title: docs: split the oversized Python syntax guides
body:
### Component

Documentation

### Description

`docs/en/dev/language/00-python_syntax.md` and its Chinese mirror are both more than twice the 500-line limit in `.claude/rules/documentation-length.md`, and have been for a while — this is not caused by any single change:

```bash
$ wc -l docs/en/dev/language/00-python_syntax.md docs/zh/dev/language/00-python_syntax.md
 1147 docs/en/dev/language/00-python_syntax.md
 1083 docs/zh/dev/language/00-python_syntax.md
```

The rule prescribes splitting anything over 700 lines into focused topic documents. The directory already has the right shape for that — `01-external-kernels.md` (162 lines) is a focused sibling — so the split would move self-contained topics (parameter directions and writing outputs, scopes, control flow, tasks and manual dependencies, directives) into numbered siblings and leave `00-python_syntax.md` as the overview plus an index.

The reason this needs its own issue rather than riding along with a feature PR: the file is referenced from at least eight places across both language trees, including `mkdocs.yml` nav, `docs/{en,zh}/dev/language/index.md`, `docs/zh/dev/ir/index.md`, `docs/en/dev/passes/31-init_memref.md`, `docs/zh/dev/codegen/00-pto_codegen.md`, and several `docs/zh/user/language/` pages — some with deep anchors (`#手工依赖原语`, `#under-the-ptoas-memory-planner`, `#槽位`). Splitting means re-pointing every one of those, in both languages, without breaking anchors.

### Additional Context

Raised during review of #2362, which added a section to this file and was flagged for growing an already oversized document. That PR deliberately did not attempt the split.

title: feat(runtime): add submit task timing slots
body:
For L3 kernels, PyPTO’s current benchmark runtime cannot avoid including launch skew or all-rank barrier time in the reported device_wall duration. This makes it difficult to measure the actual payload time.
Simpler already provides selective task timing slots. This change exposes that capability through PyPTO’s `pl.submit` and `pl.spmd_submit` APIs via `timing_slot=0..15`, allowing users to bracket only the target device tasks and read the corresponding `task_slot_<N>` trace span.

- Adds `timing_slot=<literal 0..15>` to `pl.submit` and `pl.spmd_submit`.
- Lowers the selected slot to runtime `set_task_timing_slot()`.
- Emits one device trace span per completed slot: `simpler_run.runner_run.device_wall.task_slot_<N>`.
- Documents the API in English and Chinese.
- Adds parser and orchestration codegen coverage.

See [allgather_mm.py#L366](https://github.com/Shenggan/pypto-ccfusion/blob/acf7fa3df99d454435791ecf02e652e0a89f3476/pypto-l3/allgather_mm.py#L366) and [allgather_mm.py#L435](https://github.com/Shenggan/pypto-ccfusion/blob/acf7fa3df99d454435791ecf02e652e0a89f3476/pypto-l3/allgather_mm.py#L435) to see how to use task timing slots.

title: feat(distributed): add deferred task completion waits
body:
## Summary

A blocking `pld.system.wait` occupies its AIV until a remote signal is ready. If a task graph fills the available AIVs with waiters before the publisher can run, those waiters can prevent forward progress.

This PR adds `pld.system.defer_wait`. A dedicated waiter task registers `signal >= expected` and returns from the kernel, allowing the physical AIV to be reused. Its scheduler `TaskId` remains incomplete until the condition is satisfied, so continuation tasks use the existing `deps=[wait_tid]` mechanism.

This reuses the deferred-completion API already available in the pinned Simpler runtime. It does not modify Simpler, change the runtime gitlink, or alter the existing blocking `pld.system.wait`.

## Changes

- Add the `pld.system.defer_wait` DSL and IR operation.
- Add argument, type, range, and comparison validation.
- Validate deferred waiters as dedicated pure-AIV tasks and reject unsafe continuation work inside the waiter kernel.
- Lower deferred registrations through a checked adapter to Simpler's `AsyncCtx`.
- Add the hidden raw dispatch context only to generated kernels that use deferred completion.
- Reuse ordinary `TaskId` dependencies; no new dependency type or `completion_deps` API is introduced.
- Add English and Chinese documentation.
- Add unit, simulator, and onboard coverage.

## Notes

- V1 supports `WaitCmp.Ge` on an INT32 distributed counter.
- A deferred waiter does not resume after the condition is satisfied; continuation work must be placed in a dependent task.
- Deferred counters use non-negative, monotonically increasing values.

## Verification

- Build and affected unit tests passed.
- The full unit suite introduced no new failures.
- A2/A3 and A5 simulator tests passed.
- A2/A3 onboard tests passed, including AIV saturation, repeated epochs, and already-ready counter reuse.
