title: feat(ir): add MX quantization and GM-staged matmul
body:
## Summary

- Add the public `pl.quant_mx` API for Ascend950 MX block-32 dynamic quantization, with `MX_A_ZZ` / `MX_B_NN` layouts and MXFP8 / MXFP4 outputs.
- Lower `tile.tquant_mx` to destination-passing grouped TQUANT and X-to-ZZ TMOV operations with explicit scratch and output tiles, so memory planning sees every simultaneous lifetime.
- Support `quant_mx` feeding `matmul_mx` through separate AIV and AIC kernels: quantized data and FP8E8M0 scales are staged in GM, then scale backing tensors are exposed to PTOAS as packed rank-5 MX views.
- Extend the scale-address pass to InCore/AIC/AIV variants and reject unsupported MX tensor consumers explicitly.
- Update the official remote PTOAS toolchain pin from v0.57 to v0.58. Keep the compatibility rewrite narrowly limited to v0.58 grouped MX TQUANT output and the runtime's pinned PTO-ISA.

## Known limitation

`quant_mx` and `matmul_mx` are not yet supported in the same InCore mixed task. Use separate AIV/AIC kernels and stage both the quantized data and FP8E8M0 scales through GM. Automatic mixed-kernel data-plus-scale transport is deferred to a follow-up PR.

title: [Feature] Expose pto.trecip high-precision mode through pl.recip
body:
## Background

In pypto-lib PR #937, `models/deepseek_v4_flash_dspark/decode_sparse_attn_swa.py`
shows input-sensitive precision failures on `a5sim` when the TP1 output projection
computes the INT8 dequantization scale as:

```python
g_sq_row = pl.div(g_scale_num, g_amax)
scale_dq = pl.recip(g_sq_row)
```

This lowers to default-precision `pto.tdiv` followed by default-precision
`pto.trecip`.

Two A5Sim CI executions at the same PR head produced different failure ratios:

- 46,271 / 524,288 mismatches (8.8255%, allowed 0.5%):
  https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-lib/actions/runs/31683238535/job/94397842201
- 2,927 / 524,288 mismatches (0.5583%, allowed 0.5%):
  https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-lib/actions/runs/31683238535/job/94404800132

The variation follows the randomly generated inputs; it is not evidence that
identical `TRECIP` executions are nondeterministic.

Rewriting the algebraically equivalent dequantization scale as:

```python
scale_dq = pl.mul(g_amax, 1.0 / 127.0)
```

emits `pto.tmuls` and passes A5Sim:

https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-lib/actions/runs/31687734713/job/94407727562

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `a3076021bdd17e805eb0c4c189f1f65318b952a9` (PR #937 merge commit; head `81fe974c55de24a14573207562579ad5983351e8`) |
| pypto | `7d8f90f456d30a495db0d0d0eb27396121fcae33` |
| simpler | `3165cc89b6ea6b58a0bc01cbec2d5f72f2029c35` |
| ptoas | `0.57` |
| pto-isa | `83d01313d9bfc247c4b7c8bcf969d1019f0d106f` |
| CANN | Not used by A5Sim |
| Host | Linux (aarch64) |

All components matched the versions pinned by PyPTO.

The public reproduction sources and their local helpers
(`decode_sparse_attn_swa.py`, `decode_o_proj.py`, `config.py`, and `golden/`)
are available in the merge commit above. Because the symptom is input-sensitive,
run the case repeatedly:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-lib.git
cd pypto-lib
git fetch origin a3076021bdd17e805eb0c4c189f1f65318b952a9
git switch --detach FETCH_HEAD

for i in $(seq 1 20); do
    python models/deepseek_v4_flash_dspark/decode_sparse_attn_swa.py -p a5sim || break
done
```

Diagnosis: **PyPTO frontend feature gap**. PTOAS 0.57 and the pinned PTO ISA
already support `precisionType = #pto<recip_precision high_precision>`.
However, PyPTO's unified, tensor, and tile `pl.recip()` APIs expose no precision
argument, and codegen always emits a bare `pto.trecip`, selecting the default
lower-precision mode.

## Summary

Expose PTO's high-precision reciprocal mode through the PyPTO unified, tensor,
and tile APIs while preserving the current default behavior.

## Motivation / Use Case

Kernel authors currently cannot request high-precision reciprocal operations
from Python. On A5, the default reciprocal is intentionally faster but less
accurate, which can cause accumulated model outputs to cross precision
thresholds for some inputs.

Other operations already expose comparable controls, including
`pl.div(..., high_precision=True)`, `pl.log(..., high_precision=True)`, and
tensor `pl.rsqrt(..., high_precision=True)`.

## Proposed API / Behavior

```python
# Existing behavior remains unchanged.
result = pl.recip(input)

# Select PTO's high-precision reciprocal mode.
result = pl.recip(input, high_precision=True)
```

Apply the same optional argument to:

```python
pl.tensor.recip(input, high_precision=False)
pl.tile.recip(tile, high_precision=False)
```

When enabled, codegen should emit:

```mlir
pto.trecip ins(%src : ...)
           outs(%dst : ...)
           {precisionType = #pto<recip_precision high_precision>}
```

The tensor-to-tile conversion should preserve the flag, and unsupported dtypes
should be rejected consistently with other high-precision operations.

## Alternatives Considered

- The pypto-lib kernel now uses `amax * (1 / 127)` as a valid local workaround,
  but this only applies when the reciprocal can be algebraically eliminated.
- Raw PTO can select the precision attribute, but bypasses the PyPTO DSL and its
  validation/codegen layers.
- Changing the default precision would affect performance and existing kernels;
  an opt-in flag preserves backward compatibility.

## Additional Context

The analogous high-precision frontend support for `pto.trsqrt` was requested
and implemented in:

- https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/1000
- https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/1070

title: chore(runtime): update Simpler to 0d74814d and PTOAS v0.59
body:
## Summary

- update the Simpler submodule to current main at `0d74814d` and keep PTO-ISA aligned through `runtime/pto_isa.pin`
- update PTOAS to `v0.59` with verified aarch64 and x86_64 wheel checksums
- port PyPTO to Simplers self-describing Buffer ABI for L2 and distributed execution
- adopt the current ChipTensor, TaskArgs, CallConfig, CommDomain, swimlane, and simulator interfaces

## CI failure analysis and fixes

The previous run exposed three API mismatches introduced by the newer Simpler pin:

1. `make_tensor_arg` now requires the owning Worker. Generated distributed orchestration now binds the active Worker, while direct L2 execution uses `make_chip_tensor_arg`.
2. hierarchical device memory now uses owned `Buffer` handles instead of raw pointer calls such as `malloc(nbytes, worker_id)`. PyPTO retains those handles behind its existing pointer-facing API and uses shared staging Buffers for L3 copies.
3. `CallConfig.enable_l2_swimlane` and `l2_swimlane_records.json` became `enable_chip_swimlane` and `chip_swimlane_records.json`.

The port also updates CommDomain buffer views, persistent-window reset, mapped SubWorker arguments, chip task-argument conversion, and A2/A3 plus A5 simulator adapters.

title: docs(user): add the Performance and Precision chapters
body:
## What

Two sibling loops (B5): **measure → locate → change → confirm** for slow, and a five-step narrowing procedure for wrong.

| `performance/` | |
| -------------- | - |
| `index.md` | Chapter map; states plainly that it gives no speedup figures |
| `00-methodology.md` | Five questions, six tools, and why the order matters |
| `01-single-node.md` | Six groups of techniques, each with cost and confirmation |
| `02-distributed.md` | Rank skew, mesh vs ring, overlap, residency |
| `03-cases.md` | Six cases end to end |

| `precision/` | |
| ------------ | - |
| `index.md` | The semantic-vs-data split that decides which tool to reach for |
| `00-workflow.md` | Five steps, the tools, the acceptable-difference table |
| `01-cases.md` | Five cases — two of which are not bugs |

## The deliberate omission

**No page states a speedup percentage.** Those depend on shape, platform and version; a number written here would be stale in a way the reader cannot detect. Every technique instead carries **which of the six tools shows it worked** — the durable half, and the one people skip.

The cases pages follow the same rule: symptom → the tool that located it → the change → how the change was confirmed. Run the confirmation on your own kernel and you get your own number.

## Ordering is the content

Both chapters are built around putting the cheap checks first:

- **Performance** — a scheduling fix cannot help when step 2 shows the time is on the host, and no tuning recovers a tile `PH001` already flagged. Four of the six cases are located in steps 1, 2 or 5; only then does the per-instruction view earn its cost.
- **Precision** — three of the five cases are settled at step 2, which costs minutes, and **two of those are not bugs at all**. Starting at step 4 would have spent hours on them and found nothing.

## Corrects a claim carried in the plan

The plan listed "multi-hop cast, 1 ULP difference" as an expected-difference case. It is not: on A5 the `INT32→FP16` expansion to `INT32→FP32→FP16` is **bit-identical** to a direct conversion — FP16 saturates above 65504, every integer below that is exact in FP32, so the intermediate hop never rounds (`docs/en/dev/passes/14-legalize_tile_cast.md:39`).

The pages give the *test* for whether a chain is in that class rather than the conclusion, so a reader can judge their own cast.

## Verification

Every named tool was traced to its definition rather than taken from the plan — which is how the `memory_map` entry got corrected (its input is a **pass dump**, not a run) and how `DeviceTensor` was placed in `pypto.runtime` rather than `pl`.

`check_docs_symbol_coverage` / `check_docs_en_zh_parity` (144 paired) / `check_docs_nav` (144 entries) / `check_english_only` all exit 0; markdownlint 0 errors; no link problems introduced.

title: fix(ir): reject NZ layout on tensor types in MaterializeTensorStrides
body:
## Summary

`MaterializeTensorStrides` declares `TensorViewCanonical` among its produced
properties, but when it met an NZ `TensorView` on a `TensorType` /
`DistributedTensorType` it returned the malformed slot untouched and left the
rejection to the paired verifier. That made a pass invariant conditional on a
verification setting: with `PYPTO_VERIFY_LEVEL=none` no verifier runs, so the
invalid layout survived the pass silently and only resurfaced downstream as an
opaque ptoas layout mismatch (`user-specified layout=nz but inferred=nd`)
against a line in a generated `.pto` the user never wrote. The pass now rejects
NZ itself, so a `pl.Tensor[..., pl.NZ]` annotation fails at every verification
level with a source-located `ValueError` instead of flowing through.

NZ is a fractal, tile-only layout with no logical-stride representation, so a
tensor type carrying it is invalid IR — the judgement `tensor.view`,
`CheckCanonicalView`, and the `TensorViewCanonical` verifier already share.
Verification is configurable, so every invariant a pass claims to produce
belongs in the pass; the verifier stays as the paired re-check that catches
regressions here and in anything downstream that rewrites tensor types.

## Changes

- `src/ir/transforms/materialize_tensor_strides_pass.cpp`: `MaterializeType`
  rejects an NZ view with `CHECK_SPAN` instead of returning it unchanged, and
  takes a `Span` from the IR node carrying the type (`Var`, `IterArg`, `Call`,
  `Submit`, function param, function return) so the message points at the
  user's annotation. The check runs *before* the "stride already explicit"
  short-circuit, mirroring the verifier's ordering — an NZ view is invalid
  whether or not its stride is materialised, and letting one through would
  leave the pass claiming a property the IR does not satisfy.
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_materialize_tensor_strides_pass.py`: the two
  `..._rejected_by_paired_verifier` tests become `..._rejected_by_pass` and
  expect `ValueError` rather than `pypto.Error`, since a `CHECK` surfaces as a
  builtin `ValueError`. Two cases are added: an NZ view with explicit stride,
  and an explicit `VerificationLevel.NONE` context that guards against the
  delegation regressing. The first test also asserts a source-location token in
  the diagnostic, so the `Span` reaching `CHECK_SPAN` is covered rather than
  only the message text.
- `docs/en/dev/passes/30-materialize_tensor_strides.md`,
  `docs/zh/dev/passes/30-materialize_tensor_strides.md`: a rejection row
  replaces the NZ pass-through row, the explicit-stride pass-through row is
  qualified with `layout in {ND, DN}` so the rows are mutually exclusive, and a
  note records that the verifier is a paired re-check rather than the sole
  enforcement point.

### Behavior change

A `pl.Tensor[..., pl.NZ]` (or `pld.DistributedTensor[..., pl.NZ]`) annotation
that reached this pass previously continued and failed later in ptoas; it now
fails in the pass:

```text
MaterializeTensorStrides: NZ layout is tile-only and not allowed on a tensor
type. Annotate the tensor as pl.ND or pl.DN, and produce NZ on a Tile instead.
[<string>:8:17]
```

Under the default `PYPTO_VERIFY_LEVEL=roundtrip` this IR was already rejected
by the verifier, so the change is the error's origin, span, and wording rather
than whether valid programs compile.

### Deliberately out of scope

The annotation still survives parsing. Rejecting NZ at the type resolver would
be the earliest fix, but it changes behavior pinned by the JIT specializer,
type-resolver, and MemRef parsing suites, and `tests/ut/jit/` documents the
carry-through as intentional parity — dropping the layout is what silently
produced an ND buffer from an NZ annotation. That remains a separate design
decision.

## Verification

- `cmake --build build --parallel 2`: exit 0
- `pytest tests/ut/`: exit 0 — 9640 passed, 3 skipped
- `pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_materialize_tensor_strides_pass.py` at
  `PYPTO_VERIFY_LEVEL` `none`, `basic`, `roundtrip`: exit 0 — 20 passed each.
  Before this change the two renamed tests failed under `none` with
  `Failed: DID NOT RAISE <class 'pypto.Error'>`.
- `tests/lint/clang_tidy.py --diff-base HEAD`: exit 0 on the changed
  translation unit
- `tests/lint/check_docs_en_zh_parity.py`, `check_no_broad_raises.py`,
  `check_english_only.py`, `check_headers.py`, `check_op_name_literals.py`,
  `check_docs_nav.py`: exit 0

title: feat(ir): default the cross-core pipe ring to 2 slots
body:
## Summary

An automatically built cube<->vector pipe reserved 8 slots per direction (4 each way when bidirectional), and every slot holds the **full** tile that crosses the boundary. The ring lives in the consuming core's on-chip memory — L1 for V2C, UB for C2V — so the default spent 8x the crossing tile before a single compute tile was placed: a `[128, 128]` FP32 boundary tile reserved 512 KB of a 184 KB vector budget. The mixed kernel in `docs/en/user/tutorials/03-mixed-kernel.md` could not be compiled at all without an explicit `pl.cross_core_slot(slot_num=2)`.

This defaults the ring to **2 slots in every direction** — the shallowest depth that still double-buffers the handoff, letting the cube fill one slot while the vector drains the other. A mixed kernel that previously failed to allocate now compiles unchanged; one that depended on the deep ring for producer run-ahead restores it with `pl.cross_core_slot(slot_num=N)`, whose upper bound is unchanged (positive integer; PTOAS bounds only `slot_num > 0` and `local_slot_num <= slot_num`).

The depth can only shrink safely if it is **stated**. The automatic setup previously emitted no `slot_num` clause and leaned on PTOAS deriving the same 8/4 from `dir_mask`, so reserving 2 slots while PTOAS still indexed 8 would have walked off the end of the buffer. `BuildAutomaticPipeSetup` now always emits the resolved `slot_num`, which makes the reserved buffer and the depth PTOAS indexes unable to disagree.

## Changes

- `src/ir/transforms/utils/cross_core_pipe.cpp`, `include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/cross_core_pipe.h`: new `kDefaultAutoPipeSlotNum = 2` replaces the `dir_mask`-derived 8/4 policy for automatic pipes, and `CreateInitializePipe` takes a plain `int slot_num` that is always emitted rather than an optional override. `GetSlotNumForDirMask` is renamed `GetPtoasImplicitSlotNum` to mark it as a mirror of PTOAS's fallback rather than a tunable policy knob.
- `src/ir/verifier/mixed_kernel_expanded_verifier.cpp`, `include/pypto/codegen/gm_pipe_layout.h`: unchanged behaviour — both still model PTOAS's implicit 8/4, which now governs only hand-written `pl.system.{aic,aiv}_initialize_pipe`. Comments record that boundary.
- `python/pypto/language/optimizations.py`: `pl.cross_core_slot` docstring documents the new default and reframes the knob as one that deepens the ring.
- `docs/en/**`, `docs/zh/**`: passes 20/21/34, `00-python_syntax`, `04-scopes`, and tutorial 03 updated in both languages. The tutorial's "the ring will not fit by default" step became "the ring spends your vector budget", since its premise no longer holds.
- `examples/advanced/03_mixed_kernel.py`: drops the `pl.cross_core_slot(slot_num=2)` entries that only worked around the old default.
- `tests/ut/**`: mixed-kernel expansion expectations now assert `slot_size * 2` reserve buffers and an explicit `slot_num=2`; `test_bidirectional_mixed_kernel_keeps_combined_pipe` asserts the emitted clause. `test_slot_num_omitted_by_default` is unchanged and still covers the hand-written path where PTOAS's fallback applies.
- `tests/st/codegen/dsl/test_split_aiv_gather_row_codegen.py`: the overflow-diagnostic test used to rely on the *default* ring overflowing L1, which no longer happens at depth 2 (131072 x 2 = 256 KB fits). It now requests the 8-slot ring explicitly, so the overflow is deliberate; every byte assertion is unchanged and the fixture/test are renamed accordingly. The test still proves what it existed to prove -- that the diagnostic attributes the reserved bytes and names the knob.

## Behavior change

Mixed kernels using `pl.split` / `pl.split_aiv` without `pl.cross_core_slot` get a 2-slot ring instead of 8 (or 4 bidirectional). This reduces consumer-side on-chip reservation and, on 910B, also shortens the GM ring. Kernels tuned around the deep default should set `pl.cross_core_slot(slot_num=N)` explicitly. Hand-written pipe setup is unaffected.

A follow-up worth considering, not included here: on 910B the ring data sits in the GM workspace while the on-chip cost is governed by `local_slot_num` (which defaults to `slot_num` because it is never emitted). Emitting `slot_num=8, local_slot_num=2` there would keep the GM run-ahead while cutting the on-chip footprint; PTOAS supports that only on a2/a3, so it belongs behind `BackendHandler` rather than in a flat constant.

## Verification

- `cmake --build build --parallel "$PYPTO_BUILD_JOBS"`: exit 0
- `python -m pytest tests/ut -n "$PYPTO_TEST_JOBS"`: 9670 passed, 3 skipped
- `python -m pytest tests/st/codegen/dsl/test_split_aiv_gather_row_codegen.py`: 3 passed
- `pre-commit run --files <changed>`: all 17 hooks passed (clang-format, cpplint, markdownlint-cli2, ruff, pyright, docs en/zh parity)
- `ruff check .`: all checks passed; `ruff format --check .`: clean
- The push transaction re-ran the build and both suites above at the pushed commit before pushing.
- Not run locally: the `a2a3sim` end-to-end numerical path, which needs `g++-15` (unavailable on the authoring machine). CI covers it: `system-tests`, `system-tests-direct`, `system-tests-a5sim`, `dist-system-tests`, and `pypto-lib-model` are green on this head.

title: fix(codegen): dispatch dual_aiv_dispatch AIV kernels on both vector lanes
body:
Fixes #2006

A `pl.split_aiv` region is task-parallel: both AIV lanes run the body on disjoint
work selected by `aiv_id`. SplitVectorKernel stamps such an AIV kernel
`dual_aiv_dispatch`, but only the mixed-kernel Group submit honoured it. The three
single-kernel dispatch paths — direct call, Spmd wrapper, and AIV-only Group — all
built their submit through `CoreTypeToSubmitPrefix()`, which unconditionally yields
`rt_submit_aiv_task` for VECTOR.

`rt_submit_aiv_task` fills only the AIV0 slot of MixedKernels, so the active mask
carries one core bit and the runtime schedules an AIV-shape task: one AIV core per
block. The second lane never launches, and the lone lane that does reads a
`get_sub_block_id()` the runtime documents as meaningless for a single-AIV task
(runtime `common/intrinsic.h`); the scheduler seeds that value per core from the
core's fixed position in its cluster, so `aiv_id` is that position rather than a
per-block lane id. Half the work is silently dropped — the destination rows come
back as exact zeros, with no error, no NaN, and a block-parity pattern for which
lane survives. A pure-vector kernel (no cube work) hits this on the Spmd-wrapper path.

Route the three single-kernel paths through a shared `BuildSingleKernelSubmit()`,
which emits `MixedKernels{INVALID_KERNEL_ID, id, id}` + `rt_submit_task` for a
`dual_aiv_dispatch` VECTOR kernel. Two active AIV slots make it a MIX-shape task, so
the scheduler places both lanes of one cluster under the same block_idx and gives them
sub_block_id 0 and 1; the cluster's AIC core is unused. No runtime change is needed.

A plain vector kernel carries no `dual_aiv_dispatch` and keeps `rt_submit_aiv_task`,
so it retains its full independent-AIV parallelism; mixed kernels are untouched.

The existing NONE-region codegen ST compiled this exact shape but only asserted a
.pto was emitted, which is why the defect shipped; it now also asserts the submit
launches both lanes.

Supersedes #2012, which was opened against a month-old main and no longer applies.
Two parts of it are deliberately left out here:

- Its print->parse commit is obsolete. #2298 has since made *absence* the canonical
  encoding of `SplitMode::NONE` at the function-attr level, solving the same problem
  the opposite way.
- Its parser change — treating a core function body as an implicit InCore scope so a
  bare `pl.split_aiv` is emitted in place — is a semantic decision that belongs in its
  own PR. main now pins the opposite behaviour: `test_scope_nested_region_rejected`
  requires a top-level region in an InCore body to be wrapped and then rejected by
  LowerAutoVectorSplit. Without that change, post-outline IR whose core-function body
  directly holds a `SplitAivScopeStmt` still does not survive print -> parse, so the
  new UT narrows its instrument set to property verification (the pattern already used
  by `test_materialize_comm_domain_scopes`). That gap is in the parser, not in dispatch.

Verified on an Ascend 910B (a2a3), runtime 3165cc89 / pto-isa 83d01313 / ptoas v0.57,
with a probe kernel that writes each lane's observed `block_idx` and `block_num`:

  before: 16 of 32 lanes never written — [1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 10, ...] (block-parity)
  after:  32 of 32 lanes written, block_idx == lane // 2 for every lane

and with the issue's reproducer, whose split_aiv arm goes from 64/128 wrong items
(max_err 4.18) to bit-exact. Note that arm must be run first and alone: when the
plain-spmd control arm runs before it in the same process, the reused output device
buffer still holds the control arm's correct rows and the dropped lanes read back
correct, masking the defect entirely.

Testing:
- cmake --build build --parallel
- python -m pytest tests/ut/ (9633 passed, 8 skipped)
- on-board python -m pytest tests/st/runtime/cross_core/ --forked --platform=a2a3
  (49 passed, 3 skipped, 1 xpassed)

title: fix(codegen): reject set_validshape on a tile view instead of failing in ptoas
body:
## Summary

`tile.set_validshape` lowered unconditionally to a runtime `pto.set_validshape`
against its operand. That instruction mutates the operand's `valid_row` /
`valid_col` operands, so the operand has to be a handle that owns them — an
alloc, an `scf.if` result, a cross-core pop slot. A *view* (the `pto.subview` a
`tile.slice` lowers to, or a `pto.treshape`) carries its valid extent in its own
type instead, and ptoas rejects it:

```text
error: 'pto.set_validshape' op expects source tile_buf to have
       dynamic validShape (?, ?)
error: 'pto.set_validshape' op requires a locally bound tile source;
       function arguments/results are unsupported
```

So `pl.set_validshape` on a sliced tile passed every PyPTO check and then failed
in the assembler, with no PyPTO-level diagnostic and nothing pointing at the fix.

PyPTO now rejects it up front, naming the alternative: pass `valid_shape=` to the
slice (it lands in `pto.subview`'s `valid [...]` clause and accepts runtime
extents), or narrow the source tile before taking the view.

The narrowing could instead have been re-expressed as another `pto.treshape`,
and an earlier revision of this change did that. It was dropped: it only works
for a compile-time constant extent, and it gives one operation two different
aliasing semantics — mutating the shared handle for an alloc, where every holder
observes the narrowing, versus binding a fresh view for a slice, where only later
uses do. Diverging on operand provenance is the trap that silently shifted
DeepSeek-V4-Flash `decode_csa` numerics while this path was being developed.

Alloc-backed operands are untouched: same instruction, same in-place semantics.

## Changes

- reject `tile.set_validshape` on a view operand with an actionable message
- decide by asking whether the operand IS a view, tracked at the two emission
  sites (`pto.subview`, `pto.treshape`) behind a new
  `PTOCodegen::RegisterTileViewName` / `IsTileViewName`. The rendered valid dims
  cannot decide it: a `tile.slice` given a runtime `valid_shape` renders
  `v_row=?, v_col=?` exactly as an alloc-backed handle does
- drop the stale "internal op / compiler-generated code only" claims on
  `tile.set_validshape` and `tensor.set_validshape`. Both are public: exported
  from `pl`, `pl.tile` and `pl.tensor`, covered by runtime tests, and used
  directly by pypto-lib kernels. Replaced with guidance on where to express a
  valid extent instead (9 sites: 2 op registrations, 5 docstrings, en/zh docs)
- add codegen regressions for a slice operand and for a runtime-`valid_shape`
  slice, whose dynamic valid dims must not launder it past the view check
- document which operands accept the op, in `docs/en` and `docs/zh`

## Verification

- CMake build (`RelWithDebInfo`, gcc-15)
- `tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen_ops.py -k SetValidShape`: 5 passed
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_lower_composite_ops.py`: 123 passed
- `tests/ut/` excluding `tests/ut/runtime`: all passed. `tests/ut/runtime`'s 14
  failures + 4 errors are a pre-existing environment mismatch (installed
  `_task_interface` built from a different runtime commit than the pinned
  submodule) and fail on `main` too
- `ptoas 0.54 --pto-level=level3` still accepts the alloc and reshape operand
  forms; the two view forms now stop at a PyPTO error instead of reaching it
- the five existing `set_validshape` ST programs keep the runtime path unchanged,
  and 42 kernels compiled from three pypto-lib models (DeepSeek V4 `hc_pre` /
  `moe`, V4-Flash `hc_pre`) keep all 38 `pto.set_validshape` ops on it, with zero
  rejections — a view operand could not assemble before this change, so nothing
  that worked is now refused
- `tests/lint/`: docs en/zh parity, docs nav, english-only, headers,
  broad-raises, op-name-literals
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` on all six changed Python files
- `clang-format --dry-run --Werror` on the changed C++ files
- `git diff --check`
- push-transaction revalidation at the pushed commit `b52b6117` (rebased onto
  `main` at b22cee1e): CMake build, `-k SetValidShape` 5 passed,
  `tests/ut/codegen/` 864 passed 2 skipped

title: fix(ir): reject incoherent mixed GM stores
body:
## Summary

InCore lowering now rejects a GM tensor that is written through both the MTE3 bulk-store path and the scalar D-cache path. The pass follows parameter aliases through assignments and control flow and reports an actionable source-span error instead of emitting potentially corrupt code. Mixed store paths to distinct GM tensors remain valid.

## Changes

- Record bulk and scalar store spans by underlying GM parameter in `ConvertTensorToTileOps` and reject mixed paths.
- Add rejection and allowed-path regressions while preserving lower-level pointer SSA coverage on already-lowered IR.
- Document the coherence restriction and the single-UB-store workaround in English and Chinese.

## Verification

- Affected transform and codegen test files: 289 passed.
- Ruff checks and formatting, clang-format, documentation parity/navigation, headers, English-only, broad-raise, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Broad unit-test split found only three environment-isolation failures: one subprocess resolved the primary checkout's editable package, and two optional-runtime tests loaded a stale `simpler` binary from a different submodule commit. No product-test failure was related to this change.

Fixes #2005

title: fix(codegen): clear inherited AI Core atomic mode
body:
ATB _npu_matmul_add_fp32 can leave an AI Core in atomic-add mode. PyPTO wrappers previously entered the PTOAS body without clearing that per-core state, so an ordinary L0C-to-GM store could add into the existing output instead of overwriting it.

Emit the CCEC set_atomic_none() builtin as the first hardware-only operation in kernel_entry, before runtime identity setup and argument unpacking. Keep CPU simulation and cost-model output unchanged, and avoid coupling PyPTO to AscendC headers or SDK include layouts.

Add codegen coverage for the hardware guard, entry ordering, and dependency-free wrapper output.

title: docs(user): rewrite the Performance chapter around single-card tuning
body:
Replaces #2375, which was closed: its structure (a five-step measurement loop plus a
technique catalogue) did not match how a single-card kernel is actually tuned.

The chapter now walks down where the time goes, in the order the costs bite:

| Page | Covers |
| ---- | ------ |
| `00-swimlane` | Capturing the L2 swimlane + `deps.json`, opening it in the PyPTO Toolkit plugin or Perfetto, and reading the four timestamps |
| `01-task-granularity` | Dispatch cost; growing a task via tiling / an inner loop / merging, and the core-count ceiling on the other side |
| `02-runtime-overhead` | Mixed kernel, SPMD, `allow_early_resolve`, in-kernel `syncall` |
| `03-dependencies` | The three inference steps, the serialization they cause, and the narrowest opt-out for each |
| `04-incore` | `pl.pipeline` vs explicit `pl.MemRef` slots, split-K, L0 instruction traces, PH001 granularity, `external_source` |
| `05-memory` | The four scope-depth rings, why default scope placement wastes them, scope-stats before sizing |
| `06-host` | `DeviceTensor` residency, register-once dispatch |
| `07-distributed` | Kept from the old chapter — per-rank measurement, beyond the single card |

## Grounding

Every claim is taken from the source rather than inferred:

- dependency rules — `pto_dep_compute.h` (creator retention / producer lookup / registration) and `war-anti-dependency.md`
- four rings and `min(scope_depth, MAX_RING_DEPTH - 1)` — the orchestrator's `Ring`
- 48 vector / 24 cube — `backend.h`
- `PH001`'s 512 B L2 line and the measured 16–25% `b_trans` penalty — `92-diagnostics.md`
- `PH-MR-001`'s "only M of N buffers fit" report — `memory_reuse_pass.cpp`
- hard `syncall` full-occupancy rule — the `HardSyncallOccupancy` verifier
- PTOAS rejecting two co-live slots per iteration — `test_memory_planner_ptoas.py`

No speedup numbers: the chapter states the confirmation step instead, so a reader
measures their own.

## Verification

Snippets that were composed rather than copied from a working source were
compile-checked on `a2a3sim`. That caught a real defect: a cube+vector merge in one
scope does not fit without `pl.split(...)`, so the granularity page now shows a
same-engine merge and points cross-engine merges at the mixed-kernel page.

Gates: `check_docs_en_zh_parity`, `check_docs_nav`, `check_english_only`,
`check_docs_symbol_coverage`, markdownlint — all pass. Every relative link and anchor
in the chapter resolves.

title: fix(ir): materialize unaligned Vec slices
body:
## Summary

Canonical Vec slices can carry operand bases that are not 32-byte aligned, which can hang affected A3 kernels. This change materializes those slices into fresh Vec buffers whenever alignment cannot be proven, while retaining zero-copy subviews for provably aligned cases.

Refs #1789

## Changes

- Compute slice alignment from the concrete MemRef byte offset and physical storage bit width, including packed 4-bit and BOOL storage.
- Materialize unsafe constant or dynamic Vec slices and generalize direct extract folding across canonical slices.
- Cover aligned, unaligned, dynamic, packed-storage, and codegen consumer cases.
- Document the behavior in the synchronized English and Chinese pass documentation.

title: [Bug] RunConfig.enable_l2_swimlane is a bool, so only swimlane level 1 is reachable from Python
body:
### Component

Python Bindings

### Description

L2 swimlane collection is **levelled** on the runtime side, but PyPTO's `RunConfig` field is still a `bool`. `True` therefore requests level **1**, and levels 2–4 cannot be requested from Python at all.

The runtime's contract:

| Level | Adds |
| ----- | ---- |
| 0 `DISABLED` | — |
| 1 `AICORE_TIMING` | AICore per-task start / end + task record buffer |
| 2 `AICPU_TIMING` | + AICPU-stamped dispatch / finish |
| 3 `SCHED_PHASES` | + scheduler main-loop phase records |
| 4 `ORCH_PHASES` | + orchestrator phase records |

`CallConfig::enable_l2_swimlane` is an `int32_t` (`runtime/src/common/task_interface/call_config.h:115`) and `set_l2_swimlane_enabled(int level)` casts it straight to `L2SwimlaneLevel`. PyPTO copies the bool into it verbatim, so `True` lands as `1`.

**The levels are real guards in the collectors, not a verbosity setting.** In the schedulers:

- `l2_swimlane_level_ >= AICPU_TIMING` gates the dispatch/finish stamping
- `>= SCHED_PHASES` gates the scheduler-loop records
- `>= ORCH_PHASES` gates the orchestrator records

So at level 1 the dispatch and finish timestamps are **never stamped**, and no post-processing recovers them.

Consequences for a `RunConfig`-driven capture:

- `sched_overhead_analysis` cannot be used — its scheduler-loop parts need level ≥ 3
- the `[dispatch, start]` pickup gap cannot be read
- the PyPTO Toolkit plugin's Scheduler View / AICPU Orchestrator views are empty

The naming makes this easy to trip over: the runtime harness's **bare** `--enable-l2-swimlane` defaults to level **4**, so the same-named switch means "everything" upstream and "AICore timing only" from PyPTO.

Note that the two sibling DFX knobs were already migrated to `int` levels — `enable_dump_args` (`0/1/2`) and `enable_pmu` (event type) — so this looks like one that was missed rather than a deliberate difference.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run any kernel with swimlane capture through `RunConfig`:

   ```python
   from pypto.runtime import RunConfig

   cfg = RunConfig(platform="a2a3", enable_l2_swimlane=True,
                   enable_dep_gen=True, save_kernels=True)
   ```

2. Inspect `<work_dir>/dfx_outputs/l2_swimlane_records.json` — records carry AICore `start` / `end`, with no AICPU dispatch/finish stamps and no scheduler-phase records.

3. Try to feed it to the overhead analysis, which needs level ≥ 3:

   ```bash
   python -m simpler_setup.tools.sched_overhead_analysis \
       --l2-swimlane-records-json <records>.json --deps-json <deps>.json
   ```

The relevant declarations:

```python
# python/pypto/runtime/runner.py:239
enable_l2_swimlane: bool = False

# python/pypto/runtime/runner.py:824 — copied into an int32_t field
cfg.enable_l2_swimlane = run_config.enable_l2_swimlane   # True -> 1 == AICORE_TIMING

# python/pypto/runtime/execute_artifact.py:361
parser.add_argument("--enable-l2-swimlane", action="store_true", ...)
```

```text
runtime/conftest.py:142
  --enable-l2-swimlane  nargs="?"  const=4  default=0  type=int  metavar=PERF_LEVEL
  "Bare flag=level 4 (full). 1=AICore timing, 2=+dispatch/fanout, 3=+sched phases, 4=+orch phases"
```

### Expected Behavior

`RunConfig` can request any collection level the runtime supports, the way `enable_dump_args` and `enable_pmu` already do.

### Actual Behavior

Only level 1 is reachable. `enable_l2_swimlane=True` silently under-collects relative to the same-named runtime flag, and the features that need levels 2–4 are unavailable from Python with no diagnostic.

### Proposed fix

Type the field as a level while keeping `bool` accepted, mirroring `enable_dump_args`:

```python
enable_l2_swimlane: int | bool = 0   # 0=off, 1=AICore timing, 2=+dispatch/finish,
                                     # 3=+sched phases, 4=+orch phases
```

Also update `_DfxOpts` (`runner.py:521`), the `--enable-l2-swimlane` CLI in `execute_artifact.py` (to `nargs="?" const=<N> type=int`), `tests/st/conftest.py:215`, and the `RunConfig` docstring.

**One decision needed: what should `True` mean?**

- **A — `True → 4`**, matching the runtime's bare-flag semantics. The capabilities above become available immediately, but existing `=True` callers start collecting much more, which perturbs timing more.
- **B — `True → 1`**, preserving today's behaviour exactly and adding ints for 2–4. Safer, though the "same flag name, different meaning" trap remains until someone reads the docstring.

B looks preferable — it changes no existing behaviour and matches how `enable_dump_args` grew — but the choice is worth making explicitly.

### Git Commit ID

1c66f01c180e1fc3a858817dfb8f52d6ecefff88

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Found while writing the user-manual Performance chapter (#2383). That page originally documented the dispatch gap, the scheduler/orchestrator views, and `sched_overhead_analysis` without noting that none of them is reachable through `RunConfig`; it has since been corrected to state the level each one needs. Once this is fixed, those caveats can be dropped.

title: fix(ir): carry a ragged valid shape across the AIV split boundary
body:
## Summary

A `valid_shape`-padded accumulator silently lost its real data crossing
`pl.aiv_shard`. On a `[16, 256]` accumulator valid to 5 rows, lane 0 dropped
rows 3-4 and lane 1 wrote two rows of padding over real output — wrong numbers,
no diagnostic, in both release and debug builds.

Two independent defects caused it. The Cube->Vector pop transported the wrong
geometry whenever the kernel was split, and the split-axis valid extent kept a
lane-agnostic `ceil(V / 2)` guess that is wrong for *both* lanes. Both are
fixed: a ragged row extent under `UP_DOWN` now crosses the boundary intact, and
the shapes that provably cannot cross are refused up front with a message naming
the DSL alternative, instead of producing silent garbage.

### Why the pop was wrong

PTO's C2V FIFO always copies the physical consumer box. pto-isa builds the GM
slot view from the popped tile's compile-time rows/cols and the producer's box
row pitch (a2a3 `TPush.hpp` `popVecTileFromGMFiFo`: `gmValidR`/`gmValidC` =
`ConsM`/`ConsN`, `gmStrideR = ProdN`), then strides that view with the tile's
*runtime* `validCol` (`TLoadGm2ubNd2nd`: `lenBurst = validCol`, `gmGap =
gStride3 - gShape4`). Requiring the GM advance per burst to equal one
producer-box row gives

```text
validCol*s + (ProdN - ConsN)*s == ProdN*s   =>   validCol == ConsN
```

so a narrowed `validCol` collapses the gap to zero and the pop reads one
contiguous run instead of one box row per burst. PyPTO widened the push to the
full box at every split but widened the pop only at `split == 0`, so both split
lanes mis-strided. The matching `PTO_ASSERT(validCol == gShape4)` is compiled
out in release builds, so nothing caught it.

### Why a ragged row is supported and a ragged column is refused

That derivation pins only the *column* field — `ProdN` cancels, leaving
`validCol == ConsN` whatever the split mode. The row field is free
(`nBurst = gShape3 = ConsM`). So a per-lane ROW extent rides across on the TPOP
`valid_row` operand, while a per-lane COLUMN extent has no carrier at all: the
only way to rebuild a narrowed column after the full-box transport,
`pto.treshape`, takes no operands and so can express only compile-time static
extents. The two split modes are geometrically symmetric; the transport is not.

## Changes

- `src/backend/common/pto_ops_crosscore.cpp`: widen the TPOP transport to the
  full box at **every** split, not only `split == 0`, matching the producer-side
  widening already done in `EmitTpushTransportValidShape`. A statically empty
  pop still moves nothing, so the dual-AIV pipe-balancing replay is unchanged.
- `src/ir/transforms/utils/split_axis_utils.{h,cpp}`: give each lane its true
  split-axis extent `clamp(V - L*half, 0, half)` and carry it to consumers that
  pass the extent through unchanged. Two new entry points —
  `LocalizeShardValidForLane` (a single shard result type) and
  `LocalizeExplicitBoundaryValid` (a whole `pl.split_aiv` region body). The walk
  descends into loops and branches, so a nested shard, consumer, or store is
  repaired exactly like a top-level one. An empty lane's `tile.store` is guarded
  behind `extent > 0` while its `tpop`/`tfree` stay unconditional, keeping the
  cross-core pipe balanced. The clamp is built as `min(max(V, off) - off, half)`
  rather than `max(min(V - off, half), 0)`, which wraps when the valid extent
  carries an unsigned dtype (`tile.set_validshape` accepts UINT64) and would
  then hand the empty lane a full half.
- `src/ir/transforms/lower_auto_vector_split_pass.cpp`: apply that localization
  on both arms — the AUTO C->V synthesis and the explicit-boundary region — and
  restore the pre-shard extent on `tile.aic_gather`, rejecting a
  provably-partial untracked operand there.
- `src/ir/op/tile_ops/cross_core.cpp`: reject at deduction what cannot cross,
  each message naming the DSL fix — a per-lane column extent under
  `LEFT_RIGHT`, a runtime-valued narrowed column, and `UP_DOWN` carrying both a
  per-lane row extent and a narrowed column. The gather's band rule moved *out*
  of the deducer: it runs before per-lane extents exist, so it judged the join
  on the `ceil` guess and misreported the author's own numbers.
- `src/ir/transforms/utils/dead_code_elimination.cpp`: count Vars referenced
  from a defined var's **type** as live. A localized extent is an expression
  over the region's subblock index, so without this the index binding is
  deleted and the type dangles.
- `docs/{en,zh}/dev/codegen/00-pto_codegen.md`,
  `docs/{en,zh}/dev/passes/20-lower_auto_vector_split.md`: document the
  transport rule, the support matrix, the gather geometry, and the empty-lane
  guard.

## Behavior change

Programs that were silently producing wrong data now either produce correct data
(ragged rows under `UP_DOWN`) or fail to compile with an actionable error
(ragged columns, and the mixed row+column case). Nothing that previously
compiled *and* produced correct results changes: a fully-valid split axis takes
the deducer's exact type as before, and the localization walk returns its input
untouched in that case.

## Verification

Run on this branch, at the machine-local 2-job limit.

- `cmake --build build --parallel 2` (RelWithDebInfo): exit 0, no errors or new
  warnings
- `pytest tests/ut/ -n 2`: **9689 passed, 3 skipped** in 325s
- `pytest tests/st/codegen/ -n 2`: **50 passed**
- `pre-commit run --files <15 changed paths>`: **all 17 hooks pass** —
  check-headers, check-english-only, check-docs-en-zh-parity, check-docs-nav,
  check-docs-symbol-coverage, check-no-broad-raises, check-op-name-literals,
  clang-format, cpplint, markdownlint-cli2, ruff check, ruff format, pyright.
  (`tests/lint/` holds `check_*.py` scripts rather than pytest tests, so
  pre-commit is what actually runs them.)
- `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `git diff --check`: clean

Revalidated at the pushed commit `5491838e`, rebased onto `main` at `a83d185c`:

- `cmake --build build --parallel 2`: exit 0
- focused — `test_cross_core_ops.py`, `test_pto_codegen_cross_core.py`,
  `test_lower_auto_vector_split.py`, `test_split_vector_kernel.py`:
  **166 passed**
- broader — `tests/ut/codegen`, `tests/ut/ir/transforms`: **3767 passed**
- `tests/st/codegen`: **50 passed**

Hardware, recorded earlier in this task on this change: an A2/A3 device with
random inputs reproduced the loss (224/235/223 of 512 elements wrong; then bad
row ids `[3, 4]`, bad col ids `[16..31]`) and confirmed both fixes, with the
ragged-column form rejected at compile time.

## Review hardening (folded into the same commit)

Found by review of this change and fixed in `5491838e`:

- recurse into `WhileStmt` bodies as well as `ForStmt`/`IfStmt`/`SeqStmts`
- index chained-store destinations **once, recursively** over the whole region
  (`CollectChainedStoreDestinations`). The previous sibling-only scan missed a
  chained store nested in a branch or loop, which would have let the empty-lane
  guard skip a store another store writes through; it was also O(S^2) in the
  region's store count
- require a static **physical** box, not just a static valid extent, before the
  full-box + `treshape` pop — a dynamic split axis lowers to `floordiv(dim, 2)`,
  so without this a dynamic-shaped tile hit an `INTERNAL_CHECK` instead of the
  direct-TPOP fallback
- seed DCE live roots from every control-flow **binder** type, not just the
  assign LHS (`MarkBinderTypeRefsLive`) — a binder is not an `AssignStmt`
- refuse a per-lane value carried across a `pl.range` / `pl.while_` boundary
- clang-tidy: add the direct `span.h` / `type.h` includes, drop a dead store

## Notes for review

- **One pinned test expectation changed**, in
  `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_split_vector_kernel.py`. It asserted the old
  clamp form; the rewrite is the unsigned-underflow fix described above, not an
  accommodation. At `subblock_idx = 1` the old form yields a full half where the
  lane holds nothing.
- **One review thread is deliberately left open**
  ([retyping control-flow boundary variables](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/2388#discussion_r3785873067)).
  The underlying defect is real and is now *refused* at compile time rather than
  supported: a per-lane value carried across a `pl.range` / `pl.while_` boundary
  would keep the lane-agnostic extent, so `RejectLocalizedCarry` stops it with a
  message naming the authorings that avoid it. Implementing the retype means
  changing SSA binder construction, and I could not build a kernel that
  exercises it — untested there means silent wrong data, which is what this PR
  exists to remove. Worth a deliberate follow-up with a test; flagging rather
  than guessing.
- `docs/en/dev/passes/20-lower_auto_vector_split.md` is 548 lines against the
  500-line guideline in `documentation-length.md` (509 before this change). It
  was condensed twice already; the sibling `00-pto_codegen.md` sits at 798.

title: docs: raise the file length limit and split the Python syntax spec
body:
## Summary

`.claude/rules/documentation-length.md` capped `docs/**.md` at 500 lines while 17
of 272 documentation files were already over it, and the rule disagreed with
itself: the limits table said 500, but the workflow section below it treated
500-700 as "condense" and >700 as "split". This raises the cap to 1000, realigns
the split and condense thresholds with the table, and brings the two files
furthest over their limits back into compliance.

For readers, the visible change is the Python IR syntax specification: it was one
1149-line page (1085 in Chinese) and is now four, reachable from a nav table on
the entry page and from the Language index. Every anchor that pointed into it
still resolves. No source, build, or test behavior changes — the rule and skill
files govern assistant workflows only.

## Changes

- `.claude/rules/documentation-length.md`: `docs/**.md` limit 500 -> 1000, with
  split now ">1000 (over the limit)" and condense "800-1000 (approaching the
  limit)" so the two sections agree. Skill supporting files keep their own
  tighter 500-line limit, which the text had described as "the 500-line docs
  limit" — no longer accurate once the docs limit moved, so it is now stated
  independently.
- `docs/{en,zh}/dev/language/`: the syntax spec splits into `00-python_syntax.md`
  (module structure, types, expressions), `01-statements.md` (assignment,
  if/for/while, scopes, yield, directives, SSA phi nodes),
  `02-manual_dependencies.md` (`pl.manual_scope`, `deps=`, dispatch predicates,
  array-carry fences), and `03-functions.md` (function types, parameter
  directions, cross-module reuse, printing). Largest resulting page is 435 lines.
- `docs/{en,zh}/dev/language/04-external-kernels.md`: renamed from `01-` so file
  numbers still match reading order. All 11 inbound links and the `mkdocs.yml`
  nav entry move with it; no content change.
- Anchor continuity: `#slots` and `#under-the-ptoas-memory-planner` stay on the
  entry page, so links to them are untouched.
  `#manual-dependency-primitives` became the h1 of `02-manual_dependencies.md`,
  which keeps the slug identical — only the file part of its six referring links
  changed.
- `.claude/skills/add-op/`: `SKILL.md` 393 -> 197 lines, back under its 200-line
  cap, by dropping code templates `reference.md` already carried. The
  `REGISTER_OP` template (missing from `reference.md` section 1) and the
  file-location table moved there rather than being deleted; the table is now
  section 11.
- `docs/zh/dev/passes/27-lower_pipeline_to_slots.md`: two links pointed at
  `00-python_syntax.md#slots`, but the Chinese heading is `#### 槽位`, so that
  anchor never resolved. Fixed to `#槽位`.

## Verification

- `pre-commit run --all-files`: all 17 hooks pass, including
  `check-docs-en-zh-parity`, `check-docs-nav`, `check-english-only`, and
  `markdownlint-cli2`. Run again by the push transaction's validation runner at
  the rebased commit, with the same result.
- Split content preservation, checked line by line: every non-blank line of both
  original files appears in the four resulting pages, in both languages. The only
  additions are the nav table, page titles, intros, and See Also sections.
- Link sweep over `docs/**` (code fences excluded): 0 broken relative `.md`
  links, and no anchor broken by this change.

No tests were run: this range changes documentation and assistant-workflow files
only, and touches no C++ or Python source.

## Follow-up not included here

Chinese anchors do not resolve on the built site at all: `mkdocs.yml` configures
`toc` with no `slugify`, so Python-Markdown's ASCII-only default applies and an
all-CJK heading slugs to the empty string. That affects every `docs/zh/**` anchor
and is independent of this split — GitHub renders those anchors correctly, which
is why the docs read fine in-repo. Fixing it needs a Unicode-aware slugger plus
matching changes to the `check-yaml` hook and `tests/lint/check_docs_nav.py`,
which is a lint-policy decision better reviewed on its own.

title: fix(ir): preserve valid_shape on tensor elementwise ops
body:
Elementwise ops allocate fresh storage, so they must not turn padding into valid data. This PR only cherry-picks the two latest commits from `nalinaly/pypto` onto current `upstream/main`; it does not include the other fork-only work.

## Changes

1. **Tensor-scalar elementwise** inherit the operand's effective `valid_shape` via `MakeFreshTensorType`, and drop source alias / layout / stride / padding metadata. Covers the usual promotion path and the dtype-preserving bitwise/shift path.
2. **Tensor-tensor elementwise** keep that exact valid region when both operands share the same physical shape and their effective `valid_shape`s are provably equal. Arithmetic and the already-verified bitwise/shift ops are included.
3. **Conservative exclusions** where the current lowering contract is incomplete: `cmp`, `xor`/`xors`, `part_*`, broadcast, unequal valid regions, and direct distributed windows. Also stop the first commit from propagating a partial valid region through scalar `cmp`/`xors`.

Docs (zh/en) and IR / A3 narrow-write tests are updated with the new contract.

title: fix(ir): treat pld.system.notify's target as a param write
body:
## Summary

A waiting task must depend on the task that notifies it. Without that
dependency the scheduler is free to place the `pld.system.wait` tasks first;
they occupy every core spinning on a signal cell that only `pld.system.notify`
can set, no core is left to run the notifying task, and the communication card
deadlocks.

That dependency is derived from parameter directions, and the direction was
wrong. `ConvertTensorToTileOps` infers InCore parameter directions from an
alias-origin read/write analysis, but `pld.system.notify` had no entry in either
`GetWriteTargetExpr` or `AnalyzeCallAccess`. It fell through to the default
branch, which counts every argument as a read, so a signal window written only
by TNOTIFY stayed `In` — the notifying task looked like a pure reader of the
signal, no RAW edge was emitted to the waiter, and the two tasks were
schedulable in any order. Composite collectives that lower to notify
(`pld.tensor.barrier`, `allreduce`, `broadcast`, ...) already mark their signal
read+write, so only the raw `pld.system.notify` path was affected.

After this change an unannotated signal parameter of an InCore function becomes
`Out` when only notify touches it, and `InOut` when a companion
`pld.system.wait` reads it back, so the waiter now carries a real dependency on
the notifier and cannot be scheduled ahead of it. Parameters already declared
`Out` / `InOut` are unchanged, and no public API moves.

## Changes

- `src/ir/transforms/convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp`: register notify's
  `target` (`args_[0]`) as a write target and give it an `AnalyzeCallAccess`
  branch, mirroring the existing `pld.tile.remote_store` / `put` / `get`
  handling; `peer`, `offsets` and `value` stay reads. Write-only is correct for
  both `NotifyOp` values — the accumulate half of `AtomicAdd` runs atomically on
  the *peer* rank's slot, so the notifying kernel never reads its local buffer.
- `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.py`: two before/after
  cases in the existing param-direction group — notify alone yields `Out`
  (`NotifyOp.AtomicAdd`), notify plus wait yields `InOut` (`NotifyOp.Set`), so
  both notify semantics are pinned.
- `docs/en/dev/passes/10-convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.md`,
  `docs/zh/dev/passes/10-convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.md`: the direction-upgrade
  step was undocumented; describe it as Phase 1 step 5 and list every op
  recognised as a write target.

All of the following ran on this branch rebased onto `main` at 68956620.

- `cmake --build build --parallel 2`: exit 0
- `python -m pytest tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.py tests/ut/codegen/distributed/ tests/ut/codegen/test_spmd_scope_tid_codegen.py -n 2 -q`: exit 0
- `python -m pytest tests/ut/ -n 2 -q`: 9563 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed. Two exclusions, neither related to this change: five `tests/ut/runtime` files that fail on a stale local `_task_interface.so` (`ImportError: MAILBOX_FRAME_SIZE`), and `test_declared_memref.py::TestLoopCarryRoundtrip::test_signature_memref_base_prints_as_a_string`, which was reproduced red on an unmodified checkout of the base commit.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: exit 0, all 17 hooks pass (clang-format, cpplint, markdownlint, ruff, pyright, and the repository's docs/lint scripts)

title: [Bug] Codegen swaps loop-carried Out tensor handles
body:
### Component

Codegen (orchestration lowering of loop-carried `pl.Out` tensors)

### Description

When an inline helper returns two same-shaped `pl.Out` tensors from a `pl.range` loop, orchestration codegen can cross-wire the loop-carried tensor handles. The generated C++ contains an adjacent two-way assignment such as:

```cpp
a__rv_v2 = b__rv_v2;
b__rv_v2 = a__rv_v2;
```

This is a handle swap, not two independent loop-carried updates. The next loop iteration therefore submits the buffers under the wrong tensor names. Compilation succeeds, but the generated orchestration is semantically incorrect.

The repro deliberately declares the FP32 output `b` before the INT32 output `a` in the helper signature and returns `b, a`. The reversed lexical/parameter order makes the issue deterministic while keeping the tensors otherwise identical in shape. The different element types make the handle mix-up easy to identify in generated code.

### What `write_two` does

`write_two` receives a dynamic row count, an FP32 input `x`, and two output tensors. For two loop iterations, each iteration launches 16 SPMD blocks. Each block owns one row and independently writes:

- `b[row, :] = x[row, :] + 1.0` (FP32),
- `a[row, :] = round(x[row, :])` (INT32).

The helper returns both `Out` values, and the outer JIT function assigns the returned pair back to `b, a`. This forces the compiler to materialize loop-carried versions for both outputs.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a PyPTO checkout at commit `e2079529db77e2a726169f18d9c6e161ef51ec1b` (or a revision containing the same frontend/codegen behavior).
2. Install PyPTO and PyTorch.
3. Save the following file as `tests/repro_out_loop_carry.py`.
4. Run:

   ```bash
   python3 tests/repro_out_loop_carry.py --platform a2a3sim
   ```

5. Inspect the generated `orchestration/repro.cpp`. The script also scans all generated orchestration C++ files and exits with status 1 when it finds the adjacent swap.

```python
"""Minimal PyPTO repro for cross-wired tensor loop carries."""

import argparse
import re
from pathlib import Path

import pypto.language as pl
import torch
from pypto.runtime import RunConfig


ROWS = 32
COLS = 512
CHUNK = 16
ROUNDS = 2
ROWS_DYN = pl.dynamic("REPRO_OUT_LOOP_ROWS")


@pl.jit.inline(auto_scope=False)
def write_two(
    n: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32],
    x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS_DYN, COLS], pl.FP32],
    b: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS_DYN, COLS], pl.FP32]],
    a: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS_DYN, COLS], pl.INT32]],
):
    rows = pl.tensor.dim(x, 0)
    for i in pl.range(n):
        with pl.spmd(CHUNK, name_hint="repro_out_write"):
            row = i * CHUNK + pl.tile.get_block_idx()
            if row < rows:
                src = x[row : row + 1, :]
                b[row : row + 1, :] = pl.add(
                    src,
                    pl.full([1, COLS], dtype=pl.FP32, value=1.0),
                )
                a[row : row + 1, :] = pl.cast(
                    src,
                    target_type=pl.INT32,
                    mode="rint",
                )
    return b, a


@pl.jit
def repro(
    n: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32],
    x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS_DYN, COLS], pl.FP32],
    b: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS_DYN, COLS], pl.FP32]],
    a: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS_DYN, COLS], pl.INT32]],
):
    x.bind_dynamic(0, ROWS_DYN)
    a.bind_dynamic(0, ROWS_DYN)
    b.bind_dynamic(0, ROWS_DYN)
    b, a = write_two(n, x, b, a)
    return b, a


ASSIGNMENT = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?P<lhs>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*__rv[A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*=\s*"
    r"(?P<rhs>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*__rv[A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*;\s*$"
)


def find_swaps(work_dir: Path):
    swaps = []
    for source in work_dir.rglob("*.cpp"):
        if "orchestration" not in source.parts:
            continue
        lines = source.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
        for line_no, (first, second) in enumerate(zip(lines, lines[1:]), 1):
            lhs = ASSIGNMENT.match(first)
            rhs = ASSIGNMENT.match(second)
            if lhs and rhs and lhs["lhs"] == rhs["rhs"] and lhs["rhs"] == rhs["lhs"]:
                swaps.append((source, line_no, first.strip(), second.strip()))
    return swaps


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--platform", choices=("a2a3sim", "a2a3"), default="a2a3sim")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    x = torch.arange(ROWS * COLS, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(ROWS, COLS)
    b = torch.zeros_like(x)
    a = torch.zeros((ROWS, COLS), dtype=torch.int32)
    compiled = repro.compile(
        ROUNDS,
        x,
        b,
        a,
        config=RunConfig(platform=args.platform, save_kernels=True),
    )
    work_dir = Path(compiled.output_dir)
    print(f"compiled: {work_dir}")

    swaps = find_swaps(work_dir)
    if not swaps:
        print("no adjacent __rv swap found")
        return 0

    for source, line_no, first, second in swaps:
        print(f"cross-swap: {source}:{line_no}")
        print(f"  {first}")
        print(f"  {second}")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

### Expected Behavior

The two loop-carried handles must remain independent. A representative generated orchestration sequence should preserve the mapping established at entry:

```cpp
Tensor b__rv_v2 = ext_b;
Tensor a__rv_v2 = ext_a;
// submit the iteration using b__rv_v2 for b and a__rv_v2 for a
// advance each handle independently to its own successor
```

The exact SSA suffixes and temporary names may differ, but there must be no assignment that maps `a` to `b` or `b` to `a`. Each output's successor must be derived from the same output's predecessor.

### Actual Behavior

On the affected revision, compilation succeeds but generated orchestration contains:

```cpp
a__rv_v2 = b__rv_v2;
b__rv_v2 = a__rv_v2;
```

The script reports this as `cross-swap` and exits 1. The two assignments are adjacent and exchange the two tensor handles. In a real multi-iteration program, subsequent task arguments can therefore bind the FP32 and INT32 outputs to the wrong buffers.

### Git Commit ID

`e2079529db77e2a726169f18d9c6e161ef51ec1b`

### NPU Kind

`N/A (frontend/orchestration codegen repro; reproduced with a2a3sim)`

### Host Platform

Linux aarch64, Python 3.11.14, PyTorch `2.11.0+cpu`

### Additional Context

Validated in the PyPTO checkout used by the DeepSeek V4 decode work. The repro does not launch device execution; it only compiles and scans generated orchestration C++. Affected output was generated under `build_output/_jit_repro_out_loop_carry_*/orchestration/repro.cpp`.

Related open issues #2234 and #1326 discuss other loop-carry or multi-output limitations, but neither reports this cross-wired two-`Out` handle assignment.
